en: I praise Agni, the domestic priest, the god who is the officiant of the sacrifice, the invoker,
the bestower of the most abundant treasures.
Agni is to be praised by the ancient seers and by those of the present;
may he bring the gods here to us.
Through Agni may one obtain wealth and nourishment day by day— wealth that is glorious and most rich in heroic sons.
O Agni, whatever sacrifice or rite you encompass on every side—
that alone goes to the gods.
Agni, the invoker, possessing the wisdom of a seer, true and most renowned for his splendor—
may the god come hither with the gods.
Whatever good you shall do for the donor, O Agni,
that is truly yours, O Aṅgiras.
O Agni, illuminator of the darkness, day by day we approach you with our prayer,
bringing homage as we come.
Him who reigns over the sacrifices, the radiant guardian of the Cosmic Order,
increasing in his own abode.
O Agni, be easy of access to us, like a father to his son;
attend to us for our well-being.
O Vāyu, come hither, O beautiful one; these Soma juices have been prepared.
Drink of them and hear our call.
O Vāyu, the singers praise you with hymns; seeking you, they have pressed the soma and know the days.
O Vāyu, your mingling speech goes forth to the donor,
far-reaching for the drinking of Soma.
O Indra and Vāyu, come hither with refreshments to these pressed juices;
for the drops long for you both.
O Vāyu and Indra, you two who possess wealth in horses, take notice of the pressed juices;
come both of you hither with speed.
O Vāyu and Indra, come to the prepared place of the one who presses the soma;
quickly, O heroes, with such a thought as this.
I invoke Mitra of purified will and Varuṇa, the destroyer of enemies, as they perfect our prayer that drips with clarity.
By means of *ṛta*, O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who increase *ṛta* and touch *ṛta*, you have attained great mental power.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, our seers, of many births and wide dominion, you two bestow skillful and active power.
O Aśvins, lords of splendor with swift hands, you who enjoy many things, take pleasure in these sacrificial offerings.
O Aśvins, you of many wondrous deeds, O heroes, with powerful insight, you who are worthy of praise,
accept our songs.
O wonder-workers Nāsatyas, these pressed juices are for you; the sacrificial grass is strewn.
Come hither, O you whose path is like that of Rudra!
O Indra of wondrous luster, come hither; these pressed juices long for you, purified by the fine fingers in a continuous stream.
O Indra, come, impelled by our prayer and urged on by the sages,
to the sacred formulations of the worshiper who has pressed the soma.
O Indra, Lord of the Bay Horses, come swiftly to our sacred hymns;
take pleasure in the pressed soma juice.
O protectors, sustainers of the people, all you gods, come hither;
you who give, [come] to the pressed juice of the giver.
O All-Gods, you who cross the waters, come quickly to the pressed juice,
as cows go to their stalls.
May all the gods, the undeceivers, possessing the power of illusion and free from malice, come as bearers of the sacrifice and take pleasure in the oblation.
May Sarasvatī, the purifier, rich in spoils through her bounties, who possesses wealth through her wisdom, desire our sacrifice.
Impelling truthful words and awakening gracious thoughts,
Sarasvatī has established the sacrifice.
The great ocean, Sarasvatī, makes herself known by her signal;
she illumines all thoughts.
For our protection, we invoke day by day the maker of beautiful forms, as one calls a good milch-cow for the milker.
Come to our libations; O drinker of Soma, drink of the Soma!
Indeed, the exhilaration of the wealthy one bestows cattle.
Then may we find the most intimate of your favors;
do not overlook us, but come to us.
Go forth and ask the wise Indra, the invincible one,
who is more excellent for you than [all] your friends.
And let our revilers say, "We have turned away from others," while they offer worship only to Indra.
And may the people, O Wondrous One, call us fortunate;
may we abide in the protection of Indra.
Bring this swift one to the swift, who is the glory of the sacrifice and the delight of men;
flying, he gladdens his friend.
Having drunk of this, O Śatakratu, you became the slayer of the Vṛtras; you protected the victor in the contests for booty.
O Śatakratu, we urge you on, the prize-winner, in the contests for booty;
O Indra, for the winning of riches.
To him who is a great source of wealth, easy to cross over, and the friend of the one who presses the soma—
to that Indra, sing!
Come hither and sit down; sing forth to Indra, O friends who bring hymns of praise.
To Indra, the most frequent among many, the lord of desirable things, when the Soma is pressed.
May he indeed come to us for our yoking; may he come for wealth and for inspired wisdom;
may he come to us with spoils of war.
Sing for that Indra, at whose presence the enemies do not withstand his two bay steeds in battles.
To the one who drinks the pressed juice, these pure pressed juices go for his enjoyment— Soma-draughts mixed with curd.
O Indra, you of noble wisdom, having grown great at once for the drinking of the pressed juice, you were born for preeminence.
O Indra, lover of songs, may the swift Soma juices enter you; may they be a source of well-being for you, the wise one.
The hymns have magnified you, and the recitations have magnified you, O Lord of a hundred powers;
may our songs magnify you.
May Indra, whose protection is imperishable, win this thousandfold booty,
in which all manly powers reside.
O Indra, lover of songs, let not mortals do harm to our bodies;
as the sovereign lord, ward off the weapon of death.
Those who stand around harness the ruddy, red-hued steed as he moves; the luminous realms shine in the sky.
They yoke his two beloved bay horses to the chariot on its two sides—
red, bold, and carrying the hero.
Making a signal for the signalless, O men, making a form for the formless,
you were born together with the dawns.
Then indeed, according to their own nature, they have again assumed the state of embryos,
assuming a name worthy of sacrifice.
O Indra, with those who shatter even what is firm and with those who are the carriers [of the sacrifice],
you found the ruddy cows even in the cave.
Seeking the gods, they have raised their voices toward the one who finds wealth, according to their thought—
toward the great and renowned one.
For you shall be seen united with Indra, having come together with him who is fearless— both of you joyful, equal in splendor.
With blameless, radiant hosts beloved by Indra, the sacrifice shines with power.
From there, O wanderer, come hither, or from the luminous realm of heaven;
our songs strive together toward him.
From here we seek bounty, or from heaven, or from the earth,
or from the great mid-air— Indra.
To Indra alone have the singers sung aloud; to Indra with hymns have the chanters chanted;
to Indra have the voices cried out.
Indra indeed is joined with the two bay steeds, mingled together, yoked by a word; Indra is the wielder of the thunderbolt, the golden one.
Indra raised the sun high in the sky for far-reaching vision; he split the mountain open with his rays of light.
O Indra, protect us in battles for booty and in contests for a thousandfold prizes, O fierce one,
with your fierce aids.
We invoke Indra in the great contest, Indra in the small; we call upon the wielder of the thunderbolt as our ally against the Vṛtras.
O Bull, O ever-giving one, open up for us that vessel of oblation;
be irresistible for us.
At every pressing, whatever hymns of Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt,
are superior— none of them equal his perfect praise.
Like a bull among the herds, he drives the people forward with his might;
he is the sovereign, unopposed.
He who alone rules over the people, over the treasures—
Indra, the lord of the five tribes.
We invoke Indra for you from all sides, away from other people;
may he be ours alone.
O Indra, bring for our protection that most excellent wealth which is winning, victorious, and ever-conquering.
By means of which we may, aided by you, strike down the Vṛtras with our fists and overcome them with our horses.
O Indra, protected by you, may we take up the thunderbolt as a weapon;
may we completely conquer our rivals in battle.
O Indra, with you as our ally, may we, through brave archers,
overcome those who attack us.
Great is Indra, and let his majesty extend even further to the wielder of the thunderbolt; in breadth, his power is like the sky.
Or those men who have sought refuge in you during confusion for the winning of offspring—
whether they be inspired poets yearning for prayerful vision.
His belly, the greatest drinker of Soma, swells like the ocean;
it is like the waters from the vastness of the palate.
For thus indeed is his gracious bounty— abundant, rich in cattle, and great—
like a branch laden with ripe fruit for the donor.
For thus indeed are thy powers and aids, O Indra, for one such as I;
they are instantly available to the donor.
For thus indeed are his desirable things: the hymn and the recitation are to be chanted for Indra, for the drinking of the Soma.
Come, O Indra, and exhilarate yourself with the soma-juice at all the soma-pressings;
you are great, a helper by your might.
Release this exhilarating one for the exhilarated Indra at the pressed juice—
for him who performs all deeds.
O fair-cheeked one, lord of all people, rejoice with these exhilarating hymns of praise at these libations.
O Indra, songs have been poured forth for you; they have risen up toward you, longing for the bull, the lord.
O Indra, impel toward us a wonderful and choice gift; may it be abundant and sufficient for you.
O Indra, impel us well therein toward wealth— us who are impetuous,
O thou of many glories, and full of renown.
O Indra, bestow upon us wide and lofty fame, rich in cattle and in booty;
grant us all-encompassing, imperishable life.
Bestow upon us great renown and splendor that wins a thousandfold;
O Indra, grant us those nourishments borne on chariots.
Praising with songs Indra, the lord of wealth, the one worthy of hymns,
may we bring him here for our protection.
At every pressing, for him who is the master of the home, the noble one sings forth a great hymn of praise to the mighty Indra.
The singers of the *gāyatrī* chant thee; the reciters of hymns praise thy song.
O Śatakratu, the priests have raised thee up like a pole.
When he climbed from ridge to ridge and beheld much that was yet to be done, Indra perceived the goal; the bull moves forward with his herd.
Yoke, O Indra, your two long-maned, bay steeds, the vigorous ones that fill out their girths;
then, O Soma-drinker, come to listen to our songs.
Come hither, respond to our hymns, sing aloud, and roar!
O Vasu, Indra, favor our prayer and increase our sacrifice.
A hymn worthy of praise, a source of strength for Indra, who bestows many gifts—
so that Śakra may take delight in our libations and in our friendship.
Him indeed we seek for friendship, him for wealth, him for heroic power;
may that Śakra Indra be able to help us, bestowing riches.
Well-opened and well-cleared is this glory, O Indra, won by thee;
unbar the stall of the cows and bestow thy bounty, O wielder of the stone.
For neither of the two worlds, heaven and earth, can restrain you when you are wrathful;
conquer the waters rich in light, and shake down the cattle for us.
O you whose ear is ready to hear, listen to my call; now indeed take up my songs.
O Indra, place this hymn of mine even closer than your own companions.
For we know you as the most virile one, who hears our invocation in the contests for booty;
we invoke the aid of the most virile one, that which bestows a thousandfold gain.
O Indra, son of Kuśika, rejoicing, drink our pressed soma!
Prolong our new life; make the seer a winner of a thousandfold.
O lover of songs, may these songs encompass you on every side;
may these increases increase your life-span, and may these delights be welcome to you.
All songs have magnified Indra, who is as expansive as the ocean;
the best of charioteers among charioteers, the lord and true master of spoils.
In your friendship, O Indra, we who possess strength—O Lord of Might—let us not fear.
We cry out toward you, the unconquered victor.
The many gifts of Indra do not fail;
his aids do not cease, when he bestows the wealth of cattle-filled booty upon his worshippers.
The breaker of forts, the youthful sage, of immeasurable power, was born— Indra,
the sustainer of every deed, the wielder of the thunderbolt, praised by many.
O wielder of the stone, you opened the cave of Vala, who possessed the cattle;
the gods, being urged on, came to you while remaining fearless.
O Hero, through your gifts I have come back, calling out to the river; O lover of songs, the poets who know you have stood near you.
O Indra, with your wondrous powers you overthrew the guileful Śuṣṇa;
the wise know this deed of yours—exalt the fame of those sages.
The hymns have sung aloud to Indra, the ruler by his might,
whose gifts are a thousandfold or even more abundant.
We choose Agni as our messenger, the invoker, the all-knowing,
the skillful performer of this sacrifice.
With invocations, they ever call upon Agni after Agni, the lord of the people,
the bearer of oblations, the one beloved by many.
O Agni, being born, bring the gods here for the one who has trimmed the sacrificial grass;
you are our invoker, worthy of praise.
Awaken them who desire you, O Agni, when you go on your mission as messenger;
sit together with the gods upon the sacrificial grass.
O Agni, invoked with clarified butter, shining one, burn against those who seek to harm us—
burn against the sorcerers!
By Agni is Agni kindled— the sage, the master of the house, the youth, the bearer of oblations, whose mouth is the sacrificial ladle.
Praise Agni, the seer, whose laws are true at the sacrifice—
the god who drives away disease.
O Agni, for that lord of oblations who worships you as his divine messenger,
be his protector.
O Purifier, be gracious to him who, possessing oblations, seeks to win over Agni for the feast of the gods.
O purifying, radiant Agni, bring the gods here to us—
to our sacrifice and our oblation.
Being thus praised with this newest song, bring us wealth and food accompanied by heroic sons.
O Agni, with your bright radiance and with all invocations of the gods,
graciously accept this hymn of praise from us.
O Agni, well-kindled, bring the gods here for the one who offers the oblation;
O purifying Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice.
O Sage Tanūnapāt, make our honey-sweet sacrifice reach the gods today, so that they may partake of it.
I invoke here at this sacrifice Narāśaṃsa, the beloved one,
honey-tongued and prepared with oblations.
O Agni, being invoked, bring the gods on your most comfortable chariot;
you are the Hotṛ-priest appointed by Manu.
O wise ones, spread the sacrificial grass in due order, its back anointed with ghee,
where the vision of immortality is found.
May the divine doors, which increase the cosmic order and are unfailing, swing wide today and now for the sacrifice.
I invoke Night and Dawn, the beautifully adorned, to this sacrifice,
so that they may sit upon this sacred grass of ours.
I invoke those two fair-tongued divine Hotṛs, the sages;
may they perform this sacrifice of ours.
Iḷā, Sarasvatī, and Mahī— may these three goddesses, who bring delight,
sit upon the sacrificial grass, O infallible ones.
I invoke here Tvaṣṭṛ, the foremost, who possesses all forms;
may he be ours alone.
O divine Lord of the Forest, release the oblation for the gods;
may the intention of the giver be fulfilled.
With the cry of Svāhā, perform the sacrifice for Indra in the house of the sacrificer;
there I summon the gods.
O Agni, come with all these gods to our service and our songs for the drinking of Soma; come and perform the sacrifice.
The Kaṇvas have called upon you; O inspired one, they sing your hymns.
O Agni, come hither with the gods!
Indra and Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Mitra and Agni, Pūṣan, Bhaga, the Ādityas, and the host of Maruts.
Your exhilarating, intoxicating drops are being brought forth—
the drops of honey resting in the vessels.
Seeking your aid, the Kaṇvas, who have trimmed the sacrificial grass, invoke you;
they bring oblations and have prepared the offerings.
May the steeds who carry you— their backs anointed with ghee, yoked by thought— bring the gods here for the drinking of Soma.
O Agni, make those worshipful ones who increase the cosmic order possessed of their wives;
O fair-tongued one, cause them to drink the honeyed draught.
O Agni, may those who are worthy of sacrifice and those who are to be praised drink of this honeyed [oblation] with your tongue at the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*.
From the very realm of light of the sun, may the inspired priest, the Hotṛ, bring here all the gods who awaken at dawn.
O Agni, drink the Soma mead with all [the gods], with Indra and Vāyu, according to the ordinances of Mitra.
O Agni, you, established by Manu as the Hotṛ-priest, sit at the sacrifices;
therefore, perform this sacrifice for us.
Yoke, O God, the ruddy mares to your chariot, the bay and the red ones;
with them, bring the gods here.
O Indra, drink the Soma according to the season; let the drops enter you—intoxicating ones that dwell in that very place.
O Maruts, drink according to the season from the Potar’s cup; purify the sacrifice, for you are indeed the bounteous givers.
O Gnas, favor our sacrifice; O Neṣṭar, drink according to the season, for you are the bestower of treasures.
O Agni, bring the gods here; seat them in the three wombs;
attend to them and drink according to the season.
O Indra, drink the Soma from the Brahmin’s gift according to the seasons;
for your friendship is invincible.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you two who uphold the sacred law, have through the cosmic order attained the invincible skill for the sacrifice.
The givers of wealth, with pressing-stones in hand at the sacrifice,
invoke the god for wealth during the rites.
May Draviṇodas grant us those riches which are renowned;
may we win them among the gods.
The giver of wealth desires to drink; offer the oblation and step forward!
Send it forth from the office of the Neṣṭṛ according to the seasons.
When we worship you, the giver of wealth, with the four seasonal offerings,
then indeed become a bestower of gifts for us.
O Aśvins, drinkers of the sweet mead, with blazing fires and pure vows, you who convey the sacrifice according to the season, drink [the soma].
O truthful one, you are the leader of the sacrifice through the domestic fire and according to the season; worship the gods for the sake of the one who seeks the gods.
Let the bay steeds bring you hither, O Indra, the bull, for the drinking of the Soma; let those with sun-like vision bring you, O Indra.
May these roasted grains dripping with ghee bring the two bay steeds here; may they bring Indra upon his most comfortable chariot.
We invoke Indra in the morning; we invoke Indra as the sacrifice proceeds;
we invoke Indra for the drinking of the Soma.
Come to our pressed juice with your long-maned bay horses, O Indra;
for we invoke you when the soma is pressed.
Come to this our hymn of praise; come to this pressed libation.
Drink like a thirsty buffalo.
These Soma drops, the pressed juices, are upon the sacred grass;
O Indra, drink them for the sake of strength.
May this foremost hymn of praise reach your heart, most healing;
then drink the pressed Soma.
Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, goes to every pressed libation for exhilaration, to drink the Soma.
Fulfill this desire of ours with cattle and horses, O Śatakratu;
we, with pious thoughts, shall praise you.
I choose for myself the protection of Indra and Varuṇa, the two sovereign kings;
may they both be gracious to us in such a state.
For you two are indeed the ones who come for the protection of the invocation of a sage such as I; you are the sustainers of the people.
O Indra and Varuṇa, satisfy us with wealth according to our desire;
as such, we seek you most closely.
For may we be among those favored by your powers, favored by your benevolences,
and recipients of your gifts of booty.
Indra is the most bountiful among those who give a thousandfold; Varuṇa is the most worthy of praise among those to be extolled; he becomes the praiseworthy power of the hymn.
Through the protection of these two, may we win and store up [wealth];
may there also be a surplus for distribution.
O Indra and Varuṇa, I invoke you both for wondrous bounty;
make us truly victorious.
O Indra and Varuṇa, now indeed, while our prayers desire to win you,
grant protection to us.
O Indra and Varuṇa, may this fair praise reach you both, which I invoke— the joint hymn of praise that you two bring to fulfillment.
O Brahmaṇaspati, make Soma our resonant leader—
him who is Kakṣīvat, the son of Uśij.
May he who is wealthy, the dispeller of disease, the finder of riches, the increaser of prosperity— may he, the swift one, attend to us.
May the curse of the stingy mortal, his treacherous assault, not reach us.
Protect us, O Brahmaṇaspati!
That mortal whom Indra, Brahmaṇaspati, and Soma impel— truly, that hero does not come to harm.
O Brahmanaspati, O Soma, and Indra— may Dakṣiṇā protect that mortal from distress.
I have approached the wonderful Lord of the Assembly, the beloved and desirable friend of Indra— the winner of prizes and the source of wisdom.
Without whom even the sacrifice of the wise man does not succeed, he promotes the application of our prayers.
Then he makes the oblation successful; he makes the sacrifice proceed forward;
the invocation goes to the gods.
I have beheld Narāśaṃsa, the most courageous and most far-extending,
like the dwelling-place of heaven, full of sacrificial zeal.
To this beautiful sacrifice you are summoned for protection;
O Agni, come with the Maruts.
Neither god nor mortal surpasses your great power of will; O Agni, come hither with the Maruts.
O Agni, come with the Maruts— those all-gods who know the great mid-region and are free from malice.
Those who, fierce and unassailable by their might, have sung the hymn of praise—
O Agni, come with those Maruts.
Those who are radiant, of terrible aspect, possessing good dominion, and destroyers of enemies—
with those Maruts, O Agni, come hither!
O Agni, come with the Maruts, those gods who dwell upon the luminous vault of the firmament in heaven.
O Agni, come hither with the Maruts— those who cause the mountains to tremble and pass across the surging ocean.
Those who stretch across the ocean with their rays by means of their might— O Agni, come hither with those Maruts.
I pour forth for you the Soma-mead for the first draught;
O Agni, come hither with the Maruts.
This hymn, O gods, has been fashioned for the sake of the people by the inspired poets with devotion; it is the bestower of the most excellent treasures.
Those who for Indra fashioned with their minds the two bay steeds yoked by speech, they have attained the sacrifice through their labors.
For the Nāsatyas they fashioned a comfortable, all-encompassing chariot;
for them they fashioned a cow that milks forth abundance.
The *Ṛbhus*, whose mantras are true and who strive for rectitude, have made their aged parents young again through their skillful labor.
Your exhilarations have come together with Indra, who is accompanied by the Maruts,
and with the Ādityas, the kings.
And that new beaker of the divine Tvaṣṭṛ, which had been fashioned,
you made into four again.
Bestow upon us treasures—threefold sets—for the one who presses the Soma;
grant them one by one in response to our excellent praises.
The bearers [of the sacrifice] have maintained [the order]; through their skillful action, they have obtained among the gods their share worthy of sacrifice.
Here I invoke Indra and Agni; we desire their hymn of praise.
They two are the greatest drinkers of Soma—[the drinkers] of Soma.
Praise them at the sacrifices, O men—Indra and Agni—and adorn them;
sing of them in *gāyatra* hymns.
Those two, the praises of Mitra— Indra and Agni— we invoke them as Soma-drinkers for the drinking of the Soma.
Being mighty, we invoke you both to this pressed libation;
may Indra and Agni come hither.
O Indra and Agni, you two great lords of the assembly, crush the demons;
let the devourers be childless.
By that truth, be watchful upon the conscious station;
O Indra and Agni, grant us protection.
Awaken the two Aśvins who yoke their chariot at dawn; let them come here to drink of this Soma.
Those two who possess excellent chariots, who are the best of charioteers, the two gods who touch the heavens— those Aśvins we invoke.
O Aśvins, with that whip of yours which is honeyed and full of pleasant truth, sprinkle the sacrifice.
For there is no place far away for you two, where you do not go by chariot,
O Aśvins, to the house of the Soma-presser.
I invoke Savitṛ, the golden-handed, for aid;
he, the god, is the knower of the path.
Praise Savitṛ, the Son of the Waters, for his protection;
we desire to follow his sacred laws.
We invoke Savitṛ, the beholder of men, the distributor of wonderful wealth and gracious bounty.
O friends, sit down; Savitar is now to be praised by us—he, the giver of riches, makes them beautiful.
O Agni, bring hither the willing wives of the gods,
and Tvaṣṭṛ, for the drinking of the Soma.
O Agni, youngest one, bring hither the divine dames for our protection— the Hotrā, the Bhāratī,
the Varūtrī, and the Dhiṣaṇā.
May the goddesses, the wives of the lords of men, with their great protection and shelter, come to us with their unbroken wings.
I invoke Indrāṇī hither for our well-being, Varuṇānī for our prosperity,
and Agnāyī for the drinking of Soma.
May the great Heaven and Earth bedew this sacrifice for us; may they fill us with nourishments.
The inspired poets lick with their prayers the ghee-rich milk of those two,
in the fixed place of the Gandharva.
O Earth, be pleasant, thornless, and a place of rest for us;
grant us wide-spreading shelter.
May the gods protect us from that place whence Viṣṇu strode forth across the seven domains of the earth.
Viṣṇu strode through this [universe]; in three places he planted his step; the whole world is gathered in his footstep-dust.
Viṣṇu, the infallible guardian, strode forth his three steps,
thereby upholding the sacred laws.
Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu, through which he has made his ordinances visible;
he is the close-allied friend of Indra.
The wise ever behold that highest step of Viṣṇu,
like an eye fixed in the sky.
The inspired poets, ever-watchful and full of praise, kindle that highest step of Viṣṇu.
Strong are these Soma juices; come hither! These pressed libations are accompanied by blessings; O Vāyu, drink them as they are presented.
We invoke both gods, Indra and Vāyu, who touch the heavens,
for the drinking of this Soma.
Indra and Vāyu, swift as thought, the inspired poets invoke for aid— the thousand-eyed lords of our prayers.
We invoke Mitra and Varuṇa for the drinking of Soma— those two who,
from their very birth, possess purified strength.
Those two who, by means of *ṛta*, increase *ṛta* and are the lords of the light of *ṛta*—
those Mitra and Varuṇa I invoke.
May Varuṇa be our protector and Mitra with all his aids;
may they both make us richly blessed.
We invoke Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, for the drinking of the Soma; may he, in harmony with his host, satisfy himself.
With Indra as their chief, the hosts of Maruts, the gods who grant prosperity through Pūṣan—
may all of you hear my call.
O bounteous ones, with Indra as your powerful ally, slay Vṛtra;
let not the malevolent one have power over us.
We invoke all the gods and the Maruts to drink the Soma;
for they, the sons of Pṛśni, are mighty.
Like the thundering of victors, the roar of the Maruts goes forth boldly when you go toward glory,
O heroes.
Born from the laughter of lightning, may they protect us;
may the Maruts be gracious to us.
O Pūṣan, O glowing one, bring [the horse] that is upon the variegated sacrificial grass, the support of heaven,
like a lost animal.
The glowing Pūṣan found the king who was hidden, concealed in a secret place, upon the variegated sacrificial grass.
And so, by means of the drops, may he drive toward me six yoked [steeds],
plowing barley with cattle as it were.
The waters go along their paths like sisters for those performing the sacrifice,
blending milk with honey.
Those [goddesses] who are near the sun, or those with whom the sun is joined—
may they speed our sacrifice forward.
I invoke the divine waters where our cattle drink;
an oblation is to be prepared for the rivers.
Within the waters is immortality, within the waters is healing; for the praise of the waters, O gods, become winners of the prize.
Soma has told me within the waters that all healing remedies are there— Agni, who brings well-being to all, and the waters, which possess every medicine.
O Waters, bestow healing medicine as a protection for my body,
so that I may long behold the sun.
O Waters, carry away this whatever evil is in me—
whatever I have committed as treachery, or whatever curse I have uttered, or even untruth.
Today I have entered the waters; we have united with their essence.
O Agni, come hither full of milk; endow me with splendor.
O Agni, endow me with splendor, with progeny, and with long life.
May the gods take note of this of mine; may Indra, together with the seers, take note.
Of which of the immortals, of whom indeed, shall we now proclaim the dear name of the god?
Who will give us back to mighty Aditi, so that I may behold my father and my mother?
We meditate upon Agni, the first of the immortals, the lovely name of the god. May he restore us to great Aditi, so that I may behold my father and my mother once again.
O God Savitṛ, sovereign lord of all desirable things, we ever seek a portion from you, O bounteous one.
For whatever Bhaga, exerting himself thus from of old before reproach,
has placed in your hands that which is free from hatred.
May we, through your protection, rise up as those who have received our portion from you, grasping at the head of wealth.
Neither thy dominion, nor thy might, nor thy wrath have these birds flying through the air attained;
nor have these waters flowing unceasingly, nor those who disregard the power of the wind.
In the bottomless [depth], King Varuṇa, whose will is pure, establishes the summit of the tree upright.
Their branches point downward; their base is above. May our banners be established within it.
For King Varuṇa has made wide for Sūrya a path to follow;
he has provided feet where there were no feet to set them down, and he is the remover even of that which pierces the heart.
A hundred physicians are yours, O King, a thousand; let your benevolence be wide and deep.
Drive Nirṛti far away to the distance, and release us from whatever sin we have committed.
Those stars which were placed on high and are seen at night—where indeed do they go by day?
Unswerving are the ordinances of Varuṇa; the moon moves through the night, looking upon them all.
I seek that from you, worshipping with a sacred prayer; the sacrificer desires that through his oblations.
O Varuṇa, be present here without anger; O you of wide renown, do not steal away our life.
That indeed they tell me by night, that by day; that very thought my heart perceives clearly:
may King Varuṇa, whom Śunaḥśepa called upon when he was seized, release us.
For Śunaḥśepa, seized and bound to three wooden posts, called upon the Āditya.
May King Varuṇa release him; may the wise, undeceived one loosen his bonds.
O Varuṇa, we appease your anger with prostrations; we entreat it away with sacrifices and oblations.
O wise Asura, O King, as you dwell among us, loosen the sins we have committed.
O Varuṇa, loosen the uppermost bond from us, untie the lowest, and release the middle one.
Then, O Āditya, may we be sinless before you and before Aditi, remaining steadfast in your law.
For whatever transgression of your law we may commit day after day, O God Varuṇa, as people do— whatever it may be.
Do not deliver us to the weapon of one who seeks to slay, nor to the wrath of one who is angry.
O Varuṇa, with our songs we would loosen your mind for mercy, as a charioteer loosens a harnessed horse.
For my prayers, free from anger, fly forth toward the desire for wealth,
like birds to their nests.
When shall we bring hither Varuṇa, the hero, the glory of dominion, the far-seeing one, for the sake of his mercy?
That same [work] both of them perform together; longing for it, they do not turn away from the donor who maintains the sacred law.
He who knows the track of birds flying through the mid-air, he who knows the ships of the ocean— [he is Agni].
He who is firm in his vows knows the twelve months and those offspring that are born. He knows him who is being born.
He knows the path of the wind, vast, exalted, and great;
he knows those who dwell upon it.
Varuṇa, whose holy law is firm and who is most wise, has sat down in his dwellings for sovereign rule.
From there, the wise one beholds all wonders—
those things already done and those yet to be done.
May that Āditya, the one of noble wisdom, make for us fair paths at all times;
may he prolong our lives.
Wearing a golden mantle, Varuṇa has clothed himself in a bright garment;
his spies have settled all around him.
Him whom the seekers of harm do not seek to injure, nor the malevolent among men, nor the enemies of the gods— [that god].
And he who has established incomparable glory among men—
may it be within our very bellies.
My thoughts go forth like cattle to their pastures,
seeking the one of wide vision.
Let us two speak together again, since the honey has been brought for me;
like a Hotṛ-priest, you shall consume the beloved [soma].
Behold now him who is visible to all; behold his chariot upon the earth.
May he take pleasure in these my songs.
O Varuṇa, hear this my invocation today and be gracious; seeking your aid, I long for you.
O wise one, you rule over all that is in heaven and on earth;
as such, listen to us at our approach.
Release us from the highest bond; loosen the middle one;
cast off the lowest so that we may live.
Clothe yourself in garments, O worthy of sacrifice, O Lord of nourishments;
as such, perform this sacrifice for us.
O Agni, most youthful one, may you, the desirable Hotṛ-priest, always [be present] for us through our prayers, with your word that shines from heaven.
For indeed, the father sacrifices for his son,
the kinsman for his kinsman, and the excellent friend for his friend.
May Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, who destroy the enemies, sit upon our sacred grass, as they did for Manu.
O ancient invoker, rejoice in this our friendship;
truly, hear these songs of ours.
For whenever we sacrifice to god after god in an eternal succession,
it is in you alone that the oblation is offered.
May the lord of the people be dear to us—the delightful and choice-worthy Hotṛ-priest;
may we, possessing good fires, be dear [to him].
For the gods, having good sacrificial fires, have bestowed desirable wealth upon us; we, too, with our sacrificial fires well-tended, meditate [upon them].
Then, O Immortal One, may there be mutual praises between us, both the mortals and [the immortals].
O Agni, with all your fires, accept this sacrifice and this speech;
grant us delight, O young son of strength!
I would praise you with prostrations like a prize-winning horse, Agni,
the sovereign ruler of sacrifices.
May he indeed, our son, by his might, far-reaching in his course and most gracious,
become a bountiful giver for us.
Do thou, who art all-encompassing life, protect us always from the malevolent mortal, both from afar and from near at hand.
O Agni, do you indeed proclaim this our newest song of praise, this our gain, among the gods.
Grant us a share in the highest spoils, and in those that are middling; bestow upon us wealth from even the nearest source.
O you of variegated luster, you are distributed in the wave of the river nearby;
instantly you flow for the donor.
O Agni, that mortal whom you protect in battles and whom you urge on in the contests for booty—
he shall be the master of eternal nourishments.
O conqueror, no one at all can overcome him;
his strength is worthy of renown.
May he, who belongs to all people, be a conqueror of booty with his horses; may he be a winner of wealth with his inspired singers.
O Jarābodha, bring forth that for every worshipper who is worthy of sacrifice—
a beautiful hymn of praise for Rudra.
May he, the great one, free from pride, whose banner is smoke, and who is many-shining, impel us toward wisdom and toward booty.
Like a wealthy lord of the people, may the divine banner, Agni of the lofty luster, hear us through our hymns of praise.
Homage to the great ones, homage to the small ones; homage to the young, and homage to the aged.
Let us sacrifice to the gods if we are able; O gods, may I not incur the reproach of one who is superior.
Where the broad-based pressing-stone stands upright for the sake of extracting the juice— there,
O Indra, may you drink greedily of the drops pressed out by the mortar.
Where the two pressing-boards are fashioned like two buttocks— there, O Indra, you have drunk with eager thirst the juices pressed out by the mortar.
Where the woman learns both the non-shaking and the shaking, there,
O Indra, you have known how to gulp down the juices pressed by the mortar.
Where they bind the churning-sticks like one who restrains reins— there, O Indra, you have known and eagerly drunk of the juices pressed by the mortar.
For although you, O mortar, are joined in every single house,
here speak most brilliantly, like the drum of victors!
Moreover, O Lord of the Forest, the wind blows right at your tip;
therefore, O mortar, press out the Soma for Indra to drink.
The two who win the sacrifice, the best at gaining booty— they indeed are held aloft,
devouring the soma-juices like two bay horses.
O lofty Vanaspatis, press today for us with your lofty pressers this honeyed juice for Indra.
Bring the remnant from the two ladles; pour the Soma onto the filter;
place it upon the cow's hide.
For even if, O truthful Soma-drinker, we are as if unpraised,
O Indra, most wealthy one, do you indeed grant us hope for thousands of beautiful cattle and horses.
O Siprin, Lord of spoils, possessor of power, by your wondrous deed,
O Indra, most wealthy one, do you now grant us a share of thousands of beautiful cattle and horses.
Lull them to sleep, O you two of diverse appearance; let them lie down and not wake.
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful cattle and horses!
Let those enemies sleep; O Hero, let the patrons wake!
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful cattle and horses.
O Indra, crush the donkey who brays with such wicked intent!
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful cattle and horses!
Let the wind blow far away from the forest with its whirling eddies;
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful cattle and horses!
Slay every reviler; crush the Kṛkadāśva!
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful cattle and horses.
Like those seeking booty, we pour out the most bountiful Indra with drops of soma, as one pours for the hundred-fold powerful Krivi.
He who [offers] a hundred of the pure or a thousand of the milk-mixed [oblations]— verily,
he flows like water down a slope.
When he comes together for the sake of the exhilarating draught, these [soma-juices] indeed find a place within his belly; he possesses a vast capacity like the ocean.
This [soma] of yours you swallow up, like a pigeon its nest;
yet you do not heed that word.
O Hero, Lord of bounties, you who are borne by songs of praise, may your splendor and your truthful word be abundant for him who offers this hymn to you.
Stand up for our protection in this contest, O Lord of a hundred powers;
let us two converse together concerning other matters.
In every endeavor and in every contest for booty, we, as friends, invoke Indra, the most powerful one, for our protection.
May he indeed come if he hears us, with his thousandfold aids and with strengths, to our invocation.
I invoke the hero of many powers from his ancient dwelling,
whom your father invoked before you.
O you who are invoked by many, O possessor of all boons, we entreat you—
O Friend, O Vasu— for those who sing your praises.
O Soma-drinker, among us who have beautiful jaws and who drink the soma, O friend, wielder of the thunderbolt, [be the leader] of our friends.
O Soma-drinker, O friend, wielder of the thunderbolt, let it be so; act accordingly, so that we may desire your favor.
May there be for us, at our common feast with Indra, opulent riches accompanied by abundant strength—
those through which we, possessing food, may rejoice.
O bold one, you who are like yourself, having come to the singers of praise in person, you have granted them [wealth] as if you were removing a wheel from two chariot-axles.
When you, O Lord of a hundred powers, accept the service and the desire of the singers,
you fulfill it with your mighty deeds as one turns the axle of a wheel.

Evermore Indra has won riches with his snorting, roaring, and panting [steeds]. May he, the wonder-worker, grant us a chariot of gold; may he, the winner, give us for our winning; he has bestowed it upon us.
O Aśvins, come with your powerful chariot to this place rich in horses; O wonder-workers, [come] with wealth in cattle and gold.
For your immortal chariot, O wonder-workers, yoked with a single team,
travels upon the ocean, O Aśvins.
You two have fixed the wheel of the chariot upon the head of the inviolable one; the other wheel moves around the sky.
O Uṣas, dear to all, what mortal has enjoyed thee, O immortal one?
Whom dost thou approach, O radiant one?
For we have meditated upon you from near and from afar,
O you who are bright and ruddy like a horse.
Come to us with those same strengths, O Daughter of Heaven; bestow wealth upon us.

O Agni, you were the first Aṅgiras, the seer; as a god, you became the auspicious friend of the gods. Under your ordinance, the Maruts—sages active through their wisdom and possessing flashing spears—were born.
O Agni, you are the first, the best of the Aṅgiras; as a seer, you encompass the sacred law (*vratam*) of the gods.
Pervasive for the entire world, wise, born of two mothers, you lie down in many ways for the sake of the living man.
O Agni, you were the first for Mātariśvan; you became manifest through your skillful wisdom for Vivasvat.
Both heaven and earth trembled at your election as the Hotṛ-priest; O Vasu, you bore the burden unswervingly and sacrificed to the great ones.
O Agni, you caused the sky to roar for Manu; for the well-doing Purūravas, you, the greater doer of good, [acted].
When you were released from your parents by means of strength, they led you forward first and then back again.
O Agni, you are the bull who increases prosperity; you become worthy of renown for the one who raises the ladle.
You who know the oblation and the *vaṣaṭ*-utterance, you, as the sole life-force, seek to win over the clans at the beginning.
O Agni, you deliver the man who follows crooked paths at the meeting-place in the assembly, O far-seeing one;
he who, in the clash for heroes or in the pursuit of wealth, even with few companions, slays the many in the encounter.
O Agni, you establish that mortal in the highest immortality for the sake of glory day by day—
you who, being thirsty, create bliss for both kinds of beings and provide nourishment to the patron.
O Agni, being praised, make us a glorious singer for the winning of riches;
may we succeed through this new work and ritual action. O Heaven and Earth, together with the gods, protect us!
O Agni, you, the blameless and watchful god among the gods, are in the lap of our parents; be the protector of our bodies and the guardian of the singer. O auspicious one, you bestow all wealth.
O Agni, you are our guardian, you are our father; you are the maker of our strength, for we are your kinsmen.
Hundreds and thousands of riches come together unto you, the protector of the sacred law, the invincible one who possesses heroic sons.
O Agni, the gods made you the first living being for the living man, the lord of the clans of Nahuṣa;
they made Iḷā the instructor of Manu’s progeny, when a son is born from his father.
O Agni, O worshipful god, protect us with your guardians, both our patrons and our own bodies;
you are the savior of our offspring and progeny, and of our cattle, watching over them without blinking in your sacred law.
O Agni, you are kindled as a four-eyed guardian close at hand for the sacrificer who is unarmed;
you favor with your mind the prayer even of the poor man who has offered oblations so that he may dwell in safety.

O Agni, for the worshipper who praises you widely, you win that most excellent and desirable wealth; you are called the protector and father even of the weak. You instruct the simple and, as one who knows better, point out the directions.
O Agni, you protect the man who offers the sacrificial fee on every side, as if with well-sewn armor;
he who provides sweet food, who makes his dwelling pleasant, and who performs the sacrifice of living beings—he is the peer of heaven.
O Agni, forgive this our transgression; forgive this path which we have traveled from afar.
You are the kinsman, the father, the protector of those worthy of Soma; you are the refuge and the inspirer of mortals.
O Agni, O Angiras, like Manu, like Angiras, and like Yayāti, come to our seat as of old, O pure one!
Approach, bring hither the divine host, seat them upon the sacred grass, and sacrifice to the beloved ones.

O Agni, grow strong by this sacred prayer (*brahman*), whether we have performed it for you with skill or with knowledge. And lead us forward toward greater prosperity; unite us with your benevolence that is rich in strength.
I shall now proclaim the heroic deeds of Indra, those which the wielder of the thunderbolt performed for the first time:
he slew the serpent, he pierced the waters, and he split open the bellies of the mountains.
He slew the serpent as he lay coiled upon the mountain; Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for him the resounding thunderbolt.
Like lowing cows, the flowing waters went straight down to the ocean.
Acting like a bull, he chose the Soma; at the Trikadruka rites, he drank of the pressed juice.
Maghavan took up his missile, the thunderbolt; he slew him, the first-born of the serpents.
When you, O Indra, slew the first-born of the dragons, and destroyed the magic powers of the deceivers along with their magic;
then, generating the sun, the sky, and the dawn, from that time on you truly found no enemy at all.
Indra slew Vṛtra, the worst of Vṛtras, the shoulderless one, with his great thunderbolt, his deadly weapon;
like tree trunks hewn down by an axe, the serpent lies prostrate, pressed against the earth.
Like a mad warrior, he indeed challenged the great hero, the mighty repeller, the drinker of the *ṛjīṣa*;
he did not survive the onset of his weapons; Indra’s enemy was crushed, his joints shattered.
Footless and handless, he challenged Indra; Indra struck his thunderbolt upon his back.
Vṛtra, the eunuch who sought to be a match for the bull, lay scattered in many places.
Over him who lies there like a shattered reed, the waters flow surging upward;
even those which Vṛtra encompassed with his might, over them the serpent has become one whose head lies at their feet.
Her strength was humbled; Indra struck down the weapon against Vṛtra’s son.
The mother was above, the son was below; Dānu lies there like a cow with her calf.
Amidst the standing, unsheltering ridges, his body was laid low;
the waters flow over Vṛtra’s secret place, for he whose enemy is Indra has been cast into long darkness.
The waters stood confined, with the Dāsa as their lord and the serpent as their guardian, like cows held captive by the Paṇis.
Having slain Vṛtra, he threw open that which was the closed-up mouth of the waters.
O Indra, you became like a horse's tail when the god, alone, struck at you with his bolt;
you won the cattle, O hero, you won the Soma, and you released the seven rivers to flow.
Neither lightning nor thunder could restrain him, nor the mist and the hailstorm that he scattered;
when Indra and Ahi fought, the Bounteous Lord emerged victorious over them all.
Whom did you see as the pursuer of the serpent, O Indra, when fear entered your heart after you had struck him down?
And when you crossed the ninety-nine flowing rivers, like a hawk afraid, you traversed the regions of space.

Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, is the king of all that moves and rests, of the peaceful and of the horned. He alone rules as king over the peoples; he encompasses them all, as the felly surrounds the spokes.
Come hither, O seekers of cattle, to Indra; may he increase our excellent providence.
Being free from debt, will he not surely incline toward us the highest desire for this wealth of cattle?
I have approached the unassailable giver of wealth; like a hawk to its nest, I fly to him who is well-pleased.
Paying homage to Indra with these highest hymns—Indra who is to be invoked by those who praise him on his journey.
With his full army, he has hung down the quivers; the noble lord drives away the cattle of whomever he desires.
O Indra, bestowing abundant wealth, do not become a niggardly trafficker toward us, O you who have grown great!
For you, O Indra, moving alone with your companions, have slain the wealthy Dasyu with your weapon;
from the wealth [of the foe], they fled in all directions, and the ancient non-sacrificers went to their destruction.
Even those who did not sacrifice, O Indra, contending with the sacrificers, turned their heads away from you.
When you, O fierce Lord of the Bay Steeds, driver from heaven, blew the godless ones away from both worlds.
They sought to fight the army of the blameless one; the Navagva peoples exerted themselves.
Like castrated bulls with virile weapons, they fled in defeat; through their cries, they were made aware of Indra.
O Indra, you fought these weeping and laughing ones at the far limit of the mid-air;
you burned down the Dasyu from on high from heaven, and you protected the prayer of those who press the juice and offer praise.
Forming an enclosure around the earth, adorning themselves with gold and jewels, they did not overtake Indra as they sped along; he placed his spies all around him by means of the sun.
When you, O Indra, encompassed both heaven and earth on all sides with your greatness,
you blew away the Dasyu with your sacred prayers— those who were conscious against those who were unconscious.

They who have not reached the limit of heaven or earth, nor have they overcome the Giver of Wealth with their magic powers—Indra, the Bull, made the thunderbolt his ally; with light, he milked the cows out from the darkness.
The waters flowed according to their own nature; he grew great in the midst of the navigable rivers.
With a concentrated mind, Indra struck him down with his most powerful blow for all time.
Indra pierced through the strongholds of Ilībiśa and split asunder the horned Śuṣṇa.
O Maghavan, with as much speed and as much power as you possessed, you slew the attacking enemy with your thunderbolt.
The successful one has overcome his enemies; with his sharp bull-like weapon, he shattered the fortresses. Indra struck Vṛtra with his thunderbolt; triumphing, he furthered his own purpose.
O Indra, you protected Kutsa in whom you took delight; you helped the fighting bull Daśadyu.
The dust raised by his hooves reached the sky, and Śvaitreya stood firm for the conquest of men.
O Maghavan, you protected Śambara, the bull of the Tugryas, and the white cow during the contest for land;
though they stood there for a long time, you made them turn away and brought low the possessions of those who acted as enemies.
O Aśvins, be mindful of us even thrice today; far-reaching is your journey and your bounty.
For your guidance is like a garment in winter; may you be drawn toward us by the wise.
Three are the fellies on your honey-bearing chariot; all indeed know the longing for Soma. Three are the supports fixed for you to grasp; thrice by night and thrice by day you travel, O Aśvins.
On this same day, O you who conceal what is blameworthy, sprinkle the sacrifice thrice today with honey;
O Aśvins, swell for us thrice the food rich in booty at evening and at dawn.
Come three times to our dwelling, three times to the people who follow your law; bestow your aid three times upon the one who offers well, like a threefold gift.
O Aśvins, bring us joy thrice; let your nourishments swell for us three times, like inexhaustible waters.
O Aśvins, bring us wealth thrice; thrice in the assembly of the gods and thrice protect our prayers.
Thrice grant us prosperity and thrice grant us renown; thrice has the daughter of the Sun mounted your three-seated chariot.
O Aśvins, bestow upon us thrice the celestial medicines, thrice the earthly, and thrice those from the waters.
O Lords of Splendor, bring threefold protection and well-being for my son; grant him refuge in the three worlds.
O Aśvins, worthy of sacrifice, thrice every day you have traversed the threefold earth for us.
O Nāsatyas, chariot-borne ones, come from the far distance to our dwellings like the wind to its own resting places.

O Aśvins, thrice with the seven mother rivers, three are the mixing-vessels, and the oblation is prepared in three ways. You protect the three earths from above and the vault of heaven established by days and nights.

Where are the three wheels of your threefold chariot? Where are the three seats that share a common origin? When is the harnessing of the vigorous donkey by which you, O Nāsatyas, come to our sacrifice?
Come hither, O Nāsatyas; the oblation is being offered. Drink the honeyed draught with your honey-drinking mouths.
For Savitṛ sends forth your wondrous, butter-rich chariot at the first flush of dawn for the sake of the cosmic order.
O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, come here with the thirty-three gods to the drinking of the honeyed mead.
Prolong our lives, wipe away our sins, drive off our enemies, and be our companions.
O Aśvins, on your three-wheeled chariot, bring hither to us wealth consisting of heroic sons. Hearing me, I call upon you for protection; be present for our increase and for the winning of booty.
I invoke Agni first for well-being; I invoke Mitra and Varuṇa here for protection. I invoke Night, who brings rest to all that moves; I invoke the god Savitṛ for aid.
Advancing through the dark expanse, establishing both the immortal and the mortal,
the god Savitṛ comes upon his golden chariot, beholding all beings.
The god goes by the downward path, he goes by the upward path; the worshipful one goes with his two bright bay horses.
The god Savitṛ comes from afar, driving away all difficulties.
Enveloped in pearls, multiform, with golden pins, the worshipful and great Savitar,
of wondrous luster, has mounted his chariot, bestowing power upon the dark regions.
The dark ones with white feet, drawing the chariot with its golden pole, have looked out upon the people;
all the clans and all beings abide in the lap of the divine Savitṛ.
Three heavens there are for Savitṛ; two are his laps, and one is in the realm of Yama, where he dwells among heroes.
Like the linchpin of a chariot, they have stood upon the Immortal. Let him who understands this declare it here.
The well-winged one has surveyed the mid-air; the Asura of deep inspiration is a good leader.
Where now is the Sun? Who knows? Which heaven has his ray extended across?
He has illuminated the eight quarters of the earth, the three desert regions, and the seven rivers.
The golden-eyed god Savitṛ has arrived, bestowing desirable treasures upon the donor.
Savitar, the golden-handed, the all-beholding, moves between both heaven and earth;
he drives away disease, impels the sun, and reaches the sky through the dark expanse.
May the golden-handed Asura, the good leader, the very gracious and self-strong one, come hither;
driving away the Rākṣasas and Yātudhānas, the God has taken his stand at every twilight, being praised.
O Savitṛ, those ancient paths of yours, dustless and well-prepared in the mid-air—
by those easy-to-traverse paths, protect us today and speak for us, O God.
We entreat with hymns and words Agni, the vigorous one among you many tribes who seek the gods— the very one whom others likewise invoke.
People have established Agni as the increaser of strength; we, possessing oblations, shall worship you.
As such, be well-disposed toward us here today, our protector in battles, O truthful one.
We choose you as our messenger, the all-knowing Hotṛ-priest.
As you exist in greatness, your flames spread abroad; your rays touch the heavens.
The gods—Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman—kindle you, the ancient messenger.
O Agni, that mortal who offers oblations to you wins all wealth through you.
O Agni, you are the delightful Hotṛ, the lord of the household, and the messenger of the people.
In you all the firm laws (*vratā*) are gathered together, which the gods have established.
In thee alone, O Agni, most youthful and fortunate one, is every oblation offered.
As such, being well-disposed toward us today and in the future, sacrifice to the gods for us so that we may possess heroic strength.
To him indeed, the self-radiant one, the reverent ones sit down;
with oblations men kindle Agni, having overcome all failures.
Slaying Vṛtra, they crossed over heaven and earth and the waters; they have made wide room for their dwelling.
May the Bull, invoked with oblations, be present in glory for Kaṇva; may the horse neigh in the raids for cattle.
Sit down together; you are great. Shine forth, O best invoker of the gods!
O Agni, worthy of the sacrificial food, O praised one, emit your ruddy smoke, beautiful to behold.
O bearer of oblations, you whom the gods established here for Manu as the most excellent sacrificer;
you whom Kaṇva Medhyātithi, Vṛṣan, and Upastuta [invoked] as the winner of wealth.
That Agni whom Medhyātithi Kaṇva kindled from the Eternal Order—his flames have shone forth; we magnify that Agni with these very hymns.
Fill us with wealth, O self-dependent one; for you, O Agni, possess kinship among the gods.
You rule over glorious booty; as such, have mercy on us, for you are great.
Stand up erect for our protection like the god Savitṛ;
standing erect, you are the winner of booty when we, with ointments, call upon you together with the priests.
Standing upright, protect us from distress with your banner; burn up every *atri* (devourer).
Raise us up so that we may move and live; find for us favor among the gods.
Protect us, O Agni, from the *rakṣas*; protect us from the malice of the stingy;
protect us from him who seeks to harm us or would slay us, O youngest one of great luster!
Like a club, strike down in every direction the stingy ones, O you with the burning jaws, whoever seeks to harm us!
Whatever mortal whets his weapons against us through the nights—let not that enemy have power over us.
Agni has won great heroic power; Agni has won prosperity for Kaṇva.
Agni, as well as Mitra, protected Medhyātithi; Agni protected Upastuta in the winning of booty.
Through Agni we call Turvaśa and Yadu from afar, along with Ugrādeva;
Agni brought Navavāstva, Bṛhadratha, and Turvīti as a force for subduing the Dasyu.
Manu established you, O Agni, as a light for all people forever;
you shone forth, O Kaṇva, born of Truth and nourished by oblations, you whom the human races revere.
The brilliant, impetuous flames of Agni are like terrors; they are not to be withstood.
O you who possess the power to consume, burn forever every demon, every sorcerer, and every devouring fiend.
Sing forth, O Kaṇvas, to your sporting host of Maruts, the unassailable, who shine upon their chariots!
Those who were born with spotted deer, spears, axes, and ointments, possessing their own inherent luster.
As if right here one hears the whips as they crack in their hands; on their journey, they display wondrous power.
Sing forth the prayer bestowed by the gods for your impetuous host, of brilliant splendor and mighty strength.
Praise the bull among the cows, for the Marut host is sporting;
it has grown strong upon the juice in its throat.
Who among you, O heroes, shakers of heaven and earth, is the most exalted,
when you shake them as if shaking the hem of a garment?
At your approach, O fierce ones, no mortal can withstand your wrath;
even the mountain, the rocky peak, yields.
At whose marches the earth trembles in fear during their journeys, like an aged lord of the people.
For firm indeed is their birth, their vigor to emerge from the mother, so that their strength is doubled thereafter.
These sons have raised their voices; they have extended the race-courses in their charges, lowing as they go knee-deep.
Even that long and broad son of the mist, the unassailable one,
they cause to move forth on their journeys.
O Maruts, when your strength has caused the people to tremble, you have caused even the mountains to tremble.
When the Maruts go forth, they speak together on the way;
does anyone hear them?
Come forth swiftly with your swift steeds; there are honors for you among the Kaṇvas.
Rejoice there indeed!
For there is indeed enough for your exhilaration; we truly belong to them.
May they grant us the full span of life that we may live.
When indeed, O you for whom the sacred grass is trimmed, do you now hold [us] in your hands like a father who loves his son?
Where now, and for what purpose, will you go from heaven or from earth? Where do you rejoice, like cattle?
Where, O Maruts, are your newest favors? Where are your blessings? And where are all your auspicious gifts?
O you whose mother is Pṛśni, if you were mortals,
your worshipper would be immortal.
May your singer not be one who is unpleasing to you, like a wild beast in a pasture;
may he not go upon the path of Yama.
Let not Destruction, the ill-fated one, strike us down further and further;
let her perish along with Thirst.
Truly, these fierce and impetuous sons of Rudra,
even upon the desert, create rain that is free from wind.
Like a lowing cow, the lightning bellows; it follows [the rain] as a mother follows her calf, when their rain has been released.
Even by day they create darkness with Parjanya, the water-bearer,
when they drench the earth.
Then, at the roar of the Maruts, every earthly dwelling trembled;
all human beings shook.
O Maruts, with your firm-hoofed steeds, travel along the variegated riverbanks with unwearied courses.
May your fellies be firm, may their chariots and horses be so; may the reins be well-fashioned.
Address yourself with this continuous song to praise Brahmaṇaspati;
[praise] Agni, who is as beautiful to behold as Mitra.
Fashion the hymn within your mouth; spread it abroad like Parjanya. Sing the song worthy of praise.
Worship the Marut host— the brilliant, praiseworthy, and hymn-singing one—
so that they may grow strong for us here.
When you thus cast forth your measure like a flame from afar—
by whose wisdom, O Maruts, by whose form, to whom do you go, and whom, O shakers?
May your weapons be firm for driving away the foe, and strong for resisting the enemy;
may your power be most praiseworthy, and not that of the deceitful mortal.
When you strike down what is firm, O heroes, and roll away what is heavy, you pass through the trees of the earth and through the regions of the mountains.
For no enemy of yours has been found in heaven nor upon the earth, O you who destroy the foe. O Rudras, may your power remain with your own bodies as an ally; never indeed is it to be assailed.
They cause the mountains to tremble; they shake the lords of the forest.
O Maruts, you have come forth like those intoxicated with wine—O gods, together with your entire host.
You have harnessed the spotted deer to your chariots; the ruddy steed draws as the leader at the side.
Even the earth itself has listened to your coming, and mortal men were struck with fear.
O Rudras, we quickly choose your protection for the sake of our offspring; come now to us with your aid as you did of old, even for the trembling Kaṇva.
O Maruts, whatever terrifying thing, sent by you or sent by mortals,
assails us— drive it away with your might, drive it away with your strength, and drive it away with your protections.
For you, O wise Maruts, who are worthy of sacrifice, have bestowed the Kaṇva in full abundance; come to us with your complete aids, as lightning brings rain.
O bounteous ones, you possess complete vigor; O shakers, you possess complete might.
O Maruts, full of wrath against the hater of the seer, do not discharge your hatred like an arrow.
Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati! We, seeking the gods, entreat you.
May the Maruts, the bounteous givers, come forward; O Indra, be swift in our company.
For it is you alone, O Son of Strength, that the mortal calls upon when the prize is set;
may he who longs for you, O Maruts, obtain great heroic power and noble horses.
May Brahmanaspati come forward; may the goddess Sūnṛtā come forward.
May the gods lead our sacrifice toward the heroic man, the benefactor of the fivefold assembly.
He who gives excellent wealth to the singer wins imperishable fame;
for him we offer the oblation that brings heroic sons, providing great victory and freedom from harm.
Now indeed Brahmaṇaspati utters the hymn worthy of praise,
in which Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, and the gods have made their dwellings.
Let us recite this hymn at the assemblies, O Gods—a hymn that brings prosperity and is free from blemish.
And may you welcome these words, O Heroes; may it attain all that is auspicious from you.
Who has reached the man who seeks the gods, who has trimmed the sacred grass? The donor has stepped forth with his dwellings; he has established a home within the waters.

May he augment his sovereign power; with kings he slays [the foe] and even in the midst of danger he establishes a secure dwelling. For the wielder of the thunderbolt, there is no one to obstruct him or overcome him, whether in a great battle or a small one.
The person whom the far-seeing Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman protect—
never indeed is that man harmed.
The mortal whom they carry across as if with their arms and protect from harm,
remains unharmed and prospers in every way.
The kings of these [Maruts] strike down the difficult passes and the enemies before them; they lead them across all misfortunes.
Easy to traverse is the path, thornless for the one who walks the *ṛta*, O Ādityas;
there is no devouring here for you.
O heroes, O Ādityas, whatever sacrifice you lead by the straight path—
may that reach your thought.
That mortal, unassailed, goes forth to every treasure and wealth, as well as to his offspring, by his own self.
How, O friends, may we accomplish the hymn of praise for Mitra and Aryaman—
the great refreshment of Varuṇa?
I do not speak back to you who strike nor to him who curses, for he seeks the gods;
with hymns of praise alone I strive to win your favor.
One should fear even one who bestows fourfold wealth until he has laid it down;
one should not long for ill-spoken words.
O Pūṣan, traverse the paths; O Son of Deliverance, drive away distress. Come, O God, and go before us.
O Pūṣan, whatever malevolent wolf or ill-disposed enemy threatens us,
drive him away from our path.
Drive far away from the path that robber who lies in wait, the thief who plots with deceit.
O Aja, drive him far from the track.
Trample with your foot the burning heat of that two-faced, evil-speaking person, whoever he may be.
O wondrous Pūṣan, rich in wisdom, we choose that aid of yours by which you urged on our ancestors.
Then, O Lord of all prosperity, most excellent wielder of the golden axe, make our riches easy to win.
Lead us beyond those who obstruct us; make our paths easy to traverse and fair to walk upon.
O Pūṣan, find wisdom for us here.
Lead us toward good pasture; let there be no new fever upon our path.
O Pūṣan, find wisdom for us here.
Be able; fill us; bestow gifts; sharpen our wits; open wide your belly.
O Pūṣan, find the power of will for us here.
We do not revile Pūṣan; we praise him with hymns.
We beg the wondrous one for riches.
What may we utter to Rudra, the wise, the most bountiful, the most powerful,
that is most pleasing to his heart?
So that Aditi may grant us the Rudra-power for our cattle, for our men, for our kine, and for our offspring.
So that Mitra and Varuṇa, so that Rudra, and so that all the gods may be mindful of us with one accord.
To Rudra, the lord of songs, the lord of sacrifices, the one whose medicine is healing—
him we seek for auspicious favor and well-being.
He who shines like the bright sun, like gold,
the most excellent Vasu among the gods.
May he grant well-being to our horse, a good path for the ram and the ewe,
and for the men, the women, and the cattle.
O Soma, bestow upon us the glory of a hundred men—
great renown and abundant manly strength.
Let not those who obstruct the Soma, nor the enemies, deceive us;
O Indu, grant us a share in the prize.

Those offspring of yours who are in the highest abode of immortality, in the realm of *ṛta*—O Soma, as the head and the navel, you, the lover, know them as they adorn themselves; O Soma, you are their wealth.
O immortal Agni, bring hither from the dawn the wondrous gift, O Jātavedas; today bring the gods who awaken at dawn to the one who offers oblations.
For you are the beloved messenger, the bearer of oblations, O Agni, the charioteer of the sacrifices.
In harmony with the Aśvins and Uṣas, bestow upon us heroic strength and lofty renown.
Today we choose as our messenger Agni, the Vasu, the beloved of many—
the one whose banner is smoke, who is radiant with light, the glory of the sacrifice at the break of dawn.
I praise Agni Jātavedas at the break of dawn— the most excellent, the youngest guest, well-invoked, beloved by the person who offers oblations— so that he may go toward the gods.
I shall praise you, O immortal sustainer of all; O Agni, worthy of the sacrificial food, most excellent sacrificer and bearer of oblations, I praise you as the immortal protector.
O youngest one, be a bringer of good praise to the singer; you whose tongue is honeyed and who are well-invoked with *svāhā*.
Prolonging the life of Praskaṇva so that he may live, pay homage to the divine host.
For the people kindle you, the all-knowing Hotṛ;
therefore, O Agni, much-invoked and wise one, bring the gods here swiftly.
At the dawning of the night, the Kaṇvas, having pressed the Soma, kindle Savitṛ, Uṣas, the Aśvins, Bhaga, and Agni— the bearer of oblations, O performer of fair rites.
For you, O Agni, are the lord of sacrifices and the messenger of the people;
bring hither today the gods who awaken at dawn and behold the light of heaven, for the drinking of the Soma.
O Agni, rich in radiance, you have shone throughout the former dawns, visible to all.
You are the protector in the settlements, the domestic priest; you are the friend of men at the sacrifices.
O Agni, we establish you as the accomplisher of the sacrifice, the Hotṛ priest, the officiating Ṛtvij— like Manu, O God, the wise, the swift, the immortal messenger.
When you, O god of Mitra-like splendor, go as the domestic priest and the intimate messenger between the gods,
the flames of Agni flash forth like the roaring waves of a river.

Hear us, O Agni, you whose ear is keen, together with the gods who are the bearers [of the sacrifice] and your fellow-travelers. Let Mitra and Aryaman, those who go forth at dawn, sit upon the sacrificial grass at this rite.

May the Maruts, the bounteous givers, whose tongue is Agni and who increase the cosmic order, hear our hymn of praise. May Varuṇa, the upholder of sacred law, drink the Soma together with the Aśvins and Uṣas.
O Agni, sacrifice here to the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas—
to the people born of Manu, who perform the rite well and sprinkle the clarified butter.
For the wise gods are ready to listen to the donor, O Agni;
O lover of songs, bring here those thirty-three who have ruddy horses.
O Jātavedas, like Priyamedha, Atri, and Virūpa,
and like Aṅgiras, you of mighty vows, hear the invocation of Praskaṇva.
The Mahikerus and the Priyamedhas have invoked for their protection Agni,
who rules over the sacrifices with his bright radiance.
O you who are invoked with clarified butter, O Holy One, truly hear these songs by which the sons of Kaṇva call upon you for protection.
O Agni, most rich in wondrous fame, the people among the clans invoke you,
whose hair is flame, you who are beloved by many, to carry their oblations.
The inspired singers have established you, O Agni, as the Hotṛ priest and officiant at the sacrifices, the best finder of wealth, with ears that hear, most far-reaching in the rites for the gods.
The inspired singers, having pressed the soma, have drawn you toward the offering;
O Agni, bearing great light, come for the sake of the mortal who presents the oblation.
O bounteous one, son of strength, worthy of praise, seat the divine folk here today upon the sacrificial grass for the morning journey, that they may drink the Soma.
O Agni, with joint invocations, worship the divine host so that they turn hitherward;
O bounteous ones, drink this Soma which has been pressed for the past day.
This unprecedented Dawn, the beloved of heaven, shines forth.
O Aśvins, I praise you both with a lofty hymn.
O wonder-workers, sons of Sindhu, discoverers of riches,
O gods who find wealth through inspired thought!
Your lofty steeds are urged forward upon the ancient expanse,
when your chariot flies with winged horses.
The lover of the waters, the fulfiller, fills [us] with oblation, O heroes;
he is the father of the dwelling, the one who observes mankind.
O Nāsatyas, you who have words inspired by thought, you are the receptacle for our prayers;
drink of the Soma with boldness.
O Aśvins, grant us that nourishment which may carry us across the darkness, full of light. Grant us that sustenance.
Come to us in the vessel of our prayers, that we may reach the further shore; O Aśvins, yoke your chariot.
Your oar is broad as the sky; your chariot is at the crossing-place of the rivers. The drops have been yoked by prayer.
O Kaṇvas, the drops [of Soma] are from heaven; [they are] at the place of the rivers' treasure. Where will you two place your own covering?
Light has indeed appeared for the sake of the Soma-stalk; the sun shines back like gold.
With his dark tongue, he has looked out across [the world].
A path for crossing to the further shore has indeed appeared for the sake of the *ṛta*; the stream from heaven has been seen.
This very aid of the Aśvins, who protect us while we are exhilarated by Soma, the singer honors again and again.
Dwelling with Vivasvat through the drinking of Soma and by means of our song, O bringers of well-being,
come hither like unto Manu.
Dawn has followed after the splendor of you two who travel around;
you win the cosmic order through the nights.
Drink both of you, O Aśvins; grant us protection both of you, with your unfailing aids.
O you two who increase the cosmic order (*ṛta*), this most honey-sweet Soma has been pressed for you;
O Aśvins, drink it, which was prepared yesterday, and bestow treasures upon the donor.
Come hither, O Aśvins, on your well-adorned chariot with its triple seat and triple framework;
the Kaṇvas offer prayers for you at the sacrifice—listen well to their call.
O Aśvins, increasers of cosmic order, drink the most honey-sweet Soma.
And now today, O wonder-workers, bearing wealth upon your chariot, come to the donor.
O possessors of all wealth, sprinkle the sacrifice with honey upon the three-seated sacred grass;
the Kaṇvas, having pressed the Soma and looking toward heaven, invoke you both, O Aśvins.
O Aśvins, lords of splendor, with those same aids by which you protected Kaṇva, protect us as well; drink the Soma, O you who increase the cosmic order.
O wonder-workers, O Aśvins, bearing wealth upon your chariot, bring nourishment to Sudās;
bestow upon us riches from the ocean or from heaven—riches that are desired by many.
Whether you are in the distance, O Nāsatyas, or whether you abide among the Turvaśas,
come hither from there on your well-rolling chariot together with the rays of the sun.
May your coursers, who grace the sacrifice, bring you both hither to the libations;
bestowing nourishment upon the doer of good deeds, O bounteous givers, sit upon the sacred grass, O heroes.
With that chariot of sun-like skin, O Nāsatyas,
come hither— by which you have constantly brought wealth to the donor for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
With hymns and songs of praise, we call hither for protection the two lords of abundant wealth;
for in the beloved assembly of the Kaṇvas, O Aśvins, you have repeatedly drunk the Soma.
O Uṣas, daughter of Heaven, shine forth for us together with the desirable;
O radiant goddess, bestowing wealth, shine forth with great splendor.
Rich in horses, rich in cattle, bestowing all wealth, they hasten forth in abundance to shine. O Uṣas, send forth the true blessings toward me; impel the bounty of the liberal patrons.
The goddess Dawn has shone forth and shall shine again; she is the awakener of chariots—those who, like those seeking glory upon the ocean, have set their hearts upon her arrivals.
O Uṣas, those wise patrons who yoke their minds for the sake of giving during your advances—
among them, Kaṇva, the best of the Kaṇvas, here celebrates the name of these men.
Like a noble woman, Dawn approaches, bestowing gifts;
making all that has feet grow old, she moves forth and causes the birds to fly up.
She who sends forth the assembly and the seekers of wealth, she goes about like one seeking her own station;
at your dawning, O lady rich in booty, no birds that have flown forth remain still.
She has yoked [her horses] from afar, from the rising of the sun; with a hundred chariots, this auspicious Dawn approaches human beings as she spreads out.

The whole world has bowed down before her glance; the noble daughter of heaven makes light for the living. May the wealthy Dawn, the daughter of heaven, shine away our hatreds and drive away our enemies.
O Uṣas, daughter of heaven, shine upon us with your radiant and beautiful light,
bringing us abundant fortune as you dawn during our sacrifices.
For you alone are the breath and the life of all, O noble lady, when you shine forth.
As such, O radiant one, hear our call with your lofty chariot, O goddess of wondrous wealth.
O Uṣas, win for us the prize that is wondrous among the human folk;
with that, bring the well-performed sacrifices hither to those who, as priests, praise you.
Bring all the gods from the mid-air, O Dawn, for the drinking of the Soma!
Bestow upon us wealth in cattle, wealth in horses, praiseworthy strength, and heroic vigor, O Dawn.
She whose radiant, auspicious rays have appeared—
may that Dawn grant us wealth containing all boons, well-fashioned and easy to attain.
For even those seers of old who invoked you for aid and for great protection— that [aid] of yours, O Dawn,
accept our hymns with your radiant luster, together with wealth.
O Uṣas, when today with your radiance you open wide the two doors of heaven,
grant us a broad, secure shelter free from danger, O Goddess, and grant us nourishments rich in cattle.
