O Dawn, bestow upon us great wealth adorned with every beauty; endow us with refreshing offerings, with all-conquering splendor, O mighty one, and with riches, O thou who art rich in booty!
O Uṣas, come with auspicious things even from the luminous realm of heaven;
let those whose steeds are ruddy bring you to the house of the Soma-presser.
O Uṣas, with that well-adorned and easy-to-ride chariot upon which you have mounted, protect today,
O Daughter of Heaven, the people who possess great renown.
O radiant Uṣas, even the winged birds, the bipeds, and the quadrupeds have awakened according to their seasons from the very ends of heaven.
For as you shine forth with your rays, you illuminate the entire radiant realm;
as such, O Uṣas, the Kaṇvas, desiring wealth, have invoked you with their songs.
Upward those rays of light bear him, the god Jātavedas,
the Sun, so that everyone may behold him.
Like thieves, those stars depart with the nights for the Sun who beholds all things.
His banners have become visible; his rays extend across the people, shining like blazing fires.
O Sūrya, you are the one who carries us across, visible to all, the maker of light; you illuminate the entire radiant realm.
Facing the clans of the gods, facing men, you rise up;
facing all the light of heaven, so that we may see.
O Purifier, with that eye wherewith you, O Varuṇa, behold the people as they stir about, [look upon us].
O Sūrya, you traverse the sky and the broad expanse, measuring out the days with your rays, beholding all living beings.
O divine Sūrya, seven bay horses carry you in your chariot— you who have flaming hair, O far-seeing one.
The Sun has yoked the seven bright mares, the daughters of his chariot;
with them, as his own team, he goes forth.
Beholding the higher light beyond the darkness,
we have come to Sūrya, the god among gods, the supreme light.
Rising today, O Sūrya, you who possess the greatness of Mitra, ascending to the highest heaven, destroy my heart-disease and my jaundice.
We place my yellowness in the parrots, in the starlings;
and so we deposit my yellowness in the yellow-woodpeckers.
This Āditya has risen with all his power, subjecting my enemy to me; may I not be subject to my enemy.
Exhilarate with songs that Indra, the ram, the much-invoked, the worthy of hymns, the ocean of wealth;
him whose [powers] move like the heavens among men, the most generous, praise the inspired singer for our enjoyment.
His aids have favored him, the one who possesses excellent assistance, who fills the mid-air and is encompassed by powers;
the skillful Rbhus have mounted Indra, the distiller of exhilaration, the lord of a hundred powers, with swift and pleasant speech.
You opened up the cow-stall for the Aṅgirases; as their protector, you found the way for Atri among the hundred doors.
You brought wealth even with his army to Vimada; in the battle, you made the pressing-stone dance for the one who clothed himself in the prize.
You opened the coverings of the waters; you held fast the watery wealth within the mountain.
When you, O Indra, slew the serpent Vṛtra with your might, you then caused the sun to ascend in heaven so that it might be seen.
By your wondrous powers you cast down the sorcerers who, by their own self-willed acts, offered oblations upon the funeral pyre.
O hero-minded one, you shattered the fortresses of Pipru and protected R̥jiśvan in the slaying of the Dasyus.
You protected Kutsa in the slayings of Śuṣṇa; you delivered Śambara over to Atithigva.
You trampled even the great Arbuda with your foot; from of old, you were born for the slaying of the Dasyus.
In you all powers are gathered together; your bounty rejoices for the drinking of Soma.
Your thunderbolt, placed within your arms, is manifest; shatter all the manly strengths of the enemy.
Distinguish between the noble ones and those who are Dasyus; subjecting the lawless, bring them under the control of the one who offers the sacrificial grass.
Be powerful, an instigator for the sacrificer; I delight in all these deeds of yours at our common feasts.
Surrendering those of evil conduct to him who follows the right path, Indra, with his helpers, struck down the powerless;
though he was already grown, as he grew further seeking to reach the heavens, the praised Vamra shattered the obstructing masses.
When Uśanas fashioned for you power with might, your strength forced apart heaven and earth by its greatness.
O you whose mind is heroic, the mind-yoked steeds of the wind carried you toward glory as you were being filled [with power].
When Indra rejoiced with Uśanas Kāvya, he mounted his two swift steeds, the swifter of the two.
The fierce one set the flowing waters loose in their current; he shattered the strongholds and cast down the fortresses of Śuṣṇa.
O you who have strong hands, you mount his chariot; among those offerings of Śāryāta, you take your delight.
O Indra, as you have always found pleasure in the pressed Soma, you ascend to the unassailable fame in heaven.
O Indra, you gave the maiden Vṛcayā to the great and eloquent Kakṣīvat, who was pressing the soma;
O wise one, you became the wife of Vṛṣaṇaśva. All these deeds of yours are to be proclaimed at the Soma-pressings.
Indra has been established in the exclusive presence of the pious; among the Pajras, his praise is like a sacrificial post fixed in the doorways.
Seeking horses, seeking cattle, seeking chariots, and seeking wealth—Indra alone rules over riches as their bestower.
This homage has been spoken to the bull, the self-ruling one, whose strength is truth and who is powerful:
O Indra, in this assembly, may we, with all our heroes and together with the patrons, abide under your protection.
That ram, the finder of light, whom I greatly magnify—he from whom a hundred well-formed steeds issue forth together;
like a prize-winning steed, like a chariot that hastens to the call, may I turn Indra hither for protection with my well-fashioned hymns.
Like a mountain unshakable upon its foundations, he of a thousand aids has grown strong in his powers;
when Indra, exulting in the soma-juice, struck down Vṛtra who encompassed the rivers, he cast down the floods.
For he is the opener among openers, the filler of the udder, with a base like the moon, increased by exhilaration through the wise.
I have invoked that Indra with a prayer of skillful workmanship, for he is the most liberal giver; he is the one who fulfills the draught of soma.
Him whom those seated on the sacred grass in heaven fill, like the ocean with their own well-being and desires;
him Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, his aids followed in battle—his impetuous powers, unassailable and of unbending form.
In the exhilaration of this [soma], as he fought for his own rain, his aids sped forth like swift mares down a slope;
when Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, boldly aided by the plant, shattered the enclosures of Vala as Trita did.
He moves about with heat; his power has blazed forth. Having encompassed the waters, he lay upon the foundation of the firmament.
When, O Indra, you struck Vṛtra—who was difficult to seize on the slope—with the thunderbolt between his jaws, [you sent him] down the steep descent.
For the waves do not overwhelm you, O Indra, like those entering a lake—those prayers of yours which are your means of strengthening.
Tvaṣṭṛ himself increased your fitting might; he fashioned the thunderbolt of overwhelming power.
Having slain Vṛtra with your bay steeds, O Indra of gathered power, you made a path for the waters for the sake of man.
You hurled the iron thunderbolt from your arms; you established the sun in heaven so that it might be seen.
When they, out of fear, made for themselves that great, self-luminous, and powerful ascent to heaven worthy of praise;
when the Maruts, who conquer men and seek the light, rejoiced in Indra as their aid during the human battles.
Even the heaven itself trembled in fear at the roar of your serpent-slaying bolt, O Indra;
when, in the exhilaration of the pressed juice, you by your might split asunder the head of Vṛtra as he was pressing against both heaven and earth.
When indeed, O Indra, the earth was tenfold and all the peoples spread through the days, even then,
O Maghavan, your renowned power became equal to heaven in its might and its fury.
On the far side of this space, of the firmament, you—possessing innate power and bold spirit—have acted for our protection;
you have made the earth a measure of your might, encompassing the waters, the sun, and reaching unto heaven.
You have become the counterpart of the earth; you have become the lord of the lofty, vast [heaven] with its exalted heroes.
You have filled the entire mid-air with your greatness. Truly, indeed, there is none other like you.
Neither heaven and earth, nor the rivers have reached the limit of his expanse in the mid-world;
nor even his own rain when he fights in his exhilaration. Alone, you have brought all else into being in due succession.
The Maruts sang their hymns here in this very battle; all the gods rejoiced after you, O Indra, when with your sharp-edged weapon you struck down Vṛtra’s breath.
We bring forth this speech as an offering to the Great One; we offer songs to Indra at the dwelling-place of Vivasvat.
For never indeed have they found wealth like those who sleep; a poor hymn is not praised among the givers of riches.
Thou art the opener of the stall for horses, O Indra, the opener of the stall for cattle, the opener of the stall for barley; thou art the powerful lord of wealth.
A helper of men from of old, never failing those who desire nothing else, a friend to his friends—him indeed do we praise here.
O powerful Indra, doer of many deeds, most resplendent one, this wealth all around you is renowned as yours alone.
Therefore, grasping it from there, O conqueror, bring it hither; do not frustrate the desire of the singer who seeks you.
With these days, with these drops, being well-disposed, driving away want with cattle and horses;
with Indra and his drops, may we shatter the Dasyu and, free from hatred, obtain nourishment.
O Indra, may we grasp wealth; may we grasp nourishment; may we grasp prizes that are many-glittering and resplendent.
May we grasp divine providence, which is full of heroic vigor, preceded by cattle, and rich in horses.
Those exhilarations gladdened you, those manly powers, O Lord of the Good, those Soma-draughts in the slayings of Vṛtra—
when for the singer who spread the sacrificial grass, you, irresistible, struck down ten thousand Vṛtras.
Battle after battle you indeed go forth with boldness; you utterly destroy fortress after fortress with your might.
When, O Indra, through your friendship, you struck down the guileful one named Namuci in the distance with your bending weapon.
You slew Karañja and Parṇaya with the most piercing path of Atithigva;
you shattered the hundred forts of Vaṅgr̥da, which were besieged by R̥jiśvan, O irresistible one.

O you who are renowned, with your chariot wheel you struck down sixty thousand and ninety-nine of those men belonging to Janarāja, who had approached with their kinsman Suśravas— the twice-ten— making them difficult to tread upon.
You protected Suśravas with your aids, and with your protections, O Indra, you helped Tūrvayāṇa.
You made Kutsa, Atithigva, and Āyu subject to this great, youthful king.
O Indra, may we be your most auspicious friends at the end of the day, protected by the gods;
through you, possessing excellent heroes, we shall praise you, extending our lifespan even further.
O Maghavan, do not abandon us in this distress amidst these battles; for there is no limit to the full extent of your power.
You made the rivers roar and the forests cry out; how indeed did the two worlds shrink together in fear?
Worship Śakra, the powerful one, the possessor of might; magnifying him, praise Indra who hears you—he, the bull, by his bold strength and virility, subdues both heaven and earth.
Sing forth a powerful hymn to the lofty Heaven, whose bold spirit possesses self-sovereignty;
he is the Asura of great renown, made mighty by his own strength—for he is the bull, the chariot, drawn by two bay steeds.
You made the ridge of the vast heaven tremble; with your own bold self, you shattered Śambara.
When, O bold one, with your exhilarating [Soma], you attacked the deceptive and arrogant [demon] with the sharp-edged thunderbolt from your hand.
When you strike down upon the head of the snorting one— the woods resounding with the cry of the wounded Śuṣṇa—
with a forward-striving and powerful mind, even today, who shall stand against you as you act?
You protected Narya Turvaśa and Yadu; you, O Śatakratu, protected Turvīti and Vayya.
You protected the chariot and Etaśa in the decisive contest for wealth; you destroyed ninety-nine fortresses.
He indeed, the King, the true lord of men, has grown mighty—he who, having been offered oblations, fulfills the command;
or he who welcomes our hymns with bounty. As a liberal giver, he causes the lower regions of heaven to swell for us.

Incomparable is their dominion, incomparable their wisdom; let these Soma-drinkers excel through their skillful deeds—those who, O Indra, increase your great dominion, your steadfast power, and your virility as they bestow gifts upon you.

For you alone are these abundant juices, pressed by stones, resting in the bowls, the draughts for Indra’s drinking. Pervade them, satisfy your desire for them, and then direct your mind toward the bestowing of wealth.
The mountain stood within the belly of Vṛtra, in the darkness that obstructs the support of the waters.
Indra strikes down all those rivers held back by the obstructor as they flow toward their downward slopes.
May he bestow upon us glorious splendor that increases our welfare; O Indra, conqueror of men, grant us great and powerful dominion.
Protect our patrons, guard our wise leaders, and establish us in wealth, in good offspring, and in nourishment.
Even the breadth of heaven has spread itself out before him; even the earth does not equal Indra in greatness.
Terrible and mighty, a scorcher for the sake of the people, he whets his thunderbolt for brilliance like a bull.
Like the ocean receiving the rivers that flow toward it with its vast expanses, Indra, the bull, longs for the drinking of Soma; from of old, he the warrior is praised for his might.
O Indra, you rule over that mountain-like [host] for the enjoyment of the great; you ordain the laws of manly power.
He is distinguished among the gods by his heroic might; the fierce one is placed at the forefront for every deed.
He indeed is celebrated among the people with reverent words in the forest, proclaiming his noble power among men;
he becomes a desirable bull, a lovely bull, when the bounteous Maghavan stirs the cow with security.
He, the warrior, by his might and through his power, brings about great battles for the sake of men;
yet even then, they do not have faith in the radiant Indra as he repeatedly hurls the thunderbolt, his weapon of destruction.
For he, seeking glory, increasing upon the earth with his might, destroys the man-made dwellings;
creating safe lights for the sacrificer, the one of excellent wisdom has released the waters to flow.
O drinker of Soma, let your mind be inclined toward giving; turn hither your two bay steeds, O you who hear our praise.
Those charioteers of yours who are most skilled in seeking you out, O Indra—your fervent intentions do not deceive you.
You carry in your hands wealth that is unasked for; you, the renowned one, have placed invincible might within your body.
Like wells surrounded by those who dig them, O Indra, many powers reside within your person.

He has lifted up these many ladles for him, as a steed springs toward a maiden; he, the active one, makes himself drink skill for the sake of greatness, having turned his golden chariot yoked with bay horses, the work of the *Ṛbhus*.
To him the songs of praise and abundant offerings have gone forth, like those seeking gain hastening to the ocean at its crossing;
they have ascended with splendor upon the lord of skill and the assembly, as lovers ascend a mountain with their longing.
Victorious and great in manly power, he shines with impetuous strength like a peak of the mountain;
by him, in the exhilaration of the Soma, the iron-strong one brought down the guileful Śuṣṇa into the bonds and fetters of the irresistible ones.
If the divine power, increased by thee, follows after Indra for aid as the sun follows the dawn—
he who with bold strength drives away the darkness, he, roaring aloud, stirs up the dust high above.
When, by your might, you established the firm and unshakable realm across the expanse of heaven;
when, O Indra, in the exhilaration of the soma-pressing, you joyfully struck down Vṛtra and released the flood of waters.
By your might, O Indra, you established the support of heaven and the greatness of earth in their places;
in the exhilaration of the pressed soma, you released the waters and shattered the bony jaw-joints of Vṛtra along his entire length.
I bring a hymn to the most generous, the lofty one of vast wealth, whose strength is true and who is powerful—
to him whose bounty, like water on a slope, is irresistible and whose all-sustaining power is unobstructed.
Then let all follow after your sacrifice with longing, as waters flow downward to the libations of the one who offers oblations;
when, like a mountain, the beloved golden thunderbolt of Indra has settled, it shall strike down the foe.
To this formidable one, bring worship with reverence at the sacrifice, like the radiant Dawn, for he is most worthy of praise;
he whose majestic power and name, his Indra-like light, have been made manifest for glory, so that he may be led hither like a bay horse.
O Indra, much-praised one, we here are yours—those who move about having taken hold of you, O Lord of abundant wealth.
For none other than you, O lover of songs, can sustain our hymns; accept this speech of ours as you would the people.
Abundant is your heroic power, O Indra; we belong to you. O Maghavan, fulfill the desire of this singer.
The vast heaven yields to your heroism, and this earth, too, bows before your might.
O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, you shattered that great and wide mountain into pieces with your bolt;
you released the obstructed waters so they might flow, and you have truly possessed all conquering power as your own alone.
Never indeed does the immortal one, born of strength, cease his piercing when he has become the Hotṛ-priest and messenger of Vivasvat;
with the most effective paths he traverses the mid-air, and at the assembly of the gods, he seeks to win [the gods] with the oblation.
Assuming his own food, undecaying, and eager to consume, he stands among the dry woods;
like a horse, his back shines with the sprinkling of moisture; thundering like the ridge of heaven, he has bellowed.
Active with the Rudras and the Vasus, the immortal Hotṛ-priest seated in front, the winner of wealth,
like a chariot moving swiftly among the people, the god bestows desirable boons one after another upon the living beings.
Impelled by the wind, he spreads through the dry brush; with his tongues as sickles, he roars loudly.
When you, O Agni, like a bull, thirstily advance toward the trees, O ageless one with radiant waves, this path of yours becomes black.
With burning jaws, driven by the wind through the forest, the bull-like steed blows down like a conqueror among the herds.
Advancing with his power through the inexhaustible space, he strikes terror into all that is stationary, all that moves, and even the winged birds.
The Bhr̥gus established you among men, like desirable wealth, easy to invoke for the people—
the Hotr̥, O Agni, the excellent guest, as dear as a friend to the divine race.

The Hotṛ-priest, the most skilled in sacrifice, whom the seven sacrificial ladles and the officiating priests choose at the rites— Agni, the steward of all treasures— I honor with an offering and seek his gift.
O Son of Strength, O Agni of friend-like majesty, grant today unbroken protection to us who praise you; O Son of Power, deliver the singer from distress with your iron fortresses.
O radiant one, be a shelter for the singer; O bounteous Maghavan, be a protection for the generous patrons.
O Agni, deliver the singer from distress. May he who is enriched by prayer come quickly in the morning.
O Agni, these other fires of yours are indeed branches; in you all the immortals rejoice.
O Vaiśvānara, you are the navel of the settlements; like a pillar, you support the people.
Agni is the head of heaven, the navel of the earth; he has become the messenger of both worlds.
You, the god Vaiśvānara, the gods brought forth as light for the Ārya.
As the rays are fixed in the sun, so have treasures been placed in Agni Vaiśvānara:
those which are in the mountains, in the plants, in the waters, and those which are among men—you are their king.

Like the two worlds, vast as they are, singing for their son, so do these many youthful songs— like a skillful human Hotar-priest— proceed toward Vaiśvānara, the most heroic one, who possesses true vigor and dwells in the light of heaven.
Even from the great heaven, O Jātavedas Vaiśvānara, thy majesty has surpassed all;
thou art the king of the human tribes, and through battle thou hast created wide space for the gods.
Now I shall proclaim the greatness of the Bull, whom the Pūrus follow as the slayer of Vṛtra.
Having struck down the Dasyu, Agni Vaiśvānara shook the barriers and shattered Śambara.
Vaiśvānara, who belongs to all peoples by his greatness, the worshipful and radiant one among the Bharadvājas—
Agni, rich in true blessings, is praised with hundreds of songs by Śātavaneya at the many festivals.
Mātariśvan brought to Bhr̥gu the bearer of oblations, the glorious banner of the assembly, the excellent messenger who swiftly achieves his purpose— the twice-born one, praised like wealth, a gift.
Both his instructors attend upon him—the *uśij* who offer oblations and the mortals alike.
Even before [the dawns of] heaven, the invoker has sat down, the question-worthy lord of the people, the ordainer among the clans.
May our newest hymn of praise reach him as he is born from the heart— him whose tongue is honeyed—
whom the human priests, the Āyus, providing sacrificial food, have brought forth in the assembly.
Desiring [oblations], purifying, and a Vasu among men, the excellent Hotṛ has been established among the clans;
as the domestic friend and master of the house within the home, Agni has become the lord of riches among all treasures.
We, the Gotamas, praise you with our hymns, O Agni, as the lord of riches;
grooming you like a swift steed that brings the prize, may he who is enriched by our prayer come quickly at dawn.

To him, the very powerful and swift one, I offer this hymn of praise like a refreshing draught—to the majestic Indra, who is worthy of the song, to the irresistible one; I present these most excellent prayers.

To him indeed I offer this praise like a gift; I bring forth a hymn of laudation with skillful turning. For Indra, the ancient lord, they cleanse their thoughts with the heart, the mind, and inspired wisdom.
To him indeed I bring this supreme, sun-winning hymn with my mouth; with the most liberal invocations of our thoughts and with well-fashioned praises, I seek to magnify the patron.
To him indeed I fashion this hymn, as a carpenter fashions a chariot for its master;
and songs well-refined, which move all things, for Indra, the wise one who is borne by songs.
For this Indra, with my ladle, I anoint the hymn like a prize-winning steed,
desiring to praise the hero who dwells in bounty, the shatterer of forts whose fame is celebrated.
For him indeed Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the thunderbolt, most skillfully wrought and resounding for the battle;
with it, the Lord, striking down Vṛtra, pierced his vital spot—how great was his power as he struck!

At the libations of his mother, having immediately drunk the great draught and the delicious foods, the mighty Viṣṇu, more powerful than the strongest, carried off the cooked [meat]; as a shooter, he pierced the boar beyond the mountain.
For him indeed, for Indra, even the divine ladies, the wives of the gods, wove a hymn upon the slaying of the serpent.
He has encompassed the two wide worlds, heaven and earth; they have not reached the limit of his greatness.
His greatness indeed surpasses that of heaven, earth, and the intermediate space.
Self-ruling Indra, praised by all in his own home, the self-resounding and invincible one, has grown strong for the battle.
By his very might, Indra shattered with his thunderbolt Vṛtra who was swelling;
like penned cattle, he released the flowing waters, being intent on bestowing glory.
At his fierce impetus the rivers were stayed when he hemmed them in with the thunderbolt;
acting as a sovereign lord, bestowing gifts upon the worshipper, the victorious one made a ford for Turvīti.

For him, indeed, bring forth with haste the thunderbolt, O Lord of manifold power, against Vṛtra! Split his joints asunder like those of a cow, piercing across them so that the floods of waters may flow.
Proclaim with new hymns the ancient deeds of this swift one,
when, brandishing his weapons for battle, he, roaring in fury, lays low his enemies.
Out of fear of him, even the firm mountains and heaven and earth tremble at his birth.
Urging on the protection of the longing one, Nodhas has instantly become ready for heroic deeds.
To him indeed was granted that [booty] of theirs, which he alone won as the lord of abundance;
Indra aided Pr̥itaśa, the winner of the prize, as he strove against Sūrya at the contest for the possession of fine horses.

Thus have the Gotamas fashioned these well-wrought prayers for you, O Indra, worthy of the yoking of the bay steeds. Bestow upon them a thought adorned with every beauty; may he who is enriched by prayer come quickly at dawn.

We meditate upon a strengthening hymn of praise for the powerful one, a song of laudation for the lover of songs, as did Aṅgiras; with well-fashioned hymns let us sing a song of worship to the one worthy of praise, the renowned hero.

Bring forth great homage for the Great One; offer a song of praise, a *sāman*, to the Mighty One, by which our ancient fathers, the Aṅgirases, who knew the tracks, found the cows while singing their hymns.
When Indra and the Aṅgirases were active, Saramā found nourishment for her offspring;
Bṛhaspati split the mountain and found the cows; the men lowed together with the ruddy kine.

With the *suṣṭubh* and *stobha* chants, with the seven seers, with the resonant voice, and with the Navagvas, O Indra, you who are worthy of praise, you shattered the mountain Phaliga and Vala with a roar, together with the Saraṇyus and the Daśagvas, O Śakra.
Praised by the Aṅgirases, O Wondrous One, you opened up the darkness with the dawn, with the sun, and with the rays of light.
You spread out the surface of the earth, O Indra, and you propped up the intermediate region of heaven.
That deed of his, the wondrous one, is most manifest and most beautiful;
it is a marvel that at the secret place he caused the four rivers, flowing with honeyed waters, to swell from the heights.
Twofold he has disclosed himself, born of old, dwelling in the same nest, with his tireless hymns of praise.
Like Bhaga, the one of wondrous deeds has supported the two worlds, heaven and earth, in the highest firmament.
From of old, from heaven and from the earth, the two young maidens of different forms, ever-renewed, move one after the other by their own laws:
Night with her dark limbs, Dawn with her radiant bodies.

Seeking to perform noble works, the Son of Wonderous Deeds has established a friendship that endures to the end; by his might, he has placed the ripe milk within the raw cows—white milk within the black and the ruddy ones.
From of old, the sisters dwelling in the same nest, the unaging and immortal ones, protect the laws with their powers;
like wives, many thousands of them serve the one who is free from shame.
Seeking the ancient [deeds], with reverence and new hymns, the thoughts seeking wealth have run forth to you, O Wonder-worker.
Like longing wives to a husband, these inspired prayers touch you, O Lord of Might, who desires them.
From of old, O Wondrous One, the riches in your hand have neither diminished nor failed;
you are brilliant, O Indra, wise and full of power. With your powers, O Lord of Might, grant us your aid.

For him who desires the ancient [gifts], O Indra, Gotama has fashioned a new prayer for the yoking of the tawny steeds. O powerful one, may Nodhas, rich in vision, come quickly to us at dawn with his guidance.
O Indra, you are great, you who at your birth established heaven and earth with your powers;
when all the mountains, even those vast and firm, trembled before you in fear like dust before the wind.

When you, O Indra, come toward your two bay steeds that turn in different directions, your singer places the thunderbolt in your arms— that [thunderbolt] by which, O Lord of unassailable will, you, O much-invoked one, strike down many enemies and their numerous fortresses.
O Indra, you are the true one, the bold; you are R̥bhukṣan, the friend of men, the subduer.
You slew Śuṣṇa in the contest at the prize of food for the sake of the youthful and radiant Kutsa.
O Indra, you indeed, as a friend, impelled that [Vṛtra]; when you, O wielder of the thunderbolt, O performer of manly deeds, struck down Vṛtra.
When, O hero of virile mind, you, the victorious one, scattered the Dasyus far away in their dwelling place at will.

O Indra, when you were about to strike, even against the firm resistance of mortals in their displeasure, you cleared the path for our horse; O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, crush our enemies like wooden stakes.
O Indra, in that contest for waters, in the struggle for light, and in the battle-cry, men call upon you.
O self-dependent one, let this aid of yours be brought swiftly to us in the contests for booty.
O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, you indeed shattered those seven fortresses for Purukutsa while fighting;
just as you spread the sacrificial grass effortlessly for Sudās, O King, you created wide space for Pūru from out of distress.
O Indra, O God, you have caused that wondrous nourishment of ours to swell like waters flowing in every direction—
that food, O Hero, with which you yourself bestow upon us strength, so that it may flow forth for all time like vital energy.
O Indra, these prayers have been fashioned for you by the Gotamas; they have been spoken with reverence for your two bay steeds.
Bring us well-adorned booty; may he who is enriched by prayer come quickly to us at dawn.
O Nodhas, bring forth a well-fashioned hymn for the Maruts— the vigorous host, the liberal givers, the wise ordainers—
just as a skillful-handed sage with a clear mind adorns his songs in the sacrificial assemblies, they who are ever-present at the rites.
They were born from heaven, the lofty bulls, the youths of Rudra, the Asuras free from blemish; purifying and bright like suns, they are like warriors, droplets of fierce appearance.
The youthful Rudras, ageless, slayers of those who do not give, irresistible, have grown like mountains;
by their might they cause even all firm earthly and celestial beings to tremble.
With brilliant ointments they anoint themselves for beauty; upon their chests they have fastened golden ornaments for splendor.
Upon their shoulders the spears rest firmly; these heroes were born together by their own inherent power from heaven.
The roaring ones, destroyers of enemies, acting as lords, have created the winds and lightnings by their powers;
the shakers milk the celestial udders, and wandering all around, they swell the earth with milk.
The bounteous Maruts cause the waters to swell; present at the sacrifices, they provide milk mixed with ghee.
Like a swift steed for the sake of rain, they lead forth the prize-winner; they milk the thundering, inexhaustible spring.
Like mighty buffaloes, wondrously radiant, like mountains self-strong and swift-gliding;
like wild elephants you devour the forests when you have yoked your powers among the ruddy dawns.
Like lions they roar, the wise ones; like boars, well-furbished, they are all-knowing.
Quivering through the nights with spotted deer and spears, they come together in their haste, possessing the fury of serpents through their power.

Address the two worlds, O you who possess the glory of a host, you heroes who pursue men, whose minds are like those of serpents through their might; like a brilliant vision upon a chariot-seat, like lightning, your splendor has taken its place upon your chariots, O Maruts.
O all-knowing ones, dwelling together with riches, united with powers, and overflowing with strength— those heroes,
whose mouths are like bulls and whose vigor is boundless, have taken up their arrows in their hands as archers.
With their golden fellies, increasing the waters, they strike up like mountain torrents;
the Maruts—vigorous, tireless, self-moving, shaking the firm, makers of the storm, with glittering spears.
We praise with our invocation the impetuous, purifying, forest-dwelling, all-beholding son of Rudra;
we follow for the sake of glory the host of Maruts, who traverse the mid-air, who are powerful, who possess the Soma-residue, and who are virile.
That mortal indeed surpasses all people in strength, whom you, O Maruts, have favored with your aid.
With his horses he wins booty, with his men he acquires wealth; he dwells in a state of inquiry for wisdom and prospers.
O Maruts, bestow upon our patrons a praiseworthy, invincible, and radiant strength;
grant us wealth-seeking, hymn-worthy, and all-people-sustaining offspring, so that we may nourish our children and grandchildren for a hundred winters.

Now, O Maruts, bestow upon us enduring wealth, rich in heroes, which overcomes the onset of enemies—a thousandfold, hundredfold, and ever-increasing. May he who is enriched by our prayer come quickly in the morning.
Like a thief lurking in a cave, he who yokes himself with homage and carries it away.
In unison, the wise ones followed along your tracks; all the worshipful ones sat down near you.
The gods follow the ordinances of *ṛta*; let there be encompassing protection, as the sky does for the earth.
The waters, with praise, strengthen him who is well-formed, the newborn in the womb, the seat of Eternal Order.
Like nourishment, it is delightful; like a wide dwelling, it is spacious; like a mountain, it is a source of enjoyment; like water, it is auspicious.
Like a steed urged forward in the race, like the flood of a river— who can restrain him?
A kinsman of the rivers, he devours the forests like a brother his sisters, or as a king devours the elephants.
Or when, impelled by the wind, Agni has spread through the forests, he indeed shears the hair of the earth.
He breathes within the waters like a swan resting there; most wise in his mental power, he awakens at dawn for the sake of the people.
Like Soma, he is a wise ordainer born of the Eternal Order; like a young animal, he is pervasive and his light shines afar.
Like wonderful wealth, like the sight of the sun, like life, like breath, he is like an eternal son.
Like a swift, restless deer he hastens toward the woods; like a cow with milk, he is bright and radiant.
He maintains security like a pleasant home; he is like ripened grain, the conqueror of men.
Like a praising seer among the people, like a well-pleased steed, he bestows vitality.
Difficult to approach in his brilliance, like the eternal will, he is sufficient for everyone, like a wife in her dwelling.
When he has shone forth, variegated like a white horse among the people, brilliant like a golden chariot in battles.
Like an army let loose, he bestows strength; like the missile of an archer, his appearance is dazzling.
Yama indeed was born; Yama is the progeny yet to be born; he is the lover of maidens and the husband of wives.
May we approach him for his dwelling, as cattle go to their stall when he is kindled.
Like the flood of the Sindhu, they have rushed downward; the cows have lowed at the sight of the sun.
Born in the forests, a friend among mortals, he chooses obedience like an undecaying king.
May he be a secure refuge, a virtuous plan, and auspicious; may he be a self-reliant invoker and the bearer of oblations.
Holding all manly powers in his hand, he placed the gods within the secret cave, remaining hidden.
There, the men who conceive inspired thought find her, as they recite the mantras fashioned in their hearts.
Like the Unborn, he has supported the earth and propped up the sky with true mantras.
O Agni, protect the dear tracks of the cattle; as the life of all, you have gone from secret place to secret place.
He who has perceived him dwelling in the secret cave, he who has sat down at the stream of the Eternal Order (Ṛta).
Those who, honoring the cosmic order (*ṛta*), perform their work, for them indeed he has proclaimed riches.
He who by his greatness has established himself within the plants, and within offspring and their sources.
The wise ones, possessing all life, have fashioned him like a dwelling within the house of the waters, as if through inspired thought.
Blending [the oblations], the restless one has approached heaven; he has uncovered the nights for all that stands and moves.
When he alone encompassed all these gods by the greatness of his divinity.
Then indeed all [the gods] took pleasure in your wisdom, O God, when you were born alive from the dry wood.
All partake in the name "Godhead," honoring the Eternal Law (ṛta) and immortality through their courses.
The impulse of *Ṛta*, the thought of *Ṛta*—all have performed all their works throughout their lives.
O wise one, bestow wealth upon him who offers to you or who strives to serve you.
The Hotṛ priest, seated among the offspring of Manu, is indeed the lord of these riches.
Desiring seed for one another’s bodies, the unerring ones have come together through their own innate powers.
Like sons following the will of a father, the swift ones have taken pleasure in his rite and shall listen to his command.
The possessor of much food has thrown open the doors of wealth; the friend of the household has adorned the firmament with stars.
Bright and glowing like the lover of the Dawn, he has filled the two joined worlds like the light of heaven.
Once born, you have encompassed all through your power; though being their son, you have become the father of the gods.
The wise and unerring Agni, discerning, is like the udder of cows; he is the sweetness of nourishments.
Like a kinsman dear to the people, worthy of invocation, he sits in the midst, delightful within the dwelling.
Like a son born in the home, delightful, like a prize-winning steed well-pleased, he has crossed over the people.
When I call upon the clans together with the heroes from their common dwelling, may Agni attain all divine powers through his godhead.
No one violates these laws of yours, since you have granted a hearing to these men.
That indeed is your wondrous deed, that you struck down [the foes] with your peers, when, joined by men, you rent asunder the obstacles.
Like the lover of the Dawn, the radiant one, whose form is well-known, may he take heed of this man.
Carrying themselves by their own power, they opened wide the doors; they all shouted aloud at the sight of the sun.
May we win many thoughts from the noble one; may Agni, shining beautifully, attain all things.
He who understands the divine ordinances and the origin of the human race.
He who is the embryo of the waters, the embryo of the forests, the embryo of all that stands, and the embryo of all that moves.
Even within the rock, within the dwelling, he is like the immortal one among the clans, well-disposed toward his own kin.
For he, Agni, is the lord of riches at night for the one who serves him well with hymns of praise.
O wise one, protect these beings; you who know the generations of the gods and mortals alike.
May the many nights of diverse forms increase him, who is the chariot of the steadfast, impelled by the *ṛta*.
The Hotṛ has been propitiated, seated in the light, performing all true deeds.
You bestow renown upon the cattle and within the forests; may all bring us tribute to the light of heaven.
Men have worshipped you in many places; they bring forth your wealth as sons do for their living father.
Like a skillful man, not greedy; like a hero with a sword; like a terrifying warrior, impetuous in battles.
Like wives of the same dwelling, longing for their own husband, they have stirred him who longs for them;
like cows toward the dappled Dawn as she shines forth, the sisters have delighted in the dark and the ruddy [Dawns].
Even the firmest strongholds, our fathers, the Aṅgirases, shattered with their hymns; they cleft the mountain with their roar.
They made for us a path to the vast heaven; they found the day, the light, and the banner of the dawn.
Establishing the cosmic order (*ṛta*) and stimulating his inspired thought, the noble ones, though diverse, desire to support it;
unthirsting and active, they move toward the gods, strengthening the divine race with nourishment.
When Mātariśvan churned him forth, he who was distributed from house to house became the red, victorious one;
then, like a companion to a more powerful king, the Bhr̥gu-like one undertook his office as messenger.

When he prepared that juice for his great father Dyaus, the wise one stealthily approached the Pṛśanī. The archer boldly released the missile at him; the god cast his brilliance upon his own daughter.

O Agni, he who shines within his own house for you, or who offers homage day after day to you who desire it—O Agni of double strength, increase his vitality; may he whom you urge on reach his goal with wealth in the same chariot.
All nourishments attend upon Agni, as the seven mighty rivers flow toward the ocean.
Our strength is not distinguished by its kinsmen; O Knower, find for us favor among the gods.
When the brilliance reached the lord of men for the sake of nourishment, the pure seed was poured down by Heaven in the encounter;
Agni brought forth and perfected the blameless, youthful, and well-disposed host.
He who, like thought, traverses the paths instantly, the sole hero who rules over all wealth;
the two kings Mitra and Varuṇa, fair-handed, guarding the beloved nectar among the cattle.
O Agni, do not forget our ancestral friendships, you who are a wise seer among those who know. Old age impairs the form like a cloud; before that curse reaches us, take heed!
Holding in his hand many manly poetic insights for the sake of the eternal ordainers, Agni has become the lord of riches; he has truly accomplished all immortal deeds.
The all-wise immortals, seeking him, did not find the calf hidden among us;
exhausted from their search, following his tracks and devoted to meditation, they stood at the highest station, the beautiful place of Agni.
When, O Agni, the pure ones for three autumns worshipped you, the pure one, with clarified butter,
they assumed even worshipful names and perfected their bodies, being well-born.
Making themselves known throughout the two great worlds, the worshipful sons of Rudra have come forth.
The mortal, discerning in the distribution of the sacrificial portions, has found Agni stationed in the highest place.
In agreement, they sat down on their knees; accompanied by their wives, they paid homage to him who is worthy of homage.
Having cast aside [their former] bodies, they fashioned for themselves new forms, as friends guarding the blink of an eye for their friend.
When the worshipful ones discovered the thrice-seven secret steps hidden within you, they, being of one mind, guard the immortality with them; protect the cattle, and guard all that stands and moves.

O Agni, knowing the ways of the peoples, bestow nourishment in due order for our living. Knowing the paths traveled by the gods within, you have become the tireless messenger, the bearer of the oblation.
The wise ones, knowing the cosmic order (*ṛta*), have opened wide the doors of wealth—the seven mighty streams from heaven.
Saramā found the firm enclosure of cattle, by which the human race now prospers.
They who have established all noble offspring, preparing a path toward immortality—
by their greatness, the great Aditi, the mother, has spread out the earth with her sons for the nourishment of the bird.
The immortals established beautiful splendor upon him when they created the two eyes of heaven.
Then, like rivers set loose, the downward-flowing red ones have surged forth; O Agni, they recognized them.
Like wealth inherited from his father, he bestows vital strength; like the instruction of one who knows, he is a perfect guide.
Like a guest resting on a comfortable couch, being well-pleased, he has crossed over the dwellings of the worshipper like a Hotṛ priest.
Like the god Savitṛ whose thoughts are true, he protects all settlements with his wisdom;
highly praised like the immortal one, he is true, and like a dear self, he is to be cherished.
Like a god who sustains all, he dwells upon the earth like a king with well-loved friends; like heroes seated in the citadel for protection, they are blameless like a woman beloved by her husband.
O Agni, men have attended upon you, who are perpetually kindled in their homes, in secure dwellings.
They have bestowed abundant splendor upon you; be the sustainer of all life and the upholder of riches.
O Agni, may the liberal patrons obtain nourishment; may the wise givers attain a full span of life.
May we win booty in battles against the enemy, establishing our portion among the gods for the sake of glory.
For the cows of Truth, lowing and bestowed by Heaven, have swelled with full udders;
seeking favor from afar, the rivers have flowed forth across the rock.
O Agni, seeking your favor, the worshipful ones have established glory in heaven;
they have made Night and Dawn of different forms, and they have joined together the dark hue and the ruddy one.
O Agni, may we and our patrons be those mortals whom you lead to wealth;
like a shadow, you accompany the entire world, having filled the two worlds and the intermediate space.
O Agni, aided by you, may we overcome steeds with steeds, men with men, and heroes with heroes;
being masters of wealth inherited from our fathers, may our wise patrons live for a hundred winters.
O Agni, O Ordainer, may these hymns of praise be pleasing to your mind and heart.
May we be able to control your well-yoked riches, while bestowing upon ourselves the glory allotted by the gods.
Approaching the sacrifice, let us address a prayer to Agni,
who hears us even from afar.
He who, being foremost among the people gathered together in their longing,
protected the household for the donor.
And let the people say: "Agni has been born as the slayer of Vṛtra, the winner of wealth in every battle."
In whose house you are the messenger, and whom you visit to enjoy the oblations—
you perform that sacrifice wondrously.
Him indeed, O Angiras, the people call one to whom oblations are well offered, a possessor of good gods, O son of strength, and one for whom the sacrificial grass is well prepared.
And bring those gods here for our praise,
O bright-shining one, so that they may enjoy the oblations.
No sound of a horse's hooves is heard, nor any rattling of a chariot,
when you, O Agni, go forth on your mission as messenger.
Favored by you, O Agni, the modest steed, urged forward from the one before him to the one behind, has stepped forth to the donor.
And, O divine Agni, you win for the worshipper great splendor and abundant heroic strength from the gods.
Accept this most expansive word, most delightful to the gods,
as you offer the oblations into your mouth.
Now, O Agni, best of the Aṅgirases and most skilled in sacred rites, let us speak to you a beloved prayer that wins the prize.
Who among men is your kinsman, O Agni? Who performs the sacrifice for you?
Who indeed are you, and upon whom do you rest?
O Agni, you are the kinsman of men; you are their dear friend, a companion to be praised by your companions.
Sacrifice for us to Mitra and Varuṇa; sacrifice to the gods and to the lofty *ṛta*.
O Agni, sacrifice to your own household.
What approach is there for the favor of your mind, O Agni? What inspired thought would be most peaceful? Or who has attained your skill through sacrifices? Or with what mind shall we worship you?
Come, O Agni, sit down here as our Hotṛ; be for us an undeceivable and excellent leader.
May the all-pervading Heaven and Earth protect you; sacrifice to the gods for our great favor.
O Agni, burn up all the Rākṣasas; become the protector of our sacrifices against curses.
Then, bring the Lord of Soma with his two bay horses; we have prepared a guest-offering for this most bountiful one.
With offspring-bestowing speech and with my mouth, I call upon you as the bearer; sit down here together with the gods.
Perform the office of the Hotṛ and the Potṛ, O worshipful one; be the giver and the progenitor of riches.
Just as you, O seer, being a seer yourself, sacrificed to the gods with the oblations of the sage Manu,
so now, O most truthful Hotṛ, O Agni, sacrifice today with your joyous ladle.

How shall we offer worship to Agni? What song, beloved by the gods, is recited for him, the radiant one— he who, being immortal among mortals, the observer of *ṛta*, the most excellent invoker (*hotṛ*), brings the gods here?
Him who is the most peaceful at the sacrifices, the upholder of *ṛta*, the Hotṛ—bring him hither with salutations!
When Agni goes to the gods for the sake of the mortal, may he be aware of it and worship them with his mind.
For he is the will, he is the hero, he is the perfect one; like Mitra, he has become the charioteer of the wondrous.
Him, the marvelous one, the Aryan clans seeking the gods address first at the sacrifices.

May Agni, the most heroic among men, the destroyer of enemies, accept our songs, our prayer, and our protection. And may those most powerful patrons, impelled by strength, who are ever-present, further our thought with nourishment.
Thus has Agni, the observer of Truth, Jātavedas, been praised by the inspired Gotamas.
May he increase their splendor among them; may he, being wise, come according to his pleasure and bestow upon them strength and prosperity.
O Jātavedas, who art far-seeing, we the Gotamas extol thee with our song; we praise thee aloud with splendors.
Desirous of wealth, Gotama honors you with his song; we praise you aloud with splendors.
As such, we invoke you, the greatest winner of booty, like Aṅgiras;
we celebrate you aloud with splendors.
We praise you aloud with splendors— you, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, who have shaken off the Dasyus.
We, the Rahūgaṇas, have spoken a honeyed word to Agni;
we praise him aloud with splendors.
Golden-haired in the expanse of the atmosphere, the serpent is roaring like the rushing wind;
he is the radiant one who knows the dawns, as glorious and true as active women.
Your well-winged birds have sped along their courses; the black bull has bellowed when this occurred. He has come with auspicious, smiling [clouds]; the raindrops fall and the clouds thunder.
When Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuṇa Parijman, swelling with the milk of Truth, lead him along the straightest paths of Truth, they moisten his skin in the womb of the lower region.
O Agni, lord of wealth consisting of cattle, O son of strength,
bestow upon us, O Jātavedas, great renown.
Kindled by song, that Agni, the wise one, worthy of praise, bestows wealth upon us; O you of many aspects, shine forth for us!
O King Agni, by night and by yourself, and at the breaking of dawn,
O god with sharp teeth, burn against the Rākṣasas.
O Agni, worthy of praise in all our prayers, protect us with your aids at the offering of the Gāyatra hymn.
O Agni, bring to us wealth that is all-conquering, most excellent,
and invincible in all battles.
O Agni, with your gracious favor, bestow upon us wealth that nourishes all our lives and grant us mercy so that we may live.
O Gotama, desiring his favor, bring forward these purified words and songs for Agni, whose flame is sharp.
O Agni, may he who seeks to harm us, whether near or far, fall down;
do thou bring about our prosperity alone.
The thousand-eyed Agni, who observes all people, drives away the demons;
he is the praiseworthy Hotṛ priest who is celebrated in hymns.
Thus indeed, in the exhilaration of Soma, the priest has performed a strengthening rite;
O most powerful wielder of the thunderbolt, by your might you have driven the serpent from the earth, praising your own sovereign rule.
That bull-like exhilarating Soma, pressed and brought by the falcon, has intoxicated you— that [Soma] by which,
O wielder of the thunderbolt, you struck Vṛtra down from the waters with your might, while singing in accordance with your own sovereignty.
Go forth, advance, be bold! Your thunderbolt shall not be held back.
O Indra, for your power is manly strength; slay Vṛtra, win the waters, and sing in praise of your own sovereignty.
O Indra, you struck Vṛtra down from the earth and from the sky. Release these life-sustaining waters accompanied by the Maruts; sing in praise according to your own sovereignty.
Indra, incensed, having advanced with his thunderbolt against the ridge of the surging Vṛtra, strikes him down; impelling the waters to flow forth, he celebrates according to his own sovereignty.
He strikes down upon the summit with his hundred-jointed thunderbolt;
exhilarated by the soma-juice, Indra seeks a path for his friends, praising his own sovereign dominion.

O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, lord of the pressing-stones, yours alone is that unconquered heroic power, by which you slew with your magic that wily beast; thus they sang in praise of your sovereign dominion.
Your thunderbolts have been hurled forth along the ninety navigable rivers;
great is your heroism, O Indra, and strength has been placed in your arms. Singing praises, we acknowledge your sovereign rule.
Sing forth together a thousandfold; let twenty chant the hymn around him.
A hundred have shouted their approval for him; they sing the prayer raised up for Indra, praising his own sovereign rule.
Indra struck down the power of Vṛtra with his overwhelming force;
great was that manly deed of his. Having slain Vṛtra, he released the waters, chanting in praise of his own sovereign rule.

Even these two great worlds tremble with fear at your wrath, O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, when you, accompanied by the Maruts, struck Vṛtra with your might; they sing in praise of your sovereign rule.
Neither by trembling nor by thundering did Vṛtra terrify Indra;
rather, the iron thunderbolt with its thousand points fell upon him. They sang in praise after his own sovereign rule.
When you, O Indra, brought Vṛtra and your thunderbolt into combat with the mace, as you sought to slay the serpent, your power was established in heaven; we sing in praise of your sovereign rule.
At your shout, O wielder of the stone, both what is stationary and what moves trembles;
even Tvaṣṭṛ himself quivers with fear before your wrath, O Indra, as he acknowledges your sovereign rule.
For indeed, there is no one who surpasses Indra in heroic deeds, as we acknowledge;
in him the gods have concentrated manly strength, wisdom, and power. Singing his praises, they follow after his self-sovereignty.

The prayer which Atharvan, Manu’s father, and Dadhyanc extended—their sacred formulations and hymns have gathered together toward that Indra in the ancient manner; they have sung in accordance with his self-sovereignty.
Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, has been strengthened by men for exhilaration and for power.
Him indeed we invoke in great battles and in small; may he further us in the contests for booty.
For you, O Hero, are worthy of armies; you are the one who bestows much.
You are the increaser even of the meager; you grant wealth in abundance to the sacrificer who presses the soma for you.
When battles arise and wealth is staked for the bold, yoke your two bay steeds that flow with exhilaration. Whom will you slay? To whom will you grant riches? O Indra, place us in riches!
Great through his power, according to his own nature, the terrible one has increased his might.
Sublime in glory, the fair-cheeked, bay-horsed god has placed the iron thunderbolt in his two hands at the very forefront.
He has filled the earthly space and has propped up the luminous realms in heaven.
O Indra, no one like you has ever been born, nor will anyone be born; you have grown beyond all.
May Indra, who bestows upon the worshipper the food of mortals, grant us his aid; distribute your abundant wealth among us, and may I partake of your bounty.
For time and again the one of upright intent has given us herds of cattle;
gather up with both hands many hundreds of riches, sharpen us for wealth, and bring it hither!
Rejoice, O Hero, in the pressed juice for the sake of strength and bounty;
for we know you as the possessor of many riches, and we have released our desires toward you—therefore, be our protector.
O Indra, these people of yours nourish every desirable thing; for you, as the noble one, look within upon the wealth of those people who do not give. Bring that wealth to us!
Listen well, O Maghavan, to our songs as to a mother; when you have acted for us who possess true wealth, then indeed fulfill our purpose. Now, O Indra, yoke your two bay horses.
They have eaten and they have rejoiced; the dear ones have shaken themselves free.
The self-luminous sages have offered praise with a most recent hymn: "Now, O Indra, yoke your two bay steeds!"
O Maghavan, we shall pay homage to you, who are so beautiful to behold.
Now, O you whose chariot-seat is full, being praised, go according to our desires; yoke now, O Indra, your two bay steeds.

He indeed shall mount that bull-like chariot, the winner of cattle, who, O Indra, keeps in mind the full vessel for the *hari-yojana* (the yoking of the bay steeds). Now, O Indra, yoke your two bay horses!
May your right hand be yoked, O Śatakratu, and also your left.
With that, being exhilarated by the soma-juice, go toward your beloved wife. Now, O Indra, yoke your two bay horses.
I yoke for you with a sacred prayer the two long-maned bay steeds; come hither, for you have taken them in your hands.
The impetuous pressed juices have exhilarated you; accompanied by Pūṣan, O wielder of the thunderbolt, you have rejoiced together with your wife.
O Indra, the mortal man whom you protect with your aids goes first to wealth in horses and cattle;
him indeed you fill with even greater riches, as the conscious waters flow from all sides toward the ocean.
Like the divine waters, they approach the Hotṛ’s station; they look down as if upon the wide expanse of the atmosphere.
The gods lead the seeker of the gods forward with their rays; like suitors, they take pleasure in him who loves the sacred word.
You have bestowed praiseworthy speech upon the two who, with uplifted ladles, perform worship as a pair.
Unrestrained, he dwells and prospers within your sacred law; auspicious is the power for the sacrificer who presses the soma.
Then indeed the Aṅgiras first attained vital strength, they whose fires were kindled by their sacred labor and skillful work.
Those heroes found all the Panis' provisions; they brought back cattle consisting of horses and kine.
Atharvan first stretched out the paths with sacrifices; from there Sūrya was born, the guardian of the law, the seer.
Uśanas Kāvya drove forth the cows together; we sacrifice to the immortal birth of Yama.
Whether the sacrificial grass is trimmed for the sake of good offspring, or the hymn proclaims its fame in heaven,
or where the pressing-stone speaks and the singer is worthy of praise— Indra takes delight in those occasions when they have come to his aid.
The Soma has been pressed for you, O Indra; most powerful and bold one, come hither!
May Indra-power fill you, as the sun fills the mid-air with its rays.
The two bay steeds carry Indra, whose power is unassailable,
toward the praises of the seers and toward the sacrifice of human beings.
Mount the chariot, O slayer of Vṛtra; your two bay steeds have been yoked by our sacred prayer.
May the pressing-stone, with its sound, turn your mind toward us.
O Indra, drink this pressed juice, the supreme, immortal exhilaration;
the streams of the bright [Soma] have flowed toward you at the seat of the Eternal Order (Ṛta).
Sing now for Indra and proclaim your hymns;
the pressed drops have exhilarated him. Pay homage to his supreme power.
No one is a better charioteer than you, O Indra, when you guide your two bay horses; no one has ever equaled you in might, nor has anyone with fine steeds attained your level.
He alone who bestows wealth upon the mortal who offers oblations—
Indra, the sovereign and irresistible one, truly is he.
When will he trample with his foot the ungenerous mortal like a mushroom?
When indeed, O Indra, will you truly listen to our songs?
For whosoever, having pressed the Soma, seeks to win you away from many—
Indra alone possesses that fierce power.
From this very center, the Gauri cows drink of the sweet honey;
they who, moving together with the bull Indra, rejoice for the sake of splendor—being excellent, they follow their own sovereignty.
These spotted cows of his, longing for the touch, mix the Soma;
Indra’s dear milch-cows urge on his bolt, the missile, according to his own excellent sovereignty.
With homage, these wise ones serve his conquering power;
they follow his many ordinances for the sake of primordial awareness, following the excellent sovereignty of the self-ruler.
With the bones of Dadhyañc, Indra, irresistible, struck down ninety-nine Vṛtras.
Desiring the horse’s head that was hidden away in the mountains,
he found it at Śaryaṇāvatī.
There they recognized the secret name of Tvaṣṭṛ’s cow,
even here in the dwelling of the moon.
Who today yokes to the pole of Order the impetuous, fierce, and ill-disposed bulls?
He who provides for their maintenance—those who have arrows in their mouths, who pierce the heart, yet are sources of bliss—he shall live.
Who flees? Who is struck with fear? Who is afraid? Who will recognize Indra as being present and near?
Who will speak in favor of offspring, of cattle, of wealth, or of his own body, or for the sake of the people?

Who praises Agni with an oblation of clarified butter? Who shall sacrifice with the ladle according to the fixed seasons? To whom shall the gods bring [the offering] quickly for the oblation? Who, possessing a good god, will consider himself a master of the sacrifice?
O most powerful god, you alone shall truly praise the mortal;
O Maghavan Indra, there is no other besides you who is a comforter—this word I speak to you.
O Vasu, let not your bounties nor your aids ever fail us;
O Manu’s son, bestow upon us all riches from among the peoples.
Those sons of Rudra who, like wives or like coursers on their way, adorn themselves with wondrous deeds;
for the Maruts have made heaven and earth grow—they, the bold heroes, rejoice in the assemblies.
Having grown strong, they have attained greatness; the Rudras have established their seat in heaven.
Chanting their hymn and generating vital power, those sons of Pṛśni have clothed themselves in splendor.
When the sons of the cow adorn themselves with ointments, the radiant ones have placed shining ornaments upon their bodies;
they drive away every adversary, and ghee flows along their paths.
Those who shine forth as great warriors with their spears, shaking even the unshakable by their might—
when you Maruts, whose hosts are like bulls, yoked the spotted deer to your chariots that are swift as thought.
When you have harnessed the spotted deer to your chariots, O Maruts, speeding the stone in the contest for booty;
then the streams of the ruddy one burst forth, and as with water upon a hide, they drench the earth.
May your coursers, swift-gliding and rapid-flying, carry you hither; come forth with your arms.
Sit upon the sacred grass; a wide seat has been prepared for you. O Maruts, rejoice yourselves in the sweet juice of the soma plant.
They grew strong by their own power through their greatness; they took their stand upon the firmament and made for themselves a wide dwelling.
When Viṣṇu ran toward the bull who distills exhilaration, they sat down like birds upon the dear sacrificial grass.
Like heroes indeed, like warriors they have gone forth; seeking glory, they have exerted themselves in battles.
All beings are afraid of the Maruts; like kings, these men are of dazzling appearance.
When Tvaṣṭṛ, the skillful craftsman, fashioned the well-made golden thunderbolt with its thousand points, Indra took it up to perform manly deeds; he slew Vṛtra and released the flood of waters.
By their might they pushed the well upward; they split even the firmly fixed mountain asunder. Blowing their flute, the bounteous Maruts performed deeds of joy in the exhilaration of Soma.
They pushed the well sideways in that direction; they poured out the spring for the thirsty Gotama. Coming with help, O you of wondrous luster, you satisfied the desire of the sage by your powers.
Those threefold protections which you have for the one who exerts himself, grant them to the donor.
Extend those to us, O Maruts; bestow upon us wealth, O bulls, with excellent heroes.
O Maruts, great in majesty, that person in whose dwelling you drink [the soma] from heaven is indeed the most well-protected of men.
O Maruts, who carry the sacrifice by means of sacrifices, or by the hymns of the inspired singer, hear our invocation!
Or he for whom the prize-winners have fashioned a sage— he shall go to a stall rich in cattle.
Upon the sacrificial grass of this hero, Soma is pressed during the celestial rites;
his hymn of praise and his exhilarating draught are recited.
May all the peoples listen to him who prevails over them;
may the strengthening draughts flow even toward the Sun.
For through many autumns, O Maruts, we have offered worship with the protections granted by you to the peoples.
O Maruts, may that mortal be fortunate whom you, O worthy of sacrifice,
carry across his offerings.
O heroes of true strength, you who are mindful of the sweat of him who exerts himself,
take note of the desire of the longing one.
O you of true strength, manifest that [power] through your greatness;
pierce the demon with your lightning bolt.
Concealing the secret darkness, drive away every devouring demon; create the light that we desire.
Exceedingly vigorous, powerful, and overflowing with strength, unbowed and unshakable, they who possess the soma-dregs;
most beloved and most manly, they have adorned themselves with ointments, like certain bulls with their stripes.
When you, O Maruts, have gathered like birds on some path upon the slopes, the casks drip upon your chariots; sprinkle the honey-colored ghee for the singer!
At their onset, the earth trembles as if unsteady during their marches when they yoke themselves for glory;
they, the playful, the roaring, with glittering spears—the shakers—themselves proclaim their own greatness.
For he is the self-moving host with spotted horses, the youthful one; you are the lord, surrounded by powers, irresistible.
You are the true one, the seeker of debts, beyond reproach; you are the furtherer of this prayer and the bull-like host.
We speak by the birth of the ancient Father; the tongue of Soma goes forth with his vision.
When the singers have reached Indra with their labor, they assume the names worthy of sacrifice.
For the sake of glory, they have mingled themselves with splendors; they are well-armed with rays and with singers.
Armed with spears, impetuous, and fearless, they have found the beloved domain of the Marut host.
O Maruts, come hither with your lightning-bright chariots, well-sounding, armed with spears, and winged with horses;
fly toward us like birds with most abundant food, O you of wondrous power.
They come for our choice, with ruddy, tawny horses that hasten the chariot for our welfare;
like a brilliant golden ornament, equipped with axes, they strike the earth with the fellies of their chariot.
For the sake of beauty, do you place axes upon your bodies? May they raise them up like forests, as if through inspired wisdom.
For your sake, O well-born Maruts of great splendor, they set the pressing-stone into motion.
The days have come around to you, O eagles, for this prayer and the divine song of praise.
Making the sacred formulation with their hymns, the Gotamas have pushed up the water-vessel from its seat so that you may drink.
This very thing, O Maruts, has become manifest to you, even as Gotama perceived you—
beholding the boars with golden wheels and iron tusks as they ran about.
O Maruts, this voice of yours is a bringer of support; it resounds like the chant of a priest. It has spontaneously caused the songs to resound, following its own inherent power from the hands.
May auspicious intentions come to us from every side—intentions that are undeceived, unassailable, and victorious.
May the gods be ever present for our prosperity, our guardians day by day, never failing in their protection.
May the auspicious favor of the gods, who are upright in their striving, be ours; may the bounty of the gods turn toward us.
We have sought the friendship of the gods; may the gods extend our life-span that we may live.
With the ancient invocation we call upon them: Bhaga, Mitra, Aditi, Dakṣa the infallible, Aryaman, Varuṇa, Soma, and the Aśvins. May Sarasvatī, the bringer of good fortune, grant us bliss.
May the Wind blow that healing medicine to us which brings delight; may Mother Earth grant it, and Father Heaven grant it.
May the pressing-stones that press the Soma, bringing delight, grant it; and do you two, O Ashvins, the wise ones, hear this!
We invoke for our protection that Lord, the master of all that moves and stands, the inspirer of the intellect;
may Pūṣan be the increaser of our wealth, our protector and undeceivable guardian for our well-being.
May Indra of far-reaching fame grant us well-being; may Pūṣan, the knower of all, grant us well-being;
may Tārkṣya with uninjured wheels grant us well-being; may Bṛhaspati bestow well-being upon us.
The Maruts, whose horses are spotted, whose mother is Pṛśni, who move in splendor and frequent the assemblies;
the Manavas, whose tongue is Agni and whose eyes are the sun—all you gods, come here to us with your protection.

O Gods, may we hear with our ears what is auspicious; O Holy Ones, may we see with our eyes what is auspicious. With firm limbs and bodies, having offered praise, may we attain the full span of life ordained by the Gods.
A hundred autumns indeed are before us, O gods, within which you have ordained the aging of our bodies;
wherein sons become fathers—do not harm our life-span in its course.
Aditi is heaven, Aditi is the mid-region; Aditi is the mother, she is the father, she is the son.
All the gods are Aditi, the five peoples are Aditi; Aditi is what has been born, Aditi is what is yet to be born.
May Varuṇa and Mitra, the wise ones, lead us by a straight path,
together with Aryaman and the gods, in perfect harmony.
For they, the masters of wealth, are the dispensers of riches; they, being undeluded by their own greatness, guard the sacred laws at all times.
May they, the immortals, grant protection to us mortals,
driving away our enemies.
May Indra and the Maruts mark out our paths for our well-being;
may Pūṣan and Bhaga, worthy of praise, do the same.
And may our prayers, headed by the desire for cattle— O Pūṣan, O Viṣṇu, you who move swiftly—
make us possessed of well-being.
The winds blow honey for the one who follows the cosmic order; the rivers flow with honey; may the plants be sweet for us.
May the night be honey-sweet, and may the dawns be honey-sweet; may the earthly realm be full of honey, and may our father, the sky, be honey-sweet for us.
May the Lord of the Forest be full of sweetness for us; may the Sun be full of sweetness;
may the cows be sweet for us.
May Mitra be auspicious to us, may Varuṇa be auspicious, and may Aryaman be auspicious to us.
May Indra and Bṛhaspati be auspicious to us, and may Viṣṇu of the wide stride be auspicious to us.
O Soma, you are preeminent in wisdom; you lead us along the straightest path.
Under your guidance, O Indu, our wise fathers obtained their share of treasure among the gods.
O Soma, through your powers you have become one of noble will; through your skills you have become one of great skill, the knower of all.
As a bull by your bull-like qualities and through your greatness, you, the beholder of men, have become resplendent with splendors.
Truly, thy laws are those of King Varuṇa; great and profound, O Soma, is thy domain.
Thou art pure, dear like Mitra, and worthy of skillful service like Aryaman, O Soma.
Those abodes of yours which are in heaven, those on earth, and those in the mountains, in the plants, and in the waters—
with all of them, O King Soma, being well-disposed and free from anger, accept our offerings.
O Soma, you are the lord of the virtuous; you are the king and the slayer of Vṛtra;
you are the auspicious power of will.
And you, O Soma, being well-disposed toward us, grant us life; may we not die. You are the Lord of the Forest, whose hymns of praise are beloved.
O Soma, you bestow great fortune upon the aged, and you grant skill for living to the youth who follows the cosmic order.
O Soma, O King, protect us from every side against the one who seeks to do us harm;
a friend such as you shall never suffer injury.
O Soma, those bliss-bestowing aids of yours that exist for the donor—
with those, be our protector.
Enjoying this sacrifice and these words, come hither;
O Soma, be for our prosperity.
O Soma, we who are skilled in speech magnify you with our songs; enter into us as one who is most gracious.
O Soma, be a good friend to us— you who increase the dwelling, drive away disease, find wealth, and augment prosperity.
O Soma, take delight in our heart, as cattle do in pastures,
like a young man in his own home.
O divine Soma, whatever mortal delights in your friendship,
him the wise and skillful seer attends.
Deliver us from reproach, O Soma; protect us from distress.
Be a most gracious friend to us.
Swell up! Let virile strength gather from every side, O Soma; be present at the gathering of booty.
Swell up, O most intoxicating Soma, with all your stalks;
become for us a most glorious friend for our prosperity.
May thy milks, and thy strengths, and thy bull-like powers that overcome the assailants come together;
swelling for the sake of immortality, O Soma, bestow upon us the highest glories in heaven.
Those abodes of yours which they worship with oblation—may all those be encompassers of the sacrifice for you.
Increasing the household, furthering us, rich in heroes, not slaying our men—O Soma, enter the dwellings.

Soma gives a milch-cow; Soma gives a swift steed; Soma gives a hero who is skillful in action—one who is a good householder, fit for the assembly, worthy of the council, and a glory to his father—to him who offers oblations to him.
Unconquered in battles, the filler of armies, winner of the light, winner of the waters, guardian of the stronghold,
born for the fray, providing secure dwelling, of great renown, and victorious— O Soma, may we rejoice after you!
O Soma, you generated all these plants; you generated the waters and the cows.
You have stretched out the wide mid-air, and with light, you have dispelled the darkness.
O divine Soma, with your divine mind, O powerful one, fight for our share of wealth! Let it not fail you; you are the master of heroic power. Provide for both sides in the quest for cattle.
These Dawns have indeed raised their banner; in the eastern half of the mid-air, they anoint themselves with light.
Like bold warriors preparing their weapons, the ruddy cows, the mothers, come forth toward us.
The ruddy beams have flown upward at will; they have yoked their own red, well-yoked cows. The dawns have performed their ancient works; the ruddy ones have assumed their radiant light.
The women sing out like active workers with their tasks, traveling from afar by the same path;
bringing nourishment to the well-doing, bountiful giver, they do so every day for the sacrificer who presses the soma.
Like a dancer, she puts on her ornaments; like a cow baring her udder, she uncovers her breast. Creating light for the whole world, Dawn has flung open the darkness as cows leave their pen.
Her radiant beam has been seen facing us; it spreads abroad and drives away the black monster.
Like one anointing a sacrificial post with ornaments at the rites, the Daughter of Heaven has extended her wondrous luster.
We have crossed to the further shore of this darkness; the dawning Uṣas makes the paths of knowledge manifest.
Smiling for the sake of beauty like a lover, she shines forth with radiant countenance and has awakened us for goodwill.
Radiant leader of true blessings, the Daughter of Heaven is praised by the Gotamas.
O Dawn, bestow upon us strengths that consist of progeny, heroes, and horses, with cattle at their head.

O Uṣas, may I obtain that glorious wealth consisting of brave sons, with Dāsas as its foremost part and horses as its foundation—wealth that you, O auspicious one, radiate forth with wondrous fame, impelled by strength. May it be great!
Beholding all beings, O Goddess, she shines forth widely with her eye turned toward us;
awakening every living creature to movement, she has found the speech of every thoughtful person.
Born again and again, ancient, adorning herself with the same color,
like a skilled gambler winning the stakes, the goddess wears away the life of mortals.
Uncovering the ends of heaven, she has awakened; she drives her sister far away. Diminishing the ages of men, the maiden shines forth with the eye of her lover.
Like a wondrous, fortunate cow spreading her cattle, like a river’s flood she has shone forth widely.
Not violating the divine ordinances, she is seen visible with the rays of the sun.
O Uṣas, rich in prizes, bring to us that wondrous gift by which we may obtain both children and grandchildren.
O Uṣas, rich in cattle and horses, radiant one, shine forth here today; O you who possess pleasant gifts, dawn upon us with wealth.
Yoke, O Uṣas rich in steeds, your ruddy horses today;
then bring to us all auspicious fortunes.
O Aśvins, wonder-workers, come to our dwelling rich in cattle and gold;
with one mind, direct your chariot hither.
Since you two have thus brought forth renown from heaven and light for mankind,
O Aśvins, bring nourishment hither to us.
May the gods, the wonder-workers who bring bliss, whose paths are golden, and who awaken at dawn, come here to drink the Soma.
O Agni and Soma, you two bulls, graciously hear this my invocation;
accept these hymns with favor and be a source of joy to the donor.
O Agni and Soma, to him who honors you both today with this speech,
bestow heroic vigor, abundance of cattle, and excellence in horses.
O Agni and Soma, whoever offers an oblation or presents a prepared sacrifice to you,
he shall attain full life, abounding in offspring and heroic strength.
O Agni and Soma, that heroic power of yours is celebrated, whereby you stole the food, the Pani, and the cows;
you struck down the offspring of Bṛsaya and found the single light for many.
