O Agni and Soma, you two of one mind have placed these luminous realms in heaven;
O Agni and Soma, you released the rivers from reproach and from disgrace when they were seized.
Mātariśvan brought one from heaven; the falcon churned the other from the mountain.
O Agni and Soma, having been magnified by our prayer, you have made wide space for the sacrifice.
O Agni and Soma, enjoy this presented oblation; O bulls, desire it and take pleasure in it.
For you have become providers of good protection and excellent aid; therefore, bestow well-being and prosperity upon the sacrificer.
O Agni and Soma, protect the vow of him who honors you with an oblation, who honors you with a mind directed toward the gods, and who honors you with clarified butter;
guard him from distress and grant great protection to his people and his household.
O Agni and Soma, possessing common wealth and invoked together, accept our songs; you have both become present among the gods.
O Agni and Soma, for him who honors you with this [oblation] or with clarified butter,
shine forth greatly for him.
O Agni and Soma, may you both graciously accept these our oblations;
come together unto us.
O Agni and Soma, protect our horses; let the cows that yield the oblation swell with milk.
Bestow strength upon us and upon our patrons, and make our sacrifice successful and full of prompt obedience.
For this worthy Jātavedas, let us fashion this hymn of praise with our intellect, as one fashions a chariot;
for his providence is auspicious for us in the assembly. O Agni, in your friendship, may we never suffer harm.
He for whom you sacrifice prospers; he dwells free from enemies and gains great heroic might.
He thrives, and no distress reaches him. O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.

May we be able to kindle thee; may our prayers be fulfilled. In thee the gods eat the offered oblation. Bring hither the Ādityas, for we desire them; O Agni, in thy friendship may we never suffer harm.
Let us bring fuel and prepare oblations for you, mindful of you at every joint of the seasons.
Further our prayers so that we may live; O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.
The guardians of the people, his creatures, move about by night—both bipeds and quadrupeds.
Wondrous is the herald of the Dawn; great art thou, O Agni. In thy friendship, may we never suffer harm.
You are the Adhvaryu and the ancient Hotṛ; by birth you are the Praśāstṛ, the Potṛ, and the Purohita.
Knowing all priestly duties, O wise one, you cause them to flourish. O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.

O Agni, you who are beautiful to behold from every side and uniform in appearance—you shine forth like lightning even when far away. O God, you see beyond even the darkness of night; in your friendship, may we never suffer harm.
O Gods, let the chariot of the one who presses the soma be foremost; may our hymn of praise overcome the malicious.
Take note of this word and let it flourish; O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.

Strike down with weapons those of evil intent and the malevolent; whoever are devourers, whether they be far or near—then make the path easy for the sacrifice and for the singer. O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.

When you have yoked to your chariot the two ruddy, red steeds, impelled by the wind—your roar is like that of a bull; then you consume the trees with your smoke-bannered flame. O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.

Then at your roar, even the winged birds were struck with fear, when your sparks, devouring the grass, scattered abroad. May that path be easy for you and for your chariots; O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.
May this [hymn] serve for the sustenance of Mitra and Varuṇa, and may it appease the wondrous wrath of the Maruts.
O Agni, be gracious to us and turn their minds toward us again; in your friendship, may we never suffer harm.
O God, you are the wondrous friend among the gods; you are the Vasu among the Vasus, beloved at the sacrifice.
May we abide in your most extensive protection; O Agni, may we never suffer harm in your friendship.
That is your blessing, that when kindled in your own abode and invoked with Soma, you awaken as the most merciful one.
You bestow jewels and wealth upon the donor; O Agni, in your friendship may we never come to harm.
O Aditi, possessor of excellent wealth, to whomsoever you grant freedom from sin in its full perfection,
and whomsoever you impel with auspicious power and with bounty consisting of progeny— may we be those people.
As such, O Agni, you who know the way to prosperity, prolong our lifespan here, O God.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the Sindhu, the Earth, and also the Sky grant us this.
Two of different forms move toward their own goal; one after the other, they suckle the calf.
With the one, he becomes golden-hued and self-dependent; with the other, he is seen bright and full of splendor.
The tireless young women brought forth this child of Tvaṣṭṛ, the widely-spread one;
they lead him around, he who has sharp-edged weapons, self-glorious, and shining brightly among the people.
They honor his three births: one in the ocean, one in heaven, and one in the waters.
Governing the seasons, he has duly distributed them according to the eastern quarter of the earthly realms.
Who among you has perceived this hidden one? The calf has brought forth his mothers by his own powers.
As the embryo of many, the great seer goes forth from the lap of the active waters, self-sustained.
The lovely one, worthy of invocation, grows within these [waters]; rising upright in their lap with his own glory, he is the lord of those who lie prostrate.
Both [worlds] are afraid of Tvaṣṭṛ as he is being born; turning toward him, they both take pleasure in the lion.
Both auspicious ones delight him like two women; like lowing cows they have approached him in their accustomed way.
He has become the lord of skills among the skillful, he whom they anoint from the right with oblations.
Like Savitṛ, he stretches out his arms; as he moves forward, the terrible one strives to reach both edges.
He draws up a bright garment for himself alone, and leaves new raiments for his mothers.
He assumes a brilliant form, even higher, as he mingles with the waters and the milk in his dwelling;
the sage, through his inspired thought, polishes the foundation. This has become the assembly at the gathering of the gods.
Wide extends your course around the foundation, the shining domain of the Great Bull.
O Agni, kindled with all your own glories, protect us with unfailing guardians.
In the desert he creates a stream, a path, and a wave; with his bright waves he reaches the earth.
He places all ancient things within his bellies; he moves within the newly born plants.
Thus, O Agni, increasing by our fuel, O purifier, shine forth with wealth for the sake of glory!
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
Born by force as of old, he has instantly assumed all poetic wisdom.
Both the waters and the Dhiṣaṇā have established him as a friend; the gods have maintained Agni, the bestower of wealth.
By means of the ancient invocation and through his wisdom, he brought forth these progeny of men;
with Vivasvat as their eye, the gods maintained Agni, the giver of wealth, as the lord of heaven and waters.
The Āryan clans magnified him, the first accomplisher of sacrifice, who is invoked and who strives forward;
the gods maintained Agni, the son of strength, the Bharata, the giver of flowing gifts, the bestower of wealth.
May Mātariśvan, whose nourishment is many boons, find a path for his offspring, he who wins the light;
the guardian of the people, the progenitor of heaven and earth—the gods have established Agni as the bestower of wealth.
Night and Dawn, changing their colors as they meet, suckle the one infant together;
between Heaven and Earth the golden disk shines forth; the gods have established Agni, the giver of wealth.
The foundation of wealth, the gatherer of treasures, the banner of sacrifice, the fulfiller of thought, the bird—
guarding their immortality, the gods maintained this Agni as the giver of riches.

Now and of old, the gods have maintained Agni as the abode of riches, the guardian of what has been born and of what is being born, and the protector of what exists and of what shall become abundant; they uphold him as the giver of wealth.
May the Giver of Wealth bestow upon us the wealth of the swift; may the Giver of Wealth grant us the wealth of heroes.
May the Giver of Wealth provide us with food accompanied by valiant sons; may the Giver of Wealth grant us long life.
Thus, O Agni, growing strong by our fuel, shine forth with wealth, O Purifier, for the sake of glory.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
May our evil be burned away; O Agni, shine wealth upon us;
may our evil be burned away.
With a desire for good fields, for a good path, and for wealth, we sacrifice;
may he burn away our evil.
When he is praised as the most excellent among these, and when our wise patrons are likewise praised,
may he burn away our evil.
O Agni, when through thee the wise patrons are born, may we also be born through thee;
may thy light drive away our evil.
When the rays of the powerful Agni go forth in all directions,
may he burn away our evil.
For you, O you who face in every direction, encompass all things from every side;
burn away our evil.
O you who face in every direction, carry us across our enemies as if with a boat;
burn away our evil.
May he carry us across for our well-being, as one crosses to a river by boat;
may he burn away our evil.
May we abide in the good-will of Vaiśvānara, for he is the king, the glory of all beings.
Born from here, he beholds this entire universe; Vaiśvānara strives in harmony with the sun.
Sought in heaven, sought on earth, Agni has entered into all plants;
Vaiśvānara Agni, sought with power, may he protect us from harm by day and by night.
O Vaiśvānara, let that be true for you: may riches and liberal patrons attend us.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the Sindhu, the Earth, and also Heaven grant us this.
Let us press the Soma for Jātavedas; may he burn away the wealth of the one who acts with hostility.
May Agni carry us across all difficulties, as a boat carries one across a river, beyond all misfortunes.

May that Indra, the bull who dwells together with his virile powers, the sovereign lord of the great heaven and earth, whose warriors are true, who is to be invoked in battles— may he, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.
He whose course is unassailable like that of the sun, who possesses the strength of a Vṛtra-slayer in every battle;
may Indra, the most virile one, accompanied by his own friends, the Maruts, come to our aid with his protection.
Whose paths, like the streams of heaven’s seed being milked, go forth unassailable by might;
he who overcomes hatreds and is victorious through his manly powers—may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.
He, the best of the Aṅgiras, became one with the Aṅgiras; the bull with the bulls, the friend with the friends;
the singer with the singers, the most excellent with the songs—may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.
Like a skillful son with the Rudras, he has overcome his enemies in the battle for men;
surpassing those of common origin toward glorious deeds—may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.
He who quells the fury of battle, the maker of the fray, may he win the sun with our men;
on this very day, may Indra—the lord of the virtuous, much-invoked, and accompanied by the Maruts—be with us for our protection.
His aids have made him rejoice in the battle for booty; the people have made him the protector of their security.
He alone is the lord of every pious deed; may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.
Men seek him out for help in the celebrations of strength; they seek that hero for aid and for wealth.
May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, find light even in the blinding darkness; may he be our protection.
With his left hand he restrains even those who are swelling with power; with his right hand he gathers the spoils of war.
Even through the singer, he wins riches; may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.
He wins with his hosts and he wins with his chariots; today he is known by all the tribes.
He overcomes the revilers through his manly deeds—may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.
When he, invoked by many, comes with his own ways to the battle— whether with kinsmen or with strangers—
to win the waters, offspring, and progeny, may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.
May that Indra—wielder of the thunderbolt, slayer of the Dasyus, terrible, fierce, thousand-witted, hundred-fold leader, and skillful;
like the draught of Soma in power, the protector of the five peoples—accompanied by the Maruts, come to our aid.
His thunderbolt roars, winning the light of heaven; like the brilliant and impetuous roar of the sky, it resounds.
Victories attend him, and riches attend him; may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be with us for our protection.
He whose hymn of praise, through his constant power, encompasses both heaven and earth on every side—
he, Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, may he protect us with his wisdom and be our aid, rejoicing in his own strength.
Neither gods nor mortals, nor even the waters, have reached the limit of his power;
he who has overspread both earth and heaven with his might—may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.
The ruddy mare, bright with ornaments, marked with a blaze, celestial, and the bringer of wealth for R̥jrāśva—
she who bears the stallion-drawn chariot at the yoke-poles, the joyous one, has been made manifest among the tribes of Nahusha.
This very hymn of praise, O Indra, the bull-like one, the Vārṣāgiras offer to you as a gift of bounty:
Ṛjrāśva with his side-horses, Ambarīṣa, Sahadeva, Bhayamāna, and Surādhās.
O you who are invoked by many, having slain the Dasyus and the Śimyu with your weapons according to your ways, you have struck them down upon the earth.
With your brilliant companions, the wielder of the excellent thunderbolt has won the land, he has won the sun, and he has won the waters.
May Indra be our advocate every day; may we, unassailed, win the prize.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
Sing forth a word full of nourishment to the exhilarated one, who with Ṛjiśvan struck down those whose wombs were black.
Seeking aid, we invoke for friendship the bull who wields the thunderbolt in his right hand, accompanied by the Maruts.
Indra, who with his exultant fury struck down Vyansa, who slew Shambara and the lawless Pipru, and who cast down the insatiable Shushna— we invoke him, accompanied by the Maruts, for friendship.
He whose great manly power is heaven and earth, in whose ordinance Varuṇa and Sūrya abide,
and whose law the rivers follow— that Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, we invoke for friendship.
He who is the master and controller of horses and of cattle, who is present and steadfast in every ritual act—
he who is Indra, the slayer even of the strong one who pours no libation, him, accompanied by the Maruts, we invoke for friendship.
He who is the lord of all that moves and breathes, he who first found the cows for the Brahman,
Indra who cast down the Dasyus— him, accompanied by the Maruts, we invoke for friendship.
He who is to be invoked by the brave and by the timid, who is called upon by those fleeing and by those victorious—
he, Indra, whom all beings have brought together under their protection, him we invoke, accompanied by the Maruts, for friendship.
The far-seeing one goes forth by the direction of the Rudras; with the Rudras, the maiden extends her broad course.
The inspired thought praises the famous Indra; we invoke him, accompanied by the Maruts, for friendship.

Whether, O Lord of the Maruts, you rejoice in the highest dwelling place, or whether you delight in the lowest assembly, come from there toward our sacrifice; desiring you, we have prepared the oblation, O you whose gifts are true.
For you, O Indra, we have pressed the Soma, O most skillful one; for you we have prepared the oblation, O you who are drawn by prayer.
Therefore, O Lord of the teams, accompanied by the host of Maruts, rejoice at this sacrifice upon the sacred grass.
Rejoice with the bay steeds that are yours, O Indra; unbind your jaws and let loose your two lips.
Let the bay horses, O fair-jawed one, bring you hither; desiring our offerings, graciously accept them.
Guardians of the host that praises the Maruts, may we, through Indra, win booty.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
I offer this great prayer to you, the Great One, since my inspired thought has been polished for this hymn of praise.
At his festival and at his impulse, the gods have acclaimed Indra, the conqueror, with their power.
The seven rivers bear his fame; heaven and earth and the broad world bear his visible form.
O Indra, Sūrya and Candramas move in their alternating course for us to behold, so that we may have faith.
O Maghavan, favor that victorious chariot of yours for our gain, which we shall cheer on in the encounter;
O Indra, praised by many, with your mind protect us in the fray, O Maghavan, and grant us shelter to those who are devoted to you.
May we, with you as our ally, conquer the foe; in every battle, uplift our portion.
O Indra, grant us wide space and easy passage; O Maghavan, shatter the virile strength of our enemies.
For these people, praising you with their hymns, invoke you from various sides, O upholder of riches, seeking your aid.
Ascend our chariot for the sake of winning; for victorious, O Indra, is your steadfast mind.
His arms win cattle; he is the peerless one of boundless power. At every deed, he provides a hundredfold aid and stirs the battle-dust.
Indra is beyond compare in his might; thus, people who desire to win call upon him.
O Maghavan, your fame among the people has surpassed a hundred, and indeed more than a thousand; you have exceeded them all.
Your measureless wisdom has glowed mightily for you, so that now, O Purandara, you may strike down the Vṛtras.
A match for thy might is the threefold heaven; O Lord of men, thou hast surpassed the three earths and the three luminous realms.
Thou hast grown beyond this entire world; O Indra, from of old, by thy very birth, thou art without an enemy.
We invoke you first among the gods; you have become the conqueror in battles.
May Indra place this singer Upamanyu at the forefront in our enterprise, as one who breaks through obstacles like a chariot.
You have conquered; you have not withheld wealth in battles, O Maghavan, whether among the small or the great.
We sharpen you, the fierce one, for our protection; therefore, O Indra, impel us in our invocations.
May Indra be our advocate every day; unassailed, may we win the prize.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
That supreme power of yours, O Indra, the seers sustained in the distance before this world existed.
One part of it is here on earth, another is in heaven; these two are joined together like a banner at a gathering.
He supported the earth and spread it out; having struck with his thunderbolt, he released the waters.
He slew the serpent, he split Rauhiṇa asunder, and Maghavan struck down Vyaṃsa by his mighty deeds.
Bearing his innate strength and full of faith, he advanced, shattering the forts of the Dāsas.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, knowing well, hurl your weapon at the Dasyu; O Indra, increase the Aryan power and your glorious splendor.
To him who spoke thus, these human ages have come, as Maghavan bears a name worthy of praise;
approaching for the slaying of the Dasyus, the wielder of the thunderbolt has indeed established his name for the sake of glory as a son.
Behold this vast abundance of his; place your faith in the heroic power of Indra.
He found the cattle, he found the horses; he found the plants, he found the waters, and he found the forests.
For the bull, the showerer of benefits, the performer of many deeds, whose strength is true—let us press the Soma for him;
he who, like a hero ambushing on the road, goes about distributing the wealth of the non-sacrificer.
O Indra, you truly performed that heroic deed when you awakened the sleeping serpent with your thunderbolt;
the wives, the birds, and all the gods rejoiced after you as you were filled with joy.
When you, O Indra, slew Śuṣṇa, Pipru, Kuyava, and Vṛtra, and shattered the fortresses of Śambara—
may Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that as a great gift.
A seat has been prepared for you, O Indra, to sit upon; sit down there like a neighing steed.
Unyoke your birds and unfasten your horses, you who carry us most swiftly at evening, at dawn, and at the start of the journey.
Those heroes have indeed come to Indra for aid; may he speedily traverse those paths to reach them.
May the gods quell the wrath of the Dāsa, and may they lead our people toward prosperity.
He himself brings down the one who knows the signal; he himself brings down the foam from the water.
Bathed in milk, the two wives of Kuyava shall lie slain in the steep descent of the Śiphā river.
The kinship of the lower Āyu has perished; the hero extends further with his ancient [deeds] and rules as sovereign.
Añjasī, Kuliśī, and Vīrapatnī, swelling with milk, bring forth [the waters] with their floods.

When that path of the Dasyu was revealed, she who knows her way went toward our dwelling as if to her own home. Now, O Maghavan, remember us; do not cast us away like a careless gambler throws away his wealth.
As such, O Indra, grant us a share in the sun, in the waters, and in sinlessness, for the sake of our living praise.
Do not harm our inner enjoyment; we have placed our trust in your great Indra-power.
Now, therefore, I believe that faith has been placed in you; as a bull, rouse yourself for great wealth.
O Indra, invoked by many, do not leave us in an unprepared dwelling; give food and drink to those who hunger.
Do not slay us, O Indra; do not abandon us; do not steal away our dear enjoyments.
O Maghavan, O Śakra, do not pierce our eggs; do not shatter our vessels that are born together with us.
Come hither; they say you desire Soma—here it is pressed, drink of it for exhilaration.
O wide-extending one, pour it into your belly; being invoked, hear us like a father.
The moon moves within the waters; the fair-winged bird hastens through the sky.
O ye lightnings with golden rims, no one finds your track. O Heaven and Earth, discover this for me.

Indeed, for the sake of wealth, the seeker of wealth approaches; the wife unites with her husband. They both bestow virile vigor; having given over the milk, she milks out the essence. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
O gods, let not that light fall down from heaven; let us never be deprived of the blissful Soma. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
I ask about the lowest sacrifice; let that messenger proclaim it. Where has the ancient *ṛta* gone? Who maintains it now? O Heaven and Earth, find this out for me.
O you gods who abide in the three luminous realms of heaven—what for you is the right, and what is the wrong? Where is your ancient oblation? Discern this for me, O Heaven and Earth!
What is the support of the Eternal Order? What is the gaze of Varuṇa?
How may we, O Heaven and Earth, avoid stepping upon the path of the great Aryaman and the evil-minded? Be aware of this for me.
I am he who, in the past, spoke various words when the soma was pressed.
Desires pursue me, as a wolf pursues a thirsty deer; O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
My ribs pain me on all sides like rival wives;
my testicles gnaw at me like rats. O Śatakratu, you devour your praiser. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
Those seven rays which exist—therein my navel is extended. Trita, the son of Āptya, knows that; he proclaims it out of kinship. O Heaven and Earth, bear witness to this for me!
Those five bulls who stand in the midst of the great heaven—to be proclaimed among the gods, they have turned together toward one goal; O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
These well-winged ones sit in the midst of the ascent of heaven;
they ward off the wolf from the paths as it crosses the swift waters. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
This is a new, praiseworthy, and well-proclaimed hymn, O Gods;
the rivers flow according to *ṛta*, and Sūrya has spread out the truth. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
O Agni, that kinship of yours which is worthy of praise exists among the gods.
Seated like a man, sacrifice to the gods for us—you who are most wise. Take note of this, O Heaven and Earth!
Seated like a man, the Hotṛ priest, most wise, goes forth toward the gods;
Agni, the god among the gods, the sage, prepares the oblations. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
Varuṇa, the priest, makes [the path] one who knows the way; we entreat him.
He unfolds the thought from the heart; may a new [insight] be born. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this truth for me.
That path of the Sun which has been made manifest in heaven—O gods, mortals do not overstep it; you do not see it. O Heaven and Earth, bear witness to this for me!
Trita, cast down into the well, called upon the gods for help;
Bṛhaspati heard that, making wide room from distress. Hear this of mine, O Heaven and Earth!
A ruddy wolf indeed saw me once as I was going along the path;
having observed me, he has risen up like a carpenter with a back-ache. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
Through this hymn of praise, may we, accompanied by Indra and with all our heroes, prevail in the struggle.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
We invoke Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni, the host of Maruts, and Aditi for our protection.
O Vasus, bounteous givers, deliver us from all distress as one delivers a chariot from a difficult pass.
O Ādityas, come hither for our complete well-being; O gods, be our benefactors in the battles against Vṛtra.
Like a chariot from a difficult pass, O Vasus, you who are bounteous givers, deliver us out of every distress.
May the Pitṛs, worthy of our praise, and the two goddesses, mothers of the gods and increasers of Cosmic Order, protect us.
Like a chariot from a difficult pass, O Vasus, you bounteous givers, deliver us from every distress.
Seeking strength, we here implore Narāśaṃsa, the prize-winner, and Pūṣan, the lord of heroes, with our prayers for favor.
Like a chariot from a difficult pass, O Vasus, you bounteous givers, rescue us from every distress.
O Bṛhaspati, always make for us an easy path; we beg for that which is auspicious and beneficial, established by Manu.
Like a chariot from a difficult pass, O Vasus, you who are liberal givers, deliver us from every distress.
Kutsa, the seer, pressed down in the pit, called upon Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra and lord of power, for aid.
O bounteous Vasus, deliver us from all distress, as one delivers a chariot from a difficult pass.
May the goddess Aditi protect us with the gods; may the god Trātṛ protect us, never failing.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
The sacrifice goes forth toward the favor of the gods; O Ādityas, be gracious. May your benevolence turn hitherward, which finds wider space even from out of distress.
May the gods come to us with their protection, being praised by the Sāmans of the Aṅgirases;
may Indra with his powers, the Maruts with the Maruts, and Aditi with the Ādityas grant us shelter.
May Indra grant us this, may Varuṇa, Agni, Aryaman, and Savitar find it pleasing;
may Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven bestow this upon us.
O Indra and Agni, that most wonderful chariot of yours which looks upon all beings—
mounted upon it, come together on the same car, and then drink of the pressed soma.
As vast as this entire world exists— wide-reaching in its extent and profound—
so great let this Soma be for your drinking, O Indra and Agni, sufficient for your minds.
For you two have made for yourselves a blessed name in common; O slayers of Vṛtra, you are indeed united.
Therefore, O Indra and Agni, sitting together as the two bulls, rain down the bull-like Soma.
When the fires are kindled, having anointed yourselves and extended the sacrificial grass with uplifted ladles,
come hither, O Indra and Agni, for our goodwill, after the sharp Soma juices have been poured around.
O Indra and Agni, those heroic deeds which you have performed, those forms and powers as well—
by virtue of those ancient and auspicious friendships of yours, drink of the pressed Soma.
When I first spoke to you two while choosing, saying, "This Soma is to be invoked by us against the Asuras," come indeed toward that true faith; then drink of the pressed Soma.
O Indra and Agni, if you rejoice in your own dwelling, or with a priest or a king, O worshipful ones, come hither from there, O bulls; then drink of the pressed soma.
O Indra and Agni, whether you are among the Yadus, the Turvaśas, the Druhyus, the Anus,
or the Pūrus— come hither from there, O bulls, and drink of this pressed soma.
O Indra and Agni, whether you are in the lowest earth, the middle one, or even the highest, come hither from there, O showerers of blessings; then drink of the pressed Soma.
O Indra and Agni, whether you are in the highest earth, in the middle one, or even in the lowest, come hither from there, O bulls; then drink of the pressed Soma.
O Indra and Agni, whether you are stationed in heaven, on earth, or among the mountains, in the plants, or in the waters—from there, O bulls, come hither; then drink of the pressed Soma.
O Indra and Agni, when you rejoice according to your own nature at the rising of the sun and in the midst of heaven, come hither from there, O showerers of blessings; then drink of the pressed soma.
Thus, O Indra and Agni, having drunk of the pressed juice, win for us all treasures.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us.

For I have looked with my mind, O Indra and Agni, desiring what is better—whether kinsmen or fellow-clansmen; there is no other youthful providence for me than you two. Therefore, I have fashioned this hymn that strives for strength.
For I have heard that you two are more liberal givers than a father-in-law or even a brother-in-law;
therefore, O Indra and Agni, as the Soma is offered to you, I generate a new hymn of praise.
"May we not sever the reins," thus they pray, while following the powers of the fathers;
for Indra and Agni, the bulls rejoice, for those two stones are in the lap of the Dhiṣaṇā.
For you two, O Indra and Agni, the goddess Dhiṣaṇā, desiring it for your exhilaration, presses the Soma.
O Aśvins, you who have auspicious hands and fair palms, hasten hither; mingle [the draught] with honey in the waters.
O Indra and Agni, I have heard that you two are most powerful in the distribution of wealth and in the slaying of Vṛtra;
therefore, having seated yourselves upon the sacrificial grass at this sacrifice, O leaders of men, rejoice in the pressed soma.
You two surpass all people in the calls to battle; you two exceed both the earth and the heavens in greatness.
You two surpass the rivers and the mountains in majesty; O Indra and Agni, you two transcend all other beings.
Bring hither, bestow your gifts, O you whose arms wield the thunderbolt; O Indra and Agni, protect us with your powers.
These indeed are the rays of the Sun, by which our fathers attained kinship.
O Purandaras, wielders of the thunderbolt, grant us aid; O Indra and Agni, protect us in battles!
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us.
That work of mine was performed, and it is performed again; the sweetest prayer is recited for the hymn of praise.
This ocean here belongs to all the gods; O Ṛbhus, satisfy yourselves with that which has been consecrated with the cry of Svāhā!
When they went forth seeking enjoyment, some of my kinsmen turned westward while others turned eastward;
O sons of Sudhanvan, you arrived at the house of the liberal Sāvitr with the fullness of your journey.
May Savitar speed you toward immortality, since you have come seeking to be heard, unhidden. That very drinking-cup of the Asura, which was but one, you made fourfold.
Having performed their work with skill and swiftness, the Ṛbhus, though being mortals, attained immortality as priests;
the Ṛbhus, sons of Sudhanvan, who possess the vision of the sun, were united with their sacred thoughts within the year.
Like a field, the Ṛbhus measured out with a measuring-stick the single, quivering vessel;
praised with hymns, seeking the highest, they strove for glory among the immortals.
With wisdom, let us offer our inspired thought to the heroes of the mid-air, like clarified butter poured from a ladle.
The *Ṛbhus*, who by their skillful crossing followed this Father, have ascended to the realm of heaven for the sake of booty.
R̥bhu is Indra by his might, most recent; R̥bhu is the giver of wealth with riches and treasures.
O gods, through your protection on the day of our joy, may we overcome the hostilities of those who do not press the Soma.
O Ṛbhus, you fashioned the cow from the hide; you reunited the mother with her calf. O sons of Sudhanvan, by your skillful craftsmanship, you made your aged parents young again.
With strengths, aid us in the winning of booty; O Indra, rich in *ṛbhus*, bestow upon us wondrous wealth.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us abundantly.
The R̥bhus, whose works are performed with wisdom, fashioned the well-rolling chariot; they fashioned the two bay steeds that carry Indra, rich in virile wealth.
The R̥bhus fashioned vital strength for their parents; they fashioned for the calf a mother who was to accompany it.

Fashion for our sacrifice a vital strength endowed with skill; grant us nourishment accompanied by good progeny for wisdom and capability, so that we may dwell with a clan consisting entirely of heroes. Bestow upon our host that very power of yours.

O R̥bhus, fashion for us the means of victory; O heroes, fashion the means of victory for our chariot and the means of victory for our steed. May you always grant us victorious power, a force that overcomes both kin and stranger in battles.
I invoke Indra, the lord of the *Ṛbhus*, for our protection; the *Ṛbhus*, the *Vājas*, and the *Maruts* for the drinking of the Soma.
May both Mitra and Varuṇa, and now the Aśvins, impel us toward gain, toward prayer, and toward victory.
May Ṛbhu sharpen our gain for the sake of the prize; may Vāja, the winner in battle, protect us. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us.
I praise Heaven and Earth for the first thought, Agni, the Gharma, and the brilliant light for the journey and for the sacrifice.
With those aids wherewith you quicken the prize-winning chariot for the sake of the portion, with those very aids come hither, O Aśvins!
To give you gifts, the well-prepared, inexhaustible [offerings] have mounted upon your chariot, as if for the sake of thought, so that it may be mindful.
With those aids by which you protect our prayers for the successful performance of the rite—come hither with those very aids, O Aśvins!
By your power, you two rule over those divine clans under the command of immortality;
O heroes, with those aids wherewith you cause the barren cow to swell, come hither to us, O Aśvins, with those very succors.
With those [powers] by which Parijman, through the greatness of his offspring, and the son of two mothers, swift among the swift, displays his splendor;
with those by which Trimantu became far-sighted—with those excellent aids, O Aśvins, come hither!
With those [powers] by which you caused Rebha, who was bound and confined within the waters, and Vandana, to emerge so that he might behold the sun;
with those [powers] by which you protected Kaṇva as he strove to win—come hither, O Aśvins, with those very aids!
With those unerring aids wherewith you quickened the weary Antaka in the conflict, and wherewith you revived Bhujyu,
and wherewith you strengthened Karkandhu and Vayya— with those very succors, O Aśvins, come hither to us.
With those aids by which you [granted] Śucanti, the winner of wealth and worthy of fair praise, the heated *gharma* oblation full of refreshment for Atri;
with those aids by which you protected Pṛśnigu and Purukutsa—with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither to us.
With those powers by which, O bulls, you enabled the blind man and the cripple to see and walk;
with those [powers] by which you released the swallowed quail—come hither, O Aśvins, with those very aids!
With those aids by which you made the Sindhu honey-sweet and inexhaustible, with which you, O ageless ones, quickened Vasiṣṭha,
and with which you protected Kutsa, Śrutarya, and Narya— with those very succors, O Aśvins, come hither to us.

With those aids by which you quickened Viśpalā, the winner of wealth, who was healed by Atharvan, when she had been cast down a thousandfold in the race; with those aids by which you protected Vaśa Aśvya and Preṇi—come hither, O Aśvins, with those very succors.
With those aids by which, O bounteous ones, the vessel of honey flowed for the merchant Dīrghaśravas, the son of Uśij;
with those aids by which you protected Kakṣīvat, your praiser—come hither, O Aśvins, with those excellent succors!
With those [powers] by which you made the Rasā river swell with the flood of food, with which you helped the horseless chariot to victory,
and with which Triśoka drove out the cows— with those excellent aids, O Aśvins, come hither!
With those [helps] by which you went around the sun in the distance, and protected Mandhātṛ in his lordships over the lands;
with those by which you helped the sage Bharadvāja—come hither, O Aśvins, with those excellent aids.
With those aids by which you protected the great Atithigva, Kaśoju, and Divodāsa in the slaying of Śambara;
with those aids by which you protected Trasadasyu in the breaking of the forts—with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither to us.
With those [aids] by which you honored Vamra when he was drinking deeply and receiving praise, with which you favored Kali who had won his wife,
and with which you protected Vyaśva and Pṛthi— with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither to us.
With those aids wherewith you, O Heroes, found a path for Śayu, for Atri, and for Manu in the past;
with those wherewith you struck down the arrows for Syūmaraśmi—come hither, O Aśvins, with those very succors.
With those [powers] by which Paṭharvā blazed forth through the greatness of his belly, like Agni piled up and kindled on his course;
with those by which you protected Śaryāta in the great contest for wealth—with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither to us!
With those [powers] by which, O Aṅgiras, you two went forth in spirit and reached the front in the opening of the flood of cattle;
with those [powers] by which you aided the heroic Manu with nourishment—with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither!
With those [powers] by which you brought home wives for Vimada, or with which you bestowed the ruddy cows,
and with which you granted Sudās the favor of good gods— with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither to us!
With those aids by which you become sources of peace for the donor, with which you protect Bhujyu, and with which you protect Adhrigu—
with those most gracious and well-sustaining aids, O Aśvins, who praise the Truth, come hither to us.
With those aids wherewith you honored Kṛśānu at the throw of the die, and wherewith you helped the young man’s steed in the race;
with those aids wherewith you bring dear honey to the bees—come hither, O Aśvins, with those very succors.
With those aids wherewith you quicken the man who fights for cattle in the contest of men, and assist him in winning the field and in obtaining offspring;
with those aids wherewith you protect chariots and wherewith you protect the coursers—with those very succors come hither, O Aśvins!
With those aids by which you, O Śatakratus, protected Kutsa, the son of Arjuni, and furthered Turvīti and Dabhīti;
with those aids by which you protected Dhvasanti and Puruṣanti—with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither to us.

O Aśvins, make our speech effective; O wonder-workers, bulls, fulfill this prayer of ours. In this non-gambling [contest], I invoke you both for protection; be present for our increase and for the winning of the prize.
O Aśvins, protect us day and night with unimpaired blessings of well-being.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us.
This most excellent light among lights has come; the bright, far-reaching signal has been born.
Just as she was impelled for the impulse of Savitṛ, even so has Night yielded her womb to Uṣas.
Bright with her radiant calf, the shining one has come; the dark one has entered her dwellings.
Of common kinship, immortal, following one after the other, the two heavens move along, wearing away their color.

Common is the path of the two sisters, endless; taught by the gods, they travel it one after the other. They do not clash, nor do they stand still; well-established, Night and Dawn are of one mind, though diverse in form.

Radiant leader of true blessings, the wondrous one has been perceived; she has thrown open the doors for us. Stretching forth the world, she has revealed wealth to us; Dawn has awakened all living beings.

O Bounteous One, for the crooked-eyed one to move, for enjoyment, for sacrifice, and for wealth— for those who see but little, you have awakened all beings far and wide with your broad vision, O Uṣas.
For dominion you [have awakened], for glory you, for greatness; for sacrifice you, for wealth as it were, for movement you.
Beholding diverse ways of life, Dawn has awakened all beings.
This daughter of heaven has appeared, shining forth, a young woman clothed in radiant garments.
O Uṣas, sovereign lady of all earthly wealth, shine forth here today, O auspicious one!
She follows the path of those who have departed and is the first of the endless mornings yet to come. Dawn, shining forth, stirs the living, though she awakens no one who is dead.
O Uṣas, that you have caused Agni to be kindled, that you have shone forth with the eye of Sūrya,
and that you have awakened the men who intend to sacrifice— that you have performed a blessed service among the gods.
How great is that which shall be when she has come together with those that have shone forth and those that shall now shine?
Yearning for the former ones, she laments; reflecting, she goes gladly with the others.
Those mortals who went before and beheld the Dawn as she shone forth have passed away;
now she has become visible to us, and those who shall behold her in future ages will likewise depart.
Driving away enemies, guardian of the cosmic order (*ṛta*), born of the cosmic order, bestowing favor, and sending forth pleasant truths—
O Dawn, most auspicious, bringing the feast for the gods, shine forth here today as the most excellent.
Again and again the goddess has shone forth from the east; and so today, the wealthy one, she has shone here.
And so she shall shine through future days as well; undecaying and immortal, she moves by her own inherent powers.
With her bright ornaments she has shone across the expanse of heaven; the goddess has cast off her black garment. Awakening all, Dawn approaches on her well-yoked chariot with her ruddy horses.
Bringing nourishing and desirable boons, she displays a wondrous banner as she shines forth with intelligence.
The first of the eternal dawns that have passed away, Uṣas has shone brightly as she breaks forth.
Arise! The living breath has come to us; darkness has departed and light approaches.
She has cleared a path for Sūryā to travel; we have arrived where they prolong our lifespan.
Like a weaver with his shuttle, the singer, being praised, raises up his voice for the shining Dawns.
O bounteous one, shine forth that [light] today for the one who praises you; bestow upon us a life rich in progeny.

Those Dawns which shine forth for the mortal donor, rich in cattle and possessing all heroes—may the presser of Soma attain them at the rising of true blessings, like the outpouring of Vāyu’s breath; may he obtain them as givers of horses.
Mother of the gods, the face of Aditi, the banner of sacrifice, O Great One, shine forth!
Bringing praise to our sacred prayer, dawn upon us; O possessor of all boons, bring us to the people.
Whatever wonderful wealth the Dawns bring as a gift— auspicious for the one who has sacrificed and performed his labor—
may Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant that to us.
We offer these prayers to Rudra, the powerful one with matted hair, the lord of heroes,
so that there may be well-being for our bipeds and quadrupeds, and so that everything in this village may be nourished and free from disease.
Be gracious to us, O Rudra, and grant us joy; we shall worship you with homage, O Lord of heroes.
Whatever blessing and prosperity our father Manu won through sacrifice, may we attain that under your guidance, O Rudra.
May we obtain your favor through the sacrifice to the gods, O bounteous Rudra, ruler of heroes;
coming to us with goodwill, approach our people, and may we, with our heroes unharmed, offer the oblation to you.
We invoke for our protection the brilliant Rudra, the fulfiller of sacrifice, the swift one, the seer;
may he cast far from us the divine wrath, for we choose only his goodwill.

With reverence we invoke the ruddy boar of heaven, the one with braided hair, the brilliant form. May he, bearing in his hand the most excellent medicines, grant us protection, armor, and a secure dwelling.

This speech, sweeter than the sweet, is spoken for the father of the Maruts, for the strengthening of Rudra. And grant us, O Immortal One, the food of mortals; be gracious to ourselves, to our children, and to our descendants.
Do not harm our great ones, nor our small ones; do not harm our growing ones, nor those already grown.
Do not slay our father, nor our mother; O Rudra, do not injure our dear bodies.
Do not harm us in our children or grandchildren, nor in our own lives; do not harm us in our cattle or our horses.
O Rudra, do not slay our heroes in your wrath. Bearing oblations, we invoke you forever.

Like a herdsman, I have brought these hymns of praise near to you; O Father of the Maruts, grant us your favor. For your benevolence is auspicious and most compassionate; therefore, we choose only your protection.
Far from us be your cow-slaying bolt and your man-slaying bolt, O Lord of Heroes; let your favor be with us.
Be gracious to us, speak for us, O God, and grant us protection, you who are doubly mighty.
Seeking aid, we have uttered our homage to him; may Rudra, accompanied by the Maruts, hear our call.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
The brilliant face of the gods has risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni.
Sūrya, the soul of all that moves and stands, has filled the heaven, the earth, and the mid-air.
Sūrya follows after the radiant goddess Uṣas, as a youth approaches a maiden;
there, where men seeking the gods extend their generations toward the auspicious for the sake of good fortune.
The auspicious horses of the Sun—the bay, the dappled, the variegated, the swift—are worthy of our praise;
paying homage, they have ascended to the back of heaven and traverse heaven and earth in an instant.

That is the divinity of Sūrya, that is his greatness: in the midst of his work, he withdraws what was spread out. When he has unyoked his bay steeds from their station, then Night spreads her garment over all.
In the lap of heaven, Sūrya assumes that form of Mitra and Varuṇa for all to behold;
one part of his radiant power is endless and white, while the other is black, which the coursers bring together.
O gods, at the rising of the sun this day, deliver us from distress and from reproach!
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this!

To the two Nāsatyas I spread forth my hymns as one spreads the sacrificial grass; I send them out like the wind driving the clouds. They, on their swift chariot, brought back a wife for the young Vimada by means of their powerful vehicle.
Whether by means of strong-winged, swift-gliding [birds], or by the impulses of the gods,
exulting in his strength, the donkey, O Nāsatyas, won a thousand in the race at the prize-contest of Yama.
Tugra indeed abandoned Bhujyu in the cloudless rain, like one who has died leaving behind his wealth;
you carried him away with self-propelled ships that glide through the mid-air and exclude the waters.
O Nāsatyas, with winged steeds passing over three nights and three days,
you carried Bhujyu across the ocean, on the far shore of the moist desert, by means of three chariots having a hundred feet and six horses.
In the supportless, placeless, and ungraspable ocean,
you two displayed your heroism, O Aśvins, when you carried Bhujyu home, who had boarded a ship equipped with a hundred oars.
That white horse which you two, O Aśvins, gave to Aghāśva as perpetual well-being—that great gift of yours is worthy of high praise; that Pedu’s steed is ever to be invoked by the noble man.
O Heroes, for Kakṣīvat, the son of Pajra who praises you, you dug out abundant wealth;
from the hoof of the stallion horse at the straining-vessel, you poured out a hundred jars of *surā* liquor.
With snow you warded off the scorching heat from Agni; you bestowed upon him nourishing food rich in milk.
O Aśvins, you brought forth Atri, who had been cast into the pit, together with all his followers, in safety.
O Nāsatyas, you raised up from afar that well with its bottom turned upward and its opening tilted;
you made the waters flow for the drinking of Gotama, who was parched with thirst, so that he might obtain wealth by the thousands.
O Nāsatyas, you stripped away the aged skin from Cyavāna like a garment, as he grew old;
O wonder-workers, you prolonged the life of the abandoned man and made him the husband of young maidens.
O Nāsatyas, that praiseworthy and effective protection of yours, which brings desired aid—
since you, O wise ones, like a hidden treasure, brought it forth from the depths for Vandana to behold.
O Heroes, I make manifest that fierce deed of yours for the sake of gain, like thunder making rain manifest,
since Dadhyañc Ātharvaṇa, with the head of a horse, proclaimed to you the honeyed secret.
O Nāsatyas, you who possess many enjoyments, Purandhi invoked you both for the great journey;
hear that, O Aśvins, as you did for Śasu, the wife of Vadhrimatī, when you gave her a son with golden hands.
O Heroes, O Nāsatyas, you released the quail from the jaws of the wolf in the encounter;
and you, O lords of many enjoyments, made the lamenting seer see clearly once more.
For in the contest for the prize, you cut off the leg like the wing of a bird;
instantly, you fitted an iron leg for Viśpalā so that she might run when the wealth was at stake.

To him who had carved out a hundred rams for the she-wolf, R̥jrāśva’s father made him blind. For him, O Nāsatyas, you two, the wonder-workers and physicians, bestowed eyes that see clearly, O matchless ones.
The daughter of Sūrya mounted your chariot, as a mare wins with her steed;
all the gods approved it in their hearts, and you, O Nāsatyas, are united with splendor.
When you two, O Aśvins, hastening, went on your circuit for Divodāsa Bharadvāja, your accompanying chariot brought wealth; a bull and a porpoise were yoked to it.
O Nāsatyas, bringing wealth with good dominion, offspring, long life, and heroic strength,
you came together with vigor to the daughter of Jahnu, who offered you a portion three times a day.

Jāhuṣa was besieged on all sides; you two carried him away by easy paths through the regions of space at night. O Nāsatyas, with your piercing chariot, you two who do not age, traversed the mountains.
From one dwelling you two brought Vaśa to the battle for the Aśvins to win thousands;
together with Indra, O bulls, you drove away misfortune and the hostilities of Pṛthuśravas.

Even for Śara Ārcatka, you brought down from the heights the waters that were below, so that he might drink. O Nāsatyas, by your powers, you made the barren cow swell with milk for the exhausted Śayu.
O Nāsatyas, by your wondrous powers,
you restored Viṣṇāpū to Viśvaka, who was seeking your aid, offering praise, and acting with integrity, so that he might see him again like a lost animal.
For ten nights and nine days, Rebha was bound and pierced within the waters;
you two drew him out, like Soma with a ladle, from the water in which he had been cast down and submerged.
I have proclaimed your wondrous deeds, O Aśvins; may I be the master of this [wealth], possessing good cattle and brave sons.
And beholding and attaining long life, may I reach old age as if returning home.
O Aśvins, the ancient Hotṛ priest invites you both for the exhilaration of the sweet Soma;
the sacrificial grass is spread, the gift is distributed, and the song is offered—come hither, O Nāsatyas, with nourishment and with strengths.
O Aśvins, that chariot of yours, swifter than thought, drawn by noble horses, which comes to the people—
the one by which you go to the dwelling of the righteous— come to us on that path, O heroes!
O Heroes, you released the seer Atri, who belongs to the five peoples, from the narrow pit and from distress with your host;
destroying the magic powers of the malevolent Dasyu, O Bulls, you urged him forward in succession.

Like a horse hidden by the wicked, O Aśvins, you two heroes, O bulls, rescued the seer Rebha from the waters; you restored him with your wondrous deeds when he was shattered. Your ancient exploits do not grow old.
Like one who has fallen asleep in the lap of Destruction, or like the sun dwelling in darkness, O wonder-workers,
you two Aśvins raised up Vandana for glory— him who was like a brilliant golden ornament buried in the earth, beautiful to behold.

O Nāsatyas, O heroes, that deed of yours was worthy of praise by Kakṣīvat, the son of Pajra, as you traveled around; from the hoof of a swift horse, you poured out for the people a hundred jars of honeyed mead.
O Heroes, you gave Viṣṇāpū to Viśvaka, the son of Kṛṣṇa, who praised you.
O Aśvins, you gave a husband even to Ghōṣā, who was growing old in her father’s house and longing for one.
O Aśvins, you gave a radiant [maiden] to Śyāva, and to Kaṇva, the descendant of Mahat Kṣoṇa;
that deed of yours, O bulls, is worthy of proclamation, that you bestowed glory upon the son of Nṛṣad.
Assuming many forms, O Aśvins, you brought the swift horse to Pedu—
a steed that wins thousands, invincible, slaying the serpent, worthy of renown, and a conqueror.
These glorious deeds of yours, O bounteous givers, are the prayer, the hymn of praise, and the dwelling place between the two worlds;
since the Pajras invoke you, O Aśvins, come with nourishment and bring strength to the wise man.
O Aśvins, being praised by the son’s hymn, you who are swift and bestow strength upon the sage;
having grown mighty through the prayer of Agastya, O Nāsatyas, you restored Viśpalā.
Where were you two going when you found the fair praise of Kāvya, O sons of Heaven, mighty ones, in his dwelling?
Like a buried jar of gold, O Aśvins, you raised him up on the tenth day.
O Aśvins, by your powers you made Cyavāna, who was growing old, young again; O Nāsatyas, the daughter of Sūrya chose your chariot along with splendor.
O youthful ones, you two became mindful again for Tugra through your ancient ways;
you two carried Bhujyu out from the ocean, from the midst of the waters, with winged, ruddy horses.
The son of Tugra called upon you, O Aśvins, having been cast into the sea yet remaining unshaken;
you brought him out safely with your well-yoked chariot, swift as thought, O mighty ones.
The quail invoked you, O Aśvins, when you released her from the jaws of the wolf;
with your victorious chariot you traversed the ridges of the mountain, and you slew Jātaviṣvāc with poison.

To him who offered a hundred rams to the she-wolf, and was led away into darkness by his malevolent father—O Aśvins, you restored the two white-eyed ones to Ṛjrāśva; you provided light for the blind so that he might see.
"Success! For the blind man, O Aśvins, bulls among heroes, she the she-wolf called out, 'O men!
Like a youthful lover who carves up his food, R̥jrāśva [offered] one hundred and one rams."
Great is your aid, O Aśvins, bringing bliss; you heal even the cripple, O wise ones.
Therefore Purandhi has called upon you both; come to her with your protections, O bulls.
O Aśvins, wonder-workers, you made swell the barren, milkless cow that was bound for Śayu;
by your powers, you brought home the wife of Purumitra, the daughter of Vimada.
O Aśvins, wonder-workers, you sow barley with the wolf, milking nourishment for mankind;
blowing away the Dasyu with the *bakura* wind, you have created vast light for the Ārya.

O Aśvins, for Dadhyañc the son of Atharvan, you restored the horse's head. He, observing the cosmic order (*ṛta*), proclaimed to you both the honey—the Tvaṣṭṛ-made secret that was hidden within your armpits, O wonder-workers (*dasrau*).
O Sages, I ever desire your favor; O Aśvins, further all my prayers.
O Nāsatyas, bestow upon us vast wealth, renowned and accompanied by offspring.
O Aśvins, bestowing gifts, you gave a son with golden hands to Vadhrimatī, O heroes; O bounteous givers, you raised up Śyāva, who had been cut into three pieces, so that he might live.
O Aśvins, these heroic deeds of yours, performed in the past, the Āyus have proclaimed.
Performing sacred prayer for you two, O bulls, may we, possessing noble heroes, speak at the assembly.
O Aśvins, may your chariot, winged like a falcon, most gracious and self-reliant, come hither—
your chariot which is swifter than the mind of a mortal, three-seated, O Bulls, and possessing the speed of the wind.
Come hither on your well-rolling, three-wheeled chariot, triple-seated and threefold;
swell our cows, quicken our horses, and, O Aśvins, increase the hero among us.
O wonder-workers, on your well-rolling chariot that moves forward, hear this song from the pressing-stone!
Why indeed do the ancient sages say that you, O Aśvins, are the ones most ready to turn back toward us?
O Aśvins, let the falcons carry you both on the chariot—swift, winged steeds yoked thereto;
those who cross the waters like divine eagles, bringing nourishment, O Nāsatyas.
May the youthful daughter of Sūrya ascend your chariot here, O heroes, having found favor with you. May your beautiful, winged steeds, the ruddy birds, carry you both forward in the encounter.
By your wondrous deeds, O wonder-workers, you raised up Vandana; by your powers, O mighty ones, you raised up Rebha.
You brought Tugrya out from the ocean, and you made Cyavāna young again.
O Aśvins, you bestowed nourishing strength and protection upon Atri when he was cast into the heated pit;
you restored sight to Kaṇva, who had been robbed of it, accepting his beautiful hymn of praise.
O Aśvins, you caused the cow to swell for the ancient Śayu who had petitioned you;
you released the quail from distress, and you restored the leg of Viśpalā.
O Aśvins, you two gave to Pedu the white horse, impelled by Indra, the slayer of the serpent—
a steed to be loudly invoked, the overcomer of the enemy, fierce, winning thousands, virile, and firm-limbed.
O well-born heroes, we, imploring you for aid, call upon you both, O Aśvins.
Come to us with your chariot laden with wealth, graciously accepting our songs for our prosperity.
Come to us with the fresh speed of a hawk, O Nāsatyas, acting in harmony;
for I, having offered oblations, call upon you both at the dawning of every most recent dawn, O Aśvins.

I call hither for life your wondrous, mind-swift chariot, drawn by vigorous horses, worthy of sacrifice; that chariot with its thousand banners, rich in wood, possessing a hundred treasures, obedient, and bestowing wide space, toward the offerings.
The prayer has been directed upward at his approach; the quarters of heaven have come together for the praise.
I prepare the hot offering; the aids come toward it. O Aśvins, Urjānī has mounted your chariot.
When they have come together, vying with one another, the vigorous and immeasurable conquerors for glory in the fray—
then your chariot, O Aśvins, is made manifest on the slope as you bear the patron to his choice.

You two went with your self-yoked birds to Bhujyu as he was sinking, carrying him back to his ancestors. O Bulls, you traveled to the dwelling that was to be sought; for Divodāsa, your great protection was renowned.

O Aśvins, for the sake of beauty, the two voices have guided toward you your own yoked chariot, which is full of vigor. Having come to you for friendship, the noble maiden chose you both as her husbands, she who possesses the power of flight.
You rescued Rebha from his confinement; you quenched with cold the heat that had scorched Atri.
You caused the cow of Śayu to swell with nourishment, and Vandana was made to cross over to a long life.
O Wonder-Workers (dasrā), you restored Vandana, who was seized by old age, as craftsmen repair a chariot;
through your inspired praise, you brought forth the sage from the earth. May your wondrous deed manifest here for the one who honors you.

You two came to him who was lamenting in the distance, oppressed by the abandonment of his own father. From here, your aids were full of light; indeed, your wondrous assistances were present for help in the encounter.
And for you two, this honeyed [drink] the bee has hummed; in the exhilaration of Soma, the son of Uśij calls out.
You two won over the mind of Dadhyac, and then the horse's head spoke to you.
O Aśvins, you bestowed upon Pedu the white horse, the granter of many boons, the overcomer of enemies;
a steed shining with arrows, invincible in battles, worthy of praise, and subduing the people like Indra.
Which oblation will be successful for you, O Aśvins? Or what is pleasing to both of you?
How can one who lacks wisdom perform the ritual service?
The two wise ones indeed may ask about the doors; the other, the ignorant and witless one, truly does not know at all—never even for a moment among mortals.
Knowing this, we invoke you two; as those who know, may you two declare our prayer today.
The one devoted to you, seeking to win favor, has raised his voice in praise.
I ask the gods with simple sincerity about the wondrous oblation consecrated by the *vaṣaṭ* call, O wonder-workers:
protect us from the stronger foe and guard us from the more violent.
The speech which shines forth like [the song] of Ghoṣa Bhr̥gavāṇa, with which the son of Pajra worships you both— may that speech be directed forward by one who knows, like a messenger.
I have heard the Gāyatra hymn of Takavāna; for I have indeed sung praises to you both, O Aśvins.
O Lords of Splendor, look upon us with your eyes.
For you two were present at great contests, or when you two brought forth [the prize];
as such, O Vasus, be our good protectors; protect us from the wolf, from the one who intends evil.
Do not deliver us over to any enemy; let not the milch-cows depart from our houses anywhere, even those that yield milk for the suckling calves without their mothers being present.
May they yield milk for our alliance with you; may you two measure out for us wealth consisting of booty, and may you measure out for us nourishment consisting of milch-cows.
The chariot of the Aśvins, which is without horses yet possesses steeds, is a weapon;
with that, I have great delight.
This chariot, easy to drive, shall carry me along with the people to the drinking of Soma.
Now, let there be no knowledge of sleep nor of the wealthy man who does not enjoy; both of these perish at dawn.

When will he, hastening, hear the songs of the Aṅgirases—those men who are devoted to the gods as their vessel? When the worshipful one has reached the people of the house, he strides widely at the sacrifice.
He propped up the sky and sprinkled the foundation; as a *Ṛbhu*, he bestowed wealth upon the hero for the sake of strength.
The buffalo gazed upon his own kin, the cow; he beheld the mare as the mother of the horse and the cow.
May the ruddy Dawns reach the ancient call of the sovereign, the swift lord of the Angirases, day after day.
He fashioned the thunderbolt and harnessed the team; he propped up the sky for the four-footed cattle and for the two-footed human being.
In his exhilaration, he gave forth the resonant, hidden face of the cows for the sake of Truth;
when the three-peaked one turned back at the onset, he threw open the doors of the human oppressors.
For you, O possessor of noble seed, the two parents brought milk as a gift when they were hurrying in their zeal;
they offered to you that pure wealth, the milk of the prolific, ever-yielding cow.
Then he has been born; may the swift one exhilarate himself. He has shone forth like the sun from this dawn.
The drop, with which [the sacrificers] who offer sweat as their oblation have reached it, flows with the ladle, pouring toward the ancient abodes.
When the wood-pile, well-fueled, performs its work at the sacrifice, the Sun [releases] the enclosures of the cow;
when you shine through the days for the sake of the one who acts with skill, for the swift one who desires cattle and seeks to reach them.
From the great heaven, bring hither the two bay steeds that win the light; as one who fights for the spring, draw forth the well.
When they have pressed with stones the exhilarating, golden-hued draught for your increase—the juice that is impetuous like a bull and stirred by the wind—then come.
O skillful one, you turned back the iron rock brought down from heaven;
where, O much-invoked one, winning for Kutsa, you encompassed Śuṣṇa with endless weapons of death.
When the sun was still hidden from the darkness, O wielder of the stone, you hurled that bolt, the *phaliga*, against him;
you consumed even that power of Śuṣṇa which was invested and firmly bound from heaven.
The two great, wheelless expanses, heaven and earth, rejoiced in your deed, O Indra.
You, with your mighty thunderbolt, struck down Vṛtra as he lay upon the rivers, the boar who obstructed the streams.
O Indra, you who protect men, mount the manly, well-yoked, and most swift steeds of Vāta;
[mount] that exhilarating, Vṛtra-slaying, and decisive thunderbolt which Kāvya Uśanas fashioned for you.
You, O Indra, made the sun’s bay horses rest for the men; Etaśa brought the wheel, as it were.
You cast the ninety-nine navigable rivers across to the further shore, and you rolled back the non-sacrificers into the pit.
O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, protect us from this malevolent assault and from misfortune in the encounter.
Bestow upon us wealth consisting of chariots and horses, for our nourishment, for glory, and for the joy of true prosperity.
O you who are great in strength, let not that benevolence of yours fail us; may they gather together plenteous foods.
O Maghavan, grant us a share of the cattle of the enemy; may we be your most liberal companions at the feast.
O you of swift wrath, bring forward the juice for your drink; present the oblation to the bounteous Rudra.
With the heroes of the Asura of heaven, I have praised the Maruts, who are like those seeking to win the two worlds.
Like two wives eager for the first invocation, Dawn and Night, appearing in many forms, have increased [the sacrifice];
like a barren woman wearing a loose garment, she is beautiful to behold with the golden splendor of the Sun.
May the all-pervading one, who strikes at dawn, exhilarate us; may the wind, the bull of the waters, exhilarate us.
O Indra and Parvata, sharpen our wits for us; may all the gods grant us this wide space.
And those two glorious ones, who enjoy and drink [the offerings], must be invoked by me, the descendant of Uśij, for the sake of white splendor.
Bring forward the Son of the Waters; bring forward the two Parents of the impetuous Āyu.
The son of Uśij shall call upon your roaring one, as Ghoṣa did in the winning of Arjuna’s praise.
I shall proclaim to you, to Pūṣan, for the sake of giving, the wealth-bestowing power of Agni.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, hear my invocation; hear it from every side in this assembly.
May the one who hears us, the one who grants hearing, the one who listens well, and Sindhu with her waters, grant us fair fields.
I praise that gift of yours, O Varuṇa and Mitra: hundreds of cattle bestowed upon the Pajras at the *pṛkṣayāmas*.
Receiving [the gifts] from Śrutaratha and Priyaratha, they have come, immediately securing for themselves abundant prosperity.

I praise the bounty of this one whose wealth is great; may we, together with our brave sons, obtain the gifts of Nahus—the patron who possesses abundant wealth for the Pajras, a benefactor who provides me with horses, chariots, and heroes.
The man who, being a deceiver, pours out the waters for you, O Mitra and Varuṇa, with crooked intent—
himself he lays disease upon his own heart, since he, though observing the cosmic order, has failed to offer oblations.

Impelled by wondrous deeds, he is the subduer of the mighty Nahuṣas; he whose glory is praised among men, the overcomer of hosts, moves with unrestrained speed, ever the hero in all battles, dispensing his bounty.
Then may you two come at the call of the liberal patron, O kings of immortality, you who are delightful;
when you, swift as clouds, bestow your bounty upon the one with the great chariot for the sake of his praise.
"This is the host of that patron," they have said, "at the distribution of the tenfold gift.
May those in whom splendors and riches delight, all of them, win booty in the contests for prizes.
We rejoice in the tenfold nourishment when the twice-five come bearing foods.
Do these masters, with their desired horses and desired reins, urge on the men as conquerors?
The ocean with golden ears and jeweled neck—may all the gods grant us space for that.
May the songs of the noble one, having come instantly, and the dawns, take pleasure in both of us.
Four horses of Maśarśāra’s young son, and three of King Āyavasa, the victorious, carry me.
Your chariot, O Mitra and Varuṇa, with its long-reaching waters and reins as its rays, has shone like the sun.
The chariot of Dakṣiṇā is broad; the immortal gods have yoked it and have mounted it.
From the darkness has she arisen, the noble and far-reaching one, providing guidance for the human dwelling.
Awakened before all the world, the vast one, winning booty and gathering wealth, the youthful Dawn has looked out on high, born again; she has come as the first at the morning invocation.
O goddess Uṣas, nobly born among mortals, when you today distribute a portion to men,
may the divine Savitṛ, the friend of the household, declare us sinless before Sūrya.
Day after day, the Dawn goes toward every house, bestowing her names. Desiring to win, the radiant one has come again and again; she enjoys the very best of all treasures.
Sister of Bhaga, kinswoman of Varuṇa, O Uṣas, true and generous one, be the first to be awakened by our praise!
May he who is the establisher of evil be left behind; may we conquer him with the chariot of the sacrificial gift.
Let the refreshing gifts rise up, let the inspired thoughts arise; the Agnis have risen up, shining brightly.
The radiant Dawns reveal the desirable treasures that were hidden by darkness.
One departs and another arrives; the two days of diverse form move together. One hides the darkness within the enclosure, while Uṣas has shone forth on her brilliantly glowing chariot.
Equal today and likewise equal tomorrow, they follow the long-lasting ordinance of Varuṇa.
Blameless, each one traverses thirty leagues in an instant, encompassing his will.
Knowing the name of the first day, the bright one has been born from the black as the white one;
the maiden of *ṛta* does not violate her laws, coming every day to the appointed place.
Like a maiden displaying her body, O Goddess, you go toward the god who desires to sacrifice;
smiling, a young woman, as you shine forth, you reveal your breasts before him.
Radiant as a maiden groomed by her mother, you reveal your body so that it may be seen.
O auspicious Dawn, shine forth even more widely; no other Dawns have attained what you possess.
Rich in horses, rich in cattle, possessing all desirable things, striving with the rays of the sun,
the Dawns go forth and come back again, bearing auspicious names.
Following the rein of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*), bestow upon us every auspicious intention.
O Dawn, easy to invoke, shine forth for us today; may riches be with us and with our patrons.
As the Dawn shines forth while the fire is kindled, and as the Sun rises, he has spread his light far and wide.
May the god Savitṛ now impel our purpose here, so that bipeds and quadrupeds may go forth.
Not violating the divine ordinances, yet shortening the human generations,
Dawn has shone forth as the foremost of the endless dawns that have passed and of those yet to come.
This daughter of heaven has appeared, clothing herself in light, from the east in her constant course.
She follows the path of *ṛta* perfectly; like one who knows, she does not miss the directions.
The breast of the pure one has been seen, as it were; like Nodhas, she has revealed her dear things.
Like one sitting at the feast, awakening those who sleep, she has come again, the most constant of those who return.
In the eastern half of the unattainable realm, the mother of the cows has raised her banner;
she spreads herself out further and wider, filling both the laps of her parents.
Thus indeed she, most abundant for all to see, spares neither stranger nor kinsman.
Displaying herself with a stainless body, she does not shrink from the small nor from the great as she shines forth.
Like a brotherless woman, she goes toward the men; like one ascending the chariot-seat to win riches, like a longing wife well-attired for her husband, Dawn, like a smiling maiden, bares her bosom.
The sister has yielded her place to her elder sister; she departs from her as if to look back upon her.
Shining forth with the rays of the sun, she anoints herself with ointment like women going to a festival.
Of these former sisters, in the course of days, each later one follows after the earlier;
may those Dawns, newer than the ancient ones, now shine richly upon us with auspicious days.
Awaken, O wealthy Dawn, those who bestow gifts; let the stingy misers sleep on, remaining unawakened.
Shine forth with wealth for the patrons, O bounteous one; shine forth with riches for the singer, O true and joyous one, as you bring us to old age.
The young woman has been seen approaching from the east; she yokes her team of ruddy kine.
Now let her shine forth; her light shall appear. Agni shall attend every single house.
Even the birds have flown up from their dwelling to you at the breaking of dawn, as have the men who partake of food.
O Goddess Dawn, you bring much that is desirable to the mortal who gives offerings and dwells at home.
O Dawn-dawns worthy of praise, you have been lauded by my prayer; you have increased us, O longing ones. O goddesses, through your protection may we win booty consisting of hundreds and thousands.
The early-coming one bestows treasure at dawn; the wise man, having accepted it, lays it aside.
Increasing his offspring and lifespan thereby, he, possessed of brave sons, abides in the abundance of wealth.

May he be rich in cattle, rich in gold, and rich in horses; to him Indra bestows great vital strength— to him who, O *prātaritvan*, as you approach with wealth, seizes you like a bird snatching its prey from the footstep.
Desiring good fortune this morning, I have come today with a wealth-filled chariot, seeking the son of the sacrifice.
Make him drink of the exhilarating juice of Aṃśu; increase the hero who dwells among men with our truthful hymns.
The rivers flow toward him, bringing refreshment; like milch-cows, they approach the one who has sacrificed and the one who is about to sacrifice.
Seeking glory, the streams of clarified butter come from every side to the one who bestows gifts and the one who fulfills them.

He who gives stands supported upon the ridge of the firmament; he indeed goes among the gods. For him the waters and the rivers flow with clarified butter; for him this sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) ever overflows.

These wondrous things belong indeed to those who give sacrificial gifts; in heaven, the suns belong to those who give sacrificial gifts. Those who give sacrificial gifts partake of immortality; those who give sacrificial gifts prolong their life.

Let those who give not fall into misfortune and sin; let not the wise ones, who observe good vows, suffer decay. Let there be someone else as their protection; let sorrows fall upon the one who gives nothing.
With inspired thought, I offer forth unceasing hymns of praise for Bhāvya, who dwells upon the river—
he, the unconquered king, seeking glory, who measured out for me a thousand libations.
A hundred gold coins from the king who entreated me, and a hundred horses presented at once—I have accepted them.
Kakṣīvat [received] a hundred cows from the lord; he has extended his undecaying glory unto heaven.
Ten chariots with yoke-poles and mares, bestowed by Svanaya, have come near to me;
sixty thousand head of cattle followed after them. Kakṣīvat won this at the close of the days.
Forty chestnut horses of Daśaratha lead the procession at the head of a thousand; the Pajras and Kakṣīvat have groomed these coursers that drip with ichor and are adorned with pearls.
Following the ancient impulse, I have received from you three harnessed oxen and eight barren cows;
those well-allied Pajras, like common folk with their wagons, have sought renown.
She who clings and clings all around, who wriggles like a worm;
she, the long-tailed one, grants me hundreds of things to enjoy from the swift steeds.
Come close and touch me; do not think my hairs are few.
I am entirely hairy, like the sheep of the Gandhāris.
I honor Agni as the Hotṛ-priest, the bountiful, the Vasu, the Son of Strength, Jātavedas— the wise one like a sage, Jātavedas— who, a god with a straight rite, with a form directed toward the gods,
desires the radiant glow of clarified butter, of the offered fat that blazes with flame.

We, the sacrificers, invoke you, the most excellent sacrificer, the eldest of the Aṅgirases, O inspired one, with our prayers—O bright one, with the prayers of the inspired. Like the sky encompassing all, you are the Hotṛ-priest of the peoples;
we call upon the flame-haired bull whom these clans shall favor for their impulsion, even as they favor him.

For he, shining with his many-fold radiant power, becomes the subduer of the wicked; like an axe, he is the subduer of the wicked. At whose onset even the firm thing yields like forests when they are struck;
prevailing, he restrains them and leads them away, as one who overcomes the desert leads his way.

Even firm things yield before him, as is well known; with the sharpest kindling-sticks one offers to Agni for his aid, one offers for his aid. He who plunges into many [woods] hews them like forests with his flame;
even solid foods he crushes with his might, even solid things he crushes with his might.
