At dawn, the new chariot has been yoked—the winner, with four poles, three crossbars, and seven reins; ten-wheeled, man-like, and winning the light of heaven, it has become swift through our offerings and prayers.
He is prepared for him at the first, at the second, and also at the third; he is the Hotṛ of man. Others have generated him as the embryo of another; he, the noble bull, unites with others.
I shall now yoke the two bay steeds of Indra to his chariot with a new and well-spoken word, so that he may come.
Let not the many other wise sacrificers detain you here.
O Indra, come with two bay horses, come with four, come with six, being summoned;
come with eight, with ten, to the drinking of the Soma. This [Soma] has been pressed; O you of great deeds, do not neglect it.
Come hither with twenty, with thirty, or with forty bay horses, yoked to your chariot; O Indra, come with fifty, sixty, or seventy well-yoked steeds to the drinking of the Soma.
Come hither with eighty, with ninety, or with a hundred bay horses being borne along;
for this Soma among the Śunahotras has been poured out for you, O Indra, out of love for you, for your exhilaration.
Come toward my prayer, O Indra; yoke both bay horses to the pole of your chariot.
For you have become one to be invoked in many places; O hero, rejoice at this libation.
May my friendship with Indra never fail; may his sacrificial gift yield for us.
Under his highest protection and in his hand, may we be victors in every endeavor.
Surely, O Indra, may that wealthy sacrificial gift of yours yield a boon to the singer;
bestow it upon the praisers so that our fortune does not fail. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly of the wise.
The wise have drunk of this pressed juice for exhilaration, of the nourishing food;
in it Indra, increasing from of old, has made his dwelling, as have the men who offer prayers.
Intoxicated by this mead, Indra, thunderbolt in hand, rent asunder the dragon that encompassed the floods;
when, like birds toward their nests, his refreshments and the offerings of the rivers sped forth.
The mighty Indra, slayer of Ahi, drove the flood of waters toward the ocean;
he generated the sun, found the cattle, and established the ordinances of days by means of night.
Indra bestows many invincible things upon the man who offers gifts; he slays Vṛtra for the donor.
He who has become instantly accessible to men who strive together in the winning of the sun.
Indra, the god, being praised, released the sun for the mortal who presses the juice; when Netaśa, bestowing his portion, brought him wealth that removes reproach, like a share of the sun.
He delivered Śuṣṇa, the insatiable, and Kuyava to his charioteer Kutsa; Indra shattered ninety-nine fortresses of Śambara for Divodāsa.
Thus, O Indra, have we offered this hymn to you out of a desire for glory, as if striving for strength by our own selves.
May we, longing for it, attain that seventh [step]; may the weapon of the godless scorner fall prostrate.

Thus have the Gṛtsamadas fashioned hymns for you, O Hero, like those seeking help fashioning the paths of wisdom. O Indra, may these seekers of sacred prayer obtain for themselves new food, strength, a secure dwelling, and bliss.
Surely may that wealthy sacrificial gift of yours, O Indra, yield its boon to the singer;
grant gifts to those who praise you, let not our fortune fail us. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
We offer these songs to you, O Indra; take note of us well. Like one seeking booty, we bring forth our chariot;
we, the praisers, meditating with inspired thought, desire the favor of a hero such as you.
O Indra, through your protections, you guard the people who seek you and desire you;
you are the lord and the protector of the one who offers oblations, for he approaches you with such focused intent.
May that Indra, who is to be invoked by us, be our friend, auspicious,
and the protector of men— he who, with his aid, shall lead forward the one who recites, the one who exerts himself, the one who cooks, and the one who praises.
I praise that Indra, I sing his praises—he in whom men of old increased and found their strength.
May he, when approached, fulfill the desire for wealth of the one who offers prayer, the newest man of the Āyu lineage.
Delighting in the hymns of the Aṅgirases, Indra, the priest, urged them forward, seeking a path;
stealing away the dawns with the sun while being praised, he shattered even the ancient fortresses of Aśna.
He, the god renowned by the name Indra, has arisen for man as the most wondrous of doers;
the self-dependent one, having overcome him, struck off the dear head of the Dāsa who acted like a leper.

That Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra and destroyer of forts, drove away the Dāsa women of black origin. He generated for mankind both the earth and the waters; he has ever strengthened the praise of the sacrificer.
To him, the powerful Indra, the gods have granted enduring strength in the struggle for the waters;
when they placed the thunderbolt in his two arms, he struck down the Dasyus and cast down their iron fortresses.
Surely, O Indra, may that wealthy sacrificial gift of yours yield a boon to the singer;
bestow it upon those who praise you, let not our fortune perish. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
To him who conquers all, who conquers wealth, who conquers heaven, who conquers by sacrifice, who conquers men, who conquers fields;
to him who wins horses, who wins cattle, who wins waters—to Indra, the worshipful one, bring the beloved Soma.

To the conqueror, the one who shatters, the winner, the unconquered, the subduer, the ordainer; to the one of mighty stride, the bearer, the one whose path is hard to traverse, the ever-conquering—proclaim homage to Indra!

Ever-conquering, devourer of men, subduer of people, shaker, warrior, grown according to his pleasure; gatherer of hosts, victorious, honored among the tribes—I have proclaimed the heroic deeds performed by Indra.
The unyielding bull, the slayer of the turbulent, profound, lofty, and of unattainable wisdom;
the impeller of the weak, the piercer, the firm, the broad—Indra, the performer of perfect sacrifice, generated the dawns and the sun.
Through sacrifice, the seekers, the wise ones who yearn for the gods, have found the path across the waters;
sending forth their prayers and seeking help, they have attained cattle through their invocations and have won riches by impelling them toward Indra.
O Indra, bestow upon us the most excellent riches:
the insight of skill, good fortune, the increase of wealth, the safety of our bodies, the sweetness of speech, and the auspiciousness of our days.

At the Trikadruka festivals, the mighty bull, possessing great strength, drank his fill of the barley-mixed Soma pressed by Viṣṇu, according to his desire. It exhilarated him for the sake of performing a great deed; it accompanied him—the great and wide one. Thus the true drop attended upon the god Indra, the true god.
Then, radiant with brilliance, he overcame Krivi in battle by his might; he filled the two worlds, heaven and earth, with his majesty and grew even greater.
He placed one [portion] within his belly, while the other overflowed; thus the god accompanied the god, the true Indu [the drop] accompanied true Indra.
Born together with wisdom, you have grown strong together with power; increased together with heroic deeds, you are the overcomer of adversaries, O far-seeing one.
You are the giver of wealth and desirable riches to the one who praises you; thus may the god, the true Soma-drop, attend upon the god, the true Indra.

O dancer, O Indra, that manly deed of yours was the first and ancient one, worthy of proclamation in heaven—the deed which, by the power of the god, you performed when you released the life-force and let the waters flow. By his might, he overcame every godless one; the Lord of a Hundred Powers found strength, he found nourishment.
We invoke you, the Lord of hosts, the sage among sages, possessed of most exalted fame;
the supreme king of sacred prayers, O Brahmaṇaspati, hearing us with your aids, sit upon your seat.
O Bṛhaspati, even the gods, the wise ones of your divine power, have obtained their share of the sacrifice;
like the sun with its light makes the great rays visible, you are the progenitor of all sacred hymns.
Having driven away the surrounding waters and the darknesses, you mount the radiant chariot of Cosmic Order,
O Bṛhaspati— the terrifying one, the subduer of enemies, the slayer of demons, the breaker of the cow-pens, and the finder of the light.
With your excellent guidances you lead and protect the person who offers gifts to you; may distress never reach him.
You are the scorcher of those who hate sacred prayer and the subduer of their wrath; O Bṛhaspati, such is your great majesty.

Neither distress nor misfortune from any quarter, nor enemies, nor the double-tongued have overcome him whom you, O Brahmaṇaspati, protect as a good guardian; indeed, you drive away all deceivers from him.
You are our protector, the maker of paths, the far-seeing; for your service we age with our prayers.
O Bṛhaspati, whoever lays a snare for us, may his own fierce misfortune crush him.
Or if some mortal, a malicious enemy or a lurking wolf, should harm us though we are innocent—O Bṛhaspati, turn him away from our path; make a good way for us toward this feast of the gods.

We invoke you, the protector of our bodies, the savior, the advocate who is well-disposed toward us. O Bṛhaspati, strike down those who revile the gods; let not the evil-doers attain the highest bliss.
O Brahmaṇaspati, through you, our excellent increaser, may we bestow upon men desirable wealth.
Those enemies who are far away, those who are near, and those who assail us—crush them all, so that they have no share in prosperity.
Through you, O Bṛhaspati, may we obtain supreme vitality, with you as our fulfilling and winning ally.
Let not the malevolent one who seeks to harm us prevail; may we, through our well-spoken hymns, advance toward prosperity.
The bull who never yields, who goes to the challenge, the scorcher of the enemy, victorious in battles;
you, O Brahmaṇaspati, are the true avenger of debts, the tamer even of the fierce one who exults in his strength.

He who seeks to harm with an ungodly mind, thinking himself fierce and desiring to slay us—O Bṛhaspati, let his deadly weapon not reach us; we cast down the wrath of that arrogant one who acts with evil intent.
To be invoked in battles and to be approached with homage, he goes among the spoils as a winner of wealth after wealth;
Bṛhaspati has shattered all the attacks of the enemy who seeks to harm us, like chariots.

With your most piercing heat, burn away the demons who have held you in contempt, O you of proven heroism! Make manifest that power of yours which is worthy of praise; O Bṛhaspati, destroy those who surround us with their waters.

O Bṛhaspati, that which belongs to the noble one, which shines forth brilliantly and powerfully among the people through its wisdom— that wealth, born of the *ṛta* and radiant with might, bestow upon us as a wondrous treasure.
Do not deliver us to the thieves who, seated at the place of the oppressor, are enemies coveting our food.
They disregard the protection of the gods; they know no bounds in their hearts, O Bṛhaspati, nor do they understand the *sāman*.

For Tvaṣṭṛ, the seer, brought you forth from all beings, from every *sāman*. He is the debt-collector, the debt-claimer, Brahmaṇaspati, the slayer of the deceitful, the upholder of the great cosmic order (*ṛta*).
For your glory the mountain opened wide when you, O Aṅgiras, released the herd of cattle.
With Indra as your ally, O Bṛhaspati, you unbarred the flood of waters that was encompassed by darkness.
O Brahmanaspati, be the controller of this hymn and prosper our offspring. All that which the gods favor is auspicious; may we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
Favor this offering, O Lord, for you are the master; we shall worship you with this new and great song.
O Bṛhaspati, just as our liberal patron is praised by you as a friend, so may you fulfill our prayer.
He who, by his might, bent down those things that were unbendable, and with fury shattered the strongholds of Śambara;
Brahmaṇaspati caused even the unshakable to tremble, and he entered the mountain rich in treasures.
That deed for the most divine among the gods was performed: they loosened what was firm and made the solid things yield.
He drove forth the cows, split Vala with his sacred prayer, concealed the darkness, and revealed the light of heaven.
Brahmaṇaspati pierced with his might that well whose mouth was stone, which had a stream of honey;
all those who behold the light of heaven drank from it, and together they poured forth the water-bearing spring in abundance.
Ancient indeed are those worlds that have come into being; through the months and autumns, they have opened wide for you.
Without striving, they move one after another—those paths which Brahmaṇaspati has fashioned.

Those who, approaching, reached that treasure of the Paṇis—hidden in the highest cave—they, being wise, having perceived the falsehoods, returned; from where they had come, they rose up again to enter.
The upholders of *ṛta*, having beheld the falsehoods, have returned from there and stand upon the paths of the great seers (*kavayaḥ*).
That fire, blown forth by their two arms upon the stone—there is no one who can conceal it; for they have abandoned it.
With his swift bow whose string is Truth, Brahmaṇaspati reaches whatever he desires;
excellent are his arrows with which he shoots—the keen-eyed ones, whose origin is in the ears, that they may see.
He is the one who leads the host, he who possesses discipline, the domestic priest, the well-praised Lord of Prayer (*brahmaṇaspati*) in battle.
When the powerful one brings forth booty through his inspired thought, then the sun shines from that wealth, scorching with its heat at will.
The far-reaching and powerful Bṛhaspati, the first of those who bestow abundance, possesses most gracious and successful gifts.
These are the attainments of the desirable and vigorous one, by which both classes of people—the clans—enjoy their sustenance.
He who is all-pervading in the lower realm, great and most delightful, has grown mighty through his own power;
that god has spread himself wide against the gods—he, Brahmaṇaspati, encompasses them all.
O Maghavans, everything is true for you both; even the waters do not violate your decree.
O Indra and Brahmaṇaspati, come to our oblation and our food like two prize-winning horses yoked together.

And the swiftest bearers hear him; the eloquent sage, fit for the assembly, wins wealth through his hymns. He who hates the stubborn, who according to his will exacts the debt—he, the powerful *Brahmaṇaspati*, is the victor in the encounter.
The true wrath of Brahmaṇaspati became according to his will as he was about to perform great deeds;
he who drove out the cows distributed them to heaven, and like a mighty stream, he flowed forth separately by his own might.
O Brahmanaspati, may we always be masters of well-governed wealth that provides vital strength;
bestow heroic sons upon our heroes, since you, as the sovereign lord, come to my invocation through this prayer.
O Brahmanaspati, be the controller of this hymn and prosper our offspring. All that which the gods favor is auspicious; may we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
Kindling the fire, he shall conquer those who attack; having offered prayers and presented oblations, he shall prosper.
He surpasses every being born with that which was born before him—whomever Brahmaṇaspati makes his ally.
With heroes he shall conquer heroic foes who attack him; with cattle he shall extend his wealth and be mindful by himself.
His offspring and his progeny increase—whomever soever *Brahmaṇaspati* makes his ally.
Like the surging flood of the Sindhu, he is impetuous and fierce; like a bull toward castrated steers, he overcomes his enemies with might.
Like the spreading flame of Agni, he cannot be turned back—whomever Brahmaṇaspati makes his ally.
For him flow the celestial, inexhaustible [streams]; as the first among beings, he goes forth for the sake of cattle.
With unabated power, he slays by his might whomever Brahmaṇaspati makes his ally.
For him all the roaring rivers flow; they have provided many flawless shelters.
Blessed by the favor of the gods, he prospers—whomever Brahmaṇaspati makes his ally.

The upright singer shall conquer those who attack him; the one seeking the gods shall prevail over the godless. The well-aided man shall conquer in battles that are hard to overcome; the sacrificer shall divide the food away from the non-sacrificer.
Sacrifice, O hero; go forth to those who long for you; form an auspicious mind for the conquest of Vṛtra.
Prepare the oblation so that you may be fortunate; we choose the protection of Brahmaṇaspati.

He, together with his people, his clan, his kin, his sons, and his men, wins booty and wealth— he who, with a mind full of faith, seeks to win over the Father of the Gods, Brahmaṇaspati, with an oblation.
Whosoever has worshipped him with oblations rich in ghee—him Brahmaṇaspati leads forward.
He delivers him from distress, guards him from harm; even from narrow straits, the wonderful one makes wide room for him.
These songs, dripping with clarity, I ever offer with the ladle to the Ādityas, the kings.
May Mitra, Aryaman, and Bhaga hear us, as well as Varuṇa of many births, Dakṣa, and Aṃśa.
May Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa, acting with one accord, accept this hymn of mine today—
the Ādityas, who are pure, cleansed by the stream, free from crookedness, blameless, and unharmed.

Those Ādityas—vast, profound, undeceived, many-eyed, and seeking to consume the malevolent—behold both the crooked and the upright within; for these kings, even the most distant things are near at hand.
The Ādityas sustain that which moves and that which stands; they are the gods, the guardians of the entire world.
Far-sighted, they protect their divine power (*asurya*); abiding in cosmic order (*ṛta*), they take account of debts.
O Ādityas, may I obtain this knowledge of your protection, O Aryaman, which brings joy even in the midst of fear.
Under your guidance, O Mitra and Varuṇa, may I avoid all difficulties as one avoids pitfalls.
For easy to travel is your path, O Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuṇa—thornless and straight. By that path, O Ādityas, speak for us; grant us a protection that is difficult to overcome.
May Aditi, the daughter of royalty, and Aryaman carry us across all hostilities by easy paths.
May we, possessing many heroes and unharmed, abide under the lofty protection of Mitra and Varuṇa.
Supporting the three earths and the three heavens, they maintain three ordinances within their assembly.
By the Eternal Law (*ṛta*), O Ādityas, your greatness is mighty; that is beautiful, O Aryaman, Varuṇa, and Mitra.
They uphold the three celestial luminaries; golden-hued, pure, and purified by their own radiance;
sleepless, unblinking, undeceived, and far-famed for the sake of the upright mortal.
O Varuṇa, you are the king of all—of both the gods, O Asura, and of mortals. Grant us a hundred autumns to behold; may we attain the well-established lifespans of former times.
Neither the right nor the left is distinguished, neither the east, O Ādityas, nor the west.
O Vasus, whether by simplicity or by wisdom, may I, led by you, attain the light that is free from fear.

He who offers gifts to the kings who uphold the cosmic order (*ṛta*), and whom constant prosperities cause to grow— he, wealthy and the first to travel by chariot, goes forth as a giver of goods, highly praised in the assemblies.
Pure, with good pastures, undeceived, and possessing heroic sons, he dwells among the waters, having reached advanced age.
No one slays him, neither from near nor from afar, who abides under the guidance of the Ādityas.
O Aditi, Mitra, and Varuṇa, be gracious even for whatever offense we have committed against you.
May we attain the vast, fearless light; O Indra, let not the long darknesses overtake us.

Both [worlds], meeting together, cause rain from heaven to swell for him; thriving, he bears the name "Fortunate. Conquering both dwellings, he goes forth into battles; both halves of the world become favorable to him.

O worshipful Ādityas, those magical powers of yours intended for the deceiver, and the snares spread out for the enemy—may we pass beyond them like a horse with a chariot; may we remain unharmed within your broad protection.

O Varuṇa, may I not suffer loss through a dear and liberal patron who gives much, nor through my own kinsman. O King, may we not be deprived of well-governed wealth; may we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
May all these peaceful things of the poet Āditya, the self-ruling one, surpass [all others] in greatness;
he who is the delightful god for sacrifice—I beg for the high renown of the abundant Varuṇa.
Under your ordinance, O Varuṇa, may we be fortunate, praising you with pious intent;
day after day, like fires at the dawning of the cattle-rich mornings, may we approach you singing your praises.
May we abide in the protection of you, O Varuṇa, leader of wide renown, who possess many heroes;
O undeceived sons of Aditi, O gods, grant us your forgiveness for our kinship.
The Āditya, the Ordainer, has sent them forth; the rivers flow according to the Law (*ṛta*) of Varuṇa.
They do not weary, nor do they cease; like birds, they fly swiftly across the expanse of the earth.

Loosen from me my sin like a tethering rope; may we succeed in finding the spring of your *ṛta*, O Varuṇa. Let not the thread snap while I weave my prayer; let not the measure of my work be cut short before the appointed time.
O Varuṇa, keep fear far from me; O sovereign lord of cosmic order, hold me in accordance with the Truth.
Release me from distress as one releases a calf from its tether; for not even for a moment can anyone exist apart from you.

O Varuṇa, do not strike us with those weapons of yours, O Asura, which consume the one who commits sin while performing your sacrifice. May we not go forth from the light; utterly loosen our adversaries so that we may live.
Homage to thee, O Varuṇa, both now and hereafter, even in the future, O thou of many births;
for in thee alone, O invincible one, are our unshakable laws established, like mountains.

Release me from the debts contracted by me; O King, let me not suffer for what has been done by another. There are yet many dawns that have not dawned; O Varuṇa, while we are still alive, establish us within them.
O King, whoever—whether an ally or a friend—has spoken fear to me, who am afraid, in my dream; or whoever, like a thief or a wolf, seeks to harm us—O Varuṇa, protect us from that.

O Varuṇa, may I not experience the destitution of a dear, liberal, and helpful patron; O King, may we not be deprived of well-governed wealth. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
O Ādityas, firm in your vows and vigorous, keep my sin far away as if it were a secret-born offense.
O gods Varuṇa and Mitra, you who hear me and know what is auspicious—I invoke you for protection.
O gods, you are our providence; you are our vigor; drive away our enemies to a distance.
As those who bestow gifts, look upon us with favor and grant us forgiveness; be merciful to us this day and hereafter as well.
What indeed may we perform for you with future friendship, or what with past, O Vasus?
O Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Indra, and Maruts, grant us well-being.
O gods, you indeed are our kinsmen; have mercy upon me who implores you.
Let not your chariot be held back midway, nor let us weary ourselves among those who are not your kin.
One [of you] has forgiven my many offenses; you have instructed me like a father instructs a gambler.
O Gods, let your snares be far away, let misfortunes be far away; do not seize me, as one seizes a bird, because of my son.
O worshipful ones, turn toward us this day; fearing, I would enter into your heart.
O gods, protect us from the devouring wolf; protect us, O worshipful ones, from the pit and from falling.
O Varuṇa, may I not suffer the loss of a wealthy, beloved, and most generous friend;
O King, may we not fall away from well-governed riches. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
The waters do not rest for Savitṛ, the god who ordains the cosmic order (ṛta), nor for Indra, the slayer of the serpent.
Day after day the darkness of the waters passes away; how far extends their first emission?
The Mother spoke forth to him who was wise, concerning him who would bring destruction upon Vṛtra;
carving out paths for him according to his pleasure, the roaring rivers go day by day toward their goal.
For he has risen up aloft into the mid-air, and then he hurled his weapon at Vṛtra.
Enveloped in mist, Indra rushed upon him; armed with sharp weapons, he conquered the enemy.
O Bṛhaspati, pierce the heroes of the Asura Vṛkadvaras with your heat, like with a firebrand;
just as you have boldly struck them down even in former times, so now, O Indra, slay our enemy.
Cast down from on high the stone from heaven, with which, being exhilarated, you shall utterly consume the enemy.
For the winning of many offspring and descendants, O Indra, make us the masters of cattle.
For you two increase the mental power which you both desire; you are the inciters of the worshipper who is diligent.
O Indra and Soma, protect us; in this time of fear, create for us a place of safety.
Let not weariness, nor fatigue, nor sloth overcome me; let us not say, "Do not press the Soma.
May he who gives to me, who bestows, who takes heed of me, and who approaches me with cattle when I am pressing the Soma, [grant me his favor].
O Sarasvatī, protect us; accompanied by the Maruts, may you boldly conquer our enemies.
Even that arrogant one, though displaying his power, Indra slays—the bull of the Śaṇḍikas.
Whoever seeks to harm us from afar or whoever would strike us down—beholding him, pierce him with your sharpened bolt.
O Bṛhaspati, conquer the enemies with your weapons; O King, deliver the one who intends us injury into the power of the malevolent.
O Hero, with our own heroic warriors, perform those deeds of valor which are yours to accomplish. Let them long remain scorched by your heat; having slain them, bring back their riches to us.
Seeking your favor, I address with reverence and homage that divine host of Maruts,
so that we may obtain wealth consisting of all-heroic sons, accompanied by progeny, and renowned day by day.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, protect our chariot together with the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus,
as we fly forth like birds from our dwelling, seeking glory, exultant, and seated upon the woods.
Now, O gods, being of one accord, protect our chariot as it seeks booty among the people;
when the swift steeds, crossing the dust with their feet, strike against the ridges of the earth with their hooves.
And may that Indra, the lord of all people, of great wisdom, come with the host of Maruts from heaven;
may he follow our chariot with his wolf-free protections for the sake of great gain and the winning of booty.
And may that god Tvaṣṭṛ, the master of the world, in harmony with the divine wives, speed forth our chariot;
may Iḷā, Bhaga, Bṛhaddiva, the two worlds, Pūṣan, Purandhi, and the Aśvins, the lords, likewise do so.
And these two goddesses, auspicious and of dual aspect, Dawn and Night, who stir all living beings—
I praise you both, O Earth, with a new hymn, so that the threefold vigor of all that stands and moves may be spread abroad.
And may Ahi Budhnya, Aja Ekapād, Trita, R̥bhukṣan, and Savitṛ grant you favor; may the Son of the Waters, the swift impeller, grant it through prayer and ritual labor.
O worshipful ones, I desire these uplifted [prayers] for you; the Āyus have fashioned them for a new [purpose].
Seeking renown and longing for booty, may they—like a chariot-steed—attain our devotion.
O Heaven and Earth, be the protectors of this my word as I strive for the truth and desire to win;
you two who possess this furthering life, praised of old, I, seeking wealth, place you in the forefront of my great work.
Let not secret deceits of the living man harm us on this day; do not deliver us over to these calamities.
Let our friendship not be severed; take note of that with a mind inclined toward our welfare—for that very thing we entreat you.
With a mind free from anger, bring hither the favoring ear; bring the milch-cow who yields her milk, the swelling, the inexhaustible.
O you who are invoked by many, I urge you every day with my feet and with my word—you who are swift and full of vigor.
I invoke Rākā, who is easily summoned, with a beautiful hymn; may the fortunate one hear us and take notice of us herself.
May she sew together our work with a needle that does not break, and may she grant us a praiseworthy hero-son who bestows a hundredfold wealth.
O Rākā, those benevolent thoughts of yours which are well-formed, by which you bestow riches upon the donor—
with those, come to us today with a gracious mind, O Blessed One, granting us thousandfold prosperity.
O Sinīvālī, broad-tressed one, you who are the sister of the gods, accept this offered oblation; O goddess, grant us progeny.
To her who has beautiful arms, lovely fingers, who is well-nourished and prolific—
offer the oblation to that Sinīvālī, the mistress of the people.
Gungū, Sinīvālī, Rākā, and Sarasvatī—
Indrāṇī I invoke for aid, and Varuṇānī for well-being.
O Father of the Maruts, let your favor come to us; do not deprive us of the sight of the sun.
May your hero be gracious toward our horse; may we, O Rudra, be propagated with offspring.
O Rudra, through these most auspicious medicines bestowed by you, may I attain a hundred winters. Drive far away from us hatred, drive away distress, and scatter our diseases in all directions.
O Rudra, you are the most excellent of all that is born in glory; you are the strongest of the strong, O wielder of the thunderbolt.
Carry us across to the further shore of distress in safety; ward off all assaults of the malicious.
O Rudra, let us not provoke you to anger with our prostrations, nor with ill-praises, O Bull, nor with joint invocations.
Raise up our heroes with your medicines; I hear that you are the best of physicians among physicians.
With invocations and oblations, may I propitiate Rudra with hymns—he who is invoked by those seeking his call.
May he of the soft belly, the one easy to invoke, the tawny one with beautiful jaws, not deliver us over to this wrathful intent.
The bull, accompanied by the Maruts, has gladdened me with his most vigorous strength as I implored him.
Like one seeking shade from the heat, may I, free from harm, obtain the favor of Rudra; may I win his goodwill.
O Rudra, where is that merciful hand of yours which possesses healing medicine and relief? O Bull, as the remover of divine affliction, look now with favor upon me.
To the brown, white-shining bull, I send forth a great and mighty hymn of praise. With prostrations we honor the radiant one; we celebrate the fierce name of Rudra with our salutations.
With firm limbs, multiform, fierce, and tawny, he has adorned himself with bright golden ornaments.
From Rudra, the lord of this vast world, let not his asura-power ever depart.
Worthy, you carry your arrows and your bow; worthy, you wear the worshipful, multiform golden necklace.
Worthy, you bestow all this vast power; indeed, O Rudra, there is nothing more mighty than you.
Praise the famous one, the youth seated upon the chariot-throne, fierce and striking like a terrifying beast.
O Rudra, being praised, be gracious to the singer; let your missiles strike down someone other than us.
Even a youth bows before his father who approaches him with reverence; O Rudra, you praise the lord of the virtuous, the giver of abundant wealth. Being praised, may you grant us healing remedies.
O Maruts, those pure medicines of yours, which are most healing, O bulls, and which are bliss-bestowing—
those which Manu chose for us, our father— I desire those as health and prosperity from Rudra.
May the missile of Rudra avoid us; may the great ill-will of the impetuous one pass us by.
O Bounteous One, relax your firm [bow] for the sake of our patrons; be gracious to our children and descendants.
Thus, O tawny bull, you who are observant, O God, so that you neither grow angry nor strike us down;
hear our invocation here, O Rudra, and may we, with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
The Maruts, pouring down rain, bold in their might, terrible like wild beasts in their strength, blazing with splendor;
glowing like fires, drinkers of the *ṛjīṣa*, blowing away the whirlwind, they disclosed the cattle.
Like the heavens with their stars, the ring-adorned ones have shone forth; like rain from a cloud, they have flashed out.
O Maruts, with Rudra as your leader, you whose chests are adorned with golden ornaments, you were born from the bright udder of Pṛśni, the bull.
They groom their horses like swift steeds in the races, hastening with the ears of the river through their fleetness.
O Maruts, wearing golden helmets and shaking [your spears], you who are of one mind, come with your spotted deer to our nourishment.
They have grown strong for nourishment, surpassing all beings; or rather, they are ever-givers of quickening gifts to Mitra.
With spotted horses, possessing inexhaustible wealth, they sit at the pole in their courses like soaring birds.

With your blazing spears, come like swans to their own resting places by dustless paths, with your swelling-milking cows and fuel-bearing [chariots], O Maruts of one mind, for the exhilaration of the sweet mead.
O Maruts, of one mind, come to our prayers and to our libations like the praise of men;
swell us like a mare, like a cow with her udder; and make the prayer beautiful with strength for the singer.
O Maruts, grant us that vigorous chariot, a prayer that awakens our understanding day by day;
grant nourishment to your praisers, and to the poet in the assemblies, grant gain, wisdom, inviolable and invincible power.
When the Maruts, with golden ornaments upon their breasts, yoke their horses to the chariots— O Bhaga, they who are bounteous givers—
they swell forth great nourishment for the person who offers oblations, just as a cow yields milk for her calf in the stalls.
O Maruts, O Vasus, if a mortal enemy should set himself against us with wolfish intent, protect us from harm!
Turn him back with your glowing wheel; O Rudras, strike down the weapon of the one who curses us.
O Maruts, that wondrous journey of yours is made manifest, when you, the allies, milked even the udder of Pṛśni;
or when, O sons of Rudra, you who are invincible, brought Trita to old age for the sake of reproach against the one who reviles.

We invoke you, the great Maruts who move with the speed of birds, at the offering of the swift Viṣṇu. With ladles uplifted and devoted to sacred prayer, we seek from those golden-hued and preeminent ones the praiseworthy gift of wealth.
They, the Daśagvas, first brought the sacrifice; may they urge us on at the dawning of the mornings.
Like Dawn, she uncovers the dark nights with her ruddy rays, with great, glowing light that swells with a flood of kine.
Those Rudras have grown strong in the seats of cosmic order (*ṛta*) with their hosts and with ruddy ointments;
raining down moisture with their swift power, they have assumed a most radiant and well-fashioned color.
Approaching that great protection for our aid, we indeed praise them with this homage—
those whom Trita, like the five Hotṛ-priests, brought hither from afar on his chariot for our protection and assistance.

That aid by which you carry the distressed across distress, and by which you release the worshipper from reproach—may that favor of yours, O Maruts, come hither; may your benevolence speed toward us like a lowing cow.
Seeking booty, I have sent forth this eloquent speech; may the Eater take pleasure in my songs.
Will the Son of the Waters, who impels the swift, make them well-adorned? For he indeed shall find them pleasing.
From our own hearts, let us speak this mantra, well-fashioned for him; will he indeed take heed of it?
The Son of the Waters, by the greatness of his divine power, has brought forth all the worlds of the noble one.
Some flow together, others approach; the rivers fill the common ocean.
The pure waters have gathered around that pure, shining Son of the Waters.
The waters, young women who do not smile, go around him, the youth, as they cleanse themselves;
he, bright with his brilliant rays, has shone richly for us—unfanned by wood, clothed in ghee within the waters.
To him, the unshakable god, these three goddesses—women—present food.
For he has glided forth like a prepared [sacrifice] into the waters; he drinks the milk of those who have first brought forth.
Here is the birthplace of the horse and of this [soma]; protect the patrons from the malicious enemy and from harm.
Beyond the raw fortresses, let the enemies and falsehoods not reach that which is unassailable.
In his own home is the cow that yields milk well; she swells with his self-sustaining power, and he, being strong, eats the food.
That Son of the Waters, bestowing strength within the waters, shines forth for the sake of granting wealth to the one who serves him.
He who, true to the cosmic order (*ṛta*), eternal, and pure by divine nature, shines far and wide within the waters—
he is the one from whom all other beings, like branches, spring forth, and from whom the plants are born through their progeny.
For the Son of the Waters has indeed taken his station in the lap of the prostrate ones, standing erect and clothed in lightning.
Carrying his supreme majesty, the swift, golden-hued rivers flow around him.
Golden in form, golden in appearance, the Son of the Waters is indeed golden-hued;
having sat down from his golden womb, the givers of gold present food to him.
That countenance of his, and his beloved name, the secret one, increases—the grandson of the waters—whom the young maidens thus kindle together; he is golden-hued, and clarified butter is his food.
To him, the nearest friend among many, let us do service with sacrifices, with homage, and with oblations.
I smooth his back, I provide for him with hollowed vessels, I sustain him with food, and I praise him all around with hymns.
He, the bull, begat the embryo in them; as an infant he sucks them, and they lick him.
He, the Son of Waters, of unblemished hue, has here entered another’s body as it were.
To him who stands upon this highest step, shining forever with stainless rays—
the mighty waters, bringing ghee as food for their offspring, themselves fly around him with their garments.

O Agni, I have offered a secure dwelling for the people, and I have offered a well-fashioned hymn to the patrons. All that which the gods favor is auspicious. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
For you, the waters have been sped forth; the men have milked them out with the sheep’s wool and the stones.
O Indra, drink the Soma offered with *svāhā* and consecrated with *vaṣaṭ* from the Hotṛ’s bowl—you who are the first lord of it!
Blended with sacrifices, with spotted deer and spears, you who are radiant on your journey and fond of ointments—
having sat upon the sacrificial grass of Bharata, O sons of Heaven, O heroes, drink the Soma from the Potar’s cup.
Come indeed to us, O you who are easy to invoke; sit down upon the sacred grass and take your delight.
Then, O Tvaṣṭṛ, being well-pleased with the soma juice, rejoice together with the gods and their wives in your excellent company.

O sage, bring the gods here; sacrifice and sit down, O Hotṛ, upon the three seats. Accept the Soma-sweetness that has been set forth; drink from the Āgnīdhra vessel and satisfy yourself with your portion.
This [Soma] is indeed for you, increasing the manly vigor of your body; from of old, power has been placed within your arms.
Pressed for you, O Maghavan, brought for you—drink of this to your heart's content from the cup of the Brahmin.

May you two enjoy the sacrifice; be mindful of my invocation. The Hotṛ priest has sat down according to the ancient invocations. O Kings, homage approaches you both; drink the Soma-sweetness from the Praśāstṛ.

Rejoice according to your pleasure from the oblation of the soma-juice; O Adhvaryus, he desires the full ladle poured out. Bring this to him, for he is its master; as the giver of wealth, drink the Soma from the Hotṛ’s cup with the seasonal rites.
Him whom I invoked before, him I invoke now; he indeed is to be invoked, he who is master of the name "Giver.
O Giver of Wealth, drink with the seasons the Soma-sweetness set forth by the Adhvaryus from the Potar’s cup.
May thy draft-horses be fatened by which thou goest; O Lord of the Forest, be firm and uninjured.
Drawing near and summoning them, O bold one, drink the Soma from the Neṣṭar’s cup with the seasons, O Giver of Wealth.

From the *hotṛ*’s cup and from the *potr*’s cup he has drunk; from the *neṣṭṛ*’s cup he has rejoiced in the offered food. May Draviṇodas drink from the fourth cup—the uninjured, immortal one—of him who bestows wealth.

Yoke today your chariot that comes hitherward, which is swift and carries heroes; let its unyoking be here for you both. Mix the oblations with honey, for you have come; then drink the Soma, O you who possess abundant wealth.
O Agni, accept the fuel; accept the oblation; accept the prayer of the people; accept the fair hymn of praise.
O Vasu, with all [the gods] and according to the season, desiring them, cause the desiring gods to drink the great oblation.
Up has risen this god Savitṛ for his impulsion; the bearer has stood firm for that most constant [work].
Now indeed he bestows treasure upon the gods, and so he has granted the one who offers the oblation a share in well-being.
For, standing erect with broad hands, the God stretches forth his arms that all may hear him.
Even the waters bend down at his command; even this wind rests in its circling course.
Even with his swift steeds he now unyokes; he has brought even the weary traveler to rest from his journey.
Even among the serpents, I have subdued them for the sake of food; by the law of Savitṛ, the releaser has arrived.
Weaving it out, she has spun it out again; the skillful one has laid down his strength in the midst of his work.
Having gathered it up, he has risen; he has distributed the seasons. Savitar, the god of perfect wisdom, has come.
The houses spread out in various directions for the full span of life; the flame of Agni is its source.
The Mother has bestowed the supreme portion upon her son, according to his will as impelled by Savitṛ.
He who stood firm, desiring victory, has returned; the desire of all who wander has come home.
Having cast off his altered form, he has come according to the ordinance of the divine Savitṛ.
The waters have spread out their watery portion set by you within the waters; even the desert wastes have become full of moisture.
No one violates these ordinances of the god Savitṛ, which he has established for the birds and the forests.

As Varuṇa, swiftly moving, reaches the watery womb that is not to be disregarded even for a moment, so every bird has entered its nest; Savitṛ has distributed all living beings according to their stations.
Whose sacred law neither Indra, nor Varuṇa, nor Mitra, nor Aryaman, nor Rudra violates,
and whom no enemies harm— that god Savitṛ I here invoke for well-being with prostrations.
Seeking fortune, inspired thought, and abundance, may Narāśaṃsa and Gnāspati protect us.
May we be dear to the god Savitṛ at the gathering of wealth and the attainment of all that is desirable.
May that desirable wealth granted by you from heaven, from the waters, and from the earth come to us—
wealth, O Savitṛ, which brings well-being to the praisers, to our kin, and to the singer who extols you widely.

Like two pressing-stones, you two truly exert yourselves for this purpose; like two vultures toward a tree containing a treasure, like two priests at the assembly reciting hymns, like two messengers with offerings to many people.
Setting out at dawn like two chariot-heroes, like two noble brothers, you two attain the boon;
like two women adorning their bodies, like a husband and wife, you find wisdom among the people.
Come toward us first, like two horns; come swiftly with your aids, like two hooves darting about.
Like two ruddy geese at dawn, come hitherward, O mighty ones, like two chariot-horses.
Like two ships, carry us across; like two yokes, like two hubs, like two inner-boards, like two outer-boards;
like two dogs, O you who do not fail, protect our bodies; like two cranes, protect us from falling apart.
Like the wind, ageless; like the flow of rivers; like two eyes with sight, come hither!
Like hands most beneficial to the body, like two feet, lead us toward greater prosperity.
Like two lips speaking honey from the mouth, like two breasts, nourish us so that we may live. Like two nostrils, be the protectors of our bodies; like two ears, be well-hearing for us.
Like two hands, bestow power upon us; like two feet, traverse for us the realms of space. O Aśvins, sharpen these songs of ours directed toward you, as one sharpens an axe with a whetstone.
O Aśvins, these strengthening prayers, this hymn of praise, the Gṛtsamadas have fashioned for you.
O Heroes, graciously accepting them, come hither; may we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
O Soma and Pūṣan, progenitors of riches, progenitors of heaven, progenitors of earth,
born as the guardians of the entire world, the gods have made you the navel of immortality.
May these two gods, at their birth, be pleased; may they conceal the unpleasant darkness.
With these two, Soma and Pūṣan, Indra generated the cooked [milk] within the raw cows.

O Soma and Pūṣan, you two, O bulls, quicken that seven-wheeled chariot which measures the mid-region, which moves through all things, which turns in every direction, is yoked by thought, and possesses five reins.
One has made his dwelling in the heavens on high; the other is upon the earth and in the mid-air.
May those two disclose for us an abundance of many desirable things and much food—an increase of wealth that reaches our very core.
One has generated all beings; the other moves about beholding the universe.
O Soma and Pūṣan, favor my prayer; with you two may we conquer all hostile armies.
May Pūṣan, the stirrer of all, quicken our prayer; may Soma, the lord of wealth, bestow riches upon us.
May the goddess Aditi, who is free from enemies, protect us. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
O Vāyu, with those thousandfold chariots of yours, come hither, drawn by your teams,
for the drinking of the Soma.
O Vāyu, come with your team of horses; this bright [soma] is offered to you.
You shall go to the house of the one who presses the juice.
O Indra and Vāyu, who possess the teams of horses, come today to the bright soma mixed with milk;
drink it, O heroes!
O Mitra and Varuṇa, increasers of Truth, this Soma has been pressed for you;
hear my invocation here.
The two kings, free from malice, sit upon the firm and supreme seat,
seated upon a thousand pillars.
Those two sovereign kings, the Ādityas, who drink the clarified butter and are lords of bounty,
dwell together in a place free from reproach.
O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, come hither with cattle and with horses;
O Rudras, protectors of men, come to our dwelling.
O you of mighty wealth, let no enemy from afar nor any from near,
no malevolent mortal foe, prevail against us.
O Aśvins, you who are worthy of praise and finders of wide space, bring hither to us wealth that is golden-hued in appearance.
Indra indeed shall drive away even great fear;
for he, the active one, is steadfast.
May Indra be gracious to us; may no evil reach us from behind;
may there be good fortune for us from the front.
May Indra grant us freedom from fear from all directions; may he, the all-seeing conqueror of enemies, protect us.
O All-Gods, come hither; hear this my invocation.
Sit down upon this sacrificial grass.
This intense, honey-sweet, exhilarating draught is for you among the Śunahotras;
drink this desirable one.
With Indra as their chief, the hosts of Maruts, the gods whose gifts are Pūṣan—
may all of you hear my invocation.
O Sarasvatī, most encompassing, most excellent of rivers, most divine!
We are, as it were, unworthy of praise; O Mother, grant us renown.
In you, O goddess Sarasvatī, all lifespans are centered;
rejoice among the descendants of Śunahotra, O goddess, and grant us progeny.
O Sarasvatī, rich in sacrificial food, accept these prayers;
O observer of Truth, those beloved thoughts which the Gṛtsamadas offer to you among the gods.
We choose you two here, Agni and the bearer of oblations, the two who bring prosperity to the sacrifice for our ancestors.
May Heaven and Earth today present this successful sacrifice, which touches the sky, among the gods.
May the gods worthy of sacrifice, free from malice, sit upon your lap here today for the drinking of Soma.
Crying out repeatedly, proclaiming his birth, he sends forth his voice like a rower propelling a boat.
O auspicious bird, may you be a bringer of good fortune; let no calamity from any quarter find you.
May the hawk not strike you down, nor the eagle; may the arrow-bearing hero who shoots not find you.
Crying out toward the direction of the fathers, may you, auspicious and speaking blessings, speak here.

Cry out from the right of our houses, O bird, you who are auspicious and a speaker of blessings! Let not the thief nor the malevolent one master us. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
The singers praise him from the right, like birds, the winged ones, speaking in due season;
like a singer of Sāmans, he utters both voices; he shines forth according to the Gāyatrī and the Triṣṭubh meters.
Like a *udgātṛ* priest, O bird, you sing the *sāman*; like a son of a *brahman*, you recite at the libations.
Like a stallion, you go toward the mother-cows; O bird, proclaim auspiciousness for us from every side, O bird, proclaim merit for us from all sides.
O bird, as you speak, utter auspicious words; sitting silently, consider our well-being.
When you fly up, may you call out like a karkari-bird; may we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
O Agni, you have made me the bearer of the powerful Soma to sacrifice in the assembly;
shining toward the gods, I harness the pressing-stone. For the sake of well-being, O Agni, take pleasure in this body of mine.
We have performed the sacrifice directed eastward; let the song increase. With fuel and reverence, they have honored Agni.
From heaven, they have ordained the assemblies of the sages; they have sought a path for the one who is wise and powerful.
The wise one, of purified will, has conceived the joy; by birth he is the close kinsman of heaven and earth.
The gods found the beautiful Agni within the waters, in the labor of the sisters.
The seven mighty rivers have magnified the fortunate one; he was born white and ruddy in his greatness.
Like mares rushing toward a newborn foal, the gods, at his birth, gazed upon Agni with wonder.
Spreading his brilliance through the mid-air with radiant limbs, purifying his wisdom by means of the sages' filters,
and clothing himself in light, he measures out the vast and perfect glories of the waters around the life-force.
He has gone toward those who do not eat, the undeceived, the mighty daughters of heaven, who are unclothed yet not naked;
here, the ancient ones, now youthful, dwelling in the same womb, have conceived a single embryo, the seven voices.
His piled-up masses, assuming every form, are spread out in the womb of clarified butter, in the flow of honeyed streams.
Here stand the swelling milch-cows; the two great, united Mothers of the Wondrous One are present.
O Son of Strength, being nourished, you have shone forth today, assuming brilliant and impetuous forms;
streams of honey and ghee drip down where the Bull has grown great through poetic wisdom.
From birth he discovered his father’s udder; he released its streams and its milky flows.
Though moving in secret with his auspicious friends, the great ones of heaven, he was not hidden away.
He bore the embryo of both the father and the progenitor; alone he sucked at many swelling breasts. O two wives of equal kinship, protect him, the bull, the pure one, for the sake of humanity.
In the wide, unconfined space, the great one has grown; for the glorious waters have gathered together around Agni.
As the domestic lord, Agni lay in the womb of *ṛta*, in the activity of his sisters who are kin.

Like a horse bearing the prize in the encounter of the great [waters], he is to be beheld by his son, he whose light is straight; he who as progenitor brought forth the ruddy cows, Agni, the most manly child of the waters, the mighty one.
The forest has brought forth the lovely child of the waters and the plants, the blessed one of manifold forms.
Even the gods have come together in spirit; they have honored the most praiseworthy one, born with great power.
Mighty indeed are his rays; the bright lightnings attend upon Agni Bhr̥jīka, as if milking nectar within his own secret, vast, and boundless seat, grown great like one hidden in a cave.
I praise you with oblations as a sacrificer; desiring your friendship and favor, I praise you.
Together with the gods, bestow protection upon the singer, and guard us with your domestic splendors.
O Agni, our excellent leader, may we— your assistants, possessing all riches and exulting in glorious seed—
overcome the godless who attack us in battle.
O Agni, you have become the banner of the gods, the delightful one who knows all poetic wisdoms;
as the domestic lord, you have caused mortals to dwell [in peace]; as a charioteer, you go fulfilling [the purpose] of the gods.
The immortal king has sat down in the dwelling of mortals, accomplishing the sacrificial rites.
With his face anointed with ghee, Agni has shone forth widely, knowing all poetic wisdoms.

Come to us with your auspicious friendships, you who are great, with your mighty aids, moving swiftly toward us. Bestow upon us abundant wealth that overcomes enemies, and grant us a glorious portion accompanied by fair renown.

These ancient births of yours, O Agni, and these new ones, I have proclaimed to you, the primordial one. These great libations have been prepared for the Bull; in every birth, Jātavedas has been established.
In birth after birth, Jātavedas, established by the Viśvāmitras, is kindled perpetually. May we abide in the favor of that one worthy of sacrifice, and in his auspicious goodwill.
O powerful one, O wise one, bestowing gifts, place this sacrifice of ours among the gods. O Hotṛ, Agni, grant us abundant nourishments; through sacrifice, win for us great wealth.
O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you the *iḷā*—the gift of cattle, wondrous and most enduring.
May there be to us a son, a spreading progeny; O Agni, let that benevolence of yours be with us.
For Vaiśvānara Agni, who increases the cosmic order (*ṛta*), we fashion our prayer like purified clarified butter;
twice over, the human priests and singers fashion him with their thought, as a craftsman fashions a chariot with an axe.
By his very birth, he illumined both worlds; he became the praiseworthy son of his two mothers.
Agni, the bearer of oblations, ageless and well-disposed, the invincible guest of the people, is rich in radiant light.
By the power of their skillful will, according to the ordinance of the victorious one, the gods generated Agni through their thoughts.
Desiring to win the prize like a swift steed, I address him who shines with luster and great light.

Desiring to win, we choose from the delightful one that which is most excellent, the unashamed, praiseworthy strength; Agni, the gift of the Bhr̥gus, the eager one with the insight of a seer, who reigns with his divine radiance.

For the sake of bliss, people who have spread the sacrificial grass here have placed Agni at their head—him whose fame is won through strength, the one with the beautiful luster, common to all the gods, the Rudra of sacrifices, who fulfills the desires of those who perform the work. With uplifted ladles, they have established him.
O Purifier of Radiance, O Hotṛ, for around your dwelling at the sacrifices, men who have trimmed the sacrificial grass seek your friendship;
desiring your favor, O Agni, they wait upon you for wealth—bestow riches upon them.
He filled the two worlds and the great sky when he was born, as the skillful ones sustained him.
He, the sage, is led forth for the sacrifice like a steed set loose for the winning of booty.
Worship him who accepts the oblation; honor the domestic Jātavedas who performs the sacrifice well.
Agni, the charioteer of the lofty cosmic order, the one who beholds all people, has become the domestic priest of the gods.
The immortal *uśijaḥ* purified the three fuel-sticks of the mighty, encompassing Agni;
of these, they placed one as sustenance for mortals, while two entered the world of kinship.
The human offerings have sharpened him, the sage of the people and lord of the clans, like an axe for its keenness.
He goes to the heights and the depths, busily active; he has established his seed within these worlds.
Having been born, he stirs within the bellies, like a roaring lion, a bull among the variegated ones. Vaiśvānara, the immortal one of broad radiance, bestows goods and treasures upon the donor.

Vaiśvānara has ascended to the vault of heaven, the back of the sky, as of old, being glorified by those of good intent. Like the ancients, generating wealth for living beings, he, the watchful one, goes around the common course.

The upholder of *ṛta*, worthy of sacrifice, the inspired sage deserving of praise, whom Mātariśvan established as a dweller in heaven—him we implore: Agni, whose path is wondrous, whose hair is golden, the brightly shining one, for new-found prosperity.

Like the pure one on his path, the impetuous, the beholder of heaven, the banner of the sky stationed in the luminous realm, awakening at dawn—Agni, the head of heaven, the unassailable, the possessor of great strength; him we implore with prostration.

We ever seek for wealth that delightful Hotṛ, the pure one, free from duplicity, the domestic friend, worthy of praise, who belongs to all people; like a brilliant chariot, beautiful to behold, established by Manu, we pray for him.
For Vaiśvānara, whose belly is broad, they have offered inspired songs as jewels so that he may go to his foundations;
for the immortal Agni honors the gods, and thus he has not violated the eternal laws.
The wondrous messenger moves between the two worlds, seated as the Hotṛ-priest appointed by man;
Agni, impelled by the gods and rich in wisdom, adorns his vast dwelling day by day.
The sages have magnified Agni with their thoughts—the banner of sacrifices, the accomplisher of the assembly—in whom they have concentrated their works and their songs;
in him, the sacrificer seeks blessings.
Father of sacrifices, lord of the wise, Agni is the measure and the means of knowledge for the officiating priests;
he has entered the two worlds of manifold forms, and the sage, beloved by many, is glorified through his manifestations.

The gods have established here the radiant Agni, who possesses a radiant chariot, whose laws are golden, who dwells in the waters, who finds the light of heaven, who plunges forward, who is swift, who is encompassed by powers, and who is impetuous and most glorious.

Agni, spreading the sacrifice richly adorned with wisdom through the gods and the human race, moves as a charioteer between them with successful offerings; he is the swift master of the house, the dispeller of curses.
O Agni, awaken us for a life rich in noble offspring; swell us with vigor and shine food upon us.
Quicken our progeny and the great ones, O watchful one; you are the yearning desire of the gods, the wise seer of inspired songs.

The men always praise with reverence and with incitements for their own prosperity Jātavedas— the lord of the people, the mighty guest, the leader of prayers, the eager one of the sacrificers, and the conscious witness of the rituals.
Radiant, a god who brings joy, Agni has encompassed the dwellings with his power, he whose chariot is auspicious.
May we, in our home, honor the ordinances of him who nourishes many, with well-fashioned hymns.

O Vaiśvānara, I long for your powers by which you became the finder of heaven, O far-seeing one; as soon as you were born, you filled the worlds and the two realms, O Agni—you encompass all those things by your own self.
By his skillful work, the solitary sage has brought forth a great song from the wondrous deeds of Vaiśvānara;
magnifying both his parents, Agni was born from Heaven and Earth, who are rich in seed.
At every kindling of the fuel, be well-disposed toward us; at every flash of light, bestow upon us the favor of wealth.
O God, bring the gods here for the sacrifice; as a friend, O Agni, worship the friends with a gracious mind.
O Tanūnapāt, whom the gods— Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni— worship thrice a day, day after day,
do thou make this sacrifice of ours honey-sweet for us, even for the one who honors thee and whose source is ghee.
The prayer, containing all desirable things, goes forth first to worship the Hotṛ of the *iḷā* offering;
with homages, one approaches to praise the Bull. May he, the most excellent sacrificer, being impelled, perform the sacrifice for the gods.
Upright has your path been made for the sacrifice; upright have the flames ascended through the regions.
Or rather, the Hotṛ has sat down at the navel of heaven; we spread out the sacrificial grass, wide enough to encompass the gods.
Choosing the seven priestly offices with their minds, impelling all things, they come hither according to the *ṛta*;
adorned by men, born at the assemblies, they have entered this sacrifice in their many forms.
When the two Dawns, near at hand, are being praised, they smile with their bodies though they are of different forms,
so that Mitra and Varuṇa may be pleased with us, and Indra with the Maruts by his great powers.
I honor the two divine Hotṛ-priests first; the seven nourishers rejoice according to their own nature.
Praising the *ṛta*, they speak only of the *ṛta*, as guardians of the vow, meditating upon the sacred law.
May Bhāratī, in harmony with the Bhāratīs; Iḷā with the gods; and Agni with men;
and Sarasvatī with the Sarasvates—may these three goddesses sit together upon this sacred grass.
O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, being gracious, release for us that generative seed which nourishes,
from which is born a hero— skillful in action, highly dexterous, a preparer of the pressing-stones, and a lover of the gods.
O Lord of the Forest, release [the oblation] toward the gods; let Agni, the immolator, prepare the offering.
He, the most truthful Hotṛ, shall sacrifice, for he knows the generations of the gods.
Come hither, O Agni, being kindled, on the same chariot with Indra and the swift gods.
Let Aditi, mother of noble sons, sit upon our sacred grass; let the immortal gods rejoice in the *svāhā*!

Agni, the inspired sage and leader of the seers, has awakened, shining forth toward the dawns. With broad radiance, kindled by those seeking the gods, the bearer of oblations has thrown open the doors of darkness.

Agni has grown strong before us through the praises, songs, and hymns of his worshippers—he who is worthy of homage. Delighting in the many manifestations of the Eternal Order (Ṛta), he has shone forth as the messenger at the dawning of the dawn.
Agni has been established among the human tribes, the offspring of the waters, fulfilling his purpose through the *ṛta* like Mitra.
The beloved and worshipful one has taken his place upon the high ridge; he has become the inspired sage, to be invoked by our hymns.
Agni becomes Mitra when he is kindled; Mitra is the Hotṛ, Varuṇa is Jātavedas.
Mitra is the vigorous Adhvaryu, the friend of the household; Mitra is [the lord] of the rivers and of the mountains.
He guards the beloved summit of the bird, the enemy’s foremost station; the mighty one guards the course of the sun.
At the navel, Agni guards the seven-headed one; the lofty one guards the delight of the gods.
The Ṛbhu fashioned for himself a beautiful name worthy of praise, he the god who knows all ways;
he guards that very place, the skin of the plant and the footstep rich in ghee, Agni, never failing.
Agni has taken his place at the ghee-rich womb, wide-extending and longing, he who longs for it;
shining, pure, lofty, and purifying, he makes his two parents ever new again and again.
As soon as born, he grew by means of the plants when the sprouts nourish him with clarified butter;
like waters gliding down a slope, Agni has found wide space in the lap of his parents.
Praised with kindled fuel, the mighty one has shone forth from the height of heaven, at the navel of the earth.
Agni is Mitra, worthy of invocation; as Mātariśvan, may he, the messenger, carry the gods here for the sacrifice.
The lofty Agni, becoming the highest of the luminous realms,
propped up the firmament with his fuel when Mātariśvan kindled the oblation-bearer who was hidden from the Bhr̥gus.
O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you a nourishing gift of cattle, wondrous and most enduring.
May there be for us a son, a spreading progeny; O Agni, let that benevolence of yours be with us.
O singers, being urged by your thoughts, you who seek the gods lead her toward the gods.
Carrying sacrificial gifts, rich in strength, she goes eastward; ladling with ghee, she brings the oblation to Agni.
At your birth, you filled the two worlds, O most worshipful one, and indeed you have transcended them;
by your greatness, O Agni, let your seven-tongued carriers of oblations reach even beyond heaven and earth.
Heaven and Earth, and the worshipful gods, establish you as the Hotṛ priest for the home,
when the human clans, seeking the gods and offering nourishment, praise your bright flame.
The great one is seated firmly in the assembly hall, between the two mighty worlds, being desired;
the two co-wives, unaging and inviolate, the two cows that yield nectar, belong to him who strides widely.
O Agni, your vows are great, the vows of the Great One; by your wisdom you have stretched out the two worlds, heaven and earth.
At your birth you became the messenger; you, O Bull, are the leader of the peoples.
Or rather, yoke to the pole with the driving-rods the two long-maned, ruddy steeds of Truth that drip with clarity;
then, O God, bring hither all the gods, and make our sacrifice successful, O Jātavedas.
Even from heaven thy lights have shone forth; thou outshinest the many dawns as they break.
O Agni, when thou burnest eagerly for the waters in the woods, the gods marvel at the joyous Hotṛ-priest.
Whether they are the gods who rejoice in the wide mid-air, or those who dwell in the luminous realm of heaven;
or those helpful, adorable ones who are easy to invoke—O Agni, let the chariot-horses draw them hither.
Come hither with these, O Agni, on one chariot or on various chariots, for your horses are powerful;
bring the thirty-three gods accompanied by their wives according to your wont, and rejoice!
He is the Hotṛ-priest at whose sacrifice even the two wide worlds, Heaven and Earth, praise him for the prosperity of every rite;
they stand facing forward like well-established sacrificial paths, the two well-formed, law-abiding ones, true to the Law-born.
O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you the *iḷā*—the gift of cattle, wondrous and most enduring.
May there be to us a son, a spreading offspring; O Agni, let that benevolence of yours be with us.

Those who have ascended from the nourishment of the white-backed one have entered the two parents and the seven voices. The two parents, dwelling around, move together; they glide forth toward long life for the sake of manifestation.
The milch-cows dwelling in heaven, the mares of the bull—divine, they have approached him, carrying sweetness.
In the seat of *ṛta*, the one cow moves around you who bring peace, following your path.
He, the wise lord and finder of riches, mounted them as they became easy to control;
he of the dark back and many-formed countenance caused them to dwell upon the food of the brushwood.
The mighty, ageless, and strengthening [waters] carry him who is being propped up;
flashing with his limbs in the place of assembly, he has entered the two worlds as if they were one.

They know the auspiciousness of the ruddy bull, and they rejoice under the command of Bradhna; they shine with celestial luster, radiant and resplendent, for whom the nourishing and mighty song belongs to the host.
And so they proclaimed aloud the roar of the two great parents, their mighty strength,
when the Bull, at the conclusion of the night, has grown strong according to his own nature for the singer.
Seven sages, together with five *adhvaryu* priests, guard the beloved, hidden station of the Bird.
Moving forward, the ageless bulls rejoice; for as gods, they have followed the ordinances of the gods.
I honor the two divine Hotṛ-priests first; the seven nourishers rejoice according to their own nature.
Praising the *ṛta*, they speak only of the *ṛta*—the guardians of the vow, meditating upon the sacred law in accordance with its ordinance.
The many reins, easy to guide, act like stallions for the great steed, for the wonderful bull.
O divine Hotṛ, most delightful and wise, bring hither the great gods and the two worlds, Rodasī.
The dawns, rich in food, worthy of sacrifice, possessing fine speech and fair splendor, have shone forth with wealth.
And so, O Agni, by the greatness of the earth, forgive even the sin that has been committed, for our great welfare.
O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you the *iḷā*—the gift of cattle, most wondrous and most constant.
May there be to us a son, a spreading progeny; O Agni, may that benevolence of yours be with us.
O Lord of the Forest, those seeking the gods anoint you with divine honey at the sacrifice.
Whether you stand upright and bestow wealth here, or whether you dwell in the lap of this mother earth, grant us riches.
Standing before the kindled fire, winning for us the unaging, heroic prayer (*brahman*), driving far away from us all lack of understanding— rise up for our great good fortune!
Rise up, O Lord of the Forest, upon the height of the earth;
being measured with perfect skill, bestow splendor upon the one who carries the sacrifice.
A youth, well-attired and girt with the sacrificial cord, has come; he becomes even more excellent as he is born.
Wise poets, seeking the gods with devout minds and pious thoughts, lead him forward.
Born, he is born again on the auspiciousness of days, increasing at the assembly and the sacrifice;
the wise, skillful ones purify him with their inspired thought; the seer, seeking the gods, raises up his voice.
O Lord of the Forest, those whom the god-seeking men have set up, or whom the axe has carved out— you,
O gods who dwell in the light and stand firm, may you bestow upon us wealth accompanied by progeny.
Those which have been cut upon the earth, set up with uplifted ladles— may they,
who prosper the field, win for us what is desirable among the gods.

May the Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus, the excellent leaders; may Heaven and Earth, the broad Earth, and the Mid-region—may these gods, being of one accord, protect the sacrifice and raise high the banner of the rite.
Like swans moving in rows, the sacrificial posts have come to us, clothed in brilliance;
being raised up by the sages in the east, they go as gods to the path of the gods.
Like the horns of horned animals, the sacrificial posts with their head-pieces appear upon the earth;
listening to us at the invocation by the invoking priests, may they protect us in the contests for booty.
O Lord of the Forest, grow forth with a hundred branches; may we grow forth with a thousand branches—yea, you whom this sharpened axe has brought forward for great good fortune.
O friends, we mortals have chosen you as our god for protection—
the Son of the Waters, the fortunate one, of splendid luster, the swift victor, free from blemish.
When you, desiring the woods, went to your mothers, the waters—
that turning back of yours, O Agni, when you were far away yet became present here, cannot be effaced.
You have grown beyond the harsh; thus indeed you are well-disposed. Some go forth ever further, while others sit around, in whose friendship you are established.
Having passed beyond all failures and beyond all perpetual pursuers,
the observant and guileless ones found him who had taken refuge in the waters, like a lion.
Like one who has run his course by his own nature, Agni was thus hidden away;
Mātariśvan brought him hither from afar, having churned him out from among the gods.
The mortals have grasped you, O bearer of oblations to the gods,
since you, O youngest one, protect all sacrifices with your wisdom, O friend of man.
That auspicious wondrous power of yours reveals itself even to the simple-minded,
O Agni, when the cattle gather around you as you are kindled at the close of day.
Offer oblations to the one who performs the fair sacrifice, the sharp one with purifying luster;
serve the god with obedience—the swift, agile, ancient messenger who is worthy of praise.
Three thousand, three hundred, thirty, and nine gods have honored Agni;
they have sprinkled him with clarified butter, they have strewn the sacrificial grass for him, and then they have seated him as the Hotṛ-priest.
O Agni, the wise mortals kindle you, the god and sovereign lord of all people, at the sacrifice.
In the sacrifices, they invoke you, O Agni, as the officiating priest and the Hotṛ;
shine as the guardian of the Cosmic Order within your own abode.
He indeed who offers to you, O Jātavedas, with kindled fuel—he, O Agni, possesses great heroic strength; he prospers.
May Agni, the banner of sacrifices, come with the gods; being anointed by the seven hotṛ-priests, he approaches the one who offers the oblation.
Bring forth a lofty, ancient word for Agni, the Hotṛ-priest, who,
like a wise ordainer, bears the lights of inspired songs.
May our songs increase Agni, from whom the praiseworthy one was born—
the beautiful one, for the sake of great strength and wealth.
O Agni, best of sacrificers at the ritual, worship the gods for the one who seeks the gods; as the joyous Hotṛ-priest, you shine forth beyond all failures.
O Purifier, shine upon us with glorious and heroic strength;
be most intimate to those who praise you for our well-being.
The inspired poets, praising you and remaining vigilant, kindle you—
the immortal bearer of oblations, the increaser of strength.
Agni is the invoker, the domestic priest of the sacrifice, the all-seeing; he knows the ritual in its proper sequence.
He, the immortal bearer of oblations, the eager messenger who is well-disposed,
Agni, brings all things together through our prayer.
Agni, the ancient banner of the sacrifice, takes heed through our prayer;
for his purpose is to carry us across.
The gods have made Agni— the son of strength, renowned from of old, Jātavedas— their bearer.
Agni, the undeceivable leader of the human tribes,
is a swift chariot, ever new.
Overcoming all assailants, the unimpaired will-power of the gods— Agni is most highly renowned.
Through his vehicle, the mortal who offers oblations attains the sacrificial foods and the dwelling of the one with purifying luster.
May we, the inspired singers, through our prayers obtain all the well-established [blessings] of Agni Jātavedas.
O Agni, may we win all desirable things in the contests for booty;
in you the gods have placed their power.
O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed juice with our songs, to the desirable cloud;
drink of this, impelled by our prayer.
O Indra and Agni, the conscious sacrifice goes forth together with the singer;
through this [hymn], drink this pressed soma.
I choose Indra and Agni, who delight in the seers, with the impulse of the sacrifice;
may they both satisfy themselves here with the soma.
I invoke the two impetuous slayers of Vṛtra, the victorious and unconquered,
Indra and Agni, the greatest winners of booty.
The chanters, skilled in hymns and knowing the ways of song, sing forth to you both;
O Indra and Agni, I choose nourishing food.
O Indra and Agni, with a single deed, you both shook down ninety forts belonging to the Dāsas as their masters.
O Indra and Agni, from the work of the waters, the inspired thoughts proceed along the paths of Eternal Order.
O Indra and Agni, yours are powerful abodes and sacrificial offerings; your crossing of the waters has been prepared.
O Indra and Agni, you adorn the luminous realms of heaven for the sake of spoils;
that heroic deed of yours is well known.
I shall sing forth for you the most exalted hymn to this god Agni;
may he come to us with the gods, and as the best of sacrificers, may he sit upon our sacred grass.
He who is the upholder of cosmic order (*ṛtāvā*), whose skillful power both heaven and earth attend,
him the offerers of oblations invoke, seeking to win his protection.
He is the guide of these inspired singers; for he is indeed the master of sacrifices.
Pay homage to that Agni of yours, who is the giver and the winner of wealth.
May Agni grant us most peaceful protections for our enjoyment,
from which he may shower wealth upon us in heaven, among the dwellings, and in the waters.
The chanters kindle Agni—the resplendent, the peerless—with his excellent thoughts; they enkindle him as the Hotṛ-priest, the lord of the people, of the clans.
And may you, O Brahman, most invoked by the gods, protect us during our hymns;
O Agni, increased by the Maruts, shine upon us for our welfare as the greatest winner of thousands.
Now grant us, O Agni, wealth consisting of thousands, offspring, and prosperity— glorious, rich in heroic strength, most excellent, and undecaying.
The joyous Hotṛ has taken his place at the assemblies; he is the true sacrificer, the most wise, the ordainer.
Agni, whose chariot is lightning, the son of strength, with flaming hair, has spread his brilliance over the earth.
I offer this word of homage to you; accept it, O observer of Truth, for you are mindful, O powerful one.
Knowing, bring hither the wise ones; sit down upon the sacred grass in the midst, O worshipful one, for our protection.
May the two Dawns, seeking booty, hasten toward you, O Agni, along the paths of the wind;
when they anoint the ancient one with oblations, they stand in the dwelling like two riders upon a chariot-seat.
O powerful Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa, as well as all the Maruts, sing your song of favor,
so that with your flame, O son of strength, you may stand over the dwellings, spreading out men like the sun.

We have indeed fulfilled your desire today, having approached you with uplifted hands and with reverence. O Agni, as a sage (*vipra*), worship the gods with a most sacrificial mind and with an unfailing thought.
For from you, O Son of Strength, many aids of the god go forth, as do his spoils of victory.
Grant us thousandfold wealth, O Agni, through your truthful word that is free from guile.
