The gift of treasure from the Ṛbhus has arrived here; there has been the drinking of the well-pressed Soma, since by your skillful work and dexterity you fashioned the single chalice into four.
"You have fashioned the chalice into four parts," he said, "O friend, teach us how! Then, O Vājas, you R̥bhus with skillful hands, reached the path of immortality, the assembly of the gods.
Of what material was this ladle made, which you fashioned into four by your wisdom?
Now press out the libation for exhilaration; drink, O Ṛbhus, of the honeyed Soma.
By your skillful power you made your parents young again; by your skillful power you fashioned the chalice for the drinking of the gods.
By your skillful power, O Ṛbhus, possessors of the treasure of booty, you fashioned the two bay steeds that carry Indra and win the prize.
O Vājās, for him who presses for you at the close of days this strong libation for exhilaration—
O Ṛbhus, O bulls, rejoicing, fashion for him wealth consisting of all heroic sons.
O Lord of the Bay Horses, you drank the pressed juice in the morning; the midday libation is yours alone.
Drink now together with the *Ṛbhus*, the bestowers of jewels—those whom you, O Indra, have made your friends through your noble deeds.
O gods who have become perfected through good deeds, who sit upon the heaven like falcons; O sons of Śavas, sons of Sudhanvan, bestow wealth upon us—you have become immortal.

O Ṛbhus, you who are deft-handed and skillful, that third libation which you fashioned as a bestowal of treasure—that has been poured out for you; drink it together with your exhilarating, Indra-like powers.
Born without horses and without reins, the praiseworthy three-wheeled chariot rolls around the realm.
O Ṛbhus, that proclamation of your divine power is great, in that you nourish both heaven and earth.

O Vājas and Ṛbhus, you who with wise intent and through the meditation of the mind fashioned a well-rolling chariot that does not waver, we now announce you for the drinking of this libation at this sacrifice.
O Vājas and Ṛbhus, that greatness of yours among the gods has become worthy of high praise,
O Vibhūs, since you fashioned your aged parents— who were worn out by years— once more into youths for the sake of movement.
You made the single chalice fourfold; by your insights, you brought forth the cow from the hide.
Then, through your readiness, O Vājas and Ṛbhus, you attained immortality among the gods—this deed of yours is worthy of praise.
From the *Ṛbhus* comes wealth most renowned; that which the heroes, famed for their vigor, have generated.
Fashioned by *Vibhvan*, it is to be proclaimed at the assemblies—he whom you gods protect is the one who observes all people.
He is the prize-winning steed; he is the seer through his eloquence; he is the hero, the archer, invincible in battles.
He possesses the increase of wealth and true heroic might—him whom Vāja, Vibhvan, and the Ṛbhus have aided.
The most excellent and beautiful ornament has been placed upon you; O Vājas and Ṛbhus, take pleasure in this hymn of praise.
For you are wise, seers, and inspired poets; as such, we make ourselves known to you with this sacred prayer.
From your inspired thoughts (*dhiṣaṇā*), you who are wise, [bestow] upon us all manly enjoyments;
O *Ṛbhus*, fashion for us resplendent strength, most excellent vigor, wealth, and vitality.
Bestowing upon us offspring here and wealth here, fashion for us a fame accompanied by heroic sons;
O Ṛbhus, grant us that wonderful prize by which we may distinguish ourselves above others.
O Vājas, R̥bhukṣans, and gods, come to our sacrifice by the paths traveled by the gods,
just as you have accepted the sacrifice among these human clans, O joyful ones, on the auspicious days of the year.
May these sacrifices be pleasing to your heart and mind; may they, adorned with ghee, go forth today as offerings you enjoy.
May the pressed juices, full to the brim, delight you; when drunk, may they exhilarate you for wisdom and skill.
O Vājas, O Ṛbhukṣans, just as this threefold rising praise, ordained by the gods,
has been offered to you, so do I, like Manu, pour out Soma for you among the later clans dwelling in the high heaven.

O you who have fat horses, bright chariots, iron helmets, and golden ornaments—you swift ones—O sons of Indra, O grandsons of strength, this foremost [draught] has been prepared for your exhilaration; may it be pleasing to you.

O lords of the *Ṛbhus*, we invoke for the sake of booty the *Ṛbhu*— the possessor of wealth, the most victorious ally in battle— who is accompanied by Indra, who is ever most successful, and who possesses the *Aśvins*.
O Ṛbhus, that mortal whom you and Indra protect— may he be a winner through his inspired thoughts at the winning of wisdom, and may he be successful with his steed.
O Vājas, O Ṛbhukṣans, find for us the paths so that we may sacrifice;
O wise ones, being praised, enable us to cross over all directions.
O Vājas, O Ṛbhukṣans, O Indra, O Nāsatyas, bestow upon us that wealth and horses from among the people; praise us abundantly for the granting of riches.
For indeed, yours were the ancient gifts which Trasadasyu bestowed upon the Pūrus;
you two gave him mastery over the fields and the fertile lands, a fierce and overwhelming blow against the Dasyus.
And you two have granted us Dadhikrā, the prize-winner who overcomes many, who belongs to all people— the straight-flying,
swift hawk, dappled and fleet, worthy of praise like a noble hero and a king.
Him whom every man exults and gladdens as he rushes forth like a torrent,
him who seizes with his feet like a hero eager for spoil, who outstrips the chariot and speeds like the wind— him [the Maruts] follow.

He who, obstructing the foe in battles, moves forward as a conqueror, going among the cattle; manifest and straight-acting, he has observed the assemblies, passing beyond the obstruction of the mortal man.
And indeed, the people cry out after him in battles as if after a thief who steals a garment;
he who stoops low like a weary falcon, yet rushes toward glory and toward the herd of cattle.
And he, about to race as the first among us, speeds along with rows of chariots;
like a handsome suitor preparing his garland, he licks the dust, tossing up the spray as he gallops.
And this vigorous steed, victorious, faithful to the cosmic order, listening with his whole body in the battle,
speeding among those who speed, straight-flying as he rushes forward, stirs up the dust above his brows.
And at his roar, as if from the sky, those who attack him tremble in fear when he is wrathful; when he fights against a thousand, he becomes irresistible and terrible as he advances.
And indeed, people praise his impetuous speed, the overwhelming might of the swift one who wins the land.
And of him they say, as they disperse in the encounter: "Dadhikrā has sped away with thousands."
Dadhikrā has overspread the five peoples with his power, as the sun with its light overspreads the waters.
May the prize-winning steed, winner of thousands and hundreds, fill these words with sweetness.
Let us now praise that swift Dadhikrā; let us also celebrate him who belongs to heaven and earth.
May the dawning Dawns inspire me; may they carry me across all difficulties.
I celebrate the great deeds of the steed Dadhikrāvan, the boon-bestowing bull who fulfills our intentions—
him whom you two, O Mitra and Varuṇa, gave to the Pūrus, shining like Agni and victorious.
May Aditi make him sinless— he who has offered praise for the horse Dadhikrāvan when the fire is kindled at the dawning of the Uṣas— being in harmony with Mitra and Varuṇa.
We have meditated upon the food and the great strength of Dadhikrāvan, and upon the auspicious name of the Maruts.
For our well-being, we invoke Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, and Indra, who wields the thunderbolt in his arm.
Like Indra, both sides invoke him as they rise up and proceed toward the sacrifice;
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you have granted us the horse Dadhikrā, the benefactor for mortals.
I have celebrated Dadhikrāvan, the victorious, the spirited horse;
may he make our mouths fragrant and may he prolong our lives.
Let us now celebrate Dadhikrāvan; may all the dawns inspire me.
[May he inspire me] with the waters, Agni, the dawn, Sūrya, and Bṛhaspati, the victorious son of Aṅgiras.
May the being who nourishes, who seeks cattle, who is worthy of worship, and who hastens toward the food of the dawn for the sake of glory,
the true one, the swift runner, the mover, the bird-like one— may Dadhikrāvan generate food, strength, and the light of heaven.
And indeed, as he runs and hastens, eager for the prize, the wind blows after him like the wing of a bird;
as Dadhikrāvan speeds along with his might, he passes through the curve like a swooping eagle.
And this vigorous steed, bound by the neck, at the flanks, and in the mouth, hastens toward the whip;
Dadhikrā, displaying his strength, has leaped along the curves of the paths.
The swan dwelling in the pure realm, the Vasu dwelling in the mid-air, the Hotṛ-priest dwelling at the altar, the guest dwelling in the house;
dwelling among men, dwelling in the best of places, dwelling in the Truth, dwelling in the sky; born of the waters, born of the kine, born of the Truth, born of the mountains—the Truth itself.
O Indra and Varuṇa, what hymn accompanied by oblations has reached you for favor— like an immortal Hotar-priest—
that inspired prayer, uttered by us with reverence, may touch your hearts, O Indra and Varuṇa?

The mortal who, providing sacrificial food, has made Indra and Varuṇa his allies for friendship—those two gods—he slays his enemies, the Vṛtras, in battles; through their great protections, he becomes renowned.
Indra and Varuṇa are indeed the most liberal bestowers of treasure upon the men who labor for them;
when they, as friends for friendship's sake, delight themselves with pressed Soma juices and abundant food.
O Indra and Varuṇa, you two fierce ones, hurl your most powerful bolt against this one who is evil-minded toward us, the wolf-like Dabhīti; measure out your overwhelming might upon him.
O Indra and Varuṇa, become the lovers of this prayer, as two bulls are of a cow. May she yield for us like a great cow that has gone to pasture, with a thousand streams of milk.
For our offspring, for our well-placed progeny, for fertile fields, for the sight of the sun, and for manly heroism—
may Indra and Varuṇa be ours here with their protections, O wonder-workers, in the decisive struggle.
For it is you two alone, the abundant ones, who are well-disposed toward us for our ancient protection; we choose you for dear friendship, O heroes, most liberal, bringing bliss like parents.

These prayers of ours, seeking strength for your protection, have gone forth like racers longing for you, O bounteous givers. Like cows approaching the soma for its glory, my songs and inspired thoughts have come to Indra and Varuṇa.
These my inspired thoughts have gone forth to Indra and Varuṇa, seeking wealth;
they have approached them like those who delight in riches, like swift mares seeking a share of glory.
May we ourselves be masters of the prosperity of horses and chariots, and of eternal wealth. May they, performing their aids with ever-newer help, attend us with riches and teams of horses.

Come to us, O Great Ones, with your mighty aids, O Indra and Varuṇa, in the struggle for booty. When the flashing arrows play in the battles, may we be the winners of that prize in the contest through you both.
Twice over is the kingdom mine, the Kṣatriya’s, as all the immortals have ordained for Viśvāyu.
The gods follow the will of Varuṇa; I rule over the people, the most excellent enclosure.
I am King Varuṇa; for me those first divine powers were established. The gods follow the will of Varuṇa; I rule over the people, over the highest dwelling-place.
I am Indra and Varuṇa through our greatness; the two vast, deep, well-established realms are ours.
Like Tvaṣṭṛ, knowing all beings, I have brought the two worlds together and uphold them.
I caused the swelling waters to flow; I supported heaven in the seat of *ṛta*.
By *ṛta*, the son of Aditi, a protector of *ṛta*, has spread out the earth in its threefold expanse.
Men seeking booty with their own horses call upon me when they are hemmed in by the enemy in battle.
I, Indra, the bounteous one, create the fray; I, possessed of surpassing strength, raise up the dust.
I have performed all these deeds; no divine power can restrain me, the irresistible one.
When the Soma juices exhilarate me and when I am praised with hymns, both the boundless realms of space tremble in fear.
All beings know this of you; as such, O Ordainer, you proclaim these things to Varuṇa.
You are renowned for having slain the Vṛtras; you, O Indra, have set free the obstructed rivers.
Our fathers were here, those seven seers, when Durgaha was being bound;
they sacrificed for this Trasadasyu, who was like Indra, the subduer of Vṛtra, the demi-god.
For Purukutsānī served you both with oblations and with homages, O Indra and Varuṇa;
therefore, you two gave her King Trasadasyu, the slayer of Vṛtra, the demi-god.
May we, having won wealth, rejoice in it, as the gods do in the oblation and the cattle in pasture;
O Indra and Varuṇa, grant us every day that cow who never falters.
Who shall hear us? Which one among those worthy of sacrifice? Which god will take pleasure in our praise?
To whose heart shall we offer this divine, most beloved hymn of beautiful praise, accompanied by excellent oblations, among the immortals?
Who will show mercy? Which one is most ready to come? And which among the gods is the most beneficent?
Whom do they call the swift chariot with running horses, whom the daughter of the Sun chose?
For you two come swiftly on such days as these, like Indra exerting his power in the decisive struggle.
Born from heaven, divine birds of beautiful wings—by what power among powers do you become most mighty?
What kind of approach has been for you? By what means, O Aśvins, do you come when you are invoked?
Who among us, even in the face of great abandonment, have you protected? O Madhvīs, O Dasras, [come] to us with your aid!

Broad is your chariot as it reaches across the sky when it turns back from the ocean. O lovers of sweetness, honey flows for you; when they have cooked the sacrificial foods for you, they sprinkle them with honey.
The Sindhu indeed sprinkled your horses with the Rasā; the ruddy birds flew around from the heat.
That swift vehicle of yours was well-known, by which you became the two husbands of Sūryā.
Whatever I have here and there offered to you both together, may this be for us a favor, O you who possess wealth as your prize! Protect the singer; for our desire, O Nāsatyas, is fixed upon you.
O Aśvins, we invoke today that chariot of yours which has a wide course, the gathering-place of the cow;
it which carries Sūryā on its seat, is praised by songs, is most abundant, and seeks wealth.
O Aśvins, you two win that glory from the gods; O sons of Heaven, you win it by your powers. Your wondrous form is attended by nourishments when your lofty steeds draw you in the chariot.
Who today, having offered oblations, will bring you both with hymns for aid or for the drinking of the pressed juice?
Or who, offering homage, will turn you toward him, O Aśvins, as he seeks the ancient lover of the Eternal Order (Ṛta)?
O Nāsatyas, you who exist in many places, come to this sacrifice on your golden chariot;
drink of the honeyed Soma and bestow treasure upon the person who honors you.
Come to us from heaven and from earth upon your golden, well-rolling chariot!
Let not other seekers of the gods detain you, for our ancient kinship with you has been established.
Now, O wonder-workers, measure out for us great wealth consisting of many heroes among both our groups;
since the men of the Ājamīḷha clan have brought you praise, O Aśvins, they have come to this joint hymn of praise.
Whatever I have here and there offered to you both together, may this be for us a favor, O you whose treasure is booty! Protect the singer; for our desire, O Nāsatyas, is directed toward you.
This very light rises up; the chariot is harnessed, it that travels around upon the ridge of this heaven.
Within it are three nourishing pairs; the fourth, the leather bag, overflows with honey.
Your nourishing, honey-sweet offerings rise up; your chariots and horses [speed forth] at the dawning of the Uṣas.
Uncovering the darkness that enveloped it, they spread the bright light through the mid-air like the sun.
Drink of the honey with your honey-drinking mouths; moreover, harness your dear chariot for the sake of the honey.
You quicken the tracks and the paths with honey; O Aśvins, you carry a honey-filled skin.
The swans that carry you, full of sweetness, tireless, with golden wings, rising at dawn;
plunging into the waters, exhilarating, touching the exhilarating draught—like bees to honey, you come to the libations.
Performing the sacrifice well, rich in sweetness, the fires awaken at dawn for the Aśvins at the break of day,
when the skillful one with cleansed hands has pressed the honey-sweet Soma with the stones.
The seekers of the light, shaking off [darkness] through the days, extend the bright heaven across the mid-air as if with a thread.
Even the Sun goes forth having yoked his horses; you two, by your own inherent power, perceive all the paths.

O Aśvins, I have proclaimed for you this prayer, the upholder of thought; [I proclaim] that chariot with good horses which is ageless, by which you traverse the regions in an instant toward the one who brings oblations, the swift, the liberal giver.
Drink first of the pressed sweet juices, O Vāyu, at the sacrifices;
for you are the one who drinks first.
With a hundred aids, O Vāyu, accompanied by your teams and with Indra as your charioteer, sate yourselves with the pressed soma.
O Indra and Vāyu, may a thousand bay steeds bring you both toward the offerings for the drinking of Soma.
O Indra and Vāyu, come to this chariot with its golden seat, which is well-worshipped and touches the heavens.
Come to the donor with your chariot of broad splendor;
O Indra and Vāyu, come here!
O Indra and Vāyu, this [Soma] has been pressed; drink it together with the gods in the house of the donor, being of one accord.
O Indra and Vāyu, let your journey be here; let there be your unyoking here for the drinking of the Soma.
O Vāyu, the bright first portion of the honeyed mead is offered to you at the sacrifices;
come, O desirable god, with your team of horses, for the drinking of the Soma.
O Indra and Vāyu, you two deserve the drinking of these Soma juices;
for toward you the drops flow together, like waters descending to the lowlands.
O Vāyu and Indra, you two impetuous lords of power, come on the same chariot with your teams of horses for our aid; come to drink the Soma.
O Heroes, Indra and Vāyu, those many-desired teams of yours which belong to the donor— bestow them upon us, you who bring the sacrifice.
Accept the invocations; let the prayers bring us the wealth of the noble one.
O Vāyu, come with your shining chariot to drink of the pressed juice.
Driving away the curses, O Vāyu, accompanied by your team and with Indra as your charioteer, come on your shining chariot to drink of the pressed soma.
The two dark treasuries of wealth, adorned with every ornament, have followed along;
O Vāyu, come on your shining chariot to drink of the pressed juice.
May ninety-nine horses, yoked by thought, carry you hither;
O Vāyu, come on your shining chariot to drink of the pressed juice.
O Vāyu, harness a hundred bay steeds, well-nourished and fit for you; or let your chariot come hither with its thousandfold power.
This beloved oblation is placed in your mouth, O Indra and Bṛhaspati;
the hymn and the exhilarating draught are recited.
O Indra and Bṛhaspati, this Soma is poured out for you both—
delightful for exhilaration and for drinking.
O Indra and Bṛhaspati, come to our house; O Soma-drinkers, come for the drinking of Soma.
O Indra and Bṛhaspati, bestow upon us wealth consisting of hundreds,
abounding in horses, and reaching into the thousands.
O Indra and Bṛhaspati, we invoke you with songs when the Soma is pressed,
for the drinking of this Soma.
O Indra and Bṛhaspati, drink the Soma in the house of the donor; rejoice there, you whose home is that.
Bṛhaspati, who dwells in the three abodes, has by his roar suddenly propped apart the ends of the earth;
him, the sweet-tongued one, the ancient seers, the inspired sages, have placed at the forefront with their meditations.
O Bṛhaspati, may those who, rushing like storms and rejoicing in their keen insight, have assailed us—
protect the source of this [sacrifice], the speckled, flowing, and inviolable expanse.
O Bṛhaspati, from that which is the furthest distance, those who touch the cosmic order have sat down here for you;
from the dug-out wells, milked by the stones, they drip honey toward your overflowing abundance.
Bṛhaspati, being first born from the great light in the highest heaven,
seven-mouthed and many-born, blew away the darkness with his roar by means of his seven rays.

With his well-praising, hymn-chanting host, Bṛhaspati shattered the Vala cave and the Phaliga stronghold with a roar; bellowing aloud, he drove out the lowing, ruddy cows that provide the sacrificial oblation.

Thus may we serve the Father, the one belonging to all the gods, the Mighty One, with sacrifices, with homage, and with oblations. O Bṛhaspati, may we, possessing good offspring and heroic sons, be masters of riches.

He indeed, as king, has stood firm against all hostile forces by his might and heroic power— he who maintains Bṛhaspati well-nourished, honors him, and praises him as the one who receives the first portion.
He indeed dwells well-established in his own home; for him *Iḷā* swells at all times.
To that king the subjects bow down of their own accord—in whom the Brahman goes before.
Unopposed, he conquers the wealth of his enemies as well as that of his own people—the king who creates wide space for the priest seeking his favor; him the gods protect.

O Indra and Bṛhaspati, drink the Soma, rejoicing at this sacrifice, O you who possess bull-like wealth! May the self-sustaining drops enter you both; bestow upon us riches consisting of all heroic sons.
O Bṛhaspati and Indra, prosper us together; let that benevolence of yours be with us.
Favor our prayers, awaken the wisdom of the learned, and exhaust the hostilities of the enemy and of those who would attack us.
This very light, most abundant, has risen from the darkness in the east, making the way clear. Now indeed may the daughters of heaven, the radiant dawns, create a path for mankind.
The brilliant dawns have stood in the east like the erected sacrificial posts at the rites;
shining forth, the pure and purifying ones have opened wide the two doors of the enclosure of darkness.
Shining forth today, may the wealthy Dawns awaken the liberal patrons to bestow their gifts;
let the stingy niggards sleep on within the darkness, unawakened in the midst of gloom.
O Goddesses, will that ancient or new journey of yours, O Dawns, be with us today? With that [journey] by which you, O wealthy ones, shone richly upon Navagva, Aṅgira, Daśagva, and Saptāsya.
For you, O goddesses, with your horses harnessed by the cosmic order (*ṛta*), traverse all worlds in an instant;
O Dawns, awakening the sleeping world—both bipeds and quadrupeds—to movement.
Where indeed, and which one among them is the ancient one, by whose ordinance they have fashioned the forms of the *ṛbhus*?
When the radiant Dawns move toward splendor, they are not distinguished as distinct, for they are alike and ageless.
Truly, those auspicious Dawns were there of old, possessing splendor that grants aid, born of the Eternal Order (*ṛta*), and true;
in them, the sacrificer who exerts himself with hymns, praising and chanting, immediately obtained wealth.
They move together from the east, spreading out equally from the same place;
awakening from the seat of Order, the goddesses Dawn break forth like herds of cattle.
These very Dawns now move along together, uniform and of unchanging hue;
hiding the black monster with their radiant bodies, they are bright, pure, and shining.
O divine daughters of heaven, shining forth, bestow upon us wealth accompanied by progeny;
awakening from your pleasant [presence], may we be masters of heroic power.
O Dawns, daughters of heaven, shining brightly, you who have the sacrifice as your banner, we address you with this prayer:
may we be glorious among the people; may Heaven and the Goddess Earth grant us this.
This noble lady, dawning upon her sister,
has been seen from heaven— the daughter of Day.
Like a dappled, ruddy mare, the mother of cattle, the observer of cosmic order, Uṣas has become the friend of the Aśvins.
Moreover, you are the friend of the Aśvins, and you are the mother of the cows;
and, O Uṣas, you rule over wealth.
O goddess rich in true blessings, we who are conscious of you have awakened with hymns of praise to you, who drive away all enmity.
The auspicious rays have appeared like herds of cattle;
Dawn has filled the wide expanse.
O radiant one, having filled [the world], you have dispelled the darkness with your light;
O Uṣas, protect us according to your own nature.
O Uṣas, with your bright radiance, you extend across the sky, the wide and beloved mid-air, and the atmosphere with your beams.
We choose that great and desirable gift of the god Savitṛ, the wise Asura;
by which he himself bestows protection upon the donor—may that great god extend it to us throughout the nights.
The upholder of heaven, Prajāpati, the lord of creatures, the sage, puts on his tawny mantle. Far-seeing, spreading abroad and filling the wide space, Savitar has generated praiseworthy bliss.
He has filled the celestial and terrestrial realms; the god creates a song of praise for his own law.
Savitar has stretched out his arms to impel the world, laying it to rest and setting it in motion through the nights.
Unassailable, surveying all beings, the god Savitṛ protects the sacred ordinances.
He has stretched out his arms for the creatures of the world; firm in his vows, he rules over the great course of the universe.
Savitar thrice encompasses the mid-air by his greatness; he pervades the three regions and the three luminous spheres.
He impels the three heavens and the three earths; with his three ordinances, he protects us by his own self.

Possessing great bounty, the impeller, the one who brings rest to both the moving and the stationary, he who is the lord of both— may that god Savitar grant us protection, a triple-shielded refuge from distress for our dwelling.

The god has come with the seasons; may he increase our dwelling. May Savitṛ grant us food and good progeny. May he quicken us through nights and days, and may he bestow upon us wealth accompanied by offspring.
The god Savitṛ has now become worthy of our praise;
he is to be invoked by men at this time of day, he who distributes treasures to human beings, so that he may grant us the most excellent wealth here.
For you first bestow upon the worshipful gods immortality as their supreme portion;
then, O Savitṛ, you unfold the gifts for humanity and grant them successive spans of life.
Whatever we have done unintentionally against the divine folk, through feeble skill or through human frailty,
O Savitṛ, among both gods and men, do you establish us here as sinless.
That power of the divine Savitṛ cannot be measured, by which he shall sustain the entire world;
whatever he, the fair-fingered one, brings forth truly upon the breadth of the earth and the height of heaven—that is his truth.
O Savitṛ, you bestow upon these great mountains, with Indra as their chief, dwellings provided with houses;
however they flew away and scattered, even so have they now stood still at your impulsion.
O Savitṛ, those impulses of yours which three times a day, day after day, bring us prosperity—
may Indra, Heaven and Earth, Sindhu with her waters, and Aditi with the Ādityas, grant us protection.

Who is your protector, O Vasus? Who is your defender? O Heaven and Earth, O Aditi, protect us from the more powerful mortal, O Varuṇa and Mitra! O Gods, who among you will grant wide space at our sacrifice?

Those who honor the ancient ordinances when they shine forth as unerring separators—those wise ones, whose thoughts are fixed on the *ṛta*, have established them as inexhaustible ordainers; these wonder-workers have shone forth.
With hymns I praise Aditi, the river Sindhu, and the goddess Svasti for friendship.
May both the unerring Dawn and Night, like two days, protect us.
Aryaman, Varuṇa, and Agni, the lord of nourishment, have made the path clear; may they grant us a prosperous way.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, being well praised, extend to us manly protection and powerful shelter.
I have invoked the protections of Parvata, of the Maruts, and of the god Trātṛ Bhaga.
May the Lord protect us from the distress caused by strangers; may Mitra, as a friend, deliver us from the hostility of those who seek alliance.
Now let the two goddesses, Heaven and Earth, be praised by the Dragon of the Deep with these desired libations;
like those seeking gain on the path to the ocean, they have uncovered the rivers that flow with the heat of the sun.
May the divine Aditi protect us along with the gods; may the god Trātṛ protect us without fail.
For we do not deserve to violate the ordinance of Mitra and Varuṇa, nor the summit of Agni.
Agni rules over wealth; Agni rules over great good fortune. May he bestow those things upon us.
O bountiful Uṣas, O generous one, bring many desirable things to us, O lady rich in spoils!
May Savitar, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman,
and Indra come to us with bounty.
O great Heaven and Earth, you two most excellent ones, be present here with your splendor through your radiant hymns,
when the bull, building up the two vast and wide expanses, bellows with his far-reaching movements.
The two goddesses, worshipped by the gods worthy of sacrifice, stand unaging and swelling;
they are observers of *ṛta*, free from guile, mothers of the gods, leaders of the sacrifice with their radiant hymns.
He indeed was the skillful craftsman among the worlds, he who brought these two, heaven and earth, into being;
the wise one, by his power, established the two wide, deep, well-fashioned, and pillarless realms.
Now may Rodasī, together with her husband, rejoicing and bestowing nourishment, protect us with her vast and great defenses.
O all-pervading and worshipful ones, guard us through our prayer; may we ever be chariot-borne victors.
We bring forth our great hymn of praise to you two, O Heaven and Earth, pure ones, for your glorification.
Purifying each other’s bodies through your own skillful power, you rule;
from of old, you have been carried forth according to the Eternal Law (*ṛta*).
O Great Ones, you accomplish the truth of Mitra, crossing over and fulfilling the *ṛta*;
you have taken your seats around the sacrifice.
Through the Lord of the Field, as if with a friend, may we conquer;
may he who nourishes cattle and horses be gracious to us for such a purpose.
O Lord of the Field, pour out for us a honeyed wave, as a cow yields her milk;
like well-purified ghee dripping with sweetness, may the Lords of the Eternal Order (Ṛta) be gracious to us.
May the plants be rich in sweetness, may the heavens and the waters be sweet; may the mid-air be sweet for us.
May the Lord of the Field be full of sweetness for us; may we follow him unharmed.
May the draft-animals be auspicious, may the men be auspicious; may the plough furrow auspiciously.
May the leather thongs be bound auspiciously; may you raise the goad auspiciously.
O Śuna and Sīra, may you both take pleasure in this speech; with that milk which you created in heaven, sprinkle upon this [earth].
Turn toward us, O auspicious Sītā; we revere you, so that you may be fortunate for us, so that you may bear us good fruit.
May Indra take hold of the furrow; may Pūṣan guide it.
May she, rich in milk, yield for us through each succeeding year.
May our ploughshares furrow the earth auspiciously; may the plowmen go forth auspiciously with their draft-animals.
May Parjanya [bestow] auspiciousness through honey and milk; O Śunāsīras, bestow auspiciousness upon us!
From the ocean a wave rich in sweetness has arisen; through the *upāṃśu* [cup], it has attained immortality.
That which is the secret name of clarified butter is the tongue of the gods, the navel of immortality.
Let us proclaim our names; at this sacrifice, let us uphold [the offering] of clarified butter with prostrations.
May the Brahman hear the hymn being recited; the four-horned bull has bellowed this.
Four are his horns, three are his feet, two are his heads, and seven are his hands.
Bound in three ways, the bull bellows loudly; the great god has entered into mortals.
The gods discovered the clarified butter (ghṛta) hidden in three places within the cow, concealed by the Paṇis.
Indra produced one part, Sūrya produced another, and from Vena they fashioned the third by their own inherent power.
These flow from the heart, from the ocean, in a hundred streams, not to be perceived by the enemy.
I behold the streams of clarified butter; the golden reed stands in their midst.
The streams flow perfectly like rivers, being purified within by the heart and the mind;
these waves of clarified butter surge forth like wild beasts fleeing from a swift bowman.
Like swift currents on the course of a river, the mighty streams, overtaking the wind, fly forth;
the streams of clarified butter, like a ruddy steed, break through the barriers, swelling with their waves.
Like beautiful women smiling as they go to a gathering, the streams of clarified butter have approached Agni as kindling-wood; finding pleasure in them, Jātavedas desires them.
Like maidens adorning themselves for the bridal procession, I gaze upon the ointments as they are being applied;
wherever Soma is pressed and wherever the sacrifice is performed, there the streams of clarified butter flow down in purification.
Flow toward our excellent praise in the race for cattle; bestow auspicious riches upon us.
Lead this sacrifice of ours to the gods; the streams of clarified butter flow sweetly.
Upon your abode the entire world is supported: within the ocean, within the heart, and within life.
May we attain that honeyed wave of yours, which has been brought forth at the meeting-point on the surface of the waters.
Agni has been awakened by the fuel of the people, facing the Dawn as she approaches like a milch-cow.
Like great birds soaring up toward a branch, his rays stream forth toward the vault of heaven.

The Hotṛ has been awakened for the sacrifice to the gods; Agni, well-disposed, has stood upright at dawn. The radiant luster of the kindled one has been seen; the great god has been released from the darkness.
When he has awakened the tether of the host, the pure Agni anoints himself with pure rays of light;
then the prize-winning sacrificial fee is harnessed, and standing upright, he suckles the outstretched earth with his tongues.
Toward Agni, the minds of those seeking the gods move together, as eyes toward the sun;
when the two Dawns of different forms give birth to him, the white steed is born at the beginning of days.

For the Conqueror has been born at the beginning of days; the ruddy one has been placed among the woods that are prepared. Bestowing the seven treasures in every house, Agni, the most excellent sacrificer, has sat down as the Hotṛ-priest.
Agni, the most excellent sacrificer, has sat down as the Hotṛ-priest in the lap of his mother, in the fragrant place;
he is the youthful sage, established among many, the observer of Truth, the sustainer of the peoples, kindled even in their midst.

Now they indeed magnify with prostrations that inspired priest, Agni, the Hotṛ, who is effective at the sacrifices—he who has spread across the two worlds by the Eternal Law (ṛta); they groom the vigorous one constantly with clarified butter.
The domestic friend, worthy of being groomed, is cleansed in his own home; he is the auspicious guest praised by the sages.
Like a bull with a thousand horns, possessing that same vigor, O Agni, you surpass all others by your might.
O Agni, you swiftly pass beyond others for him to whom you have become most beautiful—
worthy of praise, wondrous, radiant, the beloved guest of human clans.
To you, O youngest Agni, the peoples bring tribute from near and from afar.
Take notice of the prayer of him who praises you most; great, vast, and auspicious is your protection, O Agni.
O Agni, mount this radiant, shining chariot together with the worshipful gods;
knowing the paths, bring the gods here through the wide mid-air to eat the oblation.
We have spoken a word of praise to the sage worthy of sacrifice, to the bull, the vigorous one.
Gaviṣṭhira has offered with reverence a far-reaching hymn to Agni, like a golden ornament set in the sky.
The youthful mother carries the boy hidden away in secret; she does not yield him to the father.
His face, O people, does not diminish; they behold it placed before them in the fire.
O young woman, who is this boy whom you, the handmaid, carry? The queen has given birth to him. For the embryo grew through many autumns; I saw him born when his mother brought him forth.
I saw from afar one with golden teeth and brilliant color, fashioning his weapons from the field;
giving him the unmixed ambrosia, what can those who lack Indra and are devoid of hymns do to me?
From the field I saw him wandering from afar, like a well-fed herd, shining intensely.
They did not seize him, for he has been born; even the grey-haired women become young again.
Who are these who separate my young bull from the cattle—those for whom there was no guardian, even one who was a stranger?
May those who have seized him release him; may he, the wise one, drive the herd toward us.
The enemies have placed the King of the dwelling, the abode of people, among mortals. May the sacred prayers of Atri release him from there; let the revilers become themselves objects of revilement.
Even Śunaḥśepa, who had been bound as a victim for a thousand, you released from the sacrificial post, for he had performed his service;
even so, O Agni, release the bonds from us, O wise Hotṛ, having sat down here.
For you went away from me in anger; the guardian of the laws of the gods has told me:
"Indra, the wise one, indeed beheld you. Directed by him, O Agni, I have come here.
With his lofty light Agni shines; by his greatness he makes all things manifest.
He overcomes the godless, malevolent illusions; he sharpens his two horns to gore the Rakṣasa.
And let the roarings of Agni be in heaven, with sharp weapons to slay the Rakṣasa. Even in his exhilaration, his splendors shatter [the foe]; the godless obstructors do not hold him back.
O many-born one, I, the inspired singer, have fashioned this hymn for you, as a skillful craftsman fashions a chariot.
If you, O divine Agni, should accept it with favor, may we win through it the waters together with the light of heaven.
The bull with the thick neck, growing strong, shall gather the wealth of the enemy without a foe.
Thus have the immortals spoken to this Agni; may he grant protection to the man who spreads the sacrificial grass, may he grant protection to the man who offers oblations.
O Agni, you are born as Varuṇa; when kindled, you become Mitra. In you, O Son of Strength, dwell all the gods; you are Indra for the mortal who offers oblations.
You become Aryaman when you bear the secret name of maidens, O self-dependent one;
they anoint you like a well-established friend with milk, when you make the husband and wife of one mind.
For your glory, O Rudra, the Maruts adorn themselves, for your birth is beautiful and wondrous.
Since that supreme station of Viṣṇu has been established, by it you guard the secret name of the cows.
O God, through your splendor the gods, fair to behold, have attained immortality in abundance;
men have established Agni as the Hotṛ-priest, and the yearning ones, seeking to do honor, have seated themselves to praise the benefactor of mankind.
O Agni, no Hotṛ priest before thee has been more skilled in sacrifice; none surpasses thee in wisdom, O self-sustaining Lord.
And that mortal man whose guest thou dost become, he shall overcome all other mortals through his sacrifice, O God.
O Agni, may we, aided by you, seeking wealth and awakened by our oblation, overcome [our foes] through the sacrifice;
may we, O Son of Strength, overcome mortals with riches in the assembly and in the contests of the days.
Whoever brings guilt and sin against us, place that evil upon the one who seeks evil.
O wise Agni, strike down this curse of him who harms us with duplicity.
O God, at the breaking of this dawn, the ancients, making you their messenger, worshipped you with oblations;
for when you, O Agni, go forth at the gathering of riches, you are a god kindled by mortals along with the Vasus.
Protect the father; fight as one who knows, O son of strength, for he is considered your son. O wise Agni, when will you look upon us? When, as a knower of *ṛta*, will you set us in order?
Proclaiming many names, he, the father, offers praise, O Vasu, if you should take pleasure in that.
Will not Agni, delighting in his divine power, grant us favor as he grows ever stronger?
O Agni, most youthful one, you indeed carry your singer across all difficulties;
thieves have been seen, and the treacherous people have become those whose intentions are unknown.
These journeys have been directed toward you; or rather, this very sin has been confessed to you, O Vasu.
This Agni shall not deliver us over to reproach, nor to the one who seeks to harm us, for he, having grown strong, will not give us up.
O Agni, King, I rejoice in you, the lord of riches among all treasures, during the sacrifices. Through you, seeking booty, may we win the prize; may we overcome the hostile attacks of mortals.
Agni, the bearer of oblations, our ageless father, is pervasive, radiant, and beautiful to behold for us.
With excellent household fires, shine forth nourishments; bestow upon us glorious fame.
The sage of the people, the lord of human clans, the pure, purifying Agni whose back is anointed with ghee—you establish him as the all-knowing Hotṛ-priest; he wins desirable boons among the gods.
O Agni, being of one mind with the *iḷā* and striving together with the rays of the sun, be pleased;
O Jātavedas, accept our fuel and bring the gods here to eat the oblation.
Welcomed as the domestic friend and guest in the home, come to this our sacrifice, O wise one.
Having struck down all assailants, O Agni, bring hither the possessions of those who act as enemies.
Drive away the Dasyu with your weapon, O Agni, providing strength for your own body;
since you, O Son of Strength, bring the gods across [to us], protect us, O most heroic one, in the contest for booty.
O Agni, we would worship you with hymns; we [would worship] you with oblations, O Purifier of auspicious luster.
Send to us wealth containing all boons; bestow upon us all riches.
O Agni, son of strength, dweller in the three abodes, graciously accept our sacrifice and our oblation.
May we be doers of good among the gods; protect us with your triple-layered shelter.
O Jātavedas, carry us across all difficulties as one crosses the ocean with a boat;
O Agni, being praised with homage like Atri, be the protector of our bodies.
O Jātavedas, you whom I, a mortal, calling upon you with a humble heart, invoke as the immortal—bestow glory upon us; O Agni, may I attain immortality through progeny.
O Jātavedas Agni, for that well-doer to whom you create a pleasant world,
he shall happily attain wealth consisting of horses, sons, heroes, and cattle.
Offer strong clarified butter to the well-kindled flame,
to Agni Jātavedas.
May Narāśaṃsa, the invincible one, prepare this sacrifice;
for he is the sage who holds the honey in his hand.
O Agni, being praised, bring hither the wonderful and beloved Indra on easy-gliding chariots for our protection.
Soft as wool, spread yourself out; the hymns have resounded toward you. O radiant one, become ours for the sake of gain.
O divine Doors, open yourselves wide for our easy passage and for our protection;
fill out the sacrifice further and further.
We pray to Night and Dawn, the two young mothers of Truth, who possess beautiful countenances and increase our vital strength.
Impelled by the flight of the wind, O two divine Hotṛ-priests of man,
come to this our sacrifice.
May Iḷā, Sarasvatī, and Mahī— the three goddesses who bring delight—
sit upon the sacrificial grass, they who are unfailing.
O Tvaṣṭṛ, come here as a benefactor; as an all-pervading nourisher, protect us by your own self at every sacrifice.
O Lord of the Forest, wherever you know the secret names of the gods,
there bring our offerings.
Svāhā to Agni and Varuṇa! Svāhā to Indra and the Maruts!
Svāhā to the gods—the oblation!
I think of that Agni who is the Vasu, to whom the milch-cows go home;
to whom the swift horses go home, and the constant prize-winning steeds go home. Bring nourishment to those who praise you!

That Agni is the Vasu who is praised; unto him the milch-cows come together, the swift-running steeds come together, and the well-born patrons come together. Bring nourishment to those who sing your praise!
For Agni, the lord of all people, bestows a prize-winning steed upon the clan;
Agni grants wealth that is self-sustaining. Being well-pleased, he comes to bring what is desirable. Bring nourishment to those who praise you!
O Agni, we kindle you—the radiant, undecaying god—so that this most wondrous fuel of yours may shine in heaven; bring nourishment to those who praise you.

To you, O Agni, Lord of bright radiance, the oblation is offered with a hymn—O most radiant one, wonder-worker, Lord of the people, bearer of the sacrificial food—to you it is poured. Bring nourishment to those who praise you!
Those Agnis among the fires nourish every desirable thing;
they are urged forward, they are incited, they hasten one after another. Bring nourishment to those who praise you!
O Agni, those flames of yours have grown great and powerful; they who, with the leaps of their hooves, cause the pens of cattle to tremble. Bring nourishment to your praisers!
O Agni, bring new provisions and secure dwellings to us who praise you;
may we be those who have sung your praises, having you as our messenger in every house. Bring nourishment to those who laud you!
O you who are bright with splendor, you cook both ladles of clarified butter in your mouth;
therefore, O Lord of Might, fill us up during our hymns and bring nourishment to those who praise you.
Thus have we constantly honored this ageless Agni with songs and sacrifices.
May he bestow upon us great heroic strength and that abundance of swift horses; bring nourishment to those who praise you!
O friends, bring together for Agni— him who is the highest of the peoples, the son of strength, the mighty one— your nourishment and your hymn of praise, all directed toward him in unison.
In whose gathering men rejoice wherever they are seated among heroes;
he whom even those worthy of honor kindle, and whom living beings bring forth together.
When we gather together the food offerings and the oblations of men,
then I take hold of the ray of light, of glory, of power, and of the Eternal Order (Ṛta).
He indeed raises his banner even at night for one who stays afar;
when he, the purifier, undecaying, consumes the lords of the forest.
In whose service they pour forth sweat upon the paths, him indeed— belonging to noble kinship—
the earth has borne aloft on her back, as if upon a ridge.
Him whom the mortal man, much-desiring, has established for the sustenance of all—
the sweetener of nourishments, a refuge even for the living man.
For he indeed, like a bestowing beast, cuts through the desert land;
golden-bearded, pure-toothed, skillful, and of undiminished power.
He indeed flows forth pure like Atri, as if from an axe;
the mother has brought him forth well, when, acting, she attained her portion.
O Agni, you who are invoked with clarified butter, that which is yours for our nourishment—
bestow upon these mortals splendor, renown, and wisdom.
Thus, O impetuous one, he took away the wrath of Adhrigu and received the cattle given by you. Then, O Agni, may Atri overcome the Dasyus who do not give; may he overcome the men who withhold food.
O Agni, those seeking the Truth have kindled you, the ancient one, for aid— you who were strengthened by power,
the many-shining, the worshipful, the all-sustaining, the friend of the household, the lord of the home, the most excellent.
O Agni, the people have established you as their ancient guest, the flame-haired lord of the household;
you who possess lofty banners, manifold forms, and win wealth, providing excellent protection, good refuge, and consuming the aged foe.
O Agni, the human tribes praise you—the knower of the sacrificial office, the discerning one, the greatest bestower of jewels;
you who, though dwelling in secret, O blessed one, are visible to all, possessing a mighty roar, worthy of fair sacrifice, and resplendent with ghee.
O Agni, we have approached you, the sustainer, from every side, praising you with songs and bowing down in homage.
As such, O Aṅgiras, being kindled, take pleasure in us—O god, the glory of mortals—with your radiant splendors.
O Agni, you who possess many forms, bestowing vital strength upon every clan as of old, O much-praised one;
you rule over many foods by your power. That brilliance of yours, as you blaze forth, is not to be assailed.
O Agni, youngest one, as soon as you were kindled, the gods made you their messenger, the bearer of oblations;
they established you—wide-striding, having ghee for your womb, invoked with offerings, and brilliant—as the eye that impels the thought.
O Agni, from of old, those seeking favor have kindled thee with ghee and excellent fuel when thou wert invoked;
thus, grown great and nourished by the plants, thou spreadest thyself abroad over the earthly expanses.
O Agni, mortals bearing oblations invoke you, the god;
I acknowledge you as Jātavedas, for you shall carry the offerings in due order.
Agni is the Hotṛ-priest of the liberal patron who has strewn the sacrificial grass;
he is the one toward whom the sacrifices and the prize-winning strengths, seeking glory, flow together.
And him whom the kindling-sticks have brought forth like a newborn infant—
the upholder of human clans, Agni, the performer of the perfect sacrifice.
And you are indeed difficult to seize, like the son of those who wander;
O Agni, you who burn many forests like an animal in a meadow.
Now, his smoky flames come together completely,
when Trita, as if at the divine [heaven], blows upon him like a smith, sharpening him as a smith [sharpening] his tools.
O Agni, through your protections and through the praises of Mitra, may we overcome the misfortunes and enmities of mortal men.
O Agni, bring that wealth to us, O powerful one, for the sake of our men.
May he protect us and nourish us; may he be for the winning of booty, and do thou stand by us for our increase in battles.
O Agni, bring us the most powerful splendor, O irresistible one; open for us a path to wealth and abundant nourishment.
O Agni, wondrous one, through your wisdom and the greatness of your power, the divine authority has ascended in you; acting as a friend, you are worthy of sacrifice.
O Agni, increase for us the household and the prosperity of these patrons,
those heroes who, through their hymns of praise, have attained great riches.
O Agni, those men who, possessing wealth in horses, adorn their songs for you, O radiant one— they,
the powerful heroes with their vigor, whose great fame awakens by itself even from heaven.
O Agni, those flames of yours go forth boldly,
radiant like lightning flashes that traverse the sky, or like a rattling chariot seeking the prize.
Now, O Agni, come for our protection and for the granting of gifts to us who press on;
and may our wise patrons cross over all regions.

O Agni Aṅgiras, you who have been praised and are being praised, bring to us, O Hotṛ, wealth that overcomes the mighty, for the sake of our praisers and for your own praise; and be present for our increase in battles.
The guardian of the people, the ever-watchful Agni, the highly skillful, has been born for new prosperity.
With his face anointed with ghee, reaching to the great heaven, he shines brilliantly and purely for the Bharatas.
Men have kindled Agni, the banner of sacrifice, the first domestic priest, in his threefold seat.
Riding in the same chariot with Indra and the gods, he sits upon the sacrificial grass as the Hotṛ priest of excellent wisdom for the performance of the sacrifice.
Unrubbed, you are born pure from your two mothers; as a delightful sage, you arose from Vivasvat.
They strengthened you with clarified butter, O Agni, when you were invoked; your smoke became a banner resting in heaven.
May Agni come straightway to our sacrifice; men carry Agni hither and thither from house to house.
Agni has become the messenger, the bearer of oblations; choosing Agni, they choose him who possesses the wisdom of a seer.
For you, O Agni, let this speech be most sweet; for you let this inspired thought be a blessing to the heart.
As great rivers fill the ocean, so do our songs fill you and increase you with power.
O Agni, the Aṅgirases found you hidden in secret, dwelling in every forest;
being rubbed, you are born with great might, and they call you, O Aṅgiras, the son of strength.
To Agni, the great and worshipful one, the bull of *ṛta*, the Asura, I bring this prayer;
like well-purified ghee into the mouth at the sacrifice, I offer this song directed toward the Bull.
O knower of *ṛta*, perceive the *ṛta*; pierce open the many streams of *ṛta*. I do not pursue the sorcerer by force nor through duplicity; I follow the *ṛta* of the ruddy bull.
O Agni, acting according to the cosmic order (*ṛta*) by means of the *ṛta*, with what [hymn] will you become the knower of our new song of praise?
O God, protector of the seasons, you know the seasons; I do not know the master of this wealth that he has won.
Who, O Agni, are your bondsmen for the enemy? Who are your radiant protectors who shall win the prize?
Who, O Agni, drink the draught of falsehood? Who are the guardians of the speech of the liar?
O Agni, these companions of yours have turned away; though they were once auspicious, they have become inauspicious.
They have harmed themselves by their own words, speaking crooked things to one who acts with integrity.
O Agni, he who honors your sacrifice with reverence protects the *ṛta* of the ruddy bull;
may his dwelling be broad and prosperous, and may the lineage of Nahuṣa, as he spreads forth, attain fulfillment.
Praising you, we call upon you; praising you, we kindle you;
O Agni, praising you, [we call] for your protection.
O Agni, we fashion today an effective hymn of praise for you, who touch the heavens, as we, desiring wealth, seek the favor of the god.
May Agni, who has been established as the Hotṛ among men, take pleasure in our songs; may he worship the divine host.
O Agni, you are far-extending, the beloved and most excellent invoker;
through you they extend the sacrifice.
The inspired singers magnify you, O Agni, the best winner of booty, who are well-praised;
as such, grant us heroic strength.
O Agni, as the felly encompasses the spokes, you encompass the gods;
you strive for wondrous wealth.
Awaken Agni with a hymn of praise, kindling the immortal one,
so that he may place our oblations among the gods.
At the sacrifices, mortals invoke that immortal god,
the most excellent sacrificer among the human race.
For him indeed, the gods constantly invoke with the ladle dripping with ghee—
Agni, to carry their oblations.
Agni, once born, shone forth, slaying the Dasyus and dispelling darkness with his light; he found the cattle, the waters, and the sun.
Worship Agni, the seer worthy of praise, whose back is anointed with ghee;
may he come and hear my invocation.
They have magnified Agni, who belongs to all people, with clarified butter, with hymns of praise,
and with well-composed, eloquent words.
I offer a song of praise to the ordainer, the seer, the one worthy of being known, the glorious and ancient one— Agni,
the Asura who sits upon the clarified butter, the very gracious one, the sustainer of wealth, the supporter of all treasure.
By means of *ṛta* they have established *ṛta* as a support upon the power of the sacrifice in the highest heaven;
they who, through their offspring, have reached those unborn men who sit upon the support of the law of heaven.
The seekers of aid extend their bodies for the sake of life; great and invincible is [the power] for the ancient one.
May he, newly born, overcome the enclosures; they stand around him on all sides like a provoked lion.
When, spreading out like a mother, you bear every person for their nourishment and for their vision;
when, bestowing life after life for their aging, you go about yourself in diverse forms.
May Vāja now protect the limit of your power; O God, you have granted a wide, flowing, and sustaining stream of wealth.
Like a thief hiding his tracks, you have revealed Atri for the sake of great riches, making him conscious of your bounty.
Sing forth a great hymn of praise to the radiant god Agni,
whom mortals have placed in the forefront like a friend with their eulogies.
For he, Agni, by the days of men, has been the Hotṛ-priest within the arms of Dakṣa; he, like Bhaga, distributes the sacrificial offering in due order as a desirable boon.
In the praise-song of this liberal lord, in the friendship of him whose luster is grown great—
in whom, the loudly roaring noble one, all [the gods] have placed their strength— RV_5.016.03.
For then, O Agni, by the greatness of their heroic power,
both heaven and earth have encompassed that fame, as if it were a mighty youth.
Now come to us, O Agni, being praised; bring us what is desirable.
May we and our patrons together establish well-being, and may you stand with us for our increase in battles.
O God, with sacrifices, let the mortal thus entreat the most powerful Agni for protection, when the rite is well-prepared, so that Pūru may be aided.
For by his own most glorious mouth, O Vidharman, you are esteemed;
him, the vault of heaven with wondrous luster, the delightful one, [I praise] beyond thought with my inspired wisdom.
His dwelling indeed is by means of his flame— he who has been yoked by the impetuous song—
whose lofty rays shine like the seed of heaven.
By the wisdom of this wondrous one, who is rich in insight, wealth has been placed upon his chariot;
thus Agni, worthy of invocation among all the clans, is praised.
Now indeed, O Son of Strength, let the wise patrons attend to our desirable wealth with their mouths;
protect us for our aid, grant us power for our well-being, and stand up for our increase in battles.
In the morning, may Agni, the beloved of many, be praised as the guest of the people—
he, the immortal, who delights in all the oblations among mortals.
For Dvita, who carries away what is injured, through the greatness of his own skill, he places the drop in due order; even your praiser, O Immortal One, [attains this].
With my song, I invoke that [Agni] of yours whose flame is long-lived, the patron of the wealthy;
he whose chariot, O giver of horses, moves unhindered.
Those in whom there is brilliant insight, who guard the hymns of praise,
have spread the sacrificial grass at the call of Svarṇara and have established glorious renown around them.
O Agni, you who dwell in common praise with those who have given me fifty horses— bestow upon these wealthy patrons brilliant, great, and lofty glory, O immortal one, like that of heroic men.
The various states come forth; from the enclosure, the enclosure has become manifest. He gazes out from the lap of his mother.
Observing clearly, they have offered oblations; with unblinking eyes, they guard their manly strength.
They have entered the firm fortress.
The people of Śvaitreya have flourished in splendor; the tribes have prospered.
Bṛhaduktha, with a golden necklace around his neck, seeks strength through this sweet draught as if for a prize.
Like beloved, desirable milk, [he is] the kinless one together with the two kinsmen;
like a cauldron filled with the essence of strength, he is undeceived and the deceiver of all.
Playing with us, O beam of light, come hither, finding union with the ash and the wind;
may those sharp, well-whetted, and bold flames of his, stationed in the bellies of the wood, carry [the oblation] upward.
O Agni, best winner of booty, whatever wealth you yourself deem worthy,
that glorious companion, do you proclaim among the gods through our songs.
O Agni, those who do not bring down [the gods] for you, though they have grown great through fierce power— they pursue the hatred and the crookedness of one who follows another's law.
We choose you as the Hotṛ-priest, O Agni, the accomplisher of skill;
at the sacrifices, we who offer oblations invoke you, the foremost, with our song.
Thus, O powerful one, so that day by day you may grant us aid for wealth and for the cosmic order, O wise one— may we rejoice together with cattle, may we rejoice together with heroes.
Like Manu, we set thee down; like Manu, we kindle thee.
O Agni, O Aṅgiras, like Manu, sacrifice to the gods for the one who seeks the gods.
For you, O Agni, are kindled with great delight among the human folk;
the ladles approach you in succession, O well-born one, you who are anointed with clarified butter.
All the gods, acting in harmony, have made you their messenger;
honoring you, O sage, they invoke you as a god at the sacrifices.
Let the mortal invoke for you, O gods, Agni with the sacrifice to the gods;
enkindled, O radiant one, shine forth; sit upon the seat of Ṛta, sit upon the seat of the food.
O Viśvasāman, like Atri, sing forth to the one of purifying luster,
who is to be praised at the sacrifices as the most delightful Hotṛ-priest among the people.
Place Agni Jātavedas here, the god and the officiating priest;
let the sacrifice proceed today in due order, most capacious for the gods.
We mortals, seeking your aid, have meditated upon you, the god of conscious mind; we have turned our thoughts toward you for your most excellent protection.
O Agni, O mighty one, take heed of this our speech!
You, O fair-cheeked lord of the household, the Atris exalt with hymns of praise; the Atris adorn you with their songs.
O Agni, bring us wealth that conquers by the might of its splendor—
wealth that shall overcome all peoples in the contests for booty through your presence.
O Agni, bring that wealth, which overcomes hostile armies, here by your power;
for you are the true and wonderful giver of booty consisting of cattle.
For all people, with one accord, having spread the sacrificial grass, seek you—
the beloved Hotṛ-priest in their dwellings— for many desirable boons.
For he indeed, the one who belongs to all people, has taken up overwhelming power against the assailants.
O Agni, shine upon us in these dwellings, O bright one; shine with splendor, O purifier!
O Agni, be our closest relative, our protector, and our auspicious shelter.
Agni is the Vasu, possessed of Vasu-like fame; come hither and grant us most resplendent wealth.
Be mindful of us; hear our call; deliver us from every one who intends us harm.
O most radiant one, O shining one, we now entreat you for the welfare of our friends.
I sing toward Agni, the god, for your protection; he is our benefactor. May the son of the *ṛṣis*, the upholder of *ṛta*, grant us wealth and carry us across our enemies.
For he is the true one, whom the men of old and even the gods kindled—
the Hotṛ-priest with the lovely tongue, rich in splendor through his brilliant lights.
O Agni, worthy of choice, shine wealth upon us through our most excellent prayer and our best benevolence, and through our well-fashioned hymns.
Agni reigns among the gods; Agni enters into mortals. Agni is our bearer of oblations; honor Agni with your prayers.
Agni bestows upon the worshiper a son who possesses most abundant fame, who is a supreme priest of mighty prayers, and who, being unconquered, makes his father renowned.
Agni bestows a true lord who, with his men, has conquered in battle;
Agni [bestows] a swift-running steed, a victor never overcome.
Sing forth a great hymn to Agni, O Vibhāvasu, that which is most effective;
from you, like a mighty queen, wealth and spoils of war arise.
Your radiant beams resound loudly like the pressing-stones; and your roar has gone forth of its own accord from heaven like thunder.
Thus, seeking wealth, we have paid homage to Agni, the powerful one;
may he, the wise one, carry us across all enemies as if with a ship.
O Agni, purifier, with your radiance and your pleasant tongue, O god,
bring the gods here and worship them.
We pray to you, O Agni, whose back is sprinkled with ghee, O you of brilliant luster who behold the light of heaven;
bring the gods here for the feast.
O Sage, we kindle you, the one who accepts the oblation, the radiant one,
O Agni, the great one at the sacrifice.
O Agni, come with all the gods for the giving of the oblation;
we choose you as our Hotṛ-priest.
O Agni, bring excellent heroic strength to the sacrificer who presses the soma;
sit down upon the sacrificial grass together with the gods.
Kindled, O Agni, winner of thousands, you nourish the sacred laws;
you are the praiseworthy messenger of the gods.
Establish Agni Jātavedas, the bearer of the oblation, the youngest,
the divine officiant.
Let the sacrifice proceed in due order today, most spacious for the gods;
spread the sacrificial grass for them to sit upon.
May the Maruts, the Aśvins, Mitra, and Varuṇa sit here; may the gods sit with their entire host.
The lord of the virtuous has bestowed upon me two oxen with a wagon; the most wise Asura among the wealthy is he.
O Agni Vaiśvānara, Tryaruṇa, the son of Trivṛṣan, has distinguished himself with ten thousand gifts.
O Vaiśvānara Agni, well-praised and increasing in strength, grant protection to Tryaruṇa— [the man] who gives me one hundred and twenty cows and two bay horses, well-yoked and easy to harness.
Thus Trasadasyu, desiring your favor, O Agni, has offered a new song for the ninth time to you,
the most youthful one— he, Tryaruṇa, who with a yoked [chariot] extols my many ancient hymns, O you of mighty birth.
Whoever shall speak thus to me for the sake of the wise Aśvamedha—
granting gain to him who strives with a hymn, granting wisdom to him who acts according to the Truth.
He whose hundred dappled bulls exhilarate me,
like the gifts of Aśvamedha, like Soma juices mixed with threefold milk.
O Indra and Agni, bestow upon Aśvamedha, the giver of a hundred gifts, great heroic power and a sovereign dominion that endures like the unaging sun in heaven.
Kindled, Agni has sent his flame to heaven; facing the Dawn, he shines far and wide.
Rich in all boons, the ladle dripping with ghee goes forward with obeisances, invoking the gods with the oblation.
Being kindled, you reign as the sovereign of immortality; you accompany the one who prepares the oblation for his well-being.
He whom you impel gains all wealth; O Agni, you establish him as a guest of honor before [the gods].
O Agni, be bold for great good fortune; may your splendors be most excellent. Bring together a household lordship that is easy to govern, and trample down the powers of those who act as enemies.
O Agni, kindled and of great majesty, I praise your splendor;
you are a bull, full of luster, and are enkindled at the sacrifices.
O Agni, kindled and invoked, sacrifice to the gods at this well-performed rite;
for you are the bearer of the oblations.
Offer oblations and pay homage to Agni as the sacrifice proceeds; choose him as the carrier of the sacrificial offerings.
Aryaman maintains three [realms] at the divine assembly of men; they uphold the three celestial luminaries.
The Maruts, whose wills are purified, sing hymns to you; O Indra, you are their wise seer.
When the Maruts sang in praise of Indra as he rejoiced after drinking the pressed soma, he seized his thunderbolt to strike the serpent; he released the mighty waters so that they might flow.
And may the Brahmins, O Maruts, and Indra drink of this well-pressed Soma for me;
for that is the oblation which found the cattle for Manu, when Indra, having drunk it, slew the serpent.
He propped apart the two worlds more widely; though he had clothed himself in them, he struck terror into the wild beast.
Indra, casting off the devourer, struck down the Dānava who was panting against him.
Then, O Maghavan, by your will all the gods yielded to you the drinking of Soma,
when you brought Etaśa down below the sun's bay mares that were flying ahead.
When Maghavan, with his thunderbolt, simultaneously shattered his ninety-nine coils, the Maruts sang Indra’s praise in the assembly; with a Triṣṭubh hymn, they forced open the sky.
As a friend for his friend, Agni quickly cooked three hundred buffaloes by means of his power;
Indra, for the sake of slaying Vṛtra, drank at once from the man the pressed soma from three lakes.
When Maghavan drank three hundred buffaloes' worth of Soma and three lakes of the Soma-juice,
all the gods raised a shout for Indra as he slew the dragon, just as they cry out at the winning of a prize.
When Uśanas and you, O Indra, came to the house with powerful, swift-running horses, you went there on the same chariot with Kutsa, conquering; with the gods, you indeed overthrew Śuṣṇa.
You pulled away one wheel of the sun, and you made the other path for Kutsa to travel;
you crushed the noseless Dasyus with your weapon and cast down those of insulting speech into their own dwelling-place.
The hymns of Gaurivīti magnified you; you delivered Pipru over to Vaidathina.
Ṛjiśvan turned to you for friendship; cooking the sacrificial cakes, he drank his soma.
The Navagvas and Daśagvas, having pressed the Soma, honor Indra with their hymns;
even that stall of cattle which was securely closed, the men, performing their rites, have opened.
How indeed may I, as one who knows, celebrate all thy heroic deeds, O Maghavan, which thou hast performed?
And those new ones which thou wilt perform, O Most Mighty—let us proclaim them forth to thee in the assemblies.
O Indra, you have performed all these many deeds from birth, irresistible through your heroism;
whatever bold acts you now perform, O wielder of the thunderbolt, there is no one who can withstand that power of yours.
O Indra, most powerful one, take pleasure in the prayers being performed for you, these new ones which we have fashioned for you.
Like two auspicious, well-made garments, I, seeking wealth, have skillfully wrought them as a craftsman fashions a chariot.

Where is that hero? Who has seen Indra, approaching on his easy-rolling chariot with his two bay horses—he, the wielder of the thunderbolt, who, seeking the one who has pressed the soma with wealth, comes as a helper to that dwelling, O much-invoked one?
I have declared his secret, powerful place; seeking it, I have followed the track of the one who deposited it.
I asked others, and they said to me: "May we, as men awakened, attain Indra."
Now, O Indra, let us proclaim before the pressed juice those deeds of yours which you have performed and which you have graciously accepted from us.
May he who is ignorant come to know them, and may he who knows listen; here comes Maghavan with his entire host.
O Indra, as soon as you were born, you made your mind firm; seeking alone to fight even against many, you by your might shattered the rock with lightning and found the stall of the ruddy cows.
When you, the supreme one, were born in the far distance, bearing a name renowned afar—from that very Indra even the gods were struck with fear; he conquered all the waters that had Dāsa lords.
For you, O Indra, these most gracious Maruts sing their hymn and press the Soma juice;
may Indra, by his wondrous powers, overcome the guileful serpent who dwells coiled within the waters.
From birth, you have driven away the scorners, O Maghavan, bestowing gifts while desiring to gather cattle;
it was there that you struck off the head of the Dāsa Namuci, seeking a path for Manu.
For you have indeed made me your ally, O Indra, as you shook off the head of the Dāsa Namuci;
like a whirling stone, you cast both heaven and earth away for the Maruts.
For Dāsa made women his weapons; what could his weak armies do to me?
For he perceived both his milch-cows within; then Indra went forth to fight the Dasyu.
Here the cows lowed together from all sides, having been separated here and there from their calves;
Indra reunited them by his powers when the well-pressed Soma juices exhilarated him.
When the brown, stirred Soma juices exhilarated him, the bull bellowed loudly at his dwelling-places;
having drunk of it, Indra, the breaker of forts, gave back the ruddy cows.
This was a good deed for them, O Agni; the Ruśamas, giving away four thousand cattle, have performed it.
We have accepted the offered gifts of Ṛṇañcaya, the most heroic among men.
The Ruśamas, O Agni, have sent me home well-adorned with thousands of cattle;
at the dawning of the night’s end, the strong pressed juices have exhilarated Indra.
The night, whose course was nearly ended, dawned for R̥ṇañcaya, the king of the Ruśamas. Like a swift, prize-winning steed urged forward, Babhru won four thousand.
We have received four thousand head of cattle from among the Ruśamas, O Agni;
even the heated cauldron that was there for the Pravargya rite, we sages have taken it up—the one made of iron.
Indra, the Bounteous One, prepares an easy slope for the chariot upon which he has mounted as it strives for booty.
Like a herdsman driving his cattle, he scatters the hosts; uninjured, he goes first, seeking to win.
Come hither, O Lord of the Bay Steeds; do not be reluctant. O you who bestow golden wealth, attend to us.
For there is nothing better than you, O Indra; even those who were born of the stone (the Maruts), you have made subject to yourself.
When strength was born from strength, Indra displayed all his powers;
he drove forth the well-milking cows within the cave and dispelled the encompassing darkness with light.
The Anus fashioned a chariot for your horse; Tvaṣṭṛ, O much-invoked one, forged the radiant thunderbolt.
The Brahmins, magnifying Indra with hymns, strengthened him for the slaying of the serpent.
When the strong ones sang their hymn of praise to you, the Strong One, O Indra— the pressing-stones and Aditi being of one accord—
those felloes that were without horses and without chariots, impelled by Indra, rolled against the Dasyus.
I shall proclaim your former deeds and those new ones, O Maghavan, which you have performed—
when, O wielder of power, you sustained both heaven and earth, winning for Manu the waters that are wondrous in their bounty.
That indeed was your deed, O wonder-worker, O sage—that when slaying the dragon you measured out your might;
you seized even the wiles of Śuṣṇa, and advancing, you drove away the Dasyus.
O Indra, you stayed the well-milking waters for Yadu and Turvaśa on the far shore;
you went forth with fierce power and brought Kutsa hither, when the gods and Uśanas came together to meet you both.
O Indra and Aṅgiras, as you travel on your chariot, let the coursers carry you even to the ear.
You blow away the mist from the waters and from their dwelling places; you drive the darkness from the heart of the liberal patron.
Even a seer, seeking aid, has come here desiring help, even to the well-yoked horses of Vāta.
Here, O Indra, all the Maruts were your friends; they increased your power through their sacred prayers.

Even the Sun’s chariot, which was moving forward in the race, he placed behind the one that was speeding away; Etaśa brought the wheel and joined it on; placing it in front, he shall grant us our purpose.
O people, Indra has come hither to be beheld, seeking his friend who has pressed the Soma;
the pressing-stone speaks as it is brought to the altar, and for him the Adhvaryu priests move with haste.
Those mortals who have desired you and continue to desire you, O Immortal One—let them not fall into distress.
Honor those who offer sacrifice, and bestow vigor upon those people among whom we may be numbered.
You burst open the spring, you released the channels; you set at rest the surging floods.
O Indra, when you shattered the great mountain, you let loose the streams and struck down the Dānava.
O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, you set in motion the springs of the mountain’s udder which were held fast by the seasons;
O fierce Indra, having slain even the serpent Ahi as he lay coiled, you established your own might.
Indra, by his own powers, struck down the weapon of that very great beast;
he who alone was considered irresistible, yet another even stronger than he was born from him.
Even him among them who rejoiced by his own power, the son of the mist, the well-growing one who goes into darkness—
the wielder of the thunderbolt, with his bull-like onset, struck down Śuṣṇa, the fury of the Dānava, with his bolt.
Even that [foe] who sat down by his wiles, though he was thought to be invulnerable, you have indeed found his vital spot,
O lord of good dominion, when you placed him— desiring to fight while intoxicated with pride— in the darkness of the house.
Even him who was thus lying hidden, increasing in the sunless darkness—
him Indra, exhilarated by the pressed juice, having raised his arm aloft, struck down with a roar.
When Indra raised his irresistible might as a weapon against the great Dānava,
at the hurling of his thunderbolt, he struck him down and reduced him to the lowest state among all living beings.
The fierce one seized that very honey-drinking wave, the insatiable, vast covering that lay there;
with a mighty weapon, he cast down the footless devourer, the speaker of evil words, into his own dwelling-place.
Who can withstand his fury and his might? He alone, unopposed, carries off the spoils of wealth. Even these two goddesses, the expanses of heaven, flee in fear before the power of Indra’s strength.
The divine axe has yielded to him; for Indra, the path has opened like one longing [for him].
When he gathers all strength with these [powers], the peoples bow down before him, the self-dependent one.
I hear that you alone are the lord of the virtuous, born as the protector of the five peoples, renowned among men.
May our newest prayers grasp him for me—the most recent ones—invoking Indra at evening and at dawn.
For thus indeed I hear of you as one who distributes gifts at the proper times and bestows wealth upon the inspired singers.
What do those Brahmins gain for themselves, O Indra, who as friends have placed their desire in you?

I meditate upon the great one for the sake of the great and powerful Indra, the manly one; thus does the powerless man [meditate] upon the powerful one, who, being praised among the people in the contest for booty, takes heed of this man’s devotion in the assembly.
So, O Indra, being mindful of us through our hymns, O Bull, you have harnessed the pair of bay steeds;
for you, O Maghavan, according to your pleasure, shall drive toward those who come, and you shall overcome the people.
