O Indra, those lofty steeds of yours shall not remain unyoked by us through lack of prayer; mount that chariot, O wielder of the thunderbolt, for you, O God with noble horses, shall hold the reins.
O Indra, since many hymns of praise exist for you, you have performed deeds for the cattle, fighting among the pastures;
you, the bull, fashioned even the name of the Dāsa in his own dwelling for the sake of the sun amidst the battles.

We are yours, O Indra, as are these men—your host who have been born and your chariots that have come forth. May he whose strength is like a serpent come to us, a hero to be invoked like Bhaga, beloved in the offerings at the feasts.
O Indra, you have filled yourself with strength worthy of being satisfied, for you are the immortal who displays manly deeds;
as such, O possessor of wealth, grant us brilliant riches—I praise the gift of the one of abundant bounty.
Thus, O Hero Indra, protect us with your aids; favor the singers and poets who praise you.
And at the winning of booty, be pleased with those who offer the skin [of the soma], and with the well-pressed, delightful sweet juice.

And may those ten white horses of the liberal Trasadasyu, son of Purukutsa, who possesses golden wealth, carry me; may they, through the ritual intentions of Gairikṣita, now bring me together with them.
And those crimson steeds of Mārutāśva, who through their will are bounteous at the distribution of the assembly—
Cyavatāna, giving me thousands, has sung for the sake of beauty, like the following of a noble man.
And those well-pleasing, radiant, and well-directed steeds of Dhvanya’s son Lakṣmaṇya have come to me,
like cows entering the stall of the seer Saṃvaraṇa, through the greatness of his wealth.
The ageless, heavenly *svadhā* follows the one who has no enemy, the wondrous one, according to his own measure.
Press the juice, cook the oblation for him who is borne by prayer; bestow further gifts upon him who is praised by many.
He who, having filled his belly with Soma, the bounteous lord rejoiced in the sweet juice;
when Uśanas, the wielder of great weapons, directed for him a thousand-edged bolt to slay the beast.
Whoever presses Soma for him—whether he be one who offers it from his mouth or from his udder—that man indeed becomes radiant.
Śakra drives away his sin; Maghavan, the wise friend, extends his splendor and purifies his body.

Whose father Śakra has slain, whose mother, and whose brother—he does not flee from him. He indeed accepts his offered gift; the maker of the sacrifice does not shrink from sin, for he is a mine of wealth.
He desires neither five nor ten; he does not associate with the one who does not press the soma, even if that one is prosperous.
The shaker conquers or slays by that means, and he bestows upon the god-fearing man a stall full of cattle.
Possessing powerful jaws, he strikes down the wheel in battle; turning away from those who do not press the soma, he is the prosperer of those who do.
Indra, the terrifier and subduer of all, leads the Dāsa according to his will, for he is the Ārya.
He gathers up the Pani’s sustenance to plunder it; he distributes excellent wealth to the donor.
Not even in a stronghold does the many man stand firm who has provoked his might.
When Indra Maghavan perceived two wealthy men, each with a full host, contending for beautiful cattle, he made one his ally;
trembling, he released the herd of kine for him with his warriors, the Shaker.

I praise Śatri, the son of Agniveśa, who possesses a thousand songs, O Agni—the peerless banner of the noble one. For him may the gathered waters swell; upon him let there be powerful and brilliant dominion.
O Indra, bring us that most effective will of yours for our protection— that which overcomes the people, wins the prize, and is invincible in battles.
O Indra, whatever four [powers] you have, O hero, or those three which exist,
or whatever [power] belongs to the five peoples— bring that aid well to us.
We invoke your most excellent aid, you who are most virile;
for you were born with the impulse of a bull, O Indra, victorious through your powers of being.
For you are a bull for the sake of bestowing bounty; your strength is that of a bull.
Your dominion is self-sustained, O Indra, and your mind is bold; your manly power is truly all-conquering.
O Indra, wielder of the stone, O Lord of a hundred powers, O Master of might, come down with all your chariots against that mortal who acts as an enemy.
O best slayer of Vṛtra, it is you indeed that the people who have spread the sacrificial grass invoke— the fierce one, the primordial— among many, for the winning of booty.
O Indra, protect our chariot— our invincible one that goes at the head in battles, that advances together with us in every contest for wealth, and that strives for booty.
O Indra, come to our chariot with your wisdom; O most powerful one, may we win what is desirable. May we establish glory in heaven; may we compose a hymn of praise in heaven.
May that Indra come, who knows how to bestow treasures as a gift of riches;
like a thirsty bull roaming the desert, let him eagerly drink the pressed soma-juice.
O Hero, Lord of the Bay Horses, let the Soma rise upon your jaws and cheeks like [water] upon the back of a mountain.
O King, invoked by many, may we all rejoice with songs of praise, urging you on as one urges swift steeds.
Like a revolving wheel, O much-invoked one, my mind trembles with fear, through lack of understanding, O wielder of the stone.
Would not the singer, O Maghavan, possessor of many riches, ever praise you from his chariot, O you who are ever-increasing?
Like a pressing-stone, O Indra, this singer of yours raises his voice, aspiring greatly.
O Maghavan, bestow wealth with your left hand; O Lord of the Bay Steeds, bestow it with your right—do not be averse to us.
May the Bull Heaven increase you, the Bull; as a Bull, you are borne by your two Bulls, the bay steeds.
O Bull, with your bull-chariot, fair-jawed one, Bull of mighty will, O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, grant us our share in the battle.
O Maruts, let all the peoples bow down before this youthful Śrutaratha with offerings— before him who, rich in steeds, bestowed two ruddy horses accompanied by three hundred [others].
He vies with the radiance of the sun, being invoked, his back anointed with ghee, moving with ease.
For him may the unerring dawns shine forth, who says, "Let us press the Soma for Indra."
With the fire kindled, the grass strewn, the pressing-stones yoked and the Soma pressed, he shall roar like a forest;
he for whom the pressing-stones speak with eager voice, while the Adhvaryu priest goes down to the river with the oblation.
This bride comes seeking her husband—he who carries away the vigorous queen. May his chariot win glory and let its roar resound; may it bring home many thousands.
That king does not falter in whom Indra drinks the potent Soma accompanied by the cattle;
he leads forth his warriors, slays the Vṛtra, dwells among the people, and prospers as one fortunate in renown.
May he prosper in peace and prevail in battle; may he conquer both armies when they meet.
He who has pressed the Soma and offered it to Indra shall be dear to Sūrya and dear to Agni.
O Indra, Lord of a hundred powers, the gift from your bounty is vast;
therefore, O Ruler of all people, O Lord of noble dominion, bestow splendors upon us.
O most powerful Indra, when you bestow that glorious nourishment which is worthy of renown, it spreads abroad— far-famed, of golden hue, and invincible.
O wielder of the stone, those vigorous ones who are your companions through their desire for bounty—
both you gods, as lords of heaven and earth, rule for our protection.
And so, O Vṛtra-slayer, from whatever skill of yours there may be, bring us manly strength; for you desire the welfare of men, bring it to us.
Now, O Śatakratu, through these aids of yours, may we be well-protected under your shelter, O Indra; O Hero, may we be well-protected.
O Indra, wielder of the stone, whatever wonderful wealth you have to bestow,
O finder of riches, bring that bounty to us with both your hands.
O Indra, bring us that which you deem most excellent and celestial;
may we know it from you, as you bestow it from your inexhaustible bounty.
O wielder of the stone, with that renowned and lofty mind of yours which is intent on giving and is ever victorious, burst open even the firmest obstacles to win us the prize.
To Indra, the most bountiful among your wealthy patrons and the king of the peoples, I have offered many songs for his praise; he has been pleased by them.
To him, to Indra, must poetic speech and the hymn be recited;
for him, who is borne by the sacred word, the Atris magnify their songs, the Atris adorn their songs.
Come hither; drink the Soma pressed by the stones, O Lord of Soma!
O Bull Indra, greatest slayer of Vṛtra, come with your bulls.
The pressing-stone is a bull, the exhilaration is a bull; this pressed Soma is a bull.
O Indra, bull among bulls, greatest slayer of Vṛtra!
As a bull, I call upon you, the bull, O wielder of the thunderbolt, with your wondrous aids;
O Indra, most excellent slayer of Vṛtra, come with your bull-like steeds.
The impetuous one, wielder of the thunderbolt, the bull, the subduer of the swift, the powerful king, the slayer of Vṛtra,
the drinker of Soma— having yoked his two bay horses, may Indra come hither and exhilarate himself at the midday libation.
When Svarbhānu, the Asura, pierced you, O Sūrya, with darkness,
all beings looked on like one bewildered, ignorant of the way.
Then, O Indra, when you struck down the magic illusions of Svarbhānu as they rolled from heaven,
Atri found the sun hidden by the lawless darkness through the fourth sacred prayer.
Let not the malevolent one, out of malice and fear, swallow me up while I am here belonging to you. You are Mitra, whose bounty is true; may both you and King Varuṇa protect me.
Harnessing the pressing-stones, the priest Atri, serving and honoring the gods with his hymn and bowing down in reverence,
established the eye of the sun in heaven and dispelled the magical illusions of Svarbhānu.
The Asura Svarbhānu pierced the sun with darkness;
the Atris found him there, for no others were able.
Who indeed, O Mitra and Varuṇa, seeking the *ṛta*, would offer to you from the great heaven or from the earth?
Or in the seat of *ṛta*, may you protect us; or for the one who performs sacrifice, grant him strengths like those who seek cattle.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Āyu, Indra, Ṛbhukṣan, and the Maruts be pleased with us—
those who, being of one accord, offer well-fashioned praise with prostrations as a hymn to the bounteous Rudra.

O Aśvins, I call you hither, you who are most swift to travel, in the flight of the wind and in the abundance of the chariot; or rather, bring forth this prayer to the Asura of heaven, as one brings food to a worthy sacrificer.
The conquering divine one, Kaṇva the Hotṛ, Trita from heaven, Vāta and Agni acting in concert;
Pūṣan, Bhaga, and all-nourishing Viśvabhojas have come to the offering like those with the swiftest horses to a race.

Bring forth your wealth with its harnessed horses; let the prayer be offered for the sake of finding riches and for protection—O Maruts, swift ones, the most gracious is the Hotṛ-priest of Auśija through your ways, which are your own ways.
Bring forward for you Vāyu, who yokes his chariot; bring forward the divine inspired singer with hymns of praise.
Seeking your favor, O followers of the cosmic order (*ṛta*), may the wise and excellent wives bestow upon us here for our devotion the fulfillment of our prayers.
I approach you two with venerable strengths and with brilliant hymns that illuminate the great heaven—
the Dawn and Night, who, like those possessing all knowledge, bring the sacrifice to the mortal man.
I sing praise for you, the nourishing heroes; bestowing gifts, I honor Vāstoṣpati and Tvaṣṭṛ.
May the bountiful Dhīṣaṇā, in harmony with us, through our prostrations, protect the lords of the forest and the plants as we seek wealth.
May the mountains be for our protection and extension—those well-guided ones who are like Vasu heroes.
May the worshipful Aptya, ever praised by us, the manly one, increase our prayer when he is invoked for aid.
I have praised the embryo of the bull of the earth; Trita extols the offspring of the waters with a perfect hymn.
Agni, like a steed, is glorified with his powers; he of the flaming hair consumes the forests.
How shall we speak to the great Rudra? How to Bhaga, who is mindful of wealth?
May the waters and the plants protect us, as well as the sky, the forests, and the mountains with their tree-hair.
May the Lord of Strength hear our songs—he who crosses the sky, the swift one who moves all around.
May the waters hear us, bright as fortresses, as the ladles are lifted from the mountain that is being split apart.
Truly we know you to be great, O wonder-workers; we shall proclaim it as we receive what is desirable.
Even the well-winged birds descend toward the mortal who pursues them with weapons in his agitation.
I have proclaimed for the sake of the noble sacrificer the divine and earthly births, as well as the waters.
May the heavens increase; may the songs with their bright peaks increase; may the surging floods increase against the attackers.
At every step may my old age be laid down, by Varūtrī or by Śakra with his protections.
May the great mother Rasā attend us, together with the patrons—she who is straight-handed and whose path is straight.
How may we worship with homage the bounteous Maruts when they come hither at our invocation? O Maruts, rich in fame, come hither at our invocation!
Let not Ahi Budhnya deliver us over to harm; may he be a promoter of our prosperity.
Thus indeed, O gods, does the mortal win you for the sake of offspring rich in cattle; thus, O gods, does the mortal win you.
Herein, may Nirṛti swallow up even my old age, so that there may be a nourishment for this body that is auspicious.
O Gods, may we obtain from you that benevolent favor, strengthening nourishment, through the praise of the cow, O Vasus.
May she, the bounteous goddess who is gracious, come speeding toward us for our well-being.
May Iḷā, the mother of the herd, or Urvaśī along with the rivers, favor us; or may Urvaśī, dwelling in the high heaven, being praised, cover us as she bestows the gift of the living one.
May he attend to us for the sake of strengthening nourishment.
May this most peaceful song, through its devotion, now reach Varuṇa, Mitra, Bhaga, and Aditi.
May the Asura, whose path is unassailable, who dwells in the fivefold sacrifice and is the source of joy, hear us. He is the one born from the speckled cloud, the priest of the five fires.
May Aditi accept my hymn of praise, as a mother her heart-pleasing and most kind son;
[may she accept] that beloved prayer which is ordained by the gods, and which brings bliss to Mitra and Varuṇa.
Exalt the most wise among the sages; drench him with honey and with ghee.
May that god Savitṛ bestow upon us brilliant treasures, already offered and set forth.
O Indra, Lord of the Bay Steeds, unite us with a favorable mind, with cattle, with wise patrons, and with well-being;
unite us with the sacred prayer ordained by the gods, and with the goodwill of the deities worthy of sacrifice.
May the god Bhaga, Savitṛ the apportioner of wealth, Indra the conqueror of Vṛtra and winner of riches,
Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja, and Purandhi— the immortal and swift ones— protect us.
Let us proclaim the deeds of the one accompanied by the Maruts—the unconquered, victorious, and undecaying.
Neither those of old, O Maghavan, nor those of later times, nor anyone of the present has attained your heroic power.
Praise Bṛhaspati, the first bestower of jewels, the winner of riches— he who, most beneficent to him who recites and praises, rich in many treasures, comes to the one who calls upon him.
O Bṛhaspati, accompanied by your protections, the liberal patrons remain unharmed and possess excellent heroes;
those who give horses, or those who give cattle, and those who give garments—they among them possess wealth and good fortune.
Make their wealth flee away—those who enjoy it without giving, despite our hymns;
drive the haters of prayer away from the sun, those who have broken their vows and grow strong in their transgression.
O Maruts, strike down with wheelless bolts him who at the feast of the gods honors the Rākṣasas;
he who reviles the sacred work of you who labor in worship shall have his desires rendered empty, though he exerts himself in vain.
Praise him who possesses good arrows and a good bow, who rules over every medicine.
Worship Rudra for his great benevolence; honor the divine Asura with prostrations.
May the householders, the active ones with skillful hands, the rivers who are the wives of the Bull fashioned by Vibhvan—
Sarasvatī, Bṛhaddivā, and Rākā— being gracious, may these radiant goddesses grant us wide space.
I offer this newest, newly-born hymn of wisdom to the great one, the excellent refuge— he who,
fashioning forms within the womb of his daughter, brought all this into being for us.
O singer, may you now attain with your fair praise the Lord of the Sacrifice, who thunders and roars— he who,
possessing clouds and waters, sends forth lightning and drenches both heaven and earth.
May this hymn reach the Marut host, the sons of Rudra, the youthful ones.
Desire calls me for wealth; for my well-being, praise the tireless ones who have spotted horses.
May this hymn of praise reach the earth, the mid-air, the trees, and the plants for the sake of wealth.
May every god be easy for me to invoke; may Mother Earth not hold us in ill-will.
O gods, may we abide in a wide space free from oppression.
May we go forth with the newest, joy-bestowing aid and excellent guidance of the Aśvins.
O immortal ones, bring to us wealth, heroic sons, and all auspicious blessings.
May the milch-cows, swift in their purpose, come to us with milk and honey, never failing.
For great wealth, the inspired singer loudly calls upon the seven mighty ones who bring delight.
With fair praise and with homage, I would turn hither Heaven and Earth, the bounteous ones, for the sake of strength.
Father and Mother, sweet of speech and skillful-handed, may you two glorious ones protect us in every battle.
O Adhvaryus, having prepared the sweet juices, bring the lovely, bright [Soma] to Vāyu.
Like our first Hotṛ-priest, drink of this, O God; we have offered the honeyed draught for your exhilaration.
The ten fingers and the two arms—the skillful hands that prepare the Soma—yoke the pressing-stone.
The well-hoofed stalk, dwelling on the mountain, has yielded the bright, shimmering juice of the sweet mead.

The Soma has been pressed for you who take pleasure in it, for the sake of will, for skill, and for great exhilaration. O Indra, being invoked, bring your two beloved bay horses, well-yoked to the chariot, hitherward at the time of union.

O Agni, by the paths traveled by the gods, bring hither to us the great Aramati, the divine lady who is in harmony with us, who is honored with reverence and offered oblations— the exalted one who knows the Eternal Order (Ṛta), for the exhilaration of the sweet draught.
Him whom the inspired poets anoint as if spreading him out, heating him with fire as if he were fat;
like a son upon the lap of his father, the most beloved Gharma has been set down, performing the rite for Agni.
Let the great, lofty, most auspicious song go forth like a messenger to invite the Aśvins.
O you who bring delight, come hither on one chariot; come to our treasure, as the linchpin reaches the nave.
I have proclaimed this word of homage to the most powerful Pūṣan and to Vāyu— the two who,
by their bounty, are the inspirers of thoughts, and who are themselves the givers of wealth and of strength.

O Jātavedas, being invoked, bring hither all the Maruts by their names and by their forms; O Maruts, you who are all, come to the sacrifice, to the songs, and to the excellent praise of the singer, with all your aids.
May Sarasvatī, the worshipful one, come from the high heaven and from the mountain to our sacrifice;
may the goddess, delighting in our call, dripping with clarity, and longing for us, graciously hear our effective speech.
Seat the ordainer, the blue-backed, the great Bṛhaspati, upon his seat. Let us honor him who shines within the home, seated in his proper place—the ruddy one of golden hue.
May the sustainer from the lofty heaven, bestowing gifts, come hither with all his protections when invoked—
the bull who clothes himself in the divine women and the plants, who is never-failing, whose horns are threefold, and who bestows vital strength.

To the bright one in the highest station of his mother, the active ones, full of praise and eloquent, have come. With reverence and offered oblations, they—the Āyus—purify him, the most gracious infant, as if for a garment.
Great vital strength belongs to you, O great Agni; those who grow old through devotion, paired together, attend upon you.
May every god be easy for me to invoke; may Mother Earth not hold us in ill-will.
O gods, may we abide in a wide space free from oppression.
May we come together with the newest, joy-bestowing aid and excellent guidance of the Aśvins.
O Immortals, bring to us wealth, heroic sons, and all auspicious blessings.
As of old, as before, as always, and even so now, [we praise] him, the most excellent one, seated upon the sacrificial grass, the finder of light;
with our song we milk from him the facing community, the swift victor, in whom you grow strong.
For the sake of glory, those [rays] of the upper sun which are beautiful to behold shine forth; O you who are resplendent among the quarters, you do not urge them on.
You are a good guardian, not to be deceived, O you of noble power; beyond all illusions, your name is established in the *ṛta*.
The oblation follows the steed; he is both the sustainer and the giver, the Hotṛ-priest whose path is unharmed, the bearer of strength.
Streaming along the sacrificial grass, the bull, the infant, the ageless youth has been placed in the midst of the two wide-spreading worlds.

These well-yoked [horses] of yours move forward on their course for the sacrifice; for that one [Yama], the twin sisters flow downward, increasing the cosmic order (*ṛta*). With reins that are easy to control and all-commanding, Krivi steals away their names at the descent.

Moving to and fro among the trees, well-sounding with a beautiful sacrificial ladle, you who seize the pressed juice and possess a discerning heart shine forth within the songs of praise; O singer of straight hymns, you are resplendent. Increase the wives [of the sacrifice] at the living rite.
Just as he was seen, so is he described; they have established him in the waters with his effective radiance.
Grant us great, wide space and vast dominion—mighty, heroic, and unshakable power.
Whether he is unmarried or has a wife, let Sūrya, the sage, overcome his rivals with a mind intent on battle;
may he, who possesses excellent wealth, grant us protection and a home that guards against heat from every side.
By the signal of this striving one, he moves toward the greater [deity], the lord of seers, in whom your name resides;
in whatever [vessel] it is placed, he finds it through his skillful work, and he who carries it himself shall make it ready.
The foremost of these has descended into the ocean; the libation in which she is extended does not fail.
Herein the heart of the impetuous one trembles, where the hymn exists that is bound to the purified Soma.
For he, through the intentions of Kṣatra Manasa, of Evāvada, of Yajata,
and of Sadhri— of Avatsāra— we shall win by means of our delights a most powerful strength, which is to be attained even by the wise.
The falcon is their Aditi; the exhilaration of the all-desirable, worshipful, and wondrous one is like a girth-belt.
They strive together to go toward one after another; they know the horn and your drinking-place nearby.

Sadāpṛṇa, the sacrificer, shall strike down the enemies; Bāhuvṛkta, Śrutavid, and Tarya are with you. He attains both boons and shines forth when he joins his company with those who are well-disposed toward him.
The bringer of pressed juice, the lord of the virtuous, he is the udder of all prayers and the vessel that draws them forth.
He has brought the cows; he has drawn up the flavorful milk and rests upon it. One who recites the hymns masters this, not one who sleeps.
The Ṛg-verses love him who keeps watch; the Sāman-chants go to him who keeps watch.
To him who keeps watch, this Soma says: "I am yours, dwelling at home in your friendship."
Agni is awake; the *ṛc*s desire him; Agni is awake; the *sāman*s go unto him.
Agni is awake; to him this Soma says: "I am yours, at home in your friendship."
Finding the heaven and releasing the mountain with hymns, the singers have come toward the approaching dawn.
You have opened the cow-pens and the light has gone forth; O God, you have thrown open the doors for mankind.
The Sun has spread his splendor like a radiance; the Mother of the Cows, knowing her way, has come forth from the wide space.
The rivers flow with desert-like colors, their waves a source of delight; the sky is made firm like a well-erected pillar.
For this hymn, the child of the mountain has emerged for the sake of the ancient birth of the great ones.
The mountain has opened wide; heaven has been perfected. Seeking to win favor, they have subdued the earth.
With hymns and words pleasing to the gods, I shall now invoke Indra and Agni for your protection;
for with chants, the seers skilled in sacrifice, seeking to win favor, worship the Maruts.
Come now, let us today be well-disposed; let us drive far away misfortune to a wider space. Let us cast our enemies to a distance and go forward toward the sacrificer.
O friends, let us perform this prayer by which the Mother opened the stall of the cow;
by which Manu conquered Viśiśipra, and by which the merchant Vaṅku obtained the water-rich soil.
There the pressing-stone, guided by hands, roared; thereby the Navagvas sang for ten months.
Saramā, going according to the *ṛta*, found the cows; Aṅgiras made all things true.
When at the dawning of this majestic goddess, all the Aṅgirases together shouted for the cattle,
Saramā found them by the path of Truth— those cows whose source was in the highest dwelling place.

May Sūrya come with his seven horses to the field that extends over the wide earth on his long journey. May the swift falcon fly toward the soma-plant; may the youthful sage shine brightly as he goes among the cattle.
Sūrya has ascended to the bright ocean when he has yoked his tawny, straight-backed horses.
Like wise men steering a ship through the water, the attentive waters stood still for him as he came hitherward.
I place my thought upon your waters, seeking the light of heaven, by which the Navagvas crossed over the ten months.
Through this prayer may we have the gods as our guardians; through this prayer may we overcome distress.
Like a wise horse, I have yoked myself of my own accord to the pole; I bear that which carries us across, seeking aid.
I do not desire to unyoke from it, nor to turn back again; may the wise one who goes before me lead me straight upon the path.
O Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and the gods—grant us strength, O Maruts and Viṣṇu!
May both the Nāsatyas, Rudra, the divine dames, Pūṣan, Bhaga, and Sarasvatī take pleasure in this.
I invoke Indra and Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa, Aditi, the Sun, Earth, Heaven, the Maruts, and the Mountains;
I call upon Viṣṇu, Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, Bhaga, Śaṃsa, and Savitṛ for our protection.
May Viṣṇu and Vāta grant us freedom from harm; may Draviṇodas and Soma bestow joy upon us. May the Ṛbhus and the Aśvins grant us wealth, and may Tvaṣṭṛ and Vibhvan likewise take heed of us.
And may that host of Maruts come to us, dwelling in heaven, the worshipful ones, to sit upon the sacred grass;
may Bṛhaspati and Pūṣan grant us protection, and Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman grant us a secure refuge.
And may those mountains of ours, worthy of fair praise, and the brightly shining rivers, be our protectors in our need.
May Bhaga, the distributor, come with power and aid; may the far-reaching Aditi hear my invocation.

May the longing wives of the gods protect us; may they aid us for the sake of progeny and the winning of booty. Those who belong to the earth and those who abide in the domain of the waters—may those goddesses, who are easily invoked, grant us refuge.
And let the divine dames, the wives of the gods—Indrāṇī, Agnāyī, Aśvinī, and Rāṭ—come hither;
may Rodasī and Varuṇānī hear us; and let the goddesses come, they who are the season of women.
Setting forth, she goes from heaven, speaking as the great mother awakening her daughter;
the young woman, seeking to win favor, calls aloud to the fathers at their seat with inspired thought.
Swift-moving, hastening toward those waters, they have taken their stand at the navel of immortality;
infinite and vast, their paths go all around heaven and earth on every side.
The bull, the ocean, the ruddy one with beautiful wings, has entered the womb of the ancient father.
Placed in the midst of heaven like a speckled stone, he has stepped forth; he guards the two ends of the realm.
Four bear him up, seeking security; ten suckle the embryo for its journey.
His supreme cows, possessing three natures, traverse the ends of heaven in an instant.
O people, this is that wondrous form and secret speech which the rivers and the waters have come to stand still;
for two others, born here and there, twin and kinsmen, support him from their mother.
For him they extend their prayers and perform their works; as mothers weave garments for their son, the joyful bulls, for the sake of sprinkling, go toward the brides along the path of heaven.
May that be so, O Mitra and Varuṇa; may that be so, O Agni. May this be well-being and health for us, and may this recitation be auspicious.
May we attain a firm footing and a secure foundation. Homage to the great Heaven, the dwelling place!
When shall we meditate upon our own dear domain, great with its own dominion and its own glory—
that which, within the unfailing mid-air, the wondrous one spreads out, choosing the waters from the cloud?
They have stretched out the path that provides a dwelling for heroes, across the entire expanse with a single course.
The person devoted to the gods drives away the waters behind him and pushes them forward with those already ahead.
With these pressing-stones, through the days and nights, he hurls the most excellent thunderbolt at the wielder of magic;
he who, moving within his own abode, brings together or disperses a hundred days.
I have beheld his onset like that of an axe; I have looked upon the face of this form for my enjoyment.
When he bestows treasure upon the clan that calls him to battle, it is as if he were providing a dwelling-place full of nourishment.
With his tongue, the four-faced one reaches out, Varuṇa, who, clothing himself in beauty, strives for the pious man.
We do not know him in his human form, from which Bhaga and Savitṛ bestow desirable wealth.
Today I seek for you the god Savitar and Bhaga, who distributes wealth to mankind.
O Aśvins, heroes of many enjoyments, may I turn you both hither day after day, seeking your friendship.
Knowing the departure of the Asura, worship the god Savitṛ with hymns;
let him who understands address him with reverence, [praising] him who distributes the highest treasure to mankind.
To the non-giver he grants desirable boons: Pūṣan, Bhaga, Aditi, and Uṣas shine forth;
Indra, Viṣṇu, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni—these wondrous ones have generated auspicious days.
May the invincible Savitṛ grant us that protection; may the flowing rivers follow it, seeking our nourishment.
When I, the priest of the sacrifice, address you, may we become masters of wealth, rich in the prize of booty.

Those who offer such homage to the Vasus, and who address Mitra and Varuṇa with hymns of praise—let them drive away evil and create wide space; through the protection of Heaven and Earth, may we rejoice.
May every mortal choose the friendship of the divine leader;
everyone strives for wealth, and may he choose glory so that he may prosper.
O God, O Leader, those [favors] of yours which you have bestowed upon us,
and those which you command for this [people], may we, through them, attain wealth and be united with your companionships.
Therefore, honor our men who are guests, and therefore honor our wives;
may the Dispeller drive far away all enemies who stand upon our paths.
Where the bearer has been urged forward like a beast of burden from the trough,
he, the manly-minded one whose home is heroes, wins the floods like a steady thinker.

O God, this leader of yours, the lord of the chariot, is wealth for our well-being; we meditate upon him who is auspicious for riches and auspicious for prosperity, he who is praised with food-offerings, he who is praised by the gods. We meditate upon him.
O Agni, come with all your helpers for the drinking of the pressed juice,
together with the gods, to the offering of the oblation.
O you whose thoughts are fixed on the cosmic order, whose laws are true, come to the sacrifice;
drink [the soma] with the tongue of Agni.
O wise one, come with the wise singers who travel at dawn, O truthful one, together with the gods for the drinking of the Soma.
This Soma, pressed in the ladle, is poured into the vessel, dear to Indra and Vāyu.
O Vāyu, come for the feast, graciously accepting the gift of oblations; drink of the pressed juice for the sake of refreshment.
O Indra and Vāyu, you two deserve the drinking of these pressed juices;
O stainless ones, enjoy them along with the offerings.
The Soma juices, mixed with curds, have been pressed for Indra and Vāyu;
like rivers flowing down a slope, they go toward the sacrificial food.
In harmony with all the gods, with the Aśvins, and in harmony with the Dawn, come hither, O Agni; as you did for Atri, rejoice in the pressed juice.
In harmony with Mitra and Varuṇa, in harmony with Soma and Viṣṇu, come, O Agni; rejoice in the pressed juice as you did for Atri.
In harmony with the Ādityas and the Vasus, in harmony with Indra and Vāyu, come, O Agni; as at the pressing, rejoice like Atri.
May the Aśvins and Bhaga grant us well-being; may the divine Aditi, who is free from enemies, grant us well-being.
May the Asura Pūṣan bestow well-being upon us, and may Heaven and Earth grant us well-being with their gracious favor.
For our well-being, let us address Vāyu; for our well-being, Soma, who is the lord of the world;
Bṛhaspati with his entire host for our well-being; and may the Ādityas be for our well-being.
May all the gods today grant us well-being; may Agni Vaiśvānara, the Vasu, grant us well-being.
May the divine Ṛbhus protect us for our well-being; may Rudra preserve us from distress.
May there be well-being, O Mitra and Varuṇa; may there be well-being, O wealthy Pathyā.
May Indra and Agni grant us well-being; O Aditi, bestow well-being upon us.
May we follow the path with well-being, like the sun and the moon;
may we be reunited with one who gives back, who does not strike, and who knows us.
O Śyāvāśva, sing forth boldly with the chanting Maruts—
those worshipful ones who, according to their wont, rejoice in guileless glory.
For they are the companions of steadfast power, acting with boldness;
on their journey, those who are daring protect all people by their own selves.
Like rushing bulls, they leap across the nights;
then we celebrate the greatness of the Maruts in heaven and on earth.
Let us boldly offer our hymn and sacrifice to you among the Maruts—
those who protect every human generation from the injury of mortal man.
To those Maruts, the worthy ones who bestow excellent gifts, heroes of perfect strength— to them, the worshipful ones of heaven, I sing forth the sacrifice.
With their golden ornaments and with their weapons, the lofty heroes have hurled forth their spears.
Following them, like laughing lightnings, the Maruts have come; the radiance of heaven has risen by its own power.
Those who have grown great upon the earth, those who are in the wide mid-air,
whether in the gathering place of the rivers or in the assembly hall of the great heaven.
Praise the host of Maruts, truly powerful and skillful;
for indeed, those heroes, for the sake of glory, have themselves yoked their swift-moving steeds.
Moreover, on the Paruṣṇī river, those pure ones clothed themselves in wool;
moreover, with the tires of their chariots, they split the mountain by their might.
The paths that come from afar, the divergent paths, the inner paths, and the following paths—
with these names for me, they offer the sacrifice as a wide expanse.
Then the men are drawn near; then the teams are drawn near.
Then [appear] those called "from afar"—wondrous forms worthy of being seen.
The singers of hymns, seeking the waters, have danced toward the spring;
they, like certain thieves, were helpers for me to behold their brilliance.
Those who are lofty, whose spears are like lightning, who are seers and wise ordainers—
to that host of Maruts, O seer, pay homage and delight them with your song.
O Seer, go toward the host of Maruts with your gift, as a maiden approaches her friend;
O bold ones, impelled by our prayers, hasten hither from heaven with your power.
Now, mindful of these [deeds], let him not fail to drive toward the gods; may he be united with the liberal patrons who are renowned for their journeys and adorned with ornaments.

The wise ones who, in their desire for kinship, have proclaimed for me the cow; they have proclaimed the speckled one as the mother. And then the skillful ones have proclaimed the impetuous father, Rudra.
Seven times seven powerful ones have each given me a hundred gifts. On the Yamunā, I celebrate the famous gift of cattle; I celebrate the gift of horses.
Who knows their birth, or who was formerly in the favor of the Maruts,
when they yoked their spotted deer?
Who has heard of them as they stood upon their chariots, and how did they go?
For which liberal donor did the rains flow together with the libations, like kinsmen?
They have told me of those who have come with their radiant, winged steeds in exhilaration—
of these blameless heroes and youths, look upon them and sing their praise!
Those who possess their own splendor in their ointments, or in their axes, in their garlands, in their golden ornaments, and in their rings;
those who are upon their chariots and in their bows.
O Maruts, givers of swift gifts, I set my heart upon your chariots for joy,
like the rains descending from the heavens.
The men of liberal gifts have caused the treasure-vat of heaven to shake for the sake of the donor; they release Parjanya throughout the two worlds, and the rains flow across the desert wastes.
Breaking through with their flood, the rivers have rushed forth across the mid-air like milch-cows;
like swift horses at the end of their journey, they scatter as they flow along their courses.
Come, O Maruts, from heaven, from the intermediate space, and from the earth;
do not remain far away.
May the Rasā, Anitabhā, Kubhā, and Krumu not hold you back; may the Sindhu not detain you.
May the turbid Sarayū not stand in your way. May your favor be with us alone.
That host of yours, the brilliant Marut-host of chariots, the company of the ever-new ones—
the rains follow after it.
With beautiful praises and with our prayers, may we follow after every one of their hosts, every troop, and every company.
To whom today have they gone forth— with their well-formed bodies and with oblations offered— to this sacrifice by this course, O Maruts?
With that [wealth] by which you bring inexhaustible seed-grain for our children and descendants—
grant us that gift which we implore from you, and all-encompassing prosperity.
May we pass beyond reproach through blessings, leaving behind blame and hostilities; having rained down health, peace, and water as a healing balm, O Maruts, may we be together with you.
O Maruts, that mortal man shall be a good king, possessed of noble sons and great power, whom you protect; may we be such as he.
Praise the liberal lords on the journey of this singer; let them rejoice like cattle in a pasture.
Since they are like old friends, call after them with song and celebrate those who desire you.
To the host of Maruts, self-luminous and shaking the mountains, I offer this speech;
to those who praise the heat, who sacrifice on the back of heaven, and who possess glorious fame—to them sing forth great manly valor!
O Maruts, your powerful, water-seeking, strength-increasing, horse-yoked bands move all around;
they discharge lightning, Trita roars, and the waters resound as they flow around the woods.

The Maruts, heroes of lightning-splendor, who strike with stones, who flash like the wind, and who shatter the mountains; they are accompanied by rain, suddenly covered in hail, roaring with thunder, impetuous, and of exalted might.
O Rudras, you who are skillful and shakers of all, you traverse the nights, the days, the mid-air, and the regions;
when you drive across the plains like ships upon the waters, O Maruts, you pass through difficult places without being harmed.
That heroic power of yours, O Maruts, and that greatness of yours have extended far, like the sun across its course.
Like these [horses] in their flight, you whose splendor is ungraspable, you who gave no horse, cast down the mountain.
The host of Maruts shone forth when you, O wise ones, stripped the tree like a caterpillar from its sap.
Now, being of one mind, lead our devotion along an easy path, as if leading the eye of one who travels.

O Maruts, he whom you—whether he be a seer or a king—thoroughly protect is neither conquered nor slain; he does not waste away, he does not tremble, and he suffers no harm. His wealth does not fail, nor do his aids; his resources never diminish.
Like men with teams who conquer the host, like Aryaman, the Maruts possess many forms;
when these impetuous ones roar, they swell the fountain and drench the earth with the juice of honey.
This earth is full of downward slopes for the Maruts; the sky becomes full of downward slopes for those who advance.
The paths of the intermediate region are full of downward slopes, and the mountains, which grant life-sustaining gifts, are full of downward slopes.

O Maruts, you who carry the spoils together, heroes of heaven, when the sun has risen you rejoice, O men of the sky. Your horses do not falter as they gallop; instantly you reach the end of this journey.
Upon your shoulders are spears, on your feet rings, golden ornaments on your chests, O Maruts, and splendors upon your chariot;
flames of fire are in your hands like lightning, and golden helmets are spread upon your heads.
O Maruts, you shake the bright fruit from that firmament of the noble one whose splendor is ungraspable;
the enclosures bend together when you, seeking the *ṛta*, send forth your far-reaching shout with flashing brilliance.
O wise Maruts, may we be the masters of chariots of wealth full of vigor given by you;
O Maruts, bestow upon us thousandfold riches that do not fail, like Tiṣya from heaven.
O Maruts, you grant wealth with desirable heroes; you protect the seer who is inspired by the Sāman.
You bestow a swift horse and strength upon the Bharata; you establish a king who is full of obedience.
I beg that wealth from you, O swift-aiding ones, by which we may extend ourselves over men like the sun;
O Maruts, graciously accept this word of mine, through the power of which we may cross over a hundred winters.
The Maruts, worthy of sacrifice, with glittering spears and golden discs upon their breasts, have assumed great vigor.
They speed along with swift, well-governed horses; as they go forth in splendor, their chariots have rolled forward.
You yourselves assume power as you know how; O great ones, you rule far and wide with loftiness.
They have measured out the mid-air with their might; as they go forth in splendor, their chariots have rolled along.
Born together, well-being-bringers, grown up together, these heroes have increased further for the sake of glory alone;
like the radiant rays of the sun, their chariots have turned to follow them as they go in splendor.
O Maruts, your greatness is worthy of adoration; it is worthy of being beheld like the very sight of the sun.
Furthermore, establish us in immortality. As they went forth in splendor, their chariots followed after them.
O Maruts, you raise [the rain] from the ocean; you, O possessors of the waters (*purīṣiṇaḥ*), cause the rain to fall.
Your milch-cows, O wonder-workers (*dasrāḥ*), do not fail; as they go toward splendor, the chariots have rolled forth after them.

When you have yoked the spotted mares to the poles of the horses and have put on your golden mantles, O Maruts, you scatter all rivals; for those who go in splendor, the chariots have turned in their wake.
Neither mountains nor rivers can obstruct you where you have resolved to go, O Maruts; even heaven and earth you pass around. As you proceed in splendor, your chariots have rolled forth in pursuit.

O Maruts, whatever is ancient and whatever is new, whatever is spoken, O Vasus, and whatever is recited—of all that you are the witnesses; as they go toward splendor, their chariots have turned to follow.
Be gracious to us, O Maruts; do not strike us down. Extend to us manifold protection.
Take heed of our hymn and our friendship. As they go forth in splendor, their chariots have turned toward us.
O Maruts, being praised, lead us toward greater prosperity and out from our distresses;
O holy ones, enjoy our offering of oblations, and may we be masters of riches.
O Agni, [bring] the bold host, adorned with golden ornaments and bright decorations;
today I call down the troop of Maruts even from the luminous realm of heaven.
Just as you perceive with your heart, so have my prayers reached you;
strengthen those of fearsome aspect who have come most closely to your invocations.
Like a bountiful woman, the earth, struck down, comes toward us exulting;
O Maruts, your impetuous force is like a fierce bear, like a wild bull, terrifying.
Those who by their might flow forth at will like bulls difficult to restrain—
they, with their journeys, cause even the heavenly stone, the rocky mountain, to tremble.
Arise now with the hymns of these who have been sprinkled [with ghee]—
I call upon the most abundant and unprecedented host of Maruts, like a release of cattle.
Yoke the two ruddy mares to the chariot; yoke the two red ones to the chariots.
Yoke the two swift bay steeds to the pole to draw, the best at drawing, to the pole to draw.
And may that ruddy steed, loud-sounding and worthy of praise, be established here as one beautiful to behold.
O Maruts, let him not delay you on your journeys; urge him forward upon your chariots.
We now invoke the Marut’s chariot, which seeks renown—
the chariot upon which Rodasī stands together with the Maruts, bringing forth delightful gifts.
I invoke that host of yours, brilliant on chariots, impetuous and worthy of praise—
the host in which the well-born, fortunate, and bountiful goddess exults together with the Maruts.
O Rudras, accompanied by Indra and acting in harmony, come on your golden chariots for our well-being!
This prayer of ours is offered to you with delight, like a spring from heaven to one who thirsts for water.
Armed with axes and spears, wise, with good bows, arrows, and quivers;
possessing fine horses and excellent chariots, O sons of Pṛśni, you are well-armed—O Maruts, go forth for glory!
You shake the sky and the mountains for wealth to the donor; the forests bow down before you out of fear on your journey.
O sons of Pṛśni, you stir up the earth when you, the fierce ones, have yoked your spotted deer for glory.
The Maruts, flashing like the wind, clothed in rain, are as alike as twins, well-adorned;
with tawny horses and ruddy steeds, they are stainless, impetuous in their speed, and in their greatness as vast as heaven.

Abounding in drops, adorned with ornaments, bounteous givers, brilliant in appearance, and possessing inexhaustible wealth— well-born by birth, with golden plates upon their breasts, these singers of heaven have attained immortality as their name.

Spears are upon your shoulders, O Maruts; together with you, vigor is placed in your arms and strength is established in your hands. Manly power is in your heads, weapons are upon your chariots, and all your splendor is adorned upon your bodies.
O Maruts, grant us wealth consisting of cattle, horses, chariots, and brave sons; grant us radiant bounty.
O sons of Rudra, bestow upon us high renown; may I enjoy your divine protection.

Come hither, O heroes, O Maruts; have mercy on us! You who possess abundant wealth, you immortals who know the cosmic order (*ṛta*), you who hear the truth, you sages, the youthful ones, who dwell upon lofty mountains and grow great.
Now indeed I praise that powerful host of these most recent Maruts,
who drive with swift horses like rushing winds, and who, as self-ruling lords, exercise sovereignty over immortality.
The brilliant host, powerful, with devouring hands, whose law is to shake, full of magic power, granting gifts— those who bring bliss,
immeasurable in their greatness, O sage, praise those men of abundant wealth!
May your water-bearing steeds come today, all you Maruts who impel the rain.
O Maruts, this fire has been kindled; enjoy it, O youthful sages!

O worshipful Maruts, you bring forth for the people a vigorous king, fashioned by Vibhvan; from you comes the club-wielder urged by his arm, and from you, O Maruts, comes the one with noble steeds and heroic sons.
Like spokes, they are without end; like days, they are born forth again and again, not deficient in their greatness.
The sons of Pṛśni, the most excellent and most powerful, the Maruts, have united themselves by their own intention.
When you have set forth with your spotted deer as horses, O Maruts, on chariots with strong fellies—
the waters surge, the forests give way, and let the bull of heaven, the sun, roar down from above.

Even the earth spread wide at their coming; they have brought forth their own strength like a husband his embryo. For they have yoked the winds as horses to the pole; the sons of Rudra have turned their sweat into rain.
Come, O heroes, O Maruts, be gracious to us—you who possess abundant wealth, are immortal, and know the cosmic order;
you who hear the truth, are seers, youthful, dwelling on lofty mountains, and growing great.
They have stirred themselves for you to grant us prosperity; let me sing praise to Heaven and offer the sacred Law (*ṛta*) to Earth.
They sprinkle their horses and hasten across the mid-air; they relax their own radiance with surging waves.
The earth trembles from fear of them; like a full ship, it quivers as it moves along.
Those heroes, visible from afar, who take heed with their approaches, have exerted themselves within the great assembly.
Like the preeminent horns of cattle for the sake of beauty, like the eye of the sun at the unfolding of the firmament;
like well-formed horses you are lovely, and like young men, O heroes, you take heed for the sake of splendor.
Who could reach the greatness of you, the great ones? Who, O Maruts, your poetic wisdoms, or who your manly deeds?
You indeed cause the earth to tremble like a particle of dust when you bring forth [your power] to grant us prosperity.
Like ruddy horses of the same kin, like heroes eager for combat they have indeed fought;
like well-grown youths, these men have grown strong, and with their rains they diminish the eye of the sun.
They have no eldest, no youngest, and no middle; these breakers-forth have grown great with their majesty.
Well-born by birth, sons of Pṛśni, youths of heaven—come hither toward us!
Like birds that fly in rows by their might from the ridges of the great heaven,
their horses— both kinds as they know— have shaken forth the springs of the mountain.
May Dyaus Aditi low for our enjoyment; may the Dawns, wondrous in their gifts, strive together.
O Seer, these Maruts of Rudra, being praised, have caused the celestial vessel to pour forth.

I praise Agni, the one of good protection, with prostrations; seated here, may he discern our deed. Like chariots seeking booty, I offer [this hymn]; may I succeed in the rightward-turning praise of the Maruts.

The Rudras, the Maruts, who have mounted their famous spotted deer and their easy-gliding chariots—they, O fierce ones, cause even the forests to bow down out of fear of you; even the earth trembles, and even the mountain.
Even the mountain, though greatly grown, was afraid; even the ridge of heaven trembled at your roar.
When you play, O Maruts, armed with spears, you rush together like waters.
Like prize-winning steeds, the sons of Revati have adorned their bodies with gold and their inherent powers;
for the sake of glory, these most excellent and mighty ones have fully displayed their splendors upon their chariots and their persons.
Among these brothers, there is neither eldest nor youngest; they have grown together for the sake of prosperity.
Their father Rudra is youthful and skillful; Pṛśni yields milk well for them, and the days are fair for the Maruts.
Whether you, O Maruts, are in the highest, the middle, or even the lowest heaven, O blessed ones;
therefore, O Rudras, and you, Agni, take notice of this oblation which we offer.
When you, O Maruts, possessors of all wealth, together with Agni, carry [the oblation] from the highest ridge of heaven by your paths,
then you, the roaring ones who destroy the foe, being exhilarated, bestow desirable wealth upon the sacrificer who presses the soma.
O Agni Vaiśvānara, rejoicing with the Maruts—the radiant, hymn-singing, troop-honored ones—drink the Soma;
together with the purifying, all-impelling Āyus, and with your ancient banner.
Who are these most excellent men, who have come one by one from the farthest distance?
Where are your horses, where are your reins? How did you succeed, how did you go? A seat is on your back; the yoke is on your nostrils.
A whip is on their haunches; the men have spread their thighs apart like women giving birth to sons.
Go forth, O heroes, O young men of auspicious birth,
so that you may be like those who have been heated by fire.
May she grant cattle consisting of horses and kine, numbering a hundred sheep,
to the hero praised by Śyāvāśva, for whom she has extended her arms.
Moreover, a woman who is more modest becomes even better than a man who is godless and stingy.
She who discerns the exhausted, the thirsty, and the desirous,
directs her mind toward the gods.
And yet, some unpraised man is called a "Paṇi";
he is equal [to others] only in his obligation to pay the bride-price.
And the exhilarated young woman smoothed the path for Śyāva;
the two ruddy steeds were led forth by Purumīḷha for the sage of far-reaching fame.
He who, like Vaidadaśvi, has given me a hundred cows,
like Taranta with his great bounty.
Those who carry him on their swift steeds, drinking the intoxicating honey-sweet mead, have here acquired glorious renown.
On whose chariots the two worlds shine forth with splendor,
like a golden ornament high in the sky.
That youthful host of Maruts, with its brilliant chariot, is blameless; it moves toward splendor and is irresistible.
Who indeed knows of these, where the shakers revel,
they who are born of Truth and are stainless?
O you who are eager for praise, you are the leaders of the mortal man through this very prayer;
you are the listeners at the invocations of the journey.
O destroyers of enemies, you who are worthy of sacrifice, turn toward us with those desirable and many-glittering riches.
O Night, goddess, carry this hymn of mine away to Dārbhya Ūrmya, as a charioteer carries forth his songs.
And let him speak for me thus when the soma is pressed at Rathavīti’s:
"My desire does not turn away."
This Maghavan, Rathavīti, dwells among the cattle-rich [lands],
taking refuge in the mountains.
By the Truth is your firm Truth covered, where they unyoke the horses of the Sun;
there, ten hundred stood together—I beheld that one supreme form among the forms of the gods.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, that greatness of yours—the waters standing still have milked out day by day;
you cause all the streams of the stall to swell, and for you alone the single stone has rolled onward.
O kings Mitra and Varuṇa, by your greatness you have supported both the earth and the sky.
Increase the plants and cause the cows to swell; release the rain, O you who grant life-giving gifts!
May your well-yoked horses with their reins bring you hither; may they come toward us.
A mantle of clarified butter follows after you; from of old, the rivers flow for you.
They increase the celebrated, far-reaching wisdom, guarding it as one protects the sacrificial grass with a *yajus* formula;
full of reverence and firm in their resolve, they sit upon the throne between Mitra and Varuṇa amidst the *iḷā* offerings.
With hands free from blood, protectors of the righteous, you whom Varuṇa and Iḷā guard within;
O Kings, without malice toward our dominion, you two together uphold the thousand-pillared realm.
With golden girdle and iron pillar, it shines forth like a whip for the horses in heaven. May we win the honeyed draught from the chariot-seat, fixed upon a fertile field or one rich in sesame.
O Varuṇa and Mitra, you ascend the golden throne with its bronze pillars at the dawning of the dawn and at the rising of the sun; from there, you behold both Aditi and Diti.
O bounteous guardians of the world, with that most ample, flawless protection which is not easily pierced, favor us, O Mitra and Varuṇa; may we, seeking to win, be victorious.
O guardians of Truth, you whose laws are true, you mount your chariot in the highest heaven;
for him whom you protect here, O Mitra and Varuṇa, the rain of heaven pours forth sweetness.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you two universal sovereigns rule over this world, beholding the light in the assembly.
We pray for your rain, your bounty, and immortality; the thunders roll across heaven and earth.
Sovereign kings, fierce bulls, lords of heaven and of earth, Mitra and Varuṇa, you who observe all people—
approaching with wondrous clouds, you cause the roar to arise and you make the sky rain through the creative power (*māyā*) of the Asura.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, your wondrous power rests in heaven; the sun moves as a brilliant light, a marvelous weapon.
You conceal him in the sky with cloud and rain; O Parjanya, honey-sweet drops surge forth.

The Maruts harness their easy chariot for glory, like a hero in the search for cattle, O Mitra and Varuṇa. The thundering clouds traverse the bright regions; O sovereign kings of heaven, sprinkle us with milk.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, Parjanya speaks a wondrous, brilliant, and powerful word, full of nourishment;
the Maruts clothe themselves in clouds through their great skill, and you two cause the ruddy, stainless heaven to rain.
By the cosmic law, O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who are wise, you guard the sacred ordinances through the creative power of the Asura.
By the eternal Order, you rule over the entire world; you have placed the sun in heaven as a wondrous chariot.
We invoke with a hymn Varuṇa, the destroyer of enemies, and Mitra for you;
having gone forth from the enclosure as if within our arms, they have reached the sun-like hero.
Stretch out those two arms with benevolence toward this singer who praises you;
for your auspicious and venerable friendship is proclaimed throughout all lands.
That I might now attain the goal—may I go by the path of Mitra; may they abide in the protection of this beloved one who does no harm.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, may we offer you a comparison through this hymn,
so that it may prevail in the dwelling of the wealthy patrons and for the emulation of the singers.
May Mitra and Varuṇa come to us with their radiant splendors to our common dwelling, in our own home, for the prosperity of the wealthy patrons and our friends.
O Varuṇa, you two uphold for us among those [people] a great dominion;
make wide room for us for the winning of booty, for wealth, and for well-being.
While the dawn breaks upon the divine realm and the radiant cow, O worshipful ones,
run hither on foot with your hands like pressed Soma— O heroes, bearing Arcanānas!
He who has perceived it is truly wise; let him speak for us among the gods—he whose songs Varuṇa, the beautiful one, or Mitra accepts.
For they are two kings of most excellent luster, whose fame is heard most widely; they are lords of the virtuous, increasers of *ṛta*, and upholders of *ṛta* among every people.
Approaching you both for protection, I call upon those ancient ones together;
with good horses and through your wise insight, [I call] toward the granting of spoils of war.
Mitra wins a wide path even from distress for his dwelling;
for the favor of Mitra, who overcomes all, belongs to the one who honors him.
May we abide in the most extensive protection of Mitra; through your aid, O Varuṇa, may we be entirely free from distress and possess offspring.
O Mitra, you two urge this people together and lead them on;
do not overlook the patrons, nor us sages—protect us in your shelter!
O mortal, being mindful, bring hither the two gods of noble will who destroy the enemy;
let him offer to Varuṇa, whose form is truth, for great enjoyment.
For they two have attained unswerving dominion and perfect divine power;
and like ordinances, the human race has been established, beautiful to behold like the sun.
We think of you both in this pursuit of chariots, for their wide pasture-land; we celebrate with firm hymns the fair praise of Rātahavya.
For then, O wondrous ones, you two [reveal] the poetic insights through the fortresses of Dakṣa; by the signal of men, you two of purified skill take notice.
O Earth, that is the great cosmic order (*ṛta*) of the seers who seek renown; they flow forth in their journeys, wide and ample, across the two expansive ones who extend afar.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, whose eyes reach far, may we and our wise patrons come hither;
may we strive for your sovereign rule, which is most expansive and provides abundant protection.
Truly, O Ādityas, you have attained here, O Gods, the established, lofty, and holy domain—
O Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman— the most exalted sovereignty.
When you two, Varuṇa and Mitra, sit upon your golden seat,
O sustainers of the people, O destroyers of enemies, grant us your favor.
For all the All-knowing ones—Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman—follow their laws like footsteps; they protect the mortal from harm.
For they are true, touching the cosmic order (*ṛta*), upholders of *ṛta* among every people; they are excellent leaders, bountiful givers, who provide wide passage even from distress.
Who indeed among you two, O Mitra and Varuṇa, has praised your persons? Truly, this prayer seeks you; from the Atris, this prayer seeks you.
Sing forth with an inspired song to Mitra and Varuṇa; they possess great dominion and uphold the lofty cosmic order.
The two sovereign kings who have ghee as their source, both Mitra and Varuṇa,
are the gods praised among the gods.
May you two empower us with great earthly and celestial wealth; for great is your dominion among the gods.
They honor the cosmic order with the cosmic order; they have attained impetuous skill.
The two guileless gods prosper.
The two lords of the rain-giving heaven and the flowing waters, masters of the bountiful earth,
have occupied their lofty seat.

O Varuṇa, you two uphold the three luminous realms and the three heavens; O Mitra, you maintain the three regions. Increasing in power, you guard the dominion of the sovereign according to his ageless vow.
O Varuṇa, your two milch-cows are full of nourishment; O Mitra, your rivers yield honeyed milk.
Three radiant bulls, the depositors of seed, stand over the three Dhiṣaṇās.
At dawn I call upon the goddess Aditi, at midday, and when the sun has risen;
O Mitra and Varuṇa, for wealth and for complete well-being, grant health and prosperity to our children and descendants.
O Ādityas, you who are the sustainers of the radiant realm of space, both of heaven and of earth—
O Mitra and Varuṇa, the immortal gods do not violate your firm decrees.
For even from afar, O Varuṇa and Mitra, your aid is surely present; may I now win your favor.
O you two who are free from malice, may we rightly obtain that nourishment from you for our sustenance; may we be yours, O Rudras.
O Rudras, protect us with your protections and save us, O excellent deliverers; may we overcome the Dasyus with our own bodies.
O you of wondrous power, may we not suffer for the sin of anyone with our own bodies;
may we suffer neither through our offspring nor through our descendants.
Come to us with your great power, O Varuṇa and Mitra, destroyers of enemies;
come to this beautiful sacrifice.
For you two, Varuṇa and Mitra, being wise, rule over all; as lords, cause our prayers to swell with abundance.
Come to our pressed juice, O Varuṇa and Mitra, to the giver,
for the drinking of this Soma.
Like Atri, we invoke Mitra and Varuṇa with our songs;
may you two sit upon the sacred grass for the drinking of the Soma.
By your sacred vow you are steadfast in security; by your law you cause people to come together.
Sit down upon the sacrificial grass for the drinking of Soma.
May Mitra and Varuṇa both graciously accept our sacrifice for the sake of our desire;
may they sit upon the sacred grass to drink the Soma.
Whether you are today in the far distance, O Aśvins, or whether you are nearby; or whether you are in many places, O you who enjoy many things, or in the intermediate space—come hither!
Hither [I call] those two who are most manifold in being, who bear many wondrous deeds;
I call the two irresistible ones, the most powerful, for the sake of the desirable [boon], so that we may enjoy [them].
In one place you have fixed the other, the wondrous wheel of the chariot for its beauty;
with your greatness, you fly around the other human generations and across the realms.
Truly, this deed of yours is well performed, since all our praises follow after you both;
though born separately and stainless, you have entered into kinship with us.
When Sūryā mounted your chariot that always speeds swiftly,
the ruddy birds protected you from the burning heat of the sun.
O Heroes, Atri perceives you with a mind of goodwill,
when he busies himself with the stainless *gharma* offering for you both, O Nāsatyas, with his mouth.
Fierce, preeminent, and swift-moving, your continuous roar is heard during your journeys,
O Aśvins, when Atri turns you hither with his wondrous deeds, O heroes.
O Rudras, lovers of sweetness, may the swelling draught of honey attend you,
when you carry across the ocean and bring to you ripe nourishments.
Truly, O Aśvins, they call you both the bringers of joy;
you who are most worthy of being invoked at the start of the journey, and who are most gracious upon the journey.
May these most peaceful prayers, which we have fashioned like chariots, be a source of increase for the Aśvins; we have uttered this great homage.
O Aśvins, gods rich in thought, come today from heaven to Kūṣṭha; O you who possess bull-like wealth, hear this, for Atri seeks to win you over.
Where are those two? Where indeed are the famous Nāsatyas, the gods in heaven?
To which people do you hasten, or who is with you among the rivers?
To whom do you go? To whom indeed do you proceed? Toward whom do you yoke your chariot?
In whose sacred hymns (*brahmāṇi*) do you take delight? We desire you both for our protection.
For you two enliven even the city-dweller submerged in water, O Paura and Paurāya;
when he is seized for the sake of capture, like a lion in the lair of the malicious.
From Cyavāna, who was worn out by age, you stripped away his skin as if it were a garment;
when you made him young again, he fulfilled the desire of his wife.
For here is your praiser; we are present for your glorious sight. Now hear me and come with your protections, O you who possess abundant wealth!
Who among the many mortals has won you today?
Who, O you who are borne by inspired hymns, is the sage? Who, O you whose wealth is in steeds, [has won you] with sacrifices?
O Aśvins, let your chariot—the swiftest among chariots—come hither; let our praise, longing for you, pass through many [obstacles] to reach among mortals.
May our praise be well-received by you two who long for the honeyed draught;
O wise ones, fly hitherward with your winged steeds like two falcons.
O Aśvins, whenever you might hear this invocation, may your excellent enjoyments be ours; indeed, your gifts are abundant.
O Aśvins, lovers of sweetness, the R̥ṣi who praises you adorns his chariot with a hymn of praise—a most beloved, powerful vehicle that carries wealth; hear my invocation!
Come forth, O Aśvins, passing beyond all the people;
O wonder-workers on golden paths, most gracious ones borne by the rivers, lovers of sweetness, hear my call!
O Aśvins, bringing us treasures, come to us—you two Rudras who travel on golden paths, lovers of the strong drink, possessors of wealth, and sweet ones; hear my invocation!
O you of excellent praise, possessors of rain-wealth, the voice is placed upon your chariot like a quiver.
And your towering beast, the wondrous source of nourishment, makes it manifest; O lovers of sweetness, hear my call!
With awakened minds, eager for the chariot, and hearing our invocation, O Aśvins, you come down with your birds to Cyavāna, who is free from duplicity; O lovers of sweetness, hear my call!
O Heroes, may your mind-yoked horses, dappled in hue, carry you hither for the draught, together with blessings, O Aśvins; O lovers of sweetness, hear my invocation.
O Aśvins, come hither; O Nāsatyas, do not look away from us. Even past the path of the noble one, come on your circuit, O undeceivable ones; O lovers of sweetness, hear my call.
O Lords of Splendor, invincible at this sacrifice, you two Aśvins attend to the singer who seeks your aid; O lovers of sweetness, hear my invocation.
Dawn has appeared with her radiant cattle; Agni, the seasonal one, has been established.
O wonder-workers, masters of wealth, your immortal chariot has been yoked. O lovers of sweetness, hear my call!
Agni shines forth as the face of the dawns; the god-seeking voices of the sages have arisen.
O Aśvins, come now hither on your chariot toward this overflowing warm oblation.
The two who travel most swiftly do not measure out their prepared course; the Aśvins will surely come here now to this praise.
At the arrival of day, they are most ready to come with help; they are the most beneficent turners-away of misfortune for the donor.
And come at the time of gathering, in the morning, at midday, and at the rising of the sun;
by day and by night, with your most auspicious aid, O Aśvins, let not our draught remain unextended today.
For this, O Aśvins, has been your dwelling-place since of old; these are your houses, this is your home.
Come to us from the lofty heaven, from the mountain, and from the waters, bringing food and strength.
May we come together with the newest, joy-bestowing aid of the Aśvins, through their excellent guidance.
O Immortals, bring to us wealth and heroic sons, and all auspicious blessings.
Worship first those who travel at dawn; let them drink before the greedy and stingy [Rudras].
For the Aśvins establish the sacrifice at dawn; the sages praise them as the ones who receive the first portion.
Worship the Aśvins at dawn; urge them forward. There is no sacrifice to the gods in the evening that is not pleasing.
Moreover, another besides us sacrifices, and each preceding sacrificer is more successful than the one after him.

Your chariot rolls forward, O Aśvins, with golden skin, honey-colored, dripping with ghee, and carrying nourishment; it is as swift as thought and fleet as the wind, by which you pass over all difficulties.

He who has served most abundantly for the two Nāsatyas and gives the sweetest portion of food at the distribution—may he, through his peaceful deeds, bring his offspring across; may he ever surpass those whose flames do not rise upward.
May we come together with the newest, joy-bestowing aid and excellent guidance of the Aśvins.
O Immortals, bring to us wealth, heroic sons, and all auspicious blessings.
O Aśvins, come here; O Nāsatyas, do not be indifferent. Fly hither like two swans to the pressed juices.
O Aśvins, like two deer or like two wild oxen following the pasture,
fly hither like two swans to the pressed juices.
O Aśvins, possessors of abundant wealth, may you enjoy this sacrifice for our success;
fly hither to the pressed juices like two swans.
When Atri, descending into the *ṛbīsa*, called upon you both like a woman in distress,
O Aśvins, you came with the swiftest and most recent speed of a hawk.
Open wide, O Lord of the Forest, like the birth-canal of a woman about to give birth!
Hear my call, O Aśvins, and release Saptavadhri.
For the terrified and imploring seer Saptavadhri,
O Aśvins, you two by means of your wondrous powers both joined together and then tore apart the tree.
Just as the wind stirs a lotus pond on every side, so may your embryo stir; may it come forth, having been ten months in the womb.
As the wind, as the forest, as the ocean stirs,
so do you, O ten-month-old one, come forth together with the afterbirth.
Having lain for ten months within his mother,
may the boy come forth alive and uninjured— alive from the living woman.
Awaken us today for great wealth, O Uṣas, radiant as the sun,
just as you have awakened us before for Satyaśravas Vāyya, O well-born one, rich in horses and noble gifts.
O Dawn, daughter of Heaven, who with a noble guide and a chariot of purity you have shone forth—
you, O well-born one, rich in horses and kind favors, shine forth for Vāyya, the son of Sahas, whose fame is true.
May she, who brings us wealth, dawn for us today, O Daughter of Heaven—
you who have shone forth for Sahīyas, for Satyaśravas, for Vāyya, O well-born one, rich in horses and noble gifts!
O radiant one, those priests who praise you with hymns— O bounteous lady, O nobly born one, mistress of horses and truth— may they be well-favored, rich in gifts, and liberal in their rewards.
For even if these throngs of yours do not please you for the sake of granting wealth,
they have nevertheless offered their desires around you, O noble-born one, you who are rich in horses and true bounty, as they bestow unashamed gifts.
Bestow upon these patrons, O wealthy Dawn, glory accompanied by heroes—
upon those liberal lords who have bestowed upon us undaunted gifts, O well-born one, rich in horses and noble steeds!
O generous Uṣas, bring great splendor and fame to them, those wise patrons who, O nobly born one, rich in horses and true to your gifts, grant us wealth in horses and cattle.
And bring us food accompanied by cattle, O Daughter of Heaven,
together with the rays of the sun, with bright and glowing beams— O well-born one, rich in horses and noble gifts!
Shine forth, O daughter of heaven; do not delay in spreading out your waters, lest the sun scorch you with his flame like a thief or an enemy, O well-born one, rich in horses!
O Uṣas, you ought to grant us this much, or even more— you who, O radiant one,
never fail those who praise you as you shine forth, O well-born one, rich in horses and boons.
The inspired singers praise with their hymns the goddess Uṣas, who illumines the sky, who is vast, faithful to the cosmic order, red-hued, shining brightly, and bringing forth the light of heaven.
This one, beautiful to behold, awakening the people, making the paths easy to travel, goes at the head;
the great charioted, the lofty, the all-impelling Dawn bestows light at the beginning of days.
Yoking herself with ruddy kine, she who never fails has brought hither wealth that does not perish;
carving out paths for well-being, the goddess, much-praised and possessing all boons, shines forth.
This one becomes a dappled bird, doubly great, revealing her body from the front;
she follows the path of *ṛta* correctly, as if knowing it well, and does not miss the directions.
Like a bright woman conscious of her body, she has stood up for us to behold, as if bathing in the heights;
driving away hatred and the darknesses, Uṣas, the daughter of Heaven, has come with her light.
This daughter of heaven, facing toward men like a gracious maiden, unbinds her garment.
Revealing desirable treasures for the donor, the youthful woman has once again established the light as of old.

The inspired poets harness their minds and harness their thoughts for the sake of the great, inspired, and wise one. He alone, who knows the sacred ordinances, ordains the priestly functions; vast indeed is the praise of the god Savitṛ.
The Seer puts on all forms; he has brought forth what is auspicious for bipeds and quadrupeds.
Savitar, the one to be chosen, has looked upon the firmament; he shines along the departure of the Dawn.
After whose departure other gods have followed according to the majesty of that god by his might—
he, the divine Savitṛ, the steed Etaśa, who measured out the earthly regions with his greatness.
And you go, O Savitṛ, to the three luminous realms, and you unite with the rays of the sun;
and you encompass the night on both sides, and by your divine laws, O God, you become Mitra.
And you alone are the lord of procreation; moreover, O God, you become Pūṣan through your journeys.
And you rule over this entire world; Śyāvāśva has brought this hymn of praise to you, O Savitṛ.
We choose that nourishment of the divine Savitṛ;
we meditate upon the most excellent, all-sustaining, and swift bounty of Bhaga.
For no one at all diminishes this most glorious and beloved sovereign dominion of Savitar.
For Savitṛ, as Bhaga, bestows treasures upon the donor;
him we implore for that wondrous portion.
O God Savitar, impel for us today auspicious fortune accompanied by progeny;
drive away evil dreams.
O God Savitṛ, drive all misfortunes far away;
send us that which is auspicious.
Sinless, under the impulse of the divine Savitṛ, may we obtain from Aditi all desirable things.
Today we choose with hymns the Lord of the True, the possessor of all gods, Savitar, whose impulse is truth.
He who goes before these two days, never failing—
the self-dependent god Savitṛ.
Savitṛ, who makes all these created beings hear with his song of praise, shall also impel them forward.
Speak toward the powerful one with these songs; praise Parjanya and win him over with homage.
Bellowing like a bull, the swift-giver bestows seed as a germ within the plants.
He strikes down the trees and he strikes down the demons; the entire world trembles before his great weapon.
Even the innocent man flees from the one possessing such virile power, when Parjanya, thundering, strikes down the evildoers.
Like a charioteer lashing his horses with a whip, he makes his messengers of rain visible;
from afar the roar of the lion rises up when Parjanya makes the sky rainy.
The winds blow forth, the lightnings fly down, the plants shoot up, and the sky overflows.
Nourishment is born for every living being when Parjanya protects the earth with his seed.
He under whose ordinance the earth bows down, under whose ordinance the hoofed cattle spring about,
and under whose ordinance the plants are of every form— O Parjanya, grant us great protection.
