O Maruts, bestow rain upon us from heaven; cause the streams of the stallion to swell.
Come hither with this thundering, pouring down the waters, you who are our father, the Asura.
Roar out, thunder, and deposit the embryo; fly around with your water-laden chariot.
Draw forth the leather bag, let it loose and turn it downward; let the heights and the depths become level.
Draw up the great reservoir and pour it down; let the released channels flow forward.
Drench heaven and earth with clarified butter; let there be a good drinking-place for the cows.
O Parjanya, when you roar and thunder, striking down the evildoers,
all this world rejoices at it— whatever exists upon the earth.
You have rained down rain; now lift it up and seize it! You have made the deserts passable.
You have generated the plants for the sake of nourishment, and you have found wisdom for all creatures.
Truly, O Earth, you bear the weight that crushes the mountains;
you who, possessing great power, quicken the earth with your might, O Mighty One.
O far-reaching one, hymns of praise resound toward you through the nights—
you who, O bright one, have sent forth the swelling flood like a neighing steed toward booty.
You who, by your might, firmly sustain even the great trees upon the earth;
when from the cloud and the lightning of heaven your rains pour down.
Sing forth a lofty, profound, and beloved prayer to the renowned Varuṇa, the sovereign lord,
who has spread out the earth like a butcher spreading a hide for the sun.
In the forests he has spread out the mid-air; he has placed speed in the horses, milk in the cows;
Varuṇa has established will in hearts, fire in the waters, the sun in heaven, and Soma on the mountain.
Varuṇa has released the water-skin with its opening downward toward the two worlds and the mid-air;
with it, the king of the entire world bedews the earth as rain bedews the barley.
He moistens the earth, the broad ground, and even the sky, as soon as Varuṇa desires the milked [rain] to come.
Then the mountains clothe themselves in clouds; the mighty ones, exerting their strength, relax their vigour.

I shall proclaim this great cosmic power (*māyā*) of the renowned Varuṇa, the son of the Asuras: he who, as if by measure, has established himself in the mid-air and measured out the earth with the sun.
Now, no one has ever dared to withstand this great creative power (*māyā*) of the most wise god:
that the bright rivers, though pouring forth their waters, fill but a single ocean as if with drops.

Whether toward one who is worthy of honor, O Varuṇa, or one who is friendly, or a companion, or even a brother, or a neighbor— whether constant or a stranger— whatever offense we have committed against you, O Varuṇa, loosen that from us.
Whatever the gamblers have cheated at play, whether it be what we know to be true or what we do not know—all that, O God Varuṇa, loosen like something slack; then may we be dear to you.
O Indra and Agni, that mortal whom you both protect in battles for booty—
he shall shatter even firm strongholds, just as Trita split the voices of the clouds.
Those who are invincible in battles, those who are worthy of renown in the contests for booty,
those who are supreme over the five peoples— Indra and Agni, them we invoke.
Truly, the impetuous power of those two lords is fierce; their sharp lightning-flash, with its wooden shaft, speeds forth from the hands of the bounteous slayers of Vṛtra toward the cattle.
In this pursuit of chariots, we invoke you both, O Indra and Agni—
the lords of swift bounty, the wise ones, most fond of songs of praise.
Increasing day by day for the mortal, those two undeceivable gods—
though they are worthy of worship— I place before me like two portions for a steed.
Thus has this strengthening oblation been offered to Indra and Agni, purified by the pressing-stones like clarified butter.
O you two, bestow great renown upon our patrons, and bestow wealth and nourishment upon those who sing your praises.
Let your hymns go forth to the great Viṣṇu, who is accompanied by the Maruts, born from the mountains, whose movement is swift;
let them go forth to the host that is worthy of sacrifice, easy to invoke, powerful, praised in worship, and to that strength whose law is the roaring wind.
Those who were born by their greatness, and those who now themselves proclaim [their deeds] through their wisdom—O Evayāmarut!
That power of yours, O Maruts, cannot be assailed by will; by their bounty and their majesty, they are unassailable like the mountains.
Those who are heard from afar with their song from the lofty heaven, the brilliant and well-formed ones, O Evayāmarut;
they whose common dwelling no enemy can master, like fires with their own lightning, they rush forward, the roarers of the thundering ones.
That wide-striding one has stepped forth from the great common seat, O Evayāmarut;
when he has yoked himself by his own power upon his lofty heights, he, the increaser of bliss, goes forth with his men, vying in greatness and full of splendor.
Like your own roar, the mighty bull has caused all things to tremble— the brilliant, rushing, and powerful one, Evayāmarut— by whom they advance,
conquering with their own radiance, holding golden reins, wielding excellent weapons, and impetuous.
Boundless is your greatness, O you of increased strength; let your brilliant power protect us, O Evayāmarut!
For you stand as protectors in the sight of the snare; as such, deliver us from reproach, shining like fires.
May those Rudras, who are like well-kindled fires and possess abundant splendor, protect us—O Evayāmarut!
The terrestrial seat has spread out long and wide for them, whose hosts are great in their marches, they whose offenses are wondrously absent.
O Maruts, free from hatred, find a path for us; hear the call of the singer, O Evayāmarut!
United in spirit with the great Viṣṇu, keep enmities far away from us, as charioteers ward off dangers with their wondrous deeds.
O you worthy of sacrifice, come to our well-prepared sacrifice; hear our call, O you who are without guile and whose march is swift.
Like the highest mountains in the sky, may you, O wise ones, be difficult for the reviler to overcome.
For you, O Agni, were the first inventor of this prayer, the wondrous invoker;
you, O bull, made that power invincible, for the sake of prevailing over every power.
Then you sat down as the Hotṛ, the most skilled in sacrifice, at the place of the libation, seeking nourishment, worthy of praise.
Toward you, the first one, men seeking the gods and striving for great wealth have followed.
As if moving through a veil of many riches, those who are watchful have followed after you for wealth—
the radiant Agni, the beautiful, the lofty, the fatty, who shines forever.
Seeking glory, they have attained unimpaired glory by approaching with reverence the station of the god;
they have even assumed names worthy of sacrifice, and they have rejoiced in your auspicious appearance.
The peoples upon the earth increase thee; both kinds of wealth of men belong to thee.
Thou art known as the savior in the crossing over; thou art ever the father and the mother of human beings.
Worthy of honor, beloved among the people, Agni the Hotṛ, the joyous and most skilled in sacrifice, has sat down.
As such, we, bowing low with reverence, shall sit near you as you shine within our home.
As such, we, the pure-minded ones seeking your favor and longing for the gods, implore you, O Agni, as the new one.
You, O Agni, have led the people, shining with the great light of heaven.

The sage of the people, the lord of the eternal tribes, the subduer, the bull among men; Agni, who seeks the advance of prayers, who bestows nourishment, the purifier, the ruler, the worshipful one among riches.
O Agni, that mortal has sacrificed and labored who has attained your gift of oblation with fuel; he who understands the offering with prostrations, protected by you, gains all desirable things.

To you, the great one, we pay homage with great reverence, O Agni, with fuel and with oblations. On the altar, O Son of Strength, with songs and hymns; may we strive to abide in your auspicious favor.

O Agni, you who have spread across the two worlds with your light and with your glories— you, the seeker of renown and the deliverer— shine forth for us even more widely with great, enduring, and abundant strengths.
O Vasu, grant us evermore, like a man, abundant cattle for our children and descendants;
may there be many great and sinless refreshments for us, and may auspicious glories be ours.
O King Agni, may I obtain through my devotion to you many treasures in manifold ways, for they are yours to bestow.
O Agni, Lord of many boons, there are indeed many riches within you, for you, the King, belong to the one who serves you.
For you, O Agni, possess lordly glory like Mitra;
you, O all-beholding Vasu, foster renown like prosperity.
For indeed, the peoples invoke you with sacrifices and with songs;
to you the prize-winning steed, free from malice, traversing the mid-air and beholding all people, goes forth.
In unison, the men of heaven kindle you, the banner of the sacrifice,
when this human folk, seeking favor, invokes you at the ritual.
The mortal who exerts himself with prayer for you, the Bountiful Giver, succeeds;
through the aid of the Great Heaven, he crosses over his enemies as if over distress.
The mortal who, with fuel, attains your oblation and sharpening power,
O Agni— he prospers in a dwelling rich in offspring and lasting a hundred years.
Your brilliant smoke rises up, bright and spread abroad in heaven; for like the sun in its splendor, O Purifier, you shine with your radiant form.
For thus you are to be praised among the people, our dear guest;
delightful like an aged fortress, and worthy of protection like a son.

For by your power, O Agni, you are anointed in the wooden vat like a prize-winning steed; like one who circles the earth, you are self-sustaining and a household lord; like a swift horse, you are a young child who must be summoned.
O Agni, you [devour] even those things that are immovable, like a beast in a pasture; for when your powers, O undecaying one, cut down the trees, you are the skillful one.
For you, O Agni, go as the Hotṛ-priest in the house of the people who perform the sacrifice;
O Lord of the People, bring us prosperity and graciously accept the oblation, O Aṅgiras.
O God, Agni, whose greatness is like Mitra’s, call hither the gods for us; [seek] the favor of Heaven and Earth.
Approach the men of heaven for well-being and secure dwelling; may we cross over our enemies, distresses, and difficulties—may we cross them, may we cross them by your protection.

O Agni, he shall dwell in peace, a guardian of Truth born of Truth; seeking the gods, he attains your wide light—he, the mortal whom you, O God, together with Mitra and Varuṇa, protect from distress by casting it away.
He has sacrificed with sacrifices, he has labored with holy rites, and he has offered gifts to Agni whose doors are prosperous.
Even so, no lack of glory, no distress, and no arrogance reaches that mortal.
Like the sun, whose appearance is stainless, when your terrifying vision comes upon the burning one, your thought is stirred;
like the booty of a neighing steed, this dwelling of the forest-born one is delightful wherever it may be at night.
Even his sharp form is great; with his mouth he devours like a horse controlled by the reins. His tongue flickers like an axe; burning, he consumes the wood like a swift consumer.
Like an archer about to shoot, he aims; he sharpens his brilliance like the edge of iron.
With wondrous course, he is the chariot-pole who, like a bird alighting on a tree, has swift flight and rapid strides at nightfall.
Like a singer, he clothes himself in the rays of dawn; great as Mitra, he roars with his flame—He who is ruddy by night and by day for men, the immortal one, ruddy by day for men.
Like the roar of heaven when it bestows gifts, the bull has bellowed; he has roared among the plants.
Like one who moves with fervor on his flight, he has filled the two worlds, the well-wedded pair, with wealth.
He who, with nourishing and fitting hymns, has flashed like lightning with his own vital powers;
he who, like the skillful Rbhu, fashioned the host of the Maruts—he, the impetuous and fierce, has shone forth.
Just as you, O Hotṛ, son of strength, perform the sacrifice with oblations among the gods for the sake of man,
so today, O Agni, desiring them, sacrifice to the desiring gods, bringing together those who are alike in this assembly.
May that Agni, the radiant one who beholds us at the break of day, grant us delight— he who is worthy of praise and knowledge,
the immortal who possesses all life among mortals, the guest who awakens at dawn, Jātavedas.
Whose majesty the heavens admire as if it were the sun—bright like the sun, he clothes himself in splendors;
he who, undecaying and purifying, drives forth [the darkness], has shattered even the ancient fortresses of Aśna.
For you, O Son, are a speaker; Agni, seated at the feast, has by his very birth made food for himself on his path.
As such, O winner of strength, bestow strength upon us; like a king, dwell among us in a place free from wolves.
He who sharpens his weapons and devours the resisting food, like Vāyu the sovereign, passes through the nights;
may we overcome those who oppose your commands, as a swift horse avoids falling pitfalls.
Like the sun with its radiant rays, O Agni, you have spread through both worlds with your light;
brilliant and anointed with flame, he leads us beyond the darkness, flying like the son of Uśij in his flight.
For we have chosen you, the most delightful one, with the flames of our hymns; O Agni, hear our great prayer!
Like Indra, no deity fills you with power as much as the most heroic men fill you, O best of men, with their bounty.
Now, O Agni, lead us safely by paths free from danger to wealth; carry us across distress.
Grant those blessings to our patrons and to the singer; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.
I invoke for you the Son of Strength, the youthful one, whose speech is free from guile, the youngest, with our prayers— him who, being wise,
impels riches containing all boons, he who is much-desired and free from deceit.
In thee, O many-faced Invoker, the worshipful ones have placed their treasures at evening and at dawn;
in thee, the purifier, they have gathered all blessings as all beings are gathered upon the earth.
From of old you have sat among these people; by your wisdom, you became the charioteer of desirable things.
Therefore, O wise Jātavedas, you bestow riches in succession upon the one who serves you.

O Agni, whoever from afar seeks to harm us, or whoever, though great as Mitra, would act as an enemy against us—burn him with your own ageless bulls; O most burning one, being yourself full of heat, consume him with your heat.

O Son of Strength, that mortal who honors you with sacrifice, with kindled fuel, with hymns, and with songs— he, O Immortal One, being wise among mortals, shines forth with wealth, splendor, and renown.
O Agni, do that quickly as you are impelled; O powerful one, overcome the rivals with your might.
Since you are praised with words throughout the days, take pleasure in this; let the singer’s prayer resound.
May we attain that desire of ours through your protection, O Agni; may we attain wealth, O Lord of Wealth, with noble heroes.
May we attain booty, seeking booty; may we attain your undecaying and ageless glory.
Seeking a path by means of sacrifice with a new hymn, he approaches the Son of Strength;
the Hotṛ-priest goes toward the divine one who cuts down the forest, whose path is black, who is radiant, and who is invited to the feast.
White-shining, thundering, dwelling in the luminous realm with his ageless, roaring flames, most youthful Agni— the purifier who is most manifold— goes forth devouring many broad things.
O pure Agni, your pure flames, impelled by the wind, spread forth in every direction;
fiercely consuming, like divine Navagvas, they boldly shatter the forests.
O Radiant One, those bright and pure steeds of yours, let loose, shave the earth as they go;
then your whirling flame shines far and wide, sweeping across the ridges of the speckled earth.

Then the tongue of the bull, who fights for cattle, darts forward like a released thunderbolt; like the snare of a hero, the consuming power of Agni, difficult to restrain and terrible, devours the forests.
With the radiance of the great impeller, you have boldly spread across the earthly expanses.
As such, drive away all fears with your powers; contending against rivals, burn up those who seek to harm us.

O Wondrous One, bestow upon us wondrous wealth—most wondrous, a bestower of strength, with marvelous dominion—that is bright, vast, and rich in many heroes; O Radiant One, grant it to the singer with your radiant rays.
The gods have generated from their mouth Agni Vaiśvānara— the head of heaven, the messenger of earth, born in the cosmic order (ṛta)—
the sage, the sovereign, the guest of men, as a vessel.
They have celebrated him, the navel of sacrifices, the seat of riches, the great vessel;
the gods generated Vaiśvānara, the charioteer of the rites, the banner of sacrifice.
From you, O Agni, is born the inspired singer, the winner of booty; from you come heroes who overcome the enemy.
O Vaiśvānara, O King, bestow upon us desirable riches.
O Immortal Vaiśvānara, when you were being born, all the gods celebrated you together like a newborn infant;
through your mental powers they attained immortality when you shone forth from your two parents.
O Vaiśvānara Agni, no one has dared to violate those great ordinances of yours, when,
being born in the lap of your parents, you found the banner of light in the appointed places of the days.

By the vision of Vaiśvānara and by the signal of the immortal, the ridges of heaven have been measured out. Upon his head, indeed, all beings have grown like branches; seven streams have sprouted upward.
He of skillful wisdom who measured out the realms, Vaiśvānara, the seer who [measured] the luminous spheres of heaven;
he who has spread himself around all beings, the undeceived guardian and protector of immortality.
Now I shall proclaim the power of the nourishing, virile, ruddy one; I shall proclaim the sacrificial rites of Jātavedas. A new, pure hymn flows for Vaiśvānara, as clear as Soma, beautiful for Agni.

Being born in the highest heaven, Agni, the guardian of vows, protected the sacred ordinances. With his skillful wisdom, Vaiśvānara measured out the mid-air and touched the firmament with his greatness.
The wondrous Mitra propped apart heaven and earth; he drove away the darkness with light between them.
Vaiśvānara rolled out the two worlds like two skins and assumed all manly vigor.
In the lap of the waters, the buffalo seized him; the clans waited upon the King, the one worthy of praise.
Mātariśvan, as a messenger from afar, brought Agni Vaiśvānara from the dwelling of Vivasvat.
In age after age, O Agni, bestow upon those who praise you a wealth that is worthy of the assembly, glorious, and ever-new.
O King, O Unaging One, as with a sharp blade, strike down the evildoer; smite him low with your splendor, as one fells a tree.
O Agni Vaiśvānara, maintain for us among our patrons an unaging dominion and excellent heroic power; may we, through your protections, O Agni, win booty consisting of hundreds and thousands.
O Desired One, with your undeceivable guardians, protect our patrons, O you who abide in the three places! And guard the host of us who give, O Agni Vaiśvānara; being praised, prolong our lives.
The black day and the bright day revolve by means of the known regions;
being born, Agni Vaiśvānara, like a king, has driven away the darkness with his light.
I do not know the warp nor the woof, nor that which they weave while striving together in the contest.
Who indeed, being the son here, can speak words of wisdom beyond his father who is below him?

He indeed knows the warp and he knows the woof; he shall speak the words that ought to be spoken in due season—he who, as the guardian of immortality, understands this, moving below while seeing beyond another.
This is the first Hotṛ; behold him! This is the immortal light among mortals.
He was born, firmly seated, the immortal one increasing in his body.
A firm light has been established for all to behold, the mind, the swiftest among those that fly within. All the gods, of one mind and one purpose, proceed successfully toward that single will.
My two ears fly apart; my sight flies apart; this light that was placed within my heart flies apart.
My mind wanders away, intent on distant things: what indeed shall I say, and what now shall I imagine?
All the gods, trembling with fear, paid homage to you, O Agni, as you stood in the darkness. May Vaiśvānara protect us for our aid; may the Immortal protect us for our aid.
Place before you at the commencement of the sacrifice, during the rite, the delightful, celestial Agni, with a well-fashioned hymn;
place him before you with your chants, for he, our radiant Jātavedas, shall make our sacrifices perfect.
O brilliant Hotṛ Agni, kindled by the fires of Manu, you who possess many forms—
just as one honors a guest, our thoughts purify for you this hymn of praise and strength, like pure clarified butter.
He has flourished among mortals with glory, the sage who has given to Agni with hymns of praise. To him, O you of wondrous luster, he of wondrous aids grants the winning of a stall full of cattle.
He who, at his birth, filled the two wide worlds with far-reaching light along his black path—
then the purifier, though amidst the thick darkness of night, became visible by his flame.
Now, O Agni, with your many-favored aids, bestow upon us wonderful wealth and upon our patrons—
those who, through their bounty, their fame, and their heroic deeds, surpass all other people.
O Agni, desiring it, accept this sacrifice which the offerer of oblations, sitting before you, presents with his mouth;
among the Bharadvājas, you have established the well-fashioned hymn for the winning of prize-winning booty.
Drive away our enemies; increase our prosperity. May we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.
Sacrifice, O Hotṛ, being impelled as the best of sacrificers, O Agni, like the incitement of the Maruts.
May Mitra and Varuṇa, the Nāsatyas, Heaven and Earth, turn hither for our sacrifice.
You are our most delightful Hotṛ, the guileless god among mortals at the assemblies.
O Agni, as the bearer with your purifying tongue and mouth, perform the sacrifice for your own body.
For even the blessed prayer yearns for you, so that the singer may worship the gods at the sacrifice;
when the most inspired of the Aṅgirases, the sage, the seer, utters the honeyed hymn at the rite.
He has shone forth, the self-purifying, far-resplendent Agni; perform the sacrifice for the two wide-reaching worlds, O Agni.
Him whom the five peoples, offering oblations with reverence, anoint like Āyu, he who is rich in nourishment.
When the sacred grass is trimmed with reverence for Agni, the ladle is extended, filled with ghee and well-prepared;
the dwelling-place has been established upon the seat of the earth, and the sacrifice has taken its stand like the eye in the sun.
O Agni, many-faceted Hotṛ, being kindled with the gods and with the fires, grant us favor;
O Son of Strength, clothing ourselves in wealth, may we pass beyond distress as if over a narrow pass.
In the midst of the dwelling, the Hotṛ, the king upon the sacred grass, Agni, shall worship the two worlds with his goad;
this Son of Strength, the observer of Truth, has spread himself from afar like Sūrya with his brilliance.
O King, worthy of sacrifice, you who are well-disposed toward us—may Heaven, as it were, appear at every turn for our complete success;
may he, dwelling in the three abodes, like one who has crossed over the flood, accept the offerings and the riches of men for the sake of worship.

Whose impetus is most brilliant, who rules over the woods; like a goad increasing on the path, he has shone forth. Like a guileless runner, the immortal one, irresistible among the plants, takes heed of himself.
May Agni Jātavedas be praised in our home with our impetuous songs like swift steeds;
winning the wood with his power like a racer, he has been brought to old age by our sacrifices like a father.
Now they admire his splendors when he hews them out at will and follows after the broad earth—
he who, released and rushing, runs swiftly, like a debtor or a thief crossing the desert wastes.
As such, O steed, being kindled with all thy fires, O Agni, protect us from reproach;
bring us wealth, drive away misfortune, and may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with brave sons.
From you, O blessed Agni, all fortunes issue forth like the branches from a tree;
through your readiness to hear, there comes wealth, strength in the conquest of Vṛtra, the rain from heaven, and the flow of waters—O you who are worthy of praise.
You are Bhaga for us, for you grant wealth; like one who travels all around, you dwell with wondrous luster.
O Agni, like Mitra, you are the steward of the great *ṛta* and of abundant beauty, O God.

That true lord of the people slays Vṛtra with his might; O Agni, the inspired sage brings away the prize from the Pani, whom you, O wise one born of Truth, being in harmony with wealth, urge on through the grandson of the Waters.

O Son of Strength, that mortal who, through songs, hymns, and sacrifices, has attained sharpening for you in the sacred knowledge—O God Agni, he receives every desirable thing; he possesses grain and rules over all riches.
O Agni, Son of Strength, bestow upon men those glorious and heroic riches that they may prosper;
for by your power you provide abundant nourishment for cattle against the ravenous wolf and the predatory enemy.

O Son of Strength, you who are far-reaching and eloquent, O Agni, grant us offspring and descendants rich in booty. Through all our songs, may we attain fulfillment; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.
That mortal who, with his thoughts and prayers, has delighted in the service of Agni—
may he, enjoying it, choose for us abundant food as his aid from of old.
For Agni indeed is the wise one; Agni is the most skillful seer.
At the sacrifices, the human clans invoke Agni as the Hotṛ-priest.
For various indeed, O Agni, are the riches of the enemy contending for your protection;
the Āyus, overcoming the Dasyu, strive by means of sacred observances to subdue the lawless.
Agni bestows a hero, a lord of the virtuous, who wins the waters and overcomes the attackers; at the mere sight of his might, his enemies tremble with fear.
For Agni, by his wisdom, the god protects the mortal from reproach;
he is the victorious one whose wealth is never obstructed, whose riches are unobstructed in the contests for booty.
O Agni, great as Mitra, call hither to us the gods, O god; proclaim our good will to Heaven and Earth.
Attain well-being and secure dwelling from heaven for our men; may we cross over hatreds, distresses, and difficulties—may we cross them, may we cross them by your protection.
I strive with my song toward this guest of yours, who awakens at dawn, the lord of all people;
he comes from heaven by his very birth, pure as he is, and though long established, he consumes even that which is unshakable as a child in the womb.
Like a well-placed friend whom the Bhr̥gus established in the tree, he who is worthy of praise with his flames rising upward—
O Wondrous One, being well-pleased at the sacrifice of Vitahavya, you are magnified day by day with hymns of praise.
As such, be the harmless increaser of Dakṣa’s power, the overcomer of the enemy, whether distant or near.
O Son of Strength, bestow wealth upon mortals; grant wide protection to Vītahavya, and wide protection to Bharadvāja.
I strive toward your radiant guest, Agni, the son of heaven, the invoker for men, the performer of the fair sacrifice—
toward him who, like a sage with celestial speech, is the bearer of oblations and the divine steward, with my well-fashioned hymns.
With his purifying and conspicuous form, he has shone upon the earth like the radiance of the dawn;
like one who hastens on his path, he rejoices in the delight of Etaśa, he who, ageless, has rushed forth like one parched by heat.
Worship Agni after Agni with your fuel; celebrate your beloved guest, the most dear one.
Invite the Immortal with your songs; for as a god among the gods, he wins what is desirable; for as a god among the gods, he accepts our service.
I praise with kindled wood and song Agni who is enkindled—the pure, purifying, and steadfast one at the front of the sacrifice.
We implore with prayers for favor Jātavedas, the inspired priest, the invoker, the bountiful, the guileless sage.
Thee, O Agni, the immortal messenger, the bearer of oblations, the protector worthy of praise, they have established from age to age;
both gods and mortals have seated thee with homage—the watchful, all-pervading lord of the people.
Adorning both worlds according to the sacred laws, O Agni, you traverse the two realms as the messenger of the gods.
Since we choose your devotion and your favor, be therefore auspicious to us, providing a triple protection.
Him, the fair-faced, beautiful to behold, swift-moving, the one more wise than the ignorant—may we serve.
May he, Agni, knowing all ways, perform the sacrifice; may he announce our oblation among the immortals.

O Agni, you protect and you deliver that man who has brought a prayer to you, the Seer, O Hero—whether it be for the sharpening or the furtherance of the sacrifice; him indeed you satisfy with power and with wealth.
O Agni, protect us from the one who seeks to harm us; O powerful one, guard us from reproach.
May your smoke-enveloped path reach us, and may desirable, thousandfold wealth come to us.
Agni is the Hotṛ, the lord of the house, the king; he, Jātavedas, knows all births.
He who is the best sacrificer among both gods and mortals—may he, the observer of cosmic order, perform the sacrifice.
O Agni, O Hotṛ of the sacrifice, O purifier with your bright flame, come today to the people, for you are the sacrificer.
Sacrifice according to the Truth as you manifest yourself in your greatness; O most youthful one, carry forth today those oblations which are yours.
Behold the well-prepared offerings; may one establish you between the two worlds (Heaven and Earth) so that you may sacrifice.
O Maghavan Agni, help us in the winning of booty; may we cross over all difficulties, may we cross them, may we cross them by your protection.

O Agni of the beautiful countenance, together with all the gods, sit as the first upon this wool-lined womb. Lead the sacrifice, nest-like and rich in ghee, straight to Savitṛ for the sake of the sacrificer.
The wise ones churn this very Agni, as Atharvan did,
whom they brought forth unerring from the dark-hued [plants], moving with eager haste.
Be born for the feast of the gods, for complete success and for well-being;
bring hither the immortal gods who increase the Truth, and cause the sacrifice to reach the gods.
O Agni, Lord of the House of men, we have made thee great with fuel;
may our household duties not be deficient, and sharpen us with thy keen splendor.
O Agni, you have been appointed as the Hotṛ-priest of all sacrifices among the human race, together with the gods.
With your delightful tongues, do you, O Great One, sacrifice for us at the rite; bring the gods hither and worship them.
For you, O wise one, know straightway the ways and paths to the gods at the sacrifices, O Agni of good intent.
I praise you, as Bharata did with his swift steeds for prosperity; I have sacrificed at the sacrifices to you, the one worthy of sacrifice.
You [bestowed] these many desirable things upon Divodāsa, who presses the soma,
and upon Bharadvāja, the donor.
As an immortal messenger, bring hither the divine folk,
listening to the excellent praise of the inspired singer.
O Agni, mortals with devoted minds invoke you, the god, at the sacrifices for the banquet of the gods.
I worship your appearance and your will, O bounteous one;
may all who desire it find pleasure in them.
You are the Hotṛ-priest appointed by Manu, the bearer [of oblations], more wise in speech;
O Agni, sacrifice to the clans of heaven.
O Agni, come for the feast, being praised for the giving of the oblation;
sit down as the Hotṛ-priest upon the sacred grass.
O Aṅgiras, we strengthen you with fuel-sticks and with clarified butter; blaze forth loftily, O youngest one!
O God Agni, you win for us that vast and glorious fame, and great heroic power.
O Agni, Atharvan churned you forth from the lotus,
from the head of the entire universe, for the sake of the sacrificer.
The seer Dadhyañc, the son of Atharvan, kindled you—
that slayer of Vṛtra, the shatterer of forts.
The bull Pāthya has kindled you, the greatest slayer of Dasyus,
the winner of wealth in every battle.
Come here, O Agni; I shall indeed speak these other songs to you.
May you grow strong through these drops.
Wherever you set your mind upon a higher skill,
there you shall make your seat.
For your bounty, O Vasu, has never failed those who seek it; thus you shall accept our worship.
Agni, the descendant of Bharata, the slayer of Vṛtra, the one of many insights, has come; he is the true lord of Divodāsa.
For he indeed bestows wealth upon all earthly beings by his greatness; winning it, he is unassailed and invincible.
O Agni, as in the past, with new and enduring splendor,
you have spread far and wide with your lofty light.
O friends, boldly offer a hymn and a sacrifice to your Agni; sing and chant for the Ordainer.
For he, the Hotṛ of sage-like insight, has sat down through the ages of men as the messenger and the bearer of oblations.
O Vasu, worship here those two kings, the Ādityas of pure vows, the host of Maruts, and the two worlds, Rodasī.
O Agni, son of strength, your appearance is auspicious for the mortal who seeks nourishment, for you are the offspring of immortality.
Through his wisdom, let him be the most excellent today; seeking you with beautiful gifts, the mortal has offered this well-fashioned hymn.
O Agni, those who are protected by you, seeking nourishment for their entire life-span, overcome the hostilities of the enemy; they conquer the hostilities of the enemy.
May Agni with his sharp flame strike down every devouring demon;
may Agni win wealth for us.
O Jātavedas, you who move among all people, bring us wealth accompanied by brave sons; O you of noble power, destroy the demons.
O Jātavedas, protect us from distress and from the one who intends us harm; guard us, O Sage, with your sacred power.
O Agni, whatever mortal of evil intent offers us up to slaughter,
protect us from that distress.
O God, with your tongue drive away that evildoer— the mortal who seeks to strike us down.
O victorious Agni, grant wide-spreading protection to Bharadvāja; bestow upon him excellent wealth.
May Agni, seeking wealth, strike down the Vṛtras with his inspired praise— Agni, kindled, bright, and invoked with oblations.
In the womb of his mother, the father of his father, flashing in the imperishable,
he sits within the seat of the Eternal Order (Ṛta).
O Jātavedas, you who are far-seeing, bring us a prayer that wins progeny,
O Agni, which may shine in heaven.
O Agni, son of strength, we who offer sacrificial food have poured forth our songs toward you, whose appearance is delightful.
We have come to your shelter, O Agni, who are like the shade from the heat of the sun, you who appear like gold.
O Agni, like a fierce archer-slayer, like a sharp-horned bull, you have shattered the fortresses.
Him whom they carry in their hands like a ringed weapon, or like a newborn infant— Agni, the priest of the people who performs the sacrifice well.
Bring forth the god, the best finder of wealth, for the feast of the gods;
let him sit down in his own place of birth.
Sharpen this beloved guest who has been born in Jātavedas; settle him, the master of the house, in his pleasant dwelling.
O Agni, yoke those horses of yours which are well-trained, O God; they carry you readily according to your will.
Come toward us, bring [the gods] hither to enjoy the offerings;
bring the gods for the drinking of Soma.
O Agni of the Bharatas, rise up with brilliant, unceasing radiance; blaze forth and shine out, O ageless one!
The mortal who, desiring the feast, shall honor the god Agni at the sacrifice with oblations,
and who, with outstretched hands, shall seek to win him— the priest who truly sacrifices— through adoration of both Heaven and Earth.
O Agni, we bring to you with a hymn an oblation fashioned by the heart;
may these become for you bulls, oxen, and even cows.
The gods kindle Agni as the foremost, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra,
by whom wealth has been brought hither and the demonic powers shattered, O powerful one.
Drink the Soma, O fierce Indra, which you have praised as you burst open the great cow-stall;
you, O bold one, wielder of the thunderbolt, who with your powers have slain Vṛtra and all hostile forces.
Drink this, O Indra— you who are the consumer of the dregs, the overcomer, the one with beautiful lips, the bull among hymns, the breaker of the cow-pens,
the wielder of the thunderbolt, and the one who stands upon the two bay horses— pierce through to wondrous spoils of war!
Drink thus; as of old, let it exhilarate you. Hear our prayer and grow strong through our songs.
Make the sun manifest; swell with nourishment; slay the enemies; O Indra, pierce open the cattle-pens.

O Indra, self-sustaining one, these exhilarating draughts, once drunk, have made you, the radiant and great, swell with strength; these intoxicants have gladdened you—the perfect, powerful, and pervasive lord who overcomes all.
Exhilarated by those [Soma drops], O Indra, you caused the sun and the dawn to shine forth, shattering even the firm fortresses;
you thrust out the great mountain that held the cattle, the immovable one, from its own place.
By your wisdom and by your wondrous deeds, you have placed the cooked within the raw through your power;
you threw open the doors for the ruddy cows, and, accompanied by the Aṅgirases, you released the cattle from the firm enclosure.
You have filled the wide earth, O wondrous one; lofty Indra, you have propped up the vast sky.
You have supported the two worlds, whose sons are the gods—the ancient, youthful Mothers of the Eternal Order (Ṛta).
Then all the gods, O Indra, placed you alone, the powerful one, at the front for the battle;
when the godless one challenged the gods, they chose Indra there in the struggle for the light of heaven.
Then even heaven itself, out of fear of its own wrath, trembled twice before your thunderbolt;
when Indra, possessing all life, struck down the serpent who was mocking him as he lay upon his bed.

Then, O fierce one, Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for you that great thunderbolt with a thousand spikes and a hundred edges— a weapon according to your desire and will, with which, O drinker of the soma-residue, you crushed the roaring dragon.
May all the Maruts, acting in harmony, increase him for whom you, O Indra, cooked a hundred buffaloes.
Pūṣan and Viṣṇu poured out three lakes of the exhilarating, Vṛtra-slaying Soma-stalk for him.
You released the great, encompassed flood of rivers, the gathered wave of the waters.
Along their downward course, O Indra, you urged them on the path; you sent the active waters down toward the ocean.

Thus may this new prayer turn toward you for protection, Indra, who has performed all these deeds— the great, fierce, undecaying giver of victory, possessed of noble heroes, well-armed, and wielder of the excellent thunderbolt.
O Indra, bestow upon us inspired singers for the sake of booty, renown, nourishment, and glorious wealth.
O Indra, grant us heroic patrons among the Bharadvājas; and, O Indra, be mindful of us on the decisive day of battle.
Through this [hymn], may we win god-appointed booty; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with brave sons.
Praise him indeed, Indra, who is of surpassing might, the unassailable victor, invoked by many; strengthen with these songs the fierce bull of the people, the unconquered subduer.

He is the warrior, the hero, the stirrer of battle, the one who shares the spoil, the great destroyer, roaring like a bull, the drinker of the dregs; raising a vast cloud of dust, the shaker of human tribes, he alone has become the conqueror of all peoples.
You indeed, O Indra, alone didst devour those Dasyus and protect the Aryan peoples.
Is this heroic power yours, O Indra, or is it not? Declare this truly at the proper time.
Truly, I acknowledge that power of yours, O most mighty one born with strength; it belongs to you, the swiftest of the swift.
That fierce power of the fierce, the stronger than the strong, the overcomer of the weak, has become manifest.
May that ancient friendship of ours be with you, O wonder-worker, together with the Aṅgirases who spoke thus:
you, the shaker of the unshakable, slew Vala as he was fleeing, and you shattered all his fortresses and gates.
For he, the fierce one, is to be invoked with prayers; acting as a lord, he prevails in the great battle against Vṛtra.
He, the wielder of the thunderbolt, has become one who is to be sought for the winning of offspring and progeny, and who is to be implored in battles.

By his might, he has extended beyond the generations of men with his immortal name. He is united with splendor, with power, with wealth, and with heroic strength—he who is most manly among those dwelling together.
He who does not falter, nor becomes a deceitful man— he of auspicious name, Indra— has shattered Cumuri and Dhuni,
Pipru, Śambara, and Śuṣṇa, for the destruction of their forts and for their eternal destruction.
O Indra, mount your chariot for the slaying of Vṛtra with your exalted and most praiseworthy power;
take the thunderbolt in your right hand and, O giver of many gifts, strike down the magical illusions.

Like Agni consuming a dry forest, O Indra, let your weapon burn down the *rakṣas* like a terrifying thunderbolt— he who with his deep and lofty [strength] broke down the barriers, drove away misfortunes, and struck them down.
O Indra of many glories, come hither by a thousand paths with wealth and abundant strength;
O Son of Strength, O Much-invoked One, come now, for no godless one has power to hinder you.
The greatness of the ancient, impetuous, and many-glittering one has overflowed beyond heaven and earth.
He has no enemy, no counterpart, and no firm foundation; he is the conqueror of the one possessed of manifold magic powers.
May that deed of yours performed today be manifest: that you [struck down] Kutsa, Āyu, and Atithigva for him.
You sharpened many thousands upon the earth; with boldness, you carried Tūrvayāṇa across.
Then, O God, all the gods rejoiced after you, the wisest among the wise,
when you, being praised, created wide space for the oppressed heaven, for the people, and for yourself.
Heaven and earth have yielded to this might of yours; O immortal Indra, the gods have submitted.
O Accomplisher, perform that which remains unaccomplished for you; through sacrifices, bring forth a new hymn of praise.
Great is Indra, manly, filling the peoples; moreover, doubly vast and undiminished in his powers, he has grown toward us for heroic deeds. Broad and wide, he was made well-fashioned by the makers.
The prayer has established Indra alone for the sake of winning— the great, lofty, undecaying, and youthful one—
who has increased by invincible power, he who has grown instantly and completely.
Widen your two arms and extend your hands; bestow upon us glorious renown.
Like a domestic herdsman tending his cattle to the herd, O Indra, turn toward us in the battle.
We who desire strength now invoke that Indra for you here, with his powers, so that he may protect us—
just as the singers of old were blameless, irreproachable, and unharmed.
Firm in his vows, giver of wealth, increased by Soma, he indeed possesses much desirable property;
paths of riches meet in him as rivers flow together into the ocean.
O most powerful hero, bring us the mightiest strength, the most potent force that overcomes all;
bring to us, O Lord of the Bay Steeds, all the splendors and manly powers of men, so that we may rejoice.

O Indra, that exhilarating draught of yours which is unconquered and victorious in battle— bring that to us in its full abundance, by which, aided by you, we may rejoice as conquerors in the winning of offspring and progeny.
O Indra, bring us bull-like vigor that wins wealth— vigor that is ever-increasing,
most skillful, and by which, through your protections, we may overcome our enemies in battles, whether they be kin or strangers.
O Bull, let your impetuous strength come to us from behind, from above, from below, and from the front;
let it come hither from every side. O Indra, bestow upon us the splendor of heaven.

O Indra, most manly one, may we win desirable wealth through your manly aids and through our glorious deeds, for you, O King, behold the wealth of both worlds; bestow upon us a great, firm, and vast treasure.

We invoke here for new protection that Indra, the bull accompanied by the Maruts, who has grown great, the one whose power is never failing, the divine ruler, the all-conquering, the fierce giver of victory.
O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, subject even the people who consider themselves great to these men for whom I am here;
for we invoke you upon the earth in the struggle for heroes, for progeny, for cattle, and for waters.
O much-invoked one, through these friendships of yours may we prevail over every enemy.
O hero, slaying both kinds of obstacles, may we, protected by you, rejoice in abundant wealth.
Like the sky, O Indra, that wealth which stands over men in battles through its power—
O Son of Strength, grant us that which brings thousands, wins the fields, and overcomes the Vritras.
Like that of heaven, all sovereign power was established for you by the gods, O Indra;
when, O impetuous one, acting in concert with Viṣṇu, you slew Vṛtra the serpent who had obstructed the waters.
Overpowering with greater vigor, more powerful than the powerful, Indra— whose greatness has increased through the performed *brahman*—
became the king of the honeyed Soma, since he protected the shatterer of all the fortresses.
By the hundreds, the Paṇis fled there from Indra for the sake of the ten-fingered sage at the winning of the light;
by his weapons, he overthrew the illusions of the insatiable Śuṣṇa, and nothing remained of him that was not surpassed.
The entire life-span of the great deceiver was laid low when Śuṣṇa fell at the stroke of the thunderbolt.
Indra made wide room for his charioteer Kutsa on the same chariot, in the winning of the sun.
Like a hawk, he shook off the head of the Dāsa Namuci while [extracting] for him the exhilarating stalk;
he protected Namī Sāpya as he slept, and filled him with wealth, with food, and with well-being.
O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, you shattered with your might the firm fortresses of Pipru, who possessed the craft of a serpent.
O Bounteous Giver, you bestowed that imperishable wealth as a gift upon the worshipper R̥jiśvan.
Indra, whose favor is most helpful, [overthrew] Vetasu, who had ten fingers and ten arms, the impetuous one;
he released Tugra and Ibha again and again for the sake of light, so that they might come hither like children to their mother.
He, unopposed, overcomes his rivals, bearing in his hand the Vṛtra-slaying thunderbolt;
standing upon his two bay steeds like a gambler on the gaming board, they carry the lofty Indra, yoked by a word.

May we win through your newest protection, O Indra; thus the Pūrus have praised you with sacrifices. When you shattered the seven autumnal fortresses—the Dāsa strongholds that were their refuge—you bestowed them as a gift upon Purukutsa.
O Indra, you were the ancient one who increased [the world], bestowing wealth upon Uśanas Kāvya;
you gave away Navavāstva, the son whom he had not given up, as his own grandson to his great father.
O Indra, you, the shaker, set in motion the shaking waters, flowing like rivers;
when you, O hero, carried across the ocean, bring Turvaśa and Yadu safely to the further shore.
All this was yours in the battle, O Indra; you laid Dhuni and Cumuri to sleep.
Dabhīti, kindling the sacrificial wood and cooking the oblation with hymns, shone brightly for you as he pressed the Soma.

O Hero, these invocations of the most frequent singer call upon you, the one worthy of being invoked; toward you, the ageless one who stands upon the chariot, the newest prayers are offered, and through eloquence, abundant wealth is sought.
I praise that Indra who is known, who is carried by songs, who is strengthened by hymns at the sacrifice—
he whose greatness, possessing manifold powers, surpasses heaven and earth in its vastness.
He, indeed, made the pathless darkness possessed of paths by means of the sun.
O self-powerful one, when do mortals, desiring to worship, not violate the ordinance of you, the immortal?
Where indeed is that Indra who performed those deeds? Among what people does he wander, and among which tribes?
What sacrifice is pleasing to your mind and your desire? What is the hymn, O Indra, and who is that Hotar-priest?

For now, O many-invoked one, your ancient friends of old were active for you; they were the doers of much. Be mindful of those who are in the middle, as well as the most recent, and even of the youngest.

Inquiring about him, the later ones have followed after those ancient deeds of yours, O Indra, through your renown. We sing praises to you, O hero who are borne by our prayers, as great as we know you to be.
The host of the Rakṣas has risen up against you; against that great one who has been born, stand forth well!
With your ancient, allied friend, the thunderbolt, O bold one, drive those away.
O Indra, hero who supports the singer, listen now to this new prayer of the one who reveres you;
for from of old you have been the kinsman of our fathers, ever ready to be invoked in our quest.
Bring Varuṇa, Mitra, Indra, and the Maruts to our aid for protection today;
bring Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, Agni, Purandhi, Savitṛ, the plants, and the mountains.
O you of many powers, O worthy of sacrifice, these singers here honor you with hymns.
Hear the call of those who invoke you; being invoked, there is none other like you among the immortals.
Now come to my speech, O wise one, with all the worshipful sons of strength,
who were fire-tongued guardians of the *ṛta*, who made Manu subordinate to the Dāsa.
Be our leader on easy paths and on difficult ones, you who are the knower and the maker of the way.
With those horses of yours that are unwearied, broad, and most swift to carry, O Indra, bring us to booty.
Him alone who is the one to be invoked by the peoples—that Indra I celebrate with these songs;
he who rules as a bull, possessed of virile strength, the true hero, of many wondrous powers, and victorious.

Him indeed our ancient fathers, the Navagvas, the seven sages, impelled with longing— him who reaches the giver, the overcomer standing upon the mountains, whose speech is guileless, the most powerful one— with their hymns of praise.
We beg that Indra for this wealth—abounding in heroes, rich in men, and full of food—which is unfailing, undecaying, and heavenly; O possessor of bay horses, bring that hither so that we may rejoice.
Tell us this, O Indra: have your singers of old indeed attained your favor?
What is your portion, what your food, O fierce one, you who strike down the oppressors, you who are invoked by many and possess much wealth, O slayer of the Asuras?

Seeking him, the thunderbolt-handed Indra who stands upon his chariot— to whom now belongs the trembling, eloquent song— he, the mighty-grasper, the doer of great deeds, the giver of bounty, approaches the powerful one for the sake of the path and for nourishment.

O self-strong one, with this very magic power and with the mountain swift as thought, you shattered even the unshakable, the firm, and the solid fortresses with boldness, O exuberant one of innate vigor.
Him, the most powerful one, the ancient one, we would honor with a new prayer, just as the ancients did.
May that Indra, the measureless and excellent driver, carry us across all difficult passages.
For the person who acts with malice, you have set ablaze the earthly, celestial, and intermediate spaces.
O Bull, burn them from every side with your flame; for the hater of sacred prayer, consume both the earth and the waters.
You are the king of the heavenly folk and of the earthly world, O you of brilliant aspect.
Grasp the thunderbolt in your right hand, O Indra; ageless one, you destroy all magical illusions.
O Indra, grant us well-restrained prosperity, vast and unfailing, for the overcoming of enemies—
that prosperity by which you, O wielder of the thunderbolt, make the Dāsa and Ārya Vṛtras, and the Nahuṣa foes, easy to overcome.
O much-invoked one, O wise ordainer, come to us with your teams of horses that bring all boons, O you who are worthy of sacrifice!
Those which neither the godless nor the god can restrain—with those, come quickly toward me!
O Indra, you are indeed closely united with the pressed soma, with the hymn, the prayer, and the recited chant;
or whenever, O Maghavan, you go forth bearing the thunderbolt in your arms, drawn by your two yoked bay horses.
Or when, O Indra, you aided the presser of the Soma in the decisive battle against Vṛtra for the winning of heroes;
or when, being yourself fearless, you subdued the defiant Dasyus while the skillful one was afraid—O Indra!
May the fierce Indra be the drinker of the pressed Soma; may he, the leader with his aids, protect the singer.
He creates a wide space for the hero who presses the juice, and he bestows wealth even upon the praising pauper.
He comes to the libations with his two bay steeds; he bears the thunderbolt, drinks the Soma, and gives gifts of cattle.
He is the maker of the heroic man, possessed of all heroes; he hears the call of the singer, borne by the hymns of praise.

Whatever he has desired, that we have offered to him—to Indra, who from of old has performed deeds for us. When the Soma is pressed, we praise him with recitations and hymns, so that our prayer may be a source of strengthening for Indra.

For you have made the sacred hymns your means of increase; therefore, O Indra, we serve you with our prayers. When the Soma is pressed, O drinker of the pressed juice, let us perform with sacrifices the most peaceful and delightful acts of devotion for your nourishment.
Take notice of us, O Indra, accepting this sacrificial cake; drink the Soma mixed with milk.
Sit upon this sacred grass of the sacrificer; grant wide space for those who are devoted to you.
Rejoice, O fierce one, according to your pleasure; let these sacrifices reach you. Let these our invocations reach you, who are invoked by many; toward us, O Indra, let this prayer go for your aid.

O friends, as you gather together at the pressed juices, fill up Indra, the liberal giver, with Soma draughts. Will he not surely assist us in our quest for booty? Indra will not neglect the presser of Soma when it comes to granting his aid.
Thus has Indra been praised while the Soma was pressed among the Bharadvājas; may he dwell among the wealthy patrons.
May Indra be the patron of the singer and the giver of wealth that contains all desirable things.

The bull-like exhilaration, the hymn, and the recitations are with Indra; he is the drinker of the pressed Soma, the consumer of the dregs, the one to be praised by men with hymns, the bounteous lord, the celestial king of songs whose protection is inexhaustible.
The victorious hero, manly and discerning, who hears the call of the singer and provides wide protection;
the Vasu, the praise of men, the sustainer of the poets, the prize-winner—when lauded in the assembly, he bestows strength.
O Hero, like the axle of two wheels, thy greatness has surpassed both heaven and earth.
O Indra, invoked by many, as the branches of a tree, thy manifold aids have grown forth.
O Lord of Śacī, you of many powers, your mighty deeds are like the paths for driving cattle;
they are like the tethering ropes for calves—O Indra, O Bountiful One, they are bound yet remain unbound.
One deed today, and another tomorrow; Indra makes the unreal appear as real in an instant.
In this matter, Mitra, Varuṇa, and Pūṣan are our friends; there is none who can surpass the will of the Noble One.
Like waters from the back of a mountain, O Indra, they have brought you hither with hymns and sacrifices;
seeking strength with these fair praises, those who love songs have come to you like horses to a race.
Neither autumns nor months, nor days, wear Indra down; they do not diminish him.
Though he is already grown, let his body increase further when it is extolled with hymns and recited with songs of praise.
He does not bow before the stubborn, nor before the firm, nor before the arrogant one incited by the Dasyus when he is praised.
Even the lofty mountains are like plains to Indra; even in the deep, there is a ford for him.
O Atri-foe-slayer, drinker of the pressed juice, bestow upon us with your deep and wide [chariot] swift impulses and strengths;
stand upright for our aid, remaining unharmed at the dawning of night when the time for departure has come.
Accompany this man for his protection in the encounter; O Indra, protect him from harm here.
Guard him at home and in the forest from injury. May we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.

O impetuous Indra, whatever aid you have—whether it be the lowest, the highest, or that which is in the middle—with those aids protect us well in the slaying of Vṛtra; and with these strengths, O fierce one, become great for us.
O Indra, without harming them, distress the hostile spirit of the enemy by means of these [powers], so that he may contend with his rivals.
With these, you have subdued all attacking Dāsa tribes in every direction for the sake of the Ārya.
O Indra, those who have joined as attackers—whether they be kinsmen or strangers—turning toward us;
strike down their wavering strength, destroy their manly powers, and drive them away.
Either the hero overcomes the hero with his physical forms when they both exert their power with radiant bodies;
or they both cry out in rivalry for offspring, cattle, progeny, waters, or fertile fields.
Neither the hero, nor the swift, nor the bold, nor one who considers himself a warrior has ever fought against you.
O Indra, no one among these is your equal; you surpass all these created beings.
He rules over the manly power of both races when the wise ones call upon him in the assembly;
whether for the great Vṛtra-slaying or for a dwelling rich in heroes, when they extend themselves as wide as space.
And now, O Indra, when the peoples stir themselves, be their protector and their defender;
for our own patrons, O Indra, the most heroic among men, have placed us at their head.
To thee was granted for thy great Indra-power all that was required in the slaying of Vṛtra;
to thee, O worshipful Indra, were granted dominion and might by the gods in the contest for men.
Thus, O Indra, bring our rivals together in battles; take delight in the hostile, godless hordes.
Singing your praises, may we, the Bharadvājas, find the light of day through your protection, O Indra, even now.

Hear us, O Indra; we call upon you, raining down [blessings], for the winning of great booty. When the tribes gather together in the struggle for heroes, grant us fierce protection on the decisive day.
The prize-winning steed, the son of a prize-winner, invokes you for the winning of great booty to be seized.
O Indra, the fist-fighter beholds you as the lord of the virtuous and the deliverer in battles against the Vṛtras, as he fights for cattle.

You impelled the seer in the struggle for the sun; you struck down Śuṣṇa for the sake of the worshipper Kutsa. You struck off the head of the invulnerable one, performing a deed worthy of praise for Atithigva.
You brought forward the lofty chariot for the warrior; you aided the fighting bull Daśadyu.
You slew Tugra together with Vetasu; O Indra, you strengthened Tuji as he sang your praises.
O Indra, you made that hymn of praise mighty; O Hero, you shattered hundreds and thousands. You struck down the Dāsa Śambara from the mountain and protected Divodāsa with your wondrous aids.
O Indra, exhilarated by the acts of faith and the Soma juices, you sent Cumuri to sleep for Dabhīti.
Bestowing favor upon Piṭhīnas, you struck down sixty thousand Rājīs with your power.
May I too, along with the patrons, attain that superior favor and power of yours, O Indra— when, O most mighty one,
heroes are praised by you, the protector of the good, through your threefold protection and your Nahusha-strength.
O Indra, in this invocation for glory, may we be your dearest friends through your greatness.
May Prātardani, the glory of dominion, be the most excellent in the slaying of Vṛtras and in the winning of riches.
What has Indra done in the exhilaration of this [Soma], or what in its drinking, or what in its friendship?
What delights have they found in its presence in the past, and what indeed do the present ones find?
In his exhilaration, Indra has established what is real; in his drinking of it, he has established what is real; in his friendship with it, he has established what is real.
Whether in the joy of its presence or in its settled state, those things that are real have been found by him in the past, and so too are they found now.
For we do not know the full extent of your greatness, O Maghavan, nor your wealthiness;
nor have we seen the power of your most recent bounty, O Indra—no one has beheld your *indriya*.
This very power of yours has become manifest, by which you struck down the offspring of Varaśikha;
for even from the roar of your thunderbolt when it was hurled, O Indra, the highest [heaven] burst asunder from its force.
Indra struck down the offspring of Varaśikha for Abhyāvartin Cāyamāna, seeking to help him;
when he slew Vṛcīvanta at Hariyūpīyā, the one on the further side fled in fear at the sight of the former.
O Indra, much-invoked, three thousand armored men together, seeking glory at the Yavyāvatī, fell by your arrow;
the Vṛcīvants, falling like birds, went to their destruction, shattering their vessels.
He whose two ruddy bulls, seeking good pasture, move about between [the worlds] licking their lips—
he, bestowing Turvaśa upon Sṛñjaya, gave Vṛcīvat to Daivavāta, providing for him.
O Agni, the liberal sovereign Samrāj Abhyāvartin has given me twenty chariot-horses with their mates;
this is the difficult-to-obtain sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) of the Pārthavas.
The cows have come; they have brought auspiciousness. Let them sit in the cow-pen and take delight among us.
May they be here, prolific and many-formed, yielding their milk for Indra through many dawns.
Indra bestows gifts upon the sacrificer who gives; he grants more and does not take away what is his own.
Increasing his wealth ever further, he establishes the god-fearing man upon unbroken, solid ground.
They are not lost, nor does a thief deceive them; no hostile assault of an enemy dares to overcome them.
With those [cows] by which one sacrifices to the gods and gives gifts, the master of the herd dwells together with them for a long time.
The dust-raising horse does not overtake them; they do not go toward the prepared slaughter-place.
Far-striding and fearless, those cows of the mortal sacrificer roam along after him.
The cows are Bhaga; the cows have appeared to me as Indra; the cows are the first draught of Soma.
O people, these which are the cows are Indra; with my heart and my mind, I desire Indra.
O cows, you make even the emaciated fat; you make even the unlovely beautiful of countenance.
You make the home auspicious, O you of auspicious speech; your great vitality is proclaimed in the assemblies.
May you be rich in offspring, grazing upon good pasture, drinking pure waters at a fine watering-place.
May no thief nor any evil-planner have power over you; may the missile of Rudra avoid you.
Let this mixing be added; let it be mixed into these cows, into the seed of the bull, and into your own virility, O Indra.
The men have sought Indra for friendship, seeking to attain his great favor and desiring his goodwill;
for he, the wielder of the thunderbolt, is a great giver. Worship him, the great and joyful one, for protection.
In whose hand men have placed their power, who stands upon his golden chariot;
in whose two firm hands the reins are held, and who has yoked the stallions as steeds upon the path.
For the sake of glory, your feet have been anointed with homage; bold wielder of the thunderbolt, you are rich in power and gifts on the right.
Clothed in a fragrant garment, fair to behold, you have become as vigorous as the sun, O dancer.
That Soma has become most thoroughly mixed when it is pressed—wherein the cooked offering is prepared and roasted grains are present;
while men praise Indra, performing sacred formulations and reciting hymns, they are most beloved by the gods.
No limit has been set to the extent of this thy power; indeed, by thy greatness, thou hast forced asunder the two worlds, heaven and earth.
The patron, hastening with his aid, satisfies those [desires] like one gathering herds in the waters.
Thus indeed is Indra, the lofty one, easy to invoke; whether with praise or without praise, he is the hero with golden jaws.
For even as soon as he was born, he possessed incomparable strength; he slays many Vṛtras and strikes down the Dasyus.
He has grown even greater for heroic power; alone and ageless, he distributes treasures.
Indra has surpassed heaven and earth; indeed, both worlds are but half of him.
Therefore, I consider his divine power to be vast; no one can diminish those things which he has established.
Day after day, the Sun has become visible; the wise one has widely laid out the dwellings.
Even now, indeed, that work of the rivers remains as when you, O Indra, carved out a path for them;
the mountains settled down like those sitting at a feast, and by you, O wise one, the realms were made firm.
This is indeed true: O Indra, there is no other superior to you, neither god nor mortal.
You slew the serpent as he lay encompassing the flood; you released the waters toward the ocean.
O Indra, you split apart the waters and the gates in all directions; you shattered the firmness of the mountain.
You became the king of the world and of the peoples, bringing forth at once the sun, the sky, and the dawn.
You alone have become the lord of riches among all treasures; O Indra, you have placed the peoples within your hands.
Among their offspring, their waters, their progeny, and their sunlight, the people have raised their voices in various songs.
Out of fear of you, O Indra, all the earthly realms—even those that are immovable—are shaken from their foundations;
heaven and earth, the mountains, and the forests—everything solid fears at your onset.
O Indra, with Kutsa you fought against the insatiable Śuṣṇa and Kuyava in the quest for cattle;
then, at the onset of the day, you stole the wheel of the sun and cast away his misdeeds.

You struck down the hundreds of the Dasyu Śambara’s impregnable fortresses, O Lord of Power, when you, by your might, bestowed riches upon Divodāsa, who pressed the Soma and prepared the libation, and upon the praising Bharadvāja.
O you of true strength, O one of many manly deeds, mount your terrible chariot for the great battle!
Come hither on your long path with your aid toward me; O famous one, make yourself heard among all people.
I have fashioned with my mouth most excellent and unprecedented words for this great hero, the powerful and swift one— for the exuberant wielder of the thunderbolt, for the steadfast one.
He, being praised by the wise, caused his two parents to dwell with the Sun; shattering the rock while chanting with the well-intentioned singers, he released the confinement of the ruddy cows.

With his carriers, the singers who kneel in devotion, he—the doer of many deeds—has repeatedly won the cattle; as a friend among friends and a seer among seers, he, the destroyer of forts, shattered the strongholds with his companions.
O Bull of the peoples, lover of songs, come forth toward the singer with girded robes, with great prizes, and with mighty strengths— possessing many heroes— for our well-being.
Urged on by his own impetuous strength, Indra, the subduer of the swift, drove the waters to the right.
Thus released, they flowed day after day toward their goal, irresistible and never turning back.
O Indra, O bull, grant us that most powerful exhilaration which is victorious and bountiful—
that exhilaration which wins the possession of fine horses, which overcomes Vritras in battles, and subdues enemies.
For the people with contending voices call upon you, O Indra, for aid in the battle for heroes.
You have scattered the Paṇis along with the inspired poets; protected by you, the steed wins the prize.
O Heroic Indra, you slay both kinds of enemies—the Dāsa and the Ārya foes—like trees with well-honed weapons; O most manly of men, you rend them apart in the battles.
As such, O Indra, be our friend with your unerring aids, a protector for all our life, and a helper for our prosperity.
When we call upon you in the winning of light, O Hero, as we fight in battles over the distribution of spoils.
Surely, O Indra, may you be with us for the future; be gracious to us and stand by us in our need.
Thus praising you, may we abide in the protection of the Mighty One, most rich in cattle, on the decisive day.
Many songs have come together unto thee, O Indra, and from thee proceed manifold thoughts;
both ancient and recent praises of the seers, as well as hymns and chants, have vied for Indra’s favor.
He who is invoked by many, praised by many, the skillful one, uniquely glorified through sacrifices— Indra,
harnessed for great power like a chariot, has become one to be celebrated by us with hymns.
Him whom neither prayers nor songs harm, Indra they reach and cause to grow;
when his praisers, whether a hundred or a thousand, sing to him who loves the song, that is well for him.
For him, as for the sky with the moon, the months have poured forth; Soma has been offered into Indra.
As waters flow together toward people in the desert, so have the invocations through sacrifices increased him all at once.
To him has this great hymn been spoken, to this Indra a song of praise with inspired thoughts,
so that in the great battle against Vṛtra, Indra may be the protector of all life and our increaser.
When will our prayers find their rest in your chariot? When will you grant the singer a thousandfold prosperity?
When will you clothe this hymn with wealth? And when will you make our thoughts rich in the prize of booty?
When indeed will that happen, O Indra, when you shall settle men with men, heroes with heroes, and cause the non-conquerors to flee?
May you win the threefold cattle among the herds; O Indra, bestow upon us glory like the light of heaven.

When indeed, O Indra, most powerful one, will you make that all-sustaining sacred word (*brahman*) effective for the singer? When will you yoke your teams as if they were our prayers? When will you come to the invocations accompanied by gifts of cattle?

Bestow upon the singer gifts of cattle, horses resplendent with wealth, and nourishing food; O Indra, swell the well-milking cow with milk, and let her shine forth with great luster among the Bharadvājas.
Lead us now to that very stronghold, O Hero, O Śakra, since you are praised as one who opens the doors.
Do not let the milk-cow of the bright draught go empty; O Sage, quicken the Aṅgirases with your sacred prayer.

Truly, thy exhilarations are for all people; truly, so too are the riches that belong to the earth. Truly, thou hast been the distributor of spoils, since thou didst maintain thy divine power among the gods.
I have offered praise after his people; they have truly bestowed their strength upon him for heroic valor.
Even in the slaying of Vṛtra, they direct their will toward the snare-grasper, the fierce one, and the steed.
United aids, manly powers, and heroic strengths accompany Indra;
like rivers rushing to the ocean, our songs—swelling with hymns—enter him who is wide-expansive.
Being praised, O Indra, release for us a spring of wealth, of that treasure which is most resplendent;
you have become the peerless lord of men, the sole king of the entire world.
Hear that which is to be heard, O you who are worthy of worship; like the sky [overshadows] the earth, so may you [overspread us] with the riches of the noble one.
May you be pleased with us through your power, manifesting yourself with vital strength age after age.
Hither let your harnessed bay steeds bring your chariot, O fierce Indra, which possesses all desirable things;
for even the poor man invokes you, O possessor of heaven; may we, as your companions at the feast, prosper today.
To the wooden vat the tawny drops have gone; being purified, they have become straight-flowing.
May Indra, our ancient one, drink of this; may the heavenly King drink of the exhilarating Soma juice.
Racing toward the powerful Indra on well-wheeled chariots, like horses, may they bear him toward glory, striving straight; never indeed shall the immortality of Vāyu fail.
The most excellent one sends forth his sacrificial fee; Indra is the most active among the wealthy patrons.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, with that [fee] by which you bypass distress, O bold one, you distribute riches among the wise patrons.

Indra is the giver of enduring strength; may Indra, whose greatness has increased, be magnified by our songs. May Indra be the most effective slayer of Vṛtra; as a hero, he bestows those riches upon the patron, hastening forward.
He has come from there; may he, the most wonderful, bear up for us the great and radiant invocation of Indra.
On the path of the divine host, the bounteous one wins the praiseworthy prayer and the gift of the people.
Even from afar, his ears hear; speaking aloud, he thunders at the roar of Indra. May this invocation of the gods come to him; may this recited hymn turn Indra toward me.
With the highest devotion, I have celebrated with hymns that Indra, the ancient and undecaying, whom you [gods] possess;
both prayers and songs have been offered unto him, and may the great hymn of praise increase within Indra.
May the sacrifice and Soma strengthen Indra; may the sacred formulation (*brahman*), songs, hymns, and prayers strengthen him.
May the dawns at their rising, the nights, the months, the autumns, and the days strengthen Indra.

Thus have we, O inspired singer, now sought for our protection the great and fierce one, who was born for complete power and has grown strong for renowned bounty— him we invoke in the battles against Vṛtra.
Of that sweet, exhilarating speech of the pleasant, divine, inspired poet Agni—of that which is accompanied by the gods, grant us a portion of it; bestow upon the singer wealth headed by cattle.
Desiring the kine, he has gone around the mountain, yoking his team with those whose thoughts are fixed on Truth and who are joined in the age of Truth.
Indra shattered the unshakable ridge of Vala; with his words, he fought against the Paṇis.
This drop, O Indra, has illumined the nights that were unlit, throughout the autumns, at evening and at dawn;
they have established him as the banner of the days, and he has made the Dawns of pure birth.

Shining with his light, he has caused the unshining to shine; by the Eternal Law (ṛta), he has illumined many ancient things. He has moved along with horses yoked by the Eternal Law, finding the light of heaven with a navel that fills the people.
Now, being praised, O ancient King, swell abundant nourishments for the singer so that he may bestow wealth.
Grant waters, medicinal herbs, poisonless forests, cattle, horses, and men to him who sings your praise.
O Indra, drink; the juice is pressed for your exhilaration. Unharness your two bay steeds, your companions.
And sing forth, having sat down with your host; then bestow vigor upon the singer for the sacrifice.
Drink of this, O Indra, of which you drank at birth for exhilaration and for power, O mighty one;
for you, the men, the cows, the waters, and the pressing-stone have together prepared this Soma-juice for your drinking.
The fire is kindled, O Indra, and the Soma is pressed; let thy bay steeds, most capable of carrying, bring thee hither.
With a mind directed toward thee, I call upon thee repeatedly; O Indra, come for our great prosperity.
Come hither; you have always come with longing, O Indra, with a great mind to the drinking of Soma.
Listen to these our prayers, and may the sacrifice bestow vigor upon your body.

Whether you are in heaven on the decisive day, O Indra, or elsewhere, or in your own abode, wherever you may be—come from there with your team of horses to protect our sacrifice for our aid; being of one mind with the Maruts, drink [the soma], O lover of songs!
Come without anger to our sacrifice; for you the pressed drops flow clear.
O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, like cows to their own stall, come to your home, O Indra, first among those worthy of worship.
With that well-fashioned, most excellent palate of yours, with which you constantly drink the wave of honeyed Soma—drink with it!
The Adhvaryu has stepped forward for you; let your thunderbolt, O Indra, turn toward the cattle.
This drop, the bull of all forms, the Soma, has been prepared for Indra the bull.
Drink it, O Lord of Bay Horses, driver of the chariot, fierce one, over which you rule from of old and which is your food.
O Indra, the pressed Soma is better than the unpressed; this is more excellent for the wise man's delight.
O Overcomer, come to this sacrifice; with it, fill yourself full of all powers.
We call upon you, O Indra; come hither. May the Soma be sufficient for your body.
O Śatakratu, rejoice in the pressed juices; protect us in battles and among our people.
Bring all things to him who desires to drink, who is all-knowing, who is ever-active, who moves swiftly, and who never lags behind, O hero!
Come toward him with Soma juices, [you who are] the greatest drinker of Soma;
with vessels, [come] to the impetuous Indra with the pressed drops.
When you honor him with the pressed drops, with the Soma juices—the wise one knows all;
boldly he seeks each and every one of them.
O Adhvaryu, bring forward this pressed juice for him, for him alone! Will he not surely protect us from the curse of every arrogant kinsman?
In whose exhilaration you delivered that Śambara over to Divodāsa—this is that Soma pressed for you, O Indra; drink!
O Indra, that sharp-pressed exhilarating drink whose beginning, middle, and end you protect—this is that Soma pressed for you; drink it!
In whose exhilaration you released the cows that were held within the firm rock—this is that Soma pressed for you, O Indra; drink!
O Indra, you who, exhilarated by this draught, have taken up the power of Maghavan—this is that Soma pressed for you; drink!
