O Indra, Lord of the Self-Sustaining Power, that pressed Soma which is the wealthiest among riches and most resplendent among splendors— that is your intoxication.
O Indra, Lord of the Self-Sustaining Power (*svadhā*), that pressed Soma which is effective for you, most effective, a giver of wealth and of inspired thoughts— that is your intoxication.
That pressed Soma which makes you old in strength, or swift with your own aids— that is your exhilaration, O Indra, Lord of the Self-Sustaining (svadhā).
I praise that Indra for you, the unassailable lord of power, the hero who conquers all, the most generous, who watches over all people.
The songs which magnify him, the lord of swift bounty—
him indeed, his very vigor, both the divine worlds, heaven and earth, revere.
That power of our hymn we spread out for Indra,
so that his aids may rise up like inspired songs, closely united.

As a more recent friend, he has found skill; having drunk, he has brought forth better wealth for the gods. Having won with the *staulā* and *dhautarī* dice, he has become a wide-protecting guardian for his friends.
On the path of Truth, the Ordainer has drunk; for the sake of glory, the gods have set their minds [upon him].
Assuming a great name through his words, the beloved one has revealed his beautiful form to be seen.
Bestow upon us most brilliant skill; ward off the many hostilities of men.
By your powers, grant us more abundant vital strength, and aid us in the winning of wealth.
O Indra, O Maghavan, we have become yours; O Lord of the Bay Horses, do not be averse to us as our giver.
No kinsman whatsoever is seen among mortals; why indeed do they call you the one who impels the weak?
O Bull, do not abandon us to the one who is weary; O Wealthy One, may we suffer no harm in your friendship.
Many are your restraints among men, O Indra; slay those who do not press the Soma, root out those who do not give.
Like thundering clouds, Indra sends forth gifts of horses and cattle;
from of old you have been the sustainer of the singer. Let not the stingy ones deceive you, O bountiful one.
O hero Adhvaryu, bring forth the pressed juices for the great Indra, for he is their king—
he who has grown strong through the ancient and the new songs of the praising Rishis.
In the exhilaration of this [Soma], the wise Indra, knowing many forms, struck down the Vṛtras who were irresistible.
Offer up for him that Soma rich in sweetness, so that he may drink it—the hero with the handsome jaws.
May Indra be the drinker of the pressed Soma; may he, exhilarated by it, slay Vṛtra with his thunderbolt.
May he come even from afar to the sacrifice, the Vasu who protects our prayers and sustains the singer.
This is that very vessel for Indra’s drinking; Indra’s beloved nectar has been drunk. May it exhilarate the god for his goodwill; may it drive away hatred from us and drive away distress.
Rejoicing in these, O Hero, slay the enemies—the kinsmen and the strangers, O Maghavan, the unfriendly foes.
Against those who come with their armies and aim their weapons at us, O Indra, crush them and strike them down, driving them away.
O bounteous Indra, in these battles of ours, grant us great freedom and an easy path;
for the winning of waters, of offspring, and of progeny, O Indra, place our patrons on your side.
May the bay steeds, the virile ones, being harnessed—horses with virile chariots and virile reins—come toward us;
may they, the well-yoked virile carriers of the thunderbolt, bring you here for the sake of the virile exhilaration.
O Bull, your bulls have entered the vat, dripping with clarity like waves exulting;
O Indra, for you, the bull, they bring the pressed soma with their bulls.
You are the bull of heaven, the bull of earth; you are the bull of the rivers, O bull of the standing waters.
For you, the bull, the drop has swelled—the sweet juice, the honeyed draught, for your choice.
This god, being born with power, with Indra as his ally, overthrew Paṇi;
this Indu stole away the weapons of his own father and the magic wiles of the malevolent one.
He made the dawns have a good husband; he placed light within the sun. He found the triple-hidden nectar in the three luminous realms of heaven.
He propped apart heaven and earth; he yoked the chariot with its seven reins.
By his power, he placed the cooked milk within the cows; Soma established the fountain with its ten mechanisms.
He who by his skillful guidance brought Turvaśa and Yadu from afar—
Indra, that youthful friend, is ours.
Bestowing vigor even upon one who is no sage, and with even a horse that is not swift,
Indra is the winner of the staked wealth.
Great are his guidances, and many are his praises;
his aids never fail.
O friends, sing praise and chant aloud for him who is borne by the sacred word (*brahma*);
for he is our great protector.
O slayer of Vṛtra, you are the protector of one, you are the protector of two,
and also of such as we are.
You lead us beyond our enemies; you make us proclaimers of hymns. O hero among men, you are called "possessor of good heroes."
With songs of praise, I call upon the Brahman, the bearer of the sacred word, the friend worthy of hymns, as one calls a cow for milking.
In whose two hands they say all treasures are deposited from of old—
of that hero who overcomes hostile armies.
O wielder of the stone, O Lord of Might, you who are unbending, tear asunder even the firm fortresses of men; destroy their illusions.
So we, seeking glory, have invoked you, O true one, O Soma-drinker, O Indra, Lord of spoils.
Whether you were such as you were aforetime, or whether you are now such when the prize is set,
as one who is to be invoked, hear our call.
With our prayers and with swift steeds, O Indra, may we win prizes worthy of renown and the wealth set before us.
O Hero, lover of songs, you have indeed become great, O Indra, when the prize is set; you are to be sought after in the fray of battle.
O slayer of enemies, that aid of yours which is most swift in its onset—
by that, impel our chariot forward.
As the best of chariot-warriors with our attacking chariot,
O victorious one, may you win the offered prize.
Praise him who is alone, the one who watches over all people;
he was born as the Lord of men, possessing manly power.
O Indra, you who have been a kinsman to those who sing your praises, a gracious friend with your aid— such as you are, O Indra, be merciful to us.
Grasp the thunderbolt in your hands for the slaying of the Rākṣasas, O wielder of the thunderbolt; may you utterly conquer your rivals.
I invoke the ancient companion of riches, the friend who impels the singer, the one most frequently invoked by sacred prayer.
For he alone rules over all earthly treasures; he is the greatest lover of songs, the irresistible one.
O Lord of Cattle, boldly satisfy our desire with your teams of horses, with riches consisting of horses and cattle.
Sing this for you at the pressing, for the one invoked by many, the warrior,
that which is a blessing for the powerful one, as it is for the bull.
The Vasu indeed does not withhold the gift of wealth consisting of cattle,
once he has heard our songs.
May the slayer of the Dasyus indeed go to that cow-filled stall of his;
with his powers, may he open it for us.
O Śatakratu, these songs have cried out toward you,
O Indra, like mother cows toward their calf.
Hard to win is your friendship; you are a bull to one who desires cattle, O hero;
be a horse to one who desires horses.
Rejoice indeed in the soma-juice for the sake of great bounty through your own body;
do not deliver your worshiper to reproach.
O lover of songs, these hymns reach out to you at every pressing,
like milch-cows lowing toward their calf.
Most frequent among the many, in the contest of the singers who strive for prizes with their strengths.
O Indra, may our hymn of praise be most effective and closest to you;
impel us toward great wealth.
Bṛbu has taken his stand upon the highest head of the Paṇis,
like the broad forest-thicket on the banks of the Gaṅgā.
He whose auspicious gift flows like the rushing wind, consisting of thousands, bestows it immediately for the sake of giving.
Therefore, all noble singers always praise us well:
Bṛbu, the most liberal giver of thousands, the patron who bestows thousands most abundantly.
For we poets indeed invoke you alone for the winning of booty;
O Indra, lords of the good, men invoke you against the Vṛtras, and you as the goal of the racehorse.
As such, O wondrous one with the thunderbolt in hand, being boldly praised by us, O wielder of the stone,
scatter cattle and chariot-horses upon us, O Indra, like total booty for a victor.
Him who is the all-conquering, far-seeing one—Indra him we invoke.
O thousand-testicled, many-manly Lord of the True, be our strengthener in battles.

You press down upon the people with wrath like a bull, O impetuous one, bountiful one, worthy of praise. Be our protector in the great contest for wealth, for our bodies, for the waters, and for the sun.
O Indra, bring us fame that is most excellent, most powerful, and all-filling— by which,
O wondrous one with the thunderbolt in hand and beautiful jaws, you have filled both these worlds, heaven and earth.
We invoke you, O King, the fierce one who subdues the peoples, among the gods for our protection.
O Vasu, make all our wavering things firm; make our enemies easy to overcome.
O Indra, whatever vigor and manly strength you possess among the Nahuṣa tribes, or whatever splendor belongs to the five peoples— bring all those heroic powers hither together.
Or whatever virile power you have with Tṛkṣi, O Maghavan, with Druhyu, or among the people of Pūru—
bestow that upon us for the conquest of men, to overcome our enemies in battles.
O Indra, grant a threefold refuge, a triple-layered protection, and a secure shelter for the generous patrons and for me; ward off the missile from them.
Those who, with minds intent on cattle, have overcome the enemy and strike him down boldly—
O Indra, Maghavan, lover of songs, be our closest protector of our bodies.
And so, O Indra, be for our prosperity;
do not abandon us in battle, when the winged arrows with sharpened points fly through the mid-air like lightning-flashes.
Where heroes stretch out their bodies, providing dear protection for their fathers—there, grant a shelter for our own bodies and for our offspring; ward off the unseen hatred.
When you, O Indra, urge the horses forward in the release for the great prize,
on the uneven road and the crooked path, like falcons seeking glory.
Like rivers rushing down a slope, they speed along when they resound with their own effort;
like birds circling for meat, they are held fast by the arms within the cow.
Truly, this [Soma] is sweet and indeed honeyed; truly, it is strong and indeed flavorful. And now, no one at all can withstand Indra in battles when he has drunk of it.
This sweet juice here has been most intoxicating, in which Indra rejoiced at the slaying of Vṛtra—
he who destroyed the many great deeds of Śambara and his ninety-nine fortresses.
This [Soma], when drunk, raises up my voice; this has awakened the yearning wisdom.
This wise one has measured out the six wide expanses, beyond which no world exists at all.
He is he who made the breadth of the earth and the height of heaven; he is he. This Soma has established the nectar in the three flowing rivers and the wide mid-air.
He has found the wondrously visible flood at the forefront of the dawns that dwell in the light.
This great bull, accompanied by the Maruts, has propped up the sky with a mighty pillar.
Drink boldly the Soma from the jar, O Indra, Vṛtra-slayer, hero among the riches in battle!
At the midday libation, pour yourself full; as the abode of wealth, bestow wealth upon us.
O Indra, look out for us like a leader; lead us further toward greater prosperity.
Be a good ferryman who carries us across; be a wise guide and a benevolent leader.
O Knower, lead us toward a wide world, the light of heaven, free from fear and auspicious.
High and firm are your arms, O mighty Indra; may we take refuge beneath your great protection.
O Indra, place us upon the broadest chariot-seat, drawn by your two most swift horses, O Lord of a hundred powers!
Bring us the most excellent nourishment among all refreshments; O Maghavan, let not the wealth of the enemy overcome us.
O Indra, be gracious; desire life for me. Sharpen my inspired thought like the edge of iron.
Whatever I, devoted to thee, speak here, accept that; make me one who possesses the gods.
Indra the protector, Indra the helper, the hero Indra who is easily invoked at every call—I invoke Śakra, Indra who is invoked by many; may the bounteous Indra bestow well-being upon us.
May Indra, the good protector, the possessor of wealth, with his aids, be gracious to us—he who possesses all knowledge.
May he drive away our enemies and grant us fearlessness; may we be masters of heroic vigor.

May we abide in the good-will of that one worthy of sacrifice, and also in his auspicious benevolence. May that Indra, the excellent protector and possessor of wealth, drive our enemies far away from us.
Toward you, O Indra, our songs, prayers, and teams of horses rush like waves down a slope.
Like a wide expanse of bounty, you gather for yourself many libations, waters, cows, and drops of Soma, O wielder of the thunderbolt.
Who shall praise him? Who shall satisfy him? Who shall worship him, since the bountiful one always protects the fierce one?
Striking them down like two feet, he makes one after another—first and then the next—by his powers.
The hero is heard of as subduing each fierce one with his own fierceness, leading one after another across;
increasing the hostilities, the king of both worlds, Indra, overcomes the human tribes.
He casts aside his friendships with the former ones; speeding forward, he goes with others. Shaking off those who have not attained him, Indra traverses many autumns.

He has become the counterpart to every form; that is his form for the purpose of being perceived. Indra moves in many forms through his powers of illusion (*māyā*), for his bay steeds (*harayaḥ*) are yoked—ten times a hundred.
Yoking his two bay horses to the chariot, Tvaṣṭṛ shines forth mightily here.
Who would ever sit on the side of the enemy, even while the patrons remain seated?
O gods, we have come to a land without pastures; though the earth is wide, she has become a place of distress.
O Bṛhaspati, provide guidance in the search for cattle; O Indra, show the path to this singer who stands thus.
Day after day, she drove away the similar dark-born ones from their dwelling to the other side;
the Bull slew the two Dāsas, Varcin and Śambara, who were seeking wealth, at the enclosure of the waters.
Prastoka has now given you, O Indra, ten treasures of wealth and ten prize-winning horses. From Divodāsa we have received the bounty of Atithigva; we have taken possession of the Śambara wealth.
Ten horses, ten treasure-chests, ten garments and provisions,
and ten lumps of gold— these I have won from Divodāsa.
Aśvatha gave ten chariots with side-horses and a hundred cows to the Atharvans and to Pāyu.
Sārñjaya has honored the Bharadvājas, who bestow great wealth beneficial to all people.
O Lord of the Forest, may you be strong-limbed, our friend, a furtherer, and a provider of brave sons;
you are bound with cow-hides, so be firm—may your rider win all that is to be won.
The strength drawn forth from heaven and earth, the power brought together from the lords of the forest;
the vigor of the waters, encompassed by the rays of light—worship with an oblation the chariot of Indra’s thunderbolt.
The thunderbolt of Indra, the vanguard of the Maruts, the offspring of Mitra, and the navel of Varuṇa— O divine chariot, enjoying this our offering of oblations, accept these gifts.
Make the earth and the sky resound; let the world scattered in many places take heed of you. O drum, in harmony with Indra and the gods, drive the enemies far, even to the furthest distance.
Thunder forth strength; bestow vigor upon us; roar aloud, driving away misfortunes.
O drum, blow away all calamities from here. You are the fist of Indra; be firm!
Drive those away and bring these back; the drum speaks aloud as our signal. Our heroes, winged with horses, move forward together; O Indra, let our chariot-warriors be victorious!
Sacrifice after sacrifice, with song after song, for the sake of skill,
we shall praise Agni— the immortal Jātavedas— like a beloved friend.
Let us serve the Son of Strength with this offering, for he is well-disposed toward us; may he grant us the gift of oblations.
May he be our helper in battles for booty, may he be our increaser, and our protector of our bodies.
For you, O Agni, are a bull, ageless and great; you shine with your flame. Blazing with undecaying radiance, O pure one, shine brightly with your excellent lights.

O Agni, you sacrifice to the great gods; you shall sacrifice to them in due order through your wisdom and your wondrous power. Turn them hither for our protection; grant us strength and win it for us.
Him whom the waters, the stones, and the woods nourish as the embryo of Cosmic Order—
he who is produced by men with force upon the high ridge of the earth.
He who has filled both worlds with his radiance hastens through the sky with smoke;
he has become visible through the darkness in the nights, the ruddy bull in the dark ones—the ruddy bull in the dark ones.
O Agni, with your great flames and your bright radiance, O God, being kindled by Bharadvāja, O most youthful one, shine upon us with wealth, O bright one; shine with splendor, O purifier!
O Agni, you are the lord of house of all human clans;
O youngest one, protect your kindler from distress with a hundred fortresses for a hundred winters, as well as those who give to the singers.
O Wondrous One, O Vasu, impel bounties toward us with your aid.
O Agni, you are the charioteer of this wealth; find a firm footing for our offspring.
Protect our children and grandchildren with your unfailing and tireless guardians. O Agni, ward off from us the divine wrath and the deceptions of the godless.
O friends, drive hither with a new song the cow who yields nectar;
release her who does not shrink away.
She who has milked immortal fame for the self-luminous host of Maruts;
she who is in the favor of the swift Maruts, she who comes hither with their blessings.
For Bharadvāja,
you have twice milked forth the cow who yields all things, and the nourishment that provides sustenance for all.
I praise him for my purpose— him who is like Indra in his skillful wisdom, like Varuṇa in his power of illusion, like Aryaman in his joyousness, and like Viṣṇu in his far-reaching bounty.
Like the brilliant host of Maruts, loud-sounding and irresistible, may he bring together hundreds and thousands for the sake of the people;
may he make hidden treasures manifest, and may he make wealth easy for us to find.
O Pūṣan, hasten toward me; I would speak into your ear, O glowing one:
"The hostilities of the enemy are evil."
Do not uproot the *kākambīra* tree, for you shall utterly destroy the curses;
nor shall the sun even for a single day seize the neck of the bird.
May your friendship be like that of a leather bag— free from wild beasts,
without leaks, well-filled, and overflowing with curds.
For you are beyond mortals and equal to the gods in splendor;
O Pūṣan, look upon us in battles and protect us now as you did of old.
O shakers, may the guidance of the benevolent one be for us—
his truthfulness— whether he be a god or a mortal man who strives to sacrifice, O Maruts, you who are swift in worship.
The praise of whom, even as soon as it is uttered, the god Sūrya goes around the sky;
the Maruts have assumed brilliant power, a name worthy of sacrifice, Vṛtra-slaying power—the supreme Vṛtra-slaying power.
Once indeed heaven was born; once the earth was born. Once was the milk of Pṛśni milked; no other is born after that.
I praise the people of holy vows with newest songs—Mitra and Varuṇa, who grant favor.
May they come hither; may they hear us here: the noble rulers Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni.
The one to be praised by every people at the sacrifices, whose will is undeluded, the messenger between the two young maidens;
Agni, the child of heaven, the son of strength, the banner of the sacrifice, the ruddy one—I worship him.

The two daughters of the ruddy one are of different forms: one is adorned with stars, the other with the sun. Racing together, moving apart, the two purifiers reach the celebrated hymn as they are being praised.

Toward Vāyu, the one of great wealth, the possessor of all boons, and the filler of chariots, let this lofty hymn go forth— a sage seeking the sage, O you who are worthy of sacrifice, as he comes with his teams of horses whose paths are radiant.

May that radiant chariot of the Aśvins, which yokes itself by thought, conceal my form for me— that chariot wherewithal, O Nāsatyas, O Heroes, you come to our dwelling to seek us out, for the sake of our offspring and ourselves.
O Parjanya and Vāta, bulls of the earth, quicken the watery soil;
O seers who hear the truth, by whose songs you sustain the world, bring the world into being.

May the daughter of the lightning, Sarasvatī, of wondrous life, the wife of the hero, bestow wisdom. May she, in harmony with the divine dames, grant to the singer an unassailable, flawless refuge and protection.
With eloquence, he has approached the protector of every path, impelled by desire, with his hymn of praise.
May that Pūṣan grant us riches headed by gold; may he bring each and every prayer to fulfillment.

Let the radiant Hotṛ Agni, the invoker of the worthy Tvaṣṭṛ— who is the first to receive his portion, who is glorious, the bestower of vitality, the skillful god with beautiful hands and arms, the one who is easily invoked— worship him, the worshipful lord of the dwellings.
With these songs, we shall magnify Rudra, the father of the world, by day and by night;
impelled by the sage, let us separately invoke the great, lofty, undecaying, and most gracious one.
O youthful, wise, and worshipful Maruts, come to the dwelling of the singer;
for even the dull you quicken as you grow strong, O heroes, approaching like the Aṅgirases.
Like a herdsman driving his cattle home, I have sent forth my song to the hero, the powerful and swift one;
he, the famous one, shall touch the heights of heaven with the hymns of our speech, as if with the rays of light upon his body.
Viṣṇu, who measured out the earthly realms three times for the sake of the oppressed man—
may we rejoice in wealth, in our own bodies, and in our progeny, while abiding under the protection you provide.

May Ahi Budhnya grant us this with the waters and hymns; may Parvata and Savitṛ grant us this as well. May the gods who bestow gifts together with the plants, and Bhaga and Purandhi, speed us forward toward wealth.
Now grant us wealth borne on chariots, filling the people, rich in heroes— the great guardian of Truth—
grant us an undecaying dwelling by which we may overcome the godless rival tribes and prevail over the god-fearing peoples.
With prostrations I invoke for mercy the goddess Aditi, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni;
Aryaman who bestows gifts, the very gracious one, and the gods who are protectors—Savitṛ and Bhaga.

O Sūrya, you of great splendor, seek out the gods who have Dakṣa as their father, for the sake of sinlessness— those twice-born ones who are observers of *ṛta*, truthful, radiant, worthy of sacrifice, and whose tongue is Agni.
And may Heaven and Earth grant us wide sovereignty; O most gracious Rodasīs, provide us with refuge. Grant us great freedom so that we may dwell in safety, O Dhiṣaṇās, free from all harm.
May the sons of Rudra, the unassailable Vasus, being invoked today, bow down to us—
those Maruts, the gods, whom we have called upon when placed in either small or great distress.
To whomsoever the two goddesses, Heaven and Earth, have joined together, Pūṣan, who bestows abundant sacrifice, attends.
O Maruts, when you come having heard our call, all beings tremble on the wide-stretched path.
Sing with a new prayer, O singer, to that hero Indra, the lover of songs;
may he, being praised, hear our call and, being glorified, grant us great spoils of war.
O Waters, you who belong to mankind, grant us uninjured protection and well-being for our children and descendants;
for you are the most motherly physicians, the progenitors of all that is stationary and all that moves.
May the divine Savitṛ, the protector, the golden-handed, the worshipful, come unto us— he who,
like the face of the Dawn, being rich in gifts, discloses desirable treasures for the donor.
And you, O Son of Strength, may you turn the gods toward us today at this sacrifice. May I ever abide in your bounty; may I, O Agni, through your protection, be rich in heroic sons.
And may those two Nāsatyas come to my invocation; you two, O sages, are indeed inspired by our prayers.
Just as you delivered Atri from the great darkness, O heroes, so deliver us from distress in the hour of need.

May you be the givers of wealth to us—wealth that is brilliant, full of vigor, rich in heroes, and abundant in food. Being gracious, O divine, earthly, and watery gods born of the kine, be merciful to us.
May Rudra, Sarasvatī, Viṣṇu, and Vāyu, being of one mind and bounteous, be gracious to us;
may Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja, the divine Vidhātṛ, Parjanya, and Vāta cause our nourishment to swell.
And may that god Savitṛ, Bhaga, and Apāṃ Napāt, who bestows gifts, protect us;
may Tvaṣṭṛ, in harmony with the gods and their wives, and Dyaus with the gods, and Pṛthivī with the oceans.
May Ahi Budhnya hear us, and Aja Ekapād, Earth, and Ocean;
may all the gods who increase the cosmic order (*ṛta*), being invoked, and the praised mantras recited by seers, protect us.
Thus, O descendants of mine, the Bharadvājas praise you with their prayers and hymns;
you who have been invoked as divine dames, you unassailable Vasus, you all have been lauded as worthy of sacrifice.
Up rises that great eye of Mitra and Varuṇa, the beloved and undeceivable, the pure and beautiful face of Truth; like a golden ornament, it has shone forth at the rising of heaven.
The inspired sage who knows the three assemblies of these gods and their origin from of old—
he, the Sun, beholding both the straight and the crooked among mortals, surveys the ways of the noble.
I praise you, the guardians of the great Truth—Aditi, Mitra, and Varuṇa, the well-born; Aryaman and Bhaga, whose thoughts are undeceived. I call upon those who share the same dwelling, the purifiers.

I approach with reverence the Ādityas and Aditi— the destroyers of enemies, lords of the good, undeceived, great kings, givers of fair dwellings, youthful, possessing noble dominion, and men who rule from heaven.
O Father Heaven, O guileless Mother Earth, O Brother Agni, O Vasus, have mercy on us!
O all you Ādityas and Aditi, being of one mind, extend to us manifold protection.

O worshipful ones, do not deliver us over to the wolf, nor to the she-wolf, nor to any who seeks to do us harm; for you are the charioteers of our bodies, and you have become the masters of our skill and our speech.
May we not suffer for the sin committed by another; O Vasus, may we not do that which you would punish.
For you, O All-Gods, are the rulers of all; may the enemy himself bring harm upon his own body.
Homage indeed to the Mighty One; I seek to win him with homage. Homage has supported the earth and the sky.
Homage to the gods; homage is their lord. Even a committed sin I seek to dispel through homage.

I bow with prostrations to you all, the charioteers of Truth, whose will is purified, who dwell in the home of Truth, and who are undeceivable—those far-seeing heroes; I bend myself before all of you, O great and worshipful ones.
For they possess the most excellent luster; they lead us across all difficulties.
Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni are good rulers, whose thoughts are fixed on the cosmic order (ṛta), and who are true kings of speech.
May Indra, Earth, Pūṣan, Bhaga, Aditi, and the five peoples increase our strength;
may they be for us good protectors, good helpers, good leaders, excellent saviors, and good guardians.

Now may we reach the divine dwelling; the Bhāradvāja priest approaches the gods for their favor. With the offerings placed upon the sacrificial seats, the sacrificer, seeking wealth, has paid homage to the race of the gods.
Drive away that crooked enemy, O Agni, the thief of evil intent; O Lord of the Good, make his path most distant and lead us to a way of safety.
O pressing-stones, O Soma, you have indeed lowed for us for the sake of friendship. Slay the greedy Paṇi, for he is like a wolf.
For you indeed, O bounteous ones, with Indra as your chief, are directed toward heaven; make our path easy to travel and be our guardians at home.
We have indeed entered upon the path that leads to well-being and is free from danger,
by which one avoids all enemies and finds wealth.
I do not approve of that, whether by day or on earth, nor by sacrifice, nor by these ritual labors.
May the well-formed mountains crush him; may the performer of excessive sacrifice be brought low.

O Maruts, whoever holds us in contempt, or whoever seeks to find fault with the sacred prayer (*brahman*) being performed—may burning pains be his lot for his wicked deeds; may the heavens scorch that hater of sacred prayer!

Why indeed, O Soma, do they call you the guardian of the sacred word (*brahman*), and why indeed do they call you our protector against curses? Why indeed do you look upon us as we are being reviled? Cast your burning weapon at the hater of the sacred word.
May the dawns as they are born protect me; may the swelling rivers protect me. May the firm mountains protect me; may the ancestors protect me at the invocation of the gods.
May we always be of good mind; may we indeed behold the rising sun.
May the Lord of Wealths grant this, he who, being the bestower of the gods, comes most readily with his aid.
May Indra come most near with his protection; may Sarasvatī, swelling with the rivers;
may Parjanya, bringing refreshment through the plants; and may Agni, the well-praised and easy to invoke, come like a father.
O All-Gods, come hither; hear this my invocation;
sit down upon this sacred grass.
O gods, whoever honors you with an offering dripping with clarified butter—
to him do you all go.
May the sons of immortality hear our songs; may they be gracious toward us.
May all the gods, who increase the cosmic order and hear our invocation according to the seasons,
enjoy the appropriate milk.
May Indra with his host of Maruts, Tvaṣṭṛ, Mitra, and Aryaman take pleasure in this hymn and these our oblations.
O Agni, as the Hotṛ-priest, perform this sacrifice of ours according to the sacred ordinances, you who are wise regarding the divine host.
O All-Gods, hear this my invocation—ye who are in the intermediate space and ye who dwell in heaven;
ye who have Agni for your tongue or who are worthy of sacrifice, sit upon this sacred grass and rejoice.

May all the gods worthy of sacrifice hear me, and may both the worlds and Apāṃ Napāt hear my prayer. May I not utter words that you might despise; rather, dwelling closest to you in your favors, may we rejoice.
Whosoever among the great ones, possessing the power of the serpent, were born upon the earth, in heaven, or in the gathering place of the waters—
may those gods grant us all life for our sustenance, and may they make the nights and dawns favorable to us.
O Agni and Parjanya, you who are easy to invoke, protect my prayer and our fair hymn at this invocation.
May one of you generate the sacrificial food (iḷā) and the other the germ; bestow upon us strengthening foods accompanied by progeny.
Upon the strewn sacrificial grass, while the fire is kindled, I worship you with a hymn and great reverence.
O all you gods worthy of sacrifice, rejoice today in this oblation at our assembly.
O Pūṣan, Lord of the Path, we have yoked you for our prayer, as one yokes a chariot for the winning of booty.
Bring to us manly wealth, a hero who bestows sacrificial gifts,
and a desirable master of the household.
O glowing Pūṣan, urge even the one who does not wish to give toward giving; soften the mind even of the miser.
Clear the paths for the winning of booty; scatter the adversaries.
O Mighty One, may our prayers be fulfilled.
O Sage, pierce through the hearts of the Paṇis with your iron spear;
then deliver them over to us.
O Pūṣan, pierce with your awl; seek what is dear in the heart of the stingy one, and then make him subject to us.
O Sage, tear apart and rend asunder the hearts of the Paṇis;
then deliver them over to us.
O Pūṣan,
O glowing one, with that goad which you carry as an inciter of prayer, scratch out the heart of this man and tear it to pieces.
O glowing one, that goad of yours which has cattle as its ornament and which brings cattle to success—
for that [goad] of yours we seek favor.
And make our prayer win cattle, win horses, and win booty; make it manly for our enjoyment.
O Pūṣan, lead us together with one who knows, who may directly instruct us,
and who may say, "This is indeed it."
May we go together with Pūṣan, who shall point out our homes, saying, "These indeed are they."
The wheel of Pūṣan is not damaged; the rim does not fall away;
nor does its felly waver.
Pūṣan does not overlook the one who serves him with an oblation;
he is the first to find wealth.
May Pūṣan follow after our cows; may Pūṣan protect our horses;
may Pūṣan win booty for us.
O Pūṣan, follow after the cows of the sacrificer who presses the Soma,
and also those of us who offer praise.
Let none perish, let none be harmed, let none be shattered in a pit; then come hither with those who are unharmed.
We pray to Pūṣan, who hears us, the watchful one whose wealth is never lost,
the lord of riches.
O Pūṣan, under your protection may we never come to harm;
we here are your praisers.
May Pūṣan place his right hand around us from beyond; may he bring back to us what we have lost.
Come, O Son of Deliverance, O Radiant One, let us two be united;
be the charioteer of our *ṛta*.
We implore the best of charioteers, the one with braided hair, the lord of great bounty, the friend of wealth.
O glowing one, you are a stream of wealth; O Lord whose horses are goats, you are a mass of riches, the friend of every inspired singer.
Now let us praise Pūṣan, who is drawn by goats, the vigorous one,
he who is called the lover of his sister.
I have spoken to the suitor of my mother; may the lover of my sister hear us, the brother of Indra and my friend.
Let the goats, firmly mounted upon the chariot and bearing him, carry Pūṣan— the god who is the glory of the people.
Whoever accuses Pūṣan, saying,
"He has eaten the groats," O God, he shall not succeed in accusing him.
And indeed, that most excellent charioteer, the lord of the virtuous, joined with you as a friend,
Indra slays the Vṛtras.
And there, upon the speckled ox, the best of charioteers set down the golden wheel of the sun.
O Wondrous One, most wise, whatever we may say to you today, O much-praised one,
make that prayer of ours successful.
And may you lead this company of ours to the winning of cattle;
O Pūṣan, you are renowned from afar.
We pray for your blessing, which drives away evil and brings near prosperity; may it be for our complete well-being today and for our complete well-being tomorrow.
Now, O Indra and Pūṣan, let us invoke you for friendship, for well-being, and for the winning of booty.
One has approached the Soma pressed in the ladles to drink;
the other desires the groats.
Goats are the draft-animals of one; the two bay steeds are harnessed for the other.
With these two, he strikes down the Vṛtras.
When Indra, the most virile, brought down the great waters according to the sacred law (*ṛta*),
Pūṣan was there with him.
Like the spreading branch of a tree, we grasp that benevolent favor of Pūṣan and of Indra.
We draw Pūṣan toward us, as a charioteer draws the reins;
and Indra, for my great well-being.
One of your forms is bright, the other is worthy of sacrifice; like the sky, you encompass the two days of different colors.
For you, O self-dependent one, protect all wondrous powers; O Pūṣan, may your bounty here be auspicious.
With goats for steeds, guardian of cattle, whose home is wealth, who quickens our prayers, and who is established over the entire world—
Pūṣan, brandishing his supple goad, moves as a god surveying all created beings.
O Pūṣan, those golden ships of yours which travel within the ocean and through the intermediate space—
with those you go on an embassy for Sūrya, having been made by desire and seeking glory.
Pūṣan is the close kinsman from heaven and earth, the lord of nourishment, the bountiful one of wondrous luster—
he whom the gods gave to Sūryā, the strong and swift one created by desire.
Now, while the juices are pressed, I shall proclaim those heroic deeds which you two have performed:
your fathers, the enemies of the gods, have been slain; O Indra and Agni, you two still live.
Truly, O Indra and Agni, such is your greatness, most worthy of praise;
you have a common father, you are brothers, and your mothers are here and there.
Having settled together at the pressed juice like two horses yoked to a feast,
Indra and Agni, the wielders of the thunderbolt— those two gods we now invoke here for our protection.
O Indra and Agni, you who increase the cosmic order (*ṛtāvṛdhau*), when one praises you while these Soma juices are pressed—
O gods, you who consume the oblations of the *pajra* clan, you do not disregard the words of him who speaks with pleasure.
O Indra and Agni, what mortal man among you two gods has understood this?
One of you, having yoked his horses that move in different directions, speeds along upon the same chariot.
O Indra and Agni, this footless one has come before those with feet; leaving her head behind, moving while speaking loudly with her tongue, she has stepped down thirty paces.
O Indra and Agni, for men stretch their bows in their arms;
do not abandon us in this great contest for wealth, in the quests for cattle.
O Indra and Agni, the hostilities of the enemy oppress me;
drive away our enemies and keep them far from the light of the sun.
O Indra and Agni, yours are the treasures of heaven and of earth;
bestow upon us here wealth that nourishes all our life.
O Indra and Agni, who are borne by hymns and hear our invocation,
come with all our songs of praise through these lauds, to drink of this Soma.
He pierces Vṛtra and wins booty— the one who shall worship Indra and Agni,
the two victorious ones, who rule over abundant wealth, most powerful through their might, and striving for strength.
O Indra and Agni, fight now for those cows, the waters, the sun, and the dawns that have been carried away.
O Indra, you take possession of the quarters, the sun, and the bright dawns; O Agni, drawn by your team of horses, you seize the waters and the cows.
O slayers of Vṛtra, come hither with your Vṛtra-slaying strengths, O Indra and Agni, through our prostrations. O Indra and Agni, be with us with your most excellent and ungrudging gifts.
I invoke those two by whom all this was fashioned in the past;
Indra and Agni do not neglect us.
Fierce and destroyers of adversaries, Indra and Agni we invoke; may they both show us mercy in such a plight as this.
The two lords of the virtuous have slain the Āryan Vṛtras; they have slain the Dāsa Vṛtras;
they have slain all enemies.
O Indra and Agni, these hymns of praise have resounded toward you both; O you who bring auspiciousness, drink the pressed juice.
O Heroes, Indra and Agni, with those many-desired teams of horses which you possess for the donor, come hither!
With those [horses], O heroes, come hither to this pressed libation,
O Indra and Agni, for the drinking of the Soma.
Invoke him who with his flame embraces all the forests;
he makes them black with his tongue.
The mortal who, having kindled [the fire], seeks to win the favor of Indra, crosses the waters easily for the sake of glory.
Grant us food accompanied by vigor and swift horses to carry Indra and Agni.
I invoke you both, O Indra and Agni; may you both rejoice together in the gift of wealth.
You both are givers of food and riches; I call upon you both for the winning of strength.
Come to us with wealth in cattle, horses, and riches;
we invoke those two gods, Indra and Agni, the friends who bring auspiciousness for our friendship.
O Indra and Agni, hear the invocation of the sacrificer who presses the soma; enjoy the oblations, come hither, and drink the sweet soma juice.
This [Sarasvatī] bestowed the impetuous Divodāsa, who clears away debt, upon the worshipper Vadhryaśva.
O Sarasvatī, those powerful gifts of yours—by which you consumed the Paṇi who ate up every man—[are yours].
Like one who digs for lotus-stalks, she has shattered the ridges of the mountains with her surging powers and mighty waves.
With well-fashioned hymns and inspired thoughts, let us invoke Sarasvatī, the slayer of Pārāvata, for our protection.
O Sarasvatī, strike down those who revile the gods; destroy the progeny of every deceitful Bṛsaya.
Furthermore, you found the waters for the people; O possessor of plenty, you caused the poison to flow away from them.
May the goddess Sarasvatī, rich in spoils, protect us with her bounties, she who is the promoter of our inspired thoughts.
O Goddess Sarasvatī, whoever invokes you when the prize is at stake,
as one calls upon Indra in the struggle against Vṛtra.
O Goddess Sarasvatī, you who are swift in the contests for booty, protect us; like Pūṣan, grant us a gain.
And may Sarasvatī, the terrible one whose path is golden, the slayer of Vṛtra, desire our fair praise.
She whose infinite, unassailable, shimmering, and surging ocean moves about,
roaring with might.
May she, the observer of cosmic order (*ṛtāvarī*), carry us across all hostilities and her other sister-rivers,
just as the sun extends its light beyond the darkness.
And may Sarasvatī, who is dear among the dear ones, who has seven sisters, and who is well-pleased, be worthy of our praise.
Having filled the earthly realms, the wide expanse, and the intermediate space, may Sarasvatī protect us from those who revile us.
Abiding in three places, consisting of seven elements, and nourishing the five classes of beings, she has become one to whom offerings are made in every contest for booty.

She who is distinguished above all great ones by her greatness, who excels the others in splendor as the most active among the active— Sarasvatī, vast as a chariot, fashioned for wide-reaching power, is to be praised by the wise.
O Sarasvatī, lead us toward greater wealth; do not distance yourself from us, nor fail us with your milk.
Accept our friendship and our household service; may we never go from you to foreign lands.
I praise the two heroes who rule over this heaven; singing with hymns, I call upon the Aśvins, those who at the breaking of dawn instantly strive to reach the ends of the earth and the wide expanses.
Coming to the sacrifice with their pure [rays], they have caused the splendor of the chariot to shine through the regions;
measuring out many immeasurable spaces, you two cross over the waters, the deserts, and the plains.
O ye two fierce ones, you have indeed repeatedly brought that path which is free from distress, with your steeds swift as thought and full of vigor,
so that the distress of the mortal who offers oblations may lie far away.

May the ancient, guileless Hotṛ-priest worship the two youthful [Aśvins], who have harnessed their steeds and attend to the prayer of the one who praises them anew; bringing splendor, nourishment, food, and strength.
I invoke with a new hymn those two who are beautiful, the wonder-workers, most helpful to many, the ancient ones;
they who have become the greatest bestowers of bliss to him who recites and praises, granting wondrous gifts even to the singer.
With winged birds, you carried Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, out from the waters and the ocean through the regions;
traversing dustless leagues with winged steeds, you brought him forth from the lap of the flood.
O victorious chariot-borne ones, you shattered the mountain; O bulls, you heard the call of Vadhrimatī.
Bestowing gifts upon Śayu, you made the cow swell with milk; thus, O swift and active ones, you brought favor to Cyavāna.
Whatever wrath of the gods or among mortals has existed from of old, O Heaven and Earth,
O Ādityas, Vasus, and Rudriyas, place that burning evil upon him who is joined with the *rakṣas*.
May he who ordains Mitra and Varuṇa, the two kings, according to the seasons, take heed of this:
let him cast his weapon against the deep-seated demon and against the treacherous speech of the stranger.
With your inner wheels, come on your radiant, hero-bearing chariot to provide a path for our offspring.
With your secret weapon, strike down the heads of the mortal who seeks to harm us.
Come hither with your teams of horses— the highest, the midmost, and the lowest—
open the doors of even the firm enclosure rich in cattle for the singer, O you of wondrous bounty!

Where has the reverent hymn of praise found those two beautiful ones, much-invoked today, like a messenger? For you, O Nāsatyas, have turned yourselves hither; for you shall be most dear to this man’s prayer.
Come readily to this my invocation, being praised so that you may drink the soma-juice;
go around that path from harm, so that neither the outsider nor the insider may overcome you.
The soma-juice has been prepared for you both; the sacrificial grass has been spread in the wide space, most easy of access.
With uplifted hands, seeking you, we have paid homage; the pressing-stones, approaching, have adorned you.
Upright has Agni stood for you at the sacrifices; forth goes the gift, the glowing ladle full of clarified butter.
The Hotṛ-priest, joyfully minded, choosing [the gods], has yoked those who are the Nāsatyas when he calls upon them with the oblation.
For the sake of glory, the daughter of Sūrya mounted the chariot of the two far-reaching lords who possess a hundred aids.
By means of your wondrous powers, O masters of magic, you became manifest here at the birth of the two heroes, the ones worthy of sacrifice.

With these beautiful splendors, you two brought nourishment for the sake of Sūryā’s wedding-glory; birds flew forth after you for the sake of your wondrous form; may the well-praised voice reach you, O ye who are worthy of devotion.
O Nāsatyas, may your winged horses, the best at carrying, bring you toward the offerings;
let your chariot, swift as thought, be sent forth along the many nourishing streams of food.
For manifold indeed is your gift, O you who enjoy many things; make our nourishment swell like a cow that never fails.
And may both your praise, O lovers of sweetness, and your beautiful hymn, and the juices that have followed your bounty, reach you.
Moreover, two swift, ruddy mares of Puraya, a hundred cooked [dishes] at Sumīḷha, and at Peruka—Śāṇḍa gave me these: golden ornaments, well-fashioned, ten high and powerful oxen that are submissive.
O Nāsatyas, may he who has many paths grant you hundreds and thousands of horses for my song;
O heroes, may he now grant them to the singer Bharadvāja. May the two of you, performers of many wonders, slay the demons. May they be [granted].
May we, together with the patrons, abide in your favor within the wide expanse.
The Dawns have risen up, radiant with splendor, like shimmering waves of water.
She makes all paths fair and easy to traverse; the wealthy, bountiful Dakṣiṇā has indeed appeared.
Auspicious, you have appeared; you shine far and wide. Your flames and rays have flown up to heaven.
Adorning yourself, you reveal your breast, O Goddess Uṣas, shining with great splendors.
The ruddy, radiant cows carry her forth, the auspicious one who spreads out widely.
She drives away the darkness like a hero against his enemies; she repels it like a swift steed.
O well-guided one, you cross the mountains on easy paths; O self-luminous one, you traverse the waters where there is no wind.
O daughter of heaven, bring us wealth upon your broad course, O exalted one, so that we may have nourishment.
O Dawn, bring hither with thy well-yoked steeds; thou carriest thy choice gift according to our pleasure.
O Daughter of Heaven, thou who art a goddess, worthy of being beheld, thou hast appeared with great bounty at the first invocation.
Even the birds have flown up from their dwellings at your dawning, as have the men who partake of food.
O Goddess Uṣas, you bring abundant wealth to the mortal donor who remains at home.
This daughter of heaven, born from the sky, awakening the human dwellings as she shines forth,
has been recognized by her gleaming light through the nights even across the darkness.

They have sped forth with their ruddy-yoked horses; the Dawns, shining on their radiant chariots, appear wondrously. Leading the vanguard of the great sacrifice, they drive away the darkness of the night.
Bringing renown, booty, nourishment, and strength to the mortal who offers oblations, O wealthy Dawns,
ruling over a host of heroes, bestow protection today and grant treasure to the one who worships you.
For now, O Dawns, there is treasure for the one who honors you; now, for the heroic donor;
now, for the inspired singer who recites hymns. You have indeed brought it even to one like me in the past.
For now, O Dawn, you who stand upon the mountain peaks, the Aṅgirases sing to you for the sake of the cow-pens.
With song and with prayer, they have split them open; the invocation of the gods has become true for men.
Shine forth for us as of old, O Daughter of Heaven, O Maghavan, for the one who serves you like Bharadvāja.
Bestow upon the singer wealth with noble heroes; grant us wide-reaching fame.
That form of hers must indeed be a marvel even to one who understands, for she bears the common name of "Cow" (*dhenu*).
While one [aspect] swells among mortals to be milked, Pr̥śni has once yielded her bright udder.
Those who, like kindled fires, have shone forth when the Maruts grew strong— twice and thrice—
their chariots became dustless and golden, together with their manly vigor and heroic powers.
Those who are the sons of the bounteous Rudra, whom the steadfast one must bring hither—verily the Great Mother knows them; she, the vast Pṛśni, has conceived the germ for the noble one.

Those who do not shrink from their birth, purifying themselves even while remaining within the censurable; when, being pure, they pour forth according to their pleasure, sprinkling their own bodies with splendor.
Swift indeed are they, by whom even this bold name, "the Marut," was assumed;
who are not to be mocked, who are tireless in their greatness—may the bounteous one never cause those fierce ones to desist.
These fierce ones, with their power and bold armies, have yoked both well-established worlds; then indeed, Rodasī, shining by herself, has taken her stand among them as if upon a pillar.
O Maruts, let this be your journey, which even one without horses or a charioteer drives;
traversing the mid-air, reaching both heaven and earth, it goes straight along its path, free from reins and without a bridle.
O Maruts, there is no one now to ward him off nor any to overcome him whom you protect in the contest for booty;
he who wins offspring, cattle, progeny, and waters—he shall break open the enclosure on the decisive day of battle.
Offer a brilliant hymn to the singing, swift Marut host, who possesses their own inherent strength—those who by force overcome all powers; O Agni, the earth trembles before these mighty ones.
Radiant like the flash of a sacrifice, impetuous like the tongues of fire,
singing praises like roaring heroes, the Maruts are of brilliant birth and unassailable.
I invite with my invocation that growing host of Maruts, whose spears are flashing, the sons of Rudra.
For the army of heaven, the pure prayers have vied like waters from the mountains, O fierce ones.
With songs of praise, may I magnify you two, Mitra and Varuṇa, the most eminent among all existing beings;
you who, like reins, best restrain and guide the two unequalled peoples with your own arms.
This inspired thought is spread out for you both; may it approach the dear sacrificial grass with homage.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, bestowers of good gifts, grant us that unassailable protection which is your secure shelter.
Come here, O Mitra and Varuṇa, with fair praise, being invoked with dear homage! You two, who stand together as providers of wealth, urge even those who listen like people at work by your greatness.
Like horses that are swift and of pure lineage, when Aditi bore the embryo according to the *ṛta*, you two,
the great ones being born as great [beings], were established as terrible for the mortal enemy.
When all the gods, rejoicing in their greatness and being of one accord, bestowed sovereign power upon you both; when you encompass even the two wide worlds, your spies are undeceived and unerring.
For you two maintain sovereignty day after day; you make firm the ridge as if from the highest heaven.
Firm is the constellation, belonging to all the gods; it has stretched out the earth and the sky with its nourishing stream.
You two sustain the body so that it may fill the belly, when they, gathered together, fill the dwelling-place.
The young women do not fail, when they, invigorating all, bring forth the milk that is not withheld.
May the wise one ever approach you both with his tongue, since the true impeller has come into being according to the *ṛta*.
O you whose food is ghee, let that be your greatness; may you two drive away the distress of the donor.

When those who strive against you, O Mitra and Varuṇa, violate your dear ordinances established by you— those who are neither gods through their insight nor mortals, who do not attend the sacrifice, like sons of the waters.

When the singers distribute their speech and some, meditating, recite the *nivid* formulas, then we shall proclaim true hymns to you both; for in your greatness, you two are not restrained by the gods.
Truly, under your protection, O Mitra and Varuṇa, your shelter is close at hand and not far off,
when the cattle follow the straight-flying, bold, and vigorous bull as he is harnessed for battle.
With eager hearing, may the sacrifice be raised for you both in unison, as it was for Manu, by him who has trimmed the sacrificial grass, so that he may worship.
O Indra and Varuṇa, may he turn you hither today for great refreshment and for great favor.

For they are indeed the most excellent in the assembly of gods, the most powerful among the heroes by their impetuous might; for they have become the most generous of the wealthy patrons, possessing great strength, conquerors of Vṛtra through the Eternal Law, and accompanied by all their hosts.
Praise them with reverent hymns and invocations, O Indra and Varuṇa, who take delight in our prayers.
One of you, by his might, strikes Vṛtra with the thunderbolt; the other, the sage, attends to the assemblies.
When the Gnas and the men have grown strong, and all the gods, self-praised among men,
then, O Indra and Varuna, you two have become great through your majesty, as have Heaven and Earth, the wide ones.
He indeed is the bountiful giver, possessing good horses, the upholder of *ṛta*, O Indra and Varuṇa, who worships you both with his own self.
May that liberal man overcome his enemies with nourishment; may he win wealth and [the favor of] men who possess riches.
O Gods, Indra and Varuṇa, may that wealth which you bestow upon the sacrificer who offers oblations—wealth abounding in treasures and many cattle—be ours; for it shatters the curses of our enemies.
And may there be for us, O Indra and Varuṇa, wealth for our patrons— wealth that is well-protecting and guarded by the gods—
for those whose vigor prevails in battles, and who, as conquerors, instantly extend their splendors.

Now, O gods Indra and Varuṇa, being praised, bestow wealth upon us for the sake of glorious fame. Thus extolling the host of the Mighty One, may we cross over difficulties as if crossing waters by boat.
Sing forth now a beloved hymn, wide-reaching, to the sovereign Varuṇa, the great god;
he who, by his majesty, rules over the two vast worlds, shines through his will like one undecaying with his flame.

O Indra and Varuṇa, drinkers of the pressed juice, you who uphold the sacred law, drink this pressed Soma which intoxicates. Your chariot comes toward the sacrifice for the feast of the gods, to the dwelling place, for the drinking.
O Indra and Varuṇa, you two bulls, drink of this most honeyed, potent Soma. This juice has been poured out for you among us; sit upon this sacred grass and rejoice.

I urge you both together with this rite and with food, O Indra and Viṣṇu, at the completion of this work. May you enjoy the sacrifice and bestow wealth upon us, carrying us across by paths that are free from harm.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, you who are the progenitors of all thoughts, the vessels that hold the Soma;
may our recited hymns favor you, and may our praises sung with chants be pleasing to you.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, lords of the exhilarating draughts, come to the Soma, bestowing wealth.
Let them anoint you both with the ointments of our prayers; let the hymns being recited together with the *uktha* chants [anoint you].
O Indra and Viṣṇu, let your horses, the subduers of enemies, bring you to our common feast;
may you enjoy all the invocations of our thoughts, and listen to my prayers and songs.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, that deed of yours is worthy of praise: in the exhilaration of Soma, you have made wide space. You made the mid-air broader and spread out the regions for our life.

O Indra and Viṣṇu, being strengthened by the oblation, accepting the first portion with reverence, and having been presented with the offering, you who are nourished by the clarified butter—bestow wealth upon us! You two are the ocean, the vessel that holds the Soma.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, drink of this sweet Soma; O wonder-workers, fill your bellies with it. The intoxicating juices have come to you; hear my prayers and my invocation.
Both of you have conquered; you are not defeated, nor has either one of you been defeated. O Indra and Viṣṇu, when you two contended, you divided the thousandfold [booty] into three parts.
Rich in ghee, the support of all beings, wide and broad, yielding honey and well-adorned—
Heaven and Earth, by the law of Varuṇa, are held apart, ageless and full of abundant seed.

Unfailing, with many streams, rich in milk, the two worlds, Rodasī, who rule over this universe and possess pure vows, yield clarified butter for the doer of good deeds; pour upon us that seed which was established by Manu.
O Heaven and Earth, O two Dhiṣaṇās, that mortal who offers worship to you both for the sake of upright conduct prospers;
he is born again through offspring according to the cosmic law, as his various forms, though diverse in appearance, remain united under your common vow when poured out by you.
Heaven and Earth are enveloped in ghee; they are adorned with ghee, filled with ghee, and increased by ghee.
Vast and wide, established as the chief priests for the choosing of the Hotṛ, the inspired poets praise them for their favor so that they may seek [the gods].
May Heaven and Earth sprinkle sweetness for us—those who drip sweetness, who yield sweetness, whose laws are sweet;
they who establish the sacrifice and wealth among the gods. May they grant us great renown, booty, and heroic vigor.

May both Heaven and Earth swell nourishment for us—the Father and Mother, all-knowing and of wondrous deeds. May the two worlds, harmonious and bringing welfare to all, together bestow upon us gain, strength, and wealth.

Upward has this god Savitar extended his golden arms for the sake of the libation, he of good wisdom. With clarified butter he sprinkles his hands; the youthful and skillful sacrificer [stands] in the support of the mid-air.
May we abide under the most excellent impulse of the god Savitṛ, for the granting of wealth—
[that impulse] which you, O Lord, possess as the one who brings to rest and impels the multitude of all that is two-footed and four-footed.
O Savitṛ, with your undeceivable and auspicious guardians, protect our household today.
O golden-tongued one, guard us for new prosperity; let no malevolent speaker have power over us.
Up has risen that god Savitṛ, the friend of the house, golden-handed, at every twilight.
With iron jaws, holy, and sweet-tongued, he bestows abundant wealth upon the donor.
Like a priest, Savitar has raised his golden arms, he of the beautiful countenance.
He has ascended the heights of heaven and the earth; he has brought to rest whatever beast flies about.

O Savitṛ, grant us what is desirable today, and what is desirable tomorrow, and what is desirable day by day. For you, O God, are the master of abundant desirable wealth; through this prayer, may we be partakers of that which is desirable.
O Indra and Soma, great indeed is that majesty of yours; you two performed the first great deeds.
You two found the sun, you two [found] the light of heaven; you struck down all darknesses and reproaches.
O Indra and Soma, you cause Uṣas to dwell; you lead forth the sun together with its light.
You propped up the sky with a support and spread out the earth, the mother, far and wide.
O Indra and Soma, you slew the dragon Vṛtra who obstructed the waters; the heaven rejoiced after you.
You set free the channels of the rivers and filled the many oceans.
O Indra and Soma, you placed the cooked [milk] within the raw bellies of the cows;
you seized it, unbound, within these bright, variegated, moving creatures.
O Indra and Soma, you two indeed have bestowed a victorious, renowned, and glorious offspring;
O fierce ones, you have extended manly vigor to the people, a strength that overcomes hostile armies.

Bṛhaspati, the breaker of the rock, the first-born, the upholder of cosmic order, the descendant of Aṅgiras, rich in oblations, with his double stride, seated at the *pragharma* sacrifice like our father— the Bull— roars aloud to the two worlds.
Bṛhaspati, who has created a wide world even for such people at the invocation of the gods—he, slaying the Vṛtras, shatters the fortresses; conquering his enemies and foes, he prevails in battles.
Bṛhaspati has won all treasures; this god has conquered the great stalls full of cattle. Desiring to win the waters and the light, the irresistible Bṛhaspati slays the enemy with his hymns.

O Soma and Rudra, uphold your divine power; may our offerings reach you swiftly. Bestowing the seven treasures in every house, be auspicious to us—blessing to our bipeds and blessing to our quadrupeds.
O Soma and Rudra, tear away in all directions the disease that has entered our home.
Drive Nirṛti far away; may auspicious glories attend us.
O Soma and Rudra, bestow all these healing medicines upon our bodies.
Untie and release from us whatever sin has been committed that is bound within our persons.
O Soma and Rudra, you who possess sharp weapons and sharp missiles, and who are most gracious—be merciful to us here!
Release us from the noose of Varuṇa and protect us with well-disposed minds.
Like the appearance of a rain-cloud is his countenance when, clad in armor, he goes into the lap of the combative fray. Conquer with an uninjured body; may the greatness of that armor protect you.
With the bow may we win cattle, with the bow may we win the battle; with the bow may we conquer fierce conflicts.
The bow brings about the retreat of the enemy; with the bow may we conquer all the quarters.
As if about to speak, she comes close to the ear, embracing her dear friend;
like a woman, this bowstring twangs upon the stretched bow, carrying us across in the assembly.
Moving together like a young woman to her tryst, may they bear [the arrow] in their lap like a mother her son;
may these two bow-ends, acting in concert and quivering, pierce the enemies and strike down the foes.
The father of many, he has many sons; having entered the fray, he makes a whizzing sound.
The quiver, bound upon the back, conquers all encounters and armies when it is set in motion.
Standing on the chariot, the skillful charioteer leads the spirited horses forward wherever he desires. Behold the greatness of the reins: the traces follow behind the will of the mind.
Making loud noises, the horses with strong hooves, striving for the prize along with the chariots,
trampling the enemies with their forefeet, destroy the foes without retreating.
The chariot-stand is his oblation, where his weapon and his armor are laid;
there may we sit upon the powerful chariot, always well-disposed in spirit.
The Fathers, who sit at the sweet draught, bestowers of vitality, dwelling in hardship, powerful, profound;
they who possess brilliant armies, whose strength lies in their arrows, tireless, truly heroic, vast, and conquerors of hosts.
O Brahmins, O Fathers, worthy of Soma; may Heaven and Earth, the auspicious and faultless, be gracious to us.
May Pūṣan protect us from misfortune, O increasers of Truth; guard us, and let no one who speaks evil have power over us.
She clothes herself in beautiful feathers; the deer is her tooth. Bound with cow-hides, she flies forth when discharged.
Where men run together and apart, there may the arrows grant us protection.
O *ṛjīti*, spare us; let our bodies be as stone.
May Soma speak for us, and may Aditi grant us protection.
They strike their flanks; they beat upon their haunches. O wise horse-whip, urge the horses on in the battles.
Like a serpent with its coils, he encircles the arm, warding off the strike of the bowstring; the hand-guard, knowing all the secret ways, as a man, shall protect the man from every side.
That which is smeared with poison, whose head is like a deer's, and whose mouth is of iron—
to this divine arrow, born of Parjanya’s seed, be great homage!
Released, fly away, O arrow, sharpened by the sacred word (*brahman*). Go to the enemies; fall upon them, and let not one of them remain.
Where the arrows fly together like boys with shorn hair—there may Brahmaṇaspati and Aditi grant us protection; may they grant us protection for all days.
I cover your vital organs with armor; may King Soma clothe you with immortality.
May Varuṇa make for you a space wider than the wide; may the gods rejoice after you as you conquer.
Whoever—whether our own kin, a stranger, or one from afar—seeks to harm us, may all the gods strike him down; may the sacred word (*brahman*) be my inner armor.
With their thoughts and with the movement of their hands, men have generated from the two fire-sticks Agni, the praiseworthy one,
the far-seeing lord of the house, the radiant one.
The Vasus established that Agni in his dwelling, so that he might be well-beheld from every side for our protection—
he who is worthy of skillful service and is the eternal master of the house.
O Agni, most youthful one, kindled, shine brightly before us with your unaging flame;
unto you, all strengths evermore approach.
May these fires of yours shine forth more excellently than other fires, radiant and rich in heroes,
where well-born men sit together in assembly.
O Agni, O powerful one, grant us through our prayer wealth consisting of brave sons and noble offspring,
which is highly praised and which no sorcerer can overcome by his assault.
To him, the very skillful one, the young woman approaches with the oblation at evening and at dawn—the ladle dripping with ghee;
to him approaches Aramati, seeking wealth.
O Agni, burn away all hostile powers with those heats wherewith you consumed Jarūtha; drive far away the disease that causes groaning.
O Agni, you whose face they kindle, O most excellent, bright, radiant, and purifying one—
through these our praises, may you be present here with us.
O Agni, those mortal men of our fathers who have in many places shared in your countenance—
be well-disposed toward us here along with them.
May these men, heroes in the slaying of Vṛtra, overcome all godless magical powers—
those who have admired my well-praised prayer.
O Agni, let us not sit in the void among men, nor around you in a state of lack of food, childlessness, or want of heroes; O Dweller in the House, dwell in houses filled with offspring.
May he whose sacrifice the horse-attendant constantly approaches grant us a dwelling rich in progeny and noble offspring— a dwelling that increases through its own birth and through its abundance.
Protect us, O Agni, from the unpleasant Rakṣasa; protect us from the malice of the stingy man who offers no gifts.
With you as our ally, may we overcome those who attack us in battle.
May this Agni surpass all other fires, where the vigorous son with strong hands assembles the thousandfold path of the imperishable syllable.
May that Agni protect the kindler from the one who seeks to harm him; may he deliver him from distress.
Well-born heroes move about him on every side.
This is that Agni, invoked in many places, whom the Lord, possessing oblations, kindles with fuel;
him the Hotṛ-priest goes around at the sacrifices.
O Agni, may we, being masters, offer unto thee many constant oblations;
performing both modes of conveyance at the sacrificial feast.
O Agni, bear these most welcome oblations to the assembly of the gods;
may they accept our fragrant offerings.
O Agni, do not deliver us over to one who is childless, nor to ill-will, nor to this lack of devotion;
O observer of Truth, do not abandon us to hunger, nor to the demon, neither in our home nor in the forest.
O Agni, now instruct my prayers; O God, grant them favor for the sake of the patrons.
May we both partake in your bounty. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Agni, you who are easy to invoke and of lovely aspect, shine forth with beautiful radiance, O Son of Strength!
May no one among our own kin ever harm our progeny; may no heroic man among us be deprived of his manly vigor.
O Agni, do not proclaim us to those who hold us in contempt while these fires, kindled by the gods, burn; let not your ill-will, O Son of Strength, reach us even through your impetuous wrath.
O Agni of radiant countenance, that mortal becomes wealthy who offers oblations to the immortal;
he establishes himself among the gods as a seeker of riches, whom the patron, seeking his goal, approaches with inquiry.
O Agni, you who know of great prosperity, bring vast wealth to our patrons,
so that we, O powerful one, may rejoice with undiminished life and heroic sons.
Now, O Agni, instruct my prayers; you, O God, make them effective for the liberal patrons.
May we both partake in your bounty. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Agni, enjoy our fuel today; blaze forth mightily, emitting your worshipful smoke. Touch the celestial ridge with your crests; extend yourself with the rays of the sun.
We shall praise with sacrifices the greatness of Narāśaṃsa, the worshipful one, of these [gods],
who are wise, pure, and bestowers of inspired thought— the gods who relish both kinds of oblations.

We shall ever exalt for the sacrifice Agni, who is worthy of praise, the Asura endowed with great skill, the messenger between the two worlds (Heaven and Earth) whose word is true— the one kindled by Manu, like Manu himself.
Worshipful, bringing [offerings] on bended knees, they spread the sacrificial grass with reverence before Agni.
O Adhvaryus, pouring out [the oblation], cleanse with the offering the one whose back is sprinkled with ghee, the dappled one.
The pious ones, seeking the gods, have thrown open the doors at the assembly of the deities, longing for the chariot.
Like two mothers licking their young, they have adorned themselves like virgins at festivals.
And may the two divine maidens, Dawn and Night, like a cow easy to milk,
sit upon the sacred grass— much-invoked, wealthy, and worthy of sacrifice— to bring us prosperity.
O inspired poets, singers at the human sacrifices, I deem you two to be Jātavedas, worthy of worship.
May you elevate our sacrifice during our invocations; may you win precious boons for us among the gods.
May Bhāratī, in harmony with the Bhāratīs; may Iḷā with the gods, and Agni with men;
may Sarasvatī with the Sarasvateyas—may these three goddesses sit down upon this sacred grass (barhis).
O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, being gracious, bestow upon us that generative seed which nourishes;
from which is born a hero, skillful in action, highly dexterous, one who sets the pressing-stones in motion, and a lover of the gods.
O Lord of the Forest, release [the oblation] toward the gods; let Agni, the immolator, prepare the offering.
He, indeed, as the most truthful Hotṛ-priest, shall sacrifice, for he knows the generations of the gods.
Come hither, O Agni, being well-kindled, on the same chariot with Indra and the swift gods!
Let Aditi, the mother of noble sons, sit upon our sacrificial grass; let the immortal gods rejoice in the Svāhā-call!
In harmony with your fires, make Agni your god— the most excellent sacrificer, the messenger at the rite—
who is steadfast among mortals, the upholder of cosmic order (*ṛtāvā*), whose head is flame, whose food is clarified butter, and who is the purifier.
Like a neighing horse eager for pasture when he has stepped forth from the great enclosure, the wind blows after his flame; then indeed your path becomes black.
O Agni, you for whom the ageless, kindled flames of the newly born bull rise upward;
your ruddy smoke goes toward heaven, for as a messenger, O Agni, you travel to the gods.

O you whose power spread across the earth when you swiftly seized your food with your jaws; like an unleashed army, your net advances; O Wondrous One, you consume it with your tongue as if it were barley.
Him, the youngest Agni, men groom like a steed both at evening and at dawn;
sharpening him as a guest in his own dwelling, the flame of the bull-like one blazes when he is offered oblations.
O you of beautiful countenance and lovely aspect, your face shines brightly like gold when it is near;
your roar goes forth like the thunder of heaven, and you display your splendor like the wondrous sun.
So that we may offer to you with Svāhā to Agni, with oblations accompanied by sacrificial fees and rich in clarified butter—
by means of those immeasurable glories of yours, O Agni, protect us with a hundred fortresses of iron.

O Son of Strength, Jātavedas, with those invincible hymns which you possess for the donor, or with those manly songs by which you grant us protection— guard us with them, together with our patrons and the singers.
When he goes forth, pure as a sharpened axe, shining with his own form and beauty;
he who was born from his two parents, desirable for the sacrifice to the gods, the wise and purifying one.

O Agni, shine forth these blessings upon us; may we attain a wise and noble resolve. May all things be well for those who praise you and sing your hymns. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Bring forth an offering and a well-purified hymn for your Agni, for his bright luster—
he who, by his wisdom, moves between all divine and human races.
May that Agni be skillful even though he is young, he from whom, as the youngest, he was born of his mother;
he who, bright-toothed, embraces the forests, and devours even abundant food all at once.
In the assembly and in the presence of this god, whom mortals have seized as the bright one—
Agni, who has rejected the human snare, has shone forth for the Āyu, difficult to overcome.

This seer among those who are not seers, the wise Agni, the immortal, has been established among mortals. O mighty one, do not lead us astray in this matter; may we always be well-disposed toward you.
He who has occupied the god-fashioned womb— for by his mental power Agni has transcended the immortals—
him the plants and the trees, and the earth, bear as their embryo, he who nourishes all.
For Agni is the lord of abundant immortality; he is the lord of the giver of wealth and heroic vigor.
O powerful one, may we not sit around you without sons, without cattle, or without food.
For the wealth of the stranger is to be shared; may we be masters of our own eternal riches.
O Agni, there is no offspring of another that remains as a remnant for us; do not lead us astray from the path of the thoughtless.
For a stranger, however well-disposed, is not to be grasped as one's own kin by the mind;
yet he returns again to his own home. May the prize-winning steed, our new protector, come toward us.
O Agni, protect us from the one who seeks to harm us; O possessor of power, guard us from reproach.
May your smoke-enveloped path come to us, and may desirable, thousandfold wealth be gathered for us.

O Agni, shine forth these blessings upon us; may we attain a wise and noble resolve. May all things be favorable for our worshippers and for him who praises you. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Bring forth a song of praise to the mighty Agni, the messenger of heaven and earth;
he who, as Vaiśvānara, has grown strong in the lap of all the immortals through those who remain ever-watchful.
Agni has been established in heaven and on earth; he is the leader of the rivers, the bull of standing waters.
Vaiśvānara, growing strong by his choice, shines forth upon the human tribes.
Out of fear of you, O Vaiśvānara, the dark tribes fled in different directions, abandoning their possessions, when you, O Agni, blazing for the sake of Pūru, shone forth, shattering their fortresses.
O Vaiśvānara Agni, both the earth and the sky follow your threefold law;
blazing with undying flame, you have overspread the two worlds with your light.
O Agni, the bay steeds, lowing toward you, and the resonant, ghee-dripping songs attend upon you—
the lord of the peoples, the charioteer of riches, Vaiśvānara, the banner of the dawns and of days.
In you the Vasus established their asuric power, for they took pleasure in your will, O you who are great like Mitra;
you, O Agni, drove the Dasyus from their home, generating wide light for the Ārya.
Being born in the highest heaven, like Vāyu you instantly protect the path;
generating the worlds, O Jātavedas, you cried out, bestowing gifts for the sake of offspring.
O Agni Vaiśvānara, Jātavedas, send forth to us that glorious nourishment,
by which you, O possessor of all boons, swell our wealth and grant wide renown to the mortal who offers oblations.
O Agni Vaiśvānara, bestow upon our liberal patrons that wealth abounding in food, and grant us renowned strength;
together with the Rudras and Vasus, O Agni, being well-pleased, extend great protection to us.

I proclaim the praise of the sovereign Asura, the man who is to be celebrated by the peoples; like those of Indra, the mighty deeds of him who is powerful, I, praising the wood, speak aloud as one who offers homage.
They urge forth the sage, the banner, the nourishment, the light from the mountain—the auspicious sovereignty over heaven and earth.
With songs, I celebrate the ancient, mighty deeds of Agni, the breaker of forts.

Agni has driven away those Dasyus who lack resolve, who are deceitful, whose speech is harmful, who are stingy, faithless, unprosperous, and devoid of sacrifice; he, the first, has cast the later non-sacrificers behind him.
Him who, most heroic, by his powers made the waters flowing westward turn eastward while they were rejoicing in the western darkness—
I praise that Agni, the lord of wealth, the unbending subduer of those who attack us.
