He who made the dwelling-places free from disease with his deadly weapons, and who made the Dawns have noble lords as husbands—
he, the mighty Agni, having hemmed in the Nahuṣas, by his powers made the clans bringers of tribute.
In whose protection all people have taken their stand, seeking his favor—
Agni Vaiśvānara has sat down in the choice lap of the two worlds, the parents.
The god Vaiśvānara has taken up the treasures of the deep at the rising of the sun;
from the lower ocean and from the further one, Agni has taken them from heaven and from earth.

I impel with salutations for you the god Agni, the powerful one, like a prize-winning horse; may he, the wise one, become our messenger at the sacrifice. Moving with measured pace, he has found his place among the gods by himself.
Come, O Agni, along your own paths, you who are delightful and take pleasure in the friendship of the gods;
making the ridges of the earth roar with your strength, burn down all the forests with your jaws according to your will.
The sacrifice is directed eastward, for the sacred grass is well-placed; Agni, being invoked like a Hotṛ priest, is gratified.
Calling upon the two Mothers who possess all boons, from whom you were born, O most youthful and most gracious one.
At once, at the sacrifice, the wise men brought forth the charioteer who belongs to them;
Agni, the lord of the people, has been established in the house as the beloved, sweet-tongued, and observer of Truth.

The chosen bearer has sat down, having arrived; Agni, the priest, the distributor, in the assembly of men—him whom both Heaven and Earth have magnified, whom the Hotṛ-priest worships as the possessor of all boons.
These men have surpassed all things with their splendors—those heroes who have fashioned the chosen prayer;
they who, listening, furthered the people, and those who have meditated upon this my *ṛta*.
Now we Vasiṣṭhas implore you, O Agni, the lord of riches, O Son of Strength;
grant food to our singers and to our patrons. Do you all protect us evermore with your blessings.
The noble King is kindled with prostrations, he whose face is anointed with ghee;
men, pressing forward, invoke him with oblations. Agni has shone forth at the head of the dawns.
And this very one has been known as the great, joyous Hotṛ, the youthful Agni of man;
having spread himself over the earth, he has shone forth, and with blackened furrows he has grown strong through the plants.
By what hymn, O Agni, will you favor us? What power will you exercise when you are praised?
When, O bounteous giver, shall we become masters of wealth, winners of riches that are difficult to overcome and truly excellent?
This Agni of Bharata is heard of further and further, as he shines forth with great light like the sun;
he who has stood firm against the Pūru in battles, the resplendent divine guest, has blazed brightly.
Abundant oblations are indeed placed within you; be well-disposed toward us with all your faces.
O Agni, though already praised and being lauded, you are heard; O well-born one, increase your own body by yourself.
May this speech, winning hundreds and thousands, arise for Agni with double strength—
so that it may be a blessing to the praisers and to our kinsman, brilliant, driving away disease, and slaying the Rākṣasas.
Now we Vasiṣṭhas implore you, O Agni, the lord of riches, O Son of Strength; grant nourishment to our praisers and to our patrons. Do you all protect us evermore with your blessings.
The lover of the dawns has awakened from their lap—the delightful Hotṛ, the most wise, the purifier.
He establishes the banner for both classes of beings; he places offerings among the gods and wealth among the doers of good deeds.
He is the one of excellent wisdom who forced open the doors of the Paṇis, purifying for us the hymn that provides much nourishment;
the joyous Hotṛ, the domestic lord of the people, has become visible through the darkness of the nights.
Unerring sage, Aditi, Vivasvat, Mitra who speaks well—may he be our auspicious guest.
With brilliant luster he shines at the forefront of the dawns; the germ of the waters has entered the plants.
Worthy of praise by men through the ages, Jātavedas has shone forth, gathering together from all sides;
he who shines with a beautiful appearance and radiance, the kine have awakened as he is kindled.
O Agni, go on your mission as messenger; do not fail, but proceed toward the gods with the company of those who offer prayers.
Sacrifice to Sarasvatī, to the Maruts, to the Aśvins, and to the Waters—sacrifice to all the gods so that they may bestow treasures.
O Agni, Vasiṣṭha, kindling you, has slain Jarūtha; sacrifice for wealth to Purandhi.
O Jātavedas, sing your praises in many songs; and may you all protect us evermore with blessings.
Like the lover of the Dawn, he has spread his broad radiance—flashing, shining, and glowing.
The pure, tawny bull shines with light; impelling our yearning prayers, he has awakened them.
Like the sun at dawn, Agni has shone forth at the break of day; like the *uśij* performing a sacrifice, he has extended his thought.
Agni, the god who knows all births, hastens as the messenger who goes to the gods, the most effective seeker of gain.
Toward Agni proceed our songs and god-seeking thoughts,
begging for wealth— toward him who is fair to behold, of beautiful countenance, swift-moving, the bearer of oblations, the messenger of mankind.
O Agni, being in harmony with the Vasus, bring Indra to us; bring the great Rudra with the Rudras;
bring Aditi, who is kind to all people, with the Ādityas; and bring Bṛhaspati, the possessor of all boons, with the chanters of hymns.
The eager ones invoke Agni, the most youthful and pleasant Hotṛ, at the sacrifices;
for he has become the protector of riches, the unwearied messenger for the worship of the gods.
Great is the heralding of this sacrifice; the immortals do not rejoice without you.
Come hither on one chariot with all the gods; O Agni, sit down here as the first Hotṛ.
The men who offer oblations ever invoke you, the agile one, for the office of messenger;
O Agni, he upon whose sacred grass you sit with the gods, for him the days become auspicious.
Even in three days you have made manifest the treasures within you for the mortal who offers oblations.
Like Manu, O Agni, worship the gods here; be our messenger and protector against curses.
Agni is the lord of the great sacrifice; Agni [is the lord] of every oblation that has been prepared.
For the Vasus delight in his ritual wisdom, and thus the gods have established him as the bearer of the offerings.
O Agni, bring the gods here to consume the oblation; let them, with Indra as their chief, rejoice here.
Place this sacrifice among the gods in heaven. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
We have approached with great reverence the youngest [Agni], who has shone forth, well-kindled in his own dwelling—
the one of wondrous luster between the two wide worlds, well-invoked, facing every direction.
He, Agni Jātavedas, who by his greatness overcomes all difficulties, is praised in the home;
may he protect us from distress and from reproach, both us who sing his praises and our patrons.
O Agni, you are Varuṇa and you are Mitra; the Vasiṣṭhas magnify you with their hymns.
May all treasures easy to win be found in you. Do you protect us always with your blessings.
Bring forth a prayer and a hymn for Agni, the all-purifying, the bestower of inspired thought, the slayer of the Asuras— like one who, being pleased,
offers an oblation upon the sacred grass— to Vaiśvānara, the director of our prayers.
O Agni, blazing with your flame at your birth, you filled the two worlds, heaven and earth;
O Vaiśvānara Jātavedas, by your greatness, you released the gods from the curse.
When you were born, O Agni, you looked out upon all beings like a watchful herdsman, a vigilant guardian who wanders everywhere.
O Vaiśvānara, find a path for our sacred prayer; and do you all protect us always with your blessings.
With fuel, with invocations of the gods, and with oblations, may we, full of reverence, worship Jātavedas— the god of bright luster— for Agni.
O Agni, may we worship you with fuel; may we offer to you, O Holy One, with beautiful hymns.
O Hotṛ of the sacrifice, may we honor you with clarified butter; O God of auspicious luster, may we honor you with the oblation.
O Agni, come with the gods to our invocation of the gods, enjoying the *vaṣaṭ*-utterance.
May we be those who offer gifts to you, the god; and do you, O gods, protect us always with your blessings.
Offer the oblation into the mouth of the bounteous one who is to be approached,
he who is our nearest kinsman.
He who has sat down as lord over the five tribes in every house— wise, the young master of the home.
May Agni protect our household wealth from every side;
and may he guard us from distress.
I have now generated a new hymn for Agni, the falcon of heaven; will he not surely grant us wealth?
Whose desirable splendors are for all to see, like the wealth of one who possesses heroes,
as he blazes at the forefront of the sacrifice.
May Agni accept this *vaṣaṭ*-utterance; may he enjoy our songs of praise—he who is the best of sacrificers, the bearer of oblations.
O Lord of the People, O God, we establish you, the radiant one, rich in heroes, as our guest, O Agni, when you are invoked with oblations.
Shine through the nights and the dawns; with you as our priest, may we be well-offered.
May you, possessing good heroes, be well-disposed toward us.
To you, for the sake of gain, the inspired singers approach with their prayers;
to you come the thousandfold syllables.
Agni, the immortal with bright radiance, drives away the demons; he is pure, purifying, and worthy of praise.
As the lord of power, O young son of strength, bring us riches;
and may Bhaga grant us what is desirable.
O Agni, you [grant] glory accompanied by heroic sons; and Savitṛ the god, Bhaga, and Diti bestow desirable wealth.
O Agni, protect us from distress; O God, burn against those who seek to harm us with your most scorching, ageless flames.
And so, for our protection, be a great, unassailable iron fortress for the defense of men,
a hundredfold strong.
Protect us from distress and from the one who intends evil, O illuminator of the night; protect us by day and by night, O infallible one.
With this [hymn], I invoke for you Agni, the Son of Strength,
with reverence— the beloved, most wise steward of the sacrifice, the immortal messenger of all.
He yokes his two ruddy steeds that provide all nourishment; well-invoked, he hastens forward.
The sacrifice is accompanied by excellent prayers and performed with skill for the sake of the Vasus—the divine bounty of the people.
The flame of this bounteous one has risen up as he is being invoked;
the ruddy smoke-clouds, touching the heavens, the men kindle together as they enkindle Agni.
We make you our most glorious messenger; bring the gods here for the feast.
O Son of Strength, bestow upon us all the enjoyments of mortals, whatever we entreat of you.
O Agni, you are the master of the house; you are our Hotṛ at the sacrifice.
O possessor of all boons, you are the wise Potṛ; perform the sacrifice and go to that which is desirable.
Bestow wealth upon the sacrificer, O you of noble wisdom, for you are indeed the bestower of riches.
Sharpen us at the rite, every priest who is well-praised and skillful.
O Agni, well-invoked with *svāhā*, may the wise patrons be dear to you—
those generous lords of men who bestow wide pastures of cattle.
Those in whose home Iḷā, with butter in her hand, sits down as soon as she has arrived—protect them from malice and reproach, O Victorious One; grant us shelter that is far-renowned.
With his pleasant tongue and mouth, he is the most wise bearer of oblations;
O Agni, bring wealth to our patrons and sweeten the offering of the sacrifice.
Those who bestow gifts of horses and great wealth out of a desire for high renown—
O youngest one, protect them from distress with your hundred fortresses as their deliverers.
The god Draviṇodas desires from you a full ladle poured out;
pour it up or fill it up, for then the god will take heed of you.
The gods have made him the Hotṛ of the sacrifice, the wise one, the bearer;
Agni bestows treasure and heroic strength upon the person who worships and gives.
O Agni, be well-kindled with excellent fuel, and let the sacrificial grass be spread out widely.
And let the longing doors swing wide open; and bring hither the longing gods.
O Agni, come with the oblation and worship the gods; O Jātavedas, make the sacrifice well-performed.
May Jātavedas perform the sacrifice well; may he worship the immortal gods and satisfy them.
Win for us all desirable things, O wise one; may our prayers be fulfilled this day.
The gods, O Agni, have established you as the bearer of oblations, the son of strength.
May we be those who offer gifts to you, O God; approaching you, may you distribute great treasures to us.
For in you indeed, O Indra, all our ancestors, the singers, have found all desirable things;
with you are the cows that yield milk well, and with you the horses; you are the one who most effectively wins wealth for the seeker of the gods.
For like a king, you shall dwell among your subjects; as a wise seer, protect us through the days.
O Maghavan, sharpen our songs with cattle and horses; as one who loves us, impel us toward wealth.
These delightful songs, vying with one another here, have approached you, seeking the gods.
May your path to wealth come hither; may we abide in your favor and protection, O Indra.

Like one desiring to milk a cow in a field rich with grass, Vasiṣṭha has sent forth his prayers toward you. Indeed, all people call you my lord of cattle; may Indra come hither to our benevolent favor.
Even the vast waters that had spread out, Indra made them shallow and easy to cross for Sudās.
For the bold Śimyu, the new hymn of praise brought about the curse and the curses of the rivers.
Puroḷā and Turvaśa were eager for the sacrifice; like fish in shallow water, the Matsyas were intent upon wealth.
The Bhṛgus and Druhyus showed obedience; as a friend, he helped his friend across the two opposing sides.
The Pakthas, Bhalānasas, Alināsas, and Viṣāṇins have come, they who are auspicious;
he who led them as a companion of the Ārya has come through battle to the Tṛtsus for the sake of cattle and men.
Those of evil intent, causing Aditi to flow away, mindless, have seized the Paruṣṇī.
Ruling over the earth with his greatness, the seer lay watching over the cattle.
They went for gain, not for loss; even the swift one did not reach the Paruṣṇī.
Indra subdued Sudās’s well-impelled enemies, those of emasculated speech, among the human race.
They have gone forth like cattle from the pasture without a herdsman, gathering toward their friend as they please;
with spotted kine, sent forth by the Spotted One, the teams and the chariots have rendered obedience.
The King who, out of desire for glory, cast down one and twenty people of the two Vaikarṇas;
like a skillful priest at the sacrificial seat, he trimmed the sacred grass, and the Hero Indra made their release.
Then the thunderbolt-armed one cast down the famous Kavaṣa, grown old in the waters, along with the Druhyu.
Here, those who sought your friendship and rejoiced following you chose you for their alliance.
Indra instantly shattered all their strongholds; with his might, he demolished the seven fortresses.
He won back the household of the Anu for the Tṛtsu; may we conquer Pūru, the speaker of insults, in the assembly.
The Gavyas, Anavas, and Druhyus—sixty hundred and six thousand—have fallen asleep;
sixty heroes and six more have succumbed through their own arrogance. All these were the heroic deeds performed by Indra.
Impelled by Indra, these Tr̥tsus, acting with zeal, rushed downward like released waters.
Measuring out their steps, the ill-disposed and boastful ones abandoned all their provisions to Sudās.
Indra drove away the defiant one who drank the cooked offering but was not Indra’s own; he cast that hero’s half down to the earth.
Indra, the master of the path, measured out his fury against the furious one and took possession of the track.
By that one [deed], even with the weak he achieved that; even the lioness he struck down with a ram.
Indra cut away the corners of the dwelling for the householder; he bestowed all enjoyments upon Sudās.
For all your enemies have indeed submitted to you; find the weak point even of the defiant Bheda.
O Indra, hurl your sharp thunderbolt down upon him who treats those mortals who praise you so cruelly.
The Yamunā and the Tr̥tsus aided Indra; here he stripped Bheda of all his possessions.
The Ajas, the Śigrus, and the Yakṣvas brought him tribute: they carried off horses with their heads.
O Indra, your favors and your riches cannot be fully surveyed, whether ancient or new like the dawns.
You slew even Devaka who thought himself great; you yourself shattered Śambara from on high.
Those who, out of devotion to you, have rejoiced from their homes—Parāśara, Śatayātu, and Vasiṣṭha—let them not forget the friendship of you, the Bhoja; then may fair days dawn for the patrons.
Two hundred cattle from the grandson of Devavat, two chariots with brides from Sudās—
deserving of the gift of Paijavana, O Agni, I go around the assembly like a Hotṛ priest, chanting.
The four gifts of Paijavana, accompanied by well-disposed attendants and adorned with pearls, are set apart for me;
the bay steeds of Sudās, standing upon the earth, carry my offspring to fame for the sake of our progeny.
He whose fame lies between the two wide worlds, who has distributed it as a portion for every head;
him, Indra, the seven rivers praise like flowing streams; he has sharpened his weapon for the combat in the encounter.
O Maruts, O heroes, follow this Divodāsa as a father follows his son;
favor the intention of Paijavana; grant him dominion that is difficult to overcome, undecaying, and worthy of worship.
He who, like a fearsome bull with sharpened horns, alone causes all the peoples to tremble;
you who are the one who bestows the wealth of every non-offering man upon him who presses the soma most excellently.
O Indra, you indeed protected Kutsa in that battle, listening with your own person;
for you, desiring to help the son of Arjuni, subjected the Dāsa Śuṣṇa and Kuyava to him.
O bold one, with your boldness you have protected Sudās, whose oblations were accepted, with all your aids;
you protected Trasadasyu, the son of Purukutsa, and Pūru at the winning of land and in the slayings of Vṛtra.
O you whose mind is directed toward men, O Lord of the bay horses, you slay many Vṛtras at the banquet for the gods with your heroic followers.
You sent the Dasyus Cumuri and Dhuni to sleep, making them easy to slay for Dabhīti.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, those were thy mighty exploits when thou instantly [overthrewest] ninety-nine forts;
thou didst enter the hundredth for thy dwelling, and thou didst slay Vṛtra and Namuci.
Ancient indeed are those enjoyments of yours, O Indra, granted to the liberal Sudās who offers oblations.
For you, the bull, I yoke the two vigorous bay steeds; may our prayers reach you, O most powerful one, and win us strength.

O Lord of power, O Lord of bay horses, let us not fall into misfortune through you in this encounter; do not deliver us over to the wicked. Protect us with your safe defenses, and may we remain dear to you among the patrons.
O Maghavan, may we men, as your dear friends, rejoice in your favor and under your protection.
Subdue Turvaśa and Yadu; you who intend to perform a praiseworthy deed for Atithigva, sharpen your weapons.
O Maghavan, even now, in your favor, men who recite hymns proclaim their songs of praise.
You who, through your invocations, have scattered the Paṇis—choose us for that very alliance.
O most heroic of men, these hymns of praise from us are directed toward you, offering gifts;
O Indra, be a gracious friend to them in the slaying of Vṛtra, a brave protector and helper of men.
Now, O heroic Indra, being praised for your aid, strengthened by our prayer, increase yourself in body.
Bestow upon us strengths and subjects; do you all protect us always with blessings.
Fierce and self-reliant, he was born for heroic valor; the manly one made the waters flow as he prepared to act.
The youth has come with his aids to the assembly of men; O Indra, you are our protector even from great sin.
Indra, waxing mighty, shall slay Vṛtra; the Hero has indeed protected the singer with his aid.
He has indeed created wide space for Sudās, and he has repeatedly become the giver of wealth to the donor.

Fighting, irresistible, stirring up conflict, ever-victorious, a hero, a conqueror from birth, invincible— Indra, possessing innate strength, has scattered the hostile armies and has then struck down every foe who acts as an enemy.
O Indra, mighty one, you have filled both worlds with your greatness and your powers;
Indra, the lord of bay horses, brandishing his thunderbolt, has proclaimed himself at the exhilaration of the soma-juice.
The Bull begat the Bull for the sake of battle; him indeed, the manly one, the woman brought forth.
He who stands as a leader of armies for men, an unassailable warrior, a seeker of cattle—he is the bold one.
Never indeed does that person falter, nor shall he suffer harm, who seeks to win over his formidable mind;
he who offers worship with sacrifices and pays homage to Indra, being a guardian of Truth and born of Truth, shall rule over wealth.
O Indra, when you, the elder, bestowing aid upon the younger, gave a gift to one less than yourself;
as the Immortal One, you remained far away. O Wondrous One, bring us wondrous wealth!
O Indra, wielder of the stone, that dear person who offers gifts to you shall be your exclusive friend.
May we be most highly favored by this benevolence of yours, and may we abide in the protection and the hero-guarding care of you, the unslayable one.
This hymn has cried out to you as a bull; and it has reached its goal, O Maghavan, for it has entreated you.
The desire for wealth has come upon your singer; therefore, O Śakra, do you indeed help us toward riches.
O Indra, grant him nourishment through your favor—both him and those liberal patrons who themselves incite us.
May your power be truly beneficial to the singer; and do you all protect us evermore with your blessings.
The divine juice, mixed with milk, has been pressed; Indra has taken pleasure in it from his very birth.
We awaken you, O Lord of the bay horses, with sacrifices; take notice of our hymn in the exhilaration of the soma-juice.
They go forth to the sacrifice, they spread the sacrificial grass; drinking Soma at the assembly, they are loud-voiced.
They are brought down from the grasp of glory—those far-resounding bulls who seek after men.
O Indra, you made the many waters flow, which had been obstructed by the serpent, O Hero;
at your roar, all artificial fortifications trembled in fear, like chariot-steeds, and the rivers surged forth.
The terrible Indra, knowing all manly deeds, seized them with his weapons; exulting, he shattered their fortresses and struck them down with his might, the thunderbolt in his hand.
Neither sorcerers, O Indra, nor those who praise us with their knowledge have incited us against you, O most powerful one.
May he [the enemy] prevail over the hostile person; let not those who worship the phallus obstruct our sacred law.
O Indra, you have surpassed all by your wisdom upon the earth; the realms of space cannot encompass your greatness.
For with your own power you struck down Vṛtra; no enemy could find the end of you in battle.
Even the ancient gods yielded their powers to your divine sovereignty;
Indra, having overcome all, distributes riches. Men invoke Indra for the winning of booty.
For even the lowly man has called upon you for aid, O Indra, lord of abundant prosperity.
You have become our protector, O you of a hundredfold help; you are the defender of one such as we who bestows gifts.

O Indra, may we always be your friends, increasing your glory through our homage, O deliverer by your greatness! May they indeed overcome the enemy’s assault with your protection in the encounter, and may they subdue the might of those who seek to conquer us.
O Indra, grant him nourishment through your protection—both him and those liberal patrons who themselves incite us;
may your power be truly beneficial to the singer. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Drink the Soma, O Indra; let that which the stone has pressed for you exhilarate you, well-guided by the arms of the presser like a war-horse.
O Indra, Lord of the Bay Steeds, let that exhilarating draught of yours which is worthy and pleasing— that by which you slay the Vṛtras—
intoxicate you, O Indra, Lord of abundant wealth.
O Maghavan, take heed of this speech of mine, this hymn of praise which Vasiṣṭha recites for you;
enjoy these sacred prayers at our shared banquet.
Hear the call of the pressing-stone as it drinks; take notice of the inspired thought of the chanting sage. Accept these most intimate acts of devotion; may we be united with them.
I do not forget your songs, nor the well-spoken praise of you, the swift Asura; knowing this, I ever proclaim your name, O self-glorious one.
For many are your libations among men; the wise man calls upon you alone.
O Maghavan, do not delay long against us.
For you alone, O Hero, are all these libations; for you I fashion these strengthening prayers.
You are to be invoked by men at all times.
O Dasyuh-slayer, O fierce Indra, even now they do not attain the greatness of you who are so esteemed;
neither your heroic power nor your bounty, O Indra.
Those seers of old and those who are now, O Indra, the inspired poets who have generated sacred prayers—may your auspicious friendships be with us. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
The sacred hymns have risen up, seeking glory; O Vasiṣṭha, magnify Indra in the assembly.
He who has extended all things with his might—he shall hear the words of one such as me.
The cry has been raised, O Indra, born of the gods, as you exercise sovereignty over the spoils in the contest;
for among men one’s own life-span is not known—carry us across those very straits.
I harness the booty-seeking chariot with the two bay steeds; my prayers have reached him who accepts them with favor.
By his greatness, Indra forced asunder the two worlds, he who struck down the Vṛtras without opposition.

Even the waters have swelled like barren cows; your singers, O Indra, have reached the Eternal Order (*ṛta*). Come toward us as Vāyu with his teams of horses, for through our prayers you distribute the spoils of victory.
May these exhilarating draughts delight you, O Indra, the impetuous one who bestows abundant wealth upon the singer.
For you alone among the gods take pity on mortals; O hero, rejoice at this libation.

Thus do the Vasiṣṭhas praise with hymns Indra, the bull whose arm wields the thunderbolt; may he, being lauded, grant us wealth in heroes and cattle. Do you all protect us evermore with your blessings.

A seat has been prepared for you, O Indra, in this dwelling; come to it with your men, O much-invoked one! So that you may be our protector and increase us, grant us riches and rejoice in the Soma juices.
O Indra, of double strength, your mind has been captured; the Soma is pressed, the sweet juices are poured out.
This well-fashioned hymn, a prayer that calls aloud to Indra, brings forth its voice with released milk.
From heaven and from earth, O drinker of the *ṛjīṣa*, come to this sacred grass (*barhis*) for the drinking of Soma.
Let your bay steeds carry you toward me, toward our song of praise, you who are powerful, for the sake of exhilaration.
Come to us with all your aids, O Lord of the Bay Horses, being well-pleased and enjoying our prayer; turning toward us with your steadfast [steeds], O fair-cheeked Indra, bestow upon us manly vigor.
This hymn has been offered for the great and fierce one, like a horse yoked to the pole striving for the prize;
O Indra, this song praises you for wealth—place our renown high above the heavens, even as heaven itself.
Thus, O Indra, fill us with what is desirable; may we find for ourselves your great favor.
Swell the nourishment rich in heroes for our patrons; and do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Indra, when the armies clash with equal fervor, let your great and fierce power arise;
let the lightning bolt fly from the arms of the hero—let not your mind wander away in every direction.
O Indra, strike down our enemies in difficult places—those mortals who assail us. Drive that curse of the reviler far away; bring us an abundance of riches.
O fair-cheeked one, a hundred aids are yours for Sudās; let there be a thousand praises and let your bounty be granted.
Strike down the weapon of the envious mortal; bestow upon us splendor and treasure.
For I belong to one such as you, O Indra, in wisdom; I belong to one such as you, O Hero, in the granting of aid.
Make every day a home for me, O fierce Lord of the Bay Horses, mighty and full of power; do not neglect me!
These Kutsas have offered strength to Indra, the lord of bay horses—strength impelled by the gods.
O Hero, make the Vṛtras easy to slay; may we, as conquerors, win the prize.
Thus, O Indra, fill us with what is desirable; may we find your great favor.
Swell the nourishment rich in heroes for our patrons; and do you all protect us evermore with blessings.
Unpressed Soma has never exhilarated Indra, nor have pressed juices without prayer delighted the Bounteous Lord.
Therefore, I generate a hymn that he may enjoy—a newer song, like a hero—and so that he may hear us.
At every hymn, Soma has gladdened Indra; at every chant, the pressed juices have exhilarated Maghavan.
When, pressing him hard like sons their father, they of one mind call upon him for aid.
He has performed those deeds, and he shall surely perform others now, which the wise proclaim during the libations.
Like a single common husband among his wives, Indra has brought all the fortresses under his control.
Thus they speak of him, and Indra himself hears it: he alone is the distributor of riches, the swift one whose many aids come one after another; may his dear and auspicious blessings attend us.
Thus Vasiṣṭha praises Indra, the bull of the peoples, for the aid of men at the pressing of the juice.
Bestow upon us thousandfold spoils; do you all protect us always with your blessings.
The men call upon Indra at the turning point of the race, when they harness those prayers that lead to the further shore.
O Hero, eager for strength in the battle for men, grant us a share in the stall rich in cattle.
O Indra, Maghavan, whatever vigor is yours, bestow it upon us, your friends, O you who are invoked by many;
for you, O Maghavan, are the wise one who breaks down even firm things—open up the enclosed bounty like a treasure.

Indra is the king of the world and of the peoples upon the earth; from that which exists in its manifold forms, he bestows riches upon the donor. May he, being praised, impel his bounty hitherward toward us.
Now indeed, may the bounteous Indra, when invoked together with us, bestow strength upon us for his aid—
he whose perfect sacrificial fee has overflowed, bringing desirable wealth to the men and to his friends.
Now, O Indra, grant us wide space for the sake of wealth; may we turn your mind toward us for the sake of bounty.
Desiring cattle, horses, and chariots, [we approach you]; do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Indra, come to us as a priest, you who are wise; let your bay steeds be harnessed and turned hitherward.
For all mortals indeed invoke you; hear us, O you who impel all things!
O Indra, your greatness has reached our invocation, since you, O mighty one, protect the sacred prayer of the seers.
When you, O fierce one, took the thunderbolt in your hand, being terrible yet invincible, you were born through your own power of will.
Under your guidance, O Indra, you have brought together the two worlds, like men who call upon you in prayer;
for you were born for great dominion and power, and the impetuous one has made even the non-impetuous swift.
O Indra, favor us with these days, for the peoples who are ill-disposed are being purified.
May Varuṇa, the master of wondrous power, protect us from the falsehood that the guileless one perceives against us in two ways.

We would speak to this Maghavan Indra, so that he may grant us great wealth and bounty; he who is the most helpful to the one who praises him and performs sacred prayer. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Indra, Lord of the Bay Steeds, this Soma is pressed for you; come hither, for that is your home.
Drink of this well-pressed, exhilarating juice, O Maghavan, bestowing riches upon us as we entreat you.
O Brahman, O Hero, enjoying this act of prayer, come quickly hither with your bay steeds;
at this very libation, rejoice, and listen to these our prayers.
What satisfaction do you find in our hymns? When indeed, O Maghavan, shall we serve you?
I have stretched out all my thoughts toward you; therefore, O Indra, hear these my invocations.
And indeed, those men of old were truly yours, of whom you heard, the ancient seers;
therefore, O Maghavan, I call upon you repeatedly—you, O Indra, are our providence, like a father.
Let us address this Maghavan Indra, so that he may grant us great wealth and bounty—he who is most helpful to the singer’s prayerful devotion. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Come to us, O God, with your power, O impetuous one; be the increaser of this wealth, O Indra.
For the sake of great manly valor, O Lord of Men, wielder of the fair thunderbolt, and for the sake of great dominion and heroic strength, O Hero.
The heroes invoke you, the one to be invoked, in the clash of battle for their own bodies, in the winning of the sun;
you are the one to be honored by all people as their army-leader—make the Vṛtras easy to slay.
O Indra, when the days dawn with fair weather, and you set up the foremost banner in battles,
Agni sits down like a sovereign Hotṛ-priest, calling the gods here for the sake of prosperity.
O Indra, we and those gods who praise you, O Hero, as they bestow riches—grant to our patrons the highest protection; may they, being self-sustaining, attain long life.

Let us address this Maghavan Indra, so that he may grant us great wealth and bounty; he who is the most helpful protector of the one who praises him and performs sacred prayer. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O friends, sing forth a gladdening song for Indra, the lord of the bay horses, for him who drinks the Soma.
O bounteous ones, let us recite the hymn of praise, just as men have done for you who dwell in heaven, so that we may act for him whose wealth is true.
O Indra, you are the seeker of booty for us; O Śatakratu, you are the seeker of cattle;
O Vāsas, you are the seeker of gold.
O Indra, O Bull, we who are devoted to you cry out to you;
know this of us, O Vasu.
Do not deliver us to reproach or to the censure of the stingy enemy;
for my mental power is centered in you.
You are a wide-spreading armor and a warrior fighting in the van, O slayer of Vṛtra;
with you as my ally, I speak in response.
And you are great, O Indra, whose conquering power the two self-sustaining worlds, heaven and earth, acknowledge.
May that voice, accompanied by the Maruts, encompass you—
moving along with us and reaching toward the days of light.
The drops, rising upward toward heaven, have followed you, the wondrous one;
all the peoples bow down before you.
Bring forth [the hymn] for the great one who increases the great; offer your devotion to the wise one. Go forth to the many clans, O you who fill the people!
For Indra, the wide-extending and mighty one, the sages have generated a hymn and a prayer;
the wise do not violate his sacred laws.
The voices have established Indra alone as the king, he whose wrath is unsurpassed, so that he may prevail;
for the lord of the bay horses, strengthen his allies.
Let not even the priests detain you far from us;
come to our feast even from afar, or, being here, listen to us.
For these prayers of ours, fashioned as sacred words, sit beside you at the pressed juice like bees at honey;
desiring wealth, the singers have placed their desire upon Indra like a foot upon a chariot.
Desiring wealth, I call upon the wielder of the thunderbolt, the one with the excellent right hand, as a son calls upon his father.
These Soma juices, mixed with curds, have been pressed for Indra.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, come to our home with your two bay steeds to drink them for exhilaration.
Hearing us, he whose ears are quick to hear comes for our wealth; may he never neglect our hymns. He who bestows hundreds and thousands at once—no one can restrain him when he wishes to give.
That hero, irresistible, has flourished through Indra and through men—
he who, O Vṛtra-slayer, presses out your deep libations and pours them forth.
O Maghavan, be the protector of our patrons when you encounter the defiant;
may we share in the wealth of him whom you have struck down. Bring us a home that is difficult for others to attain.
Press the Soma for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, who drinks the Soma;
cook the cooked offerings for his protection. Truly, he who bestows gifts brings joy to the one who gives.
Do not falter, O Soma-pressers; be skillful for the great [deed]. Make yourselves ready to win great wealth.
Only the one who perseveres conquers; he dwells in peace and prospers. The gods do not favor the one who is stingy.
No one has obstructed the chariot of Sudās, nor has anyone caused it to halt;
he whom Indra protects and whom the Maruts favor shall go to a stall full of cattle.
May that mortal win booty, O Indra, seeking booty, for whom you have become a protector;
be the protector of our chariots, O Hero, and of our men.
Now his portion overflows like the wealth of a victor;
him who is Indra, the Lord of Bay Steeds, no enemies can deceive. He bestows skill upon the Soma-presser.
Place within those worthy of sacrifice a mantra that is not deficient, well-established, and beautifully formed.
Even many snares do not overcome him who stands by Indra through his ritual action.
O Indra, what mortal dares to challenge him who has you as his protector?
O Maghavan, it is through faith in you that the seeker of booty strives to win the prize on the decisive day.
In the slayings of Vṛtra, urge on those generous patrons who bestow beloved wealth;
under your guidance, O Lord of Tawny Steeds, may we, together with our noble patrons, cross over all difficulties.
Thine, O Indra, is the lowest wealth; thou nourishest the middle;
truly, thou rulest over all that is highest; no one holds thee back from the cattle.
You are renowned as the giver of wealth to everyone; whatever victories there may be, they belong to you.
O much-invoked one, this entire earthly world, seeking your protection, begs for your name.
O Indra, if I were the master of as much wealth as you possess, I would surely provide for my singer; O dispenser of riches, I would grant him gifts so that he never falls into misery.
I would bestow wealth upon the one who magnifies me day after day, wherever he may be found;
for there is no kinship better than yours, O Maghavan—not even a father.
The one who crosses over desires to win the prize with Purandhi as his companion. I bend Indra, who is invoked by many, toward you with my song, just as a carpenter bends a well-fashioned felly.
A mortal does not find wealth through ill-praise; riches do not reach the one who falters.
O Maghavan, for one such as I, your gift is truly powerful on the decisive day.
O Hero, we cry out to you like unmilked cows,
to you, O Indra, the lord of this moving world, the beholder of heaven, the lord of all that stands still.
None other like you exists—neither among the dwellers of heaven nor upon earth; none has been born, nor shall ever be born.
O Indra, Maghavan, desiring horses and seeking cattle, we who are seekers of strength call upon you.
Bring that wealth toward us, O Indra, from the younger than the elder;
for you, O Maghavan, have been rich in many treasures from of old, and are to be invoked in every battle.
Drive away our enemies, O Maghavan; make riches easy for us to find. Be our protector in the great contest for wealth; be the strengthener of your friends.
O Indra, bring us wisdom, just as a father provides for his sons. O Much-invoked One, grant us aid on this journey; living, may we attain the light.
Let not unknown, malevolent, or unpropitious powers step upon us.
O Hero, with your aid we shall cross over the many flowing waters.
White-robed, with braided hair on the right, the inspirers of prayer have indeed gladdened me.
Rising from the sacred grass, I say to the men: "The Vasiṣṭhas are not far off to protect me."
From afar they brought Indra hither with the pressed juice, past the Vaiśanta pool, beyond the fierce drinker.
From the pressed soma of Pāśadyumna Vāyata, Indra chose the Vasiṣṭhas.
Verily, with these [Maruts] he crossed the river; verily, with these he slew Bheda.
Verily, O Vasiṣṭhas, it was through your sacred prayer that Indra protected Sudās in the battle of the ten kings.
O men, through the sacred prayer (*brahman*) of our fathers, you have pleased [the gods] for their favor; your axle has not failed, nor indeed shall you come to harm.
Since you, O Vasiṣṭhas, with a great roar among the *śakvarī* verses, have bestowed vigor upon Indra.
Like thirsty men gazing up at heaven, they, being hemmed in during the battle of the ten kings, looked out in their distress.
Indra heard Vasiṣṭha as he praised him; he made wide room for the Tritsus.
Like sticks, the Bharatas were cut down like cattle and became weak;
Vasiṣṭha became their leader, and then the tribes of the Tṛtsus spread abroad.
Three create seed within the worlds; three are the noble progeny, whose forefront is light. Three heats accompany the Dawn; all these the Vasiṣṭhas know.
Their radiance is like the growth of the sun; their greatness is as profound as the ocean. Like the speed of the wind, O Vasiṣṭhas, your hymn of praise cannot be followed by any other.
By means of the insights of their hearts, they move toward that secret which has a thousand branches;
weaving the enclosure spread out by Yama, the Vasiṣṭhas have approached the Apsarases.
When Mitra and Varuṇa beheld you emerging from the lightning’s light,
that was one of your births, O Vasiṣṭha, when Agastya brought you to the people.
And you, O Vasiṣṭha, are the son of Mitra and Varuṇa, born from the mind of Urvaśī through divine prayer.
All the gods received you, the fallen drop, with divine prayer upon the lotus leaf.
He, the perceiver who knows both worlds, the giver of thousands or indeed of all—
Vasiṣṭha was born from the Apsarases, about to weave the thread stretched out by Yama.
Born at the sacrifice, impelled by adorations, the two poured forth their common seed into the jar.
From its midst Māna arose; from that, they say, the seer Vasiṣṭha was born.
He who bears the bearer of the *uktha* and the bearer of the *sāman*, bearing the pressing-stone, speaks first.
Approach him with a well-disposed mind; Vasiṣṭha, the piercer, shall come to you.
May the divine inspired thought, well-fashioned by us, go forth from us like a swift chariot.
They know the origin of the earth and of heaven; the waters listen as they flow.
Even the broad waters swell for him; among the Vṛtras, the fierce heroes consider themselves mighty.
Place the horses at his poles; he is Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, whose arms are golden.
Like a charioteer setting forth toward the sacrifice, like a traveler on his way, urge yourselves forward by your own power.
By yourselves, speed the sacrifice in battles; establish a banner, a hero for the people.
From his vital strength the light has emerged; he bears the burden as the earth bears the world.
O Agni, free from sorcery, I invoke the gods; performing the rite according to the Truth, I fashion this prayer.
Direct your divine thought toward us; send forth your speech among the gods.
Varuṇa, the fierce one with a thousand eyes, beholds the course of these rivers.
King of kingdoms, ornament of rivers—may he extend his sovereign power over all life.
Protect us in all communities; make the curse of the one who seeks to harm us powerless.
Let the malevolent bolt of those who hate us pass away; drive far in every direction the affliction that harms our bodies.
May Agni carry our oblations with our reverences; this most beloved hymn has been offered to him.
In harmony with the gods, make the Son of the Waters your friend; may he be auspicious to us.
With hymns I praise Ahi, the water-born, who sits at the base of the rivers in the mid-regions.
May the Dragon of the Deep not deliver us to harm; may the sacrifice of this seeker of Truth not fail.
And may they bestow glory upon these men of ours; may the noble ones, exulting, advance toward wealth.
They scorch the enemy like the sun upon the earth; they possess great armies and strike with their terrors.
When our wives come hither to us, may Tvaṣṭṛ, the skillful-handed, bestow heroic sons upon us.
May Tvaṣṭṛ accept our hymn; may Aramati, seeking wealth, be with us.
May they, bestowing gifts, grant us treasures; may Rodasī and Varuṇānī hear us.
May Tvaṣṭṛ, providing excellent refuge with his protectresses, be our benefactor; may he, the bounteous giver, distribute riches to us.
May the mountains grant us that wealth, may the waters, the plants that accompany the gifts, and the sky grant it;
may the earth in harmony with the lords of the forest, and both heaven and earth, protect us on every side.
May the two vast worlds, heaven and earth, yield to that; may Varuṇa, dwelling in heaven and having Indra as his friend, yield;
and may all the Maruts, who are full of power, yield. May we be the sustainers of wealth so that we may offer our prayers.
May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, the waters, the plants, and the trees take pleasure in this.
May we be in the protection and the lap of the Maruts. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
May Indra and Agni be auspicious to us with their protections; may Indra and Varuṇa, to whom oblations are offered, be auspicious to us.
May Indra and Soma be for our well-being, for peace and health; may Indra and Pūṣan be auspicious to us in the winning of booty.
May Bhaga be auspicious to us, and may our praise be auspicious; may Purandhi be auspicious to us, and may riches be auspicious.
May the praise of the true and well-governed be auspicious to us, and may Aryaman, born of many, be auspicious to us.
May the Ordainer be auspicious to us, and may the Sustainer be auspicious to us; may the far-reaching [Earth] be auspicious to us with her self-sustaining powers.
May the two vast worlds, Heaven and Earth, be auspicious, may the mountain be auspicious to us, and may the propitious invocations of the gods be auspicious to us.
May Agni, with his face of light, be auspicious to us; may Mitra and Varuṇa and the Aśvins be auspicious to us.
May the good deeds of the doers of good be auspicious to us; may the swift wind blow auspiciously upon us.
May Heaven and Earth be auspicious for us at our first invocation; may the intermediate space be propitious for us to behold.
May the plants and the trees be auspicious for us; may the victorious Lord of the Atmosphere be auspicious for us.
May the god Indra with the Vasus be auspicious to us; may Varuṇa, the one of fair praise, together with the Ādityas, be auspicious.
May the healing Rudra with the Rudras be auspicious to us; may Tvaṣṭṛ with the divine dames hear us here for our well-being.
May Soma be auspicious to us, may the sacred prayer be auspicious to us; may the pressing-stones be auspicious to us, and may the sacrifices be auspicious.
May the felling of the sacrificial posts be auspicious to us, may the plants be auspicious to us, and may the altar be auspicious to us.
May the far-seeing Sūrya rise for our welfare; may the four quarters of space be auspicious for us.
May the firm mountains be auspicious for us, and may the rivers and the waters be auspicious for us.
May Aditi be auspicious to us through her sacred laws; may the Maruts, who sing beautiful hymns, be auspicious to us.
May Viṣṇu be auspicious to us, and may Pūṣan be auspicious to us; may our protection be auspicious, and may Vāyu be auspicious to us.
May the divine Savitṛ, our protector, be auspicious to us; may the dawns as they shine forth be auspicious to us.
May Parjanya be auspicious to our progeny, and may the Lord of the Field be a bringer of well-being to us.

May the gods, the Viśvedevas, be auspicious to us; may Sarasvatī, together with our prayers, be auspicious. May those who accompany us be auspicious, and may those who grant gifts be auspicious; may the celestial ones, the terrestrial ones, and the waters be auspicious to us.
May the lords of truth be auspicious to us; may our coursers be auspicious and our cattle be auspicious.
May the Ṛbhus, the skillful-handed doers of good deeds, be auspicious to us; may the fathers be auspicious to us in our invocations.

May the god Aja Ekapād be auspicious to us; may Ahi Budhnya be auspicious to us, and the ocean be auspicious. May Apām Napāt, the protector, be auspicious to us; may Pṛśni, whose guardians are the gods, be auspicious to us.
May the Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus take pleasure in this newly performed prayer;
may the celestial ones, the terrestrial ones, those born of the cow, and those worthy of sacrifice hear us.

Those among the gods who are worthy of sacrifice, who are the most worshipful among those worthy of sacrifice, who are honored by Manu, immortal, and knowers of the *ṛta*—may they grant us wide-striding space today; and may you all protect us always with your blessings.
Let the sacred prayer proceed from the seat of Cosmic Order; Sūrya has released the cows with his rays.
The wide earth has spread out with her ridges; Agni has been kindled upon her broad surface.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, O Asuras, I fashion this newest hymn for you two like strengthening food.
One of you is a powerful, infallible leader; and Mitra, speaking, stirs the people.
The arrivals of the rushing wind have come to rest; like milch-cows, the sweet juices have overflowed. Being born in the seat of the great heaven, the bull has bellowed in this very udder.

O Indra, with my song I would yoke those two beloved, swift, and well-charioted bay horses of yours, O hero, which frustrate the wrath of the one who seeks to harm. May I turn hither Aryaman, the one of perfect wisdom.
Those who offer homage worship his friendship and vital strength in the very seat of the Eternal Order (*ṛta*).
Praised by men, he has distributed nourishments; this most beloved homage is for Rudra.
When the glorious ones, lowing together, come—Sarasvatī, the seventh, whose mother is the Sindhu;
they who flow well, easy to milk, with good streams, swelling with their own milk.

And may those Maruts, being exhilarated, protect our prayer and our offspring, O you who possess strength; let not the moving, imperishable [waters] pass us by. May they increase for us that wealth which is worthy of our alliance.

Bring forward for yourselves the great Aramati; bring forward Pūṣan, like a hero fit for the assembly; [bring forward] Bhaga, the protector of this our prayer, Vāja who bestows gifts, and Purandhi, for the winning of booty.

O Maruts, may this song of praise reach you, and may it reach Viṣṇu, the protector of the poured libation, with his aids. And may they bestow vigor upon the singer for the sake of progeny. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Vājās and R̥bhukṣans, let your most swift and unassailable chariot bring you hither to be praised.
At the libations, with the triple-backed Soma juices, fill yourselves for exhilaration, O fair-cheeked ones, with your great [powers].
O R̥bhukṣans, you who behold the light of heaven, you bestow unimpaired treasure upon the liberal patrons;
O self-dependent ones, drink together at the sacrifices and distribute riches to us through our prayers.
For you have granted a gift, O Maghavan, at the distribution of wealth, both great and small;
both your hands are full of riches, and your bounty does not withhold its treasures.
O Indra, you are self-glorious, the lord of the *Ṛbhus*, like a successful prize; singing hymns, come home to us.
May we, the Vasiṣṭhas, be your givers, performing sacred prayer for you, O Lord of the Bay Steeds.
You shall win the heights even for the donor, O Lord of the Bay Steeds, through those prayers with which you have exerted yourself.
We have indeed won by your allied aids; when, O Indra, will you grant us wealth?
O Indra, you seem to cause us, the wise ones, to dwell [in security]; when will you take notice of our speech?
May the prize-winning steed, through our ancestral prayer, bring hither wealth with brave sons and nourishing food for us.
Even though the goddess Nirṛti has power over him, may the autumns rich in nourishment reach Indra;
may he, whose kin are threefold, attain old age, even though mortals have made him homeless.
O Savitṛ, may gifts be praised for us; may the riches of Parvata come to us in their bounty.
May the divine protector ever attend to us. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Upward has this god Savitṛ extended the golden radiance which he has sent forth;
now indeed is Bhaga to be invoked by men, he who, possessing abundant wealth, distributes treasures.
Arise, O Savitṛ, and hear this, O golden-handed one, at the presentation of the sacred rite.
Casting forth your far-reaching and wide-spread splendor, bestow upon men the food that sustains mortals.
May the god Savitṛ be praised, he whom all the Vasus indeed extol. May he, worthy of homage, accept our hymns with favor; may he protect our patrons with all his guardians.
Him whom the goddess Aditi praises, taking pleasure in the impulse of the god Savitṛ;
him whom Varuṇa the sovereign, Mitra, and Aryaman praise in unison.
May those who, vying with one another, bestow gifts from heaven and earth—those who follow the path of giving—and may Ahi Budhnya hear us; may Varūtrī protect us along with the Ekadhenu cows.
May the Lord of the Family, being entreated, grant us that treasure of the god Savitṛ.
The powerful one calls upon Bhaga for protection; even the weak man seeks Bhaga and attains his treasure.
May the Vājins be auspicious for us in our invocations at the assembly of the gods—those who run their measured course, the well-praising ones.
Crushing the serpent, the wolf, and the demons, may they drive away all diseases far from us.
In every contest for booty, O swift steeds, protect us; you who are wise, immortal, and knowers of the Eternal Order.
Drink of this honeyed mead and rejoice; being satisfied, go by the paths traveled by the gods.
Agni, rising up, has established the favor of the Vasus; his glowing flame goes forth toward the assembly of the gods.
The two pressing-stones have taken their path like charioteers; may the Hotṛ, impelled, sacrifice for us according to the Eternal Law (Ṛta).
The sacrificial grass, easy to tread upon, has been spread out for them; like two lords of the people, they hasten to the assembly.
At the first invocation of the night and of the dawn, may Vāyu with his team and Pūṣan come for our well-being.
On this earth the Vasus, the gods, have taken delight; in the wide mid-air the radiant ones have purified themselves.
Turn your paths hitherward, O you of far-reaching course; hear this messenger of ours who has come.

For they, the worshipful protectors, are all the gods who attend the assembly at the sacrifices. O Agni, do thou sacrifice to them—the longing ones—at the rite: to Bhaga, the Nāsatyas, and Purandhi, with ready obedience.
O Agni, from heaven and from earth, bring hither Mitra, Varuṇa, Indra, and Agni;
bring Aryaman, Aditi, and Viṣṇu. May Sarasvatī and the Maruts rejoice in these offerings of theirs.
May the insatiable one reach the oblation of the worshipful ones with our prayers, fulfilling the desire of mortals;
may he bestow inexhaustible wealth upon us ever-conquering ones. May we now indeed be united with the allied gods.
Now may Rodasī, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni—the upholders of *ṛta*—be praised by the Vasiṣṭhas. May the radiant ones grant us the highest hymn of praise. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
May the willing obedience worthy of the assembly come together; let us offer our hymn of praise to the swift ones.
Whatever the god Savitṛ shall impel today, may we be present at the distribution of his treasures.

May Mitra, Varuṇa, the two worlds (Heaven and Earth), Indra, and Aryaman grant us that which is allotted by the gods. May the goddess Aditi assign us wealth, as well as that which Vāyu and Bhaga bestow.
O Maruts, let that mortal be fierce and powerful whom you, whose horses are speckled, protect;
and whom Agni and Sarasvatī impel—for him there is no one who can surpass his wealth.
For this Varuṇa is the leader of the *ṛta*, and Mitra, Aryaman, and the Waters have established them as kings.
May the goddess Aditi, who is easily invoked and invincible, carry us across distress unharmed.
At the offering of oblations to this bounteous god Viṣṇu, the swift one, may we find the Rudra-like majesty of Rudra; O Aśvins, come to our food-providing dwelling.
O glowing Pūṣan, let not the envious Varūtrī nor those who bestow gifts hold us back;
may the joy-bringing coursers protect us, and may the wind, wandering all around, grant us rain.
Now may Rodasī, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni—the upholders of Ṛta—be praised by the Vasiṣṭhas. May the radiant ones grant us our supreme hymn of praise. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
At dawn we invoke Agni; at dawn Indra; at dawn Mitra and Varuṇa; at dawn the Aśvins;
at dawn Bhaga, Pūṣan, and Brahmaṇaspati; at dawn we shall call upon Soma and Rudra.
Let us invoke the fierce Bhaga, the winner of the morning, the son of Aditi who is the distributor;
him whom even the weak-minded man, even the swift man, and even the king says, "May I partake of Bhaga."
O Bhaga, leader; O Bhaga, whose gifts are true; O Bhaga, favor this prayer and grant us wealth.
O Bhaga, increase us with cattle and horses; O Bhaga, may we be rich in men through our heroes.
And may we now be fortunate, both at the onset of the day and at its midpoint;
and at the rising of the sun, O Maghavan, may we abide in the benevolent favor of the gods.
O gods, let Bhaga alone be the blessed one; through him may we become blessed. O Bhaga, everyone calls upon you with fervent cries; as such, O Bhaga, be our leader here.
May the Dawns incline toward our sacrifices, as Dadhikrā does toward his pure station.
May they bring hither to us Bhaga, the finder of wealth, as spirited horses draw a chariot.
May the auspicious Dawns, rich in horses, cows, and heroes, shine upon us forever. Yielding clarified butter and overflowing on every side, do you protect us always with your blessings.
Let the Brahmans, the Aṅgirases, come forward; let the roar of the celestial cloud resound.
Let the cows swimming in the waters low aloud; let the two pressing-stones be yoked, the ornament of the sacrifice.

O Agni, your path is easy to traverse, discovered from of old; yoke for the pressed juice your bay and ruddy horses, or those ruddy steeds that carry heroes to the seat. Seated there, I invoke the generations of the gods.
I celebrate your sacrifice together with reverent salutations; may the delightful Hotṛ-priest excel in our presence.
Worship the gods, O you of many faces, and bring hither Aramati, who is worthy of sacrifice.
When Agni, the guest who lies on a comfortable bed, is made known within the house of the wealthy hero— well-pleased and well-established in the home— he bestows desirable wealth upon such a people.
O Agni, graciously accept this sacrifice of ours; bestow glory upon us among the Maruts and Indra.
Let Night and Dawn sit upon the sacred grass, and worship here Mitra and Varuṇa, who are well-disposed.
Thus has Vasiṣṭha, desiring wealth that nourishes all, praised the victorious Agni. May he extend to us food, riches, and strength; and may you all protect us evermore with your blessings.
At your sacrifices, those seeking the gods sing forth with adorations to Heaven and Earth so that they may grant us nourishment—
those for whom the peerless prayers of the inspired singers spread out in all directions like the branches of a tree.
Let the sacrifice go forth like a swift steed toward its goal; lift up with one mind the ladles dripping with ghee.
Spread the sacred grass well for the rite; the god-seeking flames have risen upright.

Like sons carried upon their mother’s back, let the gods sit upon the ridge of the sacrificial grass. Let the all-pervading goddess anoint the assembly; O Agni, do not neglect us in the presence of the gods.
Those worshipful ones have yielded themselves to our pleasure, milking the well-yielding streams of *ṛta*.
Today, come to your supreme greatness among the Vasus; come together with one mind, as many as you are.

Thus, O Agni, bestow your favor upon us among the people; through you, O powerful one, may we be closely united. May we, sharing our joy with wealth as our companion, remain unharmed. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
For your aid, I invoke Dadhikrā first, the Aśvins, the Dawn, the kindled Agni, and Bhaga;
Indra, Viṣṇu, Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, the Ādityas, Heaven and Earth, the Waters, and the Sun.
Awakening Dadhikrā with homage, rising up and proceeding toward the sacrifice,
seating the goddess Iḷā upon the sacrificial grass— we, the inspired singers, shall invoke the Aśvins who are easily summoned.
Having awakened Dadhikrāvan, Agni, Uṣas, Sūrya, and the Cow,
as well as the ruddy one of Mitra and the brown one of Varuṇa— may they all drive away all misfortunes from us.
Dadhikrāvan, the first prize-winning steed, comes forward at the head of the chariots, knowing the way;
he is in harmony with the Dawn, with Sūrya, with the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Aṅgirases.
May Dadhikrā anoint our path so that we may follow the way of Truth;
may Agni hear us, and may all the mighty, unerring gods hear us.
May the god Savitṛ, possessor of beautiful jewels, come through the mid-air, borne by his horses; holding many treasures for men in his hand, he settles the world and impels it forth.
His two great, supple arms, golden-hued, have reached to the ends of heaven. Surely that majesty of his must be praised; even the Sun yields to him in active power.
May that god Savitṛ, the powerful one, the lord of treasures, impel treasures for us. Spreading out his far-reaching radiance, may he then bestow upon us the food of mortals.

These songs praise Savitar, the fair-tongued one, whose arms are full and whose hands are skillful. May he bestow upon us wonderful and mighty vitality. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Bring these songs to Rudra, the god who possesses a firm bow, swift arrows, and self-sustaining power;
to the invincible, the conqueror, the wise ordainer, the wielder of sharp weapons—may he hear us.
For he, through his dominion over earthly birth and his sovereignty over celestial birth, takes heed of us.
O Rudra, come to our protecting doors with favor; be one who is free from disease among our offspring.
That bolt of yours which, hurled from heaven, courses across the earth—may it pass us by.
O you whose breath is like a thousandfold draught, may your remedies be ours; do not harm us among our children or our descendants.
Do not slay us, O Rudra, do not abandon us; let us not fall under the wrathful grasp of your anger.
Grant us a share in the sacrificial grass and in the praise of the living. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Waters, that wave of yours which those seeking the gods first made into the drink of Indra— may we today win that wave of yours, the pure, the stainless, the sprinkler of ghee, and the honey-sweet.
O Waters, may that wave of yours which is most rich in sweetness—may Apāṃ Napāt, the swift impeller, protect it—wherein Indra rejoices with the Vasus; may we, seeking the gods, attain that today.
Flowing through a hundred filters, rejoicing in their own inherent power, the goddesses go to the domain of the gods.
They do not violate the ordinances of Indra; offer an oblation rich in clarified butter to the rivers.
Those which Sūrya has stretched out with his rays, those for whom Indra carved a path and a wave—may you, O rivers, grant us wide space; and may you protect us always with your blessings.
O R̥bhukṣans, O Vājas, O heroes, you bounteous ones, rejoice in our pressed soma!
May your powers, like those who go toward us, turn your noble chariot hither, O Vibhus.
May we, as R̥bhu with the R̥bhus, be masters over you; as Vibhū with the Vibhūs, may we overcome powers with power.
May Vāja aid us in the winning of booty; with Indra as our ally, may we conquer Vṛtra.
For they indeed overcome many with their command; Indra, Vibhvan, R̥bhukṣan, and Vāja, conquering all the hostile power of the enemy, shall by their conflict scatter the manly strength of the foe.
Now, O gods, grant us wide space; may you all, being of one mind, be present for our protection.
May the Vasus bestow nourishment upon us; do you ever protect us with your blessings.
Led by the ocean, purifying themselves from the midst of the flood, they flow without ceasing;
may those divine waters, which Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt and bull, dug out, protect me here.
The waters that are celestial, or those that flow [from the mountains], those dug out by men, or those that are self-born;
those whose goal is the ocean, pure and purifying—may those divine waters protect me here.
In whose midst King Varuṇa moves, beholding the truth and falsehood of men—
those dripping with sweetness, pure and purifying— may those divine waters protect me here.
In whom King Varuṇa, in whom Soma, and in whom all the gods revel in strength;
in whom Agni Vaiśvānara has entered—may those divine waters protect me here.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, protect me here; let not the all-pervading, nest-making [evil] come upon us.
I cast away the ill-looking goat-footed one; let not the creeping thing find me with its foot-disease.

Whatever wound has formed upon the joint of the limb, let Agni, shining brightly, drive away from here— both from the two kneecaps and around the two ankles— and let not the creeping disease find me with its foot.

Whatever poison is in the *śalmali* tree, whatever is in the rivers, and whatever is born from the plants—may all the gods drive that away from here; let not the stalk of the plant find me with its foot-disease.

Those rivers which flow down, those which flow into hollows, those which flow upward, those which are full of water, and those which are waterless—may all those divine waters, swelling with milk for us, be auspicious and free from the *śipada* disease; may all the rivers be free from the *śimidā* disease.

Through the newest protection of the Ādityas, through their most peaceful shelter, may we prevail. May the swift ones, listening to us, establish this sacrifice in sinlessness and in the state of Aditi.
May the Ādityas and Aditi rejoice; may Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa, who are most upright, be our guardians of the world. May they drink the Soma today for our protection.
All the Ādityas, all the Maruts, all the gods, and all the Ṛbhus—
Indra, Agni, and the Aśvins, being praised— do you protect us always with your blessings.
O Ādityas, may we be free from bonds; O Vasus, may we be foremost among gods and mortals.
Winning, O Mitra and Varuṇa, may we win; being present, O Heaven and Earth, may we be present.
May Mitra and Varuṇa, our guardians, grant us this protection for our children and descendants. May we not suffer for the sin committed by another; O Vasus, let us not do that which you punish.
The swift-moving Aṅgirases have attained the treasure of the god Savitṛ, making their request.
May our great father and all the gods, being of one mind and worthy of sacrifice, graciously accept this.
With sacrifices and prostrations, I fervently invoke the two great, worshipful, and divine Dyāvāpṛthivī (Heaven and Earth).
For indeed, the ancient seers, singing their praises, placed these two great ones, who have the gods as their progenitors, at the forefront.
With newest songs, bring hither to the seat of Order the two first-born parents;
O Heaven and Earth, come to us with the divine host, for great is your protection.
For indeed, O Heaven and Earth, you possess many treasures for the liberal giver; bestow upon us that which may be unfailing and abundant. Protect us always with your blessings.
O Lord of the Dwelling, acknowledge us; be one who grants easy access and be free from disease for us.
Whatever we implore of you, favor that with your acceptance; be a source of well-being for our bipeds and well-being for our quadrupeds.
O Vāstoṣpati, be our furtherer; O Indu, increase our household with cattle and horses. May we remain unaging in your friendship; favor us as a father favors his sons.
O Vāstoṣpati, may we be united with your auspicious, delightful, and path-finding assembly. Protect us in rest and in exertion; grant us what is best. And do you all protect us always with blessings.
O Vāstoṣpati, who removes disease, entering into all forms,
be a most gracious friend to us.
O Sārameya, O Arjuna, since you bark, O tawny one,
like gleaming spears in their scabbards as they devour, fall fast asleep!
O Sārameya, you bark at the thief or the robber, O Punar-sara;
yet you bark at the praisers of Indra—why do you seek to bring misfortune upon us? Go to sleep!
Pierce the boar; let the boar pierce you! You bark at the praisers of Indra—why do you seek to harm us? Go back to sleep!
May the mother sleep, may the father sleep, may the dog sleep, may the lord of the house sleep; may all kinsmen sleep, and may this person around us sleep.
Whoever sits, whoever moves about, and whoever looks upon us—
of them we shall strike down the eyes, just as we have done to this dwelling.
The bull with a thousand horns who rose up from the ocean— with him, the powerful one, we lull the people to sleep.
The women who lie on couches, those who lie on beds, and those who recline on sofas;
the women who possess auspicious fragrances—all of them we cause to sleep.
Who are these men, clearly manifest, dwelling in the same nest, the youths of Rudra, who possess noble steeds?
For no one knows their births; they alone know each other's place of origin.
Sowing with their own pure seeds among themselves, the falcons, sounding like the wind, have contended.
The wise one discerned these secrets when the Great Pr̥śni bore them in her udder.
May that clan, through the Maruts, be rich in heroes, eternally victorious, and increasing its manly strength.
They who are most swift in their course, most beautiful in splendor, endowed with glory, and fierce in their vital powers.
Fierce is your might, steadfast your powers; thus, with the Maruts, the host is full of vigor.
Resplendent is your breath, wrathful are your minds; like a roaring sage, you are the shaker of the bold host.
Keep your missile far away from us; let not your ill-will reach us here.
I invoke the dear names of you, the swift ones, so that you, O Maruts, may be satisfied and respond with longing.
Well-armed, impetuous, adorned with fine golden ornaments, they themselves beautify their own bodies.
Pure are the oblations for you, O Maruts, who are pure; I present the pure sacrifice to the pure ones.
By means of the *ṛta*, those who are true to the *ṛta* have come—the pure-born, the pure, the purifiers.
Upon your shoulders, O Maruts, are your rings; golden ornaments rest upon your chests.
Flashing like lightnings with rain, you wield your weapons according to your own nature.
Your great splendors from the depths rise up; O you who are worthy of sacrifice, extend your names.
O Maruts, take pleasure in this thousandfold domestic portion, this offering of the householder.
O Maruts, if you should take heed of this praise of the inspired singer who offers the oblation,
then quickly grant us wealth with noble heroes— wealth which no other stingy enemy can ever harm.
The Maruts, who move swiftly like coursers, have adorned themselves like youths visible to the seer;
established in their mansions, they are bright as young calves, playing about like sucklings that drink milk.

May the Maruts, bestowing gifts upon us, be gracious; may they, making the two well-established worlds wide for us, turn away your cow-slaying and man-slaying weapon. O Vasus, incline toward us with your blessings.
The Hotṛ-priest, having sat down and praising you, O Maruts, repeatedly invokes your all-encompassing bounty.
He who is the protector of one such as this, being free from duplicity, calls upon you with hymns, O Bulls.
These Maruts bring the swift one to rest; they bend down force by force. They protect the praise of the worshipper from the attacker and bestow heavy hatred upon the stingy one.
O Maruts, you rouse even the weakling, just as the Vasus take pleasure in the swift one;
O bulls, drive away the darkness and bestow upon us all our progeny and offspring.
O Maruts, may we not be excluded from your gifts; may we not be left behind when you, the chariot-borne ones, distribute the spoils.
Grant us a share in that desirable wealth which is well-born and yours, O heroes.
When the men, heroic with their fury, clash together over the great rivers, the plants, and the settlements—
then, O Maruts, sons of Rudra, be our protectors in the battles against the enemy.

O Maruts, you have performed many deeds for our fathers; those hymns of praise which are recited for you even from of old—through the Maruts, the fierce one is victorious in battles; through the Maruts, the steed wins the prize.

O Maruts, may there be among us a heroic and vigorous man, a lord who is the sustainer of people, by whom we may cross over the waters for a secure dwelling; thus may we abide in our own home under your protection.
May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, the waters, the plants, and the trees take pleasure in that.
May we be in the protection, in the lap of the Maruts. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O worshipful ones, your Marut host is like honey; they rejoice with power at the sacrifices.
They who cause even the two wide worlds to tremble, the fierce ones, swell the fountain when they have gone forth.
For the Maruts are the observers of the singer and the leaders of the sacrificer’s prayer.
Today, at our sacrificial assemblies, sit upon the sacred grass (barhis) for the feast, being well-pleased.
Other Maruts do not shine so much as these, with their golden ornaments, their weapons, and their bodies;
adorning both heaven and earth with all their beauties, they anoint themselves with a common unguent for the sake of splendor.
O Maruts, may that bolt of yours be far from us when we have committed any offense against you through human frailty.
O worshipful ones, let it not reach us; may your most gracious favor be with us.

O Maruts, even when this is done, may you take delight; you who are blameless, pure, and purifying. O worshipful ones, protect us with your favor; further us with your strengths so that we may prosper.
And may the Maruts, being praised, come to our oblations with all their names, O heroes!
Grant us a portion of immortality for our progeny; bestow upon us abundant and gracious riches.
O Maruts, all of you, being praised, come with all your aids toward our patrons for complete success—those who themselves increase us by hundreds. Do you protect us always with your blessings.
Sing forth to the troop that sprinkles together, the powerful one who belongs to the divine abode;
they stir heaven and earth with their greatness, and they reach the firmament from the abyss of destruction.
Even from their very birth, O Maruts, you are fierce in your splendor—terrible, impetuous in your wrath, and tireless.
Those who stand forth with their greatness and their might—at your approach, every one who beholds the light of heaven stands in awe.
Bestow great vitality upon our patrons; may the Maruts graciously accept our excellent praise.
As a traveled path leads a person forward, may he further us with desirable aids.
Favored by you, O Maruts, the inspired singer wins a hundredfold; favored by you, the victorious steed wins a thousandfold.
Favored by you, even the sovereign king slays Vṛtra. Let that gift of yours, O shakers, be manifest.
I desire to win over those [gods] of the bounteous Rudra; may the Maruts turn back toward us again.
Whatever they have been angry with us for in secret or openly, we implore that away from them, the swift ones.

This fine hymn of praise has been uttered for the generous patrons; may the Maruts take pleasure in this well-spoken song. O bulls, drive away our enemies even from afar! Do you protect us always with your blessings.
O Gods, whomsoever you protect here and there, and whomsoever you lead—
grant him protection, O Agni, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, and Maruts.
O gods, through your protection on the day of battle, the beloved sacrificer overcomes his enemies;
he who offers gifts according to your will expands his dwelling and increases his great provisions.
For Vasiṣṭha does not disregard even the last of you;
O Maruts, all of you who have desire, drink today at our pressed juice together.
For your aid does not fail in battles for him to whom you have granted it, O heroes.
Your most recent favor has turned toward us; come quickly, ye who desire to drink.
O impetuous ones, come quickly to these offerings for the drinking of the soma-juice;
O Maruts, I have presented these oblations to you—do not go elsewhere!
Sit upon our sacred grass and protect us, so that you may grant us desirable wealth;
O Maruts, never failing in the Soma-sweet mead, rejoice here with the cry of Svāhā!
Even those who adorn their own bodies have flown hither like swans with dark-blue backs;
the entire host has settled down around me, like joyful men rejoicing at the libation.
O Maruts, O Vasus, whoever, being ill-disposed toward us, seeks to strike at our thoughts with malice—he shall be caught in the snares of deceit;
slay him with your most scorching blow!
O Sāṃtapana Maruts, may you graciously accept this oblation; [we call] upon your aid, O destroyers of enemies.
O Maruts, you who dwell in the household, come hither; do not stay away from us, O bounteous givers, for your assistance.
O Maruts, self-strong ones, poets with sun-like skins, here, here I choose you for the sacrifice.
We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the increaser of prosperity.
May I be liberated from death, as a cucumber from its stem, yet not from immortality.
O Sūrya, when you rise today as one free from sin, speak the truth for Mitra and Varuṇa. O Aditi, may we be dear to you among the gods, O Aryaman, as we sing your praises.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, this Sūrya, the watcher of men, rises up over both worlds upon the earth;
he is the guardian of all that is stationary and all that moves, beholding the straight among mortals and the crooked as well.
He has harnessed from their station the seven tawny mares, dripping with ghee, who carry Sūrya;
he who belongs to you, O Mitra and Varuṇa, surveys all beings as if they were herds.
