Up have risen for you both the nourishing draughts rich in sweetness; Sūrya has ascended the bright ocean, he for whom the Ādityas—Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa acting in harmony—prepare his paths.
For these—Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa—are the perceivers of abundant falsehood;
they have increased in the dwelling-place of Truth, the capable sons of Aditi, who are undeceived.
These—Mitra and Varuṇa, who are difficult to deceive—awaken even the thoughtless with their skillful powers. Bestowing wise intention upon us, they lead us across even distress by a good path.
These [Maruts], the watchful ones of heaven and earth, lead the mindless one;
even in the desert there is a ford in the rivers. May they carry us across this perilous strait.
The auspicious protection that Aditi, Mitra, and Varuṇa grant to Sudās, like guardians—
placing our children and grandchildren within it, O swift ones, let us not commit any offense against the gods.
May he worship at the altar with oblations; may Aryaman ward off all those who seek to harm and are supported by Varuṇa.
O Bulls, may he encompass a wide space for Sudās, free from enmity.
For even the encounter with these [Maruts] is like that of dogs; they prevail by their secret power and overwhelming force.
O Bulls, trembling in fear of you, show us mercy through the greatness of Dakṣa.

He who offers worship for favor to the Brahman at the winning of booty and the highest wealth— those liberal patrons subdue the wrath of the enemy and have prepared a wide, well-established dwelling for their habitation.
O Gods, Mitra and Varuṇa, this priestly service has been performed for you both at the sacrifices;
carry us across all difficulties. Do you protect us always with your blessings.
The eye of you two gods, O Varuṇa and Mitra, rises up, well-formed; Sūrya goes forth, spreading his light.
He who beholds all living beings has taken notice of the mental impulse among mortals.

O Mitra and Varuṇa, this inspired sage, true to the cosmic order (*ṛta*) and hearing from afar, offers his prayers to you both—he whose sacred formulations (*brahmāṇi*) you, O wise ones, protect. May you fulfill our autumns with wisdom as if with your own power.

O Mitra and Varuṇa, bounteous givers, you two have placed your spies throughout the wide earth and from the lofty, vast heaven; moving apart among the plants and the people, you watch with unblinking eyes.
Praise the domain of Mitra and Varuṇa; their impetuous strength has firmly established the two worlds by its greatness.
May the months of those who do not sacrifice pass away without sons; may he, whose mind is set on sacrifice, extend his own community.

O unerring bulls, all these [songs] are for you two, in which neither marvel nor mystery is seen; the deceptions and falsehoods of men follow after us, yet secret things have not remained hidden from your perception.
I magnify your sacrifice together with prostrations; I call upon you, Mitra and Varuṇa, with earnest devotion.
May these new hymns for your praise and these prayers I have fashioned be pleasing to you.
O Gods, Mitra and Varuṇa, this priestly service has been performed for you both at the sacrifices.
Carry us across all difficulties; protect us always with your blessings.
The Sun has sent forth his lofty rays; he has looked upon all the many generations of men.
Shining, he is seen level with heaven; fashioned by the makers with wisdom, he has become well-fashioned.
He has risen toward the sun like a fortress, with these hymns, by means of these swift-moving Etaśas. Proclaim us as sinless before Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, and Agni.
May Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni, the upholders of cosmic order (*ṛtāvānaḥ*), bestow upon us a thousandfold riches.
May the radiant ones grant us a most excellent hymn of praise; being lauded, may they fulfill our desire.
O Heaven and Earth, O Aditi, protect us—you who were born of noble lineage by those of you who are sublime.
Let us not incur the wrath of Varuṇa, nor that of Vāyu, nor that of Mitra, the most beloved of men.
Stretch forth your arms that we may live; sprinkle our pastures with clarified butter.
O youthful ones, make us famous among the people; hear these my invocations, O Mitra and Varuṇa.
Now may Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman grant us freedom for ourselves and for our offspring. May all our ways be easy to traverse and well-prepared paths. Do you protect us always with your blessings.
The fortunate Sūrya, the all-seeing, rises up as the common property of mankind—
the god who is the eye of Mitra and Varuṇa, and who has rolled up the darknesses like a skin.
Up rises the impeller of men, the great banner of Sūrya, surging like the ocean;
he who, yoked to the pole, draws Etaśa as he seeks to turn the single wheel around.
Shining forth from the lap of the dawns, he rises up being celebrated by the singers;
this god Savitṛ has pleased me—he who does not violate the common law.
The golden ornament of heaven, far-seeing, rises up—the swift traveler, shining across the distance. Truly, men impelled by Sūrya go forth; let them accomplish their goals and perform their works.
Where the immortals have made a path for him, he follows that track like a hawk swooping down.
At the rising of the sun, we shall worship you both, O Mitra and Varuṇa, with reverences and oblations.
Now may Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman grant wide space for ourselves and for our offspring. May all our ways be easy to traverse and well-prepared paths. Do you protect us always with your blessings.
Dwelling in heaven and over the mid-air and upon the earth, may they present for you both the garments of clarified butter.
May Mitra, Aryaman, and the noble-born King Varuṇa of goodly power graciously accept our oblation.
O Kings, guardians of the great cosmic order, lords of the rivers, Kṣatriyas, come hither!
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who grant life-sustaining gifts, send down nourishment and rain for us from heaven.

May Mitra, Varuṇa, and the noble god Aryaman lead us forward by the most effective paths, so that our enemy may speak [of us] to Sudās; thus, protected by the gods, may we rejoice in nourishment together.

O Mitra and Varuṇa, may he who has fashioned this chariot-seat for you with his mind, and who shall perform and maintain this upright devotion—sprinkle him with clarified butter, O Kings; satisfy those well-settled dwellings.
This hymn, O Varuṇa and Mitra, is offered to you like bright Soma to Vāyu. Favor our prayers, awaken our abundant thoughts; protect us always with your blessings.
At the rising of the sun, I invoke you both with hymns— Mitra and Varuṇa of pure intent—
whose divine power is imperishable and supreme, who move swiftly and are ever-watchful on the path of all.

For they are the *asuras* among the gods, they are the noble ones; may you two make our dwellings full of vigor. O Mitra and Varuṇa, may we attain you both where the heavens and the days cause [all things] to swell with abundance.
Those two are the bridges of falsehood with many snares, difficult for a mortal enemy to cross; O Mitra and Varuṇa, may we cross over misfortunes by your path of Truth, as one crosses waters by boat.

O Mitra and Varuṇa, sprinkle our sacrificial offering with clarified butter, our pasture with nourishing libations. For the sake of this people, grant them their desire here; bestow upon us the lovely waters of heaven.
This hymn, O Varuṇa and Mitra, is offered to you like bright Soma to Vāyu. Favour our prayers; awaken our abundant thoughts. Do you all protect us evermore with your blessings.
Let our powerful hymn of praise go forth to Mitra and Varuṇa, accompanied by homage, toward those two of mighty birth.
Those gods who, highly skillful and sons of Dakṣa, uphold the great divine power for the sake of Asurya.
O Varuṇa and Mitra, you who protect our bodies and guard us like lords of the dwelling, fulfill the prayers of those who sing your praises.
When today, at the rising of the sun, Mitra, Aryaman,
Savitṛ, and Bhaga impel us toward sinlessness.
May that dwelling be well-protected; may those of liberal gifts now go forth on their journey, they who carry us across distress.
And those self-ruling Adityas, who possess unassailable vows,
the great kings who hold sovereign power.
At the rising of the sun, I praise you both, Mitra and Varuṇa,
and Aryaman, the destroyer of enemies.
Through wealth of gold, may this prayer bring unassailable power; may this inspired singer [attain it] for the winning of the prize of wisdom.
May we be yours, O God Varuṇa, and yours, O Mitra, together with our patrons; may we obtain nourishment and fair light.

Many are they, sun-eyed, with Agni as their tongue, increasers of the cosmic order (ṛta), who by their insights have directed the three assemblies and by their all-encompassing powers have mastered them all.
Those who have established the year, the month, and the day, as well as the sacrifice, the night, and the verse—
Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, the kings, have attained an unattainable dominion.
This we meditate upon for you today with hymns at the rising of the sun:
that which Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman approve—you who are the charioteers of Cosmic Order.
O you who are true to the cosmic order (*ṛta*), born of the cosmic order, increasing the cosmic order—terrible ones who hate untruth!
In your benevolence, which provides the most secure shelter, O heroes, may we and our wise patrons abide.
Up rises that beautiful form at the turning-point of heaven,
which the swift divine Etaśa draws, sufficient for all to behold.
The Lord of all that moves and stands, who dwells throughout the entire mid-air—
seven sister bay mares carry Sūrya in his chariot for our prosperity.
May that bright eye, established by the gods, rise up;
may we see for a hundred autumns, may we live for a hundred autumns.
O undeceivable Varuṇa and Mitra, come with your poetic wisdom, O radiant ones, for the drinking of the Soma.
O Varuṇa and Mitra, come from heaven with your divine powers, you who are free from guile; drink the Soma, O impellers!
Come hither, O Mitra and Varuṇa, accepting the oblation, O heroes; drink the Soma, you who increase the cosmic order.

O lords of men, with a sacrificial mind possessed of oblations, I shall praise your chariot so that it may come hither—your chariot which, like a messenger, has awakened us, O you who are worthy of our thought; I call to you as a son calls to his parents.
The kindled fire has shone for us; even the ends of darkness have become visible.
The banner of the Dawn has appeared in the east, being born for the glory of the Daughter of Heaven.
O Aśvins, Nāsatyas, the eloquent and skillful invoker now attends you with hymns;
come hither by many paths on your light-finding, treasure-laden chariot.
O Aśvins, desiring you, I now call upon you both with devotion, seeking wealth when the sweet soma is pressed.
Let your sturdy horses carry you hither; drink the well-pressed honeyed draughts among us.
O divine Aśvins, make my forward-striving prayer fruitful for the winning of wealth; protect all our inspired thoughts in the quest for booty. As lords of power, assist us with your powers.
O Aśvins, favor these our prayers; may our seed be prolific and free from shame.
Striving for offspring and progeny, may we, possessing fine jewels, go to the feast of the gods.
This treasure has been placed for you two, O lovers of sweetness, like one set out long ago in friendship;
come hither with a mind free from anger, eating the oblation among the human clans.

In a single course, O active ones, upon the same path, your chariot has gone around the seven flowing rivers. The well-formed, god-yoked steeds do not weary as they, swift in motion, carry you at the poles.
Be unfailing toward the generous patrons who, with their wealth, incite the giving of gifts;
they who further their kin through truthful words, bestowing bounties of cattle and horses.
Now hear my invocation, O youthful ones; come, O Aśvins, on your path rich in nourishment.
Bestow treasures and grant long life to our patrons; protect us always with your blessings.
O bright Aśvins, come with your noble horses; O wonder-workers, graciously accept the hymns of your devotee and partake of the oblations presented to you.
The intoxicating juices have been set forth for you; come readily to enjoy my oblation.
Hearing us, pass over the invocations of the enemy.
O Aśvins, your chariot, swift as thought and providing a hundredfold protection, speeds forth across the regions; O you who possess the wealth of Sūryā, it hastens toward us.
When this stone, seeking the gods, presses upward for you both as it extracts the Soma, may the inspired singer turn you, O fair ones, hither with oblations.
Truly, that wonderful nourishment which you possess—you bestowed it upon Atri, who is rich in buffaloes;
for he, being dear to you, accepts your protection.
And that deed of yours, O Aśvins, was for the aging Cyavāna who offered oblations—
a deed worthy of being witnessed— when you bestowed upon him a new form through your protection.
Moreover, O Aśvins, those evil-minded friends abandoned that Bhujyu in the midst of the ocean; but he who was devoted to you delivered him out from there, O givers of no ill.
You were able even for the wolf as he was devouring; and you were heard of when invoked for Śayu.
O Aśvins, by your powers, you made the cow swell with milk like water, and by your deeds, you restored even the barren one.
This singer, awakened at the break of dawn with well-spoken hymns, praises him with auspicious thoughts.
May the inviolable cow increase his strength with food and milk. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
May your golden chariot, pressing against heaven and earth, come hither with its stallions;
gleaming with its fellies, with paths of clarified butter, the bearer of nourishments, the lord of men, rich in prizes.
Spreading over the five worlds, let him go forth, yoked by the mind, with his triple seat—
the chariot by which you two, O Aśvins, travel to the god-seeking clans, wheresoever you direct your course.
Come hither with your noble horses, O Wondrous Ones; drink the honeyed treasure.
Your chariot, traveling with the bride, strikes against the ends of heaven by its two paths.

The Daughter of the Sun chose your splendor for herself during the final night, when you two, with your powers, protected the one seeking the gods; through your favor, his vital strength passed beyond the heat.

O chariot-borne ones, that very chariot of yours which, yoked, goes its circuit while the dawn breaks— thereby, O Aśvins, bring us well-being and security at the dawning of the dawn to this sacrifice.
O Heroes, like thirsty bulls seeking lightning, come today to our libation.
For men invoke you in many places with their prayers; let not other seekers of the gods restrain you.
O Aśvins, with your wondrous powers, you carried Bhujyu, who was cast into the ocean, out from the waters with winged steeds that do not fail, tireless and unswerving, as you brought him across.
Now hear my invocation, O youthful ones; come, O Aśvins, on your nourishing path.
Bestow treasures and grant long life to our patrons. Protect us always with your blessings.
O Aśvins, possessors of all boons, come to us! This place upon the earth has been proclaimed for you.
Like a prize-winning horse with a smooth back, he has stood ready, as you have settled into your seat like a fixed womb.
May that most delightful benevolence attend you both; even the heated offering (gharma) is present in the dwelling of man.
He who brings you across the oceans and rivers, yoking his well-yoked steeds like those of Etaśa.

O Aśvins, those places which you two establish in the great waters of heaven, in the plants, and among the people; and when you sit upon the summit of the mountain, bringing nourishment to the person who offers oblations.
O Gods, you have rejoiced in the plants and in the waters when you attained the ritual service of the seers.
Bestowing many treasures upon us, you have looked back over the ancient ages.

O Aśvins, though you have already heard many things, you look upon the sacred prayers (*brahmāṇi*) of the seers. Come forth to meet the choice of the people; may your most delightful favor be with us.

O Nāsatyas, whatever sacrifice of yours shall be accompanied by oblations, provided with sacred prayers, and contested in battle—come forward to Vasiṣṭha according to his desire; these sacred hymns are being chanted for you both.

This is the inspired thought, this is the song, O Aśvins; may you, the bulls, take pleasure in this well-fashioned hymn. May these prayers, longing for you, reach you. Do you protect us always with your blessings.
The Night departs from her sister, the Dawn; the Dark One yields the path to the Red One.
We invoke you two, who bring wealth in horses and wealth in cattle; day and night, keep the arrow away from us.
Come to the mortal who offers oblations, O Aśvins, bringing desirable wealth upon your chariot;
drive away from us lack of nourishment and disease; O lovers of sweetness, protect us by day and by night.

May the bull-like [Maruts], seeking favor, bring your chariot hither at the first flush of dawn; O Aśvins, with horses yoked by Order and holding the reins in your hands, bring the chariot rich in wealth.
O lords of men, that chariot of yours which is the bearer, three-seated, wealthy, and swift as the dawn—
come to us with it, O Nāsatyas, when the one who possesses all-nourishing food approaches you.
You two released Cyavāna from old age; you brought the swift horse to Pedu.
You delivered Atri from distress and darkness, and you placed Jāhuṣa within a secure refuge.

O Aśvins, may this inspired thought and this song reach you; O bulls, may you take pleasure in this well-fashioned hymn. May these prayers, longing for you, come to you. Do you ever protect us with your blessings.
Come, O Nāsatyas, on your chariot rich in cattle, rich in horses, and most resplendent;
all our teams attend upon you as you adorn yourselves with bodies of desirable beauty.
Come toward us with the gods, O Nāsatyas, on your chariot, being of one accord;
for our friendship with you is ancestral, and our kinship is common—be mindful of that.
The hymns of praise for the Aśvins have awakened; the kinship of the sacred prayers and the divine Dawns has been stirred.
Seeking to win over the two worlds, the inspired singer addresses these two wise ones, O Nāsatyas.
When the dawns shine forth, O Aśvins, the singers offer their prayers to you;
the god Savitṛ has sent his light upward, and the fires, kindled with fuel, sing aloud.
O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, come from behind, from the front, from below, and from above; come from every side with wealth that belongs to the five peoples. Do you ever protect us with your blessings.
We have crossed to the further shore of this darkness, offering our hymn of praise, seeking the gods.
The song calls upon the Aśvins—the doers of many deeds, the most abundant, the ancient, and the immortal ones.
The beloved Hotṛ of man has sat down, O Nāsatyas, he who sacrifices and offers praise.
Eat of the honeyed draught, O Aśvins, nearby; I, providing the sacrificial food, have called upon you at the assemblies.
We have prepared the sacrifice, choosing the broad paths; O Bulls, may you take pleasure in this well-fashioned hymn.
Like one sent with a ready ear, Vasiṣṭha has awakened for you with songs of praise, chanting your names.

May those two carriers come near to our people, O slayers of demons, you who are joined together and have strong hands. The exhilarating juices have come together; do not harm us, but come with auspiciousness.
O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, come from behind, from the front, from below, and from above; come from every side with wealth that belongs to the five peoples. Do you ever protect us with your blessings.
These morning sacrifices call you, O Aśvins, at the break of dawn;
I here invoke you for protection, O Lords of Might, for you go to every clan.
O Heroes, you two have granted wondrous nourishment; impel it toward the one who possesses the truth.
With one mind, bring your chariot hither and draw near; drink the sweet Soma juice.
Come hither, attend to us, and drink of the honeyed draught, O Aśvins!
You have milked the milk, O bulls, possessors of noble wealth; do not neglect us, but come to us!
The horses that carry you both fly toward the house of the donor;
O Aśvins, heroes, come quickly with those swift steeds, O gods, favoring us.
Then indeed, as they go forth, O Aśvins, the wise patrons attend upon you with nourishing food.
May those two Nāsatyas grant enduring glory and protection to our generous patrons, and to us.
Those who have gone forth like chariots, free from malice, the protectors of men;
those heroes have increased by their own might and they dwell in secure habitation.

Born of heaven, Uṣas has shone forth according to the Eternal Law (ṛta); manifesting her majesty, she has arrived. She has driven away the malicious darkness that was loathsome; the best of the Aṅgirases, she has awakened the paths.
Awaken us today for great prosperity; O Dawn, lead us toward great good fortune.
Bestow upon us, O divine and human goddess among mortals, wonderful wealth, glorious and renowned, that brings us fame.
These, those brilliant and immortal rays of the beautiful Dawn have arrived;
engendering the divine ordinances and filling the mid-air, they have spread abroad.
Yoking herself from afar, she swiftly traverses the five lands;
surveying the works of men, she is the daughter of Heaven and the mistress of the world.
Possessing abundance, the wife of Sūrya, rich in wondrous wealth, she is the mistress of riches.
Praised by the seers, awakening the world, the bounteous Dawn shines forth, extolled by the priests.

The ruddy horses, bright and radiant, have become visible as they carry the Dawns; the resplendent one, adorned with every ornament, approaches on her chariot and bestows treasure upon the person who honors her.
True with the true, great with the great, a goddess with the gods, worthy of sacrifice with those worthy of sacrifice—
she who breaks open the firm places and bestows the ruddy cows, the kine lowed toward the Dawn.
O Dawn, now bestow upon us wealth consisting of cattle, heroes, and horses—abundant nourishment for us.
Do not subject our sacrificial grass to the reproach of men; and do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Savitar, the god who belongs to all men, has extended the immortal light that is common to all.
Through the wisdom of the gods, the Eye was born; Uṣas has made the entire world manifest.
The paths leading to the gods have appeared before me, tireless and prepared by the Vasus.
The banner of the Dawn has arisen in the east; she has come hither from the heights of the palace.
Those were indeed many days that lay before the rising of the sun, since you,
O Dawn, have been seen appearing like a lover, as if never having departed before.
These were the companions at the banquet of the gods—the ancient seers who uphold the Eternal Order (ṛta).
As fathers, they discovered the hidden light; with true mantras, they brought forth the Dawn.
United upon a common wide space, they are in harmony; they do not strive against one another.
They do not violate the laws of the gods, for they move without fail, seeking union with the Vasus.
The Vasiṣṭhas, awakening at dawn, praise thee with hymns, O fortunate one, having offered their laudations.
Leader of the cattle, mistress of booty, shine upon us; O well-born one, be the first to awaken.
This leader of wealth and of true blessings, Dawn, shining forth, is praised by the Vasiṣṭhas;
bestowing upon us far-famed riches, protect us always with your blessings.
She has shone forth like a youthful maiden, impelling all that lives to movement;
Agni has appeared for the kindling of men, creating light and driving away the darkness.
Turning toward all things, she has risen far-extending; wearing a radiant garment, she has shone with bright luster.
Golden-hued, beautiful to behold, the mother of the cows and the leader of the days has gleamed.
The blessed Uṣas has appeared, the eye of the gods, carrying the white horse, fair to behold;
she has shone forth with her rays, rich in wondrous wealth, spreading over the entire world.
Drive the enemy far away from us; grant us a wide pasture free from fear. Ward off our foes, bring us riches, and bestow bounty upon the one who praises you, O Maghavan.
O Goddess Uṣas, shine upon us with your most excellent rays, prolonging our lifespan.
Bestowing nourishment upon us, O possessor of all boons, grant us wealth consisting of cattle, horses, and chariots.
O Uṣas, daughter of heaven, well-born one, whom the Vasiṣṭhas magnify with their hymns—you, bestow upon us vast and lofty wealth. And may you all protect us evermore with your blessings.
The first rays have become visible; her ascending banners spread abroad.
O Uṣas, on your great, luminous chariot that moves hitherward, bring us what is desirable.
The fire, well-kindled, sings her welcome; the sages, chanting with their hymns, sing her welcome.
Dawn approaches, driving away all darkness with her light, the goddess who dispels all misfortunes.
These very Dawns have appeared in the east, bestowing light as they shine forth;
they have brought forth the sun, the sacrifice, and the fire, while the hated darkness has departed toward the west.
The wealthy daughter of heaven has been perceived; all behold the shining Uṣas.
She has mounted her chariot, which is yoked by its own power, and which her well-harnessed horses draw.
May our liberal patrons and we ourselves awaken to you today with well-disposed minds. O Dawns, as you shine forth, be full of abundance for us. Protect us always with your blessings!
Uṣas has revealed the paths of men, awakening the five human settlements.
With her well-beheld oxen she has spread forth her luster; Sūrya has opened heaven and earth with his vision.
They anoint the nights at the ends of heaven; like people who have harnessed their teams, the dawns strive forward.
Your cows roll up the darkness and extend light, as Savitṛ extends his arms.
The Dawn has appeared, most like Indra, bounteous; she has brought forth glories for our well-being.
The goddess, daughter of heaven, best of the Aṅgirases, distributes treasures to the one who performs good deeds.
O Uṣas, grant us that much wealth as you have bestowed upon those who praise you when you are lauded;
you whom they brought forth with the roar of a bull, you opened the doors of the firm rock.

Impelling every god toward bounty for our sake, and sending forth pleasant truths, may she, shining forth, bestow upon us the success of our prayers; and do you, O gods, protect us always with your blessings.
With hymns and songs, the Vasiṣṭhas, the inspired poets, were the first to awaken to greet Uṣas,
who turns back the two regions that meet at their ends and reveals all living beings.
Bestowing new life upon us, Uṣas has awakened, having concealed the darkness with light;
the youthful maiden goes forth unabashed, and she has made manifest the sun, the sacrifice, and Agni.
May the auspicious Dawns, rich in horses, cows, and heroes, shine upon us evermore;
yielding clarified butter and overflowing on every side, do you protect us always with your blessings.
The daughter of heaven has been seen approaching, shining forth;
she spreads the great waters wide for us to see, and the noble lady creates light to dispel the darkness.
The sun, rising together with them, releases the radiant rays; he rises as the shining constellation.
O Uṣas, at your dawning and that of the sun, may we attain our share of food.
O Dawn, daughter of heaven, we have awakened thee, the swift one;
thou who, O bountiful lady, bringest much that is desirable, like treasure, as joy to the donor.
O Great Goddess, as you shine forth, you bestow greatness so that we may behold the light of heaven;
as such, we seek a share of your treasures, that we may be like sons to our mother.
O Dawn, bring us that wondrous bounty which is most far-renowned;
O Daughter of Heaven, grant us that food for mortals which you possess, so that we may enjoy it.
Grant immortal fame to our patrons, wealth in cattle, and booty rich in kine to us.
May Uṣas, the inspirer of the wealthy and full of pleasantness, dawn away our enemies.
O Indra and Varuṇa, grant great protection to our sacrifice, to our people, and to our clan.
May we overcome the evil-minded who seek to harm us, even those who persistently attack us in the midst of battles.
One of you is called the sovereign ruler, the other the self-ruling lord; O Indra and Varuṇa, you two are great and possessors of great wealth.
All the gods in the highest heaven have bestowed vigor upon you both, O bulls, and have concentrated strength within you.
With might you pierced the channels of the waters and set the sun, the lord, in heaven;
O Indra and Varuṇa, in the exhilaration of this inspired drink, you made the dry places swell and you caused our prayers to overflow.

Only you two, O Indra and Varuṇa, do the bearers of the sacrifice invoke in battles and in hostilities; with knees firmly set, they call upon you for the attainment of security. As masters of both kinds of wealth, we poets, easy to summon, invoke you both.
O Indra and Varuṇa, when you two created all these beings of the world by your might,
Mitra honors Varuṇa with peace, while the other, the fierce one, goes forth with the Maruts for glory.

For the sake of Varuṇa’s great prize, they two indeed measure out his own steadfast power and brilliance. One of them overcomes the unrelated one who seeks to harm; the other, with few means, prevails over many.

Neither distress, nor misfortunes, nor suffering from any quarter, O Indra and Varuṇa, shall reach that mortal to whose sacrifice you two, O gods, go and enjoy; no snare of a mortal shall overcome him.
Come hither, O Heroes, with divine protection; hear my invocation if you take pleasure in it.
For the friendship and kinship that exists between you both—O Indra and Varuṇa, bestow your mercy upon us.

O Indra and Varuṇa, in battle after battle, be our front-line warriors with your power over the peoples, when both sides invoke you in the struggle, as men do for the winning of children and grandchildren.
May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman grant us glory and great, far-reaching protection. We meditate upon the unassailable light of Aditi, the hymn of the god Savitṛ, who increases the cosmic order.
Beholding you two, O Heroes, as their kinsman, men seeking cattle with broad axes marched forward.
Slay both Dāsa and Ārya enemies; O Indra and Varuṇa, protect Sudās with your aid.
Where men gather together with raised banners, in that battle where nothing at all is dear,
where all beings tremble before the gaze of the sun— there, O Indra and Varuṇa, speak for us.
The dust-clouds have covered the ends of the earth; O Indra and Varuṇa, the shout has risen to heaven.
The hostilities of the people have come near me; hear my call with your protection and come hither!
O Indra and Varuṇa, with your irresistible weapons, you conquered Bheda and protected Sudās.
You heard their prayers at the invocation; thus did the priestly service of the Tṛtsus prove true.
O Indra and Varuṇa, the hostilities of the enemy and the enmities of our rivals press hard upon me.
For you two rule over the wealth of both worlds; therefore, protect us on the decisive day.
Both sides invoke you two in the battles, Indra and Varuṇa, for the winning of wealth—
where you protected Sudās together with the Tṛtsus when he was hard-pressed by the ten kings.
Ten kings assembled together, who were not sacrificers, did not prevail against Sudās, O Indra and Varuṇa.
The praise of these men seated at the feast was true; the gods became present for them during their invocations of the gods.
O Indra and Varuṇa, you bestowed aid upon Sudās when he was surrounded on all sides by the ten kings;
there, where the Tṛtsus, white-robed and wearing their hair in braids, with reverence and inspired thought, worshipped you.
One of you strikes down the Vṛtras in battles; the other ever guards the sacred laws.
We invoke you both, O mighty ones, with well-fashioned hymns; O Indra and Varuṇa, grant us protection.
May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman grant us glory and great, far-reaching protection.
We meditate upon the unassailable light of Aditi and the hymn of the god Savitṛ, who increases the cosmic order (Ṛta).
O Kings Indra and Varuṇa, may I turn you both toward this sacrifice with oblations and salutations.
The ladle, filled with clarified butter, held in our arms, goes forth by itself toward you who possess diverse forms.
The great realm of heaven promotes your sovereignty, you who bind with bonds that require no ropes.
May you turn away from us the wrath of Varuṇa; may Indra make for us a wide space.
Make our sacrifice dear in the assemblies; make our prayers praised among the patrons. May god-sent wealth come to us, and may you further us with desirable aids.
O Indra and Varuṇa, bestow upon us wealth that possesses all desirable things, abounding in riches and many cattle.
He, the Āditya, who destroys falsehoods, the hero, distributes boundless treasures.
May this song of mine reach Indra and Varuṇa; may it protect us, urging us on toward progeny and offspring.
Possessing fine jewels, may we go to the feast of the gods. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
I purify for you both a hymn free from demons, offering Soma to Indra and Varuṇa—like the goddess Dawn with her face of ghee. May they two protect us on our journey in the encounter.
They indeed vie with one another here at the invocation of the gods, where among the banners the missiles fly.
O Indra and Varuṇa, strike those enemies back with your arrow, scattering them in all directions.
For even the Waters, the goddesses, self-glorious in their assemblies, have established Indra and Varuṇa as deities.
One of them sustains the scattered peoples; the other slays the irresistible Vṛtras.
May he be a wise and truth-perceiving Hotar-priest, who, Adityas, being full of power and reverence, has turned you both toward us for protection;
may he, possessing oblations and providing nourishment, abide with us for our well-being.
May this song of mine reach Indra and Varuṇa; may it protect us, striving for offspring and progeny.
Bearing fine jewels, may we go to the feast of the gods. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
By his greatness, the wise one indeed separated its generations, he who propped apart even the two wide worlds;
he pushed up the lofty, vast firmament, and doubly established the starry realm and spread out the earth.

And I converse with you concerning that very body; when indeed shall I be within the presence of Varuṇa? What oblation of mine might he accept without anger, and when shall I look upon his favor with a gracious mind?
I ask about that transgression, O Varuṇa, desiring to see it; I approach you, the wise one, to inquire.
Even the seers say the same thing to me: "This very Varuṇa is angry with you."
What was the greatest offense, O Varuṇa, that you seek to strike down your praiser, your friend?
Tell me that, O invincible one, self-dependent lord; may I, free from sin, quickly approach you with my homage.
Release us from the sins committed by our ancestors, and from those which we ourselves have committed with our own bodies.
O King, release Vasiṣṭha, as one releases a thief who has stolen cattle, or a calf from its tether.
O Varuṇa, that is not one's own skill, but a delusion; it is wine, anger, dice, and thoughtlessness. The elder is present at the side of the younger; even sleep itself is no warder-off of falsehood.
Like a servant, may I do service to the bounteous, impetuous god so that I am free from sin. The noble god has enlightened the unenlightened; as a wiser seer, he stirs the skillful man toward wealth.
O Varuṇa, self-dependent one, may this hymn of praise be firmly established in your heart.
May it be auspicious for us in rest and auspicious for us in exertion. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.

Varuṇa carved out paths for the sun and opened the channels of the oceanic rivers. Like a released troop of mares, he who follows the cosmic order made the great channels flow for the sake of the days.
Your breath has roared through the mid-air like the wind; like a restless beast that has found pasture, you have run.
Between these two great and lofty worlds, O Varuṇa, all your beloved domains are established.
The spies of Varuṇa, sent forth by him, behold both the well-established worlds;
they are the upholders of *ṛta*, the seers wise in sacrifice, the far-seeing ones who impel our prayer.
Varuṇa spoke to me, the wise one: "The cow bears twenty-one names.
Knowing the secret places of the foot, the inspired sage did not speak, desiring to instruct the later age.
Three heavens are placed within him; three earths are below, forming six divisions.
The wise King Varuṇa has fashioned this golden swing in heaven for his glory.
Varuṇa stands over the Sindhu like the sky; he is like a white drop, a powerful wild beast.
Of deep renown, the measurer of the mid-region, possessing excellent dominion, he is the king of this existing world.
May he who shows mercy even to one who has committed an offense grant that we remain sinless before Varuṇa;
prospering according to the ordinances of Aditi, may you protect us always with your blessings.
O Vasiṣṭha, present to the bounteous Varuṇa this most beloved hymn,
purified for him who shall bring toward us the worshipful, thousandfold, virile, and great one.
Now, having come into his presence, I consider the face of Agni to be that of Varuṇa. When the Lord of Light has brought the celestial food down upon us, may he lead me to behold his wondrous form.
When Varuṇa and I embark upon the ship and set it forth into the midst of the ocean;
when we move over the ridges of the waters, let us swing upon the swing for the sake of glory.

Varuṇa placed Vasiṣṭha upon the ship; the skillful one made him a seer by his great powers—the inspired singer, while the days were at their best, as many as the heavens have extended and as many as the dawns.
Where have those friendships of ours gone, when we formerly dwelt together in safety?
O self-dependent Varuṇa, I have entered your lofty dwelling, your house with a thousand doors.

O Varuṇa, if a constant friend and beloved companion, being your comrade, should commit offenses against you—let us not, O worshipful one, suffer for those sins as sinners; O sage, grant protection to the one who praises you.
Dwelling in these firm habitations, may Varuṇa release the bond from us;
winning favor from the lap of Aditi—do you all protect us always with blessings.
O King Varuṇa, may I not go to a house made of clay;
have mercy, O good ruler, have mercy!
When I go forth as if quivering like an inflated leather bag, O wielder of the stone, have mercy, O good ruler; have mercy!
Through my lack of resolve, O pure one, I have indeed gone against you;
have mercy, O good ruler, have mercy!
Thirst has afflicted your singer who stands in the midst of the waters;
have mercy, O noble lord, have mercy!
Whatever offense against the divine people we humans commit here, O Varuṇa— whatever transgression of your laws we have committed through thoughtlessness— do not harm us for that sin, O God.
The pure, honeyed pressed juices have been offered to you both with heroic zeal by the *adhvaryu* priests.
O Vāyu, drive your teams hither; come near and drink of the pressed soma for exhilaration.
O Vāyu, drinker of the pure, for you who are the Lord, he who has offered an oblation—the pure Soma—to you, him you make renowned among mortals; every son born to him is born as a winner of prizes.
Him whom these two worlds, Heaven and Earth, brought forth for wealth—for wealth the divine Dhiṣaṇā establishes the god.
And may his teams attend upon Vāyu; and [may they attend] the white one, the bestower of riches, in the highest place.
The spotless Dawns have dawned with fair days; meditating, they have found the wide light.
The yearning ones have opened even the stall of cattle; after them, from of old, the waters have flowed.
With truthful minds, meditating and joined with their own purposeful will, they draw your chariot; O Indra and Vāyu, lords of all, nourishments attend your chariot that carries heroes.

May those who are lords, who bestow upon us heaven with cattle, horses, treasures, and gold— Indra and Vāyu— may these patrons, through their swift steeds and heroic sons, be victorious in battles throughout our entire lives.

Like racing steeds seeking glory, we Vasiṣṭhas, with our excellent hymns, call upon Indra and Vāyu. Striving for strength, we invoke you for our protection; do you ever protect us with your blessings.
Surely those blameless gods who in former times were strengthened by our homage—
did they not cause the Dawn to shine with the Sun for Vāyu and for Manu when he was oppressed?
Desiring [us] like two messengers, O guardians, do not deceive us; protect us through many months and autumns.
O Indra and Vāyu, this well-fashioned hymn approaches you; it implores your mercy and new prosperity.
The wise and white one, the glory of his teams, attends those who possess abundant food and increase wealth.
They, being of one mind, have stood forth for Vāyu; all these men have secured good offspring.

As far as the vigor of your bodies extends, as far as your strength, as far as you, O heroes, perceive with your sight—O Indra and Vāyu, drinkers of the pure, drink the pure Soma among us; sit upon this sacred grass.
Harnessing your teams of horses that bring desirable heroes, O Indra and Vāyu, come hither on a single chariot;
for this first portion of the sweet soma has been offered to you. Now, being gratified, unyoke your steeds for us.
O Indra and Vāyu, those hundred teams and those thousand of yours, which possess all desirable things, attend upon you;
come hither with those most gracious steeds, O Heroes, and drink of the offered honeyed draught.
Like racing steeds seeking glory, we Vasiṣṭhas, with fair praises, call upon Indra and Vāyu. Striving for strength, we invoke you for our protection; do you ever protect us with your blessings.
O Vāyu, drinker of the pure, come to us; yours are a thousand teams, O possessor of all boons.
To you this intoxicating juice is offered, of which, O God, you have the first draught.
The swift presser has stepped forth at the sacrifices so that Indra and Vāyu may drink the Soma,
when the god-seeking Adhvaryus bring the first of the sweet mead to you both with their skillful acts.
O Vāyu, with those teams by which you go toward the donor for the sacrifice in his home,
bestow upon us wealth that provides excellent enjoyment, and grant us a hero, as well as the gift of cattle and horses.
Those winds that exhilarate Indra, the divine ones who strike down the enemy, may we—along with our patrons—be slayers of Vṛtras; may we, together with our men, be victorious in battle over our foes.
Come to our sacrifice with your teams of horses, by the hundreds and by the thousands, O Vāyu; rejoice at this libation. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Indra and Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, may you today accept this pure, newly-born hymn of praise.
For I invoke both of you, who are easily summoned; you two are most swift to bestow strength upon the one who desires it.
For you two have become winners of booty through your might, growing together and increasing in power.
Dwellers over abundant wealth and pasture, bestow upon us a full portion of enduring and vigorous strength.
When the inspired singers, seeking wisdom with their prayers, come near to the assembly of the prize-winners—
like racing steeds reaching the goal— those men call aloud upon Indra and Agni.
Seeking favor with his songs, the inspired sage prays for glorious wealth that brings the first share;
O Indra and Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, wielders of the good thunderbolt, further us with new gifts.
When the two great ones, contending and vying with each other, radiant in their own forms, come together for the battle of heroes;
then, at the assembly, the godless man is utterly struck down by those seeking the gods, by the people who press the Soma.
O Indra and Agni, come hither to this pressing of Soma for our goodwill;
for you do not disregard us at all. May I turn you hither with constant offerings of strength.
O Agni, thus kindled by this homage, speak to Mitra, Varuṇa, and Indra;
whatever sin we have committed against them, forgive that, and may Aryaman and Aditi release us from it.
O Agni, may we, aspiring for these offerings, obtain strength through your companionship.
May neither Indra nor Viṣṇu, nor the Maruts, overlook us. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Indra and Agni, this ancient hymn of praise for you has arisen from this thought of mine,
like rain from a cloud.
Hear the caller’s invocation, O Indra and Agni; accept our songs.
As lords, cause our prayers to swell with abundance.
O Indra and Agni, do not deliver us to wretchedness, nor to calumny;
do not subject us to reproach.
To Indra and Agni we offer great homage and a well-fashioned hymn; with our prayer, seeking aid, we bring forth our voices.
For thus do the inspired poets, ever pressing forward, invoke them for aid,
for the winning of the prize.
Desiring to praise you with our songs and offering oblations, we invoke you both,
seeking to win gain at the sacrifice.
O Indra and Agni, you who subdue the peoples, come to us with your protection; let not the one of evil intent have power over us.
Let not the malice of any envious mortal reach us;
O Indra and Agni, grant us protection.
O Indra and Agni, may we win that wealth which we implore from you— wealth consisting of cattle, gold, and horses.
When, O Soma, the men have pressed [the juice], they have invoked Indra and Agni— the lords of the two steeds— with worshipful service.
With hymns, with songs, and with shouts of praise, they seek to win those two who are the greatest slayers of Vṛtra, even as they rejoice.
May those two strike down the mortal who speaks evil, the ill-minded one possessed by demons; may they strike him with their blow, as they struck the ocean with their blow.
With her swelling, nourishing flood, this Sarasvatī has flowed forth; she is a supporting, iron-strong fortress.
Like a chariot, she rushes on, overwhelming all other rivers by her greatness.
Sarasvatī alone among rivers has stirred herself; pure, she flows from the mountains to the ocean.
Perceiving the wealth of the vast world, she has yielded milk and clarified butter for the son of Nahuṣa.
He has grown strong among the maidens—a manly bull, a young steed worthy of sacrifice among the holy ones.
He bestows a prize-winning horse upon the liberal patrons; may he cleanse his body for the sake of winning booty.
And may Sarasvatī, the fortunate one, graciously hear us at this sacrifice;
being entreated by those who bow with measured knees, she—joined with wealth—is superior even to her friends.

Offering these oblations with prostrations before you, O Sarasvatī, accept our hymn of praise. Placing ourselves within your most beloved protection, may we come to you for refuge as one seeks shelter under a tree.

O Sarasvatī, this Vasiṣṭha has indeed opened for you the two doors of the Eternal Order, O blessed one. Prosper him, O radiant one; grant wealth to the one who praises you. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
I sing forth a lofty song to the divine power among the rivers;
O Vasiṣṭha, magnify Sarasvatī with well-fashioned hymns and with praises, as well as the two worlds.
O radiant one, since by your greatness both the Soma juices abide within you and the Pūrus dwell [therein],
be our protectress, O friend of the Maruts, and impel the bounty of the liberal patrons.
May the auspicious Sarasvatī, the possessor of many horses, bestow what is truly auspicious; she who is never stingy is mindful of us when she is praised like Jamadagni and lauded like Vasiṣṭha.
Desiring wives, seeking sons, and desiring good gifts,
we now invoke Sarasvat.
O Sarasvatī, those waves of yours which are honey-sweet and dripping with clarity—
by means of them, be our protector.
May we enjoy the swelling breast of Sarasvatī, which is visible to all;
may we enjoy offspring and nourishment.
At the sacrifice of heaven, at the assembly of men upon earth, where the god-seeking heroes rejoice;
where for Indra the libations are pressed—may he come for exhilaration and to the first stage of life.
We choose for ourselves the divine aids; may Bṛhaspati grant us great wealth, O friends, so that we may be sinless before the Bounteous One, who is our giver from afar like a father.
I praise with reverence and oblations that most excellent and very gracious Brahmaṇaspati;
may the great divine hymn of praise attend Indra, who is the king of the prayer fashioned by the gods.
May that Bṛhaspati, the most beloved, who possesses all boons, sit upon our sacred place;
may he grant us the desire for wealth and heroic strength, and carry us across our adversaries unharmed.

These immortals born of old have established for us this hymn, which is pleasing to the Immortal One—Bṛhaspati, the one who cries out pure, the worshipful lord of the dwellings, the invincible; him we invoke.
The powerful, ruddy horses, bearing him together, carry Bṛhaspati;
they who clothe themselves in his ruddy form, whose dwelling is dark-blue, carry him even with force, like the sky.

For he is pure, the hundred-winged; he is bright, with a golden axe, impetuous, and winner of light. Bṛhaspati is sublime and easy of access; he is most skilled at providing abundant nourishment for his friends.
The two divine worlds, the mothers of the god, have strengthened Bṛhaspati by their greatness.
O friends, may he, through his skill, provide easy crossings and fair paths for the prayer that deserves to be honored.
This well-fashioned hymn, O Brahmaṇaspati, has been composed for you both, and this prayer for the thunderbolt-wielding Indra.
Favor our thoughts, awaken our inspirations, and exhaust the hostilities of the enemy and of those who would attack us.

O Bṛhaspati and Indra, you two are the masters of celestial and terrestrial wealth. Bestow riches upon the one who praises you, even upon the humble singer. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Adhvaryus, offer the ruddy pressed stalk to the bull of the peoples!
From the cow comes the more excellent drinking-place; Indra goes day by day seeking him who has pressed the Soma.
Since you have accepted from of old this lovely food, day after day you desire its draught;
so, Indra, enjoying it with heart and mind, desiring it, drink the Soma juices that have been set before you.
As soon as you were born, O Soma-drinker, you drank for the sake of victory; your mother proclaimed your greatness.
O Indra, you have filled the wide mid-air; through battle, you have created freedom for the gods.
When we fight against those who consider themselves great and who boast with their arms, may we overcome them;
or when, surrounded by men, O Indra, you shall fight against us, may we win that glorious battle through you.
I shall proclaim the first deeds of Indra, and those new ones which the Bounteous Lord has performed.
When he overcame the godless illusions, then Soma became his own alone.
This entire world of cattle all around belongs to you, whatever you behold with the eye of Sūrya.
O Indra, you alone are the lord of the cattle; may we enjoy the wealth that you have bestowed.
O Bṛhaspati and Indra, you two are the lords of celestial and earthly wealth. Bestow riches upon the one who praises you, even upon the humble singer. Protect us always with your blessings.
Increasing beyond measure with thy body, they do not reach the limit of thy greatness.
We know both thy regions of the earth, O Viṣṇu; as a god, thou alone knowest the highest.
O God Viṣṇu, neither one being born nor one already born has reached the furthest limit of your greatness. You propped up the lofty, vast sky; you established the eastern peak of the earth.
For you two have become full of nourishment, rich in cows, and providing good pasture for the sake of man’s service;
O Viṣṇu, you have propped apart these two worlds, heaven and earth, and you have supported the earth on all sides with your rays.
You two have made wide space for the sacrifice, bringing forth the sun, the dawn, and Agni.
O heroes, you struck down even the magical powers of the Dāsa Vṛṣaśipra in the contests for booty.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, you shattered the ninety-nine strong fortresses of Śambara;
together you struck down a hundred and a thousand of the Asura Varcin’s heroes without resistance.

This lofty hymn of praise, increasing the great and wide-striding, the powerful one, has been offered to you both in the assemblies, O Viṣṇu; may you two, Indra and Viṣṇu, swell the sacrificial foods within our communities.
O Viṣṇu, I utter the *vaṣaṭ* for you; O Śipiviṣṭa, graciously accept this my oblation.
May my well-spoken hymns and songs increase your strength. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Now the mortal who, desiring to win, offers gifts to Viṣṇu, the wide-striding,
and who worships with a concentrated mind— he shall truly strive to win such heroic power.
O Viṣṇu, you who move with swift strides, grant us your benevolence that extends to all people, your unfailing wisdom;
so that you may provide for us abundant prosperity, consisting of many-glittering wealth accompanied by horses.

Three times this god strode across this earth, which possesses a hundred hymns, by means of his greatness. May Viṣṇu be preeminent, more powerful than the powerful, for the name of this steadfast one is resplendent.
Viṣṇu strode across this earth, bestowing it upon man for his habitation;
steadfast are his praisers among men, and he, the well-born, has created a wide dwelling-place.
Today, O Śipiviṣṭa, I, an Ārya knowing the sacred ways, proclaim that name of yours.
As one who is not powerful, I praise you, the powerful one, who dwells beyond this world-space.
O Viṣṇu, what was that which was to be concealed from you, that you proclaimed, "I am Śipiviṣṭa"? Do not hide this form from us, since you appeared in another form in the encounter.
O Viṣṇu, I utter the *vaṣaṭ* for you; O Śipiviṣṭa, graciously accept this oblation of mine.
May my songs of excellent praise increase you. Do you all protect us always with blessings.
Utter forth the three voices that have light as their foremost part, which milk this udder that yields honey. Making the embryo of the plants his calf, the bull, as soon as born, bellows loudly.
He who is the increaser of plants, he who is the lord of the waters and of the entire moving world—
that god shall grant us a triple-layered refuge and protection, a threefold light for our well-being.
Now she becomes barren, now she gives birth; according to his will, he has fashioned his own body.
The mother receives the milk from the father; by it the father thrives, and by it the son.
In whom all beings abide, in whom the three heavens and the waters have flowed in three ways; three reservoirs, pouring forth, drip honey on every side toward the overflowing abundance.
May this speech be close to Parjanya, the self-ruling lord; may he take pleasure in it from within his heart.
May there be rain-bringing showers that bring us joy, and may the plants, protected by the gods, bear good fruit for us.
He is the seed-bestowing bull of all eternal things; in him is the soul of all that moves and stands.
May that Truth protect me for a hundred autumns; do you [gods] protect us always with your blessings.
Sing forth to Parjanya, the bounteous son of Heaven;
may he seek out pasture for us.
Parjanya is he who creates the embryo of the plants, of the cows, of the horses, and of women.
Offer into his mouth this most honeyed oblation; may he grant us continuous nourishment.
Having lain still for a year, these Brahmins who observe their vows,
the frogs, have uttered forth their voice, which is quickened by Parjanya.
When the divine waters flowed over him as he lay in the pool like a dried-up skin,
then the croaking of the frogs comes together like the lowing of cows that have calves.
When rain has fallen upon these longing, thirsty ones at the arrival of the monsoon,
one goes toward the other who speaks, just as a son, having mocked his father, approaches him.
One of these two seizes the other as they rejoice when the waters are released;
when the frog, rained upon, leaps about, the speckled one joins his voice with the green one.
When one of them repeats the speech of another, like a pupil learning from a master,
all that of theirs becomes as if perfectly joined, when you, O eloquent ones, speak within the waters.
One has the cry of a jackal, one the cry of a goat; one of them is speckled, one is green. Bearing a common name, though diverse in form, they have fashioned their voices in many ways as they speak.
Like Brahmins at the Atirātra Soma sacrifice, speaking around a full pond,
you frogs occupy that day of the year which has become the rainy season.
The Soma-offering Brahmins have raised their voice, performing the sacred prayer that lasts throughout the year;
the Adhvaryu priests, heated by the cauldron and sweating, appear openly, with nothing remaining hidden.
They have guarded the divine ordinance of the twelfth month; these men do not violate the season. When the rainy season has arrived at the end of the year, the heated libations attain their release.

The bull-like one has given, the goat-like one has given; the speckled one and the green one have given us riches. The frogs, bestowing hundreds of cattle, prolong our lives at the thousandfold pressing.
O Indra and Soma, burn up the Rakṣas; crush them and cast them down, O Bulls, those who thrive in darkness.
Shatter the senseless ones; consume them with fire; slay them, drive them away, and pierce the Atriṇas to their core.
O Indra and Soma, let the evil against the one who intends evil boil up like a cauldron filled with fire.
Against the hater of sacred prayer, the eater of raw flesh, the one of terrible gaze, and the *kimīdin*, bestow unremitting hatred.

O Indra and Soma, pierce the evildoers into the depth of the pit, into the darkness where there is no support, so that not even one of them may emerge from it again; let that be your wrathful and conquering power.
O Indra and Soma, hurl down from heaven and from earth your weapon, the crusher of the one who speaks evil.
Fashion it from the mountains, the celestial bolt, wherewith you consume the waxing Rākṣasa.
O Indra and Soma, turn them back from heaven with your stone-shattering bolts heated by fire;
with your unaging, heat-smiting weapons, pierce the Atriṇas into the abyss so that they go forth voiceless.
O Indra and Soma, may this prayer encompass you from every side, like a girth around two prize-winning horses.
This oblation which I present to you with wisdom—quicken these sacred formulations (*brahmāṇi*), O lords of men.
Remember us with your impetuous aids; strike down the malicious, treacherous Rākṣasas.
O Indra and Soma, let there be no easy path for the evildoer who ever seeks to harm us with malice.
He who, with a guileful mind, accuses me with false words while I am acting with sincerity—may that speaker, O Indra, be like water held in a closed fist; may he be caught in his own falsehood.
Those who, by their ways, scatter him who speaks plainly, or those who with their own powers corrupt what is auspicious—
may Soma deliver them over to the serpent, or place them in the lap of Destruction.

O Agni, whoever seeks to harm our nourishment—whether it be that of our horses, our cattle, or our own bodies—let that enemy, thief, and doer of theft go to destruction; let him be utterly deprived of both his body and his progeny.
May he be far away from us in body and in progeny; may he lie beneath all the three earths.
May his glory wither away, O gods, who seeks to harm us by day and who seeks to harm us by night.
To the discerning person, the true and the false are easily distinguished; two words contend with one another.
Of these two, that which is truth and more upright—toward that very thing Soma gives protection; he strikes down the untruth.
Soma does not indeed favor the crooked, nor the kṣatriya who holds to falsehood.
He slays the demon, he slays the one who speaks falsely; both lie caught in the snare of Indra.

Whether I have been one who serves false gods, or whether I have recklessly esteemed even the gods as vain, O Agni—why, O Jātavedas, art thou angry with us? May those of deceitful speech fall into destruction!
May I die this very day if I am a sorcerer, or if I have consumed the vital breath of a man.
Then may he be deprived of his ten sons who falsely calls me a sorcerer.
May Indra slay with his great weapon him who says of himself "I am a sorcerer" though he is not a sorcerer, or the demon who says "I am pure"; may he fall as the lowest of all living beings.
She who comes forth at night like an owl, hiding her body with malice—may she fall into the endless pits;
may the pressing-stones strike down the demons with their loud clanging.
Spread out, O Maruts, among the people; seek them out and seize the Rākṣasas; crush them down!
Those who, having become birds, fly about by night, or those who have placed their hostility toward the divine sacrifice.
O Indra, Maghavan, hurl down the stone from heaven; sharpened by Soma, O Maghavan, whet it well. From the east, from the west, from below, and from above, strike down the *rakṣas* with the mountain.
These here fly about as dog-demons; seeking to harm, they wish to injure Indra, the unassailable.
Śakra sharpens his weapon for the treacherous; he shall now surely hurl his thunderbolt at the sorcerers.
Indra became the destroyer of the sorcerers who disturb the oblations as they seek to win him over.
Indeed, Śakra goes forth against the Rākṣasas, shattering them like an axe through a forest, as if splitting vessels with a bowl.
Slay the owl-demon, slay the screech-owl demon, slay the dog-demon and the cuckoo-demon; slay the eagle-demon and the vulture-demon—O Indra, crush the *rakṣas* like a millstone.
Let no demon possessed of sorcery overwhelm us; let the pair of Kimīdins be driven far away.
May the Earth protect us from earthly distress, and may the intermediate space protect us from celestial distress.
O Indra, slay the male sorcerer and also the woman who exults in her magic power! Let those fools who worship false gods perish with broken necks; let them not see the sun as it rises.
Look back, look around; O Indra and Soma, remain awake!
Cast your weapon at the Rākṣasas, hurl your thunderbolt at the sorcerers!
O friends, do not praise anything else; do not suffer harm.
Praise only Indra, the bull, together with the pressed juice; recite your hymns repeatedly.
Like a bull that strikes down the aged, like a cow that conquers the people, he is the one who causes hatred and reconciliation, bringing about both; most bountiful, he protects both sides.
For although these people here invoke you in various ways for aid,
O Indra, let this our prayer be your strengthener through all the days.
O Maghavan, the inspired singers of the noble folk vie with one another in their songs;
come hither, bring us strength in many forms, most near for our protection.
O wielder of the stone, O wielder of the thunderbolt, even for a great price I would not give you away— not for a thousand, nor for ten thousand, nor for a hundred, O Lord of a hundredfold wealth.

O Indra, you are more excellent than my father and even than my brother who does not enjoy [your bounty]. O Vasu, both you and my mother appear to me alike for the sake of wealth and for the granting of riches.
Where are you? Where are you now? For your mind is indeed in many places. O warrior, stir yourself, O shaker of the fray, O breaker of forts! The *gāyatrī* hymns have been sung forth.
Sing forth the *gāyatra* hymn to him, the one who is ever-active and the destroyer of forts;
may the wielder of the thunderbolt come to sit upon the sacred grass of Kaṇva and shatter the strongholds.
Those horses of yours that are in groups of ten, those that are in hundreds, those that are in thousands— those stallions of yours that are vigorous and swift-footed— with them come quickly to us!
Today I call hither Indra, the one who inspires the song, the yielder of the nectar-stream; I call the well-milking cow, the other nourishment that is wide-flowing and ready at hand.
When the Sun struck down Etaśa with the two bending, wind-winged steeds,
the Lord of a Hundred Powers bore away Kutsa, the son of Arjuni, as he stealthily overcame the invincible Gandharva.
He who, even without a bandage, before the wound reaches the collarbones,
heals the fracture— Maghavan, the possessor of many riches, is the restorer of what was broken and the mender of what was shattered.
O Indra, let us not be like outcasts or like strangers to you; O wielder of the stone, we have been thought of as ill-disposed, like abandoned forests.
O slayer of Vṛtra, we were once thought slow and lacking in strength;
but now, O Hero, through your great bounty, may we rejoice according to our hymn of praise.
If Indra hears my hymn, may our drops,
having flowed through the filter, swift and increasing the strength of Tugra’s son, exhilarate him.
Come today to this joint praise; come from your friend Vāyu.
May the hymn of the wealthy patrons favor you; therefore, I desire to offer you a beautiful song of praise.
For the presser has pressed the Soma with the stones; wash him now in the waters.
Like garments seeking a cow, the men have clothed him; they have milked him from his vital springs.
Whether from the earth or from the luminous realm of the great heaven, grow strong with this body and my song; O you of noble will, fill us with the beings you have brought forth.
For Indra, press the most intoxicating, choice Soma;
may Śakra cause it to swell, as it is urged forth by every prayer like one seeking booty.
May I not, with my song, ever provoke you—the ever-active one—at the libations, like a wild beast, while begging for the flowing Soma; for who would not beg of one who possesses power?
Impelled by exhilaration, [he is] a fierce exhilaration with fierce power; the overcomer of all, distilling exhilaration—for in exhilaration he indeed gives to us.
The god, praised by all and extolled by many, bestows many desirable things upon the mortal who offers oblations; he grants gifts to the one who presses the soma and the one who praises him.
O Indra, come hither and rejoice with wondrous bounty, O God! Like pouring into a lake, fill your vast and capacious belly with the Soma juices and the shared libations.
May a thousand and a hundred horses, yoked to your golden chariot— tawny steeds with long manes, harnessed by prayer— bring you, O Indra, for the drinking of Soma.
May the two bay steeds with peacock-tailed manes and white-backed, bring you upon the golden chariot for the drinking of the exhilarating, sweet-scented soma-juice.
Drink of this pressed juice, O lover of songs, like one who drinks first;
this well-prepared draught of the flavorful juice is offered as a delightful exhilaration for you.
He who alone by his wondrous power is great and fierce through his holy ordinances—may he, the fair-cheeked one, come;
may he not stay away, but come to our call and not pass us by.
You crushed the moving fortress of Śuṣṇa with your weapons;
you followed after the light from of old, O Indra, when you became one to be invoked.
My hymns of praise have turned toward you, O Vasu, at the rising of the sun, at midday, and at the onset of evening and the following night.
Praise him! Praise him indeed! These are truly the most generous among the wealthy patrons for you—Ninditāśva, Prapathin, Paramajyā, and Medhyātithi, O Maghavan.
When I mounted the chariot with faith, bringing horses that desire the woods,
then he who possesses the desirable wealth of Yadu became aware of the cattle.
He who has granted me two bay horses together with golden trappings—
may this chariot of Saṅga, which resounds like thunder, surpass all things in prosperity.
Then Plāyogi surpassed all others, O Agni; Āsaṅga [was given] by ten thousand.
Ten bright ones stood up for me like reeds from a lake, O Adhokṣaṇa.
His massive [thigh] was seen from the front; boneless, it hung down like a thigh.
The woman, looking upon him constantly, said: "O noble one, you bear a most auspicious meal."
O Vasu, drink this pressed soma; fill your belly completely. O fearless one, we have offered it to you.
Shaken by men, pressed with stones, purified through the sheep’s wool filter, he is like a horse washed in the rivers.
We have made this [soma] sweet for you with milk, as if mixing barley;
O Indra, [be present] with us at this common feast.
Indra alone is the drinker of Soma; Indra, the sustainer of all life, is the drinker of the pressed juice, standing between the gods and mortals.
Neither the bright [Soma], nor the ill-prepared [mixture], nor the parched [grains] can turn away him who is wide-extending and of kind heart.
When others, like hunters seeking game, pursue him with their cattle,
they surround him with milch-cows.
May there be three pressed Soma draughts for the god Indra, in his own dwelling, for the drinker of the pressed juice.
Three vessels drip forth; three ladles are well-filled, upon a common support.
You are pure, established in many places; you are mixed with milk in the middle, most gladdening for the hero with curds.
O Indra, these strong Soma juices of yours have been pressed for us;
clear, they beg for the milk-mixture.
O Indra, mix this *āśir* milk, the sacrificial cake, and this Soma;
for I hear that you are wealthy.
Having drunk [the soma], they fight within their hearts like those intoxicated by wine;
like naked men, they cry out at the udder.
O wealthy one, the praiser of a bountiful patron like you would indeed be prosperous; O Lord of the Bay Steeds, let the fame of such a renowned one spread abroad.
Even the hymn being recited, the enemy who possesses no cattle does not perceive; nor does he perceive the *gāyatra* song being sung.
O Indra, do not deliver us over to the scorner nor to the arrogant; O possessor of power, help us with your powers.
O Indra, we indeed, as your friends seeking you, praise you with hymns— the Kaṇvas laud you with their chants for this very purpose.
O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, in the newest work of the active ones, I have indeed perceived nothing else;
it is your praise alone that I have understood.
The gods desire one who presses the soma; they do not long for sleep.
Unwearied, they go toward the one who is free from negligence.
Come forth quickly with your strengths; do not be angry with us, like a great man with a youthful wife.
May he not, being ill-tempered today, cause us harm this evening; may he stay far from us like an ungracious son-in-law.
For we know the bounteous favor of this hero, who is born in the three [worlds] and possesses many thoughts.
Pour forth [the soma] for Kaṇva and his kin; indeed, we know none more glorious than the mighty one who possesses a hundredfold aid.
O presser, bring the Soma for Indra, the hero, the powerful Śakra— the most eminent one— to drink, for he is the friend of men.
He who is most well-known among those who do not falter, [grants] to his singers wealth consisting of horses,
and to his praisers wealth consisting of cattle.
O pressers,
pour out the most excellent Soma for exhilaration, for the heroic and brave hero.
May the slayer of Vṛtra, the protector, come to our pressed juice; may he whose aid is a hundredfold draw near to us.
May the two powerful bay steeds, yoked by prayer, bring the Friend hither—
the one renowned through hymns, who delights in songs.
Sweet are the Soma juices; come hither! The Soma juices are prepared;
come hither, O fair-cheeked one, O seer-like one, O powerful one, toward this communal feast.
And those hymns which, when praised, increase you for great bounty and manly strength— O Indra, they strengthen the one who performs sacred rites.
The songs which are for you, O you who are borne by songs, and those hymns intended for you—
these have truly established your powers.
Truly, this one of many exploits, the wielder of the thunderbolt in his hand,
alone from of old bestows undiminished strengths.
Indra, the much-invoked, the great one with his mighty powers, slays Vṛtra with his right hand.
In whom all people, as well as great deeds and expanses, find their delight; he, the exhilarating one, follows after the wealthy patrons.
Indra has performed all these deeds— he who is renowned as surpassing all,
the giver of booty to the wealthy patrons.
He brings forward the chariot seeking cattle, even from afar, for he whom he protects; as the lord, he is indeed the bearer of wealth.
The inspired sage is a winner with his steeds; the hero is a slayer of Vṛtra with his men; he is the true protector of the one who serves him.
Worship this Indra with a focused mind, O Priyamedhas—
he who has truly become exhilarated by the Soma juices.
O Kaṇvas, sing praise to Gāthāśravas, the lord of the virtuous, who desires glory, the many-famed, the possessor of strength.
He who, being powerful, is a friend to men, gives even cattle back from their tracks,
for those who have placed their desire in him.
Thus, O wielder of the stone, you went toward Medhyātithi, the descendant of Kaṇva, who was possessed of inspired thought; becoming a ram, you approached him.
O Vibhindu, bestow upon him four tens of thousands;
give him eight thousand more.
And truly, those two daughters of the joyous one, who increase the milk,
have been bestowed for the sake of procreation.
Drink of the flavorful pressed juice; O Indra, intoxicate yourself with our soma mixed with milk. Be our kinsman and our companion at the feast for our prosperity; may your insights protect us.
May we, as victors, abide in your favor; do not abandon us to the assault of the enemy. Protect us with your wondrous aids and lead us toward happiness.
O Lord of abundant wealth, may these songs of mine increase you;
the wise ones, pure and bright as fire, have celebrated you with hymns of praise.
This one, made mighty by a thousand seers, has spread himself out like the ocean. True is that greatness of his; his power is praised at the sacrifices in the kingdom of the inspired poets.
Indra alone we invoke for the service of the gods; Indra, as the sacrifice proceeds;
Indra, we who long for victory invoke in the encounter; Indra, for the winning of wealth.
By his greatness Indra spread out heaven and earth; by his might Indra caused the sun to shine.
In Indra all beings have found their support; in Indra the pressed drops find their rest.
O Indra, for the first draught, the Āyus have called out to you with hymns;
the R̥bhus, coming together, have raised their voices, and the Rudras have sung your ancient praise.
In the exhilaration of this pressed juice, at the sacrifice, Indra’s manly power and strength have increased.
Today, as in former times, living beings praise that greatness of his.
I beg of you that heroic power, that sacred prayer for the sake of primordial consciousness,
by which you protected the *yatis* and Bhr̥gu when the prize was staked, and by which you aided Praskaṇva.
O Indra, that by which you released the ocean and the great waters—that is your virile power.
That majesty of his is not to be attained all at once, he whom the worlds have cried out after.
Be gracious to us, O Indra, for I entreat you for wealth and for heroic strength.
Be gracious for the sake of the prize for him who desires to win it first; be gracious for our hymn of praise, O Primordial One.
Be gracious to us, O Indra, for you have protected Paura; help the prayers of him who desires to win.
Be gracious, O Indra, just as you protected Ruśama, Śyāvaka, Kṛpa, and Svarṇara.
What new praise can a mortal sing for the swift one among the flaxen plants?
For those who sing his majesty and his Indra-power have not yet attained the light of heaven.

When do those praising [you] strive for the gods? Who among the seers is considered a sage? When, O Indra, Lord of Bounty, will you come to the call of the one who presses the juice, and when to the one who praises?
Upward these most honey-sweet songs, these hymns of praise, surge forth— songs that win the prize, secure wealth, and provide inexhaustible aid, like chariots seeking booty.
Like the Kaṇvas, like the Bhr̥gus, like suns, they have attained every desire;
magnifying Indra with hymns of praise, the Āyus and the Priyamedhas have raised their voices.
Yoke, O Indra, best slayer of Vṛtra, your two bay steeds from afar;
come hither, O Maghavan, mighty one, with the Ṛṣis, for the drinking of the Soma.
For these singers of yours have yearned with their prayer, as inspired poets for the winning of the prize;
so, O Maghavan Indra, lover of songs, hear our call like a longing lover.
O Indra, you hurled Vṛtra down from the lofty mountains;
you drove out the cattle from Arbuda, from the guileful Mṛgaya, and from the mountain.
The fires shone forth, and the sun shone forth, and the Soma, the essence of Indra, shone forth;
from the mid-air you blew away the great serpent—this, O Indra, is your manly deed.
Him whom Indra and the Maruts gave to me— Pākasthāman Kaurayāṇa—
the most beautiful of all by his own nature, as if running toward heaven.
Pākasthāman has given me a red horse, well-yoked and filling out its girths,
a steed that awakens wealth.
To whom ten other draft-horses carry the yoke,
as birds [carry] Tugra to his home.
The self is the father’s body, the garment; the strength-giver is the ointment. I have declared the fourth [gift] of Rohita to be the liberal donor Pākasthāman.
O Indra, when you are invoked by men from the east, the west, the north, or the south—being impelled by many heroes—you are with the Ānava; O bold one, you are with Turvaśa.
Or whether, O Indra, you take delight together with Ruma, Ruśama, Śyāvaka, and Kṛpa—O Indra, the Kaṇvas, bringing hymns of praise through their sacred prayers, draw you hither; come!
As the thirsty buffalo goes to the water-hole that has been dug for it, so come quickly to us at the beginning and at the end of the journey; drink well among the Kaṇvas.
O Maghavan Indra, may these drops gladden you for the sake of bestowing wealth upon the one who presses the juice.
You drank the Soma pressed in the ladle from that [place]; therein you have established your supreme power.
By his might he overcame might; by his strength he shattered fury.
O Indra, O youth, all those who sought battle against you have bowed down like trees.
He who has offered praise to you is accompanied as if by a thousand young warriors;
he makes his son preeminent in heroic power and serves you with words of homage.
Let us not fear, let us not grow weary in the friendship of you, the fierce one.
Great is the deed to be beheld by you, the bull; may we see Turvaśa and Yadu.
The bull has settled along his left hip; his gift does not provoke anger.
The cows are mixed with honey from the bee-hive; come quickly, run hither, and drink!
O Indra, your friend is possessed of horses, chariots, fine form, and cattle; endowed with strengthening vigor, he always thrives and, radiant, approaches the assembly hall.
Like a thirsty antelope coming to a watering hole, come and drink the Soma according to your desire;
