raining down [bounty] day after day, O Maghavan, you have assumed the most powerful strength.
O Adhvaryu, cause the Soma to flow; Indra thirsts for it.
He has now yoked his two vigorous bay steeds and the slayer of Vṛtra has arrived.
Even that person considers himself a donor where you, O Soma-drinker, are satisfied; this is your fitting food, sprinkled together—come here, hasten forward, and drink!
O Adhvaryus, press the Soma for Indra who stands upon his chariot;
the pressing-stones, while pouring out the juice that brings the worshipper offerings, look out across the ruddy [sun].
Let the two beloved, vigorous bay horses carry Indra toward the radiant [sun] during the rites;
let the seven coursers, the ornaments of the sacrifice, bring you hither to the soma-pressings.
We choose Pūṣan, the possessor of many riches, for our alliance.
O Śakra, invoked by many, O liberator, grant us through our prayer the power to win wealth.
Sharpen us like a razor in the hands of a barber; grant us wealth, O Deliverer!
With you, this bright, golden treasure is easy for us to find, for you impel that mortal man toward it.
I desire you, O Pūṣan, to come to me; I desire to praise you, O glowing one.
I do not desire that which belongs to another, for it is alien, O Vasu; I praise [this] for the sake of the *pajra* melody.
The cows have gone forth to some pasture, O glowing one; our own wealth is eternal, O immortal Pūṣan. Be our gracious protector, most bountiful for the winning of booty.
We have celebrated the massive gift of a hundred horses from King Kuruṅga at the dawn-sacrifices; we have praised it among the Turvaśas during the offerings of that brilliant and fortunate king.
Through the inspired hymns of the victorious Kaṇva, and by means of the beloved Medhas who shine toward heaven,
the seer won sixty thousand head of cattle and drove out the herds from Nirmaja.
Even the trees rejoiced for me at my arrival;
they obtained cattle in abundance, they obtained horses in abundance.
When the ruddy one has shone forth from afar as if from nearby,
he has spread his light in every direction.
O wondrous Aśvins, like men, you accompany the Dawn with your mind-yoked chariot of broad radiance.
O you two who possess wealth in horses, the hymns of praise have appeared before you both;
I have sent forth my voice like a messenger.
The Kaṇvas praise the Aśvins, who are beloved by many, most gladdening, and possessors of abundant wealth, for our protection.
Most bountiful, best at winning booty, impelling [all things], Lords of Splendor,
you who go to the house of the donor.
For the liberal donor who is skilled in the gods, sprinkle the pasture with clarified butter— [a pasture] that is wise and provides no crossing.
Come quickly to our hymn of praise with swift falcons;
come, O Aśvins, with your horses.
With those [horses] by which you traverse the three distant realms, all the luminous spheres of heaven,
and the three nights.
And may you, O finders of the day, open up for us paths rich in cattle and full of gain,
so that we may win booty.
O Aśvins, bring to us wealth consisting of cattle, excellent heroes, and fine chariots; bring us food accompanied by horses.
Increasing in strength, O Lords of Splendor, wonder-workers with golden paths,
drink the Soma-sweetness.
O you two who possess abundant wealth, grant us and our liberal patrons a wide-reaching,
invincible protection.
Come quickly to the prayer of the people that has reached you;
do not stay with others.
Drink of this lovely, exhilarating draught, O Aśvins; drink of the honeyed juice offered to you, O ye who are worthy of our prayer.
Bring to us wealth consisting of hundreds and thousands,
abounding in food, and providing sustenance for all.
For in many places indeed, O heroes, the wise invoke you;
O Aśvins, come with the officiating priests.
O Aśvins, the people who have spread the sacrificial grass, who possess oblations, and who have prepared the offerings, call upon you both.
O Aśvins, may this hymn of ours today be most effective and most intimate for you both.
O Aśvins, from that skin-bag of honey which has been placed upon your chariot, O you who move among the people, drink from it!
O you two who possess abundant wealth, with that [gift] bring us well-being for our cattle, our offspring, and our kine; bring us plenteous nourishments.
And may you, O finders of the day, pour down for us celestial refreshments and the rivers,
like water through two doors.
When will the son of Tugra, cast away upon the sea, worship you, O heroes,
so that your chariot may fly with its winged steeds?
O Nāsatyas, you have constantly bestowed your aids upon Kaṇva, who was confined within his dwelling.
Come hither with those most recent aids and excellent praises,
O you two whose wealth is rain, when I call upon you.
Just as you protected Kaṇva, Priyamedha,
and Upastuta, O Aśvins, [you protected] Atri and Śiñjāra.
And as [you helped] Aṃśu for the sake of wealth to be won, Agastya for the sake of cattle, and Sobhari in the contests for booty; so [help us now].
O Aśvins, lords of wealth, we who sing your praises implore this much from you, or even more than this, for your favor.
O Aśvins, mount the chariot with its golden seat and golden reins,
for it reaches unto the heavens.
Golden is your supporting pole, golden the axle,
and both wheels are golden.
By that means, O you who possess abundance of steeds, come to us even from afar,
to this my well-spoken hymn of praise.
O immortal Aśvins, you who consume the many offerings of the Dāsas, come hither from afar.
Come to us with splendors, with renown, and with wealth, O Aśvins; come, O Nāsatyas, who possess manifold light.
May the dappled-winged birds carry you both hither,
toward the people who perform the perfect sacrifice.
I sing after your chariot, which rolls along with its provision of food;
no obstacle hinders its wheel.
Upon a golden chariot with swift-footed horses, O Nāsatyas, you who are impelled by our prayers.
O you two of mighty wealth, you two enjoy the wakeful wild beast;
as such, provide us with food and riches.
O Aśvins, take note of these new gifts of mine,
just as Kaśu, the son of Cedi, gave a hundred camels and ten thousand cattle.
He who bestowed upon me ten kings as bright as gold—
beneath the feet of Caidya are the people, the subjects all around, like those treading upon skins.
Let no one go by that path along which these Cedis travel;
no other patron shall be considered more liberal in giving than this man.
Great is Indra, who by his might is like Parjanya rich in rain;
he has grown strong through the hymns of Vatsa.
When the bearers, the inspired singers, bring forward the offspring of the Eternal Order,
they fulfill it by means of the vehicle of the Eternal Order.
When the Kaṇvas have made Indra the accomplisher of the sacrifice with their hymns, they proclaim his kinship as his weapon.
All the tribes, all the peoples, bow down before his wrath,
as rivers flow toward the ocean.
His vital power blazed forth when Indra rolled together both worlds like a hide.
With his hundred-jointed, virile thunderbolt, he indeed split asunder the head of the violently shaking Vṛtra.
We praise these [songs] aloud, these thoughts at the forefront of inspired prayers,
like the flashing brilliance of Agni’s flame.
Though dwelling in secret, the inspired thoughts have by themselves shone forth,
O Kaṇvas, through the stream of the Eternal Order.
O Indra, may we obtain that wealth consisting of cattle and horses; may our prayer be foremost for the sake of gaining his favor.
For I have indeed received from my father the wisdom of the Eternal Order;
I have been born like the Sun.
With an ancient hymn, I adorn my songs like Kaṇva,
by which Indra has indeed assumed his strength.
O Indra, those seers who have not praised you and those who have praised you—
grow strong for me, being well-praised.
When his wrath thundered, shattering Vṛtra limb by limb,
he sent the waters toward the ocean.
Against the Dasyu Śuṣṇa, O Indra, you cast down your enduring thunderbolt;
for you are renowned as a fierce bull.
Neither the heavens, nor the mid-air regions, nor the earths can contain Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, by his might.
O Indra, him who lay prostrate, obstructing your mighty waters—
he you struck down upon his feet.
O Indra, him who has seized these two great worlds, heaven and earth, together— you have hidden him in darkness.
O Indra, you whom the Yadus and the Bhṛgus have praised—
O fierce one, hear my invocation!
O Indra, these spotted cows of yours yield clarified butter and the milk-mixture;
they have swelled with this [milk] of the cosmic order.
O Indra, those who by their own power have made you their embryo,
like the sun encompassed by its heat.
O Lord of Might, the Kaṇvas have magnified you with their hymn;
the pressed Soma drops have magnified you.
O Indra, wielder of the stone, under your guidance and your praise, the sacrifice is to be extended far and wide.
O Indra, burst open for us great nourishment like a fortress rich in cattle,
and grant us progeny and heroic strength.
And that famous wealth of horses, O Indra,
which shone forth at the beginning among the tribes of the Nahuṣas.
Like a pen, you have extended [your protection] for us, O Sūrya, so that we may behold you closely;
for when you, O Indra, show us mercy.
O Indra, since you, the truly mighty one, rule over the peoples,
you are great and boundless in your power.
To you, the one of wide stride, the people bearing oblations call for protection with drops of Soma.
In the secret place of the mountains and at the confluence of the rivers,
the sage was born through inspired thought.
From there, the wise one looks down upon the ocean from the heights, from where he stirs as he drinks the inspired songs.
Then indeed they behold the morning light of the ancient seed, which is kindled beyond the sky.
O Indra, all the Kaṇvas increase your thought and your manly power; and also, O most mighty one, your virile strength.
O Indra, take pleasure in this well-spoken hymn of mine;
protect me well, and further increase my inspired thought.
Moreover, O mighty wielder of the thunderbolt, we inspired singers have fashioned these prayers for you,
so that we may live.
The Kaṇvas have shouted toward Indra with a hymn that seeks his favor, like waters flowing down a slope.
Hymns have magnified Indra, as rivers swell the ocean—
him whose fury is unsurpassed and who is undecaying.
Come to us from afar with your two beloved bay horses;
O Indra, drink this pressed soma.
O best slayer of Vṛtra, the people who have spread the sacrificial grass invoke you alone for the winning of booty.
Both worlds follow you as the two wheels follow the steed Etaśa;
so too do the pressed Soma drops follow you.
Rejoice well, O most heroic Indra, at Śaryaṇāvat;
exhilarate yourself with the hymns of Vivasvat.
Growing great unto heaven, the bull, wielder of the thunderbolt, has roared;
he is the slayer of Vṛtra, the greatest drinker of Soma.
For you are the first-born seer, the sole lord by your might;
O Indra, you bring forth wealth.
May our hundred bay horses with smooth backs carry you toward the pressed juices and the offerings.
The Kaṇvas have strengthened this ancient prayer, which overflows with honey and clarified butter, by means of their hymn of praise.
Among the most mighty ones, let the mortal choose Indra at the sacrifice;
let him who desires to win choose Indra for his protection.
O you who are praised by many, may the two bay steeds, lauded by the Priyamedhas,
bring you hither to drink the Soma.
A hundred have I received from Tirindira, and a thousand from Parśu—
gifts from the Yadus.
Three hundred steeds and ten thousand kine have they given to Pajra Sāman.
The preeminent one has reached up to heaven, giving away camels yoked in teams of four,
surpassing the Yadu people in renown.
O Maruts, when the inspired singer has poured forth for you the *triṣṭubh* hymn as nourishment,
you shine forth across the mountains.
O brilliant ones, when you, seeking power, have indeed determined your course,
the mountains have bowed down.
The lowing ones, whose mother is Pṛśni, have risen up with the winds;
they have milked forth swelling nourishment.
The Maruts sow the mist and make the mountains tremble when they go on their course with the winds.
When the mountain and the rivers have yielded to your march, to your ordinance,
and to your great impetuous might.
We invoke you by night for our protection, and we invoke you by day;
we invoke you as the sacrifice proceeds.
Up rise those bright ones, ruddy-hued, with their journeys;
lowing, they move across the ridge of heaven.
They release the ray with might so that the sun may travel its path; they have spread themselves out with their beams.
O Maruts, accept this song of mine; O R̥bhukṣans, accept this hymn of praise; accept this my invocation.
The dappled cows have milked three lakes of honey for the wielder of the thunderbolt: a well, a water-skin, and a spring.
O Maruts, when we call upon you from heaven seeking your favor,
come quickly to us.
For you, O bounteous Rudras, lords of the *ṛbhus*, abide in the home; and you are wise in the exhilaration of the soma-draught.
O Maruts, send us from heaven wealth that is intoxicating, rich in food, and all-sustaining.
When, O radiant ones, you have determined your course as if over the mountains,
you exhilarate yourselves with the pressed drops.
Even for so great a company as these, a mortal should beg for their favor with his prayers,
for they are invincible.
Those who, like drops, blow through heaven and earth with their rains,
milking the inexhaustible spring.
Up they have risen with their roars, up with their chariots, and up with their steeds;
up with their hymns of praise, O sons of Pṛśni.
By which [you protected] Turvaśa and Yadu, by which you [protected] Kaṇva who won the wealth— may we truly meditate upon that [power] for the sake of riches.
O bounteous givers, may these refreshments, swelling like clarified butter, strengthen you through the hymns of Kaṇva.
Where now do you, the bounteous givers for whom the sacrificial grass is spread, rejoice?
Which priest honors you?
For indeed, O you for whom the sacrificial grass is trimmed, it has not been so since of old that you have gladdened the hosts of the Cosmic Order with our hymns of praise.
Together they have gathered those great waters, together the two worlds, and together the sun; together they have fashioned the thunderbolt joint by joint.
They have rent Vṛtra limb from limb and split apart the mountain ranges that lack a king, performing manly deeds of heroism.
They followed the strength and the will of Trita as he fought,
and they followed Indra in the conquest of Vṛtra.
With lightning in their hands, reaching toward heaven, with golden helmets upon their heads, the radiant ones have adorned themselves for glory.
When Uśanas went from afar to the hollow of the bull,
he roared with fear like the sky.
O gods, come to us for the giving of the sacrifice, with your horses that have golden hooves.
When the spotted deer and the ruddy steed draw as the side-horse at their chariot,
the bright ones go forth, letting the waters flow.
To Suṣoma, Śaryaṇāvat, Ārjīka, and Pastyāvān,
the men have gone with their low-rolling chariot.
O Maruts, when will you come to the inspired singer who thus invokes you, with your mercies, to him who implores you?
What now, and for what reason, did you abandon Indra? Who among you can claim the friendship [of a god]?
O Kaṇvas, may we indeed be victorious through Agni with his thunderbolt in hand, together with the Maruts who carry golden axes; thus do I praise him.
O, may I turn hither the vigorous ones, worthy of sacrifice, who possess wondrous strength, toward new and auspicious prosperity.
Even the mountains bow down, thinking themselves to be mere clods of earth;
even the rocky peaks submit.
Moving crosswise, they carry [the offerings] as they fly through the mid-air;
the Ordainers bestow vital strength upon the one who praises them.
For Agni was born as the first, like the Sun with his radiance through his splendor;
they have spread themselves abroad with their beams.
Come to us with all your aids, O Aśvins; O wonder-workers who travel on golden paths, drink the Soma-mead.
Come now, O Aśvins, with your chariot that has the brilliance of the sun; you who are enjoyers, adorned with golden ornaments, poets of profound insight.
Come hither from the Nahuṣas and from the mid-air with our well-fashioned hymns;
O Aśvins, drink the sweet mead pressed at the libation of the Kaṇvas.
Come to us from heaven and from the mid-air, O you who are dear to the oblation;
here the son of Kaṇva has pressed for you the sweet Soma juice.
O Aśvins, having heard us, come to us for the drinking of the Soma;
Svāhā! O sages, O heroes, you who increase the hymn of praise, [come] with your inspired thoughts.
For indeed, O Heroes, since the seers of old invoked you for protection, come, O Aśvins; come to this my well-spoken hymn of praise.
Even from the luminous realm of heaven, come to us, O finders of the light; you who are mindful of Vatsa through our prayers, and hear our invocation through our hymns of praise.
What others sit around you with their hymns, O Aśvins?
Vatsa, the son of Kaṇva, the seer, has magnified you both with his songs.
The inspired singer has invoked you both here for protection with hymns, O Aśvins.
You who are stainless and the greatest slayers of Vṛtra—be the bringers of bliss to us.
When the young woman mounted your chariot, O lords of ample wealth,
you Aśvins reached all our prayers.
From there, O Aśvins, come on your chariot adorned with a thousand ornaments;
Vatsa, the seer and sage, has recited this honeyed word for you.
O Aśvins, you who are much-gladdening, possessors of many riches, and discoverers of wealth— O bearers of the sacrifice, may you both respond favorably to this hymn of mine.
O Aśvins, bestow upon us all gifts that are not to be put to shame; act for us like those who observe the sacred seasons, and do not deliver us over to reproach.
Whether you are in the distance, O Nāsatyas, or whether you are in the sky above,
come from there on your chariot adorned with a thousand ornaments, O Aśvins.
O Nāsatyas, to that seer Vatsa who has magnified you both with his songs,
bestow food dripping with clarity, adorned with a thousand ornaments.
O Aśvins, you two bestow upon him strength that drips with ghee,
for he who praises you for the sake of favor and seeks wealth, O Lords of Bounty.
Come to us, O destroyers of enemies, to this hymn of praise, O you who enjoy many things! O heroes, bestow upon us great glory and grant these gifts for our protection.
The Priyamedhas have invoked you both with all your aids,
O Aśvins, you who rule over the sacrifices at the calls of departure.
Come to us, O Aśvins, you who bring happiness and are sources of well-being,
for Vatsa, the praiser, has magnified you with his inspired thoughts and songs.
With those [powers] by which you aided Kaṇva and Medhātithi, with those by which you [aided] Vaśa Daśavraja, and with those by which you protected Gośarya— with those, O heroes, protect us.
With those aids wherewith you, O Heroes, protected Trasadasyu in the winning of prize-winning wealth— with those, O Aśvins, protect us here for the acquisition of booty.
May our hymns of praise, these well-fashioned songs, exalt you both, O Aśvins.
You who are the greatest slayers of Vṛtra in many places, become those who are much desired by us.
The three steps of the Aśvins, which were hidden far away, have become manifest; O sages, by the paths of Truth, come hither from among the living.
O Aśvins, come now indeed for the protection of Vatsa; grant him a wide, secure shelter free from danger, and drive away those who are hostile.
Whatever manly strength is in the mid-air, whatever is in heaven, and whatever is among the five tribes of men— that, O Aśvins, bestow upon us.
O Aśvins, just as the inspired poets have grasped your wondrous deeds,
so too take notice of Kaṇva.
O Aśvins, this hot offering is poured out for you with a hymn of praise;
this is the honeyed Soma, O lords of ample wealth, by which you take notice of Vṛtra.
Whatever [you have done] in the waters, whatever in the tree, whatever in the plants, O you of many wondrous deeds—
by that, O Aśvins, protect me.
Whether, O Nāsatyas, you hasten forth, or whether, O Gods, you practice healing, this Vatsa here does not find you through his prayers alone; for you go to him who possesses the oblation.
Now indeed the seer has fashioned a hymn for the Aśvins with skill;
let him pour out the most honey-sweet Soma and the heated milk-offering (gharma) for Atharvan.
O Aśvins, now indeed mount your chariot that moves swiftly;
may these hymns of mine cause you to hasten hither like a cloud.
O Nāsatyas, whether today we have drawn you near with hymns, or with our songs, O Aśvins, take heed of Kaṇva’s call.
Whether Kakṣīvat or whether the seer Vyaśva invoked you, or whether Dīrghatamas offered you oblations,
or whether Pṛthī, the son of Vena, called upon you at the sacrificial sites— on account of all this, O Aśvins, take heed of us even now.
Come as protectors of our dwelling and be our defenders against the enemy; be the guardians of our world and the protectors of our bodies.
Come to provide a secure path for our children and our descendants.
O Aśvins, whether you travel on the same chariot with Indra, or whether you share a common dwelling with Vāyu,
or whether you are in harmony with the Ādityas and the Ṛbhus, or whether you stand in the wide strides of Viṣṇu— [we call upon you].
If today I should invoke the Aśvins for the winning of booty, or if I should overcome [the enemy] in battles— that most excellent aid of the Aśvins is [for me].
Come now, O Aśvins, to these oblations prepared for you;
these Soma-draughts are for you among the Turvaśas, and these among the Kaṇvas as well.
O Nāsatyas, whatever medicine exists for you in the distance or nearby,
with that, O wise ones, grant protection now to Vimada and to Vatsa.
I have awakened together with the divine speech of the Aśvins;
O Goddess, you have disclosed the thought and the gift for mortals.
Awaken the Aśvins, O Uṣas; awaken them, O great Goddess Sūnṛtā!
O Hotṛ of the sacrifice, awaken them in due order for the sake of exhilaration and lofty renown.
O Uṣas, when you come with your radiance, you shine together with Sūrya;
then this chariot of the Aśvins comes to the dwelling that protects men.
When the pressed stalks have been milked like cows with their udders,
or when the voices of those seeking the gods have sounded forth, O Aśvins.
Forward for glory, forward for power, forward for protection that overcomes men,
and forward for skill, O ye two wise ones!
O Aśvins, whether you now sit upon the father’s seat with your prayers, or whether you do so with blessings, O you who are worthy of praise.
Whether you two are in Dīrghaprasadman, or in the bright realm of heaven,
or in a house fashioned upon the ocean— from there, O Aśvins, come hither!
Or if you have prepared the sacrifice for Manu, even so, take notice of Kaṇva.
I invoke Bṛhaspati, all the gods, Indra and Viṣṇu, and the two Aśvins who possess swift horses.
I now invoke those two Aśvins, the performers of wondrous deeds, who have been made ready for capture;
they whose friendship with us exists, as well as their kinship among the gods.
Upon whom the sacrifices and the wise patrons depend even in the darkness—
those two who are the conscious overseers of the sacrifice and the rite, who by their own inherent power drink the Soma-sweetness.
O Aśvins, lords of wealth, whether you are now in the west or in the east,
whether with Druhyu, Anu, Turvaśa, or Yadu— since I call upon you both, come now to me.
Whether you fly through the mid-air, O you who enjoy many things, or whether you traverse these two worlds,
or whether you mount your chariot by your own powers, come hither from there, O Aśvins!
O Agni, you are the guardian of vows, a god among mortals;
you are to be praised at the sacrifices.
O conqueror, you are to be praised in the assemblies;
O Agni, you are the charioteer of the sacrifices.
As such, O Jātavedas, keep our enemies far from us;
O Agni, ward off godless hostilities.
O Jātavedas, you do not attend the sacrifice of a mortal enemy, even though it is right before you.
O immortal one, we mortals, the inspired poets, meditate upon your many names, O Jātavedas.
The wise ones call upon the wise one for protection; mortals call upon the god for aid—with songs of praise, we invoke Agni.
May Vatsa draw your mind hither, even from the most distant dwelling,
O Agni, with a song that yearns for you.
For you are the same in many places, the lord over all the tribes;
we invoke you in the battles.
Seeking strength, we invoke Agni for protection in the battles,
him who bestows wonderful wealth in the contests for booty.
For you are the ancient one worthy of praise at the sacrifices; as the Hotṛ priest from of old, sit here as both the ancient and the new.
O Agni, satisfy your own body, and win for us prosperity through sacrifice.
O most powerful Indra, we pray for that exhilaration which is the greatest drinker of Soma, which is conscious, and by which you strike down the devourer.
We pray for that [help] by which you protected Daśagva, Adhrigu, Vepayan, and Svarṇara, and by which you protected the ocean.
We pray for that [power] by which you impelled the Sindhu and the great waters like chariots, so that the path of *ṛta* might be traveled.
O wielder of the stone, this hymn of praise, purified like clarified butter, is for our assistance—
by which power you have indeed grown great this very day.
O lover of songs, take pleasure in this; like the ocean it swells. O Indra, with all your aids you have grown great.
The god who from afar has granted us his friendship—
like rain from heaven spreading wide, you have grown great.
His banners have grown strong, and the thunderbolt is in his two hands,
when, like the sun, he caused the two worlds to expand.
O Lord of the Good, if a wicked man should bring a thousand buffaloes as an offering,
even then your great *indriya* power increases further.
Indra, with the rays of the sun, burns down the one who causes harm;
like Agni consuming the forest, he has grown victorious.
This newest prayer of yours, timely and full of devotion, approaches;
serving you, much beloved, it measures itself out.
The embryo of the sacrifice, longing for the gods, purifies the ritual power in due order;
he has grown strong through the hymns of Indra and measures them out.
Indra has spread wide the gain of Mitra for the drinking of Soma;
like a forward-pointing axe, he measures it out for the one who presses the juice.
Whom the inspired poets, the Āyus who carry the hymns, have gladdened— may he swell like clarified butter in his mouth when the Truth (Ṛta) is uttered.
And Aditi has brought forth a hymn for Indra, the self-ruling lord,
which is highly praised for his aid and which belongs to the Eternal Order.
The bearers have shouted for aid and for praise;
O God, your two bay steeds do not turn back from the path of Truth.
Whether you, O Indra, rejoice in the Soma with Viṣṇu, or with Trita Āptya,
or whether you delight among the Maruts with the drops— [we offer it].
Or if, O Śakra, you rejoice in the distance or upon the ocean,
take delight only in our pressed juice together with the Soma drops.
Whether you are the strengthener of the one who presses the juice, O Lord of the Truth, or of the sacrificer for whom you take delight in his hymn along with the drops;
Praising Indra after Indra, and god after god, for your protection—
thereby they have attained success for the swift performance of the sacrifice.
With sacrifices they have strengthened Indra, the bearer of sacrifice; with Soma libations, the greatest drinker of Soma; with invocations, they have increased him and attained their goal.
Great are his guidances, and many are his praises;
all treasures have reached the one who offers oblations.
The gods placed Indra at their head to slay Vṛtra;
the voices of praise have shouted after Indra for his might.
We, with our greatness, with hymns of praise, and with songs of adoration, loudly celebrate the Great One who hears our invocation, for the sake of his power.
Neither the two worlds nor the mid-air regions can contain the wielder of the thunderbolt;
at his very onset, they tremble before his overwhelming might.
O Indra, when the gods placed you at their head in the battle for supremacy,
then indeed your two beloved bay horses carried you forward.
When you, O wielder of the thunderbolt, slew Vṛtra who obstructed the rivers with your might,
then indeed your two beloved bay horses bore you forward.
When Viṣṇu strode out his three steps by means of your power,
then indeed your two beloved bay steeds carried you forward.
When your two beloved bay steeds grew in strength day by day,
then indeed all beings submitted to you.
When the Marut clans submitted themselves to you, O Indra,
then indeed all beings submitted to you.
When you established that bright light, the sun, in the sky,
from that moment all beings submitted to your power.
O Indra, this well-fashioned hymn of praise, which carries us like a kinswoman across the path, the inspired singer offers to you with his meditations at the sacrifice.
When they have sung together in his beloved abode, at the navel of the sacrifice, the milkings [of the soma] flow forth during the ritual.
O Indra, grant us great heroism, abundance of horses, and plenty of cattle,
just as a Hotṛ priest at the sacrifice does for the first invocation.
When the Soma juices are pressed, Indra purifies his praiseworthy resolve;
he has found the power of the increasing strength, for he is great.
In the first firmament, in the dwelling place of the gods, he is the increaser;
he is the one who brings safe passage, the most renowned, the conqueror of the waters.
I invoke that Indra for the winning of booty, the impetuous one, for the sake of victory;
be our closest friend for our welfare and for our increase.
O Indra, lover of songs, this gift of the one who presses the juice flows for you;
rejoicing in it, you shine forth upon this sacred grass.
O Indra, surely grant us now that for which we, pressing the Soma, entreat you:
bring us manifold wealth that finds the light of heaven.
When the far-seeing praiser causes your songs to burst forth with great vigor,
they grow like branches, as they find favor.
As of old, give birth to our songs; hear the call of the singer. At every exhilaration, you have grown strong for the doer of good deeds.
His joyful songs play like waters flowing down a slope— those by which he who is called the Lord of Heaven is praised.
And he who is called the lord of the people, the sole ruler— rejoice in the pressed juice for him, who is strengthened by those seeking his aid through acts of homage.
Praise the renowned and wise one, whose two bay steeds are victorious;
they go to the house of the worshipper who offers salutations.
O you of great intellect, hastening with your dappled horses, come to the sacrifice with your swift steeds; for it is indeed for your well-being.
O Indra, most powerful Lord of the True, bestow wealth upon those who sing your praises; grant immortal fame and abundance of treasures to our patrons.
I call upon you at the rising of the sun, I call upon you at midday;
O Indra, being pleased, come to us with your steeds.
Come hither, run forward, and rejoice in the pressed soma mixed with milk;
spin out the ancient thread, as is well known.
Whether you are in the distance, O Śakra, or whether you are nearby, O slayer of Vṛtra;
or whether you are in the ocean—you are the one who aids us with the soma-juice.
May our songs increase Indra; may the pressed Soma drops increase Indra.
Among the people who possess oblations, they have found delight in Indra.
Him indeed the inspired poets, seeking aid, have magnified with flowing streams of help—
Indra, as the people strengthen branches.
At the Trikadruka rites, O gods, you spread the sacrifice that brings consciousness; may our songs of praise increase that very sacrifice which ever prospers.
When the praiser, devoted to your service, offers hymns at the proper seasons,
he is called pure, purifying, and wonderful.
That mighty power of Rudra is conscious in the ancient abodes,
wherein the wise have established the mind.
If you choose my friendship, drink of this soma-juice,
by which we may overcome all enemies.
O Indra, lover of songs, when shall your praiser become most peaceful? When will you bestow upon us wealth in cattle and horses?
And indeed, your two well-praised bay steeds, the stallions, draw your chariot— the most intoxicating [chariot] of the undecaying one, which we implore.
We implore him, the much-praised, the youthful one, with ancient aids;
he has sat down upon the beloved sacrificial grass from of old.
Grow strong, O you who are well-praised, with those aids celebrated by the seers;
milk out for us swelling nourishment and protect us.
O Indra, wielder of the stone, you have been our protector thus for the one who praises you;
from the sacred truth (*ṛta*), I send forth to you this prayer yoked by the mind.
Yoking here those two bay steeds that share the feast, O Indra, for the drinking of Soma— those which bestow wealth— respond to our call.
Let those Rudras who accompany you roar forth toward your splendor;
and let the Marut-clans come toward the offerings.
These victorious onsets of his have taken pleasure in his station in heaven; at the navel of the sacrifice they have established him, as is well known.
This [Agni], as the sacrifice proceeds eastward for long-lasting vision, measures out the sacrifice in due order, having looked upon it clearly.
O Indra, your chariot is a bull; and your two bay steeds are bulls. You, O Śatakratu, are a bull; the invocation is a bull.
The pressing-stone is a bull, the exhilaration is a bull; this pressed Soma is a bull.
The sacrifice which you impel is a bull, and the invocation is a bull.
As a bull, I call upon you, the bull, O wielder of the thunderbolt, with your wondrous aids; for you have favored our hymn of praise—the bull is the call.
O Indra, if I were the sole lord of wealth just as you are,
my worshiper would be a possessor of cattle.
O Lord of Might, I would bestow [wealth] upon this wise man and I would desire to give it to him,
were I a lord of cattle.
O Indra, your bountiful cow yields for the sacrificer who presses the soma both cattle and horses.
O Indra, there is no restrainer of your bounty, neither god nor mortal,
when you, being praised, desire to bestow wealth.
The sacrifice strengthened Indra when he spread out the earth,
fashioning for himself a diadem in the sky.
O Indra, we choose for ourselves your protection— you who have grown great and have won all treasures.
In the exhilaration of Soma, Indra extended across the mid-air and the luminous realms when he split Vala asunder.
He drove forth the cows for the Aṅgirases, making manifest those that were hidden in the cave; he pushed Vala downward.
By Indra the luminous realms of heaven were made firm and strengthened; they are steadfast and shall not be cast down.
Like a wave of waters, O Indra, exhilarated, this hymn hastens toward you; your exhilarations have shone forth.
For you, O Indra, are the increaser of the *stoma* and the increaser of the *uktha*; you are the bringer of auspiciousness to those who praise you.
May the two long-maned bay steeds carry Indra to the drinking of the Soma,
to the sacrifice of the bounteous giver.
With the foam of the waters, O Indra, you struck off the head of Namuci,
when you conquered all rival hosts.
O Indra, as they sought to escape by means of magic illusions and attempted to scale up to heaven, you shook the Dasyus down.
O Indra, you who are the supreme drinker of Soma, you have scattered in all directions the assembly of those who do not press the juice.
Sing forth to him who is invoked by many and praised by many;
with songs, seek to win over the powerful Indra.
He whose great power is twofold has sustained the two worlds— heaven and earth—
with his manly strength, as well as the mountains, the plains, the waters, and the sun.
As such, you alone, O much-praised one, rule as king; you strike down the Vṛtras, O Indra, so that we may attain victories and glorious renown.
We praise that exhilarating draught of yours, the bull-like one who conquers in battles, O wielder of the stone,
the maker of wide space, who is radiant with golden hue.
By which [light] you discovered the luminaries for Āyu and for Manu;
rejoicing in this sacred grass (*barhis*), you shine forth.
Even today, the chanters of hymns praise that [deed] of yours as they did of old;
day after day, may you win the waters whose lord is the rain-giver.
That great power of yours, O Indra, your vigor and your wisdom—
the Dhiṣaṇā sharpens that desirable thunderbolt of yours.
O Indra, heaven increases your manly power, and earth increases your fame;
the waters and the mountains urge you on.
Viṣṇu, the lofty dwelling, Mitra, and Varuṇa praise you;
the host of Maruts exults after you.
You, O Indra, were born as the bull of the people, the most bountiful;
you truly possess all things that bring good offspring.
Truly, O much-praised one, you alone crush the Vṛtras;
no other than Indra performs a greater deed.
O Indra, when they invoke you from various sides with their prayers for aid,
conquer the light of heaven here with our men.
Sufficient for our great dwelling, entering all forms—
gladden Indra, the Lord of Might, for victory!
Let the praiser extol with new songs Indra, the sovereign lord of the peoples, the hero who overcomes men, the most bountiful.
In whom all hymns of praise and all glorious deeds find delight,
like the favor of the waters in the ocean.
I invite him with excellent praise— the supreme king, the achiever in battle, the possessor of great strength— for the sake of winning vast prizes.
Whose full, deep, and wide exhilarations are victorious and full of joy in the battle for heroes.
Him indeed they invoke for a word of favor when the spoils have been set out;
those whose Indra is on their side are victorious.
Him the people honor with mighty deeds and with their works;
this Indra is the creator of wide space.
Indra is the priest, Indra is the seer, Indra is the one invoked by many;
great with his mighty powers.
He is worthy of praise, he is to be invoked—the true hero, of many deeds; though he is alone, he is the conqueror.
The people, the inhabitants of the earth, magnify that Indra with hymns of praise, with chants, and with *gāyatra* verses.
The leader toward greater wealth, the creator of light in battles, the one who overcomes enemies in combat.
May he, the much-invoked Indra, our protector, carry us safely across all enemies by means of his ship.
As such, O Indra, favor us with spoils of war; grant us a path and lead us toward happiness.
Come hither, for we have pressed it for you; O Indra, drink this Soma!
Sit upon this sacrificial grass of mine.
O Indra, may your two long-maned bay horses, yoked by prayer, bring you hither;
listen to our sacred invocations.
O Indra, we who possess the Soma, the offerers of prayer and the pressers of juice, invoke you as our companion, the drinker of Soma.
Come to us who have pressed the juice; come to our beautiful hymns of praise.
Drink well, O fair-cheeked one, of the soma-plant.
I pour it into your two flanks; let it flow through your limbs. Seize the honey with your tongue.
May it be sweet for your enjoyment, honeyed for your body;
may the Soma be a blessing to your heart.
O you who are seen by all people, like a woman surrounded [by her kin],
let this Soma flow toward you, O Indra.
With powerful neck, pot-bellied, and strong-armed, Indra, in the exhilaration of the soma juice, smites down the Vṛtras.
O Indra, go forth at the head; you are the lord of all by your might.
O slayer of Vṛtra, strike down the Vṛtras.
May your hook be long, with which you bestow wealth upon the sacrificer who presses the soma.
O Indra, this Soma of yours has been purified upon the sacred grass; come hither, hasten to it, and drink!
O Śācigu, for you who are honored for your power, this [soma] is pressed for your delight;
O Ākhaṇḍala, you are being invoked.
O grandson, great-grandson, you who are the bull-horned one, the drinker from the vessel—
let your mind be fixed upon this man.
O Vāstoṣpati, you are the firm pillar and the protection of those who offer Soma; Indr̥, the drop that shatters eternal fortresses, is the friend of the sages.
The worshipful Pṛdākusānu, seeking cattle, though being alone, overcame those who were more numerous;
with his swift grasp he led the impetuous horse Indra forward to drink the Soma.
Now, indeed, let the mortal beg for this unprecedented favor of these Ādityas at their impulse.
For unassailable is the path of these Ādityas; undeceived are their guardians, who increase our well-being.
May Savitṛ, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman grant us that wide-spreading protection which we implore.
O divine Aditi, with your gods, come hither, O you whose protection is unharmed; come together with the patrons, O you who are much beloved, providing excellent refuge.
For these sons of Aditi know how to ward off hostilities; they are wide-ruling and free from blemish, even when one is in the midst of distress.
May Aditi protect our cattle by day, and Aditi, free from guile, by night;
may Aditi, the ever-increasing, protect us from distress.
And may that Aditi, our thought by day, come to us with her aid;
may she grant us peace and joy, and drive away our enemies.
And may those two divine physicians, the Aśvins, grant us well-being; may they drive away from here all infirmity and misfortunes.
May Agni bring us peace with his fires; may Sūrya warm us with his heat for our well-being. May the wind blow auspiciously and free from harm, driving away all enemies.
Drive away disease, drive away misfortune, and drive away ill-will;
O Ādityas, keep us far from distress.
O Ādityas, ward off the arrow from us, and also [ward off] ill-will; O possessors of all wealth, keep our enemies far away.
O Ādityas, grant us that protection which releases even the sinner from his sin,
O you of liberal gifts.
Whatever mortal, through his demonic nature, seeks to harm us— may that person, by his own ways, bring destruction upon himself.
May that evil reach the mortal enemy who speaks ill of us, he who is hostile toward us and double-dealing.
O gods, you are accessible to all; you know the mortal man within his heart, O Vasus, both the double-tongued and the single-minded.
We choose for ourselves the protection of the mountains and the shelter of the waters;
may Heaven and Earth drive away from us the evil we have committed.
O Vasus, with your auspicious protection, ferry us across all difficulties by means of your ship.
O Ādityas, most glorious ones, grant us that for our offspring and progeny, so that we may live a longer life.
O Ādityas, the sacrifice is indeed within your reach; be gracious!
We truly belong to you in our kinship.
We implore the great protection of the Maruts, the divine savior Aśvins,
Mitra, and Varuṇa for our well-being.
O Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa, grant us, like heroes, a blameless and praiseworthy shelter with triple protection, O Maruts.
O Ādityas, since we humans are indeed subject to the kinship of death,
do you extend our span of life so that we may live.
Sing praise to him, the golden hero; the gods have established him as the divine messenger.
They have offered the oblation among the gods.
O sage Sobhari, invoke Agni, the giver of abundant wealth, whose radiance is manifold,
the controller of this Soma-offering, the ancient one for the sake of the sacrifice.
We have chosen you, the most excellent sacrificer, the immortal god among the gods, the priest of this sacrifice, the one of skillful wisdom.
To Agni, the Son of Strength, the fortunate one of beautiful luster, whose flame is most excellent—
to him may he sacrifice for our well-being in heaven, [the well-being] of Mitra, of Varuṇa, and of the Waters.
The mortal who has worshipped Agni with fuel, with oblations, and with sacred knowledge; he who, performing the rite well, has honored him with reverence.
His swift and fleet-footed horses hasten forward; his glory is most resplendent.
No distress caused by the gods, nor any wrought by mortals, shall reach him from any side.
O Son of Strength, Lord of Power, may we be well-provided with fires through your fires; you, being well-disposed toward us, grant us heroic sons.
Praising him like a friendly guest, Agni is like a chariot to be known;
in you are found secure and perfect dwellings; you are the king of riches.
O Agni, that mortal who performs the sacrifice well is indeed fortunate; he is to be praised, and by his prayers, let him be a winner of wealth.
He for whose sacrifice you stand upright, O Lord of heroes, succeeds;
he wins with his swift horses, he with his praisers, and he wins the prize with his heroes.
In whose house Agni, the possessor of all desirable things, accepts the hymn with pleasure, or who, as a ministering priest, zealously offers the oblations— him [Agni protects].
O Son of Strength, at the gifts of the inspired singer who praises you most swiftly, O Vasu,
make the word of the one who has found [you] heard by the gods above and by mortals below.
Whoever seeks to win over Agni—the highly skillful one who blazes with strength—with offerings of oblations, with salutations, or with song;

The mortal who, with kindled fuel and sharpened devotion, worships Aditi through his ritual stations— he, being fortunate, shall by his prayers and splendors pass over all people, just as one crosses over waters.
O Agni, bring us that splendor which shall overcome every devourer in our dwelling,
and the wrath of the evil-minded person.
That by which Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman perceive, by which the Nāsatyas and Bhaga perceive— that, O Indra, may we worship with your power as those who best know the path, being protected by you.
O Agni, they indeed are well-disposed who, as inspired poets, have established you— the one who beholds men— as their priest, O God, the possessor of good wisdom.
They have prepared the altar for you, O Blessed One; they have prepared the oblation and the pressing of the soma in heaven.
They indeed have won great wealth through their spoils—those who have directed their desire toward you.
May Agni, when invoked, be auspicious to us; may the gift be auspicious, O fortunate one, and may the sacrifice be auspicious;
and may our praises also be auspicious.
Make your mind auspicious for the conquest of Vṛtra, by which you may prevail in battles;
loosen the many firm [bonds] of those who are arrogant, and may we win through your assistances.
I praise with song the one established by Manu, whom the gods appointed as messenger and steward—
the best of sacrificers, the bearer of oblations.
To Agni, who has sharp fangs, who is young and resplendent—to him you sing forth your offerings;
he who, when offered oblations of clarified butter, fashions heroic power through his truthful blessings.
When Agni, invoked with clarified butter, brandishes his axe up and down,
he is like an Asura displaying his bright garment.
The god established by Manu, who has sent forth the oblations with his fragrant mouth—
the immortal, divine Hotṛ priest who performs the sacrifice well— seeks to win desirable boons.
O Agni, son of strength, invoked with oblations, if you were a mortal and I were an immortal, O you of Mitra-like majesty!
O Vasu, may I not deliver you over to calumny, nor to evil, O Truthful One;
may my praiser never be in distress or ill-fated, O Agni, nor suffer through sin.
Like a son well-nourished in his father's house, may our oblation go forth to the gods.
O Agni, may I, a mortal, always enjoy your most intimate aids according to your pleasure, O Vasu, the god.
By your wisdom may I win, O Agni, through your gifts and your praises;
they call you alone my providence, O Vasu—be glad, O Agni, to grant us wealth.
O Agni, he whom you favor with your friendship advances by means of your protections— those which bring heroic sons and the bearing of strength.
Your dark-blue drop, bellowing at the proper season, kindled by the zealous one, has been taken up.
You are the beloved of the great Dawns; you reign over the manifestations of the night.
To him, the thousand-testicled one, the most helpful, the sovereign lord of Trasadasyu, we Sobharis have come for protection.
O Agni, you whose other fires depend upon you like branches,
I win for myself the splendors of men like inspired songs, increasing your sovereign powers.
O Ādityas, free from malice, you who lead the mortal man to the further shore— O bounteous givers, [you do so] for all the wealthy patrons.
O you kings, subduers of the people, whoever among you dwells over the human race—
may we, O Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, be the charioteers of your eternal Law (ṛta).
Trasadasyu, the son of Purukutsa, has given me fifty brides;
he is the most bountiful noble, the lord of the virtuous.
And for me, at the ford of the Suvāstu river, Śyāva became the leader of the two Prayiyas and the two Vayihas; he was the lord of the Vasus and the master of the gifts.
Come hither; do not fail us, O you who set forth together, do not stay away, O you of one mind, you who can bend even what is firm.
O Maruts, lords of the *Ṛbhus*, come with your strong-fellied chariots, O Rudras, with your brilliant splendors!
Come today with food, you who are much-desired, to our sacrifice, you who long for the *Sobharis*.
For we know the fierce might of the sons of Rudra, of the impetuous Maruts,
the bounteous ones of the swift-moving Viṣṇu.
The islands were scattered and misfortune stood still; both heaven and earth were joined together when you, O bright-helmeted ones, self-luminous, stirred up the desert wastes as you moved forth.
Even the immovable mountains and the lord of the forest roar at your onset;
the earth trembles during your marches.
To let you pass through, O Maruts, the vast heaven has opened wide above for your approach,
where the heroes, displaying their strength in their own bodies, manifest the power of their arms.
According to their own nature, the men—great, brilliant, impetuous, and bull-like in form—bear along their glory; they bear it with unswerving forms.
The arrow of the Sobharis is anointed with the milk of cows upon the golden seat of the chariot.
O well-born kinsmen of the cow, great ones, come now for food and enjoyment, not merely for our protection.
O Maruts, you who possess spotted deer as steeds, bring forth oblations for your vigorous host,
for the one whose strides are powerful.
O Maruts, on your chariot drawn by stallions, with its powerful horses and powerful nave—
come like winged falcons at will, O heroes, to enjoy our offerings.
Their ointment is the same; their golden ornaments shine upon their arms, and their spears flash brilliantly.
Those fierce ones, the bulls with fierce arms, have not striven against one another in their bodies;
firm are the bows and weapons upon your chariots, and glory rests upon your faces.
Whose name is like a far-spreading flood, the one among many that is wondrous for enjoyment— like ancestral vitality, their power is overwhelming.
Worship them, the Maruts; praise them, for of those roaring ones there is no last, as among the spokes of a wheel; such is their bounty, such is their greatness.
O Maruts, he was fortunate under your protections in former dawns,
and he shall be so even now and hereafter.
Or that hero to whom you, O Vājin-s, come as men to enjoy his offerings—
he, O Shakers, shall obtain your favors through splendors and the winning of prizes.
Just as the sons of Rudra, the youthful ones, desire from the divine Asura, the ordainer of heaven, so may it be for you two.
And those Maruts, the bounteous givers, who are worthy of praise and who move among us as munificent lords—
from them even, O youths, turn toward us with a more gracious heart.
O Sobhari, with a most new song, sing toward the two young, purifying bulls,
as one who ploughs sings to his oxen.
Those who are victorious, like a prize-winning boxer to be invoked, in all battles among the priests— those Maruts, most glorious like shining bulls, do thou indeed honor with thy song.
Even the cows, O Maruts, being of one mind, kinsmen by common birth,
lick each other’s humps.
O dancers with golden ornaments upon your breasts, even a mortal man seeks your brotherhood.
O Maruts, look upon us, for your friendship is forever steadfast.
O Maruts, you of liberal gifts, bring to us the healing medicine of the Marut-host;
you are our friends and our steeds.

With those aids by which you protect the Sindhu, by which you overcome [the foe], and by which you show favor to Krivi— O you who bring delight, may your auspicious protections, which are free from malice, be a source of joy to us.
O Maruts who possess the noble sacrificial grass, whatever healing medicine is in the Sindhu, in the Asiknī, in the oceans, or in the mountains— [that we bring to you].
Beholding all things, you carry them within your bodies; with that, speak for us!
O Maruts, forgive the sin of our sick man, and restore what was shattered.
O matchless one, we, seeking your aid, call upon you—the wondrous one—for strength, just as those carrying a heavy load call for support. We invoke you in the contest for booty.
Come near to us for help in this rite, O fierce one, who hast boldly come to our side;
for we, as friends, have chosen you alone, O Indra, as our victorious protector.
Come here to these Soma drops, O Lord of horses, Lord of cattle, Lord of the fertile fields; drink the Soma, O Lord of Soma.
For we, O Indra, being without kin, have drawn you, who possess many kinsmen, as our guide—we, the inspired singers.
O Bull, come with all those powers of yours that exist, for the drinking of the Soma.
Sitting like birds at honeyed, intoxicating, and exhilarating mead mixed with milk,
O Indra, we cry out to you repeatedly.
We address you with this homage; why do you hesitate even for a moment? O Lord of Bay Horses, there are desires; you are the giver. We exist, and our prayers exist as well.
O Indra, we have indeed become yours anew through your protection;
for we have known your abundance from of old, O wielder of the stone.
We know your friendship and your bounty, O Hero; those we seek from you, O Wielder of the Thunderbolt.
Furthermore, O Good One, sharpen us for the prize consisting of cattle in this very contest, O fair-cheeked one.
Him who brought this and that wealth to us in the past— him, Indra, I praise for you, O friends, for our protection.
The Lord of the virtuous, master of bay horses, subduer of the peoples— for he indeed has rejoiced—
may that Maghavan bestow upon us, his worshippers, hundreds of cattle and horses.
O Bull, with you as our ally, may we indeed speak back to the one who breathes fiercely at us in the assembly of people rich in cattle.
O much-invoked Indra, may we, as performers, conquer in our performance; may we overcome the evil-minded. With our men, may we slay Vṛtra and may we flourish. O Indra, further our prayers.
O Indra, by your very birth you have from of old been without rivals and without kin;
yet through battle you seek companionship.
You do not find the wealthy man for friendship; they revile you, O Surāśva.
When you make a roar and gather [the waters] together, then indeed you are invoked like a father.
O Indra, let us not sit down together at the pressed juice like fools who have grown old, as if we were unworthy in the friendship of one such as you.
O giver of cattle, Indra, may we not be excluded from your bounty; may we not fail to receive it from you.
Even the firm [fortresses] of the noble foe, seize them and bring them here; for your gifts cannot be thwarted.
Either Indra indeed bestows such wealth, or the auspicious Sarasvatī grants riches;
or you yourself, O Citra, [give] to the donor.
Truly, Citra is a king, while others are merely kings who dwell along the Sarasvatī;
for like Parjanya with his rain, he has extended [his bounty], giving away thousands and tens of thousands.
Hither I call today that most wondrous chariot for aid,
O Aśvins, you who are easy to invoke and whose paths are red, upon which you mounted for Sūryā.
The one of ancient life, easy to invoke, much-desired, the deliverer Bhujyu, preeminent in battles—
him who is accompanied by favors, O Sobhari, the one who drives away hatred and is free from blemish.
Hither, with our salutations, we bring those two Aśvins, the most manifold beings, the gods,
to turn toward us for our protection, they who go to the house of the donor.
One wheel of your chariot moves around; the other speeds along its path. O Lords of Splendor, may your favor hasten toward us like a milch-cow.
O Aśvins, that chariot of yours which has three seats and golden reins,
renowned as it circles around heaven and earth— come upon it, O Nāsatyas.
Bestowing gifts upon Manu, you two plow the ancient grain in heaven with the wolf;
as such, O Aśvins, lords of splendor, we shall extol you today with our hymns of favor.
Come to us, O lords of ample wealth, by the paths of cosmic order, those paths by which you, O bulls, quickened Tr̥kṣi, the son of Trasadasyu, for the sake of great dominion.
This Soma has been pressed for you with stones, O heroes, possessors of bull-like wealth;
come hither for the drinking of Soma, and drink in the house of the donor.
O Aśvins, lords of wealth, mount indeed upon the golden seat of your chariot;
yoke your abundant nourishments.

With those aids wherewith you helped Paktha, wherewith you helped Adhrigu, and wherewith you helped Babhru when he was bereft of his companions—with those very aids, O Aśvins, come to us quickly and swiftly; heal whatever is diseased.
When we, the Adhrigus, invoke the Aśvins at this very time of day with our songs, we who are skilled in praise— may they come to us.
With those [powers], O bulls, come hither to my call—[the call] which provides all food and contains all that is desirable.
O heroes, most bountiful with nourishment and most abundant in being, come hither with those [powers] by which you strengthened Krivi.
Even now, at this very time of days, I address those two Aśvins with praise;
them indeed we implore with acts of homage.
Those two indeed at evening and those at dawn, O Lords of Splendor, those who travel on paths like Rudras—
O Rudras, you who possess abundant wealth, do not overlook us to the enemy mortal.
For the sake of easy passage, I, Sobhari, call upon the Aśvins— who by their chariot are conquerors from the very dawn— as one might call upon a father for a happy journey.
O bulls, swift as thought, distilling exhilaration, come with your most rapid aids;
even from afar, be present for our protection with your many ancient succors, O you who provide manifold nourishment.
O Aśvins, most liberal drinkers of the honey-mead, O heroes, come to our dwelling bringing horses,
cattle, and gold, O wonder-workers!
Excellent protection, heroic strength, most desirable wealth— unassailable by the Rakṣas-demons—
at this approach of yours, O lords of ample riches, may we obtain all precious things from you both.
Invoke indeed the one worthy of worship; sacrifice to Jātavedas, whose smoke wanders abroad and whose radiance cannot be grasped.
O Viśvacarṣaṇi, with my song I praise Agni, the giver, the one who belongs to all men;
and I extol the competing chariots.
Those whose pressure is worthy of hymns, for whom food and strength are to be seized—
the bearer of the oblation finds wealth through their discovery.
The flame of this one has risen up, shining with undecaying light— the flame of him whose jaws are glowing, who is well-beaming, and whose glory is his troop.
Arise, O you of well-performed sacrifice, being praised with divine grace; shining brightly with great splendor, look upon us with your light.
O Agni, come with our excellent praises, as we duly offer the oblations;
for you have become the messenger, the bearer of the sacrificial offerings.
I invoke for you Agni, the ancient one, the Hotṛ-priest of the peoples;
him I laud with this speech, and him indeed I praise for you.
Through sacrifices, they have perfected him of wondrous power with their prayers— him who,
like Mitra well-established among the people, abides in the realm of Truth.
Those who seek the Truth have, with their song, approached him who is the observer of Truth and the accomplisher of the sacrifice;
they have delighted in him at the place of homage.
May our well-ordered sacrifices go forth toward him, the best of the Aṅgirases,
who is the most glorious invoker among the people.
O Agni, those kindled flames of thine, ageless, are a lofty light;
like stallions, they are vigorous and full of power.
As such, O Lord of Strengths, grant us wealth and heroic power;
protect us in battles for our children and grandchildren.
Or when the Lord of the People, sharpened and well-pleased among the human folk,
Agni repels all the demons.
O Hero, O Lord of the People, Agni, listen with favor to this new hymn of mine;
burn down the guileful Rākṣasas with your heat.
No mortal enemy, even by means of magic,
can prevail over him who has given gifts to Agni with oblations.
The seer Vyaśva, desiring cattle, has gratified you, the finder of wealth;
for the sake of great riches, we kindle you as well.
Uśanas Kāvya established you as the Hotṛ-priest;
he established you, Jātavedas, the one who wins the sacrifice for Manu.
For all the gods, being of one accord, have made you their messenger; O god, by your readiness to hear, you have become the first worthy of sacrifice.
Indeed, let a mortal hero make this immortal one his messenger— the purifier, whose path is black, who traverses the vast expanse.
With ladles uplifted, let us invoke him, the one of beautiful luster and bright radiance— Agni, the ageless and ancient, worthy of praise by the people.
The mortal who has offered oblations to him with gifts of sacrificial food,
he bestows abundant nourishment and glory accompanied by heroic sons.
The ladle, laden with oblation, goes forth with reverence toward Agni Jātavedas, the first and foremost in sacrifices.
With these most excellent hymns, like those of Vyaśva, let us worship Agni,
whose radiance is bright, with our most bountiful thoughts.
Now indeed, O seer Vainyaśva, sing with hymns like Sthūrayūpa to the far-reaching Agni, the lord of the household.
The inspired poets invoke for protection the ancient Agni, the guest of human beings and the son of the lords of the forest.
O Agni, you who are great, sit down upon the sacred grass with reverence for the sake of all the vast oblations offered by men.
Win for us many desirable things; win riches sought by many—riches consisting of excellent heroes, abundant progeny, and glory.
O Agni, as the bestower of boons, impel wealth toward Suṣāman and his people; O most youthful Vasu, grant bounty forever to every one.
For you are indeed a great overcomer; you [grant] us food consisting of cattle. O Agni, open up for us the attainment of great wealth.
O Agni, you are glorious; bring Mitra and Varuṇa hither—the two sovereign rulers, upholders of cosmic order, whose will is pure.
O friends, let us instruct a sacred prayer for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt;
I shall indeed praise you for him who is most heroic and bold.
For you are renowned by your might as the slayer of Vṛtra through the slaying of Vṛtra;
O Hero, with your bounties you surpass even the liberal patrons.
Being thus praised, O Lord of the Bay Steeds, bring us wealth of most wondrous fame— that treasure which you, the bountiful giver, bestow even upon the lowliest.
O Indra, disclose that which is hidden and dear among the people;
O bold one, being praised, bring it hither with courage.
Neither do the destroyers ward off your left hand nor your right; O Lord of Bay Steeds, no obstacles can restrain you in the quests for cattle.
O wielder of the stone, I draw you toward me with songs as one fills a pen with cattle; fulfill the desire and the mind of the singer.
O slayer of Vṛtra, most excellent guide, O Vasu, bestow upon us all things through the wisdom of Viśvamanas; look down upon us, O mighty one!
O Vṛtra-slayer, O Hero, may we partake of this newest gift of yours,
O Vasu, O much-invoked one, a desirable wealth.
O Indra, O Dancer, for as your power is indeed unassailable, so too,
O Much-invoked One, is your gift to the donor unimpaired.
O most magnificent one, most manly, pour forth for great bounty; O Maghavan, though you are firm, make yourself even firmer for the granting of wealth.
O wielder of the stone, our hopes have never turned elsewhere than to you;
O Maghavan, grant us this with your aids.
For truly, O dancer, I find no one other than you for the granting of bounty—
for wealth, splendor, and power, O lover of songs.
Pour out the Soma-mead for Indra; let him drink it.
May he impel [us] with his bounty through his greatness.
I have addressed the Lord of the two bay steeds, the one who bestows skill; now, indeed, listen to the one who praises you, the son of Aśva.
Truly, my friend, even in the past no one was born more heroic than you;
none is equal to you in wealth, nor in such deeds, nor in glory.
O Adhvaryu, pour out for us of this sweet, most intoxicating juice;
for thus is the hero praised, he who ever prospers.
O Indra, driver of the bay steeds, no one has ever attained your ancient praise through power, nor through glorious deeds.
Desirous of glory, we have invoked him for you— the Lord of spoils,
who is to be magnified by sacrifices that do not fail.
Come now, friends, let us praise Indra, the hero worthy of hymns,
who alone stands preeminent over all the peoples.
To him who does not withhold the cow, who seeks cattle, the celestial one— to him speak a wondrous word sweeter than clarified butter and honey.
His heroic powers are immeasurable, and his bounty is not to be surpassed;
his sacrificial gift exceeds all like light.
Praise Indra like Vyaśva— him who is waveless, the possessor of vigor, the controller,
who bestows the wealth of the noble upon the worshipper.
O son of Vyaśva, thus now praise the tenth and the ninth [Indra],
the one who is well-knowing and worthy of being celebrated by those who move upon the earth.
For you indeed know how to avoid the destructive powers, O wielder of the thunderbolt;
day by day you cleanse yourself like one who avoids pitfalls.
O Indra, bring that [wealth] for our aid, wherewith you, O most wondrous one, struck down [the foe] twice for Kutsa; urge it toward us.
Therefore, we now implore you, O most wondrous one, for new wealth;
as such, may you overcome all our adversaries.
O you of many heroic deeds, release him from the distress of the bear, or from the waterless desert among the seven rivers;
humble the weapon of the Dāsa.
Just as you brought wealth to Vara for Suṣāman and to the Sanis, so bring it, O fortunate one,
rich in prizes, to the Vyaśvas.
May the sacrificial fee of the noble son of Vyashva come to us, the Soma-presser:
may there be abundant bounty, consisting of hundreds and thousands.
If one who has sacrificed should ask you, "O you of mysterious form, where are you?"— this Vala, having taken refuge there, stands by the Gomatī river.
Those two guardians of the universe, the gods among gods worthy of sacrifice,
upholders of the cosmic order (*ṛta*) with purified will— those two I worship.
Mitra and Varuṇa, who is of noble wisdom, are like two charioteers in their lineage;
they are well-born from of old, their offspring firm in their vows.
The great Aditi, true to the cosmic order (*ṛta*), brought forth those two all-knowing ones for the sake of divine sovereignty; she, the exceedingly mighty mother, gave birth to them.
Great are Mitra and Varuṇa, sovereign kings, gods and Asuras; upholding the cosmic order, they proclaim the lofty Truth.
The two grandsons of great power, the two sons of Dakṣa, possessed of excellent wisdom, bestowing flowing gifts, they dwell upon the dwelling-place of nourishment.
You two who have gathered together the gifts— celestial and terrestrial refreshments— may your rain-cloud-bearing showers come hither.
Those two who look down from the lofty heaven like herds, the observers of cosmic order (*ṛta*), the sovereign kings established for our homage.
The two observers of Truth, of noble will, have sat down for sovereign rule;
the two Kṣatriyas, firm in their vows, have attained dominion.
Even more skilled than the eye at finding the way, with unblinking vision, the two keen observers have looked down and perceived.
And may the goddess Aditi protect us, and the Nāsatyas;
may the Maruts of increased strength protect us.
O bounteous givers, protect our ship by day and by night; may we, unharmed, be accompanied by your guardians.
For the unassailable Viṣṇu, the giver of good gifts, may we remain unhurt;
O self-moving Sindhu, hear us for our first thought.
We choose that desirable, most excellent, and worthy of protection, which Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman guard.
And may Sindhu, the lord of the waters, the Maruts, and those two Aśvins,
as well as Indra and Viṣṇu— the bounteous ones— be of one accord with us.
For those impetuous heroes indeed strike back against the hostile assault of any man, as a sharp torrent strikes down [the bank].
This one alone thus looks upon many things as the lord of the people;
we follow his ordinances according to our will.
We have followed the ancient, familiar ordinances of universal sovereignty—
the far-famed laws of Mitra and Varuṇa.
He who has measured out the ends of heaven and earth with his rein has filled both worlds with his greatness.
Upward has this Sūrya extended his light from the shelter of heaven,
like the bright Agni, kindled and offered oblations.
He who possesses the power of speech for one whose dwelling is far-reaching, he is the lord of wealth consisting of cattle; for he is indeed the master in bestowing wholesome food.
Therefore, O Sūrya, I address you and both Heaven and Earth at evening and at dawn; may you always rise up for us among those who provide sustenance.
We have won the straight-gliding, silver chariot harnessed for the journey, at the sacrifice of Ukṣaṇyāyana and Suṣāmaṇ.
These two [steeds] of mine, the givers of bay horses, are the bestowers of steeds;
and indeed, they are the bearers of men, the accomplishers of deeds.
With our newest hymn,
we, the inspired poets, have brought together the two great prize-winning steeds, which possess reins and whips.
I invoke your chariot for joint praise among the patrons—
O bulls of unassailable skill, possessors of bull-like wealth!
O Nāsatyas, you two come with your aids for Varo Suṣāman and for his great lineage, O bulls, O possessors of bull-like wealth.
We invoke you both today with oblations, O lords of ample wealth,
you who bestow many refreshments throughout the nights.
O Aśvins, heroes, let your most swift and renowned chariot come hither;
behold the hymns of the zealous one for the sake of glory.
O Aśvins, possessors of bull-like wealth, even if you are provoked to anger, take heed;
for you two, O Rudras, shall carry us across our enemies.
For, O wonder-workers, you fly swiftly all around the universe with your rapid steeds; O Lords of Splendor, you who are honey-colored, you who stir the prayer.
Come to us, O Aśvins, together with wealth that nourishes all, you bounteous lords, rich in heroes, and unshakable.
O Indra and Nāsatyas,
come today to my welcome offering, you gods who are most worthy of being honored by the gods.
For we, like Vyaśva, call upon you two while seeking nourishment;
O wise ones, come hither with your benevolent thoughts.
O seer, praise the Aśvins themselves; will they not surely hear your call? May they drive the Paṇis even closer to us.
O heroes, listen to the son of Vyaśva; may you and Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, acting in harmony, take heed of this my prayer.
O wise ones, day after day grant me a portion of that which has been bestowed by you and brought by you through the patrons, O showerers of blessings.
He who has encompassed you both with sacrifices, like a bride beneath her veil— the Aśvins, being honored, have made him beautiful.
O Aśvins, he who perceives your most spacious protection for men— come around to his dwelling, being well-disposed toward us.
O you who possess bull-like wealth, come to us for our protection;
like two seekers of the sacrifice, you have carried [the offering] here by means of our song.
O Aśvins, may this most excellent hymn, the best of invocations, become for you two a messenger calling you, O heroes.
Whether you are there in the ocean of heaven or rejoicing in the home of nourishment,
O immortal ones, hear my call!
And may that Śvetayāvarī river, the most swift-coursing of all rivers for you two, the Sindhu with its golden path, [bring you here].
O Aśvins, with this well-praised white hymn, you who travel in splendor, come hither.
Yoke, O Vasu, your chariot-drawing horses; harness the well-fed ones.
O Vāyu, drink our honeyed mead; come to our libations.
O Vāyu, Lord of Cosmic Order, Wondrous Son-in-law of Tvaṣṭṛ, we choose your protections for ourselves.
We, possessing pressed soma, seek Vāyu— the son-in-law of Tvaṣṭṛ, the lord of wealth— for splendor, as do other people.
O Vāyu, come from heaven auspiciously; bring us excellent horses. Bring [us] greatness on your chariot with its broad sides.
For we invoke you, the most beautiful in form, in the assemblies of men; like a pressing-stone with a horse’s back, we call upon you with great magnificence.
So do you, O divine Vāyu, exhilarated in your mind as the foremost one, grant us strength, waters, and inspired thoughts.
Agni is the domestic priest at the hymn; the pressing-stones and the sacred grass are at the sacrifice.
With a verse I seek the Maruts, Brahmaṇaspati, and the gods for their desirable aid.
Sing forth to the cattle, to the earth, to the trees, to Dawn and Night, and to the plants!
And you all, O Vasus, possessors of all wealth, be the furtherers of our prayers.
May our sacrifice proceed forth to the gods, O Agni, as the ancient one—
forward to the Ādityas, to Varuṇa of steadfast vows, and to the Maruts who shine with universal splendor.
For all you who possess all-knowledge have indeed become the increasers of Manu, O destroyers of enemies.
O possessors of all-knowledge, with your unharmed protections, grant us a dwelling free from wolves.
Come to us today with one mind, all of you in harmony; O Maruts, Goddess Aditi, come to our dwelling and great household with song and hymn.
O Maruts, come toward our dear offerings for your horses; O Mitra, come forth to the oblations!
May Indra, Varuṇa, and the swift heroes, the Ādityas, sit upon our sacred grass.
We, having trimmed the sacrificial grass and prepared the oblations in due order,
having pressed the Soma, O Varuṇa, call upon you all, like Manu, with our fires kindled.
Come forth, O Maruts, Viṣṇu, Aśvins, and Pūṣan, with a thought directed toward me!
May Indra come first with those who desire to win, he the bull, the slayer of Vṛtra, who is praised by us.
O guileless gods, grant us a flawless protection,
O Vasus, such that this shelter cannot be assailed from afar nor even from near at hand.
For there is kinship with you, O destroyers of enemies; O gods, there is fellowship with you. Proclaim us for former prosperity, and quickly [proclaim us] for new favor.
Now indeed I have sent forth this praise to you, for the enjoyment of your wealth—
O possessors of all knowledge, I, bowing in homage, have released it unto you like a separate stream.
Up has risen for you that Savitṛ, the excellent leader, the one to be chosen; he stands erect.
Bipeds and quadrupeds, seeking their goals, have settled down, as have the winged birds.
God after god we invoke for your protection; god after god for our assistance;
god after god we call upon for the winning of booty, praising them with divine prayer.
For all the gods, being of one mind with Manu, have granted their gifts together;
may they today and in the future be finders of wide space for our progeny.
I proclaim for you, O guileless ones, this gathering of hymns of praise.
No harm, O Varuṇa and Mitra, reaches that mortal who honors your divine ordinances.
He extends his dwelling and spreads forth great refreshments who offers gifts according to your will.
He is propagated with offspring in accordance with the sacred law; unharmed, he prospers in every way.
Without conflict he wins battles; by easy paths he travels his way—whom Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuṇa protect with one accord, they being bounteous givers.
Even on level ground, you have made for him a downward slope; even in difficult terrain, you have made a smooth path.
May even this thunderbolt vanish far away from him, failing its mark.
O you who hold sovereignty dear, whatever truth (*ṛta*) you establish today when the sun rises,
when it sets, when it awakens, O all-knowing ones, or at midday of heaven— [may that be ours].
Or when, O Asuras, at the time of arrival, you grant a shelter to the one who follows the *ṛta* and to the donor;
may we, O Vasus, possessors of all wealth, abide in the midst of that [shelter] of yours.
Whatever good you bestow today upon Manu when the sun has risen, at midday, or at its setting— O possessors of all wealth, you who have offered oblations for the sake of the wise one.
O Universal Sovereigns, we choose from you that protection which is like a son’s, providing manifold succor.
O Ādityas, may those who offer the oblation attain it, through which we may reach what is better.
The thirty-three gods who have sat upon the sacred grass— may they indeed find us and sit down twice.
Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, and the Agnis who bestow gifts together,
accompanied by their wives, are consecrated with the cry of *vaṣaṭ*.
May they be our guardians from the west, from the north, and likewise from below; may they protect us from the east with their entire host.
As the gods desire, so shall it be; none can hinder this of theirs—not even a hostile mortal.
The seven have seven spears; seven are their splendors; they have assumed seven glories.
The one tawny, manifold, noble, and youthful [Agni] puts on his golden ornament.
One, radiant and wise, has taken his seat within the womb among the gods.
One bears an iron axe in his hand, firm among the gods.
One bears the thunderbolt placed in his hand; with it, he strikes down the Vṛtras.
One bears a sharp weapon in his hand; he is pure, fierce, and possesses healing medicines.
One man swells his wealth on the road like a thief; he alone knows the hidden treasures.
The Wide-Strider, the One, has stepped out three steps where the gods rejoice.
Two move with birds and with one [bird] together; they dwell as if on a journey.
The two supreme sovereigns, who drink the clarified butter, have established their most excellent seat in heaven.
Some, chanting, conceived the great Sāman; by means of it, they caused the sun to shine.
For among you, O gods, there is no one who is small, nor any who is a child; all of you are indeed great.
Thus have you been praised, O destroyers of enemies, you who are the thirty-three gods of Manu, worthy of sacrifice.
As such, protect us; as such, help us; and as such, speak for us:
do not lead us far away from the ancestral path of Manu into distant realms.
O you gods who are here, all you Vaiśvānaras,
grant us wide-reaching protection for our cattle and our horses.
