He who sacrifices, has sacrificed, will sacrifice, and prepares the oblation—
he, as a priest, has found favor with Indra.
Whoever offers him the sacrificial cake and the pressed Soma mixed with milk—
Śakra indeed delivers such a person from distress.
His chariot shall be radiant, impelled by the gods, and it shall prevail;
conquering all those who act with hostility.
In his house, the prolific and inexhaustible Iḷā, rich in milch-cows, yields her milk day after day.
O gods, with your constant mixture of milk, [you favor] the husband and wife who, being of one mind, press the Soma and wash it.
The two who eat together from this sacrificial food, moving in unison toward the sacred grass—
those two do not fail in the contests for booty.
They do not disregard even the favor of the gods; they do not seek to hide it; they strive to win great renown.
Possessing sons and possessing daughters, they enjoy the full span of life; both are adorned with golden ornaments.
May the two who accept the oblation and bestow wealth grant their favor for the sake of the immortal;
having struck down the hairy udder, may they perform service among the gods.
We choose the protection of the mountains and of the rivers; we choose the company of Viṣṇu’s companions.
May Pūṣan come, may wealth, and Bhaga; may he who bestows all things bring well-being. May the wide path lead to well-being.
The wise one, free from enemies, has through his mind attained all that belongs to the god;
he is the peerless one among the Ādityas.
So that Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa may be our guardians,
the paths of Ṛta are easy to traverse.
I praise with song Agni for you— the ancient god among the Vasus—
serving him who is beloved by many, like Mitra, the one who brings success to the fields.
Swift is the chariot of the one who favors the gods, like a hero in any battles whatsoever—
he, the sacrificer, who strives to win the minds of the gods, shall surely prevail over those who do not sacrifice.
O sacrificer, you shall not come to harm; O presser of the juice, nor you who are devoted to the gods.
He who, as a sacrificer, strives to win the hearts of the gods, shall surely prevail over those who do not sacrifice.
No one shall overtake him by his ritual act, nor shall he be left behind;
he who, as a sacrificer, strives to win the minds of the gods, shall indeed surpass those who do not sacrifice.
In this there shall be great heroic power and that wealth of swift horses;
for the sacrificer who strives to win the favor of the gods shall surely prevail over those who do not sacrifice.
O Kaṇvas, proclaim the deeds of the impetuous Indra with a song, while he is exhilarated by the soma!
He, the fierce one, who slew Sṛbinda, Anarśani, Pipru, Dāsa, and Ahīśuva, released the waters.
O Indra, you have struck down the lofty height and the vast domain of Arbuda; you have performed that heroic deed.
Boldly, like the roar of a torrent from a mountain, I call upon the fair-cheeked one for aid, you who are renowned for hearing us.
Rejoicing in the Soma-pressings, O Hero, burst open the stall of cattle and horses, as one would shatter a fortress.
If you have taken pleasure in my pressed juice or find delight in my hymn, come from afar according to your own nature.
O Indra, lover of songs, we indeed belong to you as your praisers;
O drinker of Soma, quicken us.
And bring us food, O bounteous one, being well-disposed toward us—food that is inexhaustible; for abundant is your wealth, O Maghavan.
And make us possessors of cattle, of gold, and of horses;
may we grasp [thee] with our invocations.
We invoke Bṛhaduktha, whose hands are swift, for our protection—
he who acts effectively to grant us aid.
He who, even at the moment of assembly, the Vṛtra-slayer Śatakratu, bestows these riches upon his singers— he is the possessor of many treasures.
May he, the powerful Indra, who brings the Dānavas within his grasp, be able to aid us with all his protections.
Sing forth to that Indra, who is a great river of wealth, easy to cross, and the friend of the one who presses the soma.
To the one who comes, the great and steadfast, who has won glory in battles,
the lord of abundance through his might.
No one is the restrainer of his powers or of his gracious gifts;
no one can say, "He does not give."
Surely there is no debt to the zealous priests who press the Soma;
the Soma has not been drunk in vain.
Sing forth to the Worthy One; recite hymns to the Worthy One;
offer prayers to the Worthy One.
The praiseworthy, unimpeded, prize-winning Indra has shattered hundreds and thousands, he who is the increaser of the sacrificer.
Go forth indeed according to your own will toward the invocations of the people;
O Indra, drink of the pressed juices.
Drink, O Indra, of the self-sustaining milk-mixtures, both those which were with Tugrya and this one which is yours.
Pass by the one who utters insults while pressing the juice for his own enjoyment; drink this offered libation that has been pressed.
Go to the three distant realms; go beyond the five peoples, O Indra, looking toward the lowing cows.
As the sun sends forth its ray, so may my songs draw you hither,
like waters flowing together toward the lowlands.
O Adhvaryu, pour out the Soma for the hero with the beautiful jaws;
bring the pressed juice for his drinking.
He who split open the water-cask, who sent the rivers downward, and who placed the cooked milk among the cattle.
O worthy of praise, you slew Vṛtra, Aurṇavābha, and Ahīśuva;
with frost, you struck down Arbuda.
Sing forth the god-given prayer for your fierce, relentless, unconquerable, and all-conquering [Indra].
Indra, who among the gods takes heed of all sacred ordinances in the exhilaration of Soma’s juice, is preeminent.
Hither let those two bay steeds, companions at the feast, with golden manes, carry you toward the prepared food.
O you who are praised by many, may the two bay steeds, lauded by the Priyamedhas,
bring you hither to drink the Soma.
O Vṛtra-slayer, we who have pressed the soma and spread the sacred grass, like waters, sit around you as your praisers at the outpourings of the filter.
O Vasu, when the Soma is pressed, the men who offer hymns sing out to you alone;
O Indra, when will you come to the pressed juice, thirsty for it as to your home, like a bellowing bull?
O bold one, with the Kaṇvas, boldly strike out thousandfold booty; O Maghavan, O far-seeing one, we quickly implore you for that wealth of golden hue consisting of cattle.
O Medhyātithi, protect the singers while they are exhilarated by the soma-juice for Indra—
[that Indra] who is joined with his two bay steeds, who is present at the pressed juice, the wielder of the thunderbolt, whose chariot is golden.
He who is excellent on the left and excellent on the right, the lord praised as one of noble wisdom;
he who is the bringer of thousands, he whose wealth consists of hundreds—Indra, who is honored as the breaker of forts.
He who is bold, he who is unrestrained, he who dwells upon his beard— the one of far-reaching splendor, the shaker, the much-praised, powerful in will like a bull.
Who knows him as he drinks at the pressed juice? What vital power does he bestow?
It is he who, exhilarated by the soma-plant, shatters the fortresses with his might, O fair-cheeked one.
Like a wild elephant with its tusks, he has established his course in many places;
no one can restrain you. Come to the pressed soma; you move as a great one by your own might.
He who, being fierce, unsubdued, and steadfast, is prepared for battle—
if Maghavan Indra hears the call of the singer, he will not stay away but shall come.
Truly, you are thus a bull; our impulse is a bull, unobstructed.
For you, O fierce one, are heard as a bull in the distance, and as a bull you are renowned nearby.
O Śatakratu, your reins are bulls, your golden whip is a bull;
O Maghavan, the chariot is a bull, the two bay steeds are bulls, and you yourself are a bull.
O Bull, let the presser press for you; O Bull, O you of straight-flowing drops, bring [the Soma] hither!
The Bull has flowed toward the bull [Soma] in the rivers, for you, O driver of the bay steeds.
O most powerful Indra, come for the drinking of the sweet Soma;
may this bountiful one, the possessor of noble wisdom, hear our songs, our sacred prayers, and our hymns.
Let the bay steeds yoked to the chariot carry you, who stand upon the chariot;
O Vṛtra-slayer, O Śatakratu, pass even beyond the libations of the noble one, those which belong to others.
O most magnificent one, accept our hymn today as your closest;
may our libations be most pleasant for your exhilaration, O celestial drinker of Soma.
For neither in your teaching nor in mine, nor in the teaching of another, does anyone take delight,
O hero, who has brought us here.
Even Indra himself has said this: "The mind of a woman is impossible to control," and indeed, her resolve is fickle.
Even the two steeds, exhilarated by the intoxicating draught, draw the chariot as a pair;
even so is the yoke of the Bull placed above.
Look downward, not upward; keep your feet closer together. Let them not see your private parts, for you, a woman, have become a Brahmin.
O Indra, come hither with your bay steeds to the beautiful hymn of Kaṇva;
from that heaven you rule, you who have gone to heaven, O you whose wealth is light.
May the Soma-pressing stone, speaking here with its sound, draw you hither—
from that heaven where you rule, O you who go to heaven, O Lord of the Dawn!
Here their rim shakes [the earth] like a wolf shaking sheep;
by the command of yonder heaven, you have gone to heaven, O ye who possess wealth by day!
The Kaṇvas call upon you here for protection and for the winning of booty—
O you who rule from yonder heaven, who have gone to heaven, O you whose wealth is light!
I offer you, the bull, the first draught of the pressed juices, as one who rules from yonder heaven;
go to heaven, O you whose wealth is light!
Come to us with your wisdom, O you who are wise in every way, for our protection!
From the command of that heaven, come from heaven, O you whose wealth is light!
Come to us, O great-minded one, with a thousandfold power and a hundredfold wealth!
From the command of that heaven, come from heaven, O you who are rich in light!
May the Hotṛ priest, established by Manu and worthy of praise among the gods, bring you hither— from that heaven where you rule, O you who dwell in heaven, O Lord of Radiant Wealth!

May your two bay steeds, dripping with exhilaration, carry you hither like two wings carrying a hawk—from that very heaven, by the command of Heaven, O you who dwell in light! O Lord of the Radiant Abode, come to heaven!
Come from afar, O noble one; Svāhā! For the drinking of the Soma.
From the command of yonder heaven, come to heaven, O you who are rich in light.
Come to us, having heard our call; take delight here in our hymns, O you who rule from yonder heaven, who have gone to heaven, O Divāvasu!
Come to us with those steeds of like form, well-groomed, O you whose horses are well-groomed;
from the command of that heaven, go to heaven, O you who are rich in light!
Come from the mountains, from the expanse above the ocean; come from that heaven, O you who rule over heaven, you who have gone to heaven, O Divāvasu!
O Hero, burst open for us thousands of cattle and horses!
From the command of yonder heaven, come to heaven, O you whose wealth is light!
Bring to us thousands, tens of thousands, and hundreds from that yonder heaven, O you who rule from heaven, O you whose wealth is light, you who have gone to heaven!
When Indra and I received a thousand of Vasurocis’s wealth—
the most powerful herd of horses.
Those which are dark-brown, with the speed of the wind, ruddy and swift-gliding,
shine like suns.
In the gifts of the Pārāvata, with swift-gliding wheels,
he stands in the midst of the wood.
Together with Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Viṣṇu, the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus;
being of one accord with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, drink the soma.
With all holy thoughts, with the world, O possessors of vigor, together with heaven, earth, and the mountains,
in harmony with the Dawn and with Sūrya, drink the Soma, O Aśvins.
O Aśvins, together with all the gods—the thrice eleven—here with the waters, the Maruts, and the Bhṛgus; being of one accord with Uṣas and Sūrya, drink the soma.
May you two enjoy the sacrifice; be mindful of my invocation. O two gods, come here to all the libations.
Being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, bring us nourishment.
May you both enjoy this hymn as a youth enjoys a maiden; O two gods, come here to all the libations.
Being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, bring us nourishment.
O Gods, may you enjoy our songs; may you enjoy the sacrifice. Come here to all the libations, O two gods, in harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya. O Aśvins, bring us nourishment.
Like two *hāridrava* birds, you fly toward the forest; like two buffaloes, you descend to the pressed Soma.
In harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, come three times on your circuit.
Like two swans you fly, like travelers on the road; like two buffaloes you descend to the pressed Soma.
In harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, come three times to our dwelling.
Like two hawks you fly for the giving of the oblation; like two buffaloes, you descend toward the pressed Soma. In harmony with Uṣas and with Sūrya, O Aśvins, come three times on your circuit.
Drink and be satisfied, and come hither; bestow progeny and bestow wealth.
Being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, grant us nourishment.
Conquer and be praised; protect us and bestow progeny; grant us wealth.
Being of one mind with the Dawn and with Sūrya, O Aśvins, grant us nourishment.
Slay the enemies and strengthen those who are our friends; bestow progeny upon us and bestow wealth.
Being of one mind with the Dawn and with Sūrya, O Aśvins, grant us nourishment.
Accompanied by Mitra and Varuṇa, and by Dharma, and by the Maruts, come to the call of the singer.
Being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, and with the Ādityas, come, O Aśvins!
Accompanied by the Aṅgirases, by Viṣṇu, and by the Maruts, come to the call of the singer;
being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, come, O Aśvins, together with the Ādityas.
O Ashvins, rich in Rbhus, powerful bulls, accompanied by the Vajas and the Maruts, come to the call of the singer;
being of one mind with Ushas and Surya, come hither with the Adityas.
Quicken the sacred word and quicken our prayers; slay the demons and drive away diseases. Being of one mind with the Dawn and with Sūrya, O Aśvins, [favor] the one who presses the Soma.
Quicken the ruling power and quicken the men; slay the demons and drive away diseases.
O Aśvins, being in harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya, [protect] the one who presses the Soma.
Quicken the milch-cows and quicken the people; slay the demons and drive away diseases. O Aśvins, being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, [protect] the one who presses the Soma.
O Aśvins, like those of Atri, hear the ancient praise of Śyāvāśva, the presser of the soma that distills exhilaration; being of one accord with Uṣas and Sūrya, come from beyond the day’s distance.

Like two creators fashioning streams, O Ashvins, who are exhilarated by the intoxicating draughts of Shyavashva as he presses the juice, come with the Dawn and Surya, being of one accord, across the day.
Like reins, hold fast the sacrificial rites of Śyāvāśva as he presses the juice, O you who flow with exhilaration; being of one mind with Dawn and Sūrya, O Aśvins, come from beyond the day.
Drive your chariot hither; drink the Soma-mead.
Come, O Aśvins, arrive! Seeking your aid, I invoke you both; bestow treasures upon the donor.
When the sacrifice has proceeded with the utterance of homage, O Heroes, come for the drinking of the exhilarating draught!
O Aśvins, arrive; I call you as one seeking aid. Bestow treasures upon the donor.
Satisfy yourselves, O two Gods, with this pressed soma-juice over which the *svāhā* has been uttered.
Come, O Aśvins; arrive! Seeking your aid, I call upon you both; bestow riches upon the donor.
You are the protector of the one who presses the juice and spreads the sacrificial grass; drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu!
You whom they have set apart as your portion—you who conquer all hostile armies, you of wide range, winner of the waters—O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, Lord of the virtuous!

Protect the singer, O Maghavan; protect yourself. Drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu, you who have established that portion for yourself which you, conquering all hostile armies and possessing wide dominion, win along with the waters, accompanied by the Maruts, O Indra, Lord of the Good.
With nourishment, O God, protect us; with power, protect you yourself. Drink the *soma* for exhilaration, O Śatakratu!

You, who have established your portion for yourself—conquering all hostile armies, wide-striding, winning the waters together with the Maruts—O Indra, Lord of the Good, [come] accompanied by the Maruts.
The progenitor of heaven, the progenitor of earth—O Śatakratu, drink the Soma for exhilaration!
You who have established this portion for yourself, overcoming all hostile armies, O wide-striding Indra, Lord of the Good, accompanied by the Maruts, conqueror of waters.
You are the progenitor of horses, the progenitor of cattle; O Śatakratu, drink the Soma for exhilaration!
You who have established this portion for yourself—conquering all hostile armies and possessing wide dominion—you, Indra, Lord of the Good, accompanied by the Maruts, are the winner of the waters.
O Lord of the Stone, make great the hymn of the Atris; drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu!
You who, conquering all hostile armies, possess wide-reaching power, you who win the waters with the Maruts—O Indra, Lord of the Good, [drink]!
Hear of Śyāvāśva as he presses the juice, just as you heard of Atri while performing his rites;
O Indra, you alone have protected Trasadasyu in the battle for men, strengthening him with sacred prayers.

O Indra, Lord of Might, you have favored this prayer in the battles against Vṛtra; with all your aids, O slayer of Vṛtra, blameless wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of the Soma at the midday libation.
O fierce Indra, Lord of Might, overcoming hostile armies with all your aids,
O Vṛtra-slayer, blameless wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of the Soma at the midday libation.
O sole ruler of this world, you reign, O Indra, Lord of Might, with all your aids.
O slayer of Vṛtra, blameless wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of the Soma at the midday libation.
O sole lord of power, Indra, you alone, accompanied by your six steeds, keep [the enemies] at bay with all your aids.
O Vṛtra-slayer, blameless wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of the Soma at the midday libation.
O Lord of Might, O Indra, you are the master of both security and exertion through all your protections;
O slayer of Vṛtra, O blameless wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of the Soma at the midday libation.
You have helped for the sake of the nobility, yet you have not helped me, O Lord of Might, Indra, with all your aids.
O Slayer of Vṛtra, blameless wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of the Soma at the midday libation.
Listen now to the chanting of Śyāvāśva as he performs his rites, just as you listened to Atri when he performed his deeds.
O Indra, you alone aided Trasadasyu in the conquest of men, increasing his sovereign powers.
For you two are the officiating priests of the sacrifice, the winners in contests and ritual acts;
O Indra and Agni, take heed of that!
O you two who are eager, who travel in the chariot, slayers of Vṛtra, and unconquered— Indra and Agni, take heed of this!
O Indra and Agni, the men have milked this intoxicating honey for you with the stones; take heed of it!
May you two enjoy the sacrifice for the sake of the offering; O Indra and Agni, heroes who share the same praise, come to the pressed Soma!
O Indra and Agni, heroes, may you take pleasure in these libations by which you have carried away the offerings; come hither!
O Indra and Agni, heroes, come to this well-praised hymn of mine that follows the path of the Gāyatrī; take pleasure in it.
Come with the gods who travel at dawn, O you two noble lords of wealth,
Indra and Agni, for the drinking of the Soma.
O Indra and Agni, hear the invocation of Śyāvāśva as he presses the juice, and that of the Atris, for the drinking of the Soma.
Thus have I called you both for aid, just as the wise sages have called,
O Indra and Agni, for the drinking of the Soma.
I choose the protection of Indra and Agni, who are accompanied by Sarasvatī,
they for whom the Gāyatra hymn is sung.
I have praised Agni, the one worthy of hymns; I shall worship Agni with the *īḷā* invocation.
May Agni anoint the gods for us, for as a seer he moves between both assemblies on his mission as messenger. Let all others, the insignificant ones, perish!
O Agni, with our newest speech, suppress the praise of these men within their own bodies; subdue the hostilities of the stingy ones.
May all the enmities of the enemy depart from here; may the adversaries perish, and may all others who oppose us be destroyed.
O Agni, we offer these prayers to you like clarified butter poured into your mouth;
make them known among the gods, for you are the ancient, auspicious messenger of Vivasvat. Let all others perish!

Agni bestows that very vital power for each person according as they pray; he, the oblation of strength among the Vasus, bestows well-being, prosperity, and joy for every invocation of the gods. May all others perish!
He has been perceived through his most powerful and wondrous deed;
he is the Hotṛ-priest of all the eternal ones, encompassed by sacrificial fees. He bestows what is to be offered. May all others, however, perish!
Agni is the one born among the gods; Agni knows the secret of mortals.
Agni is the giver of wealth; Agni, well-invoked with a new [offering], throws open the doors. Let all others, however many they be, perish!
Agni dwells among the gods; he dwells among the clans worthy of sacrifice.
With joy, the god who is worthy of sacrifice among the gods nourishes many poetic insights throughout the whole world, like the earth. May all others, the base ones, perish!

The Agni who dwells among the seven human tribes, who rests within all the rivers—to him we have come, to the one with three abodes, the greatest slayer of Dasyus for Mandhātṛ, to Agni, the foremost in sacrifices. May all others, however insignificant, be destroyed!
Agni, the sage, dwells in the three triadic domains of the sacrifice;
may he, the inspired priest and our consecrated messenger, worship and satisfy the thirty-three gods here. May all others, the base ones, be destroyed!
O Agni, you alone rule over wealth among our lives and among the gods, O Primordial One;
the waters flowing in all directions go around you with their own channels. May all others who are equal to them be destroyed.

O Indra and Agni, you two, as conquerors, bestow wealth upon us well—that wealth by which we may overcome even the firm and solid things in battles, like Agni consuming forests with the wind. May all others who are equal [to us] fall to pieces!
For we do not exclude you two; rather, we worship Indra alone, the most powerful hero among men.
May he come to us at any time with his steed for the winning of booty; may he come for the winning of wisdom. Let all others who are equal to him perish!
For Indra and Agni dwell as lords over the midst of the offerings;
they, the two sages, being questioned with wisdom, bestow the gathered thought upon the one who seeks their friendship, O heroes. May all others, the lowly ones, be destroyed!
Sing forth with a sacrificial song to Indra and Agni, as Nabhaka did;
they for whom this entire world exists, and this great heaven and earth bear wealth within their lap. Let all others who are base perish!
Offer prayers like Nabhaka unto Indra and Agni;
they who have opened the ocean with its seven foundations and its downward-opening gate—Indra, ruling by his might—let all others who are base perish!
Tear it away as of old, like the tangled growth of a creeping vine; strike down the power of the Dāsa.
May we, with Indra’s aid, divide among ourselves that accumulated wealth of his. Let all others perish, even the lowly ones!

O Indra and Agni, when these people invoke you with various songs, may we, through our own men, overcome those who attack us and conquer those who seek to vanquish us; let all others perish, however many they be.
The two white ones that rise from heaven day after day according to the ordinances of Indra and Agni—the rivers flow forth, released from their bond; may all the others perish!
Many are your aids, O Indra, and many your praises, O Son of the Impeller, Lord of the Bay Steeds!
May the riches of the hero come to us without fail, and may our prayers now be fulfilled. Let all others who are equal to them perish!

Sharpen him with well-fashioned hymns—the brilliant warrior worthy of praise—especially him who by his might shatters the eggs of Śuṣṇa; may he win the water-laden waters. May all others, the insignificant ones, be destroyed!

Sharpen him, the true hero, who follows the seasons and performs the sacrifice well—him who indeed brings down the testicles of Śuṣṇa with his arrows and wins the sunlit waters. May all others who are equal to him perish!
Thus, for Indra and Agni, a new song has been proclaimed like that of the fathers, like Māndhātṛ, and like Aṅgiras.
With your triple-layered protection, guard us; may we be masters of riches.
To him for our great prosperity—to Varuṇa and the Maruts, who are most wise—sing forth a hymn;
he who protects the thoughts of men as one guards cattle. May all others, the lowly ones, perish!

Him indeed we celebrate with a song in common, and with the hymns of the fathers, and with the praises of Nābhāka—him who dwells at the source of the rivers, he whose sisters are seven, he who is in the midst; may all others, the base ones, be destroyed!
He has embraced the nights; by his creative power he has established the dawns. He is visible all around the universe.
Following his law, the longing ones—the three Dawns—have caused him to grow. May all others who are inferior perish!
He who established the quarters upon the earth, he who is beautiful to behold—he is the measurer of the ancient station;
that is the domain of Varuṇa, for he is the guardian, as it were, the noble one. Let all others, however they may be, perish!

He who is the upholder of the worlds, who knows the secret and hidden names of the dawns—he, the seer, nourishes many poetic insights like the sky assumes its manifold forms. May all others, the insignificant ones, perish!
In whom all poetic insights are centered as if upon a nave—worship Trita with fervor! Like cows in a pen, they have harnessed their horses for union; may all others perish, even those who are near!
He who lies within their garment, encompassing all their births, and touching all the abodes of Varuṇa before our home—all the gods follow his ordinance; let all others perish, the base ones alike.
He is the secret ocean; swift as heaven, he ascends when he has deposited the sacrificial formula (*yajus*) within these [fingers].
With his flaming foot, he has struck down the magical illusions and ascended to the firmament. May all others, the petty ones, be destroyed!

He whose white, far-seeing [rays] preside over the three earths, and who thrice filled the higher realms—he, the firm seat of Varuṇa, rules over the seven; let all others, however many they be, perish.

He who, according to his laws, has made the white one his upper garment and the black one his lower, he has measured out the ancient abode; by his pillar he has propped apart the two worlds, as the Unborn supported the sky. May all others, the insignificant, perish!
The Asura, the all-knowing, propped up the sky; he measured out the breadth of the earth.
He, the sovereign, took his seat over all beings—all these are the sacred ordinances of Varuṇa.
Thus praise Varuṇa, the lofty one; pay homage to the wise guardian of immortality.
May he grant us a triple-layered shelter; may Heaven and Earth protect us in their lap.
O God Varuṇa, sharpen this prayer of one who strives for it; sharpen his will and skill.
May we mount the ship that provides a good crossing, by which we may cross over all difficulties.
O Aśvins, the pressing-stones and the inspired poets have, through their prayers, caused you both to hasten hither for the drinking of Soma, O Nāsatyas. May all others who are inferior perish!
Just as the sage Atri invoked you with songs, O Aśvins,
Nāsatyas, for the drinking of the Soma— let all others who are base perish!
Thus have I called upon you both for aid, as the wise sages have called, O Nāsatyas, for the drinking of Soma; let all others who are base perish!
These songs and hymns of the inspired sage, the wise Agni, who performs the sacrifice unassailable, go forth.
O Jātavedas, O all-beholding Agni, for you who take delight in this,
I generate a beautiful hymn of praise.
Truly, O Agni, your sharp flames are like rays of light;
with your teeth you devour the forests.
The bay horses, smoke-bannered and driven by the wind, strive toward heaven; the fires spread out in various directions.
These various fires, kindled separately, have become visible together like the banners of the dawns.
Black dust rises from the feet at the departure of Jātavedas,
when Agni spreads across the earth.
Making the plants his food and devouring them, Agni does not grow weary,
even as he returns again to the young ones.
Bending down with his tongues and flickering with his flame,
Agni shines resplendent among the forests.
O Agni, your seat is in the waters; you penetrate the plants, and being in their womb, you are born again.
O Agni, that flame of yours shines forth from the clarified butter when it is offered,
kissing the sacrificial ladles at its mouth.
To Agni, the ordainer, whose food is the bull and whose food is the cow, who bears the Soma upon his back— to him let us do honor with hymns of praise.
And we, O Hotṛ of most excellent wisdom, approach you with homage, O Agni, with kindled fuel.
And we invoke you, O pure Agni, who are offered oblations, like Bhr̥gu, like Manu,
and like Aṅgiras.
For you, O Agni, are kindled by fire, as a sage by a sage, being what you are;
as a friend by a friend, you are enkindled.
As such, O Agni, grant to the inspired singer who offers oblations wealth in thousands, and food accompanied by heroic sons.
O Agni, brother, created by strength, with ruddy horses and pure vows,
take pleasure in this hymn of mine.
And may my praise, O Agni,
reach you like lowing cows seeking the stall for one who welcomes them.
To you, O best of Angirases, all these well-settled people have turned separately,
O Agni, out of desire.
The wise, the intelligent, the inspired singers have urged Agni with their prayers to sit at the feast.
Thee, O Agni, the winner of booty in battles, they magnify as the bearer and the invoker while they extend the sacrifice.
For you are the same in many places, the lord over all the tribes;
we invoke you in the battles.
Praise him who, when invoked, Agni, shines brightly with clarified butter;
may he hear this our call.
As such, we invoke you, Jātavedas, who hears us, O Agni, you who strike away our enemies.
I praise this Agni, the king of the people, the wonderful overseer of the sacred laws; may he indeed hear us.
We urge Agni, who stirs all life, like a prize-winning youth set to the race, as we urge a steed to win the prize.
Slaying the obstructors and driving away our enemies, burning the *rakṣases* at all times, O Agni, shine forth with your sharp flame!
O Agni, best of the Aṅgirases, whom the people kindle in the manner of Manu— be mindful of my word.
O Agni, whether you are born of heaven or born of the waters, O you who are strengthened by power,
we invoke you with our songs.
For you indeed, these people, all these well-settled communities, each separately urge forth the nourishment for you to eat.
O Agni, may those who are well-disposed toward us, who behold men, cross over all days; may we overcome all difficulties.
We implore with our joyful hearts Agni, the delightful one, beloved by many, the fierce one with purifying luster.
O Agni, you who are rich in light, like the sun emitting its rays,
you boldly strike down the darknesses.
O powerful one, we beg of you that gift which never fails; from you, O Agni, comes desirable wealth.
Worship Agni with fuel; awaken the guest with offerings of ghee;
pour the oblations into him.
O Agni, take pleasure in my hymn; grow strong by this prayer of mine; graciously accept our well-spoken verses.
I place Agni at the forefront as my messenger; I address him, the bearer of oblations, so that he may seat the gods here.
O Agni, your great, bright flames rise up as you are kindled and shine forth.
O beloved Agni, may my ladles, dripping with ghee, approach you; graciously accept our oblations.
I invoke Agni—the delightful invoker, the officiating priest, of wondrous luster and radiant light; may he indeed hear us.
The ancient Hotṛ, worthy of praise, the beloved Agni of prophetic insight,
the glory of the sacrifices.
O Agni, best of the Aṅgirases, graciously accepting these oblations in their proper sequence, lead the sacrifice according to the seasons.
O kindled one, O truthful and bright-shining Agni, bring here the divine host,
you who are wise.
We seek the inspired singer, the guileless invoker, whose banner is smoke, the radiant one, the signal of sacrifices.
O Agni, protect us; O God, ward off those who seek to harm us. Shatter our enemies, O you who are made of strength!
Agni, adorning his own body with an ancient hymn,
the seer has been magnified by the inspired singer.
I invoke Agni, the Son of Strength, whose radiance is purifying,
at this well-performed sacrifice.
O Agni, you who possess the majesty of Mitra, with your bright flame, sit down upon the sacrificial grass together with the gods for our sake.
The mortal who serves the god Agni within his own home—
for him indeed he shines forth wealth.
Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of this earth;
he quickens the seeds of the waters.
O Agni, your pure, bright, and radiant flames rise upward;
your lights are your rays of splendor.
For you, O Agni, Lord of Light, are the master of desirable gifts;
may I be your praiser under your protection.
O Agni, the wise impel you with their thoughts;
may our songs increase you.
We choose the friendship of Agni, the undeceived, the self-dependent, the messenger who ever utters his song.
Agni, whose vows are most pure, is the pure sage, the pure seer; offered with oblations, he shines brightly, pure.
And may my meditations and songs increase you at all times; O Agni, be mindful of our friendship.
O Agni, if I were you, or if you indeed were I,
then may your blessings here be fulfilled.
For you, O Agni, are the Vasu, the lord of treasures, and you possess radiant wealth;
may we abide in your favor.
O Agni, to you whose vows are firm, our songs rise up like rivers flowing toward the ocean, lowing like cows.
I glorify with my hymns Agni— the youthful lord of the people, the seer, the all-consuming, and the one who stirs many things.
We, seeking to reach him with hymns of praise, [approach] Agni, the charioteer of sacrifices, who possesses sharp jaws and is firm.
O Agni, may this singer abide in thee, O Truthful One; have mercy on him, O Purifier.
For you, O Agni, are the steadfast one who sits at the feast, ever watchful like a sage; you shine in the sky.
O Agni, O Sage, before we fall into misfortunes and before the oppressors,
prolong our life, O Vasu.
Truly, those who kindle Agni and spread the sacrificial grass in due order—
those whose youthful Indra is their friend.
Great indeed is their fuel, abundant their praise, and wide their sacrificial post— those whose friend is the youthful Indra.
Without fighting, the hero, surrounded by warriors, conquers those who are besieged in battle— he whose youthful Indra is his friend.
As soon as he was born, the slayer of Vṛtra seized his bow; he questioned his mother:
"Who are the fierce ones? Who indeed are renowned?"
Śavasī shall speak against you; like a warrior on the mountain, she shall fight him who seeks enmity toward you.
And hear this, O Maghavan: whatever one desires from you, you fulfill it; whatever you make firm, that indeed becomes firm.
When Indra, the maker of battles, goes to the fray seeking good horses, he is the best of charioteers among charioteers.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, utterly scatter all assailants in every direction;
be for us the one who possesses the most glorious renown.
May Indra place our chariot at the front for the sake of victory—
a chariot which the malevolent cannot harm.
May we avoid your enemies; O Śakra, you are ready to give. O Indra, may we go to those who possess cattle.
O wielder of the stone, even when moving slowly, they possess horses and a hundredfold wealth; they are eloquent and free from blemish.
For upward indeed do your hundreds and thousands of bounteous gifts rise day after day; you bestow them upon those who sing your praises.
For we know you, O Indra, as the winner of wealth, who breaks even that which is firm,
like one who seizes a dwelling-place.
O Sage, let the drops exhilarate you, even though you are preeminent;
O Bold One, since we entreat you for the sake of the Paṇi.
O wealthy one, bring to us from him that knowledge— the man who, though possessing riches, was stingy and withheld [the gift] for the sake of bestowing wealth.
These Soma-offering friends of yours, O Indra, look out for you,
like those who possess abundance looking for their cattle.
And though you are deaf, we call you from afar here for our protection, you who have ears that hear.
If you should hear this invocation, and if you should perform what is difficult to accomplish,
then become our closest kinsman.
Whatever distress we have experienced when following after thee,
O Indra, grant us the gift of cattle.
O Lord of Might, we have supported you as the aged support a pillar;
we desire you in our dwelling place.
Sing a hymn of praise to Indra, the warrior of many heroic deeds,
whom no one can withstand in battle.
O Bull, I pour out the pressed juice for you to drink;
satisfy yourself and enjoy the exhilaration.
Let not the foolish, seeking to harm you, nor those who mock you, deceive you; do not favor those who hate sacred prayer.
Here, let these [soma juices], rich in milk, exhilarate you for great bounty;
drink like a wild bull at a lake.
Those deeds which the slayer of Vṛtra, whether ancient or new, has performed in the distance—
proclaim them in the assemblies.
Indra drank the pressed juice of Kadru at the thousand-armed [contest];
there he displayed his manly prowess.
That truth was known to Turvaśa and Yadu as something not to be disregarded;
he has accomplished it through his victorious effort.
I shall praise your common [deed], the one that carries you across for men and pierces through wealth consisting of cattle.
Like Ṛbhukṣan, you are not to be restrained in our hymns—you who strengthened Tugra’s son;
Indra, [come] to the pressed Soma.
He who indeed cut apart the wide mountain for Triśoka, so that it might open a path for the cattle to emerge from their stall.
Whatever you intend or plan while exhilarated, and whatever you seek to accomplish—that do not do, O Indra; have mercy!
For even a small deed performed by one such as you is heard of upon the earth;
O Indra, let your mind come hither.
These songs of praise and these eulogies are indeed yours,
O Indra, when you show us mercy.
Do not strike us for one offense, nor for two, nor for three; O Hero, do not slay us for many.
For I am indeed afraid of one such as you, O fierce one, who shatters all adversaries, the wondrous subduer of enemies.
O Lord of abundant wealth, let me not suffer the loss of a friend, nor the loss of a son;
let your mind be turned back toward us.
O men, what friend indeed, being unprovoked, has spoken thus to his friend: "Who is it that abandons us and flees from us?"
Thus, O bull, when the soma is pressed, you have unremittingly brought many boons,
moving like a gambler toward his winnings.
I grasp for you these two bay steeds, yoked by our words, together with the well-faring chariot,
so that you may grant them to those who offer prayers.
Shatter all enemies; strike down those who oppress us and destroy our adversaries;
bring to us that desirable wealth.
O Indra, whatever desirable wealth has been placed in a stronghold, in a firm place, or in a secure hiding spot— bring that here to us.
Of you, whose gift the entire human race knows as abundant,
bring here that desirable wealth.
O Indra, Lord of abundant wealth, we belong to one such as you, our leader; we are yours, O driver of the two bay steeds.
For we know you, O wielder of the stone, to be the true giver of refreshments;
we know you to be the giver of riches.
O you of a hundredfold aid, O Lord of a hundred powers, whose greatness the poets celebrate with their songs.
Truly, that mortal is well-guided whom the Maruts, Aryaman, and Mitra— those who are free from malice— protect.
Bestowing wealth in cattle and horses along with heroic strength, he, impelled by the Ādityas, prospers; he is ever possessed of much-desired riches.
We beg that Indra for bounty—him who is powerful and fearless;
we beg him, the lord of wealth.
For in him are all fearless aids found together;
let the bay steeds, the swift coursers, bring him—the possessor of abundant wealth—to the pressed juice for exhilaration.

That exhilaration of yours which is most excellent, O Indra, which is the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, which wins the light of heaven with men, and which is invincible in battles— [that exhilaration we seek].
O you who are invincible, possessor of all boons, worthy of renown, and the conqueror in battles—O most powerful Vasu, come to our libations; may we reach a stall filled with cattle.
O most magnificent one, as you did for us in the past, grant us wealth in cattle, horses, and chariots;
bestow upon us wide space.
O Hero, I truly find no end to your bounty;
O Maghavan, wielder of the stone, you have always favored our prayers with spoils of war.
He who is lofty, the friend who makes [his name] heard—he, praised by many, knows all generations.
All human beings of every age call upon that powerful Indra with uplifted ladles.
May he, the possessor of many riches, the Maghavan, the slayer of Vṛtra, be our protector in battles for booty and our leader from the front.
Sing with your song to the hero among you during the exhilarations of the soma-juice— to the great and wise one, to the one renowned by name as Indra, the powerful one, according to our word.
O much-invoked one, you have bestowed wealth upon our person, you have bestowed riches, and you have bestowed a prize-winning steed in the contests;
do so now as well.
Him who rules over all treasures, who indeed overcomes even this form of his;
he now truly transcends those who seek to harm him.
We praise you greatly for your swift aid—to the bounteous one who comes readily and moves with speed.
With sacrifices and songs, you seek to win the favor of the all-encompassing Maruts; I sing to you with reverence and a hymn.
They who cause [the waters] to fall with their rushes over the ridges of the mountains—
[I seek] the sacrifice of those who roar loudly and the favor of those who roar with great might at the rite.
O Indra, most powerful one, bring us wealth that shatters the evil-minded, a wealth worthy of our alliance— O you whose mind is stirred, bring the most excellent wealth, O you whose mind is stirred!
O winner, O excellent winner, O fierce one, O wondrous one, O most brilliant, O true one!
O sovereign ruler who prevails by force, [bestow] the victorious Bhujyu, the subduer, foremost in the contests for booty.
May he who, being godless, has taken such a gift as this, come hither—
just as Vaśa Aśvya took [the wealth] from Pṛthuśravas Kānīta at the breaking of this dawn.
Sixty thousand [cows] for the horses, ten thousand for the seat, twenty hundred camels;
ten hundred dark-brown mares, ten hundred ruddy ones, and ten thousand cows.
Ten dark-brown horses, winners of wealth, swift and with flowing manes,
have turned the felly downward with their speed.
The gifts of Pṛthuśravas, the son of Kānīta, who is most bountiful—by giving a golden chariot, he has become the most generous patron; he has achieved the highest renown.
O Vāyu, come to us for great continuity, for the sacrifice, and for splendor;
for we have performed much for you to give, even to give great wealth instantly.
He who travels with horses at dawn, [master] of thrice seven times seventy [cows],—
O Soma-drinker, drinker of the bright and purified [juice], come for the sake of giving along with these Soma-pressers and these Soma-libations.
He who himself has gladdened even me with this wonderful gift for the sake of bestowing it—
O Araṭva, O Akṣa, O Nahuṣa, you of good deeds, he is the one of excellent wisdom, most skillful toward the doer of good deeds.
To the one worthy of praise, the wondrous one who is the self-ruling lord of heaven, and to Vāyu who bathes in clarified butter—
this very thing has now been sent forth, impelled by the horses, impelled through the mid-air, and impelled by the hounds.
Then, for the vigorous one, there were sixty thousand beloved [gifts],
like stallions indeed, yet like bulls.
Like a herd of cows, the castrated ones come together; the castrated ones come toward me.
And when he bellowed for a hundred camels in the troop of Caratha,
and for twenty hundred among the Śvitnas.
A hundred [gifts] the inspired singer received from Dāsa Balbūtha and Tarukṣa.
These people here, O Vāyu, rejoice in thee; protected by Indra they rejoice, protected by the gods.
Then this great woman, turning toward Vaśa Aśvya, is led forth adorned with golden ornaments.
Great is the protection you grant, O great Varuṇa and Mitra, to the one who offers oblations.
O Ādityas, no harm shall reach him whom you guard from malice; yours are the protections that leave no room for distress, your protections that are well-bestowed.
O Ādityas, gods, you who know the removal of evils;
like birds spreading their wings above, grant us protection. Unassailable are your aids; well-aiding are your aids.
Extend that protection over us, as birds spread their wings;
O possessors of all wealth, we meditate upon all your secure shelters. Your aids are free from danger; your aids are truly excellent.
To whomsoever the wise ones have granted a dwelling and a means of life—these Ādityas indeed rule over all the wealth of Manu. Unfailing are your aids; well-aiding are your aids.
May evils avoid us as a charioteer avoids difficult roads; may we abide in the protection of Indra and in the favor of the Ādityas. Your aids are free from danger; yours are well-bestowing aids.
O gods, the person who avoids what is given by you suffers want; O Ādityas, that which you have bestowed upon us is abundant. Your aids are faultless; your aids are well-bestowing.
Neither fierce heat nor heavy burden shall overcome him whom you, O Ādityas, have granted wide protection. Unassailable are your aids; well-aiding are your aids.
O gods, we belong to you, like warriors in their armor. You protect us from great sin, you from small; yours are the aids that cause no harm, yours are the well-bestowing aids.
May Aditi protect us; may Aditi grant us shelter—she who is the mother of Mitra, of the wealthy Aryaman, and of Varuṇa. Your aids are free from harm; your aids are well-bestowing.
O Gods, whatever protection, refuge, auspiciousness, and health there is—whatever threefold shelter provides defense—grant that to us. Your aids are free from harm; your aids are truly effective.
O Ādityas, look down upon us as spies from the riverbank; lead us along a good path with easy crossings, like swift horses, for your aids are free from danger—your aids are well-bestowed.
There is no blessing here for the one who harbors demons, nor for the one who seeks to harm us, nor even for the one who approaches with malice.
But there is blessing for the cow and for the milch-cow, and for the hero who strives for glory. Unfailing are your aids; well-aiding are your aids.
O Gods, whatever evil deed exists, whether it be manifest or hidden—O Trita Āptya, place all that far away from us! Unfailing are your aids; well-aiding are your aids.
Whatever evil dream is among our cattle, and whatever is among us, O Daughter of Heaven—O Vibhāvarī, carry that away to Trita Āptya! Unfailing are your aids; well-aiding are your aids.
Whether they fashion a golden ornament or a garland, O Daughter of Heaven, we entrust all evil dreams to Trita Āptya. Your aids are free from blemish; your aids are well-bestowing.
To him who has come for that food, for that labor, for that portion— to Trita and to Dvita, carry away the evil dream! Unfailing are your aids; well-aiding are your aids.
Just as we pay back a sixteenth part, just as an eighth part, just as a debt, even so do we pay back all evil dreams to Āptya. Unassailable are your aids; well-aiding are your aids.
We have conquered today; we have prevailed; we have become free from sin.
O Uṣas, may that evil dream from which we were afraid fade away. Yours are the aids that bring no fear; yours are the well-bestowing aids.
I, the wise one, have partaken of the sweet food of the one who is most skilled in providing wide space;
he whom all the gods and mortals approach, calling him "Honey."
Passing through, may you become Aditi; may you be the one who averts the divine wrath.
O Indu, enjoying the friendship of Indra, may you advance toward riches like a draft-animal following its yoke.
We have drunk the Soma; we have become immortal; we have reached the light; we have found the gods.
What can hostility now do to us? And what, O Immortal One, can the malice of a mortal do?
Be gracious to our heart when drunk, O Indu; O Soma, be as kind as a father to his son. Like a friend to a friend, O wise one of wide renown, prolong our life, O Soma, that we may live.
These gladdening drops, when drunk, grant me glory and deliverance; like oxen harnessed to a chariot, they have bound me together at my joints.
May these Soma-drops protect me from a fracture of the limbs and keep me far from lameness.
Like fire churned forth, kindle me; grant us vision and make us more prosperous. For then, O Soma, in your exhilaration, I think you act like a wealthy man toward nourishment.
With an eager mind, may we partake of your pressed juice, as if of ancestral wealth. O King Soma, prolong our lives, as the sun lengthens the days and the mornings.
O King Soma, be gracious unto us for our well-being; we are your devotees, so take note of that.
O Indu, our skill and our spirit are stirred; do not deliver us over to the will of the enemy.
For you, O Soma, are the guardian of our bodies; as one who beholds men, you have settled within every limb.
If we violate your sacred laws, O God, be gracious to us as a good friend for our ultimate welfare.
May I be united with that friend whose heart is soft, who, when drunk, shall not harm me, O Lord of the Tawny Steeds.
This Soma which has been deposited within us—for its sake I go to Indra to extend my life.
Those ailments have departed, the maladies have vanished; the powers of darkness have fled and are afraid.
Soma has ascended into us, all-pervading; we have reached that place where they prolong our life.
O Fathers, that immortal drop which, when drunk, has entered into the hearts of mortals—that Soma we shall worship with an oblation; may we abide in his mercy and his good favor.
O Soma, being in harmony with the Fathers, you have extended yourself across heaven and earth. To you, O Indu, we pay worship with this oblation; may we become masters of riches.
O protecting gods, speak for us; let neither sleep nor idle chatter have power over us.
May we, ever dear to Soma, with heroic sons, proclaim our wisdom at the assembly.
O Soma, you are the bestower of vital strength upon us from every side; as one who beholds men, enter us as the finder of light.
O Indu, being in harmony with us through your aids, protect us from behind and also from the front.
Sing forth to Indra, the most bountiful, as he is known to you—
he who, as Maghavan, rich in many treasures, bestows gifts upon his singers as if by the thousands.
Like Śatānīka, he advances boldly; he slays the Vṛtras for the sake of the donor. Like streams from a mountain, the gifts of him who provides much nourishment overflow.
O Indra, lover of songs, may these pressed drops, these intoxicating juices, come to you;
O hero, wielder of the thunderbolt, they fill you for the sake of bounty, as waters fill a lake that is their home.
Drink this most sweet honeyed draught, which is invigorating, furthering, eloquent, and free from harm;
for, being exhilarated, do thou boldly bestow upon us [wealth] by thyself, as if scattering it like small grain.
Come swiftly toward our hymn of praise, like a horse urged on by its drivers;
O self-powerful Indra, the milch-cows provide for you that which the Kaṇvas offer as gifts.

Like a fierce hero, we have approached you with homage—you, the pervasive one whose wealth is inexhaustible. O wielder of the thunderbolt, like water poured from a well, our prayers flow forth toward you, O Indra.
Whether you are now [at home], or at the sacrifice, or upon the earth—
from that place, O mighty one, come to our sacrifice with your swift and fierce steeds, O fierce one!
Swift are those bay steeds of thine, rapid and impetuous like the winds;
with them thou goest around to the offspring of Manu, and with them thou beholdest the entire realm of light.
For this much of thy cow-abounding favor we entreat thee, O Indra:
just as thou didst protect Medhyātithi, O Maghavan, and as thou didst [protect] Nīpātithi in the contest for wealth.
As you did for Kaṇva, O Maghavan, as for Trasadasyu, as for Paktha of the ten forts, and as you were present for Gośarya and Ṛjiśvan— O Indra, grant us wealth in cattle and gold.
Sing forth for our assistance the highly renowned Śakra,
the bestower of great wealth, who grants desirable riches like a thousandfold bounty to the one who presses the Soma and offers praise.

The weapons of this Indra have a hundred edges and are invincible; his great impetuous powers swell like a mountain rich in nourishment for the sake of the bounteous patrons, when the pressed juices have exhilarated him.
When the pressed drops have exhilarated him for his beloved [friend], O Vasu, the libation has been established for me like waters; it flows for the donor like milch-cows.
For you, the unerring one who is invoked for aid, our inspired thoughts flow like streams of honey.
O Vasu, the Soma drops, being invoked, have been set by us within our hymns of praise.
Come to us at our Soma sacrifice, O performer of good rites; hastening like a courser, you bestow your gifts.
O giver of good things, those praises which they offer to you are pleasing; you take delight in the invocation of the worshipper.

Forward [I praise] the fierce hero, the separator, the winner of wealth, the lord of great bounty. Like a well, O wielder of the thunderbolt, you have ever overflowed with riches for the donor through your generosity.
Whether you are now in the far distance, or on the earth, or in heaven—
O great-minded Indra, yoking your two bay steeds, come hither, lofty one, with your lofty companions.
Your bay steeds, swift as charioteers and unerring, surpass the might of the wind;
with them you strike down the Dasyu from the mortal man, and with them you encompass the sun.
O Vasu, O Hero, may we recognize as much of this from you as something ever new, so that you might protect Etaśa in the decisive contest for wealth, and Vaśa at Daśavraja.
As you did for Kaṇva at the sacrifice and the rite, O Maghavan, in the house of Dīrghanītha;
as you did for Gośarya, O wielder of the stone, so grant me a wealth of cattle, resplendent with bay horses.
Just as you, O Indra, drank the pressed Soma with Manu Sāṃvaraṇi,
so too, O Maghavan, [you drank it] with Nīpātithi, Medhyātithi, Puṣṭigu, and Śruṣṭigu.
Pārṣadvāṇa seated Praskaṇva together, the aged man who had been cast down and was lying there.
Protected by you, the seer Dasyave Vṛka sought to win thousands of cattle.
He who does not fail because of hymns, he who is conscious and the inspirer of seers—
to that Indra speak with a new prayer, as one who is unharmed for the sake of enjoyment.
To him for whom they have sung the seven-headed hymn, three-layered, in the highest station—
he has indeed roared through all these worlds, and from him manly power was born.
Him who is the giver of riches to us, that Indra we invoke;
for we know his most recent favor—may we go to a stall full of cattle.
O Vasu, he for whom you strive to grant gifts attains an increase of wealth.
O Maghavan Indra, lover of songs, we, having pressed the soma, invoke you.
Never art thou barren, O Indra;
thou never failest the donor. More and more, O Maghavan, thy bounty as a god is poured forth.
He who has reached out with his might against Krivi, making Śuṣṇa resound with his blows;
when he propped up and spread out that heaven, then indeed was the earthly one born.
He whose every nobleman and Dāsa is a foe guarding his treasure— even from the noble Ruśama Parīru, that wealth is driven away for you.
The inspired singers, hastening, have sung their hymn, sweet with honey and dripping with ghee.
For us, wealth has spread forth, along with manly power; for us, the pressed drops [of Soma] flow.
O Śakra, just as you drank the pressed Soma when Manu Vivasvat was king,
and just as you, O Indra, took pleasure in the hymn when Trita was present, so do you rejoice together with Āyu.
O Indra, you rejoiced in the Soma pressed by Pṛṣadhra, Medhya, and Mātariśvan,
just as you did in the Soma of Daśaśipra, Daśoṇya, Syūmaraśmi, and Ṛjūnas.
He who has established the hymns as his own, who has boldly drunk the Soma—
for him Viṣṇu strode out three steps according to the ordinances of Mitra.
O Indra, Lord of a hundred powers, O seeker of booty, you who take delight in the hymns of him who offers praise—
him we invoke, seeking glory, as milkers call upon a cow that yields abundant milk.
He who is our giver is our father; he is great, formidable, and the maker of dominion.
In his approach, may the formidable Maghavan, the possessor of many riches, grant us cattle and horses.
O Vasu, he for whom you bestow gifts so that he may give, he prospers in the abundance of wealth.
Seeking riches, we invoke Indra—the Lord of Wealth and Master of a hundred powers—with our hymns of praise.
Never do you neglect; you guard both races of beings. O fourth Āditya, your invocation and your Indra-power have established immortality in heaven.
O Indra, Maghavan, lover of songs, you who bestow gifts upon the worshipper— O Vasu, listen to our hymns and our fair praise, and hear our call as you did for Kaṇva.
The ancient hymn has been praised; speak a prayer to Indra.
Many lofty songs of Truth have resounded; the inspired thoughts of the singer have been released.
Indra has shaken together vast riches, he has brought together the two worlds and the sun.
The bright, pure Soma juices, mixed with milk, have exhilarated Indra.
We implore you, O Indra Maghavan, the peer among the wealthy, the eldest of the bulls, the foremost breaker of forts, the finder of cattle, and the lord of riches.
You who, increasing day by day, struck down Āyu, Kutsa, and Atithigva— that very you, the lord of bay horses and master of a hundred powers, we invoke as we strive for the prize.
May all the pressing-stones pour out for us the essence of the honeyed juice—
the drops that are pressed among people both in distant lands and nearby.
Strike down all hostilities and drive them far away; let all win wealth.
Even among the Śīṣṭas are your intoxicating stalks, where you sate yourself with Soma.
O Indra, come nearer with aids that are well-measured; come, O most peaceful one, with most peaceful succors; come, O most sleep-inducing one, with sleep-inducing powers.
Make the true lord, the conqueror in battle, who belongs to all people, a sharer of fortune among our progeny.
Further with your powers those who, as singers of hymns, purify their will in due succession.
May we be those who are most effective for your aid; may we be yours in the battles.
Through our priestly offerings and invocations of the gods, having won the prize, we celebrate you.
For I, O Lord of the Bay Steeds, desiring strength, ever go forth to the battle with your prayers and your protections;
indeed, seeking horses and cattle, I place you alone at the forefront of the churners.
O Indra, the poets celebrate this heroic power of yours with their songs;
they, chanting praises, have brought forth strengthening food dripping with clarity; the Pauras have attained it through their inspired thoughts.
They have approached Indra for protection through their skillful deeds—those at whose pressed juices you take delight;
as you rejoiced at Saṃvarta and as you did at Kṛśa, so, O Indra, do you exhilarate yourself with us.
O all you gods, being of one accord, come hither unto us;
O Vasus and Rudras, come to us for our protection; may the Maruts hear our call.
May Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, and Sarasvatī protect my invocation, along with the seven rivers;
may the waters, the wind, the mountains, the lord of the forest, and the earth hear my call.

O Indra, most bountiful one, whatever gift of yours there is that is worthy of a patron—by that, be our companion at the feast for our prosperity; O Vṛtra-slayer, as Bhaga, grant us wealth for giving.
O Lord of the assembly, O Lord of men, you alone, O wise one, bring us here to the prize!
Having won through the invocations, the priestly offerings, and the feasts for the gods, they have become renowned far and wide.
For the noble ones have their blessings, O Indra; there is life for people.
Come to us, O Maghavan, to protect us; milk out for us swelling nourishment.
O Indra, may we worship you with our hymns; O Śatakratu, bestow upon Praskaṇva a great, solid, enduring, and abundant gift that knows no shame.
The vast heroic power of Indra has appeared; it comes forth, O Dasyave-vṛka, as your gift of wealth.
A hundred white bulls shine like stars in the sky; by their greatness, they have propped up the heavens as if they were pillars.
A hundred bamboos, a hundred dogs, a hundred tanned skins;
a hundred tufts of *balbaja* grass for me, and four hundred ruddy mares.
O descendants of Kaṇva, you are well-disposed toward the gods; moving from strength to strength, you stride like horses.
Then indeed they celebrated the great glory of the sevenfold, the complete [soma];
the dark steeds, blinding the paths, could not be overtaken even by the eye.
O Dasyave-vṛka, your gift has been revealed, a bold one;
its power is as vast as the sky in its extent.
Dasyave Vṛka bestowed ten thousand from his own wealth upon me, the son of Pūtakratu.
A hundred donkeys are mine, a hundred woolly sheep;
a hundred slaves and garlands beyond measure.
There too, she was led forth for Pūtakratu, manifest like a mare belonging to a herd of horses.
Agni has been perceived, the wise one, the bearer of oblations; he possesses a propitious chariot.
Agni, with his bright radiance, has shone forth mightily like the Sun; the Sun has shone in heaven.
O Gods, joined with your ancient wisdom on your powerful chariot, O worshipful ones, come hither with your mighty powers, O Nāsatyas; drink this third libation.
The thirty-three gods have beheld you two, the true ones, at the forefront of truth.
Enjoying our sacrifice and libation, O Aśvins, you who shine with fire, drink the Soma!
O Aśvins, that deed of yours is worthy of praise: the bull [is born] from heaven, from the mid-air, and from the earth.
And those thousand praises which are offered in the quest for cattle—all of them you should come near to drink.
This portion has been set out for you two, O worthy of sacrifice; come hither to these songs, O Nāsatyas!
Drink the honeyed Soma among us; protect the donor with your powers.

That which the officiating priests, being of one mind, fashion in many ways and carry as this sacrifice—who was that learned Brāhmaṇa who was yoked [to it]? What indeed is the shared understanding of the sacrificer in that regard?
Agni is indeed one, though kindled in many ways; the Sun is one, pervading the universe.
Dawn is indeed one; she shines upon all this. Indeed, this one has become all this.

I invoke that chariot of yours, which is luminous, possessed of banners, three-wheeled, easy to mount, comfortable to sit upon, and of many boons— the chariot at whose harnessing the goddesses of wondrous wealth were born— so that you may drink from the overflowing vessel.
These portions of yours flow forth, O Indra and Varuṇa; at the libations, we invoke you both for greatness.
At every sacrifice, you hasten to the pressings when you bestow your favor upon the sacrificer who pours the juice.
The obstructing plants and the waters stood still; O Indra and Varuṇa, you have attained greatness.
You who have sped across the path on the far side of the firmament—for those two, no godless enemy dares to prevail.

O Indra and Varuṇa, that is true: for you, the seven voices of Kr̥śa milk out a wave of sweetness. With these, O Lords of Splendor, protect the donor who, unassailable, watches over you with his thoughts.
The seven sisters, sprinkling clarified butter, gentle and quick-giving, abide in the seat of Cosmic Order;
O Indra and Varuṇa, with those [streams] which drip with clarity, bestow gifts and grant aid to the sacrificer.
For great good fortune, we have proclaimed the true, Indra-like majesty belonging to those two radiant ones.
O Indra and Varuṇa, lords of splendor, protect us who drip with clarity through the three sevens.
O Indra and Varuṇa, when in the beginning you bestowed upon the seers inspired thought, the word, the hymn, and sacred learning;
those wise ones, while performing the sacrifice, beheld through fervor the stations which they created.
O Indra and Varuṇa, bestow upon the sacrificers a benevolent and undisturbed abundance of wealth.
Grant us progeny, nourishment, and prosperity; extend our lifespan for the sake of long life.
O Agni, come with the fires; we choose you as the Hotṛ.
Let the extended ladle, filled with oblation, anoint you—the most skilled sacrificer—to sit upon the sacrificial grass.
For toward you, O son of strength, O Aṅgiras, the ladles move at the sacrifice.
We seek Agni, the son of vigor, whose hair is ghee, the foremost in sacrifices.

O Agni, you are the sage, the ordainer, the purifying invoker worthy of sacrifice; you are the delightful one, the most excellent sacrificer at the rites, to be praised by the inspired singers with their pure hymns, O radiant one.
O most youthful one, bring here the guileless gods who desire [the sacrifice], O eternal one, for the feast.
O Vasu, come toward the well-prepared offerings; rejoice, being well-disposed through our prayers.
O Agni, you alone are far-extending, O protector, a seer of the *ṛta*;
O kindled and shining one, the inspired sages and ordainers seek to win you over.
Shine forth, O most radiant one; beam out joy for the people; grant wealth to the singer—for you are great.
Under the protection of the gods, may my patrons be victorious over enemies, possessing excellent fires.
Just as you, O Agni, utterly consume even thick brushwood upon the earth,
so do thou, O thou of Mitra-like greatness, burn whoever seeks to harm us or plots evil against us.
Do not deliver us over to the mortal enemy, nor to the sorcerer, nor to the one who utters evil speech;
O most youthful one, protect us with your tireless, crossing, and auspicious guardians.
Protect us, O Agni, with one [hymn], and protect us with a second;
protect us with three songs, O Lord of Strength, and protect us with four, O Vasu.
Protect us from every malicious demon; aid us in the contests for booty.
For we approach you alone as our closest kinsman for the service of the gods, that we may prosper.

O Agni, Purifier, grant us wealth that increases our vigor and is worthy of praise; and through your excellent guidance, O Supreme Lord, bestow upon us that which is much-desired and most glorious in its own splendor.

By which we may overcome those who defy us in battles, crossing over the hostile designs of the enemy—O Lord of Power, increase us with that nourishment; quicken our thoughts so that they find wealth.
Like a bull sharpening his horns, Agni brandishes them;
his jaws are keen and not to be withstood—he of the good teeth, the mighty son of strength.
O Bull Agni, your jaws are not to be resisted when you spread yourself abroad.
As such, O Hotṛ, make our oblation well-offered; win for us many desirable things.
You rest in the two mothers' woods; mortals kindle you together.
Unwearied, you carry the oblations of those who prepare the sacrifice, and then you reign among the gods.
The seven priests indeed invoke you thus, O Agni, you who are easy to win and not to be shamed.
You cleave the rock with your heat and your flame; O Agni, rise up above all people.
Having spread the sacrificial grass and prepared the offerings, we invoke Agni after Agni, the unrestrained one; we call upon Agni, the Hotṛ of all peoples, at every perpetual sacrifice.
O Agni, he who is wise attends to you with his thought for protection and for the sake of fair radiance;
through our yearning desire, bring to us wealth of many forms, most near for our aid.
O Agni, singer, lord of the people, burning away the demons, O god, you are the great master of the house who never departs; you are the guardian of heaven, dwelling within our home.
Let not the destructive spirit enter us, O Lord of the glowing wealth; let not the sorcery of those who practice sorcery reach us.
Drive away hunger and want beyond the cattle-pasture, O Agni, and ward off those possessed by demons.
May Indra hear both these things from us;
may the most powerful Maghavan come hither with his focused thought to drink the Soma.
For the two worlds have fashioned him as a self-ruling bull for the sake of power;
moreover, you sit as the foremost among those who are compared, for your mind desires Soma.
O Indra, Lord of many riches, pour forth [the draught] of the pressed soma-juice;
for we know you, O Lord of the Bay Horses, as the conqueror in battles, who makes even the unassailable tremble.
O Maghavan, let it be so according to thy truth, O Indra, just as thou desirest by thy wisdom.
O fair-cheeked one, wielder of the stone, may we quickly win booty through thy protection as we hasten toward it.
O Indra, Lord of Power, may you indeed grant us aid with all your protections;
for we follow you, O Hero, as one who is glorious like Bhaga and a finder of wealth.
O God, you are the first provider of horses, the creator of many cattle, and a golden spring;
for no one can diminish the gift within you. Whatever I ask of you, bring that to me.
Come indeed to the singer, O Bhaga, so that you may find wealth for the sake of granting riches;
rain it down, O Maghavan, for the quest for cattle, and for the quest for horses, O Indra!
You bestow for our gift many thousands and hundreds of herds.
We have brought Indra, the breaker of fortresses, to us with the words of inspired poets, singing for his protection.
Whether it be a non-sage or a sage who has fashioned this speech for you, O Indra—let him, O Śatakratu, rejoice in his devotion to you; may he, O fiercely impetuous one, be free from harm.
If the fierce-armed Purandara, the smasher of foes, would hear my call,
we, seeking wealth, invoke Indra— the Lord of Wealth and the performer of a hundred rites— with our hymns of praise.
We do not consider ourselves sinners, nor impotent, nor dull-witted,
when we now make the bull Indra our companion at the pressed juice.

We have harnessed the fierce one, the conqueror in battles, the debt-claimer, the undeceivable; he knows even the most anxious thought, the best of charioteers who wins the prize—he whom we have indeed obtained.
O Indra, from whatever we fear, from that grant us security. O Maghavan, be gracious; with your aids, strike down our enemies and our adversaries.
For you, O Lord of Bounty, are the master of great wealth for the one who serves you;
as such, O Maghavan Indra, lover of songs, we, having pressed the soma, invoke you.

O Indra, be gracious; you are the slayer of Vṛtra and our excellent protector from afar. May he protect our last [member], may he protect our middle, and may he guard us from behind and from the front.
O Indra, protect us from behind, from below, from above, and from the front—guard us on every side!
Drive far away from us all divine fear, and keep the godless weapons far away!
O Indra, protect us today and every day, tomorrow and every tomorrow, and in the future as well; O Lord of the Good, may you guard all our singers throughout the days, by day and by night.
The breaker-down of forts, the hero, Maghavan, the possessor of abundant wealth, is united for heroic deeds.
O Śatakratu, both your arms are virile, they which have grasped the thunderbolt.
Bring forth a hymn of praise for him whom he shall enjoy;
with their hymns, the Soma-pressers increase Indra’s majestic strength. Blessed are the gifts of Indra.
Uneven and peerless among men, the tireless one alone has surpassed many peoples;
he has grown preeminent over all created beings by his might. Blessed are the gifts of Indra.
Even with a steed that has not yet been harnessed, the one who bestows life swiftly desires to win;
Indra, that deed of yours is to be proclaimed as you perform heroic exploits—blessed are the gifts of Indra.

Come hither, O Indra; let us perform for you the strengthening prayers (*brahmāṇi*) by which, O most powerful one, you may take pleasure. Here, for the seeker of glory, there is prosperity; auspicious indeed are the gifts of Indra.
O Indra, when you make even the bold mind bolder for one who honors you with potent Soma juices and adorns you with prostrations— blessed are the gifts of Indra!
The one who beholds the hymns looks down like a man from a height;
having taken pleasure in the skill of the Soma-presser, he makes him his companion and ally—blessed are the gifts of Indra.
O Indra, all the gods have granted you heroic power and mental resolve;
you have become the lord of the universe, O much-praised one. Blessed are the gifts of Indra.
I praise that supreme power of yours, O Indra, for the assembly of the gods—that you slay Vṛtra with your might, O Lord of Might. Blessed are the gifts of Indra.
As if making human generations appear beautiful and equal, Indra—renowned from of old—has attained that conscious awareness; indeed, the gifts of Indra are auspicious.

O Indra, they have greatly increased your born strength, and you yourself, as well as your wisdom—O possessor of abundant cattle, O Maghavan, they have increased much under your protection; auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
O slayer of Vṛtra, both I and you shall join together for the sake of winning spoils. O wielder of the stone, even the enemy shall acknowledge us; auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
Truly indeed do we praise that Indra, and not falsely:
great is the destruction for him who presses no Soma; abundant are the lights for him who presses it. Blessed are the gifts of Indra.
That ancient Vena has been anointed with the rites of the great ones;
through whose doors Manu’s father anointed his prayers among the gods.
Like the measure of heaven, the stone-pressers with Soma upon their backs have taken their seat;
they are to be praised with hymns and sacred prayers.
Knowing this, Indra opened up the cattle for the Aṅgirases;
I praise that manly deed of his.
Like of old, may Indra, the increaser of the sage, the carrier of the word, the auspicious one at the offering of the hymn, come to us for our protection.

Now indeed, according to your will, O Indra, those who sacrifice have offered their praise with the cry of Svāhā; the singers have sung their hymns for strength, so that you may grant the wealth of the cow-pen.
In Indra are all heroic deeds, both those already accomplished and those yet to be done— he whom the hymns know as the sacrifice.
When the shouts of the fivefold people were released toward Indra, he, the lord of the dwelling,
by his own power, strewed the inspired hymns of the noble one.
This is your hymn of praise; you have performed those manly deeds;
you have protected the track of the wheel.
The wide stride of this bull has extended for the sake of life;
he has taken [it] as cattle take barley.
Receiving that [favor], seeking protection through you, O sons of Dakṣa,
may we be for the increase of the Maruts.
O Hero, we praise you with hymns for the sake of the seasonal power;
O Indra, may we be victorious with you as our ally.
May the Rudras, the liberal ones, and the mountains be well-disposed toward us in the slaying of Vṛtra when the call to battle is raised;
may those gods, with Indra as their chief, who have been established as a firm support for him who recites and praises, protect us.
May the hymns of praise exhilarate you; bestow bounty, O wielder of the stone, and strike down those who hate the sacred word.
With your foot, trample down the stingy Panis; you are great, for no one whatsoever can withstand you.
O Indra, you are the lord of the pressed juices; you are the lord of the unpressed;
you are the king of all people.
Come hither, go forth; your dwelling is in heaven, resounding among the people. You fill both the worlds, heaven and earth.
Even that mountain, the peak with its hundreds and thousands [of treasures],
you shattered apart for the sake of your worshippers.
We indeed call upon you at the pressing during the day, and we call upon you by night;
fulfill our desire.
Where is that bull, the youth, with powerful neck and unbending?
What priest honors him?
Whose libation does the bull Indra approach with delight?
And who indeed has yearned for Indra?
Whom have your gifts reached, O slayer of Vṛtra? Whom your great heroic powers? And who indeed is the one most intimate with your hymn of praise?
This Soma is pressed for you among the human race, among the Pūrus;
come here, hasten to it, and drink!
This [Soma] of yours is dear in Śaryaṇāvat, upon the Suṣomā; it is most intoxicating in Ārjīkīya.
Him, for great bounty today, the lovely one for exhilarating joy— come here, O Indra, run hither, and drink!
O Indra, whether you are summoned by men from the east, the west, the north, or the south,
come quickly with your swift steeds.
Whether you exhilarate yourself at the fountain of heaven, O Svarṇara,
or in the ocean of the soma-juice;
With songs of praise, I call upon you, the great and wide one, as one calls a cow for nourishment— O Indra, that you may drink the Soma.
O Indra, let your bay steeds, bearing your greatness, bring forth your majesty, O God, upon your chariot.
O Indra, you who are praised and glorified, the great, fierce one who acts as the sovereign lord—
come and drink our pressed soma.
We, possessing pressed juice and offering oblations, call upon you;
sit down upon this sacred grass of ours.
For although you, O Indra, belong in common to all the many [worshippers],
we invoke you as such.
The men have milked this sweet Soma for you with the stones;
O Indra, being pleased, drink it.
Pass by all the wise enemies; come hither quickly!
