Bestow upon us lofty renown.
The King, the giver of spotted deer accompanied by gold,
may he, the bounteous one, not come to harm, O Gods.
Upon a thousand spotted deer, I have taken great, broad, bright,
and shining gold.
The grandsons of Durgaha, most bountiful with a thousandfold wealth,
have established renown among the gods for me.

With songs of praise, at the sacrifice where Soma is pressed, I call upon Indra—the finder of wealth for you—with urgent prayers for his aid; like one who sings a great song, I invoke him as a benefactor.
Him whom the fierce ones do not restrain, nor the firm destroyers in the exhilaration of the soma-juice—
him, the fair-cheeked one, who, taking heed, bestows upon the laboring presser and the singer a praiseworthy gift.
Whether it be the powerful *mṛkṣa* made of horse-wool, or the golden *kīja*,
Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, makes the opening of the stall of cattle tremble.

He who, as the wielder of the thunderbolt with beautiful jaws and bay horses, digs up even what is buried and well-accumulated wealth for the donor— may that Indra act according to his will through his power.
Whatever you have accepted in the past, O much-praised hero among men,
that very sacrifice, hymn, and swift speech we bring together for you, O Indra.
O much-invoked wielder of the thunderbolt, drinker of Soma dwelling in heaven, come with the Soma juices for exhilaration;
for you alone, O bestower of desirable wealth, have become the most generous giver to the one who prepares the sacred prayer and presses the juice.
We have indeed caused this wielder of the thunderbolt to swell here both today and yesterday;
therefore, bring him the pressed juice now as before, and pay homage to the one renowned in fame.
Even the wolf, though he is a restrainer and a destroyer of sheep, abides within his appointed courses.
O Indra, come to this our hymn, graciously accepting it, with your wondrous wisdom.
What heroic deed of this Indra remains unaccomplished?
By what renown has the slayer of Vṛtra not been heard of from his very birth?
When indeed are his great, unassailable powers? And when is the Vṛtra-slayer invincible?
Indra surpasses all the Bekanāṭas who see by day, and by his wisdom he overcomes the Paṇis.
O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, O much-invoked wielder of the thunderbolt, we indeed bring to you these most numerous prayers, as if presenting a tribute, for they are unprecedented.
For many indeed are the hopes and calls for aid directed toward you, O performer of mighty deeds, O Indra.
O Vasu, pass even beyond the libations of the enemy; O most powerful one, hear my call!
O Indra, we indeed belong to you; we are yours, O inspired singer.
For there is no one else besides you, O much-invoked Maghavan, who can grant us comfort.

Protect us from this lack of understanding and from hunger, and deliver us from reproach. With your aid and with your wondrous thought, O most powerful one, grant us help; you are the finder of the path.
Let this Soma indeed be pressed for you; O Kalayas, do not be afraid.
This one here is fleeing from the darkness; he shall surely depart of his own accord.
We now implore those Kṣatriyas, the Ādityas, for their protection— those who are most gracious, for our assistance.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman carry us across distress, as the Ādityas know best.
For theirs is a wondrous, praiseworthy protection for the donor who serves the Ādityas with devotion.
Great is the aid of you great ones, O Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman; we choose for ourselves your protections.
O Ādityas, let your breaths sustain us alive before we meet with slaughter; for how is it that you are not heard when called upon?
Whatever protection or shelter you have for the weary one who presses the soma, with that, speak in our favor.
O gods, there is wide space from distress; there is treasure for the sinless, O Ādityas, you whose offenses are wondrously removed.
Let not this bond bind us; may it release us for our great purpose.
For Indra alone is renowned as the sovereign ruler.
O gods, you who are ever-ready to help, do not let us be harmed by the weapon of our deceitful enemies; do not touch us with their malice.
And so, O Aditi, great goddess, I address you for the sake of mercy and for my protection.
O you whose sons are fierce, rescue us from the deep abyss when he seeks to slay us; let no harm come to our offspring.
O sinless one, O wide-pastured one, O far-reaching one, make [the way] wide for us to spread forth, so that our offspring may live.
Those who are the heads of the peoples, undeceived, possessing their own glory,
they guard the sacred laws without guile.
O Ādityas, release us from the jaws of the wolves,
like a thief bound, O Aditi.
O Ādityas, let this arrow of ours go forth into the waters, and let this ill-will depart from us without striking us.
For ever indeed, O Ādityas, bounteous givers, we have enjoyed your protections— both in the past and now.
O wise ones, O gods, you grant life to everyone— even to one who has committed a sin— so that he may live.
O Ādityas, may that new favor of yours, which is even better than the old, release us from bondage,
O Aditi, like one who is bound.
O Ādityas, that [power] of ours is not for leaping over;
therefore, have mercy upon us.
O Ādityas, let not the weapon of Vivasvat, nor the artificial arrow, strike us before old age.
O Ādityas, drive away hatred, drive away distress, and drive away all that is gathered against us; cast away misfortune in every direction.
We turn you hither for our aid and for our favor, even as one turns a chariot—
O Indra, most powerful Lord of the virtuous, you who are many-acting and subduer of the attackers.
O you of many powers, of many wills, possessor of might, with your all-encompassing thought, you have filled [the world] with your greatness.
By whose greatness, O Mighty One, your two hands reached around the earth as it moved, grasping the golden thunderbolt.
I invoke with my courses for aid the Lord of all men, the master of unyielding power, and the protector of the peoples and of chariots.
For our desired aid, we call upon him who ever prospers, whom men invoke from various sides for protection in the battles for the light of heaven.
Indra, who is beyond measure, worthy of praise, fierce, most bountiful,
and even the lord of riches.
I urge that very Indra on for great bounty and for the drinking [of Soma]—
he who, as a dancer, rules over the ancient hymn of praise and over the peoples.
O powerful one, no mortal has ever attained your friendship; no one can reach the full extent of your might.
Aided by you, with you as our ally, may we win great wealth in the waters and in the sun, and conquer in battles, O wielder of the thunderbolt.
We seek you with sacrifices, we seek you with songs, O you who are most fond of song;
O Indra, just as you protected Purumīḷha in the battles for booty.
O wielder of the stone, he whose friendship with you is sweet, whose guidance is sweet, for him the sacrifice is to be extended far.
Grant wide space for our bodies, grant wide space for our dwelling;
grant us wide space that we may live.
We contemplate a wide path for the men, a wide one for the cattle, and a wide one for the chariot— a feast for the gods.
Six men, two by two, stand near me, exhilarated by the soma; they are givers of sweet bounty.
Indrota received from the son of Ṛkṣa two bay horses, and from the son of Aśvamedha, two ruddy ones.
To Ātithigva, [you gave] well-charioted [horses]; to Arkṣa, those with beautiful reins; to Aśvamedha, those that are well-adorned.
Six horses with mares did Atithigva win from Indrota at the sacrifice of Pūtakratu.
Among these dappled horses, the ruddy mare, accompanied by stallions, is conspicuous; she possesses her own reins and is equipped with a whip.
O you who are bound by the prize, not even a mortal seeking to find fault with you could ever attribute blame to you.
Forth, forth [I sing] the *triṣṭubh* hymn as food for the exhilarating hero, for Soma.
With prayer and with wisdom, he seeks to win you for the acquisition of the sacrifice.
I implore you for the lord of your flowing waters, the lord of your surging streams,
the husband of your inviolable cows.
These dappled cows, yielding milk for the preparation, mix the Soma;
they are the subjects at the birth of the gods, in the three luminous realms of heaven.
Sing forth with song to Indra, the lord of cattle, as he is known—
to the son of Truth, the protector of the good.
The bay steeds have been let loose upon the ruddy [mares] on the sacrificial grass,
where we shall raise our voices together in song.
For Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the cows have yielded the milk-mixture, the honey-sweetness,
which he found in his secret hiding place.
When we two, Indra and I, go up to the dwelling-place on high, the home of the ruddy sun,
having drunk of the honeyed draught, let us stay together in the thrice-seven places of our friend.
Sing praises, sing them forth; O Priyamedhas, sing praises! Let the sons also sing; and boldly sing praises as if to a fortress.
The gargara resounds downward; the iguana has cried out all around;
the tawny one has flashed forth—this prayer is raised up for Indra.
When the dappled cows, easy to milk and never-faltering, come rushing down—
seize the faltering Soma for Indra to drink.
Indra has drunk, Agni has drunk; all the gods have become exhilarated.
Varuṇa indeed dwells here; to him the waters have cried out in unison, like mother cows lowing toward their calf.
You are a good god, O Varuṇa, you whose seven rivers flow along the palate like a hollow,
well-wrought metal tube.
He who made the well-yoked coursers spring forward for the donor— he is the swift leader, that wondrous form who was released as the highest.
Truly, O Śakra, Indra has carried us across all enemies;
he, the youth, split apart the rice-porridge being cooked beyond the mountain with his song.
Like a small child, he mounted the new chariot;
he struck down the mighty buffalo-deer for his father and mother, he whose will is all-pervading.
O fair-cheeked lord of the house, mount your golden chariot;
then let us two accompany the heavenly, thousand-footed, ruddy, well-faring, and unassailable steed.
To him indeed, the self-radiant one, the worshipful ones sit down;
for they turn back his well-placed purpose so that he may come to bestow gifts.
Following the ancient dwelling of these Priyamedhas,
those who have spread the sacrificial grass and prepared the offerings have attained the first gift of grace.
He who is the king of the peoples, who moves with his chariots unrestrained,
the overcomer of all hostile armies, the eldest, the slayer of Vṛtra— he is praised.
O Puruhanman, glorify that Indra for his protection,
he upon whose two-fold supporter the visible thunderbolt was placed in his hand, like the great sun in the sky.
No one can equal him in deed who has made him ever-increasing—
Indra, who is praised by all, the skillful, the unassailable, and the one whose might is bold, as if through sacrifices.
The unconquered, fierce one, the conqueror in battles, at whose birth the great, far-reaching ones lowed together— the milch-cows lowed, the heavens and the earths lowed.
O Indra, even if there were a hundred heavens and a hundred earths belonging to you,
O wielder of the thunderbolt, neither a thousand suns nor the two worlds could equal you at your birth.
O Bull, most powerful one, you have filled all things with your greatness, your manly vigor, and your might.
O Maghavan, wielder of the thunderbolt, protect us with your wondrous aids in the cattle-pen.
O long-lived one, no godless mortal shall attain food;
even he who yokes the swift-moving Etaśas, even Indra yokes his two bay steeds.
For your sake, [I invoke] that great Indra, worthy of worship, the conqueror, for the granting of gifts—
he who is to be invoked in shallow waters and he who is to be invoked in the deep, who is to be invoked in the contests for booty.
O Vasu, O Hero, raise up for us great wealth;
O Maghavan Indra, raise it up for great generosity and for great glory.
O Indra, you who seek the truth, you satisfy yourself with us while crushing those who revile you;
O you of many heroic deeds, clothe yourself between our arms and strike down the Dāsa with your blows.
May the mountain, our own kinsman, shake down the one who follows another's law, the non-human, the non-sacrificer, the godless; may the mountain shake down the Dasyu for easy slaughter.
O most powerful Indra, do you grasp these in our hands for our gift, as one eager for us would grasp roasted grains; grasp them twice, O you who are eager for us!
O friends, seek out the will [of the god]: how may we accomplish the praise of Śara—the liberal patron, the wise lord, who is free from shame?
You shall indeed be praised by many seers who have spread the sacrificial grass,
when you thus bestow one by one the calves as you go.
Maghavan, son of Śūradeva, having seized him by the ear, brought back our calf from the three [rivers],
just as a wise patron brings a goat to be milked.
O Agni, protect us with your great powers from every hostile force,
and also from the enmity of mortal man.
For human wrath has no power over you, O you who are born of love;
you alone are the lord of the night.
O Son of Strength, with your auspicious luster, together with all the gods, grant us wealth that contains every boon.
O Agni, the enemies do not deprive that mortal of wealth whom you, as a protector, favor for his offerings.
O inspired sage Agni, the man whom you urge toward wealth in the contest for the prize of wisdom— he, through your protection, shall attain cattle.
O Agni, you bestow wealth consisting of many heroes upon the mortal who offers oblations; lead us forward toward what is better.
Protect us, O Jātavedas; do not deliver us over to the malevolent man who harbors evil intent.
O Agni, let no godless man ward off the bounty of you, the god;
for you are the master of all treasures.
O Son of Strength, bestow upon us of that abundant wealth;
O Friend, O Vasu, grant it to those who sing thy praise.
Let our songs go forth toward him of the piercing flame, the beautiful one to behold;
let our sacrifices with homage go toward the possessor of many riches, the one highly praised, for his protection.
Agni, the son of strength, Jātavedas, for the granting of desirable boons—
he who has become doubly immortal among mortals, the most delightful invoker in the clan.
Agni for you, for the sacrifice to the gods; Agni, as the rite proceeds;
Agni, the first among inspired thoughts; Agni, for the swift steed; Agni, for the successful attainment of the field.
May Agni grant us nourishment in his friendship, for he is the lord of all desirable things; we constantly implore Agni for our children and progeny—he who is the Vasu, the protector of our bodies.
Invoke Agni with songs for protection, him of the piercing flame;
O Purumīḷha, invoke the renowned Agni for wealth, and the men invoke Agni for a well-shining dwelling.
We praise Agni so that he may ward off hatred from us; we praise Agni so that he may grant well-being and prosperity.
To be invoked like a protector among all the tribes, may he become the illuminator of the dawns.
Prepare the oblation; let the Adhvaryu priest come again;
may he, who knows his commandment, perform the rite.
The Hotṛ has sat down upon the mind, over the sharp stalk,
taking pleasure in his friendship.
They seek him within the people, Rudra, beyond the reach of thought;
they seize the food with their tongue.
The bestower of vital strength heated the bow of kinship; he ascended the forest and struck the rock with his tongue.
Moving here, the bright calf finds no one to tether him;
he seeks his mother to praise her.
And now, his great and vast chariot-harnessing, accompanied by horses, has been seen— the cord of the chariot.
The seven milk the one; two cause the five to flow forth at the ford of the river, upon its resonance.
With the ten [fingers] of Vivasvat, Indra shook down the vessel from heaven with a threefold pressure.
The most recent flame goes around the threefold sacrifice;
the Hotṛ-priests anoint it with honey.
With reverence they pour out the water for the one who moves all around with his wheel above—
the inexhaustible one whose opening is directed downward.
The pressing-stones have indeed brought forth the honey poured into the vessel at the release of the water from the well.
O cows, come hither; you two are the great ones who bestow abundance upon the sacrifice, with both your ears made of gold.
Pour out the glory upon the pressed juice, the glory that overspreads heaven and earth;
may the Rasa receive the Bull.
They recognize their own dwelling place; like calves with their mothers, they nestle together with their kin.
As they devour within their jaws, they establish a support in heaven;
to Indra and Agni be homage and the light of heaven.
The noble one has milked forth swelling nourishment and strength that extends over seven steps,
by means of the seven rays of the sun.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, the risen sun has taken up the Soma;
that is the medicine for the sick man.
And now, his station which is worthy of being set down— that of the beloved one—
he has extended with his tongue beyond the sky.
Rise up for the one who follows the cosmic order; yoke your chariot, O Aśvins. May your protection be near at hand.
O Aśvins, come even with your swiftest chariot, which is faster than the blink of an eye; let your protection be near at hand.
O Aśvins, you spread cold over the heat for Atri;
may your protection be near at hand.
Where are you? Where have you gone? Where have you flown like two hawks?
Let your protection be near at hand.
If today, at whatever time, you two should hear this invocation,
may your protection be near at hand.
O Aśvins, you who are most swift to answer the call at the journey’s start, I go to you for kinship; may your protection be near at hand.
O Aśvins, you two have made a home for Atri; may your protection be near at hand.
You two chose Agni as a protector; he spoke beautifully to Atri. May your aid be present before us.
Saptavadhri, through his prayer, won the stream of Agni. May your protection be near at hand.
Come hither, O possessors of rain-wealth; hear this my invocation. Let your protection be near at hand.
What is this that is being praised for you two, like something old as if for two who have grown aged? May your protection be near at hand.
Common is your kinship, common is your bond, O Aśvins; may your protection be near at hand.
O Aśvins, may that chariot of yours which traverses the realms and the two worlds, Rodasī, come near; let your protection be present.
Come to us with thousands of cattle and horses; let your protection be near at hand.
Do not overlook us with respect to our thousands of cattle and horses; may your protection be near at hand.
The ruddy-hued Dawn has appeared; the observer of cosmic order has made light.
May your protection be near at hand.
O Aśvins, look out clearly for us, as one with an axe looks at a tree;
let your protection be near at hand.
O bold one, shatter the fortress like one oppressed by the dark host;
may your protection be near at hand.
Seeking strength, we praise with hymns of power your Agni, the guest dear to many, who dwells in every house— your Agni, with words of speech.
Him whom people, bearing oblations, praise with hymns of praise like Mitra who is anointed with clarified butter.
To the most praiseworthy Jātavedas,
who, exalted above the gods, has sent the oblations to heaven.
We have come to Agni, the best slayer of Vṛtra, the eldest descendant of Manu,
whose face is nourished by Śrutarvan, the great son of R̥kṣa.
The immortal Jātavedas, visible through the darkness,
who receives oblations of ghee and is worthy of praise.
The people here, beset by difficulties, invoke this Agni with oblations,
offering gifts with uplifted ladles.
This newest hymn has been offered for you, O Agni, from us— O delightful one, well-born, of good wisdom, unerring, wondrous guest!
O Agni, may this [song] of yours be most healing, most pleasant, and dear;
through it, being well-praised, may you increase.
May she, radiant with splendors, bestow great renown upon our fame; may she grant us glory in the conquest of Vṛtra.
Him who possesses horses, cattle, and fills the chariot— him, the brilliant lord of the virtuous, like Indra— whose glories you celebrate, O peoples, and whose every deed is worthy of praise.
O Agni Aṅgiras, you whom Gopavana has gratified with his song—
that Purifier, hear our call!
O you whom the people, pressing forward, invoke for the winning of booty— be mindful of us in the struggle against Vṛtra.
I, being invoked by Śrutarvan, the son of Ṛkṣa,
who distills the exhilarating juice— like the herds of those possessing long-tufted wool— shall wipe away the heads of four.
May the four swift horses of the most powerful one, eager to run and yoked to a fine chariot, carry me toward the offerings like birds carrying the son of Tugra.
Truly, O great river Paruṣṇī, I have pointed you out to him;
there is no mortal who bestows horses more than the most powerful one.
Yoke, O Agni, like a charioteer, the horses that best invoke the gods; sit down as the ancient Hotṛ-priest.
And, O God, as one who knows best, speak for us to the gods;
grant us full confidence in all desirable things.
For you, O youngest son of strength, when invoked with oblations,
have become the observer of Truth and worthy of sacrifice.
This Agni is the lord of thousandfold and hundredfold strength;
he is the sage, the head of riches.
Bend toward us like the R̥bhus toward the felly, with our joint invocations;
O Aṅgiras, come closer to the sacrifice.
To him, the bull who shines toward heaven, O Virūpa, now urge forth a well-fashioned hymn with an eternal voice.
Who indeed, with the army of this Agni who looks from afar, shall we lay low— the Paṇi— amidst the cattle?
O gods, let not the clans of the gods abandon us, like cows that have bathed leaving behind a weakling,
nor like inviolable cows deserting their calf.
Let not the affliction of any malicious hater strike us down,
as a wave strikes a ship.
Homage to you, O Agni; the peoples sing praise to your might, O God;
with your weapons, crush the enemy.
O Agni, will you not surely bestow wealth upon us for the quest for cattle? O maker of wide space, make wide space for us!
Do not abandon us in this great contest for wealth, like one who carries a burden; win the prize, win the riches!
O Agni, let this misfortune, out of fear, pursue someone other than us; increase our power like that of the impetuous one.
Whose *śamī* wood— whether of one who offers homage or of one who performs no sacrifice— the gods have accepted,
him indeed Agni causes to prosper.
From the distance of the further shore, come across to these lower ones;
protect those where I am.
For we have known you from of old, O Agni, as one who provides help like a father; therefore, we now seek your favor.
Now I invoke this Indra, the wielder of magic power, who rules by his might;
accompanied by the Maruts, do not withhold him from me.
This Indra, with the Maruts as his companions, split asunder the head of Vṛtra with his hundred-jointed thunderbolt.
Growing strong with the Maruts as his companions, Indra drove Vṛtra away,
releasing the waters of the ocean.
Indeed, by this Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, this heavenly light has been won for the drinking of the Soma.
We invoke with songs Indra, who is accompanied by the Maruts, the consumer of the *ṛjīṣa*, the powerful, and the exuberant.
We invoke Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, with an ancient hymn,
for the drinking of this Soma.
O bounteous Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, O Śatakratu, much-praised one, drink the Soma at this sacrifice.
For you alone, O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, these pressed Soma juices, O wielder of the stone,
are offered with the heart by those who recite hymns.
O Indra, friend of the Maruts, drink the pressed Soma at the celestial sacrifices,
whetting your thunderbolt with might.
Rising up with vigor, having drunk from the bowl, O Indra, you shook your jaws after drinking the Soma pressed in the vats.
Both worlds, heaven and earth, cried out after you as you roared,
O Indra, when you became the slayer of the Dasyus.
I have measured out my body from Indra: speech, which has eight feet, nine corners, and touches the Eternal Order (*ṛta*).
As soon as he was born, the hundred-fold wise one asked his mother thus:
"Who are the fierce ones? Who indeed are renowned?"
Then he spoke of him to Śavas, of Aurṇavābha and Ahīśuva: "O son, let these be your destroyers."
The Vṛtra-slayer struck them down together with his bolt, as one drives out spokes from a hub; having grown great, he became the slayer of the Dasyus.
In a single draught Indra drank thirty lakes at once, desiring the soma.
Indra pierced the Gandharva in the bottomless regions for the sake of the increase of the sacred formulations (brahman).
Indra cast forth from the mountains the well-fastened *bunda* and held fast the cooked rice.
Your arrow has a hundred shafts and is all alone with a thousand feathers,
O Indra, which you have made your companion.
With that, O Ribhusthira, born at once, bring [wealth] for the sake of the male and female singers to eat.
These most exalted deeds of yours have been performed with fullness;
O firm one, you have sustained them with your heart.
All these things Viṣṇu, the wide-striding one, brought when impelled:
a hundred buffaloes, rice cooked with milk, and a boar that had stolen from Indra.
Powerful is your well-fashioned, pleasant bow; excellent is your golden arrow-head. Both your arms are delightful and well-adorned, increasing even that which is soft with their own gentleness.
O Indra, bring us a thousandfold of the pressed juice and our sacrificial cake; O Hero, bring hundreds of cattle.
Bring us a distinguishing mark: a cow, a horse, and ointment;
along with that, golden ornaments for our minds.
And bring us many ear-ornaments, O bold one; for you, O Vasu, are renowned as the one who hears us.
O Indra, no one is a better increaser for you than Vṛdhīka—neither a skilled presser nor a liberal giver; O Hero, no other is a better patron for the singer than you.
Neither can Indra be brought low, nor can the powerful Śakra be overcome;
he hears everything and sees everything.
Undeceived, he observes the fury of mortals;
before reproach comes, he seeks to act.
Truly, by his power, the belly of the swift, ordaining one, is full—
of the slayer of Vṛtra, the drinker of Soma.
In you, O Soma, all treasures and all fortunes are gathered together—
bountiful, unassailable, and never to be turned back.
To you alone my desire, seeking barley, seeking cattle, and seeking gold, reaches out; to you it yearns, seeking horses.
O Indra, through hope in you, I have taken a sickle even in my hand;
O Maghavan, fill me with a handful of barley, whether it be gathered or yet to be harvested.
This Soma is the achiever, ungraspable, all-conquering, and the breaker-open; he is the seer and the inspired singer through his poetic wisdom.
He covers what is naked; he heals everything that is afflicted.
He has made the blind see and the lame walk forth.
O Soma, you are the one who extends wide protection against the hostilities caused by ourselves and those wrought by others.
O impetuous one, by your wisdom and your skillful powers, you reach from heaven to earth; you drive away even the hatred of the sinner.
If those seeking wealth go to obtain their goal, may they find the gift of the giver;
may they satisfy the desire of the thirsty.
When he restored what was lost from of old, he raised up the one who lives by the *ṛta*; he extended his life-span that had not yet been exhausted.
Most gracious, merciful, not arrogant in will, and unassailed, O Soma, be a blessing to our heart.
O Soma, do not cause us to tremble; O King, do not terrify us.
Do not strike our heart with your fiery brilliance.
When I behold the ill-will of the gods within my own dwelling, O King, drive away our enemies; O Bounteous One, drive away those who seek to harm us.
For there is no other maker of strength to be our comforter, O Śatakratu;
O Indra, have mercy on us.
O Indra, you who have always protected us from of old, never-failing one, for the winning of booty— be gracious to us.
How much more, then, as the impeller of the weak, will you be the protector of him who presses the juice?
O Indra, will you not surely be able to help us?
O Indra, O wielder of the stone, favor our chariot even if it be behind;
place it for me in front.
Come now, what are you waiting for? Make our chariot foremost, a preeminent glory that seeks the prize!
Favor our chariot seeking booty; it is easy for you to do. What more can be said? Make us truly victorious!
O Indra, be steadfast; you are a fortress. This auspicious prayer, timely and perfect, approaches your appointed place.
Let him not bring us into reproach; the goal is wide, the prize is set, and the obstacles have been removed.
When you perform that which is worthy of sacrifice, known as the fourth [pressing], then we desire that; from that time on, you are celebrated as our Lord.
He has strengthened you, O immortals, and he has gladdened you—O gods who dwell for a single day, and you goddesses as well.
Bestow upon him a glorious gift; may he, enriched by prayer, come quickly in the morning.
O Indra, seize for us with your right hand a wonderful, food-filled prize— you who possess the great hand.
For we know you as one of many deeds, of many gifts, and of great wealth,
possessing vast measure through your aids.
For neither gods nor mortals can restrain you, O Hero, when you desire to give,
just as one cannot hold back a terrifying bull.
Come now, let us praise Indra, the ruler of wealth, the self-ruling sovereign;
may he not neglect us with his bounty.
May he praise you and sing your song; may he hear the Sāman being sung and respond with bounty.
Bring to us with your right hand; stroke us with your left.
O Indra, do not exclude us from wealth.
Come near and bring [the wealth] with boldness, O bold one, from among the people;
take the possession of him who is most unwilling to give.
O Indra, whatever prize of yours there is to be won by inspired poets—
that, indeed, do you win for us.
O Vājas, you who are swift to come, may all your gladdening gifts quickly reach us according to our desires.
Run forth from afar and from near at hand, O slayer of Vṛtra,
toward the offering of the honeyed draught!
The Soma juices are strong; come hither, for they are pressed to exhilarate you. Drink, O steadfast one, as much as you desire.
Rejoice in this nourishment; it is sufficient for your choice and your spirit. O Indra, may it be a blessing to your heart.
Come here, O you who have no enemies; you are invoked by our hymns of praise in the highest luminous realm of heaven.
For you this [Soma] has been pressed with stones and purified with milk for exhilaration;
O Indra, Soma is offered forth to you.
O Indra, hear my call well; partake of the draught and satisfaction of this pressed juice mixed with milk from us.
O Indra, that Soma which has been pressed for you in the cups and in the vats—
drink of it, for you are its lord.
Soma, who is seen in the ladles like the moon in the waters—of that, you drink; for you are its lord.
That which the falcon brought to you with his foot, across the untraversed spaces—
drink of this, for you are its master.
We choose for ourselves that great protection of the gods;
may it be for our aid from those who are strong.
May they— Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman— be our constant allies, as well as the wise ones who increase our prosperity.
Carry us across our many perils, as if across waters with ships;
you are the charioteers of the Eternal Order (*ṛta*).
May what is desirable be ours, O Aryaman; may what is desirable be praiseworthy, O Varuṇa; for we choose that which is desirable.
For you, O wise ones, are the lords of desirable wealth, O destroyers of enemies;
none among the Ādityas is a partaker of evil.
O bounteous gods, whether we are dwelling at home or traveling on our path, we invoke you for our prosperity.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, look upon these kinsmen of ours;
O Maruts and Aśvins, come hither!
O bounteous ones, we maintain our brotherhood— both now and from of old— in commonality even within the womb of our mother.
For you indeed, O bounteous ones, with Indra as your chief, are turned toward heaven;
therefore I address you now.
I praise Agni, your dearest guest, beloved like a friend, who is to be known as well as a chariot.
Him, like a seer of profound wisdom, whom the gods established among mortals from of old.
O youngest one, protect the men who offer oblations; hear our songs;
and guard our offspring as well as ourselves.
With what [hymn], O Agni Aṅgiras, son of strength, may we offer praise to you, O God, according to your desire and your will?
With what intention shall we serve at whose sacrifice, O Son of Strength?
And what word of homage shall we now speak?
And so, do you indeed grant us all secure dwellings, and make our songs rich with prizes and wealth.
Whose abundant prayers do you now quicken,
O Lord of the Household, you whose songs win cattle?
They groom him, the one of skillful intellect, the leader in battles, the prize-winner in his own dwellings.
He dwells in secure peace through auspicious means—he whom others do not slay, but who himself slays; O Agni, he prospers with excellent heroes.
O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, come to my invocation, you two,
for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
O Aśvins, hear this hymn of mine, hear this my invocation,
for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
O Aśvins, possessors of abundant wealth, this Kṛṣṇa here invokes you both for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
O heroes, listen to the invocation of the singer Kṛṣṇa as he praises you,
so that you may drink the sweet Soma.
O Heroes, grant inviolable protection to the inspired singer who praises you,
so that he may drink the sweet Soma juice.
Come to the house of the donor who thus praises you, O Aśvins,
for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
Yoke the donkey to the chariot with its strong-limbed frame, O possessors of abundant wealth,
for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
Come, O Aśvins, on your three-seated, triple-wheeled chariot,
for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, do you now favor my songs for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
For you both are the wonder-workers, the physicians who bring delight; you both have become the masters of skillful speech.
Viśvaka invokes you both for the preservation of his body; do not sever our friendship, but release us from distress.
How indeed shall I, dejected in mind, praise you two? You have bestowed wisdom upon us for the attainment of greater wealth.
Viśvaka invokes you both for the protection of his body; do not sever our friendship, but release us from our bonds.
For you two indeed granted this abundant prosperity to Viṣṇāpū so that he might attain greater wealth.
Viśvaka invokes you both for the protection of his own body; do not sever our friendship, but release us from [all] bonds.

And we invoke for protection that hero, the winner of wealth, who drinks the dregs of soma, even though he is far away—he whose most sweet favor is like that of a father. May you two not sever our friendship; release us!
By the *ṛta* the god Savitṛ has brought peace; the horn of *ṛta* has spread far and wide.
*Ṛta* has overcome even the great assailants. Do not sever our friendship; release us from bondage.
O Aśvins, your glorious hymn is like the pouring of Krivi; come hither!
O Heroes, drink of this pressed honey which is dear in heaven, as two thirsty bulls drink at a watering-place.
Drink the honeyed *gharma*, O Aśvins; sit upon the sacred grass, O heroes.
Rejoicing in the dwelling of man, protect our vital strength with your wisdom.
The Priyamedhas have invoked you both with all your aids;
come to the dwelling of him who has strewn the sacrificial grass, to the beloved sacrifice during the rites for the gods.
Drink the honeyed Soma, O Aśvins; sit upon the sacred grass with favor.
Having grown strong, come from heaven to our fair praise, like two wild bulls to a watering place.
Come now, O Aśvins, with your dappled horses;
O wonder-workers on golden paths, lords of splendor, increase the Truth and drink the Soma.
For we, the inspired singers, longing for praise, invoke you both for the winning of the prize.
O Aśvins, wondrous, skillful, and rich in deeds, come with favoring ears through our prayer.
We celebrate with songs that Indra for you— the wondrous one, the subduer of the assailant, who rejoices in the exhilarating juice of wealth— just as cows low toward their calf in the stalls.
We quickly implore him who dwells in heaven, the bountiful giver, encompassed by powers, who is like a mountain abounding in many enjoyments—
he who possesses food, who bestows booty in hundreds and thousands, and who possesses cattle.
Neither the great nor the firm mountains, O Indra, can restrain you when you wish to bestow wealth upon a singer like me; no one can diminish that of yours.
You are a warrior by wisdom, by might, and by wondrous deed; you surpass all created beings in your majesty.
May this hymn which the Gotamas have generated turn you hither for our protection.
For you have indeed cast yourself forth with might beyond the ends of heaven; O Indra, the earthly realm could not contain you, for you have grown according to your own inherent power.
O Maghavan, there is no one who can obstruct your bounty when you bestow gifts upon the worshipper. Be the inspirer of our hymn of praise, most generous one, for the winning of the prize.
Sing a great song for Indra, O Maruts, the most effective slayer of Vṛtra,
by whom the upholders of cosmic order generated light— the god who is ever-watchful for the sake of the gods.
He blew away the curses; Indra, the slayer of the revilers, then became resplendent.
O you of great luster, leader of the Marut host, the gods have striven for your friendship, O Indra.
O Maruts, sing a prayer of praise for your lofty Indra!
Let the Vṛtra-slayer, the Lord of a hundred powers, slay Vṛtra with his hundred-jointed thunderbolt.
Boldly strike out, O bold-minded one; let your fame be lofty indeed.
Let the waters flow forth with speed like mothers; slay Vṛtra and win the light of heaven!
When you were born, O matchless Maghavan, for the slaying of Vṛtra,
then you spread out the earth and you propped up the sky.
From that your sacrifice was born; from that the hymn and the joyful laughter.
Therefore you are the overcomer of all that is born and all that is to be born.
Within the raw [dawns] you have placed the cooked; you have caused the sun to ascend to heaven.
Like a cauldron heated by the *sāman* chant, heat it with well-fashioned hymns—a lofty song acceptable to the lover of praise.
May Indra, who is to be invoked in all battles, be present for us;
may the slayer of Vṛtra, the supreme victor worthy of praise, attend our prayers and the libations.
You are the foremost giver of riches; you are the true one who acts as a sovereign lord.
We choose the alliance of the greatly glorious Śavas, the son of great power.
O Indra, lover of songs, these unsurpassed prayers are being fashioned for you.
O Lord of bay horses, Indra, take pleasure in these, which we have meditated upon as your own yoking-places.
For you, O Maghavan, are true and unbowed; you strike down many Vṛtras. Therefore, O mightiest one, wielder of the thunderbolt, bring wealth hitherward to the donor.
O Indra, you are glorious, the drinker of the dregs, O Lord of Might!
You alone, the upholder of the people, slay the Vṛtras that are irresistible and unconquered.
O Asura, we now implore you, the wise one, for bounty as if for our own portion. Like a great, protective cloak, O Indra, may your favors reach us.
The maiden, drawing water, found the Soma in the filter; bringing it to her home, she said:
"I shall press you for Indra; I shall press you for Śakra."
O little hero who goes there, looking out from house to house— drink this pressed with the jaws, accompanied by parched grain, by groats, by cakes, and by hymns of praise.
We cannot discern you, nor do we grasp you;
O Indu, flow slowly, very gently, around for Indra.
Will he not move? Will he not act? Will he not make us more prosperous?
Shall we, as those who go about hating their husbands, be united with Indra?
O Indra, cause these three regions to sprout anew:
that head, the fertile field, and this one here within my belly.
And that field of ours which is there, and this body of mine,
and also the head of Tatas— make all of those hairy.
O Śatakratu, through the hole of the chariot, the hole of the cart,
and the hole of the yoke, you, O Indra, having purified Apālā three times, made her sun-skinned.
Sing forth unto Indra while he drinks of your soma-juice—
him who conquers all, the lord of a hundred powers, the most generous among the peoples.
Call him the one invoked by many, the one praised by many, the leader of songs, the one of ancient renown—
call him Indra!
O Indra, you are the giver of great spoils to us, the dancer;
as the mighty one, may you extend [your aid] with your jaws.
Indra, the broad-chested one, has drunk of the soma-juice— the well-prepared, skillful, and effusive draught— of the drop mixed with barley.
Sing forth to that Indra for the drinking of Soma;
for this indeed is his means of strengthening.
Having drunk of his exhilarating draughts, the god, by the might of the god,
has surpassed all worlds.
Bring hither for our protection that ever-conquering one of yours, who is drawn toward all our songs.
The warrior who is unassailable, the drinker of Soma, the immovable,
the hero whose will is irresistible.
O Indra, you who know much, grant us wealth, O worthy of praise;
help us in the decisive contest for booty.
From there, O Indra, come to us with food that brings a hundredfold strength,
with food that brings a thousandfold strength.
O Śakra, seeker of cattle, may we, through our inspired thoughts, direct the prayers of the wise with our swift steeds;
O wielder of the thunderbolt, may we be victorious in battles.
O Śatakratu, we cause you to take delight in our hymns, as cattle do in pastures.
For all our desires, O Lord of a hundred powers, have been fulfilled through mortal nature;
we have attained our hopes, O Wielder of the Thunderbolt.
O Son of Strength, those who desire your favor have turned toward you;
O Indra, nothing surpasses you.
O Bull, with your most bountiful, formidable, and swift-moving wisdom, and with your abundant insight, favor us.
O Indra, O Śatakratu, that exhilaration of yours which is truly the most glorious— by means of that, do you now indeed rejoice in intoxication.
O Indra, that exhilaration of yours which is most renowned, which is the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, and which bestows the most power— [that exhilaration we choose].
For we know, O wielder of the thunderbolt, you who are true to the Soma-drinker and bestow gifts;
O wondrous one, among all the peoples.
For Indra, who delights in the intoxicating draught, let our songs resound all around;
let the poets sing the hymn of praise.
In whom all glories rejoice, in whom the seven assemblies delight— that Indra we invoke when the Soma is pressed.
At the Trikadruka rites, the gods performed the conscious sacrifice;
may our songs of praise increase that very one.
May the drops enter into you, as rivers flow into the ocean;
O Indra, nothing surpasses you.
O mighty bull, wakeful one, you have expanded with your greatness the draught of Soma,
O Indra, which is within your bellies.
O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, let the Soma be sufficient for your belly;
let the drops be sufficient for your vital powers.
Śrutakakṣa sings sufficiently for the horse, sufficiently for the cow,
and sufficiently for the majesty of Indra.
For you, O Indra, are indeed ready for our pressed Soma juices;
O Śakra, you are ready to grant us gifts.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, even from afar our songs reach you;
may we come before you in due season.
For thus indeed you are one who seeks heroes, thus a hero and steadfast; thus indeed may your mind be successful.
Thus has this gift been established by all the ordainers, O Lord of abundant wealth;
even so, Indra, be with me.
O Lord of spoils, do not be sluggish like a weary priest; exhilarate yourself with the pressed juice mixed with milk.
O Indra, let not the hostilities of the sun reach us during the nights;
with you as our ally, may we overcome them.
With you as our ally, O Indra, may we answer back against our rivals;
you are ours, and we are yours.
For indeed, O Indra, the poets who love you, your friends, follow after you as they move along.
O Sūrya, you indeed rise up toward the bull of renowned wealth, the performer of manly deeds, the archer.
He who by the strength of his arms shattered ninety-nine fortresses,
he, the slayer of Vṛtra, struck down the serpent.
That Indra is our auspicious friend; he milks for us wealth in horses, cattle, and barley, like a wide-streaming cow.
O Vṛtra-slayer, whatever has risen today, O Sūrya,
all that is under your control, Indra.
Or when you, O exalted Lord of the Good, think "I shall not die," even that thought of yours is indeed true.
O Indra, you go to all those Soma juices, whether they are pressed in the distance or pressed nearby.
We urge that Indra on for the slaying of the great Vṛtra;
may he become the bull, the showerer of blessings.
That Indra is prepared for the giving; he is the most powerful, established for the exhilaration of the Soma. He is glorious, worthy of praise, and beloved by the Soma.
Gathered by song like a thunderbolt, powerful and unshakable, the lofty and invincible one has grown great.
O Indra, lover of songs, being praised, make even our difficult path easy for us;
and you, O Maghavan, shall have your will.
O you whose command and self-sovereignty no one at all disregards—
not even a god nor a humble mortal.
Then the two goddesses, heaven and earth, O fair-cheeked one, revere your irresistible might.
You have established this bright milk in the dark cows and in the ruddy ones, and in the speckled cows.
When all the gods stepped forth from the serpent’s brilliance,
they found that terror of the wild beast.
Then indeed the Vṛtra-slayer became my protector; he has displayed his manly power—he who has no enemy and is unsubdued.
I have heard of your most excellent slayer of Vṛtra, the bold host of the peoples; I call upon you for great bounty and for strength.
O you of many names, much-praised one, through this prayer for cattle,
since at every soma-pressing you have been present.
May the slayer of Vṛtra, who is abundantly invoked, be mindful of us;
may Śakra hear our prayer.
With what aid will you gladden us, O Bull? With what [aid] will you bring [wealth] to those who praise you?
At whose pressed juice does the bull, the lord of teams, rejoice—
the slayer of Vṛtra, for the drinking of Soma?
Rejoicing, do thou indeed bestow upon us thousandfold wealth; be the giver to the one who offers oblations.
These pressed juices, accompanied by their wives, go eagerly to the feast;
the gliding one has entered the waters.
The desired oblations, increasing Indra at the sacrifice, have been released; they flow with power toward the final purificatory bath.
Hither let those two bay steeds, companions at the feast, with golden manes, carry you toward the prepared food.
For you, O Radiant One, these Soma juices have been pressed and the sacrificial grass strewn;
bring Indra hither for the sake of those who praise you.
Bestowing skill upon you and radiant jewels upon the donor,
praise Indra for the sake of those who offer hymns of praise.
I bestow upon you power and all hymns of praise, O Śatakratu;
O Indra, be gracious to those who laud you.
O Śatakratu, bring us every blessing— food and strength—
when you, O Indra, show us mercy.
O Śatakratu, bring us all prosperity,
since you, O Indra, will show us mercy.
O best slayer of Vṛtra, we who have pressed the soma call upon you alone;
for, O Indra, you shall be gracious to us.
Come to our pressed juice with your bay horses, O Lord of intoxications;
come to our pressed juice with your bay horses.
Indra, who from of old is the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, he who is known as the lord of a hundred powers—
come with your bay steeds to our pressed soma.
For you, O slayer of Vṛtra, are the protector of these soma-juices;
come to our pressed libation with your two bay steeds.
May Indra grant us for our nourishment the wealth of R̥bhukṣan and R̥bhu;
may the prize-winner grant us the prize-winner.
The cow, seeking glory, suckles the Maruts—the mother of the bounteous ones;
she is harnessed as the leader of their chariots.
In whose lap all the gods maintain their sacred laws,
so that the sun and moon may be seen.
Therefore, all the noble singers always praise us well for that—
O Maruts, [come] for the drinking of the Soma.
This Soma has been pressed; the Maruts drink of it, as do the self-ruling Aśvins.
Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa drink their fill of the purified [Soma] that has three seats and is full of life.
And now may Indra, according to his pleasure, delight in this pressed juice mixed with milk,
like a Hotṛ priest at dawn.
When did the wise ones flash forth their brilliance? Like waters they flow across their adversaries, they whose will is purified.
Of you great gods, whose splendor is wondrous, what favor do I choose for myself today?
The Maruts, who have spread out all the earthly realms and the luminous spheres of heaven, [come] for the drinking of the Soma.
I call now those Maruts from heaven, whose will is purified,
for the drinking of this Soma.
I now call those Maruts who have propped apart the two worlds,
for the drinking of this Soma.
I now call upon that bull-like host of Maruts, dwelling in the mountains,
for the drinking of this Soma.
O lover of songs, may our hymns rise up to you like a charioteer when the juices are pressed;
O Indra, they have lowed toward you together, as mother cows toward their calf.
The bright pressed juices have drawn you hither, O Indra, lover of songs;
drink of this food, O Indra, for it is prepared for you among all [the offerings].
Drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Indra, the pressed juice brought by the falcon;
for you are the sovereign king of all the eternal tribes.
Hear the call of Tiraścī, O Indra, who honors you.
Fill us with wealth consisting of great heroism and cattle; for you are great.
O Indra, [the one] who has generated for you a newest, delightful song— a prayer from a conscious mind, ancient, and swelling with the Truth (ṛta)— [to him, O Indra, grant wealth].
Let us praise that Indra whom songs and hymns have strengthened;
desiring to win his many manly deeds, we shall prevail.
Come now, let us praise Indra, the pure one, with a pure *sāman*;
may he, who has grown strong through pure hymns (*uktha*), being pure himself, be exhilarated by the pure draught.
O Indra, come to us pure, with your pure aids;
being pure, bestow wealth upon us; being pure, O lover of Soma, rejoice.
O Indra, as one pure, grant us wealth; as one pure, grant treasures to the donor.
As one pure, you strike down the Vṛtras; as one pure, you seek to win the prize of strength.
For him the Dawns have lengthened their course; for Indra, the Nights with beautiful voices have flowed.
For him the Seven Mothers, the Waters, have stood ready—the rivers easy to cross for men to ford.
Pierced through by his unsteady weapon alone, the thrice-seven ridges of the mountains were shattered;
neither god nor mortal could surpass that which the grown bull performed.
The iron thunderbolt of Indra is firmly joined; in the two arms of Indra is the greatest strength.
In the head of Indra, his powers are unique; they strive together, seeking to hear him nearby.
I deem you worthy of sacrifice among those worthy of sacrifice; I deem you the shaker of the unshakable.
I deem you, O Indra, the banner of heroes; I deem you the bull of the people.
When you, O Indra, took the mace that drips with exhilaration into your arms in order to slay the serpent,
the mountains roared aloud, as did the cattle and the priests as they approached Indra.
Let us praise him who brought these worlds into being, all created things that are inferior to him.
Through our songs, may we win Mitra with Indra; let us approach the Bull with our prostrations.
Fleeing from the snort of Vṛtra, all the gods who were your friends abandoned you;
O Indra, let there be friendship between you and the Maruts, and then you shall conquer all these hostile armies.
The sixty-three Maruts, increasing in strength like heaps of dawns, worthy of sacrifice—toward you we approach; grant us our portion. We shall honor your vigor with this oblation.
The sharp weapon is the vanguard of the Maruts; O Indra, who has dared to withstand your thunderbolt?
Weaponless are the Asuras, the godless ones; O wielder of the *ṛjīṣa*, sweep them away with your wheel!
Send forth a well-fashioned hymn to the great, fierce, and powerful one, most auspicious for our cattle;
offer many songs to Indra, who is borne by songs, for his own body—surely he will take notice of us.

Send forth your inspired thought to the far-reaching one who bears the hymns, as if with a boat to the further shore of the rivers. Touch the body of the famous one, most dear to you, through your devotion; will he not surely take notice?

Perform that for which Indra takes pleasure; praise him with a beautiful hymn and win him over with reverence. Draw near, O singer; do not cry out [in vain], but make your voice heard—surely he will take note of it.
Drapa, the black one, hastening along with ten thousand [followers], descended upon the Aṃśumatī river.
Indra, with his power, protected him as he blew [the fire]; the hero-minded one cast away the dripping waters.
I saw the drop moving in the distance, in the secret hiding place of the river Aṃśumatī; like a black cloud, he stood there. O heroes, I urge you: fight in the battle!
Then Drapsa, flashing forth, established his body in the lap of Aṃśumatī;
with Bṛhaspati as his ally, Indra overcame the godless tribes that were attacking.
At your very birth, O Indra, you became the enemy of those seven who had no enemies;
you found the hidden Heaven and Earth, and you bestowed joy upon the vast worlds.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, you, bold with the bolt, struck down that peerless power;
you shattered the strength of Śuṣṇa with your weapons, and by your might, O Indra, you found the cattle.
O Bull of the people, you have indeed become the powerful slayer of Vṛtras;
you released the obstructed rivers and you won back the waters that had the Dāsas for their masters.
He is the one of noble wisdom who rejoices in the pressed juices, whose wrath is unsurpassed, and who is as wealthy as the day;
he alone is the doer of manly deeds, the slayer of Vṛtra—others they call his counterpart.

That Indra is the slayer of Vṛtra and the sustainer of the people; him, worthy of invocation, let us call with excellent praise. He, the bounteous one, is our protector and advocate; he is the giver of booty that brings renown.
That Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra and lord of the Ṛbhus, as soon as he was born, became one to be invoked;
performing many manly deeds, he is to be invoked by his friends like Soma when drunk.
O Indra, those enjoyments which you, possessor of the light, brought from the Asuras—
O Maghavan, increase the singer of this hymn and those who have spread the sacrificial grass for you.
O Indra, that horse and cow which you hold as your imperishable portion—
bestow them upon the sacrificer who presses the soma and gives the sacrificial fee, not upon the usurer.
O Indra, that unrighteous one who, godless and sleep-addicted, has disregarded you—he shall perish by his own ways;
deprive him of his nourishing wealth and cast it far away from him.
O Śakra, whether you are in the distance or nearby, O slayer of Vṛtra,
from there the one who has pressed the soma seeks to win you over with long-maned songs that ascend to heaven, O Indra.
Whether you are in the luminous realm of heaven, upon the surface of the ocean,
in a terrestrial dwelling, O greatest slayer of Vṛtra, or in the intermediate space— come hither!
O Soma-drinker, Lord of Might, at our pressed soma-juices,
exhilarate yourself with bounty and with wealth that is full of truth, O Indra, with abundant riches.
O Indra, do not turn us away; be our companion at the feast.
You are our protection, you alone are our kinship; O Indra, do not turn us away.
O Indra, sit with us at the pressed juice to drink the honeyed mead;
O Maghavan, grant great protection to the singer—sit with us at the pressed juice, O Indra!
Neither the gods nor mortals have attained you, O wielder of the stone;
you surpass all created beings in power—neither the gods have attained you.
In unison, they have fashioned and begotten Indra for sovereignty—the hero who overcomes all hostile armies;
most excellent in wisdom, a subduer of enemies, fierce, strongest, powerful, and swift.
The singers have together raised their voices for Indra to drink the Soma—
him, the Lord of Light— for his strengthening, he who is firm in his vows through his might and his aids.
With their vision, the inspired singers bend the rim [of the wheel] toward the ram with their chants;
well-shining, guileless, and impetuous, you are close to our ears along with the chanters.
I invoke that Indra, the bounteous and fierce one, who ever possesses irresistible powers;
may he, the most generous and worthy of sacrifice, turn toward us through our songs and, wielding the thunderbolt, make all paths easy for us to reach wealth.
O Indra, you, the most powerful and mighty Śakra, have known these fortresses from of old to destroy them with your might.
O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, all beings tremble at your fear—heaven and earth shake because of you.
O Indra, O hero, O wondrous one, may that truth protect me; O wielder of the thunderbolt, carry us across many hardships as if across waters.
O King Indra, when will you grant us wealth that is all-sustaining and desirable?
Sing forth a lofty *sāman* for Indra, the inspired singer, the great one— the maker of cosmic order, the wise, and the one worthy of praise.
O Indra, you are the conqueror; you caused the sun to shine.
You are the maker of all, the god of all; you are great.
Shining with light, you went to the sun, to the luminous realm of heaven;
O Indra, the gods strove for your friendship.
O Indra, come to us as our beloved, the ever-conquering, the unconcealable,
broad on all sides like a mountain, the Lord of Heaven.
For you, O true one, O drinker of Soma, have surpassed both worlds;
O Indra, you are the strengthener of the presser and the Lord of Heaven.
For you, O Indra, are the shatterer of eternal fortresses; you are the slayer of the Dasyu, the prosperer of Manu, and the lord of heaven.
Now, O Indra, lover of songs, we have poured forth our great desires toward you,
like those going upward with water.
O Hero, as the waters increase the ocean with their currents, so do our prayers increase you,
O wielder of the stone, even though you have already grown great day by day.
They harness the two bay steeds of the impetuous one with song upon the broad-yoked chariot— the steeds that carry Indra and are yoked by a word.
O Indra, bring to us strength and manly valor, O Lord of a hundred powers, O far-seeing one;
bring a hero who conquers in battle.
For you indeed, O gracious one, have become our father; you, O Śatakratu, have become our mother. Therefore, we seek your favor.
O impetuous one, much-invoked, lord of a hundred powers, I address you who are eager for the prize;
grant us great heroic strength.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, eager men have made you swell with drink yesterday and today;
as such, O Indra, hear us here who bring hymns of praise, and come to our dwelling place.
Rejoice, O fair-cheeked Lord of Bay Steeds; we entreat this of you. The wise ones attend upon you;
O Indra, lover of songs, your glories are supreme and worthy of praise when the juices are pressed.
Turning toward him as if toward the sun, may all partake of Indra's riches;
at every birth, we look toward our portion with power, as if toward our due share.
Praise him who bestows wealth and whose gifts are never-failing; auspicious are the gifts of Indra. He does not frustrate the desire of the one who serves him, but stirs his mind toward giving.
O Indra, in battles you prevail over all adversaries; you are the slayer of the malevolent, the progenitor, and the conqueror of all. You, indeed, overcome those who seek to overcome us.
The two worlds followed after your surging might, like two mothers following their child;
all your rivals yielded to your wrath when you, O Indra, overcame Vṛtra.
Hither for your aid [we call] the ageless one, the hurler who is not hurled;
the swift victor, the striker, the best of charioteers, the unconquered, the increaser of Tugra’s line.

We invoke for our protection the common Indra, the restorer who has not been restored, the one made by power, the one with a hundred aids and a hundredfold wisdom— the possessor of wealth, the one who hastens toward riches.
Here I come before you in person; all the gods follow behind me.
When you have assigned a portion to me, O Indra, then through me alone shall you perform heroic deeds.
I place before you a draught of honey; let the pressed Soma be your allotted portion.
And you, as my friend, shall be at my right hand; then we two shall slay many Vṛtras.
Bring forth a hymn of praise, seeking booty for Indra, if truth indeed exists.
"Indra does not exist"—only such a one has said this; who has seen him? Whom shall we praise?
Here I am, O singer; behold me here! I surpass all created beings in my greatness.
The quarters of the world increase me; as a shatterer, I rend the worlds asunder.
When the yearnings of Truth ascended toward me as I sat alone upon the back of the beloved one, even my mind spoke back to me from my heart; my friends, possessing children, have cried out.
All those deeds of yours are to be proclaimed at the libations, O Maghavan Indra, which you performed for the one who presses the juice—
when you opened up the wealth gathered from afar for Śarabha, the kinsman of the seers.
Now run forth each in a different direction; let him who has held you back here not remain!
Indra has hurled his thunderbolt down upon the vital organ of Vṛtra.
Moving with the speed of thought, he crossed the iron fortress;
having gone to heaven as a fair-winged bird, he brought the Soma for the wielder of the thunderbolt.
Within the ocean, the thunderbolt lies enveloped by the waters;
to it, they bring tribute from the forward-flowing streams in constant succession.
When Vāk, the delightful queen of the gods, sat down speaking words that are beyond human perception, she milked out four strengths and milks from her; where indeed has her highest part gone?
The gods generated divine speech; animals of every form speak it. May that cow-like Speech, yielding us joy, refreshment, and strength, come to us with fair praise.
O friend Viṣṇu, stride out further; O Heaven, grant space for the hurling of the thunderbolt.
Let us two slay Vṛtra and release the rivers; let them flow forth, set free by the impulse of Indra.
Truly, that mortal has indeed labored successfully for the service of the gods,
who now has brought Mitra and Varuṇa near for his assistance and for the offering of oblations.
Possessing most exalted sovereignty and wide vision, O heroes, kings of most far-reaching fame—
those two, through their wondrous deeds, move like arms upon the chariot together with the rays of the sun.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, he who ran forth as your swift messenger— the iron-headed one, impetuous in his joy— has sped along.
He who does not seek to associate, nor delights in being summoned again, nor in conversation—from him protect us today with your complete success; protect us with your two arms.
O Lord of the Sacred Law (*ṛtāvasu*), sing forth for Mitra and Aryaman a word of fellowship, a protective word, and a pleasing hymn of praise for Varuṇa among the kings.
They have sent forth the ruddy, noble treasure, the sole son of the three;
those immortal, undeceivable ones look down upon the dwellings of mortals.
Come to my uplifted words, most brilliant deeds to be performed;
O Nāsatyas, come both of you together in harmony to enjoy the oblations.
When we invoke your guileless bounty, O you who possess abundant wealth, come hither, O heroes,
accepting our forward-turned oblation, being praised by Jamadagni.
O Vāyu, come with benevolent thoughts to our sacrifice that touches the heavens;
this bright [Soma], being mixed above the filter, is offered to you.
The Adhvaryu priest brings the oblations along the straightest paths for you to enjoy;
therefore, O Lord of the teams, drink of both our offerings—drink the pure Soma mixed with milk.
Truly, O Sūrya, you are great; truly, O Āditya, you are great.
The greatness of you who are so mighty is celebrated; indeed, O God, you are great.
Truly, O Sūrya, you are great in fame; indeed, O God, you are great.
By your greatness, you are the divine Asura, the domestic priest of the gods, the far-reaching, invincible light.
This [goddess], who comes downward, chanting her hymn, fashioned by the ruddy one with her forms,
has appeared like a marvel as she approaches within the ten arms.
Three generations have passed away; others have settled around the hymn of praise.
The Great One has taken his stand within the worlds; as the purifying one, he has entered the golden rays.
The mother of the Rudras, the daughter of the Vasus, the sister of the Ādityas, the navel of immortality—I proclaim this now to the people who understand it: do not slay the cow, the sinless Aditi!
The mortal of feeble intellect has driven away the goddess Cow, who knows speech, who utters her voice, who attends with all inspired thoughts, and who has come forth from among the gods.
O Agni, you, O god, bestow great vital strength upon the donor; you are the sage, the master of the house, the youthful one.
O Agni, bring here the gods along with this our invocation, O wise and far-shining one, you who are eager to serve them.
With you indeed as our ally, O most youthful one, who are the best at impelling, may we prevail for the winning of the prize.
Like Aurva and Bhr̥gu, like Apnavāna, I invoke the pure Agni, who is clothed in the ocean.
I invoke the seer who sounds like the wind, the force that roars like Parjanya, Agni whose garment is the ocean.
I call upon Agni, who is clothed in the ocean, like the impulse of Savitṛ and like the enjoyment of Bhaga.
I call upon Agni for you— the one who causes the sacrifices to prosper, the most frequent among gods—
toward the powerful grandson.
May he come to us just as Tvaṣṭṛ comes with forms to be fashioned,
through the inspired power of this glorious one.
This Agni rules over all splendors among the gods;
may he come to us with strengths.
Here, praise among all the Hotṛ-priests the most glorious one,
Agni, the foremost in sacrifices.
Sharp and purifying in his flame, he who is the eldest in the homes has shone forth, he whose fame is most far-reaching.
O sage, praise him who is like a prize-winning steed, the impetuous one,
who stirs men like Mitra.
The sisterly songs of the one who has prepared the oblation, pointing the way toward you, have taken their stand in the presence of Vāyu.
He for whom the threefold sacrificial grass has been spread out, unbound and firmly established—
therein even the waters have set down their station.
The station of the bounteous god, with his unassailable aids,
is auspicious to behold like the sun.
O Agni, O God, glowing with the flame of your brilliance through the offerings of clarified butter,
bring the gods here and worship them.
Thee, the seer, the immortal bearer of oblations, the gods and the mothers brought forth, O Aṅgiras.
O Sage Agni, they have established you— the wise, the excellent messenger,
the bearer of oblations.
For I have no cow to sacrifice, nor an axe for the wood-cutter;
yet such as this I bring to you.
O Agni, whatever logs of wood we place upon you,
O youngest one, enjoy them all.
Whatever the upajihvikā eats, whatever the ant crawls over—
that may all be ghee for you.
Kindling Agni with his mind, a mortal should attend upon the prayer;
he has kindled Agni with the rays of light.
He has been seen, the best finder of the path, in whom they have established their sacred laws.
Let our songs reach Agni, the newborn strengthener of the Ārya.
The son of Divodāsa, Agni, has gone forth toward the gods with his might;
he has spread out across the mother earth and stands upon the summit of the firmament.
From whom the people tremble as he performs deeds worthy of praise—
he who wins a thousandfold like Medhasāta himself— honor that Agni with your prayers.
O Vasu, the mortal whom you wish to lead forth toward wealth, he who offers gifts to you—
he, O Agni, gains for himself a hero who recites hymns and possesses a thousandfold prosperity.
He pierces even the firm stronghold for booty with his steed; he wins imperishable fame.
O Lord of many riches, we ever place all desirable things in you among the gods.
He who distributes all wealth, the delightful Hotṛ of men—
to that Agni the hymns of praise go forth, like the first vessels of honey.
Like a chariot-horse, the bounteous ones, seeking the gods, groom him with their songs.
O wondrous Lord of the people, bring across both our children and our progeny, and grant us the wealth of the generous patrons.
Sing forth to the most generous one, the observer of cosmic order (*ṛtāvan*), the great one with brilliant luster—
to Agni, you who offer praise.
May the bountiful Lord, kindled and invoked with oblations, bestow upon us glory accompanied by heroes;
for will not his most recent favor come toward us with strengthening riches?
Praise Agni, the most beloved of those dear to us, the guest from afar, the driver of chariots, the one who leads.
He who, worthy of sacrifice, brings forth wealth— whether it be proclaimed, concealed, or known—
he whose waves are difficult to overcome as he speeds down the slope, seeking to win booty through his inspired thought.
May the guest Agni, the Vasu, praised by many, not be angry with us—
he who is the excellent invoker and the performer of the perfect sacrifice.
O Vasu Agni, let none of those who approach you with invocations come to harm through any of their ways;
for even the poor man, having offered the oblation, prays to you as his messenger at the well-performed sacrifice.
O Agni, come as a friend of the Maruts with the Rudras for the drinking of Soma;
come to the excellent praise of Sobhari, and rejoice, O Svarṇara.
Flow on with your sweetest and most intoxicating stream, O Soma,
pressed out for Indra to drink.
The slayer of demons, the observer of all people, has sat upon his iron-fashioned womb,
his place of assembly, with the wooden vessel.
Be the best provider of wide space, the most generous, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra;
bring across the wealth of the patrons.
Flow toward the feast of the great gods with your juice;
flow toward strength and fame.
Toward you we move, for this very purpose day after day; O Indu, our hopes are fixed upon you.
The daughter of the Sun purifies your flowing Soma with the eternal, continuous fleece.
Him, the slender fingers— the ten sisters— seize together at the gathering on the decisive day.
The maidens urge him on; they blow the leather bag like a bellows—the threefold, elephant-like honey.
The inviolable milch-cows mix this Soma, the infant, for Indra to drink.
In the exhilaration of this [Soma], Indra slays all Vṛtras;
as a hero, he bestows riches upon us.
Flow onward with speed through the filter, O Soma, winner of the gods;
as a bull, O Indu, enter into Indra.
Flow forth, O Indu, as a great draught, most resplendent bull;
as one who sustains, sit upon your seat.
They have milked the beloved honey, the streams of the pressed juice of the wise ordainer; the one of excellent power has clothed himself in the waters.
The great waters, the rivers, flow after you, the mighty one,
when you clothe yourself in the milk of cows.
The ocean has been purified in the waters; Soma, the support and sustainer of heaven, seeking us, is cleansed in the filter.
The tawny bull has bellowed; great and fair to behold like Mitra, he shines together with the sun.
O Indu, your active songs are polished with power, those by which you adorn yourself for exhilaration.
We approach you, the maker of wide space, for the sake of exhilarating joy;
great indeed are your praises.
O Indu, desiring Indra, flow for us with a stream of honey,
like Parjanya rich in rain.
O Indu, you are the winner of cattle, the winner of men, the winner of horses, and the winner of booty;
you are the primordial soul of the sacrifice.
This immortal god flies like a winged bird to settle within the wooden vats.
This god, prepared by inspired hymns, flows swiftly over the obstacles;
he is Pavamāna, the invincible.
This god, Pavamāna, the tawny one, is being cleansed for the sake of strength by those who praise him and love the cosmic order.
This Pavamāna, like a hero going forth with his warriors, seeks to win all desirable things.
This god, Pavamāna, speeds on his chariot;
he bestows gifts and makes his voice manifest.
Praised by the sages, this god plunges into the waters,
bestowing treasures upon the donor.
This Pavamāna, bellowing aloud, rushes through the mid-air regions across the sky with his stream.
This Pavamāna, the one who performs the fair sacrifice, has spread across the sky, passing through the unobstructed regions.
According to his ancient birth, this god, pressed for the sake of the gods,
the tawny one, flows through the filter.
This very one, of many vows, being born and generating strengthening foods, flows with a stream when pressed.
O Soma, as you flow clear, win and conquer great renown; and then, O Pavamāna, make us more prosperous.
Winning light, winning the sun, and all felicities, O Soma—
then make us more prosperous.
Winning skill and mental power, O Soma, drive away our enemies;
then make us more prosperous.
O purifiers, purify the Soma for Indra to drink;
and then make us more prosperous.
Grant us our share in the sun through your wisdom and your protections;
then make us more prosperous.
By your wisdom and by your protections, may we long behold the sun;
then make us more prosperous.
Flow toward us, O Soma, well-armed one, with doubly great wealth;
and then make us more prosperous.
Flow toward us, O unshakable one, as a conqueror in battles;
then make us more prosperous.
O Pavamāna, they have magnified you with sacrifices in this world;
therefore, make us more prosperous.
O Indu, bring us wondrous wealth consisting of horses and all-encompassing life;
then make us more prosperous.
Enkindled, the Lord of all, Pavamāna shines forth,
the Bull, bellowing loudly and bringing delight.
Tanūnapāt, the purifying one, flows onward sharpening his horns, shining brightly through the mid-air.
Worthy of invocation, the radiant Pavamāna shines forth as wealth,
with the streams of sweetness and with power.
Strewing the sacrificial grass eastward with his might, the tawny Pavamāna,
a god among the gods, moves forward.
The golden, divine doors have been thrown wide open by the rising [streams],
well-praised by Pavamāna.
Pavamāna yearns for the two great, vast, and well-fashioned ones, who are beautiful to behold like Night and Dawn.
I invoke both divine Hotṛ-priests who behold men;
O Pavamāna, you are Indra, the bull.
May Bhāratī, Sarasvatī, and the great Ilā of the purifying one—
these three well-adorned goddesses— come to this sacrifice of ours.
I invoke Tvaṣṭṛ, the first-born guardian who goes before;
Indu is Indra, the bull, the golden-hued, the purifying Prajāpati.
O Pavamāna, anoint the Lord of the Forest with a stream of honey—
him who has a thousand branches, who is green, radiant, and golden.
O All-Gods, come to the consecration with the cry of *svāhā* of Pavamāna—
Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Sūrya, Agni, and Indra, being of one accord.
O Soma, flow with a pleasant stream as a bull, seeking the gods, through the sheep's wool,
longing for us.
O Indu, flow toward that exhilarating intoxication, O Indra;
flow toward the prize-winning steeds.
Being pressed, flow toward that ancient exhilarating drink in the filter;
flow toward strength and fame.
The drops, the Soma-drops, have flowed along like waters down a slope; being purified, they have reached Indra.
Him whom the ten young women cleanse like a spirited steed, sporting in the wood beyond the sheepskin filter.
Mix for the sake of the sacrifice and for exhilaration that bull-like juice, pressed with milk, for the feast of the gods.
The god, pressed for the god Indra, flows forth clearly,
so that his milk may swell.
The soul of the sacrifice, pressed and flowing swiftly, purifies itself;
it guards the ancient wisdom of the seers.
Thus, being purified, seeking Indra, O most intoxicating one, flow for the feast;
even though you dwell in secret, you have accepted our songs.
The beautiful drops have been poured forth along the path according to the law of Truth,
knowing its course.
The foremost stream of honeyed juice plunges into the great waters;
the oblation among oblations is worthy of praise.
The foremost bull has bellowed toward the woods, setting in motion the joined voices;
he is the true sacrifice, proceeding toward the dwellings.
When the seer, clothing himself in poetic wisdoms and manly powers, flows around,
the prize-winning steed seeks to win the light of heaven.
Pavamāna sits over the rival clans like a king when the wise priests set him in motion.
The beloved tawny one settles within the wooden vats upon the sheep’s wool;
the singer, through his hymn, strives for him.
He goes together with Vāyu, Indra, and the Aśvins, along with the exhilarating draught,
he who rejoices according to his laws.
The waves of the sweet [Soma] flow toward Mitra, Varuṇa, and Bhaga,
made known through his powers.
O Heaven and Earth, win for us wealth, the sweetness of the prize of strength,
glory, and treasures.
These Soma juices have flowed forth toward the dear desire of Indra,
increasing his heroic power.
Being purified, seated in the vessels, and going to Vāyu and the Aśvins—
may they bestow upon us great heroic strength.
O Soma, being purified, impel the heart of Indra for the sake of bounty,
so that you may sit upon the seat of the Cosmic Order (*ṛta*).
The ten fingers cleanse you; the seven prayers impel you; the sages have rejoiced after you.
Thee, being poured forth for the exhilaration of the gods beyond the sheep's fleece,
we clothe with the milk of cows.
Being purified in the jars, the ruddy, golden-hued one has clothed himself in garments made of milk.
Flow for us from the liberal giver; strike away all enemies.
O Indu, enter into your friend.
Flow down the rain from heaven; bestow splendor upon the earth.
O Soma, grant us strength in battles.
May we partake of you, who beholds men, who are drunk by Indra, and who finds the light of heaven— may we obtain offspring and nourishment.
The sage of heaven, having been placed between the two daughters, goes forth being pressed, encompassing the dear vital strengths, he who possesses the wisdom of a seer.
Flow on and on for the dwelling, beloved by the guileless folk,
for their most delightful enjoyment.
