He, the pure son, having been born, caused his two parents to shine once they were born;
he, the great one, [shone upon] the two great ones who increase the cosmic order (*ṛta*).
Urged on by the seven prayers, he has quickened the guileless rivers,
which have strengthened his single eye.
They have established him, the unconquered and mighty youth,
the drop (indu), for your service, O Indra.
The immortal bearer, swiftly carrying [the oblation], beholds the seven;
Krivi has satisfied the goddesses.
O Soma, protect us in our ritual performances; O Purifying One, strike down those darknesses that must be fought.
Now, for our newest hymn ever more new, prepare the paths; as of old, cause the lights to shine.
O Pavamāna, bestow great renown, cattle, horses, and heroic sons;
win for us wisdom, win for us the light of heaven.
Resounding like chariots, like prize-seeking stallions,
the Soma drops have flowed forth for the sake of wealth.
Impelled like chariots, they have sped forth from the hands,
like the offerings of singers.
Like kings with praises, the Soma drops are adorned with milk,
like a sacrifice by the seven ordainers.
Being pressed for exhilaration with great power and song, the drops flow forth in a stream, the juices once extracted.
Drinking from Vivasvat, they have generated the fortune of the Dawn;
as suns, they spread across the fine strainer.
The ancient poets, the Āyus, open the doors of inspired thoughts for the impetuous might of the Bull.
The seven Hotṛ-priests, born of one mother, sit together in harmony; they fill out the station of the One.
I have joined my navel with your navel, as the eye is united with the sun;
the offspring of the Seer is milked forth.
The Sun beholds with his eye the dear place of heaven, hidden in the secret cave by the Adhvaryu priests.
Sing forth, O men, to this Indu as he purifies himself;
he seeks to reach the gods.
The Atharvans have fortified your milk with honey,
O god who yearns for the gods, for the sake of the god.
As such, flow pure for us— blessing to our cattle, blessing to our people, blessing to our horses, and, O King, blessing to the plants.
Now sing a song to Soma, the tawny one, who is self-strong, ruddy, and touches the heavens.
Purify the pressed Soma with stones moved by the hands;
pour the honey into the honey.
Approach with reverence; mix [the offering] with curd;
place the Soma-drop within Indra.
O Soma, slayer of enemies, most active among men, flow clear for the welfare of our cattle,
fulfilling the desires of the gods.
O Soma, you are poured out for Indra to drink, for his exhilaration;
you are the inspirer of thought, the lord of the mind.
O Pavamāna Soma, bestow upon us wealth consisting of heroic strength;
O Indu, together with Indra as our ally!
The Soma drops have been poured out, the pressed juices at the seat of Ṛta,
most rich in sweetness for Indra.
The sages have shouted their praise toward Indra for the drinking of the Soma, as mother cows low toward their calf.
Dropping exhilaration, the wise Soma dwells in his seat upon the wave of the river; he rests upon the two white cows.
Far-sighted at the navel of heaven, Soma, the wise seer of excellent insight, is magnified upon the fleece of the sheep.
That Soma which has been placed within the jars, inside the filter— Indu has embraced it from all sides.
The drop sends forth its voice upon the surface of the ocean, enlivening the vessel that drips with honey.
The Lord of the Forest, whose praise is eternal, the end of prayers, yielding abundance within,
impels the generations of men.
Being urged on, Soma, the seer, flows toward the dear places of heaven with the stream of the inspired singer.
O Pavamāna, bestow upon us wealth of thousandfold luster, O Indu, that which is self-sustaining.
Soma, being purified, flows in a thousand streams through the sheep’s wool,
to the appointed place of Vāyu and Indra.
O seekers of aid, sing forth to Pavamāna, the inspired sage,
who has been pressed for the banquet of the gods.
The Soma juices, possessing thousandfold power, flow for the winning of booty,
being praised for the feast of the gods.
And flow for us, O Indu, for the winning of booty and for great nourishments— splendid and rich in heroic strength.
May these pressed divine drops, the Indus, flow for us with thousandfold wealth and heroic strength.
Like coursers urged on by their drivers, the swift ones have been let loose through the sheep's wool filter for the winning of the prize.
The Soma drops flow lowing like milch-cows toward their calf;
they have run forth from the hands.
O Pavamāna, being exhilarating and pleasing to Indra, bellowing loudly,
strike away all our enemies.
Driving away the stingy ones, O purifying Soma-drops who behold the light of heaven,
sit in the womb of Cosmic Order.
The sage has flowed around, resting upon the wave of the river,
bearing the much-desired song of praise.
When the five kindred hosts, active in their work, with song prepare the steadfast one for him who is their kin.
Then all the gods have exhilarated themselves upon the juice of this impetuous one,
when he clothes himself in the products of the cow.
Striking down and scattering the bodies and arrows, he rushes forth; there, with his companion, he smites together.
He who, like a radiant youth, has been cleansed by the granddaughters of Vivasvat,
making the cows his own garment.
Crossing over with his two oblique paths, he goes forth seeking cattle through the fine strainer;
he utters the sound for which he is known.
The swift fingers have gathered together, purifying the Lord of Refreshments;
seize the back of the vigorous steed.
O Soma, stroking all the celestial and terrestrial treasures, come toward us, seeking our favor.
This hero goes by means of subtle wisdom and with swift chariots,
proceeding to the appointed place of Indra.
He, through his many thoughts, exerts himself for the great host of gods,
where the immortals sit.
This [Soma], once set forth, is led along the path that leads to the bright ones,
when the eager [pressers] urge him on.
This bull of the herd, shaking his horns, whets them;
bestowing manly powers by his might.
This vigorous steed moves along with golden ornaments and brilliant rays,
becoming the lord of the rivers.
This one, having passed over the firm joints and the rugged places,
goes down into the settling-places.
Men cleanse him who is worthy of cleansing in the wooden vats—
him who brings forth great refreshments.
Him indeed, the ten fingers and the seven prayers cleanse—
him who is well-armed and most intoxicating.
O pressers, pour forth your juice for your exhilarating, impetuous intoxication; let Etaśa speed like a released torrent.
Through the power of skill, we have followed him who is the charioteer of dexterity, who clothes himself in the waters with his juice—
the winner of cattle among the fine [strainers].
Release into the waters the unassailable Soma that is difficult to cross over;
purify it for Indra to drink.
With the intent of one being purified, Soma flows through the filter; by his mental power, he has taken his seat upon the common dwelling-place.
The Soma drops, O Indra, have been poured forth for you with prostrations—
those who perform the rite for the great prize.
Being purified, flowing toward all splendors within the eternal form,
he stands among the cattle like a hero.
Like the swelling ridge of heaven, the stream of the pressed juice of the wise one flows freely through the filter.
O Soma, being purified through the lineages among living men, you, the wise one,
flow through the sheep’s wool filter.
Like rivers flowing down a slope, the impetuous Soma drops, swiftly slaying the Vritras, have been let loose.
Like rains upon the earth, the pressed drops,
the Soma juices, have flowed toward Indra.
The exhilarating, intoxicating Soma, surging over the waves, flows through the filter,
warding off the demons while seeking the gods.
He rushes into the jars; he is poured around the filter;
he grows strong at the sacrifices through the hymns of praise.
O Soma, ascending above the three luminous realms, you shine like the sky;
sending forth your rays, you impel the sun.
The inspired singers have sung forth to him at the head of the sacrifice,
bestowing what is dear upon his sight.
Him, the prize-winning one, the sages, seeking aid, cleanse with their prayers for the sake of the gods.
Flow along the stream of honey; as the potent one, take your seat upon the common place—beautiful for the sake of the sacrifice and for drinking.
Being pressed, Soma, dwelling on the mountains, has flowed through the filter; in the exhilarations, you are the bestower of all things.
You are the inspired singer, you are the seer; the honey is born from the soma-juice. In your exhilarations, you are the bestower of all things.
All the gods, acting in unison, have attained your draught; in your exhilarations, you are the bestower of all things.
He who holds in his hands all desirable treasures— you are the bestower of everything in our exhilarations.
He who milks these two great worlds, Rodasī, like two mother cows— he,
in his exhilarations, is the bestower of all things.
He who flows instantly around both worlds with his strengths; in your exhilarations, you are the bestower of all things.
That vigorous one, being purified within the jars, has cried out;
in your exhilarations, you are the bestower of all things.
O Soma, as you are being purified, bring to us that wonderful, praiseworthy wealth which is celestial and terrestrial.
For you two, O Indra and Soma, are the lords of heaven and the lords of cattle;
as masters, cause our prayers to swell.
The bull, being purified among living beings, thundering upon the sacred grass—
being golden-hued, he has settled in his place.
The prayers have lowed over the seed of the bull,
the mothers over their son, the calf.
Purifying himself, has he not indeed bestowed the germ upon those longing for the bull—
those who milk out the bright milk?
Bestow fear upon the enemies who stand aloof;
O Pavamāna, find us wealth.
O Soma, strike down the virility of the enemy, strike down his strength, and strike down his vital power,
whether he be far away or near at hand.
The sage flows forth through the sheep’s woolly filter for the feast of the gods,
overcoming all rivalrous foes.
For he, indeed, as Pavamāna, bestows upon his singers thousandfold wealth consisting of cattle.
You encompass all things with your consciousness; you flow clear through our hymns.
O Soma, as such, find glory for us.
Flow toward us with great glory, with stable wealth for the patrons;
bring nourishment to those who praise you.
O wonderful bearer of the oblation, O Soma, being purified, you have entered the songs like a king of noble vows.
That Soma, the invoker difficult to overcome in the waters, being cleansed by the two hands, settles within the vessels.
Sporting like a generous sacrificer, O Soma, you go to the filter,
bestowing great heroic strength upon the singer.
These Soma drops run toward Indra, exhilarating, joyous, and finders of the light.
Driving away assailants, finding room for the one who presses the soma, they themselves bestow vital strength upon the singer.
Playing freely, the drops have flowed together toward their single common dwelling;
they have poured forth with the wave of the river.
These purifying Soma-drops have attained all desirable things, like well-harnessed horses yoked to a chariot.
O drops, bestow upon this man a tawny,
longing [desire] to point out him who is ungenerous toward us.
Like R̥bhu, bestow a new chariot for our purpose;
O bright ones, flow pure with your flood.
These very ones have lowed; the prize-winners have reached the goal;
from existence they have poured forth their thought.
These swift Soma drops have sped forth like chariots, like prize-winning steeds let loose in their course.
Like winds, they are wide-reaching; like the rains of Parjanya, they are impetuous; like the flickering flames of fire, they move at will.
These purified, wise Soma juices, mixed with curds,
have pervaded the prayers through inspired thought.
These immortal ones, once cleansed, have run their course and yet do not weary; desiring to sacrifice, they traverse the paths through the mid-air.
These [Soma drops], moving as priests, have pervaded the heights of heaven and earth,
even reaching this highest realm.
They have followed along the downward slopes the highest thread being stretched out;
and this is most worthy of praise.
O Soma, you held for us the wealth of cattle from the Paṇis;
you made the stretched-out thread resound.
The swift Soma drops have been poured forth in a stream of honeyed exhilaration,
toward all poetic inspirations.
The ancient Āyus have followed after the newest track;
they have brought forth the sun for splendor.
O Pavamāna, bring to us the wealth of the non-sacrificing enemy;
provide us with nourishments accompanied by progeny.
The Soma-drops, the active ones, flow toward the intoxicating exhilaration,
toward the honey-dripping vat.
Soma flows on, the sustainer, bestowing vital power and essence;
he is the possessor of noble heroes and the protector against curses.
O Soma, you flow for Indra, for the gods, as one who shares the feast;
O Indu, you desire to win us strength.
Having drunk of his exhilarating draughts, Indra, irresistible, struck down the Vṛtras and shall strike them down yet again.
The Soma drops, the purifying juices, have flowed forth;
being mixed with milk, they are cleansed in the waters.
The cows have run toward him like waters flowing down a slope; being purified, they have reached Indra.
O Pavamāna Soma, you flow forth for Indra to drink;
guided by the men, you are led out.
O Soma, flow as the exhilarator of men, for the sake of the subduer of peoples— you who are a winner of spoils and worthy of universal acclaim.
O Indu, when pressed by the stones, you run through the filter;
you are ready for the abode of Indra.
Flow on, O greatest slayer of Vṛtra, to be celebrated with hymns of praise—
you who are pure, purifying, and wonderful.
Pure and purifying is Soma called, the pressed-out honey; he is the one who favors the gods and slays the speakers of evil.
Flow on, O golden-hued one, you who accomplish skillful power, for the gods to drink;
flow as a gladdening draught for the Maruts and for Vāyu.
O Pavamāna, impelled by the prayer, crying out toward your place of origin,
enter Vāyu according to the cosmic law.
The bull, the sage, the beloved, shines together with the gods in his dwelling;
he is the slayer of Vṛtra, the one who most invites the gods.
Entering all forms, being purified,
the beloved one goes to where the immortals sit.
The ruddy Soma, engendering songs, flows on for the sake of long life,
going toward Indra with the wisdom of a seer.
Flow, O most intoxicating sage, through the filter with your stream, to sit upon the seat of the hymn.
The inspired poets have groomed that vigorous steed upon the lap of Aditi with their subtle prayer.
The cows have lowed toward him, the inexhaustible one with a thousand streams—
the drop (*indu*), the sustainer from heaven.
They have brought that creator, Pavamāna, by means of wisdom upon the sky—
the sustainer who provides abundant nourishment.
With prayer, they have sent him forth from the two arms, him who dwells with Vivasvat,
the infallible lord of speech.
Upon his back, the sisters urge the tawny one with the pressing-stones—
the beloved one, the far-seeing.
The wise ones impel you, O Pavamāna, who increase with song—
O Indu, the exhilarating one— for Indra.
This seer, highly praised, flows over the filter; purifying himself, he strikes away the adversaries.
This Soma, the winner of light, which accomplishes skillful power, is poured out for Indra and Vāyu within the filter.
This Soma, the head of heaven, the bull, pressed by men, is led forth through the wooden vats— he who knows all things.
Desiring cattle and desiring gold, this Indu, the purifying one— ever-conquering and invincible— has bellowed forth.
This Pavamāna, the exhilarating intoxicant, shines together with Sūrya in the sky as he flows through the filter.
This powerful, tawny bull has flowed through the mid-air; being purified, the drop goes toward Indra.
This prize-winning steed, sent forth by the men, the all-knowing lord of the mind,
rushes through the sheep’s wool filter.
This Soma, pressed for the gods, has flowed through the filter,
entering all the stations.
This immortal god shines forth in his dwelling;
he is the slayer of Vṛtra, the one most beloved by the gods.
This bull, bellowing loudly, guided by his ten sisters,
rushes toward the wooden vats.
This Pavamāna, the all-seeing and all-knowing, has caused the sun to shine and has illuminated all the realms.
This powerful, invincible Soma flows while being purified; he is the friend of the gods and the slayer of those who speak evil.
His streams have flowed forth by the power of the pressed bull,
as he stands ready to serve the gods.
The wise singers, chanting with their song, groom the steed—
the light that has been born, worthy of praise.
O Soma, Lord of abundant wealth, these things are easy for you to overcome as you purify yourself; increase the ocean that is worthy of praise.
Winning all treasures, flow onward, O Soma, with your stream;
drive away our enemies together.
Protect us well from the malicious man, from the shout of anyone at all, so that we may be released from blame.
O Soma, flow with your stream, purifying earthly and celestial wealth;
bring us brilliant vigor.
The streams of this impetuous one have flowed freely through the filter; purifying himself, he sends forth his voice.
The drop, urged by the pressers and being cleansed while bellowing,
sends forth the voice of Indra.
Flow for us, O Soma, with your stream— our strength that conquers men, rich in heroes, and much-desired.
Soma, being purified, has flowed forth with his stream,
to settle within the wooden vats.
In the waters they urge you on with stones— the honey-sweet, golden-hued one—
O Indu, for Indra to drink.
Press out for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the most honey-sweet Soma; press it as a lovely, exhilarating draught for the host.
The Soma drops, well-intentioned and purifying, have moved forward;
they create wealth that brings wisdom.
O Indu, from heaven and from earth, be the increaser of our splendor;
become the lord of spoils.
For you the winds blow favorably; for you the rivers flow;
O Soma, they increase your greatness.
Swell up; let virile strength come to you from every side, O Soma; be present at the gathering of booty.
For you, O tawny one, the cows have milked out imperishable ghee and milk upon the highest ridge.
O Indu, Lord of the world, you who possess excellent weapons, we desire your friendship.
The Soma drops, distilling exhilaration for the glory of our patrons,
have been pressed and have gone forth to the assembly.
Then the maidens of Trita urge the tawny one with the stones—
the drop for Indra to drink.
Then, like a swan to its flock, he has caused the prayer of every man to resound;
like a steed, he is adorned with milk.
O Soma, looking down upon both worlds, you flow like a darting deer,
settling in the womb of the Eternal Order.
The cows have lowed toward him, as a young woman toward her beloved; he has gone to the race, like one who has set his goal.
Bestow upon us resplendent glory for our patrons and for myself— gain,
inspired wisdom, and renown.
The wise Soma drops flow forth like waves of water,
like buffaloes toward the forests.
The tawny, bright drops have flowed toward the wooden vats with the stream of *ṛta*,
pouring forth strength consisting of cattle.
The pressed Soma juices flow for Indra, for Vāyu, for Varuṇa, for the Maruts, and for Viṣṇu.
Three voices rise up; the cows low as milch-kine;
the tawny one goes along bellowing.
The young mothers of the cosmic order (*ṛta*), the divine powers, have sung out toward him;
they groom the Child of Heaven.
O Soma, flow for us from every side with riches that are like the four oceans, bringing thousandsfold wealth.
Being pressed, Indu flows forth in a stream, urging himself on; with his might, he breaks through even the firmest things.
Pressed for Indra, for Vāyu, for Varuṇa, and for the Maruts,
Soma flows for Viṣṇu.
They press the bull Soma with stones, guided by the bulls; they milk the milk with skillful power.
He becomes the one to be cleansed for Trita; he becomes the intoxicant for Indra. The tawny one is anointed with his forms.
The sons of Pṛśni milk him, the summit of Truth,
for the lovely and most beloved oblation.
These unswerving songs flow toward him together;
the lowing bull has made the milch-cows bellow.
Flow toward us with your stream, O Pavamāna, bestowing vast wealth,
by which you may grant us light.
O Indu, stirrer of the ocean, flow on, O all-agiter; as the upholder of wealth, protect us with your might.
With you as our hero, may we, as heroes ourselves, overcome those who attack us;
let there flow for us what is desirable.
The drop, the seer who wins the prize, sends forth his strength, desiring to win; he knows the sacred laws and his weapons.
With our songs we clothe him who stirs the voice while being purified—
Soma, the lord of the people.
He under whose law all people abide, the lord of the sacred order, as he is being purified, O possessor of abundant wealth.
The pressed juice has been released into the two bowls like a chariot-horse; the prize-winner has stepped down upon the goal-line.
O Soma, as a wakeful bearer, flow across [the filter] to win the gods,
toward the honey-dripping vat.
O ancient Pavamāna, make the lights shine forth for us; impel us toward wisdom and skill.
Being beautified by those who love the *ṛta*, and being cleansed by the two hands,
he flows through the sheep’s wool filter.
May that Soma, for the sake of the donor, flow with all treasures from heaven, from earth,
and from the intermediate space.
O Soma, Lord of Might, seeking horses and seeking cattle, you ascend to the back of heaven; seeking heroes, you rise upward.
Pressed for the sake of drinking, that bull Soma flows through the filter,
warding off the demons and seeking the gods.
Far-sighted and tawny, he flows through the filter, the sustainer, bellowing toward his place of rest.
That vigorous steed, Pavamāna, rushes through the luminous realms of heaven,
the slayer of demons, across the woolly filter.
Pavamāna, upon the ridge of Trita, caused the sun to shine together with his kinsmen.
That Soma, the slayer of Vṛtra, the bull, the pressed one, the finder of wide space, and the invincible, has sped forth like toward booty.
Impelled by the seer, that god, Indu, rushes toward the wooden vats for Indra with great abundance.
This very bull, the chariot, flows through the woollen filter,
going toward thousandfold booty.
The maidens of Trita urge this tawny one with the stones—
the drop for Indra to drink.
Him, the golden-hued one, the ten active fingers cleanse thoroughly—
those [fingers] with which he is adorned for exhilaration.
Like a falcon settling among the human clans, he sits down; he goes like a lover toward his mistress.
This exhilarating juice, the child of heaven, looks down from on high— the drop that has entered the filter.
This golden one, pressed for drinking, flows as a steadfast supporter, crying out toward his beloved dwelling-place.
Flow swiftly, O one of lofty thought, with your beloved form,
to where they say, "The gods are."
Preparing what was unprepared, providing nourishment for the people,
flow forth from heaven as rain.
Pressed out, he goes into the filter, assuming brilliance by his might,
looking about and shining forth.
This is he who, with rapid course, from the sky has flowed through the filter; he has streamed forth upon the wave of the river.
Inviting [the gods] from afar and also from nearby,
the pressed sweet juice is poured out for Indra.
Turning together, they have sung; they urge the tawny one with the stones;
sit in the womb of Cosmic Order.
Being purified, the far-seeing one has stepped upon all adversaries;
they adorn the sage with their prayers.
The ruddy one has mounted his place; the pressed bull goes to Indra;
he sits in his firm seat.
Now, O Indu, flow forth for us from every side, O Soma, bringing great wealth in thousands.
O Soma Pavamāna, O Indu, bring all splendors;
find for us thousandfold nourishments.
As you are being purified, bring to us wealth and heroic strength for the singer; increase the hymns of the one who praises you.
O Indu, being purified, O Soma, bring us doubly-mighty wealth;
O virile Indu, [bring] that which is worthy of praise for us.
Those who have advanced like restless bulls, impetuous and unwearied,
driving away the black skin.
We meditate upon a good path across the bridge that is difficult to cross,
overcoming the lawless Dasyu.
The roar of the mighty Pavamāna is heard like the sound of rain;
lightnings flash across the sky.
Flow forth, O Indu, as pressed juice, bringing great nourishment, rich in cattle, rich in gold, rich in horses, and rich in vigor.
Flow on, O you who observe all people; fill the two great worlds, heaven and earth, as the Dawn and the Sun fill them with their rays.
O Soma, flow around us on every side with a stream that brings us protection;
spread over us like moisture over the earth.
Generating the luminous realms of heaven, generating the sun within the waters,
the tawny one clothes himself in the cows and the waters.
According to the ancient hymn, this god, pressed out for the sake of the gods,
flows forth in a stream.
The Soma juices, possessing thousandfold power, flow clear for the sake of winning booty for the one who has grown great and prevails.
Yielding its ancient milk, it is poured out across the filter;
crying out, it has brought the gods to birth.
Soma, being purified, flows toward all desirable things and toward the gods who increase the cosmic order (*ṛta*).
O Soma, being pressed, flow for us with cattle, with heroes, with horses, and with strength; flow on toward great nourishments.
He who, like a steed, is cleansed by the milk-streams for exhilaration, the beloved one—
we clothe him with our songs.
All our songs, seeking his aid, adorn him as of old—
the Indu for Indra’s drinking.
Being purified, the beloved Soma goes forth, adorned with songs, [the work] of the inspired Medhyātithi.
O Pavamāna Soma, find for us wealth accompanied by great glory;
O Indu, [find] that which possesses a thousandfold luster.
Like a courser seeking prize-winning speed, Indu roars loudly within the filter as he flows across,
longing for the gods.
Flow on for the winning of strength, for the increase of the inspired singer who praises you; O Soma, grant us heroic power.
O Indu, bearing [the Soma] like a wave for our great expansion, flow forth toward the gods, you who are unwearied.
Pleased by our hymns and impelled by our prayer, Soma, the seer, is driven forth in the distance by the stream of the inspired singer.
This Soma, watchful among the gods, goes pressed into the filter; the far-seeing one moves along.
Flow for us, seeking strength, making our sacrifice beautiful;
the one who provides the sacred grass invites you hither.
May Soma, the hero among sages and the ever-increasing one, direct us toward Bhaga and Vāyu among the gods.
May he, the knower of wills, the best finder of the path, win for us today great renown and booty for our prosperity.
Flow on for exhilaration, O you who behold men, for the banquet of the gods;
flow, O Indu, for Indra to drink.
Flow for us toward the mission of a messenger; you bestow gifts upon Indra, bringing the gods as a boon to our friends.
And we anoint you, the ruddy one, with milk for exhilaration;
open wide for us the doors to wealth.
The prize-winning steed has passed through the filter as if to the pole on his course;
Indu rules among the gods.
Together his friends have shouted for him as he plays in the wood, beyond the sheepskin;
they have sung to Indu with their voices.
Flow with that stream by which, when drunk, O Indu, you bestow great heroic power upon the singer.
The steeds have been let loose for the feast of the gods, like successful warriors,
flowing forth, increasing upon the mountains.
Adorned like a maiden seeking her father’s house,
the Soma drops have flowed forth to Vāyu.
These Soma drops, full of nourishment, pressed into the vessels,
increase Indra through their ritual acts.
O dexterous ones, run hither; seize the bright juices with the *manthin* vessel.
Mix the exhilarating draught with milk.
Flow on, O winner of wealth, bestowing great riches;
O Soma, find the path for us.
The ten fingers cleanse this Pavamāna who is worthy of being cleansed—
the exhilarating intoxicant for Indra.
Through this skillful act, Soma has increased even beyond the great;
exhilarated, he acts like a bull.
His deeds that were done and those yet to be done are manifest as the subduing of the Dasyus;
and the bold one exacts the debts.
Then, O Soma, the Indra-powering juice becomes a thousand-winning thunderbolt when his hymn of praise is born.
The poet himself, as the distributor, seeks a treasure for the sage when he thoroughly polishes his inspired thoughts.
You are one who desires to win riches, like the prize-winning steeds in races, among those who have been victorious in battles.
We, through our skillful work, seek you— the one who bears manly powers in the gathering places of the great heaven— as the beloved one.
The exhilarating drink, which crushes the bold, is worthy of praise and possesses most mighty ordinances;
it desires to shatter a hundred fortresses.
From there, O wise one, the unwavering, well-winged bird has brought you, the king of wealth, from heaven.
For every man to behold the light, he has brought forth the guardian of Truth, the common one who traverses the mid-air.
Then, being urged forth, he attained greater Indra-power and majesty—
he who brings aid and observes all people.
Flow for us, bringing rain from heaven, a wave of waters; bring us great, disease-free nourishments.
Flow with that stream by which the cows belonging to the people have come here to our house.
Flow with a stream of clarified butter, O you who are most beloved by the gods at the sacrifices;
pour down rain for us.
Flow for us with your stream through the woolly filter for the sake of nourishment;
let the gods indeed hear us.
Pavamāna has flowed forth, striking down the demons,
making the lights shine as of old.
Your vital energies surge forth like the roar of a river’s wave;
sharpen the point of your arrow.
At your impulsion, three voices eager for the sacrifice rise up,
when you go upon the back of the sheep’s wool.
They urge the beloved tawny one through the sheep’s wool with stones— the purifying one who drips with sweetness.
Flow, O most exhilarating sage, through the filter in a stream, to sit upon the seat of the hymn.
Flow on, O most intoxicating one, anointed with milk and with ointments,
O Indu, for Indra to drink.
O Adhvaryu, pour the Soma pressed with stones onto the filter;
purify it for Indra to drink.
Press out for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the most excellent nectar of heaven— the Soma that is most rich in sweetness.
O Indu, those gods and the Maruts partake of this sweet juice of yours, of you as you flow clear.
For you, O Soma, being pressed for the rousing exhilaration,
do you, O bull, strengthen the praiser for his protection.
Flow toward the filter with your stream, O far-seeing one, being pressed—
toward strength and fame.
Dwelling in heaven, winning wealth, may he bring us strength with his juice;
being pressed, flow into the filter.
By your ancient paths, the beloved one flows through the sheep’s wool filter in a thousand streams, continuing on.
Like a sacrificial oblation, O Indu, cause him to sway; like a gift, O Indu, cause him to sway;
with your weapons, O wielder of weapons, cause him to sway.
O Indu, invoked by many, bring down the strength of these people who direct their commands against us.
O Indu, flow for us with a hundred or a thousand pure aids,
bestowing abundant wealth.
O wielder of the stone, your vital powers have risen up, shattering the demons;
drive away those who are our rivals.
With this [song], you who strike down [the foe] by your might when chariots clash and wealth is staked,
you are praised with a fearless heart.
No one of evil intent can violate the laws of this Pavamāna; shatter him who attacks you!
They urge him on, the exhilarating, tawny, prize-winning steed, Indu, for Indra, the one who distills intoxication into the rivers.
Following his ancient splendor, the bold ones have milked the bright milk from the seer who wins a thousandfold.
This one is visible like the sun; he runs toward the lakes, across the seven downward-flowing rivers unto heaven.
Being purified, this Soma stands above all worlds,
like the divine Sun.
Flow around us for the feast of the gods, O Indu, bringing strengths rich in cattle, as you are purified, longing for Indra.
O Soma, flow around us with your juice, yielding grain after grain and nourishment after nourishment, and bestow all auspicious blessings.
O Indu, just as there is praise for you, and just as there is the production of your juice,
so do you sit upon the beloved sacrificial grass.
And as a finder of cattle and a finder of horses, O Soma, flow for us with your juice through these most rapid days.
He who conquers and is never conquered, who attacks and slays the enemy— O winner of thousands, flow forth as such!
O Soma, the swift one, flows around the filter according to the lofty *ṛta*,
striking down the demons and seeking the gods.
When Soma flows toward the prize in a hundred active streams,
he enters into friendship with Indra.
The ten young women have sung toward you as a maiden sings to her lover; O Soma, you are cleansed for the sake of winning the prize.
O Indu, flow forth as something sweet for Indra and Viṣṇu;
protect the men, the singers, from distress.
Your unceasing streams go forth like rains from heaven,
toward thousandfold strength.
Beholding all beloved poetic insights, he flows onward;
the tawny one, brandishing his weapons.
Being cleansed by the living ones, like a king who observes good vows,
he sits like a hawk upon the trees.
O Indu, being purified, bring to us all treasures from heaven and from the earth.
Crossing over, the exhilarating one flows; the stream of the pressed juice flows;
crossing over, the exhilarating one flows.
The Dawn knows of the treasures; the Goddess knows of the mortal’s help. Crossing over, the exhilarating one flows swiftly.
From the two Dhvasras, the lords of men, we receive thousands;
crossing over, that exhilarating one flows swiftly.
He from whom we receive thirty and thousands in succession—
he, the exhilarating one, speeds across.
Flow on, O Soma, winner of cattle, winner of horses, winner of all, winner of delights; bring us wealth accompanied by progeny.
Flow pure for the waters, O invincible one; flow pure for the plants;
flow pure for the sacred vessels.
O Soma, as you flow clear, cross over all difficulties;
as a seer, sit down upon the sacrificial grass.
O Pavamāna, finder of light, being born you became great;
O Indu, you are superior to all.
Sing forth with the *gāyatra* chant to Pavamāna,
the all-seeing one, to Indu, the thousand-eyed.
Thee, who hast a thousand eyes and a thousandfold sustenance,
they have purified through the filter.
Flowing beyond the fleece, the purifying Soma has sped forth; he rushes toward the jars, entering the heart of Indra.
O Soma, most active one, flow for the prosperity of Indra;
bring us procreative seed for our welfare.
Flow forth for this enjoyment, O Indu, which in thy exhilarations has struck down ninety-nine [foes].
Immediately for Divodāsa who thus meditated, you brought Śambara before him;
and likewise Turvaśa and Yadu.
O Indu, finder of horses, flow around us with horses, cattle, and gold;
pour forth thousandfold nourishments.
We choose for ourselves the friendship of you, Pavamāna, as you flow toward the filter.
O Soma, those waves of yours which flow toward us with their stream across the filter—
through them, O Soma, have mercy on us.
As you are being purified, O Soma, bring us wealth and food accompanied by heroic sons;
for you, O Lord, are sovereign over all.
Him, whose mother is the river, the ten fingers cleanse;
he has been made manifest together with the Ādityas.
The pressed juice goes together with Indra and Vāyu into the filter;
it goes together with the rays of the sun.
Flow for us, rich in sweetness, for Bhaga, Vāyu, and Pūṣan; flow as one pleasing to Mitra and Varuṇa.
High is the birth of your juice; seated in heaven, it has been taken down to earth—terrible protection, great renown.
Through this [Soma], we desire to win all the glories of the noble one and of human beings, seeking to acquire them.
As such, flow forth as a finder of wide space for Indra, who is worthy of sacrifice, for Varuṇa, and for the Maruts.
The gods have come near to the pressed drop, the son of the waters, who has been adorned with milk and is the breaker of obstacles.
May our songs strengthen him, as mother cows nourish their calf—
he who wins the heart of Indra.
Flow for us, O Soma, as a blessing for our cattle; milk out for us swelling nourishment;
increase the ocean worthy of praise.
Pavamāna has generated for us the great light of Vaiśvānara, like the wondrous thunder from heaven.
O King, the exhilarating juice of you, Pavamāna, which wards off misfortune,
flows through the sheep's wool filter.
O Pavamāna, your juice, your skillful power, shines forth brilliantly;
it is all-light, the sun, for all to see.
With that exhilarating juice of yours which is most excellent, flow clear, O you who favor the gods and strike down the speakers of evil.
You are the slayer of Vṛtra, the enemy; you are the winner of booty day after day;
you are the winner of cattle and the winner of horses.
Become mingled with the ruddy ones, like cows easy to tend;
settle here like a hawk upon its nest.
Flow on, you who aided Indra to slay Vṛtra,
who had obstructed the great waters.
O bounteous Soma, may we, possessing brave heroes, win riches;
as you are being purified, increase our songs of praise.
Aided by you and through your protection, may we be victors over those who attack;
O Soma, remain watchful over our sacred observances.
Striking down the adversaries, Soma purifies himself, driving away the stingy ones as he goes to the appointed place of Indra.
O Pavamāna, bring us great wealth; strike down our enemies.
O Indu, grant us glory accompanied by heroic sons.
Not even a hundred deceivers could diminish you when you desire to bestow wealth,
as you purify yourself and act like a sacrificial hero.
Flow clear, O Indu, as the pressed bull; make us glorious among the people;
strike away all our enemies.
In this friendship of yours, O Indu, and in your supreme splendor, may we overcome those who attack us.
Those terrible weapons of yours, which are sharp for striking down—
protect us from every reviler.
These swift Soma drops have been poured through the filter,
toward all auspicious blessings.
Warding off many misfortunes and providing easy paths for our offspring, O possessors of strength, you create continuous prosperity for the steed.
Creating wide space for the cattle, they flow toward our fair praise; may they grant us constant nourishment.
The stalk has been pressed for intoxication in the waters—the skillful one dwelling on the mountains; like a hawk, he has settled in his place.
The bright draught, beloved by the gods, shaken in the waters and pressed by men—
the cows sweeten it with their milk.
Then, like drivers [beautifying] a horse, they have adorned him for immortality—
the essence of honey for the communal feast.
O Indu, those streams of yours that flow dripping with sweetness for our aid— with them you have settled upon the filter.
He flows through the sheep’s woolly fleece for Indra to drink,
settling in his place within the wooden vessels.
O Indu, flow around for the Aṅgirases as the most sweet;
find us wide space, [yielding] ghee and milk.
This Pavamāna, the far-seeing one, is established; he takes notice as he impels the great kinship.
This bull, whose rite is manly, Pavamāna, the slayer of the ill-spoken,
shall bestow riches upon the donor.
Flow forth, purifying, a thousandfold wealth consisting of cattle and horses,
most radiant and much-desired.
This very one is poured out all around, being cleansed by the *āyu* priests— he who strides widely, possessing the wisdom of a seer.
With a thousand aids and a hundredfold wealth, the measurer of the mid-air, the sage,
the exhilarating juice flows for Indra.
Born here through song, the drop, praised, is placed for Indra like a hero in his dwelling-place.
Being pressed by the men, Soma Pavamāna has flowed like prize-winning strength; he has settled in the vessels with his power.
Him they yoke upon the three-backed, triple-seated chariot for his journeying,
by means of the seven seers' inspired thoughts.
O pressers, urge on that tawny, prize-winning steed who longs for wealth, so that he may go swiftly to the contest.
Entering the jar, the pressed juice flows toward all splendors; like a hero among cattle, he stands firm.
O Indu, the Āyus milk out the milk for your exhilaration;
the gods [milk] the honey for the gods.
Pour forth for us into the filter the Soma most rich in sweetness, the one most renowned among the gods, for the sake of the gods.
These Soma juices have been poured forth, being praised for great renown,
with the stream of the most intoxicating one.
Being purified, you flow toward the cattle and manly powers for our enjoyment; winning the prize, flow around us.
And flow for us with all food-offerings accompanied by cattle,
being lauded by Jamadagni.
Flow on as the foremost of speech, O Soma, with your wondrous aids,
toward all poetic inspirations.
You, the foremost, stirring the waters of the ocean with your voice,
flow on, O you who cause all things to tremble.
For you, O Sage, these worlds have been established for your greatness, O Soma;
for you the rivers flow.
Like showers from heaven, your unceasing streams flow forth toward the bright surface-covering.
Purify the Soma-drop for Indra, the fierce one, the accomplisher of skill,
the sovereign lord who bestows abundant wealth.
Pavamāna, the sage of Truth, Soma has sat upon the filter,
bestowing heroic vigor upon the singer.
Flow forth, O Soma, bringing thousandfold wealth and heroic strength; bestow upon us glorious renown.
O most intoxicating one, you swell with nourishment and vigor for Indra; you settle down within the vessels.
The pressed Soma has flowed into the jar for Indra and Viṣṇu;
may it be honey-sweet for Vāyu as well.
These swift, tawny Soma drops have been poured forth in a stream of *ṛta*, passing over all obstacles.
Strengthening Indra, crossing the waters, making all things Aryan, they strike down the stingy ones.
Pressed out according to their own nature, the brown drops flow toward the region of space;
the Soma juices go toward Indra.
Flow with this stream by which you caused the sun to shine,
impelling the waters of mankind.
Pavamāna has yoked Etaśa to the sun for the sake of the mind,
so that he may travel through the intermediate space.
And indeed, those ten bay horses of the Sun he has yoked for the journey,
while the drop proclaims, "Indu is Indra!"
Pour out on every side for Vāyu the pressed juice, and for Indra the exhilarating song;
pour it through the sheep’s wool filters.
O Pavamāna Soma, find for us wealth that is difficult to overcome,
which is hard for the attacker to seize.
Flow toward us with wealth in thousands, consisting of cattle and horses;
flow toward us with strength and glory.
Soma, like the divine Sun, flows purified by the stones when pressed,
placing his essence within the jar.
These bright ones, by the stream of Truth, have flowed toward the noble abodes and toward booty consisting of cattle.
The pressed Soma juices, mixed with curds, have flowed through the filter for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt.
O Soma, flow most richly in sweetness for the sake of wealth into the filter—
that exhilaration which is most beloved by the gods.
The Āyus cleanse him, the tawny, vigorous steed in the rivers—
the drop that exhilarates Indra.
Flow on, O Soma, bringing gold, horses, and heroic sons;
bring us strength consisting of cattle.
Pour him out for Indra, the most honey-sweet, like one seeking prize-winning strength through the sheep’s wool filter.
The inspired poets, seeking aid, cleanse the purifiable sage with their prayers;
bellowing like a bull, he flows onward.
With their prayers and inspired thoughts, the sages have together sounded forth the bull Soma, the one who crosses the waters, by means of the stream of Truth.
Flow on, O you who are dear to the gods; let your exhilarating juice go to Indra. Ascend to Vāyu according to the cosmic law.
O Pavamāna Soma, you bestow upon us wealth worthy of renown;
as one beloved, enter the ocean.
Striking down the adversaries, O Soma, you flow as the exhilarating knower of wisdom;
drive away the folk who follow no gods.
The purifying Soma drops, bright and radiant,
have been let loose toward all poetic inspirations.
The purifying, swift, and radiant drops have been let loose, O Indus,
striking away all enemies.
The purifying Soma-streams have been released from heaven, from the intermediate space,
and over the ridge of the earth.
O Soma, being purified in your stream, O Indu, drive away all failures;
slay the demons, O you of noble power.
O Soma, driving away the Rākṣasas, flow hither with a loud roar,
[bestowing] brilliant and supreme strength.
O Soma, bestow upon us treasures from heaven and from earth;
O Indu, grant us all things worthy of desire.
O Soma, you are a bull, full of splendor; O god, you are a bull whose ordinances are bull-like.
As a bull, you establish the sacred laws.
O Bull, your power is bull-like; you are a bull in the wood, a bull in exhilaration.
O Bull, you are truly a bull.
Like a horse, the bull has neighed; O *Indu*, bring together the cows and the steeds.
Open for us the doors to wealth.
The vigorous Soma juices have been poured forth, seeking cattle and horses— bright, swift, and longing for heroes.
Being beautified by those who love the *ṛta*, and being cleansed by the two hands,
they flow through the woolen filter.
May those Soma juices flow for the donor, bestowing all treasures— those of heaven, those of earth, and those of the intermediate space.
Of Pavamāna, the knower of all, thy streams have been let loose,
like the rays of the sun.
Making a banner from heaven, you flow toward all forms;
O Soma, you swell like the ocean.
Being urged on, O Pavamāna, you send forth your voice across the expanse;
like the divine Sūrya, you have stepped forth.
The conscious drop has been purified, dear to the thoughts of the seers;
he has let loose the steed like a charioteer.
The wave that has flowed around in the filter, seeking the gods,
as it settles into the womb of the Eternal Order (Ṛta).
Flow for us into the filter as that exhilarating draught which most invites the gods,
O Indu, for Indra to drink.
Flow for nourishment with your stream, being purified by the wise;
O Indu, go toward the cows with your luster.
Being purified, O lover of song, create wide space and strength for the people;
O tawny one, being released, flow toward the milk-mixture.
Being purified for the feast of the gods, go to the appointed place of Indra,
shining and guided by the prize-winning steeds.
Being urged forward toward the ocean, the swift drops have been released,
impelled by prayer.
Being cleansed, the active drops have flowed at will into the ocean;
they have gone to the womb of Cosmic Order.
Come around us, seeking us, with all treasures by your might;
protect us with hero-guarded shelter.
The steed Etaśa, the bearer of the oblation, neighs as he yokes his station with the chanters,
when he is set upon the ocean.
When the swift one settles in the golden womb of the Eternal Order,
he leaves behind those who lack understanding.
The longing ones cry out to him; the wise desire him, while those lacking discernment sink away.
O Indu, flow most sweetly for Indra accompanied by the Maruts,
to sit upon the seat of the Rta.
The inspired poets, the wise ordainers who know the sacred word, prepare you;
the active ones cleanse you thoroughly.
O Sage, Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa drink your juice;
so do the Maruts of the purifying one.
O Soma, being purified, you send forth inspired speech,
O Indu, which brings a thousandfold reward.
O Soma, Indu, as you are being purified, bring us speech that brings a thousandfold bounty and is worthy of sacrifice.
O Indu, being purified, O thou invoked by many, enter the ocean as one beloved among these people.
With flashing luster and with swelling beauty,
the bright Soma juices, mixed with milk, flow forth.
Urged on by the impellers, the prize-winner has stepped forth toward the prize, like those sitting down as eager seekers.
O Soma, gathering together for our well-being, you, the seer from heaven,
flow forth uniquely so that we may behold you like the sun.
The radiant sisters, the kinswomen, longing for the great one, send forth the great Indu, their lord.
O Pavamāna, as a god from among the gods, with light after light,
enter into all treasures.
O Pavamāna, flow for us with fair praise, rain, and service for the gods;
flow for the sake of constant nourishment.
For you are a bull by your radiance; we, with pious thoughts, invoke you, O Pavamāna, the resplendent one.
Flow forth, O well-armed one, rejoicing, bestowing heroic strength; come hither, O Indu!
When you are sprinkled with waters and cleansed by the two hands,
you reach your dwelling place by means of the wooden vessel.
Sing forth for Soma Pavamāna as did Vyaśva—
for the great one who possesses a thousand eyes.
Whose honey-dropping, golden-colored juice they urge forth with the stones—
the drop for Indra to drink.
Of you, the prize-winning steed who has conquered all riches,
we choose the friendship.
Flow on as a bull with your stream, exhilarating for the Maruts,
bestowing all things by your might.
Thee, O Pavamāna, the sustainer of the two worlds, who beholdest the light of heaven— the vigorous one—
I urge forward in the contests for booty.
O golden-hued one, being perceived by this inspired song, flow with your stream;
urge on our ally in the contests for booty.
O Indu, flow for us as one visible to all, purifying great nourishment; O Soma, find the path for us.
The jars have resounded with the streams of Soma by its might; O Indu, enter the vessels for Indra’s drinking.
O you whose intoxicating, sharp juice they milk out with the stones— purify yourself as the slayer of the arrogant foe.
The King, Pavamāna, is impelled by prayers of wisdom over the mind,
in order to travel through the intermediate space.
O Indu, bring us a hundredfold increase of cattle, accompanied by noble horses;
bring us fortune for our aid.
O Soma, being pressed for the feast of the gods, bring us conquering power and swiftness, like a form for the sake of splendor.
Flow on, O Soma, most brilliant, roaring toward the wooden vats,
settling like a hawk upon its nest.
Winning the waters, Soma flows for Indra, for Vāyu, for Varuṇa, for the Maruts, and for Viṣṇu.
Bestowing nourishment upon our offspring and upon us from every side, O Soma, flow for us with thousandfold wealth.
Those Soma juices which have been pressed in the distance, those which have been pressed nearby, or those which are in Śaryaṇāvat—
Those who are among the Ārjīkas and the Kr̥tvas, those who are in the midst of dwellings,
or those who are among the five peoples— [to them may this Soma go].
May these pressed divine drops flow for us from heaven with rain, bringing great heroic strength.
The lovely, tawny one flows, being praised by Jamadagni,
as he is urged forth upon the hide of the cow.
The bright drops, hastening like steeds urged on,
have been mixed with milk and purified in the waters.
Thee, present at the pressings, they have urged forth for the service of the gods;
so flow thou with this luster.
Today we choose for you that skillful bearer who brings bliss,
the protector who is desired by many.
To the delightful one, to the excellent one, to the inspired singer, to the wise one; to the protector, to the one desired by many.
Bring us wealth and gracious wisdom, O you of noble power, into our bodies;
bring the drink that is desired by many.
Flow on, O you who belong to all people, toward all poetic insights, as a friend to be praised by your friends.
O Soma Pavamāna, you rule over the universe through those two abodes which stand facing one another.
O Soma, you encompass all your stations on every side;
O Sage, you are Pavamāna through the seasons.
Flow on, generating strengthening foods and all desirable things,
as a friend for the sake of his friends' aid.
Your bright rays, O Soma, spread across the back of heaven through your purifying powers and your abodes.
O Soma, these seven rivers flow according to your command;
for you the milch-cows run.
O Soma, flow forth in a stream, pressed for Indra as an intoxicant,
bestowing imperishable fame.
The seven sisters, impelling you with their prayers, have together caused you to sound forth— the inspired sage—
at the sacrifice of Vivasvat.
The active maidens cleanse you together upon the sheep’s wool, on the sounding surface,
when you, the singer, are anointed in the wood.
O Sage, O Steed, the streams of you, Pavamāna, have been released,
like coursers seeking renown.
They have been poured forth toward the honey-dripping vat upon the sheep’s wool;
the prayers have lowed aloud.
Toward the ocean, the drops have gone like milch-cows to their stalls; they have entered the womb of the Eternal Order (*ṛta*).
O Indu, flow forth for our great joy; the waters, the rivers, flow on when you clothe yourself in the milk of the cows.
In this friendship of yours, O Indu, we, desiring to sacrifice and protected by you, yearn for your companionship.
Flow on for the quest for cattle, O Soma, for the great one who beholds men;
enter into the belly of Indra.
Great art thou, O Soma, the eldest; O Indu, thou art the strongest of the mighty.
As a warrior, thou hast ever been victorious.
He who is more powerful than even the fierce, more heroic than even the brave, and more liberal than even those who give much.
O Soma, you are the impeller of the sun for the winning of offspring and for the sake of our own bodies; we choose you for friendship, we choose you for alliance.
O Agni, you purify our lives; pour forth upon us strength and nourishment. Drive far away all misfortune.
Agni is the seer, the purifying one, the domestic priest of the five peoples;
we implore him, the possessor of great wealth.
O Agni, you who are skillful in your work, purify yourself for us, bestowing splendor and heroic strength;
grant me wealth and nourishment.
Pavamāna flows across all obstacles toward our fair praise,
visible to all like the sun.
Being cleansed by the Āyus, provided with nourishment for the sake of enjoyment, Indu, the far-seeing steed, flows onward.
Pavamāna has generated the lofty Ṛta, the bright light;
he has struck down the black darknesses.
As Pavamāna strikes down [the obstacles], the golden-hued drops of the tawny one have been released— swift, with their rapid radiance.
Pavamāna, the best of charioteers, most brilliantly praised with his splendors,
is golden-hued and accompanied by the host of Maruts.
Pavamāna, the best winner of booty, has pervaded all things with his rays,
bestowing heroic strength upon the singer.
Being pressed, the Indu has flowed forth across the sheep’s-wool filter; being purified, the Indu goes toward Indra.
This Soma, pressed by the stones, sports upon the skin of the cows;
he loudly calls Indra for exhilaration.
O Pavamāna, with that radiant milk of yours which has been brought down from heaven, be gracious to us so that we may live.
O Soma, you are the sustainer, the delightful and most powerful one at the sacrifice;
flow on, bestowing abundant wealth.
Pressed for Indra, you are the exhilarating lord of men, flowing as the most intoxicating sage with your juice.
Pressed out by the stones, roaring aloud,
flow toward us with brilliant and most excellent strength.
The drop, being urged forward, flows through the sheep’s woolly fleece;
the tawny one has bellowed for the prize.
O Indu, you flow through the sheep’s wool, spreading forth renown, spreading forth prosperity,
and spreading forth, O Soma, spoils of war consisting of cattle.
O Indu, bring us wealth consisting of hundreds, cattle, and horses;
O Soma, bring it in thousands.
The purifying drops, the swift Indus, have passed through the filter and reached Indra on their courses.
The preeminent, Soma-like juice, the drop, ancient for Indra— life itself, it purifies itself for the living one.
The dawns urge on the hero, the purifying one who drips with sweetness;
they have sounded together with their song toward him.
May Pūṣan, whose horses are goats, be our protector on every journey;
may he grant us a share among the maidens.
This Soma flows like ghee and honey for the one with matted hair;
may he grant us a share among the maidens.
This [Soma] of yours, O glowing one, is pressed; it flows pure like clarified butter.
May he grant us a share among our maidens.
O Soma, as the progenitor of the speech of sages, flow clear with your stream;
you are the bestower of treasures among the gods.
The falcon rushes toward the jars; he plunges into his armor, crying out loudly toward the wooden vats.
O Soma, your pressed juice has been poured forth all around into the jar;
like a darting hawk, it flows onward.
Flow clear, O Soma, exhilarating for Indra, most rich in sweetness.
They have been let loose for the feast of the gods, like chariots seeking booty.
These pressed juices, most intoxicating and bright, have been released toward Vāyu.
Struck by the pressing-stone and extolled, O Soma, you go toward the filter,
bestowing heroic vigor upon the singer.
This one, pressed and highly praised, plunges through the filter,
the slayer of demons, into the woolly fleece.
Whatever fear, whether near or far away, finds me here— O Pavamāna, strike that down!
May that Pavamāna, the all-seeing one, purify us today with the filter—
may he who is the Purifier cleanse us.
O Agni, with that purifier of yours which is spread within your flame, purify our sacred prayer (brahman).
O Agni, with that purifying power of yours which shines with light, purify us;
purify us with the inspirations of sacred prayer (*brahmasava*).
O God Savitṛ, with both— by means of the filter and by means of your impulsion—
purify me on every side.
O divine Savitṛ, O Soma, with your three most excellent abodes,
O Agni, purify us with your skillful powers.
May the divine folk purify me; may the Vasus purify me with their wisdom. O All-Gods, purify me; O Jātavedas, purify me!
Swell forth, flow onward, O Soma, with all your stalks;
you are the supreme oblation for the gods.
We have come, bearing our homage, to the beloved youth who bestows rewards, who increases through oblations.
The axe of Alāyya has perished; O divine Soma, flow for him, even as for a mere mouse, O divine Soma.
He who studies the *pāvamānī* hymns— the essence gathered by the seers—
consumes everything purified and made savory by Mātariśvan.
Whoever studies the Pāvamānī hymns— the essence gathered by the seers—
for him Sarasvatī milks forth milk, clarified butter, honey, and water.
The honeyed drops have flowed forth toward the god, like milch-cows toward their calves.
Seated upon the sacrificial grass, eloquent with their udders, they have taken the flowing Soma as their robe, the ruddy milk as their garment.
Roaring loudly, he has bellowed toward the ancient [streams]; loosening the heights, the tawny one is sweetened.
Passing through the filter and traversing the wide expanse, the god deposits his own choice of arrows as he pleases.
The exhilaration that has measured out the two meeting sisters, who increase together, swells the inexhaustible waters with milk.
Having discerned the two great, boundless regions, he has assumed an imperishable luster as he moves across them.
Moving between his two parents and seeking strength, the wise one makes his station swell with his own inherent power.
The stalk is adorned with barley; when led by the men, he unites with his kinsmen and protects the head.

By means of skillful mind, the sage is born; he is the embryo of *ṛta*, deposited beyond the twins. Though they were young, they first brought forth him who was hidden in the secret place—the one who was not yet arisen.
The wise have discerned the form of the resonant one, when the falcon brought the plant from afar.
They purified him in the rivers—the well-increasing, longing stalk, the one who encompasses all, worthy of praise.
O Soma, the ten young women purify you, the pressed one, who have been prepared by the seers with prayers and meditations;
through the sheep’s wool filters and the invocations of the gods, directed by the men, you burst forth for the winning of booty.
The inspired hymns and songs of praise have celebrated Soma as he proceeds, the one worthy of fair laudation,
who— immortal and winner of wealth— sends forth his voice from heaven with a honeyed wave in a stream.
This Soma, being purified, sends forth everything from heaven; he settles in the jars throughout the entire mid-air.
Pressed by the stones, he is cleansed with water and milk; as Indu is purified, may he find dear and wide space.
Thus, O Soma, being poured out for us, flow on, bestowing most wondrous vitality.
We invoke the benevolent Heaven and Earth; O gods, grant us wealth with heroic sons.
Like an arrow set upon the bow, the prayer is aimed; like a calf let loose to the udder of its mother, it flows forth.
Like a wide-streaming cow, she yields her milk at the beginning of his approach; within his sacred ordinances, Soma is impelled.
The prayer is blended; the honey is poured; the sweet-voiced one is urged within the mouth.
Pavamāna, the continuous flow, like a honeyed drop of those who strike, flows through the filter.
Desiring a bride, he flows through the sheep’s wool upon the skin; Aditi’s daughter loosens her bonds for him who goes toward the *ṛta*.
The golden-hued, worshipful, well-restrained exhilaration has stepped forth; sharpening his manly powers, he shines like a buffalo.

The bull bellows; the milch-cows approach him; the goddesses go to the appointed place of the god. Soma has passed through the white sheep’s wool; he has clothed himself in it like a freshly washed garment.
With an unsoiled, radiant garment, the immortal tawny one has clothed himself in his bright mantle;
with power he has made the back of heaven his mantle, providing a cloud-like covering for the two cups.
Like the rays of the sun, the exhilarating drops, flowing swiftly, surge forth together from their sleep;
like swift streams following a stretched-out thread, no station flows pure except through Indra.
Like swift waters on a downward slope toward the sea, the exhilarating draughts shed by the bull have found their course.
May there be well-being for our two-footed and four-footed creatures in their dwellings; O Soma, may strength and prosperity abide with us and our people.
Flow for us with wealth, with gold, with horses, with cattle, with barley, and with great heroic power.
For you, O Soma, are my fathers; you are the heads of heaven, established as the makers of vitality.
These Soma drops, being purified, have sped forth toward Indra like chariots for the sake of booty;
pressed out, they pass through the sheep’s-wool filter, casting off their golden covering like dappled mares toward the rain.
O Indu, flow clear for the great Indra as one who is very gracious, blameless, and a destroyer of enemies.
Bring radiant treasures to the singer; O Heaven and Earth, together with the gods, protect us!
Three times seven milch-cows have milked for him the true *āśīr* in the ancient sky;
he has made four other beautiful worlds for his adornment when he grew strong through the cosmic laws (*ṛta*).
Seeking the lovely nectar of immortality, he has separated both heaven and earth through his poetic wisdom.
With majesty, he has clothed himself in the most brilliant waters when they, by the glory of the god, recognized his dwelling-place.
May those rays of his be immortal and invincible, following both races of beings—
those by which they purify both human and divine powers, and then they seized him, the King, with their thoughts.
Being cleansed by the ten skillful hands, he moves together with the middle mothers;
guarding the laws of the lovely nectar, he, the beholder of men, looks upon both races.
Being cleansed for the sake of Indra’s nourishment, he, established between both ends of heaven and earth, exults.
As a bull, with his vital strength, he drives away the malevolent ones, pointing out the spoils like an archer aiming at his targets.
Like a young bull beholding his two mothers, he goes bellowing like the roar of the Maruts;
knowing the primordial *ṛta*, the one of noble will chose the celestial light for the sake of praise.
The terrible bull bellows with great power, the far-sighted one sharpening his golden horns.
Soma settles into his well-fashioned seat; cowhide becomes his garment, and sheep’s wool his covering.
Pure, purifying his stainless body, the tawny one has flowed down upon the back of the sheep’s wool.
Pleasing to Mitra, Varuṇa, and Vāyu, the honeyed juice is prepared in three ways by the skillful workers.
Flow clear, O Soma, for the banquet of the gods; enter the heart of Indra, the reservoir of Soma.
Before distress can reach us, carry us across all misfortune; for as one who knows the land, he points out the directions to the one who asks.
Like a well-harnessed steed toward the prize, flow on; O Indu, purify yourself into the belly of Indra.
Like one skilled in crossing a river by boat, carry us across; like a hero fighting in battle, protect us from reproach.
The sacrificial fee is bestowed; the vigorous one seeks his seat. Watchful, he guards against the malicious demon.
The tawny one makes the head-band of mist for his milk; he spreads the prayer as a carpet within the two bowls for his adornment.
Like a ploughman [toward his field], he goes forth roaring with strength; he sheds this asuric color of his.
He leaves behind his covering, goes to his father’s appointed place, and continually makes for himself a flowing robe as a garment.
Pressed by the stones, he flows from the two hands; he acts like a bull with the cloud and trembles at the hymn.
He rejoices, he approaches, he accomplishes his task through song; he cleanses himself in the waters and is worshipped in the full measure.
They pour out the celestial, mountain-increasing, exhilarating draught of honey from the dwelling, which belongs to the one who overcomes;
in whose udder the cows, eaters of the well-offered oblation, mix the foremost [milk] at the head with their wide expanses.
The ten sisters have impelled him together into the lap of Aditi, as if a chariot from the two poles;
he has gone forth and hastens toward the secret place of the cow, which his inspired thoughts have brought to birth.

Like a hawk to its nest, the god hastens to sit upon the golden seat prepared by prayer; they lead him, beloved, with song onto the sacrificial grass; like a horse, he, worthy of sacrifice, approaches the gods.
The bright, ruddy seer of heaven, the bull with three backs, has lowed toward the cows. With a thousandfold guidance, the wanderer who goes forth and returns shines over many dawns like a singer.
He assumes a brilliant form; his color is such that wherever he rests, he drives away the adversaries.
Winning the waters, he goes by his own power to the divine folk; he unites with our fair praise, which is led by cows.
Like a bull bellowing as he moves around the herds, he has clothed himself in the splendors of the sun.
The divine eagle has looked down upon the earth; Soma beholds all creatures with his wisdom.
They cleanse the tawny one; he is yoked like a ruddy steed; Soma is mingled with milk-cows in the jar.
He sends forth his voice; they urge him on with hymns—he who is beloved by many. How many indeed are those who encompass him?
Many wise ones speak together when they have poured the Soma into the belly of Indra;
when the men with skillful hands cleanse the desirable honey with the ten sisters who share a common nest.
Not resting, he passes beyond the cows, across the roar of Sūrya’s dear daughter. To him Vinangṛsa brought what was pleasing; he dwells together with his twin sisters, his female kin.
Shaken by men, pressed by stones upon the sacred grass, the beloved lord of cattle from of old, the seasonal drop— endowed with wisdom,
the accomplisher of man’s sacrifice, pure through prayer— O Indra, the Soma flows for you.

Urged by the arms of men, pressed out in a stream, O Indra, the Soma flows for you according to its nature. It has fulfilled our intentions; it has gathered our thoughts at the sacrifice. Like a bird alighting on a tree, the tawny one has settled within the two bowls.
The skillful, wise sages milk the thundering, inexhaustible stalk;
the cows and the hymns come together in unison at the seat of the womb of Eternal Order, being born again.
At the navel of the earth, the supporter of the great heaven, bedewed within the waves of the waters and the rivers—
Indra’s thunderbolt, the bull, the possessor of abundant wealth, Soma flows for the heart, the lovely, intoxicating one.
So flow thou pure around the earthly region, O wise one, bestowing gifts upon the singer and the one who shakes the ladle.
Do not exclude us from wealth that reaches our dwelling; may we clothe ourselves in abundant, golden-hued riches.
O Indu, bring to us a hundredfold gift of horses, a thousandfold gift of cattle and gold!
Bestow upon us great and wealthy nourishments; O Pavamāna, come to our hymn of praise.
At the snout of the blowing drop, they have sounded together; in the womb of *ṛta*, the navels have come together.
That Asura has made three heads for himself to grasp; the ships of truth have carried the doer of good deeds across.
Moving perfectly together, the mighty bulls have rushed forth; upon the wave of the river, the longing ones have stirred themselves.
Generating the hymn with streams of sweetness, they have increased the dear body of Indra.
Wielding the purifiers, they sit around the sacred word; their ancient father protects their vow.
Varuṇa has encompassed the great ocean; the wise have found a hold upon its foundations.
In the thousand-streamed [soma], they have resounded together like [the waters] in the vault of heaven, honey-tongued and unfailing.
His watchful spies do not close their eyes; at every step there are bridgers who bear nooses.
They who have resounded together from their father and mother, glowing with the *ṛc* and burning away the lawless ones—
by their power, they blow away from the earth and from heaven the black skin hated by Indra.
Those who have sounded forth from the ancient dwelling-place, the guides of the hymn and the counsellors of the impetuous one—
while the blind and the deaf have perished, the evildoers do not cross the path of Ṛta.
Upon the outspread filter with its thousand streams, the wise seers purify their speech.
Of these, the Rudras are vigorous and free from guile; they are swift-moving spies, fair to behold, and lookers upon men.
Guardian of the *ṛta*, he of noble wisdom cannot be deceived; he has placed three purifiers within his heart.
Knowing all, he beholds all beings; he pierces those who are unrighteous and devoid of vows into the pit.
The thread of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*) is stretched out across the filter by the power of Varuṇa’s magic at the tip of his tongue.
Even the wise reach for it and attain it; therein the powerless man falls into the pit.
Like a newborn infant, he has cried out in the wood when the ruddy prize-winning steed seeks to win the light of heaven.
He accompanies the seed of heaven, which increases with milk; we implore him for his favor and for wide-reaching protection.
The pillar of heaven, its support, stretched out by itself—the full stalk moves all around.
May this sage, through his ritual turnings, worship these two great worlds; he has held them together as they meet, and he holds together all nourishments.
Great is the refreshing draught, well-prepared and sweet as Soma; vast is the pasture for him who follows the *ṛta* of Aditi.
He who rules over the rain from here, the ruddy bull, the leader of the waters, he who goes forth from here, worthy of praise.
The vitalized cloud is milked for ghee and milk; the navel of Cosmic Order produces the immortal.
The well-disposed, bounteous men, acting in concert, delight in him; the overflowing ones pour down what is beneficial.
The stalk has roared, accompanied by its wave; it swells the skin that is dear to the gods for the sake of man.
It places the germ within the lap of Aditi, by which we may obtain both offspring and progeny.
Like those that flow in a thousand streams, may these unceasing ones, rich in progeny, abide in the third realm.
Four navels are established from beneath the sky; dripping with clarified butter, they bring the immortal oblation.

When he desires to win, Soma assumes a white form; the bountiful Asura knows the full extent of the world. Through prayer and ritual labor he accompanies [the sacrifice]; may he burst open the water-holding cask from heaven.
Then the prize-winning steed, having won, has stepped upon the white vessel anointed with milk at the place of the goal;
the god-seeking ones have sent forth with their minds a gift of cows for Kakṣīvat, who has lived a hundred winters.
O Soma, as your juice mingles with the waters, it flows through the sheep’s woolly filter, O Pavamāna.
Being cleansed by the seers, O most exhilarating one, be sweet for Indra to drink, O Pavamāna.
Willingly inclined, he flows toward his dear names, upon which the mighty one grows strong;
great and far-seeing, he has mounted the wide-reaching chariot of the lofty Sun.

The tongue of Truth flows forth as the beloved honey; the speaker, the unassailable lord of this prayer, establishes a secret third name for his parents in the luminous realm of heaven, even as a son [establishes his own name].

Shining forth, he has bellowed toward the jars; guided by men, he is in the golden vessel. The milch-cows of the Eternal Order have lowed toward him; the three-backed one shines resplendent over the dawns.
Pressed by the stones and made pleasing by the hymns, the pure one, illuminating the two parents, Heaven and Earth, flows through the sheep’s woolly fleece; a stream of honey, swelling day by day.
O Soma, flow forth for our well-being; being purified by the men, clothe yourself in the milk-mixture.
With those exhilarating draughts of yours that are impetuous and far-reaching, incite Indra to bestow wealth upon us.

The sustainer of heaven, the effective essence, the skillful power of the gods, he flows clear, to be celebrated by men. Released like a tawny steed by its warriors, he spreads his splendors at will across the rivers.
Like a hero, he takes up weapons in his hands, desiring to win the light of heaven as a charioteer in the quest for cattle.
Stirring up the vigor of Indra with his active works, the drop, being urged forward, is anointed by the wise.

O Soma Pavamāna, entering with your wave into the bellies of Indra while displaying your power, swell us like lightning filling the two worlds from the cloud; through our prayer, mete out to us eternal strengths.
The King of all, who beholds the light of heaven, flows clear; he has caused the seer to proclaim the thought of Eternal Order.
He who is cleansed by the ray of the sun, the father of hymns, whose wisdom is unsurpassed.
Like a bull toward the herds, you flow around the vat, a bellowing bull in the lap of the waters.
As the most intoxicating one, you purify yourself for Indra, so that we may conquer in battle through your aid.
This honeyed one has bellowed forth into the vat, Indra’s thunderbolt, more wondrous than the wondrous;
toward him flow the well-milking, ghee-dropping streams of Truth, like lowing cows with their milk.
That ancient one flows on, whom the hawk, sent forth from heaven, churned out across the mid-air;
trembling, he gathers the honey, fearing in his mind the archer Kr̥śānu.
May those former and later drops flow for us toward great wealth consisting of cattle— those lovely ones,
like serpents, worthy of being beheld, who have delighted in every prayer and every oblation.
May this Indu, the wise one praised by many with a focused mind, conquer those who attack us;
he who, at the seat of the Lord, has taken his place as the embryo, now flows toward the wide-open stall of the cows.
The active, effective juice, the maker of heaven, flows clear—the great, undeceived Varuṇa for the one who goes astray.
Mitra has been pressed out, worthy of sacrifice in the assemblies, bellowing like a stallion seeking the herd among the herds.
The King, generating speech, has flowed forth; clothing himself in the waters, he seeks the cows.
The fleece of the sheep retains his impurity; purified, he goes to the appointed place of the gods.
O Soma, you are poured out for Indra by the men; you, the wave, the seer who beholds men, are anointed in the wood.
For many are your paths for traveling, and a thousand are your bay horses that sit within the vessels.
The celestial nymphs of the ocean, seated within, have flowed toward the wise Soma;
they urge him on, the conqueror of the stronghold, and they beg the purifying one for imperishable bliss.
Soma flows for us, winning cattle, winning chariots, winning gold, winning light, winning waters, and winning thousands—
he whom the gods have made into a draught for drinking, the sweetest drop, ruddy, and the source of bliss.
O Soma Pavamāna, seeking us, making these true riches manifest, you flow onward.
Strike down the enemy both near and far; grant us wide pastures and security.
May our unurged drops flow forth—the golden Soma juices pressed for those of lofty heaven.
May the hostilities of the enemy depart from us; may they perish, and may our prayers win the prize.
May the drops, distilling exhilaration, flow forth for us like riches, by which we may urge on our steeds;
beyond the encompassing guile of any mortal man, may we always carry away spoils of wealth.

Whether it be from one's own hostility—for he is indeed an enemy—or from the hostility of another—for he is indeed a wolf—let not thirst overcome him as in the desert; O Soma Pavamāna, strike down those of evil intent.
In heaven, at your highest navel, he who took you up; upon the ridge of the earth, your swift fingers have grown.
The pressing-stones chew you upon the cow’s hide; the wise ones have milked you with their hands from the waters.
Thus, O Indu, the first adornments press out your essence, which is well-formed and beautiful.
O Pavamāna, drive away every reproach; let your vigor be manifest, your exhilarating joy that is dear to us.
The stream of Soma, who beholds men, flows clear; by the Eternal Law, he calls the gods from heaven. With the roar of Bṛhaspati, he flashes forth; like oceans, they have encompassed the libations.
O vigorous one, you whom the cows have lowed toward as you ascend to your iron-fashioned womb,
