radiant— prolonging the life and great glory of the patrons— you flow, O Soma, as a bull and a rapturous intoxicant for Indra.
The most intoxicating one flows into the belly of Indra, clothing himself in strength for the sake of glory, most auspicious.
Facing all beings, he has spread himself abroad; sporting, the tawny steed, the bull, rushes forward.
The men, the ten fingers, milk you out for the gods—you, the most honey-sweet, with a thousand streams.
O Soma, set in motion by the men and pressed by the stones, flow for all the gods, O winner of thousands!
The ten fingers milk you with stones—the honeyed bull in the waters.
O Soma, exhilarating Indra and the divine host, you flow as Pavamāna like a wave from the river.
The well-adorned waves of the purifying Soma go forth into the belly of Indra.
When the pressed juices, mixed with the glorious curd of cows, have been drawn up, they have exhilarated the Hero for the giving of gifts.
For Soma has flowed toward the jars like a stallion, a bull with swift-moving tracks;
thus, knowing both lineages of the gods, he attains that which is from yonder and from here.
O Soma Pavamāna, scatter wealth upon us; O Indu, be a liberal giver of great bounty. Bestow strength upon the wealthy with your gracious wisdom; do not pour away our household from us to a distance.
May Pūṣan, Pavamāna, and the bounteous Mitra come to us, as well as Varuṇa with like-minded companions;
may Bṛhaspati, the Maruts, Vāyu, the Aśvins, Tvaṣṭṛ, Savitṛ, and the well-guided Sarasvatī come to us.
Both Heaven and Earth, the all-pervading, the god Aryaman,
Aditi, the Ordainer, Bhaga, the protector of men, the wide mid-air, and all the gods— may they take pleasure in Pavamāna.
The ruddy, tawny bull Soma has been pressed; like a wondrous king, he has bellowed toward the cows.
Purifying himself, he passes through the sheep’s wool filter to sit, like a hawk, upon his ghee-filled seat.
As a sage, you move around the great vessel with wisdom; like a groomed steed, you rush toward the prize.
Warding off misfortunes, O Soma, be gracious; clothed in clarity, you go forth to your radiant garment.
Parjanya is the father of the great-winged bird; he has established his dwelling on the mountains at the navel of the earth.
The waters, his sisters, have flowed toward the cows, and he meets with the pressing-stones when the sacrifice is prepared.
Like a wife to her husband, you bestow your favor; O child of Pajrā, hear me, for I speak to you.
Enter among the songs so that we may live well; blameless, O Soma, keep watch within the community.
As for those of old, O Indu, you have brought forth booty by the hundreds, unceasingly, and by the thousands;
even so, flow on for new prosperity, for the waters follow your law.
O Brahmaṇaspati, your filter is stretched out; as its master, you move around its limbs on every side.
One whose body has not been heated by penance, being raw, does not partake of that [soma]; only those who have been cooked [by fire] and carry it attain it.
The filter of the heating [Soma] is stretched out at the station of heaven; its glowing threads have spread abroad.
His swift [drops], protecting the purifier, stand upon the back of heaven with their mind.
The foremost dappled bull has caused the dawns to shine; seeking strength, he sustains all beings.
By his creative power, the masters of illusion have measured it out; the fathers, who behold men, have deposited the germ.
The Gandharva thus guards his station; wonderful, he protects the generations of the gods.
As lord of the treasure, he seizes the enemy with his snare; those who have performed the best deeds have partaken of the draught of honey.
O possessor of oblations, clothed in the celestial mist, you go around the sacrifice with the oblation to the great seat of the gods.
King whose chariot is the filter, you have mounted for booty; with a thousand points, you win lofty fame.
Flow on as the exhilarating drink, O most active one, winning the waters for Indra, Varuṇa, and Vāyu. Grant us prosperity today with well-being; in the wide dwelling, celebrate the divine host.
The immortal Soma who has taken his stand over all the worlds flows around them;
effecting both gathering and dispersal for our aid, Indu follows after the Dawn as the Sun does.
He who is released with the rays of light among the plants, seeking the favor of the gods and bringing wealth;
pressed with the lightning-flash in a steady stream, Soma flows for Indra, exhilarating the divine host.
This very Soma flows clear, the winner of thousands, strengthening the vigorous voice that awakens at dawn.
The drop, by means of the winds, raises itself up to the ocean; it settles within the jars in the heart of Indra.

The cows mix that Soma with milk—him who increases the milk, who finds the light—with their prayers. The winner of wealth, the effective juice, flows clear; he is the inspired sage, the seer through his poetic insight, worthy of the light.
Flow forth, O Soma, well-pressed for Indra; let disease vanish along with the demons.
Let not the double-dealing ones revel in your juice; here let the drops be full of wealth.

O Pavamāna, urge us forward in the battle; for you are the skillful, beloved exhilaration of the gods. Slay the enemies who raise their shouts against us; drink the *soma*, O Indra, and strike down those who seek to harm us.
O Indu, you flow unimpaired, most intoxicating; you become the supreme nourishment for Indra’s self.
Many wise ones sing toward you; they honor the king of this world.
With a thousand songs and a hundred streams, the wondrous Indu flows as desirable honey for Indra.
Winning the field, flow hither; winning the waters, O bounteous Soma, make wide for us a path to go.
Roaring, you are anointed with milk in the jar; you flow through the sheep’s woolen filter. Being cleansed like a prize-winning steed, O Soma, you have flowed into the belly of Indra.
Flow sweet for the celestial race; flow sweet for Indra, whose name is easily invoked;
flow sweet for Mitra, Varuṇa, and Vāyu; flow as honey-sweet and invincible for Bṛhaspati.
The ten fingers cleanse the steed in the jar; the inspired thoughts and voices of the sages surge forth.
The purifying drops flow toward the hymn of praise; the intoxicating Soma-drops enter into Indra.
Flowing clear, bestow upon us heroic strength, a wide pasture, and great, far-reaching protection.
Let no one have power over our portion of this; O Indu, may we conquer wealth after wealth through you.
The far-seeing bull has ascended to heaven; the sage has illuminated the luminous realms of the sky.
The king, bellowing, passes through the filter; those who watch over men milk the nectar of heaven.
In the vault of heaven, the honey-tongued, tireless seers milk the mountain-dwelling bull;
they milk the drop that has grown great in the waters, the honey-sweet one in the ocean, in the wave of the river, within the filter.
Many songs of the longing ones have yearned for the fair-winged bird who has flown up to the firmament.
The prayers lick the infant, the one who is praised, the golden bird standing upon the earth.
The Gandharva has stood erect upon the vault of heaven, beholding all the forms of this [world].
His radiance has shone forth with bright luster; pure, he has illuminated both worlds, his parents.
O Pavamāna, your swift, exhilarating drops, impelled by prayer, flow forth of their own accord like the offspring of the fleet-footed.
Like divine, well-winged birds, the honey-sweet, most intoxicating drops settle within the vessel.
Your exhilarating, intoxicating, and swift draughts have been poured forth like chariot-horses racing apart.
Like a cow with her milk for her calf, the honeyed waves of soma-drops flow toward Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt.
Like a steed urged forward toward the prize, flow toward the sun-finding vat, whose mother is the mountain of heaven.
As a bull upon the sheep’s-wool filter, O Soma, being purified on its height, flow for the maintenance of Indra’s power.
O Pavamāna, your steeds that belong to the Aśvins, urged by prayer, have been released with their milk toward the support of heaven.
The ancient seers have poured forth the inner waters, those wise ones who, O you who are the strength of the seers, cleanse you.
O all-seeing and skillful one, your rays go forth encompassing all domains as you exist as the Lord.
Pervading with your laws, O Soma, you purify yourself; as the master of the entire world, you reign.
On both sides, the rays of the purifying one—his banners—move around him as he remains steadfast;
when the tawny one is cleansed upon the filter, he sits down in his place within the jars.
The banner of the sacrifice, the one who makes the rite successful, Soma flows; he goes to the appointed place of the gods.
With a thousand streams he rushes around the vessel; as a bull, bellowing loudly, he passes through the filter.
The King plunges into the ocean; the rivers attend upon his wave as he rests within the streams.
Purifying himself, he has mounted the woolly back of the sheep, the navel of the earth and the sustainer of the great heaven.
Like the ridge of heaven, he has thundered and roared—he by whose laws both heaven and earth abide.
Discerning the friendship of Indra, Soma flows clear; being purified, he settles within the jars.
The light of the sacrifice, the beloved honey, flows clear; the father of the gods, their progenitor, the possessor of abundant wealth.
He bestows the secret treasure of the two self-sustaining powers—the most exhilarating, intoxicating, and Indra-like juice.
Roaring toward the jar, the prize-winning steed flows on; the far-seeing Lord of Heaven with a hundred streams.
The tawny bull, being cleansed by the sheep's wool and the rivers, settles in the dwelling places of Mitra.

Pavamāna flows at the head of the rivers; as the foremost one, he goes at the head of speech toward the cows. He shares in the great prize of booty at the head; well-armed, the bull is purified by the pressers.
This Pavamāna, like a bird that has alighted, has flowed with his wave into the sheep’s wool, full of thought.
O Sage, by your wisdom, the pure Soma flows between the two worlds, O Indra, through your inspired prayer.

Clothed in his mantle that touches the heavens, the worshipful one, filling the mid-air, is established among the worlds. Born from the light, he has stepped forth with the mist; he seeks to win over his ancient father.
He bestows great protection upon his people, he who has pervaded his first abode;
from that station of his which is in the highest heaven, he comes together with all the gathered powers.

The drop has gone forth to the appointed place of Indra; as a friend, he does not violate the agreement with his friend. Like a youth with young women, Soma flows together into the jar by a path of a hundred courses.
Your exhilarating, praising, and glorious hymns have gone forth to the gathering places;
with inspired thought, the chants have celebrated Soma, and the milch-cows have yielded their milk for him.
O Soma, Indu, as you flow clear, pour out for us a continuous, swelling, and unfailing nourishment—
nourishment that yields for us thrice a day, inexhaustible, rich in food, full of strength, sweet, and accompanied by heroic might.
The bull of hymns, the far-seeing Soma, flows on, the furtherer of the day, the dawn, and the sky.
By his action, he has caused the rivers to roar toward the jars; entering the heart of Indra through the wise, he flows.
The ancient sage is purified by the wise; guided by men, he has roared around the vessels.
Producing the name of Trita, he flows with honey to perform friendship for Indra and Vāyu.
Being purified, he has caused the dawns to shine; he has become the maker of space for the rivers. This Soma, milking the thrice-sevenfold mixture, flows as a delightful exhilarant for the heart.

Flow on, O Soma, into the celestial abodes; being released, O Indu, flow into the jar and the filter. Seating yourself within the belly of Indra while bellowing, guided by the men, you caused the sun to ascend to heaven.
Pressed by the stones, you flow through the filter, O Indu, entering the bellies of Indra.
You became the one who beholds men, O far-seeing Soma; you opened the cow-pen for the Aṅgirases.
O Soma, while you were being purified, the sages, seeking aid and devoted to sacred study, rejoiced after you;
you, O Indu, adorned with all hymns of praise, the fair-winged bird brought down from heaven.
As he purifies himself with his wave in the sheep’s wool filter, the seven milch-cows low toward the golden-hued one.
In the lap of the waters, above the womb of *ṛta*, the active bulls have impelled the Seer.
Being purified, the drop plunges past all adversaries, making all paths easy for the sacrificer;
making the cows his garment, the lovely sage flows like a playful steed through the filter.
The inexhaustible, hundred-streamed, glorious waters cry out toward the golden one like those seeking water;
the swift fingers cleanse him who is enveloped in milk, upon the third ridge in the luminous realm of heaven.
These creatures of yours are born from the divine seed; you rule over the entire world.
And all this, O Pavamāna, is under your control; O Indu, you are the first establisher of the sacred abodes.
You are the ocean, O Sage, the knower of all; yours are these five directions within your cosmic order.
You have extended beyond both heaven and earth; yours, O Pavamāna, are the lights, including the sun.
O Soma Pavamāna, you are purified in the filter for the gods within the expanse of the mid-world;
the *uśij* first grasped you, and all these worlds have submitted themselves to you.
The singer goes forth across the sheep's wool filter; the tawny bull, the golden-hued one, has bellowed down into the wooden vats.
The prayers have lowed together in longing; the hymns lick the infant who is worthy of praise.
He has clothed himself in the rays of the sun, weaving the threefold thread as he knows how;
leading the most recent instructions of the *ṛta*, the husband of women goes to the appointed place.
The king of rivers flows on, the lord of heaven; he goes along the paths of *ṛta* with a loud roar.
The golden-hued one is poured out in a thousand streams; being purified, generating speech, he comes down rich in wealth.

O Pavamāna, you flow forth like a great flood, brilliant as the sun, through the sheep’s wool with your filter. Purified by the hands of men and pressed by the stones, you hasten toward great, prize-winning booty.
O Pavamāna, you flow toward nourishment and vigor; like a hawk among trees, you settle in the jars.
For Indra, you are pressed as a gladdening, intoxicating draught—the most excellent pillar of heaven, far-seeing.
The seven sisters, the mothers, [attend] the newborn infant, the noble and wise one;
they attend Soma, the divine Gandharva of the waters, who beholds men, so that he may reign over the entire world.
As Lord, you traverse these worlds, O Indu, yoking your bay, well-winged mares.
May they pour forth for you honeyed ghee and milk; O Soma, may the people abide under your law.
O Soma, you are the beholder of men on every side; O Pavamāna, O Bull, you flow through these [worlds].
As such, purify yourself for us, bringing wealth and gold; may we be among the living beings so that we may live.
Flow on, winner of cattle, winner of wealth, winner of gold, O Indu, bestower of seed, established among all beings.
You, O Soma, are the possessor of noble heroes and the knower of all; therefore the sages sit near you with their songs.
The wave of honey has established its desire; clothed in the waters, the buffalo plunges in.
The King, whose chariot is the filter, has mounted for booty; with a thousand points, he wins great renown.
He, the life of all, raises up on every day all auspicious, well-nourished, and offspring-bearing blessings.
O Indu, once drunk, do thou entreat Indra for us—brahman-power accompanied by progeny and wealth abounding in horses.
At the beginning of days, the golden-hued, desirable exhilarating juice is made conscious by the wise one through the days;
driving the two peoples apart, he moves between them—the human and the divine praise—while the upholder sustains all.
They anoint him, they anoint him apart, they anoint him together; they lick his creative power, they anoint him with honey.
As he flies at the swelling of the river, those who purify with gold seize the bull, the sacrificial victim, among these waters.
Sing forth to the wise Pavamāna; like a great stream, the Soma-juice flows.
Like a serpent gliding over its slough, the tawny bull has flowed on, sporting like a steed.
The leader, the king, the protector of waters, grows mighty; the measurer of days, established among the worlds.
Tawny, dripping with clarity, beautiful to behold, a surging sea whose chariot is light, he flows as the one who dwells in wealth.
The supporting pillar, the exhilarating juice of heaven, has been released; it flows around the threefold worlds.
The inspired hymns lick the stalk that brings wonder, when those who sing the *ṛc* have approached its radiant covering with their song.
Your streams, like those of a ram, pass through the fine woolly filter; as you are purified, your rushing currents flow together.
O Indu, when you are mixed with milk in the two bowls, being pressed, O Soma, you settle within the jars.
Flow on, O Soma, winner of wisdom, worthy of our hymns; run through the sheep’s wool filter, pouring out your beloved sweetness.
Strike down all the Rākṣasas and the devouring demons, O Indu! May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
Run forward and settle within the vessel; being purified by the men, flow toward the prize.
Cleansing you like a spirited horse, they lead you with reins toward the sacred grass.
Well-armed, the divine Indu flows clear, the slayer of the ill-spoken, guarding the community;
he is the father of the gods, their progenitor, most skillful, the pillar of heaven and the support of the earth.
The seer, the inspired singer, the leader of the people, the skillful and wise Uśanas by his poetic insight—
he indeed discovered that which was deposited as the secret, hidden name of these cows.
This honeyed Soma of yours, O Indra, a bull for the bull, has flowed through the filter;
winning thousands, winning hundreds, a bountiful giver, the prize-winner has taken his place upon the sacrificial grass forevermore.

These Soma drops have been released through the filters—seeking fame like horses eager for battle—to win thousands of cattle, great strength, and immortal glory. They flow as they are purified, like steeds rushing toward the prize.
For he, invoked by many, being purified, has indeed flowed around all the nourishments of the people.
Now, O you who are borne by the falcon, bring us refreshments; bestowing wealth, flow toward the prize of victory.
This Soma, being pressed, has run through the filter like a released steed;
sharpening his horns like a wild bull, he rushes toward the cows like a hero seeking cattle.
This one has come forth from within the highest mountain; being somewhere, she has found the cows in the wide space.
Like lightning from heaven thundering with clouds, O Indra, this stream of Soma flows clear for you.
And indeed, O Soma, being purified, you go around the heap of cattle on the same chariot with Indra;
O giver of life, bestowing many great refreshments, O possessor of power, grant us those boons which are praised by us.
This Soma, O Indra, is pressed for you; for you it flows clear; drink of this!
For you indeed have you made, for you have you chosen, the drop, the Soma, for the fitting exhilaration.
Like a chariot that wins much, he has been harnessed; the great one [has been yoked] for the winning of many riches.
Then all the human generations have raised their voices toward him, as they strive for the light in the forest of trees.

Like Vāyu with his team of horses, you whose path is swift; like the Nāsatyas at our invocation, you are the most beneficent; possessing all boons, like Draviṇodas in person, and like Pūṣan, you are the impeller of our thoughts, O Soma.
Like Indra, you who have performed great deeds, you are the slayer of Vṛtras and the breaker of forts, O Soma;
for like the steed of Pedu, you are the slayer of those called "serpents," O Soma, and the destroyer of every Dasyu.
Like Agni when released into the forest, he effortlessly displays his splendors within the rivers;
like a warrior facing a great foe, Soma Pavamāna sends forth his wave with a mighty roar.
These Soma juices have flowed through the sheep’s woolly filters like celestial water-jars raining from the clouds;
like rivers flowing downward to the sea, the pressed drops have been poured into the jars at will.
Flow onward, powerful as the host of Maruts, like the divine folk who are beyond reproach;
be swift with your favor toward us like waters, possessing a thousandfold power, like a sacrifice that conquers in battle.
Truly, thy laws are those of King Varuṇa; O Soma, thy domain is vast and deep.
Thou art pure, like the beloved Mitra; thou art to be honored like Aryaman, O Soma.
Like rain from heaven, this Soma, the purifying bearer, has flowed along his paths;
with a thousand streams, he has settled within us, in the lap of his mother and in the wooden vessel.
The King of rivers has clothed himself in his garment; he has mounted the straightest ship of *Ṛta*.
The drop has grown in the waters, urged by the falcon; the father milks it, he milks the offspring of the father.
They approach the lion, the tireless one, the tawny and ruddy lord of this heaven, who drinks of the honeyed draught.
The hero, foremost in battles, seeks the cattle; the bull protects them all around with his eye.
They yoke to the chariot the formidable, tireless horse with honeyed back, wide-wheeled and lofty;
the sisters, his kinswomen, cleanse him, and those of common origin strengthen the vigorous steed.
Four milch-cows yielding ghee attend him; seated together within the same support, they flow toward him while being purified with homage; these many ones encompass him from every side.
The support of heaven and the foundation of earth, all the settlements are in his hand.
May there be for you a fountain for the singer, O Lord of the teams; may the stalk of honey flow clear for Indra’s power.
Winning the windless [strength], flow for Indra toward the feast of the gods, O Soma, as the slayer of Vṛtra.
Be able to grant us great and most radiant wealth; may we be masters of heroic power.
Urged forward, the progenitor of the two worlds has sped forth like a chariot seeking booty;
going toward Indra, sharpening his weapons, he holds all treasures in his hands.
The voices of praise have cried out toward the three-backed bull, the bestower of vital strength;
clothing himself in the woods like Varuṇa among the rivers, the bestower of jewels distributes desirable treasures.
O you who lead a host of heroes, possessing all manly vigor, victorious and powerful, flow on as a winner of riches;
armed with sharp weapons and a swift bow, unconquered in battles, overcoming enemies in the fray.
Providing wide pastures and creating safety, flow toward the two united worlds of wisdom;
desiring to win the waters, the dawns, the sun, and the cattle, roar forth and gather for us great spoils of victory.
O Soma, exhilarate Varuṇa; exhilarate Mitra; O Indu, Pavamāna, exhilarate Indra and Viṣṇu.
Exhilarate the host of Maruts; exhilarate the gods; O Indu, exhilarate the great Indra for his intoxication.

Thus, like a king endowed with wisdom, flow on, striking down all misfortunes with your impetuous force; O Indu, bestow vital strength upon our well-spoken hymn. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
The eloquent one has been let loose like a chariot-horse in a race; the first inventor, the wise one, has been impelled by prayer.
The ten sisters drive the bearer upon the sheep’s back toward his seats.
Pressed by the *kavyas* among the divine folk and by the descendants of Nahuṣa, Indu flows forth for the enjoyment of the people—
he who, though immortal, is cleansed by mortal men with sheep’s wool, with milk, and with waters.
The bull, roaring loudly for the bull, this Pavamāna stalk sends forth the bright milk of the cow;
the thousandfold singer, knowing the words, the sun-like one, passes through the fine strainer by stainless paths.
Break down even the firm dwellings of the Rākṣasas; O Indu, as you are being purified, spread out the spoils of war.
With your swift weapon, strike down from above those who approach them from near or far.
As in the past, O possessor of all boons, prepare the forward paths for this new hymn;
may we, O doer of much, O provider of much food, overcome those great enemies who are difficult for the attacker to withstand.

Thus purifying yourself, grant us waters, light, and cattle, as well as abundant offspring and descendants; O Soma, bestow upon us health, wide fields, and many lights, so that we may long behold the sun.
Being pressed, the golden stalk has been released into the filter like a chariot urged on for the sake of gain;
being purified, it has attained Indra’s fame and has gratified the gods with offerings.
The seer, beholding men, has flowed toward the filter, assuming his name in his own womb;
settling in the vessels like a Hotṛ-priest in his seat, the seven inspired Ṛṣis have approached him.
The wise Soma, the knower of the way, belonging to all the gods, goes forth constantly as he is being purified.
He becomes the one who delights in all poetic inspirations; the sage exerts himself among the five peoples.
O Soma Pavamāna, all these gods—the thirty-three—are in your secret place;
by their own powers, the ten mighty rivers cleanse you upon the sheep’s back.
Let that indeed be the truth of Pavamāna, wherein all the poets assemble together;
for he made light for the day and created a world, and he protected Manu while making the Dasyu his adversary.

Like a Hotṛ priest going around the sacrificial enclosures rich in cattle, like a truthful king proceeding to assemblies, Soma, being purified, has gone to the jars, settling there like a wild buffalo in the forests.
The ten sisters, the flowing prayers of the sage, have cleansed him together as he is sprinkled;
the tawny one has run forth, the offspring of Sūrya, and has reached the vat like a prize-winning steed.
Like a lowing infant with its mothers, the bull, much-desired, has flowed forth with the waters; like a youth going to a tryst with a maiden, he unites in the jar with the milk-cows.
And the udder of the cow has swelled; the wise Indu accompanies her with his streams. The cows mix the head [of the Soma] with milk in the vessels, as if with freshly washed riches.
O Indu, being purified by the gods and lowing for us, bestow upon us wealth consisting of horses;
may Purandhi, the charioteer, come toward us with desire, so that she may grant us riches.
Now, O Purifying One, bestow upon us wealth accompanied by heroes, all-glittering and worthy of being protected by the wind;
O Indu, prolong the life of the singer. May he who is enriched by prayer come quickly in the morning.
When the prayers vie for him as beauties do for a prize-winning steed, like subjects for the sun;
choosing the waters, he flows as a seer, like a pen for the increase of cattle—this is my thought.
Twofold unfolding the abode of immortality, the worlds spread out for the finder of light.
Like cows swelling in the stall, the thoughts flowing toward the Truth have lowed toward Indu.

When the sage bears his poetic wisdom around all the worlds like a hero on a chariot, he provides glory for mortals among the gods; as a new source of wealth for skillful men, he abounds in many manifestations.
Born for glory, he has gone forth from glory; he bestows glory and vital strength upon his singers.
Clothed in glory, they have attained immortality; their encounters with the measurer of the earth become true.
Flow toward us with nourishment and vigor; bestow horses and cattle, and create wide light. Intoxicate the gods!
For all those things are easy for you to overcome; O Soma Pavamāna, you drive away our enemies.
The tawny one neighs loudly as he is released, settling within the belly of the wooden vessel while being purified.
Led by the men, he makes the cow his garment; therefore, generate hymns through your own inherent powers.
The golden one, being released upon the path of Truth, sends forth his voice like a rower propelling a boat.
The god makes manifest the secret names of the gods upon the sacrificial grass for proclamation.
Like the surging waves of the waters, our inspired thoughts hasten toward Soma;
bowing down, they approach him and enter into him, longing for the one who longs for them.
They milk that Soma-stalk, which is being cleansed like a buffalo on a mountain ridge—the bull dwelling upon the mountains.
To him, as he bellows, the prayers cling; Trita bears Varuṇa within the ocean.
Sending forth your voice like the Upavaktṛ priest of the Hotṛ, O Indu, as you are being purified, release your inspired thought.
Since you and Indra rule for our well-being, may we be masters of heroic power.
The hero, the leader of the chariots, goes at the head of the hosts seeking cattle; his army exults.
Making the invocations to Indra auspicious for his friends, Soma puts on his impetuous garments.
His bay horses, with their horse-like speed, groom his bay steed incessantly with prostrations.
As the friend of Indra, he mounts the chariot; knowing this, he approaches with this benevolent thought.
O God, flow for us through the service of the gods, O Soma, as a great nourishment for Indra’s drink;
creating the waters and raining down this heaven, purifying yourself, grant us wide space from the vast expanse.
Flow for invincibility, for non-violence, for well-being, and for great, complete perfection!
All these friends desire that; O Soma Pavamāna, I too desire that.
Soma flows clear, the progenitor of hymns, the progenitor of heaven, the progenitor of earth;
the progenitor of Agni, the progenitor of Sūrya, the progenitor of Indra, and the progenitor of Viṣṇu.
The Brahman of the gods, the path-maker of the sages, the seer of the inspired poets, the buffalo of wild beasts,
the falcon of vultures, the axe of the forests— Soma goes forth singing across the filter.
Soma, while being purified, has caused the wave of speech, the songs, and the inspired thoughts to flow forth like a river.
Beholding these lower enclosures from within, the bull, knowing them, stands among the cows.

O Indu, as you flow for Indra, being exhilarating, victorious in battles, unassailed, and possessing thousandfold seed, pour forth toward booty; O wise one, as you purify yourself, send up the wave of the stalk, impelling the cows.
The beloved Soma, dear to the gods, flows into the jar for Indra as a source of exhilaration.
With a thousand streams and a hundredfold strength, the drop goes forth like a prize-winning steed to the assembly.
Born as the ancient winner of wealth, being cleansed in the waters and milked from the stone,
the protector against curses and king of the world, he finds a path for the sacred prayer while being purified.

For by you, O Soma, our ancient fathers performed their sacred rites, O Pavamāna, they who were wise. Winning [the prize], unassailed, open up the enclosures; be a bountiful patron to us with heroes and horses.
As you flowed for Manu, bestowing vital strength, slaying enemies, finding wide space, and accompanied by oblations—even so flow now, bestowing wealth; unite with Indra and bring forth our weapons.
Flow on, O Soma, honey-sweet and true to the Law, clothing yourself in waters upon the sheep’s-wool ridge.
Sit down within the wooden vats that are rich in clarity—most exhilarating, intoxicating, and the drink of Indra.
Flow with a hundred streams from heaven for rain, winning a thousandfold at the feast of the gods, seeking strength;
bellowing together with the rivers in the jar, and with the milk-cows, prolonging our lifespan.
This very Soma, being purified by our prayers, like a prize-winning steed, overcomes hostilities;
he is like the fresh milk of Aditi, like a wide path, or like a well-guided draft-horse.
O God Soma, well-armed and being purified by the pressers, flow toward your secret and lovely name; flow toward booty like a courser seeking glory, toward Vāyu, and toward the cows.
The Maruts with their host cleanse and beautify the beloved infant as he is born, the bearer of the oblation;
Soma, the seer, being himself a seer through his poetic power, passes through the filter chanting with songs.

He whose mind is that of a seer, who makes seers, who wins the light of heaven, who has a thousand leaders and is the pathfinder for the poets—the mighty Soma, seeking to attain the third station, shines as a sovereign king after Virāj. *ṣṭup* (the metre).
The hawk dwelling in the bowls, the far-reaching bird, the drop that finds the kine, bearing his weapons; following the wave of the waters toward the ocean, the buffalo proclaims the fourth station.
Like a handsome youth adorning his body, like a courser who has run for the winning of riches,
like a bull toward the herds, flowing toward the vat and bellowing, he has entered the two bowls.
Flow on, O Indu, as the purifying one with your great powers; bellowing, flow through the woollen filters.
Entering the two bowls while being purified, sporting, may your exhilarating juice intoxicate Indra.

His great streams have been poured forth; anointed with the products of the cow, he has entered the jars. Creating the *sāman*, the wise singer of *sāmans* comes roaring toward his kin, like one toward a friend.
Striking down the enemies, O Pavamāna, you go forth like a lover approaching his beloved;
Indu, like a bird flying to its nest, settles in the woods—Soma, being purified, sits within the jars.
O Soma, thy radiant beams, as thou art being purified, flow like a maiden—well-yielding and with excellent streams.
The tawny one, brought hither, rich in boons, has bellowed within the waters in the jar of those who seek the gods.
Being purified by his impulse and his zeal, the god has mingled his juice with the gods. Pressed out, he goes around the filter chanting, like a Hotṛ-priest to the measured dwellings rich in cattle.
Clothed in auspicious, well-fitting garments, the great seer, proclaiming the secret words,
flow into the two bowls while being purified— far-seeing, wakeful, at the banquet for the gods.
He is cleansed together upon the sheep’s-wool back, the beloved one, most glorious among the glorious, our master.
Flow toward us as you are being purified; do you protect us always with blessings.
Sing forth! Let us worship the gods; send forth the Soma for great wealth.
Sweet, he shall flow through the sheep’s wool filter; seeking the gods, may he sit within our jar.
The drop, approaching the friendship of the gods, flows in a thousand streams for exhilaration;
praised by men according to the ancient ordinance, he has gone to Indra for great good fortune.
O tawny one, flow for the singer and for wealth; being purified, let your exhilarating juice go to Indra for his support.
Come on the same chariot with the gods toward the gift; and do you all protect us always with blessings.
Proclaiming poetic wisdom like Uśanas, the god declares the generations of the gods;
he of great vows, whose kinship is pure, the purifier, approaches the stations, lowing like a boar.
Like swans, the bull-like hosts have gone toward the *tr̥pala* plant and toward fury; they have come home.
O friends, together they sound forth the song of praise for the purifying one, the hymn that is difficult to withstand.
He hastens with the speed of the wide-striding one; like cows lowing for their calf, they measure him as he sports at will.
The sharp-horned one makes himself full of abundance; by day he appears golden, and by night he is spotted-brown.
The prize-winning drop flows, the Soma that brings abundance of cattle; it flows toward Indra, inciting him to exhilaration.
He slays the demon and drives away all enemies; as king of the community, he creates wide space.
Then, mingled with honey in a stream, milked by the stones, Indu flows through the fleece;
the exhilarating god, enjoying the friendship of Indra, purifies himself for the intoxication of the god.
Being purified, the god flows toward his dear ones, bedewing the gods with his own juice;
Indu, clothing himself in his functions according to the seasons, has enveloped the ten fingers on the sheep-wool back.
The red bull, bellowing toward the cows, goes along making the earth and heaven resound;
like the roar of Indra, he is heard in the battle, and making this speech intelligible, he flows forth.
Worthy of being tasted, swelling with milk, you go forth impelling the honeyed stalk;
O Soma, as you are being poured out for Indra, you flow as Pavamāna, creating a continuous sound.
Flow thus, O exhilarating one, for intoxication, bending down the weapons of the one who seizes with his hand;
bearing your radiant color all around, flow for us, O Soma, seeking cattle when poured out.
Having enjoyed us, O Indu, flow on easy paths through the wide space, creating broad expanses;
striking away misfortunes on every side like a club, run over the high back upon the sheep’s wool.
Flow for us with celestial rain that is swift-moving, nourishing, full of refreshment, and quick-giving;
spreading out like loosened locks of hair, O Indu, flow along these lower paths, discerning the kinsmen and the winds.
O Soma, as you are being purified, untie the knotted tangle like a knot, and distinguish between the straight path and the crooked one.
Like a neighing bay horse let loose, O divine youth, run hither like a householder.
O Indu, beloved by the gods for their exhilaration, flow over the back of the sheepskin with your swelling stream.
With a thousand streams, fragrant and inviolable, flow around for the winning of booty in the contest of men.
Those which are without reins, without chariots, unyoked, like horses released in the race—these bright Soma drops flow; O gods, come near to them to drink!
Thus, O Indu, flow for us toward the feast of the gods; like a cloud, pour out a flood into the vessels.
May Soma grant us desirable, vast, and formidable wealth, accompanied by heroic sons.
When the speech of the longing mind fashioned him, or when [the cow] lowed at the ordinance of the highest Lord within the range of the milk,
then the cows, bellowing toward their choice, went to Indu in the jar as their beloved husband.
The celestial giver, swelling with gifts, the wise one, flows for the sake of Truth according to Truth;
he becomes the upholder of the law, the king of the assembly, and is borne across the earth by his ten rays.

Being purified by means of the filters, the observer of men, the king of both gods and mortals, has from of old become the lord of riches; the drop (indus) bears the well-sustained and beautiful *ṛta*.
Like a courser toward renown and gain, flow toward the feast of Indra and Vāyu;
as you are being purified, O Soma, bestow upon us great and thousandfold nourishments, becoming the finder of wealth.
May the Soma juices, which are to be poured out for the gods, flow toward our dwelling rich in heroes;
may they, seeking sacrifice, possessing all boons, and most delightful like the heavenly Hotṛ-priests, grant us their favor.

Thus, O God, flow for the sake of the gods, O Soma, for the great feast, as the drink of the gods. For we indeed stand firm even against the mighty in the assembly; while being purified, make the two worlds well-established.
Like a neighing horse yoked with stallions, like a terrifying lion swifter than thought— by the straightest paths leading hitherward, flow for us, O Indu, bringing benevolence.
A hundred streams, born of the gods, have been released; sages cleanse these thousands of them.
O Indu, flow down from heaven as a winner of wealth; you are the leader to great riches.
Like the streams from heaven, the outpourings of days have been released; the wise king does not violate his friend. Like a son following the will of his father, flow for this people with success.
Your honeyed streams have been released as you, purified, pass through the sheep’s wool; O Pavamāna, you flow for the domain of the cows. Being born, you have swollen the sun with your hymns.
Roaring along the path of Truth, you, the bright one, shine forth as the abode of immortality.
As such, you flow for Indra as an exhilarating draught, sending forth your voice through the hymns of the sages.

O Soma, you divine bird of beautiful wings, looking down and swelling with streams at the rite for the feast of the gods, O Indu, enter the vessel that holds the Soma; go bellowing toward the ray of the sun.
The bearer of the oblation sends forth three voices: the thought of the Eternal Law (*ṛta*) and the inspired wisdom of the sacred word (*brahman*).
Like cows seeking their master, they go toward the Lord of Cattle; like lowing thoughts, the hymns go toward Soma.

The milch-cows low longingly for Soma; the inspired poets seek him with their hymns, asking after him. Pressed and anointed, Soma is purified; for Soma, the *arkas* and the *triṣṭubh* verses sing together in harmony.
Thus, O Soma, being poured out and purified, flow for our well-being;
enter into Indra with a mighty roar, strengthen our speech, and generate abundant wisdom.
The watchful sage, the Soma, being purified through the thoughts of truth, has settled in the vessels;
him the pairs of Adhvaryus, longing for him, serve—the charioteers with skillful hands.
Being purified, he has filled both worlds like the sun from its source; he has opened them wide.
He, whose dear ones are truly dear through his aid, shall surely bestow wealth upon the singer as if for a victor.
May he, the increaser who grows strong while being purified—the bounteous Soma—protect us with his light;
by whom our ancient fathers, knowers of the path and finders of heaven, heated the rock to win the cows.
The ocean has roared, establishing itself in the first firmament, generating all creatures as the king of the world.
As a bull upon the sheep's-wool back of the filter, the pressed Soma, the drop, has grown great.
Soma the buffalo performed that great deed when, as the embryo of the waters, he chose the gods.
As Pavamāna, he bestowed vigor upon Indra; as Indu, he generated light in the sun.
Exhilarate Vāyu for our sacrifice and for bounty; exhilarate Mitra and Varuṇa as you are being purified.
Exhilarate the host of Maruts, exhilarate the gods, and exhilarate Heaven and Earth, O divine Soma!
Flow straight on, O destroyer of the crooked, driving away disease and our adversaries;
blending your milk with the milk of the cows, you belong to Indra, and we are your friends.
Flow as the sweetener of honey, a spring of wealth; flow to us with a hero and with fortune.
O Indu, being purified, be sweet for Indra; flow to us with riches from the ocean.

The pressed Soma, like a horse urged forward, has flowed in a stream like a river rushing down a slope; seeking the prize, he has settled in his wooden seat while being purified. The drop, Indu, has mingled with the milk and with the waters.
This very Soma of yours, O Indra, flows for you in the vessels—wise, longing, and powerful;
he who is self-luminous, a charioteer, and truly vigorous, has been released like the desire of those devoted to the gods.
Purifying himself with ancient vital power, assuming the forms of his daughter,
and clothing himself in a triple-layered protection within the waters, he goes forth chanting like a Hotṛ-priest at the assemblies.
Now, O divine Soma, flow as a charioteer into the two bowls while being purified;
most sweet in the waters, honeyed, true to the cosmic order, like the god Savitṛ whose thoughts are truth.
Flow toward Vāyu for his enjoyment, being praised; flow toward Mitra and Varuṇa while being purified;
flow toward the hero who impels our thoughts and stands upon the chariot; flow toward Indra, the bull whose arm wields the thunderbolt.

Flow toward us with well-woven garments; being purified, flow toward us with cows that yield milk easily. O divine Soma, bring us bright gold to support us, and flow toward us with chariot-drawing horses.
Flow toward us with celestial riches, and as you are being purified, flow toward all terrestrial wealth;
flow toward that by which we may obtain treasure, and toward our ancestral lineage like Jamadagni.
Flow with this purification, purifying these riches; O Indu, flow forth into the lake, making us full of strength.
Even here, like the wind driven by the sun, let the one of many wisdoms grant a hero to the swift one.
And so, purify us with these [streams] as you flow through the famous ford of Śravāyya;
may Naiguta shake down sixty thousand treasures for our delight, like ripe fruit from a tree.
Great indeed are his two bull-like names, for his strength, whether in the *māṃścatva* or in the *pṛśana* weapon.
He has sent the attackers to sleep and softened the enemies; he has driven away the faceless and the mindless.
You go toward the three filters stretched out; you run along one as you are being purified.
You are Bhaga; you are the giver of the gift; you are the bountiful one for the bounteous, O Indu.
This wise Soma, the knower of all, flows as the king of the entire world;
sending forth his drops at the assemblies, Indu passes through the sheep’s wool filter and goes on his way.
The inviolable buffaloes lick the drop; like eager poets, the sages sing at its station.
The wise urge it forward with ten fingers and anoint its form with the essence of the waters.
O Soma, through you, the purifying one, may we continually gather the wealth that has been made for us in battle.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us.
Flow toward us with wealth that best wins the prize, most desired by many— O Indu, a thousandfold sustenance, of great glory, and all-conquering might.
Being pressed, he has clothed himself in the sheep’s fleece as if in armor upon a chariot;
the drop, placed upon the wooden vessel, has flowed forth with his streams when urged on.
Being pressed, this Indu has flowed all around the sheep’s wool, distilling exhilaration;
rising up at the sacrifice, he goes like a stream of light, seeking the cattle.
For you indeed, O God, bestow wealth upon every mortal who offers oblations;
O Indu, you win for us riches consisting of thousands and hundreds of lives.
O Vṛtra-slayer, O Vasu, may we be the ones to receive from you this much-desired wealth;
O Adhrigu, may we be closest to your nourishing gifts and your favor.
Twice do the five sisters, their own glory, bathe him who is struck by the mountain— the beloved, desirable, surging wave, dear to Indra.
They purify with the fleece that beloved, golden-hued,
brown one on every side— he who, with his exhilarating juice, goes forth to all the gods.
For through his protection, you drink this [Soma] which accomplishes skill;
he who, like the sun, has established great renown among the patrons, being as desirable as heaven itself.
At your sacrifices, O two daughters of Manu, the drop was born for you both, O Heaven and Earth;
the god, dwelling on the mountains, has not failed that one of loud sound, O goddesses.
O Soma, you are poured out for Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, to drink;
for the hero who bestows sacrificial gifts, and for the god who sits upon his throne.
Those ancient Soma juices have flowed through the filter at the break of dawn; snorting away those who plot evil, they drive off the mindless ones in the morning.
O friends, may you and we, the wise patrons, attain that one who shines before us;
may we obtain him who is fragrant with booty and win him whose home is full of wealth.
For the beloved and bold one, they stretch out the bow, a manly deed; at the head of the inspired songs, the seekers of greatness weave a bright garment for the Asura.
Then, adorned by the night, he plunges toward the spoils of war,
when the prayers of Vivasvat urge the tawny steed to speed forth.
We cleanse that exhilarating juice of his which Indra drinks most readily—
that which the cows have yielded with their mouths in the past, and which the wise offer now.
They have celebrated with an ancient song him who is being purified;
and the prayers, bearing the names of the gods, yearn for him.
They purify him, the sustaining one, as he flows through the sheep’s wool;
the wise ones look toward him with their thoughts, as if toward a messenger sent for the first awareness.
Being purified, the most intoxicating Soma settles within the vessels;
like a bull depositing seed in a cow, he, the lord of prayer, manifests his eloquence.
He, the god pressed for the gods, is cleansed by those of skillful deeds; he knows when he plunges into these great waters as he bestows gifts upon them.
O Indu, pressed out and led forth by the men through the filter, you,
the most intoxicating, are seated within the vessels for Indra.
The guileless mothers low toward Indra’s beloved and desirable [Soma], just as they lick their newborn calf at the first time of its birth.
O Indu, being purified, bring hither, O Soma, wealth of double strength;
you nourish all treasures in the house of the donor.
Release the prayer yoked by the mind, as the thundercloud releases rain; O Soma, you cause the treasures of the earth and those of heaven to flourish.
Like the stream of one who has conquered, your flow of the pressed juice runs around; rushing through the sheep’s woolly filter like a prize-winning steed.
O Sage Soma, flow with your stream for our wisdom and skill;
you are pressed for Indra to drink, and for Mitra and Varuṇa as well.
Flow, O Soma, most excellent winner of booty, pressed with your stream through the filter for Indra, for Viṣṇu, and for the gods, as the most honey-sweet.
The guileless mothers lick you, the golden one, in the filter,
just as milch-cows lick their newborn calf, O Pavamāna, in the wide expanse.
O Pavamāna, you go toward great glory with your variegated rays;
boldly striking down the darknesses, you dispel them all in the house of the donor.
O you of mighty vows, you have surpassed both heaven and earth;
O Pavamāna, by your greatness, you have clothed yourself in a mantle.
Through the prior conquest of your soma-juice, for the exhilarating draught that has been pressed—
O friends, drive away the dog, the long-tongued one.
He who, being pressed, flows all around with a purifying stream— the drop is like a horse that must be harnessed.
The men, with all-encompassing thought, impel that Soma, who is difficult to master,
toward the sacrifice with the pressing-stones.
Pressed for Indra, the most honey-sweet, exhilarating Soma drops have flowed through the filter; may your intoxicants go to the gods.
"Indu flows for Indra," thus the gods have declared;
the Lord of Speech exerts himself as a sacrificer, ruling over all by his might.
With a thousand streams he flows, an ocean that stirs the voice; Soma, the lord of riches, the friend of Indra day by day.
This Pūṣan, this wealth, this Bhaga—Soma, being purified, flows on;
as the lord of all existence, he has looked out upon both heaven and earth.
The dear, eager cows have lowed together for the exhilaration;
the Soma drops, as they are being purified, prepare the paths.
O Pavamāna, bring that which is most powerful and worthy of renown,
that which surpasses the five tribes, and by which we may win wealth.
The Soma drops flow clear for us, the best finders of the way;
pressed as friends, they are stainless, pious-minded, and finders of the light.
Pressed out by the stones upon the ox-hide,
they who find wealth have resounded on every side for us with nourishment, being manifestly visible.
These purified, wise Soma juices, mixed with curds, are beautiful to behold like suns; moving swiftly, they abide firmly in the clarified butter.
Let no mortal obstruct that speech of the pressed juice;
drive away the stingy hound, as the Bhr̥gus struck down Makha.
The kinsman has clothed himself in his garment like a son for enjoyment within his parents' embrace; he has glided forth like a lover toward a maiden, like a suitor to take his seat upon the womb.
That hero, the accomplisher of skill, who has propped apart the two worlds—
he, the tawny one, the ordainer, has clothed himself in the filter to sit upon his seat.
Soma flows through the sheep’s woolly fleece upon the cowhide;
bellowing like a tawny bull, he goes toward Indra’s appointed place.
Acting as the child of the great ones, impelling the vision of the Eternal Order (Ṛta),
he has encompassed all dear things, even doubly so.
Near the two pressing-stones of Trita, he partook of that secret place;
then, through the seven stations of the sacrifice, [he attained] the beloved [place].
With the stream of Trita, he has sent forth wealth upon the three ridges;
the one of noble wisdom measures out his distances.
When he was born, the seven mothers instructed the wise one for the sake of glory;
he, being firm, has taken notice of riches.
In his service, all the guileless gods are of one accord; their delights become desirable when they take pleasure [in him].
The one whom the increasers of Truth have brought forth as a lovely embryo to behold—
the seer, most bountiful, much-desired at the sacrifice.
The two great mothers of *Ṛta*, moving together in harmony by their own nature,
prepare the sacrifice in due order as they anoint it.
With wisdom and with bright eyes, you have opened the stall of heaven;
impelling the vision of Truth at the sacrifice.
To Soma, the purifying ordainer, let a song be raised;
with my thoughts I bring an offering as a support, so that he may take pleasure in it.
Anointed with the products of the cow, he flows through the sheep’s woolly filters; being purified, the tawny one makes for himself three dwelling places.
It flows around the honey-dripping vat through the sheep’s wool filter;
the seven voices of the seers have sung aloud toward it.
The leader of prayers, the all-god, the undeceivable one—
Soma, the tawny one, being purified, flows into the two bowls.
Go along with the divine powers according to your own nature, in the same chariot with Indra;
being purified by the priests, O immortal one, together with the priests.
Like a courser seeking prize, the god pressed for the gods,
the all-pervading Pavamāna flows forth.
O friends, sit down; sing forth to the one being purified. Adorn him with sacrifices for his glory, as one would adorn a child.
Bring together, like a calf with its mothers, that which wins the household, the exhilarating drink that delights the gods and possesses double strength.
Purify that which accomplishes skill, so that it may be for the enjoyment of the host,
and most auspicious for Mitra and Varuṇa.
The voices have sung out toward you, the finder of wealth for us;
with cows we clothe your hue.
O Indu, lord of our exhilarations, you are the celestial nymph for the gods;
like a friend to a friend, be the best finder of the path.
Drive away from us every demonic and devouring foe; keep the godless and double-tongued man far from us, and deliver us from distress.
O friends, sing toward him as he is being purified for your exhilaration; like a child, they have made him sweet with sacrifices and hymns of praise.
Like a calf with its mothers, Indu, being urged forward, is anointed; the exhilarating drink, a friend of the gods, is adorned by our prayers.
This [Soma] is the accomplisher of skill; this is for the refreshment of the host;
this, most rich in honey, has been pressed for the gods.
O Indu, flow forth when pressed, rich in cattle and horses, O thou of excellent skill;
I have placed thy pure color upon the kine.
O Indu, lord of our bay steeds, most excellent as a feast for the gods,
be like a friend to a friend, a hero for our glory.
O Indu, drive away from us the godless, devouring Atriṇ who seeks to harm; overcome the double-dealer and all oppressors.
May these pressed drops, the tawny ones, go toward Indra, the bull;
born with speed, these Soma juices find the light of heaven.
This pressed Soma, the winner of booty, flows clear for Indra to bear; it takes heed of the conqueror, as one who knows how to act.
In the exhilarations of this [Soma], may Indra seize the winning grasp;
and let him, the winner of waters, wield the bull-like thunderbolt.
Flow forth, O Soma, wakeful one; flow around for Indra, O Indu!
Bring us brilliant strength that finds the light of heaven.
Flow for Indra as a virile exhilarating draught, O you who are visible to all; you who possess a thousand paths, the maker of ways, the far-seeing one.
The best finder of the way for us, the most honey-sweet for the gods—
go by a thousand paths, bellowing aloud!
Flow on with your streams in might for the feast of the gods, O Indu;
as the honeyed Soma, take your seat within our jar.
Your drops, floating upon the water, have strengthened Indra for exhilaration;
the immortal gods have drunk you for the sake of immortality.
O pressed drops, flowing clear, bring wealth to us—
ye who cause rain from heaven, who set the waters free, and who find the light of heaven.
Soma, being purified, flows through the woollen filter with his wave; as he purifies himself, he bellows at the forefront of speech.
With their prayers they urge on the prize-winner who sports in the wood, beyond the sheepskin;
the hymns have sounded forth together toward him of the triple back.
He has been let loose toward the jars like a prize-seeking steed in the contest; purifying himself and generating speech, he has flowed forth.
The beloved, tawny one flows with speed across all obstacles;
pouring forth heroic glory for his worshippers.
Flow thus, seeking the gods; streams of sweetness have been poured forth.
Chanting, you go around the filter from every side.
Pour out on every side the pressed juice, the Soma which is the supreme oblation—he, the friend of men, who has flowed within the waters; he has pressed the Soma with the stones.
Now, being purified by the sheep’s wool, flow around, unassailable and most fragrant.
Even when pressed in the waters, we exhilarate you with the soma-juice, blending you, the supreme one, with the milk of cows.
Being pressed for all to see, the exhilarating drink, the wise Indu, is the divine inspiration.
O Soma, being purified with your stream, you flow clothed in waters;
O God, bestowing jewels, you sit upon the womb of Order, a golden fountain.
Milking the divine udder for the beloved honey, he has sat upon the ancient dwelling place;
the prize-winning one flows toward the support that must be sought, shaken by men, far-seeing.
Being purified, O Soma, the watchful one, dear to us, you pass through the sheep's wool filter;
you have become a seer, the best of the Aṅgirases—sprinkle our sacrifice with honeyed sweetness.
Soma, the bounteous giver, flows on, the best finder of the path, a seer, a sage, far-sighted. You became a seer, most beloved by the gods; you caused the sun to ascend in heaven.
Soma, being pressed by the pressers upon the backs of the sheep’s wool, goes with a stream like a bay horse; he goes with a pleasant stream.
In the marshy place, Soma, rich in cattle, has flowed with the cows; he has flowed with the milked ones.
Like the ocean, they have gone to the enclosures; the exhilarating one pours forth for intoxication.
O Soma, pressed by the stones, flow through the sheep’s woolly filter;
like a man entering a city, the tawny one has entered the two bowls; you have taken your seat among the wooden vessels.
He has cleansed himself through the fine wool of the sheep, like a prize-seeking steed at the contest;
Soma Pavamāna is to be celebrated by the wise, by the inspired singers, and by those who chant the hymns.
O Soma, for the banquet of the gods, you have swelled like a river with its flood;
with the milk of the stalk, exhilarating and wakeful, flow toward the honey-dripping vat.
The beloved one has clothed himself in a bright garment; he is to be polished like a dear son. The skillful workers urge him forth with their hands, as one urges a chariot, into the rivers.
The Soma drops, active and wise, flow toward the intoxicating joy upon the surface of the ocean— intoxicants that find the light of heaven.
May Pavamāna cross the ocean with his wave, the King, the God, the lofty *ṛta*;
flowing according to the law of Mitra and Varuṇa, he is urged forward toward the lofty *ṛta*.
Guided by men, the lovely, far-seeing king, the god of the ocean.
The exhilarating Soma, pressed for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, flows in a thousand streams through the sheep’s wool; him the Āyus purify.
Being purified in the ladle, generating inspired thought, Soma the seer rejoices among the gods;
clothing himself in waters, superior with the products of the cow, he has invested himself in the wooden vats.
O Soma, O Indu, I have taken delight in your friendship day after day.
Many [obstacles], O tawny one, lie in wait for me; pass beyond those enclosures.
And indeed, O tawny Soma, by night and by day I have sought thy friendship at thy udder;
beyond the sun that burns with heat, we have flown away like birds.
Being cleansed by skillful hands, you send forth your voice upon the ocean; O Pavamāna, you flow toward wealth that is golden-hued, abundant, and much-desired.
Being cleansed in the woolly fleece while purifying himself, the bull has bellowed in the wooden vat;
O Soma Pavamāna, being anointed with milk, you flow toward the appointed place of the gods.
Flow on for the winning of booty, toward all poetic insights;
O exhilarating Soma, you were the first to spread out the ocean for the gods.
O Soma, flow forth by your divine laws across the earthly realm and through the celestial regions;
the inspired poets, O far-seeing one, urge you on with their prayers and hymns as you shine in splendor.
The purifying Soma-streams have been released through the filter in a continuous flow—
the exhilarating, Indra-like steeds accompanied by the Maruts— toward wisdom and sacrificial offerings.
Clothed in waters, Indu flows toward the vat, urged on by the pressers;
generating light, he has made the exhilarating ones roar, as one who puts on a garment makes the cows low.
Flow clear, O Soma, most rich in sweetness, for Indra, as the best provider of wisdom and the most exhilarating intoxicant;
flow as the great, heaven-dwelling, and most intoxicating draught.
Having drunk of you, whose drink finds the light of heaven, the bull acts like a bull;
he, the one of excellent wisdom, has stepped forth toward the nourishments and toward strength, like Etaśa.
For you indeed, O Pavamāna, most resplendent one, have proclaimed the divine generations for the sake of immortality.
That by which Navagva Dadhyanc uncovered [the secret], by which the sages attained their goal—
that [Soma] through which they have gained renown among the gods, within the favor of the lovely nectar of immortality.
This very one, pressed out, flows in a stream through the sheep’s wool filter as the most intoxicating;
he plays like a wave of waters.
He who by his might cleft the cows out from within the rock that held the waters of dawn;
you have spread out the stall of cattle and horses—O bold one, break it open like a warrior clad in armor!
O presser, pour out the praise-hymn like a horse— [the hymn] that crosses the waters, crosses the mid-air, roars in the forest, and floats upon the water.
The bull with a thousand streams, who increases the milk, dear to the divine race— he who, born of *ṛta*, has grown great by means of *ṛta*, the king, the god, the lofty *ṛta*.
O Lord of food, shine forth with lofty splendor and glory, O God who loves the gods; open the central vessel.
Flow forth, O most skillful one, pressed into the two bowls, like a leader of the people, a lord of the clans.
Flow as the rain from heaven, as the stream of waters; quicken our prayers for the sake of winning cattle.
They have milked from heaven this very bull, distilling intoxication, with a thousand streams,
him who bears all treasures.
The immortal bull was born, generating [all things] and scorching the darkness with light;
well-praised by the seers, he has assumed his triple-colored mantle through his wondrous power.
He is pressed, he who is the bringer of treasures, who is the bringer of riches, who is the bringer of libations— Soma, who is the bringer of secure dwellings.
Of whomsoever Indra shall drink, of whomsoever the Maruts, or Bhaga together with Aryaman;
by means of whom we may bring Mitra and Varuṇa hither—we summon Indra for great protection.
O Soma, most intoxicating and well-armed, directed by the men for Indra to drink,
flow on as the sweetest one.
Enter the heart of Indra, the receptacle of Soma, as rivers flow into the ocean;
you who are dear to Mitra, Varuṇa, and Vāyu, the highest pillar of heaven.
Flow forth, O Soma, sweet for Indra, for Mitra, for Pūṣan, and for Bhaga.
O Soma, may Indra drink of you when pressed, for the sake of wisdom and skill, as well as all the gods.
Thus flow, O bright celestial nectar, for the sake of great immortality and for the dwelling place.
Flow clear, O Soma, as a great ocean, the father of the gods, toward all abodes.
O bright Soma, flow pure for the gods, for heaven, for earth, and for the welfare of all creatures.
You are the sustainer of heaven, the bright nectar; as a prize-winning steed, flow on in accordance with the true ordinance.
Flow on, O Soma, radiant and with a fine stream, as the ancient one through the great sheep's fleece.
Guided by men, born and purified, the exhilarating one who finds the light of heaven flows forth with all [his powers].
The drop, being purified and choosing progeny for us, shall bestow all riches upon us.
Flow clear, O Soma, for wisdom and skill, like a groomed, prize-winning horse for the sake of wealth.
The pressers purify that juice of yours, the Soma, for exhilaration and for great splendor.
They cleanse the newborn infant, the tawny Soma, the drop, in the filter for the sake of the gods.
The lovely drop has flowed for exhilaration, the sage in the lap of the waters, for the sake of fortune.
He bears the beautiful name of Indra, by which he struck down all the Vṛtras.
All the gods drink of this, which has been mixed with milk and pressed by men.
Being pressed, he has flowed forth in a thousand streams across the filter, through the sheep’s woolly fleece.
He is the prize-winning steed with a thousandfold seed, being cleansed by the waters and mixed with milk.
O Soma, go forth into the belly of Indra, pressed by the men and guided by the stones.
The prize-winning steed, Soma, has been released through the filter for Indra in a thousand streams.
They anoint this Indu with the essence of honey for Indra, the bull, for his exhilaration.
For the gods, they cleanse thee, the tawny one, who art clothed in the waters, for thy spontaneous splendor.
The drop flows for Indra, it flows down; the fierce one, mixing [the draught], releases the waters.
Flow forth abundantly for the winning of booty, you who overcome all obstacles;
crossing over our enemies, you hasten toward us like one exacting a debt.
For we rejoice after you, O Soma, when you are pressed, for the sake of great sovereignty over the battle;
O Pavamāna, you plunge forward toward the spoils of war.
For you, O Pavamāna, have generated the sun and milk in the expanse by your power,
hastening with the cow-sped wisdom of the city.
He has generated the immortal among mortals, according to the law of Truth, the lovely nectar; ever-flowing, he hastens toward the prize of booty.
For you have pierced through with glory every single inexhaustible spring that men drink from,
like one carrying arrows in both hands.
Then some, beholding him as their kinsman, the celestial ones, radiant with wealth, have sung his praise;
like Savitar the god, he uncovers the treasure.
O Soma, in thee the first [sages], having strewn the sacrificial grass, have fixed their thought upon great strength and glory;
as such, O Hero, impel us toward heroic power.
The ancient nectar of heaven, worthy of praise, they have milked forth from the great depth of the sky;
they have raised their voices together toward Indra as he was being born.
And when, O Pavamāna, you pervade these two worlds, heaven and earth, and all these beings with your might,
you spread abroad like a bull standing over his herd.
Soma, being purified in the sheep’s wool filter, flows like a child at play; as Pavamāna, the drop with a thousand streams and hundredfold strength has flowed forth.
This Soma, being purified, flows as a sweet wave for Indra— the honeyed drop in the service of Truth—
winning booty, finding wide space, and bestowing vital strength.
Flow on, O Soma, overcoming those who attack us, driving away the demons and difficult paths; well-armed and victorious, subdue our enemies.
With this golden light, purifying himself, he overcomes all hostilities with his own yoked steeds, like the sun with his own yoked steeds.
The stream of the pressed juice shines as he purifies himself, tawny and ruddy;
when he encompasses all forms with the singers, with the seven-mouthed singers.

You find that treasure of the Paṇis; you cleanse yourself with your mothers in your own home, through the meditations of the *ṛta* in your home. Like a *sāman* from afar, that [song] exists where the meditations rejoice. With the threefold red [rays], he, shining brightly, bestows vital strength; he bestows vital strength.
He moves, observing keenly, along the eastern direction; his beautiful chariot strives with its rays, the divine chariot, the beautiful chariot.
Hymns have come forth to celebrate manly deeds, gladdening Indra for victory, so that you two may become the unshakable thunderbolt and remain unshakable in battles.
Our thoughts are indeed diverse, as are the religious observances of men;
the carpenter seeks the broken wood, the physician the sick man, and the priest the one who presses the soma—flow, O Indu, for Indra.
With aging plants and with the feathers of birds, the smith seeks to fashion a golden vessel with stones and flames; O Indu, flow around for Indra!
I am a poet, a physician, a grinder of stones, and a woman;
with various thoughts and seeking wealth, we follow thee like cattle—O Indu, flow around for Indra!
The horse is the drawer of the easy-moving chariot; the frogs are the whisperers of laughter; the penis desires the two hairy testicles, as a man desires water—O Indu, flow for Indra!
Let Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, drink the Soma at Śaryaṇāvat;
bestowing strength within himself, he intends to perform great heroic deeds. Flow around for Indra, O Indu!
Flow forth, O Soma, lord of the quarters, bountiful one from Ārjīka;
pressed with the word of Truth, with Reality, with faith, and with austerity—O Indu, flow around for Indra!
The daughter of the Sun brought that buffalo, who had grown strong through Parjanya;
the Gandharvas received him, and they placed that essence in the Soma. Flow around for Indra, O Indu!
Speaking the *ṛta*, O you whose splendor is *ṛta*; speaking the truth, O you whose deeds are true;
speaking with faith, O King Soma—you who have been prepared by the Creator—flow forth for Indra, O Indu!
The flowing streams of the great and formidable one flow together;
the juices of the flavorful one come together. Being purified by prayer, O golden-hued Indu, flow around for Indra.
Where the Brahman, O Pavamāna, speaking the metrical word, is exalted by the pressing-stone at the Soma;
generating bliss through the Soma, O Indu, flow forth for Indra.
Where there is eternal light, in that world where the sun is established—place me, O Pavamāna, in that immortal, imperishable world; flow around for Indra, O Indu!
Where King Vaivasvata dwells, where the enclosure of heaven is, where those great waters flow—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow around for Indra.
Where there is movement at will in the triple vault, the third heaven of the sky;
where the worlds are full of light—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow for Indra!
Where desires and longings are fulfilled, where is the summit of the sun, where self-sustenance and satisfaction abide—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow for Indra.
Where joys and pleasures, delights and raptures abide, where the desires of desire are attained—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow around for Indra.
O Indu, he who has stepped along the stations of the purifying Soma—him they call "possessed of good offspring," O Soma, he who has meditated upon your mind; flow forth for Indra, O Indu!
O Sage Kaśyapa, increasing the songs with the hymns of the mantra-composers, pay homage to King Soma, who was born as the Lord of plants; O Indu, flow around for Indra.
The seven directions have their various suns; there are seven hotṛ-priests as officiants;
and those seven gods who are the Ādityas—with them, O Soma, protect us. Flow around for Indra, O Indu!
O King, with that oblation of yours which has been prepared, protect us, O Soma!
Let not the malevolent overcome us, nor let anything whatsoever afflict us; flow around for Indra, O Indu!
In the beginning, the great one stood upright before the dawns; emerging from the darkness, he came with light.
Agni, fair-limbed with his radiant glow, having been born, has filled all dwellings.
Born as the embryo of heaven and earth, O Agni, you are lovely, distributed among the plants;
a brilliant infant, you have gone forth from your mothers, crying aloud beyond the darkness and the nights.
Viṣṇu, thus knowing his highest [abode], the great one born, protects the third [step]. When they have offered the milk of this [world] with their mouths, those who are of one mind sing praises here.
Therefore, the mothers who bear the food-bringers approach you with foods that increase the nourishment.
You go toward them again; you are the Hotṛ among the human clans, assuming various forms.
The Hotṛ-priest with the variegated chariot, the bright banner of every sacrifice,
the counterpart of every god by virtue of his greatness— Agni, the guest of men, endowed with splendor.
Wearing well-fashioned garments, he, Agni, born at the navel of the earth, the ruddy one, the domestic priest, has taken his place at the site of Iḷā; O King, worship the gods here.
For you, O Agni, have always extended across both Heaven and Earth, like a son over his two mothers. Come forth to those who long for you, O youngest one; then, O powerful one, bring the gods here.
Satisfy the longing gods, O youngest one; knowing the seasons, O Lord of Seasons, sacrifice here.
With those who are the divine officiants, O Agni, you are the most excellent sacrificer among the Hotṛ-priests.
You perform the office of the *hotṛ* and the *potṛ* for the people; you are the wise thinker, the giver of wealth, and the observer of cosmic order (*ṛtāvā*).
With the cry of *svāhā*, let us prepare the oblations; may Agni, the worthy god, worship the gods.
We have come even unto the path of the gods, that we may strive to follow it as far as we are able.
Agni, the wise one, shall sacrifice; he is the Hotṛ priest; he shall arrange the rites and the seasons.
O gods, if we, being more ignorant, violate the vows of you who are wise,
may Agni, the knower, fulfill all that through those seasons by which he ordains the gods.
When mortals, with simple minds and feeble skill, do not conceive of the sacrifice, may Agni—
the wise Hotṛ who knows the sacred rites and is the best of sacrificers— sacrifice to the gods according to the seasons.
For the progenitor begot you as the bright banner and the face of all sacrifices.
As such, perform the sacrifice for us along the man-filled lands, so that we may obtain desirable, food-abounding, and all-people-encompassing nourishments.
O Agni, you whom Heaven and Earth, you whom the Waters, and you whom Tvaṣṭṛ of noble birth have generated—
knowing well the path traveled by the fathers, blaze forth with splendor as you are kindled.
O King, this glowing steward has been kindled; the fierce one has appeared for the sake of skillful power.
He shines forth with great light, conscious; he goes toward the bright [dawn], driving away the black night.
When he, generating the dark, spotted maiden— the daughter of the great father— overcame her with his form, he, the messenger of heaven,
shines forth with his riches, supporting the upward-reaching light of the sun.
The auspicious one has come, accompanied by the auspicious; the lover follows after his sister.
Spreading out with well-marked days, Agni, with radiant colors, has overcome the darkness.
The courses of this great Agni, the kind friend, kindle voices like those of the mighty;
at the approach of the adorable, powerful, and lofty one, his fair faces and his rays shine forth like nights.
Like thundering sounds, his radiant beams flow forth as he shines, lofty and fair of aspect;
he who reaches the sky with his most excellent, sharpest, playful, and most exalted rays.
The breaths of this one, whose fellies are visible as he speeds along with his teams, resound loudly;
he who, the most divine messenger, shines forth widely with his ancient, radiant, and far-reaching rays.
As such, bring us great wealth and sit down as the messenger between the two youthful ones, Heaven and Earth.
May Agni, the swift one with his swift horses, come here, he who is impetuous with his impetuous steeds.
I sacrifice for you; I send forth this thought to you, so that you may become worthy of praise in our invocations.
O Agni, ancient King, you are like a watering-place in the desert for the Pūru who desires to worship.
O youngest one, you whom the people approach from all sides as cattle seek their warm stall— you are the messenger of both gods and mortals; great, you move through the radiant realm with your light.
Like a noble infant, thy mother, cherishing thee, bears thee as she seeks to please;
from the dry land thou rushest down the slope, longing for it, like a beast let loose to win the prize.
O wise one, we are foolish; you alone, O Agni, truly know your own greatness.
He lies there, yet he moves about in his covering; as the lord of the people, he licks and repeatedly caresses the youthful maiden with his tongue as he devours her.
Nowhere is he born; ever new in the ancient [woods], gray and smoke-bannered, he has taken his stand in the forest.
Without bathing in the waters, like a bull, he goes forward—he whom mortals, acting with one mind, lead forth.
Like two thieves who risk their lives, seeking forest game, they have bound [the victim] with ten cords.
O Agni, this is a newer hymn for you; yoke your chariot as it were with your radiant limbs.
O Jātavedas, may this sacred prayer and this song of homage be for you a constant source of increase.
O Agni, protect our children and our progeny; guard our bodies as well, never being heedless.
The one ocean, the supporter of riches, born of many origins, gazes upon us from our hearts;
he attends to the udder in the lap of the two secret ones, where the bird’s footprint is placed in the midst of the spring.
Sharing a common nest, the bulls, clothed in their garments, have come together with the mares.
The seers guard the station of Order; they have established their highest names in secret.
The two faithful and artful ones, having measured him out, have brought him together; increasing him, they have given birth to the infant.
They move toward the navel of all that is firm, as they follow with their minds the thread of the Sage.
For the paths of Truth, from of old, accompany the well-born one with nourishment for strength;
